decision at the beginning of the mandate to give one of their own successive presidencies of parliament, my group respects their candidacy and thanks them for their contribution to this election. but issues. this has not prevented us from placing our trust in you, because in the difficult situation europe is facing, what unites us is far more important than what divides us. you have, mr president, and you have just said so, a determination to defend the general european interest with all your might against the diversity of national interests. my group can only support you fully in this mission, in this action, aware that the coming months are going to be one of the most critical periods that europe has known since its creation. we have three priorities: defending the community method, advocating the community method and safeguarding the community method. nothing is more important than defending europe's heritage, namely to safeguard the general interest, to protect the smaller states from the larger ones and to respect their views without allowing immobility. nothing is more important than to emerge from the crisis from above, namely through stronger european integration, and nothing is more important than to demonstrate to our fellow citizens that the euro will be a strong and sustainable currency, provided we do what we should have done since its creation, namely economic and political governance. finally, nothing is more important than preserving the common good of solidarity between 500 million europeans. ladies and gentlemen, in creating what was to become centuries. adenauer, schuman and de gasperi have risen to the challenge and their successors have, to this day, perpetuated this european dream despite economic and internal difficulties and the upheaval of global geostrategic data. it is up to our generation not to fail in its task. it is up to us to overcome the current financial crisis, the current crisis of confidence, to ensure for our children - and you said it - a future that is not only sustainable but above all a better future. it is to you, mr president, and to us, ladies and gentlemen, as the elected representatives of the people of europe, that this challenge is addressed in the first place. it is up to you and us, together with the european commission, the guardian of the treaties, to show sufficient responsibility to convince our states that shared sovereignty and genuine economic and political convergence are our best weapons to meet the challenge of growth. mr martin schulz, as president of this institution you will have many external challenges to face and the epp group will be with you to do so in the european spirit i have just mentioned. we also encourage you to take this message to countries like ukraine, where yulia tymoshenko is being treated in an unacceptable way, or like syria, where the will of the people for change is being suppressed in an unspeakable way. you also intend to improve the internal functioning of this parliament, and i congratulate you on that. your predecessors have shown the way, and the recent adoption of a code of conduct is in line with the wish for greater transparency and greater accountability on the part of each member. my group will therefore support you on this front. mr president, you are now the head of an institution which has no equivalent in the world: a plurinational parliament which votes laws. for two and a half years you have been the leader of a parliament which does not seek to impose on the council the idea that it is not by creating a second treaty, a second parliament, a second governance that we will overcome our present difficulties, but by convincing it of this, mr president, that we will stand behind you whenever you defend this integrated europe, this europe of solidarity, this europe of innovative solutions. we will stand behind you whenever you advocate common european policies, whenever you fight for funding commensurate with the ambitions of these common policies. finally, we will stand behind you whenever you defend and promote, beyond our borders, the ideals and values on which our union is founded, namely freedom, tolerance, respect for the weakest and solidarity. i wish you, dear martin, a successful presidency.

for the greens/efa group mr president, i would first like to thank my three colleagues who have integrated me in a spirit of solidarity into the discussion group, as decided by the chairmen of the parliamentary groups. i would like to say two things about this treaty. first of all, it's completely useless. we don't need this treaty. it is not a treaty, it is an intergovernmental agreement which, according to those who have invented it, exists only to reassure the markets by asking for the constitutionalization of the so-called debt brake or the golden rule to be incorporated into national legislation. all the markets are telling us that they're not interested anyway. so we are making an intergovernmental agreement which does not interest the markets today because they want a political conception of the european economy for tomorrow. and this treaty will not ensure that political conception. we ask the member states that sign this treaty, for example, to say: we need a road map for the commission on the financial transaction tax. we are asking for a road map for the redemption fund, for the eurobonds. we won't have that in the treaty. for our group, with this agreement - you see, i always say "agreed" when it is an agreement - we are wasting time trying to improve something that is useless anyway. we are smart, we will improve it, but it is not the necessary response to the financial and economic crisis europe is experiencing today. this parliament must be clear. if it does not take legislative initiatives to demand that the necessary be done, it will not be able to meet the requirements of what needs to be done against the crisis of today.
in writing. at a time when the member states, under the impetus of the franco-german partnership, are redoubling their efforts to bring europe out of the crisis and to establish genuine economic governance, i regret the position of the european parliament which expresses doubts as to the necessity of the governmental agreement reached last december. the aim of the agreement is to create a 'fiscal stability union' which is capable of both reducing debt and strengthening financial stability in the euro area. the member states can no longer live beyond their means and must bring their budgets back into balance as quickly as possible. budgetary discipline becomes the gold standard. i am convinced that this agreement represents a decisive step in european integration, and i have therefore voted against this resolution.
in writing. i am expressing more than my doubts today about the new treaty, which should now be called the intergovernmental treaty, which is under negotiation... we do not need a new treaty, and certainly not this one! let's do with the existing! we must focus on debt, but we must go beyond budgetary austerity: in a previous resolution this parliament called for a road map with a plan for growth, investment and employment. that's the direction we should be going. unfortunately, this parliament is not included in these negotiations. what legitimacy would an agreement negotiated in this period of deep crisis in the eu have without full and complete cooperation with the european parliament as well as with the national parliaments?
in writing. i did not vote for the resolution criticising the outcome of the european council of 8 and 9 december 2011. the agreement reached, at the instigation of nicolas sarkozy and angela merkel, provides the appropriate basis for strengthening budgetary discipline through a mechanism of automatic sanctions and the inclusion in each constitution of a golden budgetary rule. i would add that parliament's resolution implicitly and inappropriately defends the right of the court of justice of the european union to monitor the level of deficits in national budgets. it also provides for the possibility for states not participating in the enhanced economic union to take part in the negotiations on the final text!
in writing. this resolution is again off the table. the only way out of the economic and institutional crisis is to strengthen the 'community method', i.e. to build a europe without the peoples. the draft intergovernmental treaty essentially proposes 'ever closer' economic governance and quasi-automatic sanctions for member states. while claiming to 'fully respect the responsibilities of national parliaments', the text marginalises the representatives of the people a little more, places the court of justice of the eu above national constitutions and forces states to conduct an economic policy determined from outside (the policy of austerity and deflation). neither the absence of an optimal currency area nor the european market's overexposure to social and ecological dumping from low-cost countries are taken into account. with a wrong diagnosis of the crisis and a wrong remedy for it, european economies will not have the freedom they need to regain their dynamism and growth.
in writing. i was surprised to see mr douglas peterson absent from the house, as he is now more than a party to your policies. the problem is not that the new so-called 'fiscal' treaty is purely intergovernmental or in line with the community method. it is a new prison for national policies, a new prison cell that the european union is increasingly becoming. it is intended to speed up and sanctify a budgetary policing process which is already part of the six-pack. and, of course, to re-create international finance, which has become your alpha and omega. we know what is happening to the credibility of your actions on the small financial oligarchy that claims to rule the world: loss of "a" repeatedly, first of the states, then of all the communities, companies, entities that benefit from their guarantee. refusal of banks to honour their promise to contribute to the resolution of the crisis, despite the 500 billion euros made available to them by mr draghi. all this is a guarantee of new financial and economic difficulties, which will themselves lead to further deterioration in an endless vicious circle in which the eternal losers are the impoverished, precarious and oppressed peoples of europe.
in writing. i abstained on the joint resolution on the conclusions of the european council (8 and 9 december 2011) on a draft international agreement on a union for fiscal stability. the resolution stresses the need for a community approach to the establishment of a genuine economic and budgetary union, and in substance, by stressing that budgetary discipline alone cannot solve the european economic and financial crisis, but the text does not sufficiently call into question the substance of the draft agreement. the root causes of the crisis must be addressed by challenging neoliberal policies; the european parliament has been asked to vote on the report by mr glinne, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy, on the proposal for a council regulation (ec) on the conclusion of the agreement between the european economic community and the republic of iceland on trade in textile products, and on the proposal for a council regulation (ec) on the conclusion of the agreement between the european economic community and the republic of iceland on trade in textile products, and on the proposal for a council regulation (ec) on the conclusion of the agreement between the european economic community and the republic of iceland on trade in textile products, and on the proposal for a council regulation (ec) on trade in textile products. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the future of the european union.
in writing. contrary to what the resolution says, i have no doubt that an intergovernmental agreement is necessary for fiscal stability in europe. on the contrary, it is a significant step towards a strong, immediate and lasting response to the financial, economic and social crises affecting many member states of the union. it would be irresponsible and unrealistic, as the french socialist party points out, to renegotiate such an agreement! i abstained on the final vote on this resolution because the text also states that all member states, including those which do not have the euro, should participate in the euro-zone summits. this is economic and political nonsense, because the euro area member states want to strengthen economic governance and budgetary coordination.
in writing. the draft treaty currently under negotiation is unacceptable in substance and form. it is purely punitive in substance and consists exclusively in constitutionalising the 'golden rules' of deficit reduction and promoting austerity, ignoring the absolute need to invest in order to restore growth and employment. this treaty is locking europe into recession, and we cannot accept that. the form of the agreement is negotiated in secret by the heads of state, completely ignoring the role of the european parliament as co-legislator and the role of the national parliaments. the negotiating group granted to the european parliament is far from allowing a fair representation of european citizens in this discussion. the resolution adopted may express some criticisms and reservations about the draft treaty, but it is too timid on these points, which is why i abstained.
in writing. i voted against this resolution. it clearly calls into question the commitment and determination of our president of the republic, who, alongside the german chancellor, has worked tirelessly to combat the financial and economic crisis and to strengthen european economic governance. this resolution lacks all encouragement and consideration for the efforts made since the beginning of the crisis and is only too particular in its legal form. but this is primarily a political question. this resolution was adopted by 521 votes to 124. i'm sorry for what i did. the votes in favour are the result of a heterogeneous conglomerate of anti-europeans, nationalists, federalists and other pro-community people of all stripes.
in writing. i voted against the joint resolution on the conclusions of the european council of 8 and 9 december on a draft international agreement on a budgetary stability union. at the european council on 9 december, 26 eu member states committed themselves to strengthening budgetary and economic coordination and laid the foundations for a new interinstitutional treaty on european economic governance. i regret that the european parliament, through this resolution, is expressing its doubts as to the relevance of this draft intergovernmental treaty, which is a strong political act towards greater european integration and cohesion. i do not think it is any more sensible than the resolution calls for all states, including non-euro-area states, to participate in euro-area summits.
in writing. i strongly oppose the move to draw up a new treaty imposing austerity on the peoples of europe. the current negotiations bypass the representatives directly elected by the european citizens by limiting themselves to the circle of governments and excluding national parliaments and the european parliament. the adoption of the form of negotiation between states gives the most democratic bodies only a role of validating the fact of the matter. this denial of democracy is all the more intolerable, since the very future of the european project is at stake, which exchanges european solidarity for the austerity demands of the central bank and the commission. the mechanisms of supervision and sanction provided for constitute a step up in the economic policy of the states, prohibiting them from any stimulus through consumption and investment. the union must instead fundamentally revise its economic foundations and move towards a new pact for social progress which puts people at the centre of its concerns. a european central bank, at the service of the people, must be the instrument of this ambition by giving priority, through credit, to investments that create wealth and public goods in education, training, research, infrastructure and public services.
in writing. this joint resolution by the right, the social democrats and the greens marks their agreement with the substance of the treaty under negotiation, namely the imposition of a strengthened golden rule. this rule requires member states to have balanced or surplus budgets and to aim for a reference figure of 0.5% of nominal gdp of structural deficit. it forces them to engrave this dictate preferably in the marble of their constitution. it requires them to set up automatic mechanisms for 'correcting' their budgetary policies as directed by the commission. far from being concerned about such measures, the four signatory groups merely call for their participation in the process of creating the new treaty and its incorporation into community law within five years. they do not even demand the right for the people to decide by referendum on this new round of 'austerity'. i vote against it.
in writing. i am not in the habit of going against the wishes of my group, especially when it comes to giving our opinion on decisions that are so decisive for the future of our union. but the text presented calls into question all the work, all the efforts made by our governments. nicolas sarkozy and angela merkel, the initiators of the agreement, have said it many times: this text is "the best common denominator". we're not playing. this is not the time to put an end to the non-receiving in the inexhaustible battle between the "bad intergovernmental method" and the "good federalism". all wills are good to take. the agreement goes so far that we even have a major absentee: the united kingdom. i am of course in favour of a strong european parliament. we have the heavy burden of representing half a billion people. but first, let's assume our own prerogatives. the question was: how to solve the sovereign debt crisis. so it was up to them and them alone to find a solution. they have done so, as we meps have been asking for a long time. we should have stressed that point. i regret that this text was adopted.
in writing. i abstained from voting in favour of this resolution because i do not share all the conclusions it contains. it seems to me inappropriate to criticize the efforts made by the german chancellor and the french president to achieve real economic governance through an agreement that allows for the rapid adoption of courageous measures. we must welcome, on the contrary, the emergence of political will in the euro area countries to go further and faster in integrating the economies and respecting the stability pact. however, we must be careful not to create two different legal orders and to involve in an appropriate way the states which have not yet adopted the euro. finally, we must combine this policy of fiscal stability with a genuine policy of sustainable growth and employment, so as not to be locked into a recessionary spiral. the structural funds will be the essential instrument.

the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in september 2010 parliament voted in favour of the report of the committee on agriculture on ensuring fair incomes for farmers. in doing so, it sent a clear signal to the european commission to restore the balance of power between farmers on the one hand and manufacturers and distributors on the other. the report i am presenting today completes the work we have started by analysing the upstream part of the agricultural sector. farmers sell their products but are also buyers or users of many inputs, the most important of which are fertilisers, seeds and fuel. these inputs are sold to them, as a rule, by large international companies operating in a highly concentrated, non-transparent and non-competitive environment. farmers also need land and water to work. on the one hand, farmers' bills are skyrocketing, while at the same time prices for their produce are stagnating or, in some cases, falling. the peasants are caught between a rock and a hard place. the report i am presenting to you today proposes concrete solutions to improve the economic situation of farms and farmers' incomes. farmers must be supported by new agricultural development structures which will enable them to face the challenges ahead, whether environmental, such as global warming, or economic, such as market distortions caused, for example, by speculation. the measures provided for in the reform of the cap, proposed by the commission and currently being discussed in parliament, can, if effectively implemented by the states, improve soil conservation, maintain agricultural biodiversity and reduce pollution of soil and groundwater. this agronomic development will reduce the amount of synthetic fertilisers and pesticides used. at the same time, farmers will be able to retain a larger share of the surplus value generated by their labour. the impact will be multiple. it will help to boost farmers' incomes, contribute to europe's efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and reduce pollution of our water resources. european agriculture consumes more energy than it produces. without oil, we are no longer able to feed ourselves. what a paradox! between 2000 and 2010, the price of fossil fuels increased by more than 60%, without farmers being able to pass this increase on to their products. we want the european union to invest heavily in energy-saving projects. these should be based on several proposals: improving agricultural practices by making them more autonomous; reducing transport between producers and consumers; facilitating the establishment of short marketing routes and supporting local seasonal consumption; strengthening the autonomous production of energy on farms; rebalancing animal and plant production at the level of coherent production basins, by promoting agronomic practices such as crop rotation and grazing. the cost of fertilisers, meanwhile, has doubled in the last ten years, while prices paid to farmers have increased by only 25%. however, effective agronomic practices, in particular crop rotation, can greatly reduce the use of these products and thus greatly reduce leaching, which pollutes groundwater, and the emission of nitrogen oxides. improved cropping techniques also lead to a reduction in pesticides and herbicides, by reducing the pressure of pests and weeds. waste and collected water is also a potential source of fertiliser, provided that adequate measures are taken to ensure the effective separation of potentially hazardous substances. but the dependence of the european union and farmers is not limited to oil and phosphates. every year, we import 50 million tons of animal feed. these purchases in world markets cost 20 billion dollars, which has a huge impact on our trade balance. we must reduce our dependence by 70% by launching a large european programme for the production of vegetable proteins: soybeans, lupins, beans, etc. the 30% increase in average seed prices since 2000 also affects farmers' incomes. this increase is due to the increasing price of certified seed, sold by an increasingly small number of large international companies. but it is also linked to the measures taken by a number of member states to limit the use of farm seed, which costs 40% less and is produced and used by farmers themselves. but farmers are also affected by the price of land and rents, which have skyrocketed in recent years. these phenomena are mainly linked to urban sprawl, land grabbing for the production of agrofuels and the race for expansion linked to the drift of the cap. the report calls for the establishment of a land price monitoring system and appropriate measures to facilitate access to land for young people and those wishing to develop an agricultural activity. finally, irrigation is essential in many areas of the european union where global warming is already being felt. concrete and rapid measures must be put in place to conserve and preserve this resource. this report is therefore very clearly in line with the europe 2020 strategy, which was set out at the beginning of the mandate, to offer a positive perspective to the european project in the face of the crises that threaten us. agriculture is the first integrated european policy. we must not leave the peasants on the side of the road today. there will be no europe without peasants!
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank maria patrão neves for her excellent work. we welcome the general consensus that has emerged on this text. the subject matter was compelling. for years, the share of income that goes to farmers has been steadily decreasing. as the statistics show, this decline is not due to any one actor but is caused by the structural weight deficit suffered by producers within the food chain. this has already been said many times by many of us, but i do not know whether to rejoice or to worry. this has been said many times: producers must be allowed to weigh in the chain as accurately as possible and above all in proportion to their importance. the rules of competition must apply equally to all and must not lead to the profound imbalance we have already highlighted. the reality, of course, is far from that. this unequal treatment is largely due to the different application of eu rules by national competition authorities. as meps, we are on the ground, we are field agents and we can testify to the difficulties faced by many farmers or producer organisations when they want to join forces to confront processors, distributors and their own competitors. in particular, the definition of the relevant market varies from one member state to another in the case of a concentration. when producers want to group together to weigh heavier, some national competition authorities prevent them from doing so. they consider that the national market should not be subject to this concentration and the increased weight of this new organization. on the contrary, the opposite is the case in other member states. these groupings are allowed because the relevant market is the european market. their weight is then proportionally less important and their position is not considered to be dominant. it is clear that this situation is not sustainable. the commission and the court of justice, as guardians of community legality and the uniform application of the law, must ensure that these national authorities do not maintain producer organisations in a position of inferiority which affects their bargaining capacity.

in writing. since joining the wto in 2000, georgia has been steadily moving towards the european union. this agreement, which aims at the mutual protection of geographical indications, is a further sign of georgia's willingness to expand its trade relations with us. georgia is already a party to the agreement on trade-related aspects of intellectual property rights (trips). it therefore recognises the concept of geographical indications for place names used to identify the origin and quality, reputation and other characteristics of products. the agreement covers agricultural products and foodstuffs from georgia and the european union and provides for the protection of the quality and origin of products from both partners. i can only support this initiative which diversifies the european union's trade relations while protecting our producers.
in writing. i voted in favour of this agreement which will help to protect our products from the land by recognising their characteristics and preserving their specificities.
in writing. my vote went to this agreement between the european union and georgia which makes it possible to make great progress in the protection of geographical indications of agricultural products or foodstuffs. the agreement contains an extensive list of mutually recognised indications. this agreement thus provides for greater protection of the great variety and quality of our local products, which are part of our identity and our wealth.
in writing. i vote for the protection of geographical indications of our products and products in general. my vote does not amount to approval of the free trade agreement concluded between the european union and georgia.
in writing. the european union is the country's main trading partner (almost 30% of its trade). i voted in favour of this agreement because, in view of the figures, it is important to ensure effective protection of our geographical indications in this country, which will be possible under the provisions of this agreement. they include a list of geographical indications recognised by both parties, guaranteeing legal certainty for operators, specific provisions for agricultural geographical indications and an objection procedure open to interested parties (producers, businesses). moreover, this is the first time that such an agreement has been concluded with one of the countries of the european neighbourhood policy. i supported this initiative in order to send a signal to the european commission that it must start and continue negotiations on this type of agreement with the other neighbourhood countries.
in writing. the world forum of the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) aims to bring together the main vehicle manufacturing countries to harmonize standards on vehicle construction, types of parts used, etc. in this case, the protection of the occupants of the cab of a commercial vehicle was more specifically concerned. with my colleagues from the epp group, we voted in favour of this unece regulation which will pave the way for the application of the same standards in many countries, removing the administrative burdens. we have therefore authorised the european commission, as the european union's representative to the un economic and social council, to vote in favour of this regulation, which will strengthen the weight of our companies on the world market.
in writing. the regulation on the accession of the union to regulation no 29 of the united nations economic commission for europe on uniform requirements for the approval of vehicles with regard to the protection of the occupants of the cab of a commercial vehicle is a very good report. so i decided to support him.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft regulation of the united nations economic commission for europe on pedestrian safety and the draft regulation on light sources with light emitting diodes (leds). here again, the regulation is mainly aimed at removing administrative barriers and will enable european companies to be able to operate on global markets. we have therefore authorized the european commission, as europe's representative on the united nations economic commission for europe, to vote in favour of this regulation. finally, while we are seeing progress in road safety and trade, this text also has an environmental impact.
in writing. always committed to ensuring that an agreement is in conformity with european union law, i voted in favour of this agreement between the european union and indonesia as it allows for the correction of national designation clauses in bilateral agreements which had become, since a decision of the court of justice in 2002, contrary to european union law. in order to avoid discrimination between union air carriers, the national designation clauses are replaced by a union designation clause. as our rapporteur brian simpson has said, the aim is to allow all eu air carriers to have access to air links between the eu member states concerned and indonesia without discrimination. moreover, while traditional bilateral agreements tend to exempt international flights from fuel taxes, such taxation is permitted for operations carried out within the territory of the european union. the aim of the agreement is therefore to extend this right enjoyed by the member states of the union to indonesian airlines wishing to operate flights within the union.
in writing. this agreement, in line with other agreements concluded between the eu and third countries, will benefit our airlines by prohibiting any form of discrimination in access to the indonesian market.
in writing. this is a 'classic' agreement negotiated by the commission under its 'horizontal' mandate. the main objective of this agreement is to allow all eu air carriers to have access to air routes between the eu member states concerned and indonesia without discrimination. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. traditionally, international air relations with third countries have been governed by bilateral agreements, i.e. from one state to another. however, in 2002, the court of justice of the european communities censured the presence of national designation clauses in such agreements as it could lead to discrimination between carriers in the european union (eu). the agreement i voted for provides for the replacement of national designation clauses by an eu designation clause. the eu air carriers will now have access to the indonesian market without risk of discrimination.

in writing. under rule 81 of its rules of procedure, the european parliament has the right to give its consent to the conclusion of a cooperation protocol of the european union (eu). i voted in favour of the protocol which aims to strengthen relations and cooperation between the eu and the international civil aviation organisation (icao). it is essential that the european union participates in the decision-making process within icao in order to protect the competitiveness of its own industry.
in writing. as a guarantor of the mobility, safety and security of its citizens, it is essential that the european union is more involved in the international regulatory process in the field of civil aviation. the international civil aviation organization, a specialized agency of the united nations, is a privileged forum for decision-making and influence. sitting as a european entity, not as a group of member states, will accompany our efforts and accelerate our project for a single european sky. that is why i voted in favour of the cooperation protocol between the eu and icao. since these decisions have a direct effect on our community legislation, it is imperative that we ensure that they are consistent with our policy guidelines and ethical considerations. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, including the first of which is our vision for a sustainable development of civil aviation.
in writing. the european parliament paves the way for the revision of the waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee) directive, which will allow consumers to return small equipment to retailers free of charge without the obligation to make a new purchase. through my vote, i campaigned for better collection and recycling of weee. i support this agreement based on ambitious but achievable objectives. this directive strengthens the selective collection objectives, broadens the scope and imposes new take-back and treatment obligations on producers and retailers. it is a big step for the environment and for the consumer. the annual collection target of 4 kg per capita per member state shall be transformed into a collection level of 45% of weee placed on the market in the previous three years collected by 2016 and 65% in 2019. finally, the directive, while reducing the administrative burden on producers, who are financially responsible for waste management, changes the definition of producer to cover any entity placing equipment on the market.
in writing. we are now seeing all the limitations of our "short-termist" societies, which are also breathless, where hyperconsumption and disposable are king: the issue of waste treatment, recycling but also the obsolescence of everyday consumer products are at the heart of the problems we have to manage within our societies. the directive we are adopting today concerns waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee). each european citizen generates an average of 17 to 20 kg of electronic waste per year! the target is situational: the directive requires each member state to increase its collection of weee, regardless of whether or not it already meets the 4 kg per person per year target. this directive is positive for european consumers, who will now be able to return small items to retailers and businesses without the obligation to buy a new product. this directive represents a new step forward for the recycling and treatment of weee in europe. i very much welcome stricter controls on illegal shipments of weee to third countries, to prevent the treatment of weee from endangering workers.
in writing. after tough negotiations with the council, parliament can be satisfied with the ambitious targets it has just set for the whole of the european union in the area of electronic waste collection. from 2016, most member states will have to collect 45 tonnes of electronic waste for every 100 tonnes of electronic products placed on the market in the previous three years. the adoption of this agreement is all the more important as it is part of a necessary and urgent european strategy for the supply of raw materials and rare earths. only investment in recycling techniques and better collection of electronic waste will enable the european union to reduce its dependence on china, which has 95% of the raw materials needed for new technologies.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which sets more ambitious targets for the recycling of waste electrical and electronic equipment. these wastes, some of whose components can become toxic, require special treatment to ensure that they are completely safe. this text will also make it easier for our citizens to dispose of their equipment that is no longer in use, without incurring additional costs.
in writing. every year, 8.7 million tonnes of waste electrical and electronic equipment are dumped in the european union, but only 25% of this waste is collected and treated. it is not unusual to find in this type of waste components which are particularly dangerous to health and the environment, and this situation calls for a change in the practices currently in force in our member states. it is in this context that i have voted in favour of the compromise reached after many years of negotiations, which sets a target of 85% of waste to be collected by 2019. thus, despite the opposition of some companies complaining of a heavy burden, it is expected that large distributors will have to set up collection points for used phones and other small appliances to encourage consumers to recycle. a new obligation will also be introduced to prevent european companies from sending potentially dangerous goods outside the eu. finally, another advantage: the recycling of precious metals such as gold, silver and rare earths contained in these used products, which will reduce our dependence on foreign supplies for these materials.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the report on electronic waste and electronic equipment, which seals the agreement reached with the council of the european union at second reading. the aim of this revision is to improve the operation of the waste collection and treatment chain. thanks to this directive and the efforts made by the member states, the collection of waste will have to amount to 45% of the average weight of equipment sold in the territories of the member states each year. these efforts will have to be increased to 65% within four years of the entry into force of the text. the directive will also have an impact on people's daily lives, as it provides for the mandatory installation of collection points for small waste in shops selling electrical and electronic equipment. this measure, however, protects small businesses which will not be obliged to have a collection point on their premises, provided that a similar system is in their immediate vicinity.
in writing. combining new, more stringent objectives, flexibility, encouragement of the reuse of equipment and the obligation to have collection points for small waste, the florenz report is balanced. i have therefore chosen to support the agreement reached at second reading.
in writing. the report proposes to set a separate collection target of 85% of waste electrical and electronic equipment by 2016. it insists that stringent ecodesign rules be set by the end of 2013 at the latest. it calls for the possibility of selective treatment of weee containing nanomaterials to be assessed. i am therefore in favour of this report, although i deplore its obsession with respect for the sacred and holy principle of free competition.
in writing. in europe, 9.3 million pieces of electrical and electronic equipment are sold each year. refrigerators, ovens, washing machines, irons, televisions, computers, telephones, compact fluorescent lamps - all these products are waste that we will have to recycle one day. it is estimated that in 2005 more than eight million tonnes of electronic waste were produced in europe, or 20 kg per capita. this total is expected to rise to 12.3 million tonnes by 2020. the european union had to fill the regulatory gaps that prevented a real management of this waste, in terms of collection, reprocessing, recycling or combating its illegal export. the collection rate of electrical and electronic waste in eu countries will have to reach 45% of the volumes placed on the market within four years and 65% within seven years. the directive also provides for: a reinforcement of the extended producer responsibility, an increase in the collection targets for household and professional weee, an increase in the recycling targets and a reduction in the administrative burden for businesses. i therefore support this new step towards an environmentally friendly and resource-efficient economy.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which recasts a 2008 directive to set more ambitious targets for the recycling of waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee). this directive, although insufficient in itself, is a step in the right direction towards the objective of an ecological transformation of our society. it is based on a triple choice: to produce sustainable equipment, to reuse as much as possible the materials of end-of-life products, and to involve local actors in this recycling. the directive still needs to be implemented on the basis of specific criteria such as: the creation of 'convenient facilities, including public collection points, where households can deposit their waste at least free of charge'; the implementation by the member states of a minimum collection of 85% of waste electrical and electronic equipment; the provision by producers, free of charge, for each type of new eee placed on the market and within one year of the equipment being placed on the market, of information on preparation for re-use and treatment. the ecological transition also involves this type of policy choice.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft directive on the placing of biocidal products on the market, which provides for stricter controls to ensure that products do not pose a threat to humans, animals and the environment. as part of my involvement as a member of the envi commission, i supported the work of my colleague christa klass. it seemed to me that it was basic to regulate the marketing of dangerous substances, and even to ban those which are carcinogenic, affect genes or hormones, or are toxic to reproduction. under the precautionary principle, authorisation procedures will be simplified, allowing consumers to have access to safer and more effective plant protection products. this is a significant improvement on the current legislation as it provides industry with a more efficient and reliable authorisation system, both in terms of requirements and procedures, resulting in uniform safety assessments. finally, in addition to the objective of harmonising standards, measures are being taken to facilitate mutual recognition of approvals between member states.
in writing. biocides are used in all aspects of our daily lives and are designed to kill harmful organisms such as bacteria or microbes. these substances, however effective, are dangerous to human health and the environment. we adopted a regulation last wednesday by a very large majority which harmonises the european market for biocidal products and sets new deadlines for the evaluation of applications in order to better protect human health and the environment. it includes, for the first time, specific and comprehensive provisions on nanomaterials. it was urgent and necessary to fill this gap in european legislation. commercially sold articles treated with biocides will therefore have to mention all the products used on their label. substances considered to be carcinogenic or to affect genes, reproduction or hormones will be strictly prohibited in order to protect citizens and to encourage industry to innovate by developing new and safer products. however, we must remain vigilant about new authorizations and renewals of granted exemptions: states will be able to make an exception in cases of absolute necessity... the regulation is a further step towards a more sustainable economy that respects consumers.
in writing. biocidal legislation has just been updated to give europeans access to new, safer and more effective plant protection products. thus treated products - such as furniture treated with fungicides or kitchen countertops treated with antibacterials - will be subject to these rules and will have to be labelled accordingly. for products containing nanomaterials, separate safety checks and labels will be provided to inform about their presence and possible risks. the adoption of this text shows how our knowledge of the environment and plant protection products is constantly evolving and therefore requires the regular review of european texts by the european parliament to ensure the placing on the market of products that are increasingly safe for our citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which regulates the use of products dangerous to human health. the reciprocity clause will guarantee our fellow citizens that imported products will be subject to the same rules as community products and will meet european health and safety requirements.
in writing. the use of biocides is a major problem, since consumer protection and environmental protection are among the issues involved. i welcome the adoption of the text for which i voted. the aim of this is to correct the weaknesses of directive 98/8/ec of 16 february 1996 on the use of biocidal products. the new text thus makes it possible to increase the health requirements not only in the production of biocides but also in their use. it also brings about a welcome harmonisation of existing rules which considerably increases consumer safety and environmental protection and eliminates distortions of competition within the internal market. finally, the text contains a liability clause under which imported products will be subject to the same health requirements as community products.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to regulate the disposal of biocidal products, that is to say all products which are used in one way or another to eliminate organisms harmful to humans. the report seeks to strike a balance between the use of such products where they can improve human health and the fight against their negative effects on the environment or health. in the medium term, all these products will have to go through three stages of evaluation to determine whether or not they are dangerous (in particular, carcinogenic or harmful to the endocrine system) before being validated by the european chemicals agency and placed on the market. the protection of the environment and the improvement of our health are two of the main themes of this text. let us hope once again that it will be more than just nice words.
in writing. my epp colleagues and i voted in favour of the resolution on imbalances in the food supply chain , which was adopted by a general consensus. the european parliament, through this ambitious text, calls on the european and national authorities involved in production and trade to take action against abusive purchasing practices by dominant wholesalers and retail distributors. specifically, for the competitiveness of european agriculture, it was essential to talk about the increase in the prices of agricultural inputs purchased over the last ten years in areas such as energy, equipment, compound feed, fertilisers, pesticides, seeds and water. the aim is therefore to avoid distortions of competition and, by solving the problems upstream of agricultural production, to improve farmers' incomes. the overall aim is to have a better distribution policy, to ensure that all products have the same quality standards within the eu and to allow producers to weigh in on the food chain. finally, through this text, i support the european union's substantial investment in projects that promote sustainable agriculture.

in writing. this report is a good start. he half-heartedly denounces the rules that prevail in the food industry (calibration of food, discarding unsold food while it is still edible). it advocates the application of the polluter pays principle in this sector. it stresses the importance of short circuits and urges the states to support local production on a small and medium scale. it even calls for quantified targets for preventing food waste by 2014. these are all good ideas and it is regrettable that this text is purely declarative and does not propose anything binding. i vote for it.
in writing. in these times of global economic crisis and famine in the horn of africa, it is deeply disturbing to imagine that 1.3 billion tonnes of food can be lost or destroyed every year worldwide. the first and by far the most worrying impact of waste is humanitarian: despite producing enough food to feed the world's population, 25,000 people die every day from chronic malnutrition. food waste occurs at all stages of the food chain, from harvest to consumption. the environmental impact of these malfunctions is increased and affects both fisheries and energy resources and waste management. we have the instruments to develop and implement an effective policy to reduce food waste. i remain convinced that a european information and awareness campaign on this subject should be carried out so that everyone can act on his own.

tackle the fiscal laxity which is depriving us of the room for manoeuvre needed to get back to growth and employment. they have shown their ability to find european solutions to european problems, even if two member states have chosen to play it alone, which they will themselves regret. i have, at this point, three wishes. the first is that the treaty should be ratified as soon as possible, the second is that it should be applied as soon as possible and the third is that this agreement should be fully incorporated into union law, as this parliament has asked for. ladies and gentlemen, the economic crisis is forcing us to rethink our bad habits. it requires us to respect the obvious but so difficult to apply rules of budgetary balance. we have an obligation to reduce national deficits, which often also hide regional and local deficits. but the decision on the treaty is as precise and positive as the one on growth leaves me hungry. because fighting deficits and restoring growth are two sides of the same coin. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the problem of unemployment. there are two ways of restoring growth, one artificial and one-off, the other structural and therefore sustainable. the first is to stimulate the economy through expenditure. we've been doing that for years, and we've seen where it's gotten us. in addition, today spending is effectively limited, because it is time to pay off debts, not to borrow. the second method, which is advocated by the epp, is to make our economy more competitive. this can already be done, mr barroso, by completing the internal market. all the laws, all the bills were passed a long time ago. the problem, again, is that they are not enforced. i therefore ask the commission to make it known as soon as possible who is not applying these rules and to fulfil its role as guardian of the treaties by forcing those who do not to apply them - perhaps france too, my dear friend, i am no exception. every european must know which state is playing the game of the internal market, and which is holding it back or blocking it. increasing our competitiveness can also be done by reducing the burden on entrepreneurs and by reducing the considerable differences in burdens between our countries, which are detrimental to competitiveness. this can also be done by optimising the return of hitherto unused european funds returned to states. the time has come to make better use of this 'important' surplus by investing it in common projects that generate growth and jobs. finally, growth and job creation can be encouraged by redirecting non-investment-generating public funds towards research and innovation or towards training. with a quarter of young people looking for work, we have an obligation to provide them with the opportunity to acquire sound skills and to reorient them throughout the community.

in writing. the treaty on stability, coordination and governance in the economic and monetary union is a necessary step forward. in the present crisis, fiscal stability is an imperative which we cannot afford to ignore. clear and precise rules were needed to ensure compliance with the treaty. it is certainly regrettable that the treaty has not been supported by all the member states. however, the final version adopted is to be welcomed. significant progress is expected, such as formal recognition of the golden rule, reversed qualified majority voting or the intervention of the court of justice of the european union. the final text has also been made more consistent with european law, in particular the six-pack which came into force last december. finally, we must not forget the difficulty of the european negotiations: to be able to agree on such a text in such a short time is a real success. above all, this new treaty shows a clear political will: it promotes responsible economic governance.

in writing. the parliament made specific recommendations to the commission for the 14th company law directive on the crossborder transfer of registered offices. we want to avoid, on the one hand, that the transfer of the registered office of a company implies the liquidation of the company in its country of origin and, on the other hand, that workers are victims of this transfer and lose part of their social rights. as rapporteur for the employment committee, i have been keen to ensure that the transfer does not affect the rights of the partners, employees and shareholders. the social issues connected with the transfer are essential to me. we must ensure that workers are involved in the process of transferring the head office: they must be consulted, informed and have the possibility of appealing against any suspension. the worker must no longer be a victim of company transfers, but must be able to benefit from them, whether in the context of the transfer of a large or a small company. only then can we encourage the mobility of our enterprises to meet the needs of competition, while at the same time combating social dumping.
