in writing. i voted in favour of the report on budgetary control of eu humanitarian aid managed by echo. the european union is the world's largest provider of humanitarian aid. in 2010, the total union contribution was €2 957 million, with 36% being provided by the european commission and the member states. the commission thus provides funding to nearly 200 partners such as ngos and un agencies. however, the control over the use of these funds is relatively limited. the reports provided by the united nations are of a very general nature and do not contain specific information on the results. the commission should therefore address any deficiencies in transparency in order to avoid the risk of misappropriation of un funds for humanitarian aid and development activities.
in writing. this report highlights real problems, particularly with regard to the transparency of the organisation of humanitarian aid. it also calls for an increase in the eu's humanitarian budget. in that sense, i support it. i regret, however, that in terms of transparency he almost exclusively denounces the un agencies. i also regret that he is asking for the control of the use of funds to be carried out by private firms, as if this were a guarantee of independence.
in writing. the european union is the world's largest provider of humanitarian aid. in 2010, the total contribution from the european union was eur 2 957 million, 36% of which was provided through the commission. the commission manages its humanitarian activities from its headquarters in brussels and through a network of field offices around the world. the average annual budget managed by dg echo for its humanitarian aid activities between 2006 and 2010 was €889 million. the report addresses the following main issues: efficiency and effectiveness of echo's control, monitoring and supervision system, particularly when it comes to partners in the framework partnership agreement (fp) or international organisations (such as the united nations). the report also stresses the need to ensure the sustainability, coherence and complementarity of humanitarian action, which are key objectives of eu development policy. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. in the face of the increase in natural disasters, it is imperative for the european union to strengthen its capacity to react and respond to crises. in this context, i believe it is essential to maintain a consistent balance between the financing of actions aimed at preventing humanitarian disasters and those aimed at responding rapidly to emergency situations. as rapporteur for the opinion on this report, adopted unanimously by the committee on development, i welcome the quality work done by the partners of dg echo through an effective selection method - such as the framework partnership contract - and the development of standards and practices for the humanitarian field. these are the reasons why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. breast implants scandals, costa concordia sinking... there are many news stories that illustrate the willingness of citizens to file a collective complaint when abuse or harm is commonly reported. by adopting the lehne report on thursday, 2 february, the european parliament's idea, which i fully support, is to take the debate on this issue further and move towards the opening up of collective redress within the eu. this new possibility of collective action should enable complainants from the member states to come together to denounce the same damage. however, this new system will also have to take account of the lessons learned from the deviations of the american system, which is itself plagued by collective seizures which are sometimes abusive or even unfounded. to do this, the report asks the commission to take into account key elements in developing its legislative proposal: limiting the eligibility of claims to clearly defined groups by allowing a magistrate to have the discretion to check in advance the admissibility of any possible class action, and prohibiting punitive damages. the impetus came from the european parliament, and it is now imperative for the commission to fill this legal gap by responding to the fundamental right of victims to compensation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report proposing a european-wide class action option, which calls on the commission to consider what the appropriate legal basis is for any action in the field of class action. in my view, this form of redress would allow victims of illegal actions, particularly victims of minor injuries, to come together to seek redress, thereby reducing the excessive costs of justice and increasing legal certainty and respect for the rule of law in europe. i also welcomed the inclusion in this report of a clarification that europe does not, however, want to have a system identical to that of the united states, that the european collective redress system should be set up in such a way as to protect the european citizen without undermining in any way the integrity of the single market and the rule of law.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report on the establishment of a coherent european approach to collective redress, as i believe that action at european union level in this area would bring a certain added value. it is a question of taking a realistic and pragmatic approach and going beyond the ideological debate which is reduced to the rejection of the "american scarecrow". european citizens must be able to exercise their rights effectively. however, strict control of procedures must be ensured to avoid abusive complaints.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by our colleague klaus lehne on a coherent european approach to collective redress. i felt it was necessary to reflect in depth on the added value that could be created by the establishment of a system of collective redress at european level. without falling into the excesses of the us model, it is important to end the legal patchwork within the eu and to enable european citizens to enforce their rights in a safe and effective way, as access to individual remedies is often difficult and expensive. of course, this system must be strictly controlled and must strike the right balance to avoid abuse and judicialisation of our society, while respecting the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report: i have been in favour of collective action for years. the commission is frankly struggling to offer us anything serious: we have had 'green papers', 'working documents', 'draft guidelines', 'consultation documents', and in the end, nothing tangible has yet been done at european level. however, collective redress must be introduced in europe: it is clear that when a group of citizens is the victim of the same offence, individual redress cannot always be the solution, either to stop the illegal practice or to obtain redress, especially when the individual damage is minor compared to the cost of legal action. of course, as i have already said, these resources must be marked (quality for action, opt-in, no pre-financing by third parties, etc.) in order to avoid deviations from the american system. but the debate must not paralyse the legislative action! that is why i supported this report, which sets out a framework within which these remedies could be considered, even if i do not agree with all the guidelines.
in writing. european citizens must be able to enforce eu law in their national courts without difficulty. the shortcomings in collective redress weaken this right, particularly in the case of actions for compensation. while respect for the legal traditions of the different member states is a fundamental principle, we need to go beyond the european compensation system and adopt a binding legal framework which regulates collective redress throughout the union. i voted in favour of streamlining and simplifying the legal procedures for european citizens. a class action is a means of dealing with the complaints of several complainants who consider themselves to be victims of the same damage. as a member of parliament, i felt it was important to advocate a procedure which makes legal proceedings in the eu less costly and less random.
in writing. i regret the passage of the resolution opposing the adoption of the draft commission regulation on nutrition claims. i regret the result of a vote which was a little haphazard, with a very small majority of only 15 votes, and after a speech which distorted reality. far from protecting the consumer, some colleagues unfortunately tend to infantilize him. three points, however, were necessary to protect the consumer. first, the claim was quite clear: "now contains x % less than [name of nutrient]". then it was usable only from 15% reduction in nutrient content. finally, a maximum period of use of one year had been set. while the european parliament keeps on stressing the urgent need to combat obesity and to reduce the sugar, salt, fat, etc. content of food products, it is now taking the incomprehensible position of rejecting a claim which would have encouraged the food industry to go in this direction, in the interests of consumer health. thus, in the pursuit of "the best", "the good" is no longer found and the incentive of manufacturers to reformulate their products is broken.
in writing. at the plenary vote on 1 february, the european parliament, by a slim majority, chose to reject a draft regulation whose aim was to provide additional nutritional information to consumers. his concern for ever more, or even for too much, led him to take a stand that was contrary to the principles he intended to uphold. obesity has become a major health problem, a phenomenon that we must combat with strength and pragmatism. this requires progressive and non-dogmatic measures so that private actors are also involved in meeting public health objectives and contribute to improving the nutritional quality of food. the original proposal, which parliament chose to reject, provided for the compulsory nutrition labelling to be supplemented by the formula 'now contains x % less than'. this claim was usable from 15% reduction in nutrient content and only for one year, which encouraged the food industry to make ever greater efforts to be transparent to the consumer.
in writing. this is a resolution tabled in the context of the objection procedure against delegated acts of the european commission. i have decided to abstain on this particularly sensitive matter. it is true that nutrition claims on food products have a real role to play in public health. however, some of the allegations made by the commission appeared to call consumer protection into question.
in writing. all recent studies agree that excessive sugar consumption is a serious health hazard. sugar consumption has even been linked to an increase in diseases such as cancer and cardiovascular disease. diabetes and obesity also remain major health challenges. in this sense, it is essential to inform the consumer about the composition of the food he is likely to consume and to encourage the production of food products containing less fat and sugars. the commission's proposal to allow the reduction in the amount of fat or sugars in a product to be indicated on its labelling compared with the previous recipe was therefore a good one. it provides better information to consumers and encourages the reduction of sugars and fats in food products.
in writing. nutrition and health claims should only be allowed if they are accurate, unambiguous and not misleading. however, the new nutrition claim submitted to us ('now contains x % less than (name of nutrient) ') could have misled the consumer. this involved a comparison between a new formula and the old product, without the consumer necessarily knowing the initial content of this product in a given nutrient - this content may well be excessively high compared to other products available on the market (not re-formulated, therefore not able to carry the claim). another problem is that it is known that the consumer generally expects that a reduction in the sugar content will lead to a reduction in the energy value. the text would have allowed the claim 'reduced fat/sugar' even if the energy value of the product remained the same as that of a similar product. finally, there would have been a possible confusion with existing claims, such as for example 'lightweight/light', for which the requirements are in fact more stringent. for these reasons, i have rejected, by means of this vote, the proposal to amend the regulation on nutrition claims.
in writing. i have approved the motion for a resolution on the conclusions of the european council of 30 january. as the rapporteur points out, 'all the elements of the new treaty can be achieved, and to a large extent have already been achieved' thanks to the european parliament. it should be noted that many of the measures contained in the treaty were the result of debates in the european parliament. we are therefore convinced that the european parliament must play a decisive role in the economic governance under construction. we therefore need to be consulted on measures relating to stability, policy coordination and economic governance. beyond that, i have two regrets. on the one hand, the final text ignores parliament's request that its president should take part in the euro-zone summits, and on the other hand, the united kingdom and the czech republic did not want to join us. as joseph daul, the president of my political group (epp), has said, the treaty must now be signed, ratified and incorporated into the european treaties as soon as possible.
in writing. who can ignore today that the eu is going through a deep crisis, not only economic and social, but global and even a crisis of meaning? and yet our heads of state and government persist in the course which has widened the gap between the peoples and the eu. after ignoring the votes of the europeans in the referendum on the constitutional treaty, they signed a new treaty between themselves, negotiated almost behind closed doors, focused on austerity and budgetary discipline. no real involvement of the european parliament, no public debate, no cooperation with the national parliaments and, in fact, nothing about growth and future investment. as i said when we voted on our previous resolution, i have more than doubts about this new treaty! i therefore voted against today's resolution because i believe that it is no longer sufficiently critical of this treaty, which is presented to us as the only possible way forward. it is both useless in substance (since many measures can be implemented in eu law) and incomplete (since there is no balance between austerity and growth measures), but it is also frankly questionable in form: if we want to regain the credit of the european people, this is certainly not the way to do it!
in writing. i was pleased to have the opportunity to involve the european parliament in the debate on the treaty on stability, coordination and governance in economic and monetary union. i did not, however, wish to vote in favour of a resolution which is reserved about a process whose importance and urgency seem to me to be obvious. that is why i abstained in this vote, just as i abstained in the vote on the resolution of 18 january.
in writing. this resolution wrongly maintains a number of criticisms of the european parliament towards the council, whose efforts to improve budgetary discipline in a timely manner must be supported. i cannot therefore agree with this text. however, i cannot join those who refuse and reject all budgetary discipline: the present crisis is a crisis of public spending, and it will be overcome by greater collective discipline. i therefore decided to abstain on that resolution.
in writing. as i expressed my reservations on the joint resolution of the european parliament on the conclusions of the european council of 8 and 9 december 2011, i am voting against the joint resolution put to the vote on the conclusions of the european council of 30 january 2012. the resolution stresses that only the community method can bring about a genuine economic and budgetary union and that budgetary discipline alone cannot solve the european economic and financial crisis. however, the text does not call into question the international agreement on a budgetary stability union, which was approved by the heads of state and government on monday. the root causes of the crisis must be tackled by calling neoliberal policies into question, denouncing the binding austerity mechanism that will apply to the current and future governments of the member states, highlighting the ultra-technocracy involved in the agreement, which in fact widened the gap between the european institutions and the european citizens, and finally recalling that the draft agreement will institutionalize a two-speed europe, the member states party to the agreement and the others.
in writing. the treaty on stability, coordination and governance in the economic and monetary union strengthens budgetary discipline and i welcome this. it thus gives greater legal force to the golden rule of returning to a balanced public accounts. the french socialists and mr hollande are warned that none of the 25 member states which signed the treaty will be able to escape the objective of budgetary balance under penalty of sanctions imposed by the court of justice. i regret, however, that this resolution voted by parliament does not recognise the significant progress that will be made in implementing this new treaty, and fails to welcome the political will shown by nicolas sarkozy and angela merkel.
in writing. the treaty on stability, coordination and governance endorsed by 25 heads of state and government marks a major step towards stabilising our economies and is an effective tool in combating the financial crisis and restoring confidence. with its partners, france is committed to balanced budgets, convergence and coordination of our economic policies, because the vitality of the french economy also depends on that of the euro area as a whole. of course, there is still work to be done. the european parliament and the national parliaments must be able to be involved and to participate in the budgetary debates we are engaged in. certain provisions of the treaty provide for this, and it is in this spirit that a delegation from the european parliament was invited to take part in the negotiations on 30 january. however, this resolution does not sufficiently acknowledge the progress made by the new text. in repeating its support for the resolution of 18 january, which i had opposed, it is making criticisms which i think are excessive. that's why i chose to abstain.
in writing. the joint resolution on the european council of 30 january 2012 was adopted by 443 votes in favour, 124 against and 75 abstentions. i voted against this resolution with four other colleagues from the epp. if this text proposes interesting ideas, such as the creation of a depreciation fund and the introduction of a tax on financial transactions, it is clear that it once again calls into question the usefulness of the new treaty, which, let us not forget, was created thanks to the involvement and determination of our president of the republic and the german chancellor.
in writing. i wished to abstain from voting on the resolution on the conclusions of the european council of 30 january 2012 and the draft treaty on stability, coordination and governance of the economic and monetary union. i fully support the european council's statements and would like to express my satisfaction at the conclusion of the treaty. the strengthening of european economic governance and budgetary stability, which are a prerequisite for the exercise of financial solidarity, which this treaty establishes, are in my view strong political acts. i therefore regret that parliament, in its resolution adopted on 2 february 2012, refers to its previous resolution, voted on 18 january, in which it expressed its doubts as to the relevance of this draft treaty and criticised the institutional architecture envisaged. i also regret that the resolution adopted by parliament on 2 february expresses reservations about the format of the euro-area summits laid down in the treaty, which seems to me to be appropriate in this respect too.
in writing. the joint resolution of the right-wing conservatives, liberals, socialists and greens contains a multitude of contradictions. these are in fact a cover-up of the existence of the new treaty or the implementation of its extremely dangerous content. the joint resolution also calls for the adoption of a new european treaty, which would be a step towards the creation of a european union. this means that the new european treaty must be approved as a last resort. i therefore voted against this text, which is being drawn up without the opinion of the national parliaments, without consulting the european peoples, and after a negative opinion a few weeks ago from parliament itself. i call for consultation of the people, particularly by referendum where the constitutions allow it.
in writing. the merkozy duo has succeeded in imposing its "golden rule" on almost all of europe, a genuine austerity plan designed to punish member states that do not comply with the budgetary austerity demands of brussels. from spring of each year, europe will thus be introducing a real cycle of public financial surveillance. mr van rompuy talks about growth and investment for jobs, but what is apparent from this treaty is a policy designed to kill growth and to put national budgets under control. yesterday maastricht deprived us of our monetary sovereignty; today it is the european parliament which is the real problem. today we are being deprived of our budgetary sovereignty. this treaty sacrifices the will of the peoples to dispose of themselves on the altar of european economic federalism. it is a victory for the financial markets and the rating agencies over the states. your answers will only bring more suffering to the peoples of europe already hard hit by your policies. that is why we are voting against this resolution.
in writing. the joint resolution proposed by the epp, sd, alde and greens/efa groups confirms their agreement with the substance of the treaty on budgetary discipline. it announced that their representatives would validate and apply the strengthened golden rule and its constitutionalisation in the member states. as for the ratification of the treaty, the idea that it should be submitted to a vote of the peoples by means of referendums is again completely absent. i denounce the doctrinal blindness of all the supporters of liberal economics and austerity who will vote for this text or who will abstain. for me and my group the choice is clear: no!
in writing. far from providing a way out of the crisis, this agreement is an aggravated and forced submission of european states to financial and speculative logic which is harmful to the good conduct and well-being of our societies. sarkozy and merkel have imposed an ideological dictate on other governments, on all the peoples of europe, without consulting the citizens, or even going through the normal rules of constitutional amendment specific to each state. with my colleagues from the gue/ngl i have signed and tabled an alternative motion for a resolution. our resolution is the only one which clearly rejects this democratic attempt to undermine the sovereignty of the peoples; it is the only one which clearly opposes the introduction of a new rule fixing the structural deficit of the member states at 0.5% of nominal gdp, which will in fact result in permanent austerity throughout europe. it is still the only one to oppose sanctions and to call for a public consultation on the issue. i therefore voted for the resolution which i tabled with my group and against the consensus between the liberals, the conservatives, the socialists and the greens on this agreement.
in writing. mr president, i am pleased that the european parliament has strongly supported the new european treaty. it is a historic turning point: it will set the rule of balanced budgets in stone and thus strengthen mutual trust between the states. economic governance, which we meps have long called for, is now becoming a reality. from the outset, nicolas sarkozy and angela merkel were in the game. the franco-german couple started from the same observations and proposed the same solution: to get out of the crisis, we must clean up our finances. the recovery will only take place on a sound basis. that is the whole point of my unwavering support for this strategy. while the vast majority of european governments have shown pragmatism in supporting this text, i note that the french socialists have once again isolated themselves in their own european political family. they failed to impose their will to renegotiate the treaty. this leaves one wondering about the credibility of their revolutionary ideas for a strong france, in a strong europe...
in writing. in the face of an unprecedented attack on popular sovereignty, the european parliament today voted a resolution that says very little. the heads of state meeting in brussels this week agreed on a draft treaty containing: the incorporation of the golden rule into the constitutions of the member states; the reverse qualified majority rule (a state which does not comply with the maastricht criteria can be sanctioned by a minority of states); the commission has not yet decided on the criteria to be used for the correction of the budgets of the member states. the gue/ngl once again opposed this denial of democracy. in the face of such a transfer of sovereignty without any involvement of the peoples, the european parliament simply requests the presence of the president of the european parliament at the meetings of the euro-zone summits. only popular mobilization and the demand for referendums can make it possible to fight against this anti-democratic, austerity dogma.
in writing. in this joint resolution, which i have approved, we support sanctions against the iranian regime. we also want to point out that we do not approve of the fact that china and russia are still refusing to take sanctions. we have supported both the new european restrictive measures and the council's determination to work towards a diplomatic settlement of the iranian nuclear issue in accordance with the dual approach. we urge the iranian authorities to respond favourably to the offer of negotiation and to cooperate with the international atomic energy agency (iaea). iran must return to the negotiating table as soon as possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution in support of the european union's decision to impose an oil embargo on iran. this is a measure to increase pressure on a regime which is not respecting un resolutions and is pursuing a nuclear weapons programme. the oil embargo, which france has been leading, is the solution to prevent military intervention by countries that feel threatened, and a conflagration in the region.
in writing. the european union, notably through the voice of the european parliament, is firmly and daily committed to peace and security throughout the world. iran, despite repeated calls from the international community, continues to develop its nuclear programme. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution calling for new sanctions against iran, including a gradual embargo on imports of crude oil. however, these sanctions must be targeted, to spare the population as much as possible and to force the iranian leadership to return to the negotiating table. in the iranian crisis, the solution must be diplomatic, not military. i wanted to reaffirm this with my colleagues in the european parliament by supporting the vote on this resolution.
in writing. this resolution expresses the deep concern of the members of the european parliament about the possible military dimension of the iranian programme. this resolution is all the more important as it was adopted at the same time as the european union decided to adopt sanctions of unprecedented scale against iran, namely an embargo on oil from iran and a freeze on the assets of the central bank of iran. as a member of the eu-iran delegation and the subcommittee on security and defence and particularly committed to these issues, i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. i abstained on this report. as much as i am in favour of diplomatic and trade sanctions against the iranian regime as a deterrent to halting its military nuclear programme, i am concerned that this resolution will open the way to dangerous military intervention. targeted sanctions against certain iranian leaders or certain economic sectors must be envisaged, without prejudice to the iranian people. these must in no way be a prerequisite for military action. unfortunately, that is what this report is about.
in writing. while the oil embargo is a means of pressure, its inevitable consequences on the iranian population should not be overlooked; the resolution also implies a threat of military intervention in iran. nothing like this to rally the iranian people to the idea that nuclear weapons are necessary for their defense and to radicalize the iranian regime a few weeks before the parliamentary elections. this text has no spine. sanctions must be directed exclusively at political and economic leaders. the escalation of military tensions must stop. they must give way to a regional conference on peace and the denuclearisation of the middle east under the auspices of the un and to the effective, progressive and reciprocal nuclear disarmament of all the nuclear powers.
in writing. by voting, i wanted to support the eu's decision to increase pressure on iran. the iranian attitude is an affront and a challenge to our model of society, our values and our security. there is no denying that iran's belligerent rhetoric and its pursuit of nuclear energy is a threat to world peace, especially in a highly unstable region. nevertheless, if we are to maintain pressure on this despotic regime, we must continue the political dialogue, otherwise we will be witnessing an escalation with an uncertain outcome. i share the concerns of western leaders, who are concerned about iran's influence in the region and its support for authoritarian and despotic regimes. i welcome the sanctions decided by the union and i strongly hope that, after honest negotiations, we will reach a rapid resolution of this latent crisis. war is never the answer, and the consequences of military intervention would be disastrous. finally, i have a thought for the iranian people, held hostage by dogmatic and bloodthirsty leaders, who rule by repression, intimidation and deprivation. the eu must do everything possible to bring this regime to its knees, which is clearly going crazy.
in writing. i have chosen to support this report because it aims to 'cleanse' european sport by creating a european hooligan file, equating doping with drug trafficking and regulating the profession of player agents. the resolution calls for the abolition of the death penalty for all crimes against humanity and for the establishment of a european criminal record. all fraudulent activities (game-fixing, money laundering and illegal betting) are criminalised; that trafficking in doping substances be treated by the courts as narcotics trafficking; a licensing system for betting operators is put in place; the commission has also proposed that the profession of player agent be regulated, by creating a european register of agents which would list the players they represent, and by requiring agents to have a minimum level of qualifications.

in writing. a few weeks after the european commission announced the creation of a specific budget for sport, the fisas report confirms that this is indeed a european issue. a dedicated budget for sport, it was time! if the sums remain small in comparison to the money made by the sports world (30 million per year between 2014 and 2020), i welcome this step forward. the european commission has taken note of the new provisions of the lisbon treaty. the fisas report recalls that sport is a multifaceted field, which has a strong economic dimension and plays a fundamental social role. the need to promote volunteering, to prepare athletes for life after a professional sporting career through training, to combat illegal sports betting, to coordinate the fight against doping and to regulate the profession of agent... the subjects for action, and in particular those for which i had tabled amendments in the final text, such as the protection of minors in international transfers and the necessary collaboration between the eu and the council of europe (a very active body on sports matters), are not lacking ! so let's move forward on these new foundations!
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which sets out the broad lines of a future european sport policy. sport is now an integral part of human and social development, contributes to a healthy lifestyle, promotes intercultural encounters and has a real educational value, especially for the young. the development of sporting activities in the eu will therefore benefit all our citizens.
in writing. the european parliament paternally encourages us to do sport because it is good for health, because sport 'brings joy' and strengthens social cohesion. we should thank him! however, it does highlight some contradictions. after encouraging the widespread use of online sports betting, he is concerned about the system's abuses, match-fixing and corruption. at the same time, the eu wants to protect the property rights of competition organisers and promote access to free broadcasting and information for all. today, the european commission is proposing to be a platform for the exchange of good practice and, at the very least, to organise sporting events itself. it is fortunate that baron de coubertin or jules rimet did not wait for the european commission to create the modern olympic games or the world cup. the european parliament also recommends that the european flag be displayed on the home team's jerseys and in the stadium, no doubt to combat so-called nationalism. this is to omit that, for example, the 2006 world cup final attracted 80% of the evening audience, the 2009 european elections 40% of the voters.

in writing. the report by s. fisas ayxela provided an opportunity for parliament to support the european commission's communication of 18 january 2011 on the development of the european dimension in sport as the first commission policy document on this subject since it became a community competence. while i welcome the report's desire to recall the values that sport must convey and to suggest the type of actions that should reflect the community's added value in this field, i question the union's current capacity to assume this responsibility in a meaningful way. with only 4 million euros dedicated specifically to sport per year (in the form of a 'preparatory action', i.e. a temporary action), the union does not have the means to intervene effectively to combat doping, support the practice of sport by people with disabilities, promote the development of a 'european identity' through sport, etc. this is an issue that will therefore have to be addressed in the coming months, as member states are called upon to establish the union's budgetary framework for the period 2014-2020.
in writing. sport is certainly one of the most powerful vehicles for the integration of the most disadvantaged and the rapprochement of cultures, it is one of the main components of social action in promoting the integration and development of everyone, everywhere in the world. i therefore voted in favour of this report which supports the economic dimension and the social role of sport, urging and encouraging the states and the commission to do more to promote, support and encourage its development among all sections of the european population, in particular by proposing the possibility for mass sports to benefit from the erdf and the esf. i also welcomed the inclusion in this resolution of concrete proposals such as the organisation of an annual 'european day of sport', the designation of an annual 'european capital of sport', the facilitation and promotion of mobility programmes for young athletes and sports coaches, and the suggestion to fly the european flag at major international sporting events. sport is a means of promoting our values, and it is particularly important to support sport in all its dimensions, especially at a time when european values and solidarity are being weakened.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by a large majority of the report on the european dimension of sport. sports is more than just an activity. it plays a driving social role. it is a factor of integration, sociability, education and social cohesion. sport is also a generator of growth and employment. it now accounts for 15 million jobs in europe and 3.6% of european gdp. so let us not neglect this important dimension which contributes to the consolidation of our social fabric and the achievement of our public health objectives.
in writing. sport is an integral part of human and social development. i am convinced, as are my colleagues in the epp, that the european union must create a future specific programme on sport. i voted in favour of this report, which was drawn up following the european commission's communication entitled 'developing the european dimension of sport'. in order to create a genuine european dimension in sport, the report recommends taking account of certain elements, such as the social role of sport, the promotion of a healthy lifestyle, the fight against doping, violence and intolerance and, finally, better governance in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the european dimension of sport, which is the first adopted by parliament in this field since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. i welcome the fact that it emphasises the major role of sport in promoting intercultural dialogue, public health, the integration of socially vulnerable people, the fight against discrimination and the emancipation of women. another positive point is that the text affirms the importance of sports volunteers - there are 35 million of them in europe - and stresses the need for appropriate training. of course, the fight against doping is a key point in the text: we call for prevention and information campaigns to be set up and urge the states to treat the trafficking of doping substances in the same way as the trafficking of illegal drugs. the paragraph suggesting that the european flag should be flown at major international sporting events held in the union was controversial. i believe that this would help to strengthen the sense of belonging to a common whole among european citizens, even as the european project is experiencing dark days, and i supported its retention in the text.
in writing. judging from the petitions we have received, citizens of the european union are concerned about the inability of member states to have effective and sustainable waste management policies. the european parliament has heard you. like many of my colleagues, i voted in favour of the resolution which aims to improve these policies. although these are often backed by private interests, they are in some ways a public service mission. we have therefore called for clearer and more specific criteria for the location of landfills in relation to homes, schools and hospitals. it is also about communicating more about the merits of selective sorting, and making it clear that proper waste management is expensive but can attract investment and create jobs. everyone remembers the rupture of pools of toxic red mud in hungary that devastated a village, or the landfill near marseille, which in 2008 was close to saturation, despite its good management. so this is a problem for all of europe!
in writing. following the adoption of the waste framework directive in 2008, citizens are increasingly denouncing the poor management of waste in europe. and that's totally normal. they have a right to expect public authorities to provide public services which respect their health and the environment. the manifest failure of some member states to manage their waste, and in particular their toxic waste, has led to a considerable increase in the number of petitions on this subject. waste management is a major political and social problem; in the case of landfilling, the monitoring and control system is insufficient to prevent the contamination of household waste by toxic waste. let us develop these policies as far in advance as possible by improving sorting, collection and recycling to promote the recovery of waste and ensure an effective traceability system for toxic waste. landfill should be the last resort. the iturgaiz report shows that considerable efforts remain to be made and reminds us of the crucial importance of encouraging early dialogue between the competent authorities and citizens. the awareness of citizens is real, and the public authorities must respond by significantly improving waste management.
in writing. waste is a major concern for our citizens. this report is a wake-up call to the states. but the european commission must also play its part and ensure that the waste directive is properly applied. we need to make this case visible but also credible. it is worrying to see that the states do not seem to be in control of the waste management situation, only 6 member states have transposed the framework directive on waste in time, and a large number of complaints received by the committee on petitions on the subject sometimes show the lack of transparency in the choice of landfill sites. the house also called for exemplary sanctions to be introduced to prevent companies linked to organised crime from winning public contracts for the sole purpose of enrichment in this €75 billion market.
in writing. the main concern of the european citizens who petitioned the european parliament is the environment, and in particular the implementation by the member states of the waste management directive. following several fact-finding visits to ireland, italy, france and spain, the epp group supported the idea of an own-initiative report on the incorrect implementation of eu legislation by member states and inappropriate waste management facilities. the text also calls on the member states to speed up the transposition of the framework directive on waste management into national law. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. this report reminds member states of their obligation to respect the waste hierarchy in their waste management. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services. so many points i share. i regret, however, that this text is too lenient with waste incineration, a highly polluting technique which benefits large industrial groups at the expense of reuse, recycling and renewable energy. it also supports the privatisation of waste management in europe, which explains the prevalence of this harmful technique. it is high time that ecological planning was introduced, which would put aside the law of the market and organise compliance with the priorities imposed by the general interest.
in writing. between 2004 and 2010, 114 petitions were filed for infringements of the waste management directive - more than ten of them from france - representing the majority of petitions on environmental issues, which are themselves the main source of petitions. waste management is a matter of direct concern to us; the shortcomings of the system - lack of awareness, administrative capacity and financial resources in particular - must therefore be addressed as quickly and as effectively as possible. i welcome the proposals made by mr carlos josé irturgaiz angulo in this respect. the use of cohesion funds and direct financing by the european investment bank is indeed necessary, as is the strengthening of the role of the european environment agency. finally, i fully support the idea of introducing a european standard for colour coding on packaging to facilitate sorting. i also fully support recycling, which was recently the subject of one of my questions to the commission.
in writing. the vote on this report, which i supported, sends a strong signal for a strong eu initiative on waste management. the large number of petitions on this subject highlights the concerns of the citizens on this matter, which i have shared for many years. the european legislative framework is relevant, but leaves out a number of important issues, such as innovative methods of recovery, reuse, recycling and disposal of waste. i believe that this is a priority issue, both for its consequences for human health and the well-being of europeans, but also for the environment and sustainable development. i asked the commission about the efforts to be made to reduce and recover waste from consumer packaging and about the need to eliminate food waste, which is a major source of waste and an imperative of solidarity with the poorest citizens. i therefore call again on the commission to make strong proposals for sustainable waste management throughout the supply chain. that is a european expectation, and i think it is quite legitimate.
in writing. the daphne programme, which was set up in 1997, has been a real success. it is the only european programme which, for almost 15 years, has aimed to combat violence against women, children and adolescents. the programme includes more than 500 projects and increased cooperation by ngos in a range of areas such as sexual, psychological and physical violence in institutional settings, at school and in the family. these include projects to prevent child pornography and the risks of surfing the internet for children, and projects to address the health needs of women who are victims of trafficking and female genital mutilation. i therefore naturally approved the european parliament's motion for a resolution, which calls on the commission to continue to finance such projects. i am particularly in favour of this report because the programme for 2014-2020 aims, among other things, to reaffirm the need for legislative action at european level to eradicate gender-based violence. my fight for women is therefore at national and european level.
in writing. the importance of the daphne programme is beyond dispute. this is the only programme that aims to combat violence against women, children and adolescents at eu level. we must therefore ensure adequate funding, not only to be able to meet the real needs of the fight against all forms of violence, but also to be able to set up awareness-raising actions for younger generations faced with the new forms of violence linked to the increasing use of online social networks (threats, psychological pressure, moral harassment, cyber-child pornography). it is also necessary to ensure that the objectives of the daphne programme are pursued in the rights and citizenship programme and that administrative formalities and grant application procedures are simplified in order to encourage small ngos to propose daphne projects.

in writing. in the eu, between 20-25% of women have experienced physical violence at least once in their adult lives, and more than 10% have experienced sexual violence involving the use of force. similarly, 26% of children and young people say they have been physically abused. in view of the scale of this violence, the daphne european programme was set up in 1997 to protect these women, young people and children, and it has been a real success ever since. the resolution we adopted, which i of course supported, welcomes the actions undertaken under this programme and calls for its renewal for the period 2014-2020. i would like to stress certain aspects in particular: firstly, our resolution calls for more funding for projects aimed at raising awareness among younger generations of the new forms of violence (social networks, cyber-child pornography, etc.). our resolution then encourages the participation and involvement of ngos, because of their essential role in supporting victims. finally, it is important that this instrument retains its name and independence in order to guarantee a certain visibility on this programme, as well as a budget at least equivalent to the previous programme.

in writing. the objective of universal access to energy by 2030 was launched under the mdgs. in developing countries, households tend to spend a higher percentage of their budget on the purchase of poor quality fuels for lighting and cooking than households with access to electricity and liquid and gaseous fuels. in developing countries, sustainable access to energy for the poor faces several obstacles, including the inability of the poorest to pay for services, investment costs, connection costs, and the lack of domestic capacity to manufacture the necessary energy generation equipment and spare parts. the report underlines that, although none of the mdgs is specifically energy-related, access to modern and sustainable energy services for all is a prerequisite for the achievement of the mdgs. energy should therefore be placed at the forefront of the debate on poverty eradication through the establishment of a specific programme focusing on energy and development within the framework of the european union's development cooperation policy. it is on these priorities that i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. this eu-morocco agreement provides a framework for our future relations, to enable morocco to participate in eu programmes. it is a key element in deepening our relations with morocco and will allow for important sectoral rapprochements. it shall ensure the equitable participation of morocco in the budget of the union, corresponding to the specific programmes in which it will choose to participate. this is a key step in the ever closer ties which bind us to our moroccan partner, which has advanced status.
in writing. morocco is a privileged partner of the european union in the southern mediterranean region. the eu has a genuinely rich and in-depth dialogue with the country in various fields. the principle of 'advanced status' for morocco was recognised in 2008 as part of the european neighbourhood policy. the parliamentary elections of 25 november 2011 and the formation of a coalition government appointed on 3 january 2012 by king mohammed vi were major steps in the process of constitutional and democratic reform in the country. this is a movement which the european union naturally had to accompany. it's a done deal now. the european parliament gave its unreserved approval on tuesday to the protocol which will allow our strategic partner to participate in community programmes open to third countries such as the competitiveness and innovation programme (cip) or the customs 2013 programme.
in writing. morocco was granted advanced status by the european union in 2008. the aim was to take account of the strategic priorities to be pursued following the association agreement with morocco signed in 1996 and to enable morocco to be gradually integrated into the internal market. i supported this report, which aims to approve the conclusion of the protocol between the union and morocco to the euro-mediterranean association agreement.
in writing. the eu is engaged in a very thorough dialogue with morocco, a country which is peacefully moving towards greater democracy. the protocol on the participation of morocco in certain community programmes represents an important step towards enhancing relations between the eu and morocco (advanced status). signed in brussels in december 2010 and entered into force on 1 march 2000, it sets out the objectives of this increase, which is based on better taking into account the respective strategic priorities of both parties and the progressive integration of morocco into the european internal market. it provides for morocco to be allowed to participate in all current and future community programmes open to it. this new perspective is in line with the objectives of the european neighbourhood policy, which is why i supported it by voting in plenary.
in writing. i naturally voted in favour of this recommendation in the council, as it seems to me normal that the partnership between the union and the kingdom of morocco should be given a new lease of life. it was essential that our assembly send a strong political message to our moroccan friends. morocco's participation in eu programmes was envisaged as early as the conclusion of the association agreement in 1996 and then in the 2008 advanced status. for several years now, morocco has shown remarkable courage and determination to undertake profound reforms in favour of democracy, the rule of law and a strengthened dialogue with europe. it was therefore fitting to reward its efforts and to affirm its role as the eu's main partner in the arab world. this participation is not unconditional: it will be gradual and will be matched by a financial contribution from morocco to the general budget of the eu. it is also conditional on the continuation of reforms and the successful implementation of the new constitution, adopted at the end of 2011. i therefore welcome the decision taken by our parliament and am convinced that it will consolidate and enrich the eu-morocco strategic partnership.
in writing. while the eu has taken measures to control bluetongue as early as 2000, new measures to take account of new vaccination technologies are needed. i therefore voted in favour of the wojciechowski report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the directive which will finally allow our farmers to vaccinate their cattle, sheep and goats who are threatened by bluetongue, commonly known as 'blue tongue' disease. this disease, transmitted mainly by the bite of certain species of mosquitoes, affects sheep acutely but other ruminants are susceptible. even if the disease does not affect human health, either directly or through products, the consequences for livestock can be severe. the aim of this text is to update and relax the current rules on vaccination. i wanted this text to be passed quickly so that these new rules could be implemented as soon as the next vaccination season. i now urge the french government to transpose the directive into french law as soon as possible.
in writing. the objective of this report is to strengthen and improve the control of bluetongue and to reduce the burden of bluetongue on the agricultural sector. the aim is to adapt the current vaccination provisions to the recent development of the technologies used for vaccine production, a technology which has led to the development of 'inactivated vaccines' against the disease. i voted in favour of this report in the votes in plenary.
in writing. in favour of an integration of european payment markets, i supported the creation of a single european payments area (sepa). bank transfers between member states will be similar to national transfers. from now on, a single bank account will be sufficient to receive your salary, even if it is paid by another member state. similarly, there will be no further charges for transferring money to a foreign account. these provisions will enter into force for the euro area as from 2014.
in writing. as a member of the parliament's committee on economic and monetary affairs, i welcome the new regulation on the single european payments area, which represents a major step forward for businesses and consumers. throughout its preparation, i have followed step by step the objectives of a text which requires banks to speed up and lower the cost of bank transfers and direct debits in 32 countries. as rapporteur sari essayah has said, 'if a person works in another member state, he will not need a new bank account. businesses will also benefit . you, as entrepreneurs and citizens, will be able to travel, pay your bills abroad or make transactions at cost price without having to set up a separate bank account. the european union is also about simplifying your everyday life!
in writing. the migration to the single euro payments area, or sepa, will have consequences for users, including individuals and small and medium-sized enterprises, while converting the current system to a common eu-wide bank account numbering based on iban and bic codes. however, in order for the transition to this harmonised payment system within the eu to be well accepted, the banking sector needs to carry out large and targeted information campaigns to raise public awareness, including by explaining the composition of iban and bic codes. in addition, banks should generally apply a more transparent information policy in their customer activities. these steps are considered very important for the smooth and appropriate implementation of efficient and secure payment systems across the union and for the european citizens' acceptance of such changes. this is another step which may seem technical but which brings many simplifications to european companies exporting to the intra-community market.
in writing. with the single european payment area in euro, crossborder bank transfers will become faster, safer and cheaper. in concrete terms, as of 1 february 2014, eu citizens travelling within the union will be able to use a single bank account in euro to pay their wages in another member state. they will also be able to pay bills in one country through an account in another without having to worry about the country in which their bank account is located. the european parliament estimates that individuals and businesses will be able to save €123 billion over 6 years.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which will put an end to the bank charges that affect crossborder payments within the european union. they represent an additional cost to our businesses and our citizens, particularly significant in these times of economic crisis.
in writing. finally, we will have a genuine single euro payments area (sepa) which will make cross-border payments as easy as national payments. the benefits of this unified european system are: shorter payment times, better cash management for our companies and individuals, lower costs for these payments and their processing, and the conquest of new markets. on the other hand, it will reduce the level of requests and the associated operating costs of administrative services. the impact assessment estimates that the positive impact on the european economy of this approach would be between eur 100 and eur 300 billion over a six-year period. national electronic payment systems in the form of credit transfers or direct debits should be abolished within 12 and 24 months respectively after the entry into force of the regulation.
in writing. i supported the report by sari essayah on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down technical requirements for transfers and withdrawals in euro and amending regulation (ec) no 924/2009. the regulation will establish strict and transparent rules to cover the execution of all euro transfers and withdrawals in the union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to bring crossborder euro transfers and withdrawals within the eu under a single system. the establishment of a european payments market has many advantages, including the development of competition and the significant reduction of the cost of cross-border banking for citizens and businesses in the european union. according to an impact study, this measure would be likely to generate savings of between 100 and 300 billion over six years.
in writing. i voted in favour of the regulation establishing technical and commercial requirements for transfers and withdrawals in euro. i believe that in the digital age we can demand that our european banks remove the obstacles to transfers and withdrawals denominated in euro for intra-european transactions. by 1 february 2014, banks should have switched to a new single european payment area in euro and thus offer the same rates for cross-border and domestic transfers. this is a very concrete step forward for citizens who see the idea of a europe where trade between member states is simplified come to life. as trade and the movement of europeans across europe intensify, money transfers increase and their costs to customers vary or are non-existent across member states. this regulation establishes common rules and standards.
in writing. in the sepa (single euro payments area), citizens, businesses and public authorities can make and receive payments in euro under the same conditions, regardless of their geographical location. however, the migration to sepa through self-regulation has not been conclusive: important measures have not yet been fully deployed and national systems are still operating in parallel with the new system. i supported this report, which reflects the agreement between our three institutions on the final migration to the sepa by regulation, with a deadline of 1 february 2014. by then at the latest, we will be able to enjoy the full benefits of an integrated payments market: cross-border payments will be as simple as national payments and will be faster, safer and cheaper. transfers will reach the recipient by the end of the next working day at the latest and the amounts transferred will no longer be charged. companies will apply a single set of standards and be able to organise all their crossborder payments in euro from a single account of their choice, improving financial management and speeding up cash flows at a lower cost. i'm going to february 1st, 2014!
in writing. i have followed the favourable opinion of the committee on budgetary control on the proposal of the council of ministers to appoint mr baudilio tomé muguruza as a member of the court of auditors. baudilio tomé muguruza is an economist, tax lawyer and international affairs specialist, and is highly qualified for this position. the committee had the opportunity to hear him. i have full confidence in its competence and am now awaiting the final decision of the council of ministers of the european union.

in writing. i welcome the appointment of mr baudilio tomé as a member of the european court of auditors. i supported his appointment because of his technical and ethical qualities.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the eu-morocco agreement favours industrial agriculture, heavily capitalised, on both sides of the mediterranean, at the expense of family and peasant farming. the increase in reduced-rate quotas for a wide range of vegetables and fruit puts european producers in an unsustainable competitive situation without, however, promoting balanced development in morocco. the main factor in the composition of fruit and vegetable prices is labour costs. morocco now has an undeniable advantage due to the massive use of child labour and the prohibition of agricultural workers' unions. wages are 5 euros a day in morocco, while in spain they reach 50 euros. how can we cope with this kind of competition, with this social dumping? respect for trade union rights and the prohibition of child labour are prerequisites for any ratification of a new trade agreement with morocco. for european producer organisations, the circumvention of the entry price system is dramatic. this malfunction reduces the payment of customs duties. the european commission has never given itself the means to combat this fraud, and it must settle this issue before proposing a new agreement. in morocco, the management of export rights favours large groups. as regards tomatoes, 70% of moroccan exports are concentrated in three companies. the moroccan family farming sector does not benefit from this agreement. according to a study funded by the european union, the tiris euro arab investment fund from abu dhabi has obtained 700,000 hectares in southern morocco to develop citrus, olive and vegetable plantations. the land grabbing, which shocks our fellow citizens so much, is also taking place on a large scale in morocco. in the sousse region, where tomatoes are the most important crop, the water table is falling by 2 metres a year. in western sahara, industrial farms draw water from the coastal groundwater. this irrigation causes salinization of fresh water and endangers the drinking water supply of local populations. exporting 350 000 tonnes of tomatoes is equivalent to sending 35 million cubic metres of water to europe from morocco. the social, environmental and economic impacts have not been assessed by the european commission. we're still waiting on the impact study. a study is needed for parliament to make an informed decision. we have never seen an agreement go through without knowing the social, economic and environmental impacts. i raised the question of the territorial scope of the agreement between the member of the commission. - mr president, allow me to clarify some of the points that have been raised here. firstly, some of you have spoken about unfair competition or the lack of impact studies. i will give you two figures: tomato production in the european union is six million tonnes a year. the concessions we are proposing to morocco under this agreement are to increase the quota by 52 000 tonnes, which represents 0.8% of tomato production in the european union. moreover, the entry price system and the monthly distribution of this quantity protect the european market for tomatoes from morocco during the period from june to september, when production in the european union is at its highest. for the rest of the year, this quantity is distributed monthly. i also spoke about entry prices, mrs herranz garcía and mr mato adrover, and i have heard your remarks, as well as those of the agriculture ministers of these countries, and that is why i proposed to align the system for calculating entry prices with the taxation system in force in the european union, precisely to avoid that small quotas or small quantities of certain products, which are more advantageous, make the calculation of the whole transport operation take place on this basis. it is to eliminate this type of problem that we have proposed the improvement of the system for calculating entry prices. i can assure you that we will also monitor the way in which the member states carry out customs controls at the border once this change is made. some of you have said that this agreement will benefit multinationals and not small farms, but i do not know whether a trade agreement can encourage the development of a multinational or an operating model. you know that within the european union, these kinds of guidelines are defined by our own agricultural policy. morocco also has its own agricultural policy and, during the negotiations for this agreement, it presented us with this green plan, in which at least the moroccan government has undertaken to give clear support also to small farms. you also mentioned land grabbing. the information we have received from the government of the kingdom of morocco, and which is also clear in the green plan, is that foreigners' access to land is limited to 100 000 hectares in morocco and that individual farms' access is limited to a few thousand hectares per farm. in any case, mr bové, this is the information that the moroccan government has given us. as regards compliance with veterinary health standards - i have already said in my introduction - border controls ensure that products from morocco, like from other parts of the world, comply with veterinary and phytosanitary standards. all the food safety standards imposed on our producers are therefore applied to moroccan producers and, moreover, the audits recently carried out by the european food and veterinary office in morocco show us that this country also now has the capacity to ensure this control with the institutions it has created. our technical assistance programmes in morocco also aim to strengthen this capacity in the future. you also mentioned the impact on the environment, particularly with regard to water consumption. the data we have indicate that the average consumption of one kilo of tomatoes in morocco is 47 litres of water per kilo, whereas in the european union it is 45 litres per kilo. this figure is therefore close to the average for the european union, or at least that is the calculation we have, mr bové. with the drop-in technology system that morocco - as we understand it - wants to develop as part of its green plan, this consumption could be further reduced. but again, it is not by agreement that you can impose on a government choices that are its responsibility. i think that if we respect the self-determination of a state like morocco, we can rely on the information it gives us to make decisions, including on an agreement. thank you very much for these clarifications. i think my colleague, mr füle, will give you even more details on the non-agricultural aspects which you have also raised in your speeches.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioners, mr president of the council, we have just had a debate which was nevertheless interesting because for the first time we had a real debate on a free trade agreement. some spoke of facts, others spoke of ideology, even belief, belief in free trade as the advance towards democracy. i hope that these people will not one day find themselves facing the same people who have been victims of free trade agreements, whether it be fruit and vegetable farmers today or meat producers tomorrow when the mercosur agreement comes. but i would say that this free trade agreement is a bad agreement first and foremost for moroccan farmers. if the yes wins on thursday - it's possible, i don't know - it means that you are creating all the conditions for the arab spring to finally arrive in morocco. that means you're gonna be in a funny situation tomorrow. when we see that the agreement provides for an increase of more than 50% for european products in morocco, compared with only 15% for moroccan products in europe, this means that hundreds of thousands of moroccan families will be thrown out on the streets because of these exports to their own country. is that what you want? today, i get the feeling you're not telling the truth. you refuse to tell the truth. we agree to this deal because morocco is committed to protecting us from immigration coming from africa. that is what you are saying, and that is what you are saying in all your texts. are economic agreements being made only to build a wall across the mediterranean to protect europe? let's not get carried away! let us return to the facts, and the facts are agriculture. but this agreement is a bad plan for agriculture. a 1% increase in volume over supply can bring down prices. as you know very well, commissioner, the adjustment of supply and demand is fragile. 1% can bring down prices and can have dramatic consequences. we know that perpignan is now a veritable tomato-picking area. it is known that the headquarters of the two largest companies, azura and idyl, are in france. today, that is known. so why do we continue in this way? we also know that the commission has internal documents in the european union which show that more than 700 000 hectares have been given to a fund in the persian gulf. today you cannot deny it, the commission documents themselves prove it. we have to be serious, like we were about the water. we are now told that we have no data on water, whereas european, dutch, french, spanish and moroccan universities provide figures. i'm not going to go any further. as for the obligation to western sahara, i did not want to turn it into a political battle, just a question of law. and the law is stubborn. if western sahara were not excluded from this agreement tomorrow, you would be faced with the possibility of an appeal to the european court of justice.
in writing. i understand the concerns raised by this agreement, which has been under negotiation since 2008 and is about to be voted on, but guarantees have been put in place to protect the interests of european producers. the quotas remain unchanged, moroccan products will not have access to the european market during the main seasons for the sale of european products and socioeconomic and environmental criteria will have to be met by moroccans. free and undistorted competition must be ensured and the interests of european agricultural sectors must be defended. if market imbalances are found, compensatory measures for european farmers will have to be taken. with the expansion of the moroccan market, we will also be able to increase our exports to that country. it is also the reward given to morocco for its democratic reforms and to reject this agreement would be dangerous. so we must strike a balance between protecting our agriculture and establishing a privileged partnership with the moroccans. it is in this spirit that i support this agreement, while remaining vigilant about its implementation. saving our agricultural model and opening up our market are compatible. thank you.

president-in-office of the council. − mr president, the spring european council is, as you know, the european council’s annual rendezvous to discuss economic and social issues, and the next meetings of heads of state or government will be no exception. the european council will seek to address the current economic crisis, notably by providing guidance on member states’ economic and employment policies, putting particular emphasis on accelerating structural reforms to increase competitiveness and create more jobs and on fully exploiting the potential of green growth. however, let me stress that this is not to say that we are in a business-as-usual mode. indeed we cannot afford complacency. because of the crisis we need more than ever to make full use of our new tools – the european semester and the six-pack. this is an important priority for the danish presidency and we will work in all relevant council formations to ensure strict implementation of the new rules in order to ensure their credibility, but also to provide opportunity for anchoring this process at the level of heads of state and government. the european council will conclude the first phase of the european semester on the basis of the commission’s annual growth survey and the discussions held in the different formations of the council. it is the presidency’s intention to summarise all these contributions in a synthesis report. furthermore, the epsco and ecofin councils will adopt conclusions. in this context the european council will identify the main challenges facing the eu, and give strategic advice and guidance to member states on the different policies. let me recall that a number of orientations have already been set out at the informal european council on 30 january regarding stimulating employment, especially for young people, completing the single market and boosting the financing of the economy, in particular of the smes. those measures requiring actions at the national level are to be duly reflected in member states’ national reform programmes. as regards measures to be taken at eu level, the council will report back on the implementation in june. we expect the march european council to assess the economic situation and express the eu’s determination to continue to take all necessary measures. regarding guidance to member states on their national reform programmes and stability and convergence programmes, the european council will discuss the implementation of the 2011 european semester country-specific recommendations and commitments under the euro plus pact. it will call on member states to give priority to the areas identified in the commission’s ags and in the council discussion on the european semester and to reflect this in the nrps and scps. the european council will also call on the member states taking part in the euro plus pact to update their commitments and to make them more precise, time-limited, operational and measureable. regarding innovation and following up on the orientations set by the european council, the danish presidency will prepare reports setting out progress achieved in this field. on that basis we expect the european council to stress the areas where more progress is required to unlock innovation potential, for instance a single innovation indicator. on the second issue on the agenda – international summits – the forthcoming g8, g20 and rio+20 meetings will address issues important to the eu. the difficulty is, of course, that they will take place in june and the march european council should therefore take stock of preparation and signal those issues of particular importance. on the g20 and the g8, the mexican presidency has identified the following priorities for the summit: economic stabilisation and structural reforms as foundations for growth and employment; strengthening the financial system and fostering financial inclusion to promote economic growth; improving the international financial architecture in an interconnected world; enhancing food security and addressing commodity price volatility; promoting sustainable development, green growth and the fight against climate change. the mexican presidency will organise preparatory ministerial meetings on foreign affairs, tourism, agriculture and labour. the eu position at the meeting will be thoroughly prepared in the coming months in the relevant council formations in order to ensure a strong and coordinated eu position. the un rio+20 conference: at this conference it is an important priority for the danish presidency that we should promote a strengthened global institutional framework for sustainable development and advance work on global and coherent post-2015 goals for sustainable development. the european council is expected to underline its strong commitment to an ambitious outcome of the un conference to be held in rio de janeiro in june of this year and stress the need for strong participation from the private sector and civil society. the council will further develop the eu position on rio+20 in order to ensure a strong european voice in rio. in accordance with the conclusions of the european council in december 2011, the european council will also take up the issue of status as candidate country for serbia. as you are aware, the european council on 9 december 2011 noted that considerable progress has been made by serbia towards fulfilling the political criteria. with a view to granting serbia the status of candidate country, the european council tasked the general affairs council to examine and confirm that serbia has continued to show credible commitment and has achieved further progress in moving forward with the implementation, in good faith, of agreement reached in the dialogue, including on ibm, has reached an agreement on inclusive regional cooperation and has actively cooperated to enable eulex and kfor to execute their mandates. in the
