give serbia status as a candidate country but that will of course also require that serbia has done what is necessary to live up to the criteria formulated in december. finally the european council is expected to address foreign policy, probably with the focus on the southern neighbourhood and the arab spring.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, europe is in an unprecedented economic situation. after the years of crisis, our forecasts show that growth is at a virtual standstill and will remain slow for the foreseeable future. unemployment, especially youth unemployment, is unacceptably high and may remain so for many years. this is the background against which we need action and against which the actions of european institutions and national governments alike will be judged. we need to deliver on the greatest concerns of our citizens – jobs and growth – and we need to mark a turning point in the way we have addressed this crisis until now. as we already said in our roadmap last october, we need decisive action to address greece’s problems and restore public finances to health. we need to strengthen the european banking system and to build credible firewalls for the euro area, and we need stability and discipline to prevent a repeat of recent events, but unless we can also get our economy growing and creating jobs we will only have a partial solution and we will not win the support of our citizens. that is why the informal european council was such an important stepping stone for the spring european council. it represented agreement among europe’s leaders to concentrate on a few immediate priorities with substantial potential for growth and employment – first and foremost for our young people and for our smes, to help them to grow and to create jobs again. this message was already at the core of our 2012 annual growth survey (ags), adopted by the commission last november and with this ags we are launching the new european semester. as you know, our survey is a contribution to the spring european council and we will call upon the european council to give very strong backing to the priorities we have identified. i hope that we can also count on the support of this house to do so. the annual growth survey points to the number of priorities we have to achieve in the future and the priorities which should guide the member states in drawing up their own new national programmes, which are due to be presented in april. on the basis of this, the commission will put forward country-specific proposals for the discussion in may and adoption at the june european council. what is very important is that very little of what is in the annual growth survey is completely new. there is, and has been for some time, a broad consensus on the need to cover jobs and growth as well as getting public finances in order. we need a balanced approach, covering growth and jobs and the improvement of fiscal consolidations and public finances, but what we need even more is implementation and respect for the commitments which we have already undertaken. as far as new ideas are concerned, we have to remind ourselves that we already have a policy for jobs and growth. it is called europe 2020. we also have a european semester which represents a quantum leap in economic policy coordination in europe. for the first time this year, the semester will take place within our strengthened system of economic governance based on the six-pack legislation that the european parliament played such an important role in developing. what is needed now is a firm commitment at national and european levels to picking up the pace of the reforms and to carrying that commitment through to 2012. the commission has already put forward a proposal regarding the problem which is probably the most burdensome and most difficult for our citizens – namely youth unemployment. we cannot accept the fact that we have 7.5 million young people across europe classified as neets, which means that they are not in employment, education or training. they definitely do not deserve this. we need to tackle these high levels of youth unemployment and we need to do so in a sustainable manner. getting young people on to the labour market is an essential element of our efforts to ensure future growth. we have already set up action teams that will visit the eight member states with the highest youth unemployment rates and they will examine, together with national authorities and social partners, what we can do better, how we can make better use of eu and national funds and how we can focus our efforts on social policies, smes and job creation for young people. i am very happy to report that our initial contacts with the member states have been very encouraging and i hope that we will already be able to bring a positive report to the spring european council on this matter. but these actions must be part of the wider reform of labour market policies aimed at getting more europeans on to the labour market and increasing their employment opportunities. i am sure that these issues will be discussed again at greater length in a moment when you debate the cornelissen, gauzès and berès reports. i started my presentation in a slightly downbeat fashion, but i would like to conclude on a more optimistic note. while no one is brave enough yet to suggest that we have turned the corner, that the worst might be over and that we might finally be back on the road to growth, i think it is fair to say that we now at least have far greater control over our future. the new measures that have been proposed by the commission and agreed by this house – now i am talking about the six-pack and other measures – are giving much more visibility to the european semester and are allowing us to take action far earlier than before and to avoid the kind of fire-fighting that has dominated our discussions until now. yesterday, the commission adopted its first alert mechanism report according to which the 12 countries should be subject to a more in-depth review. our recommendations will now be discussed in the council and eurogroup and, of course, the feedback from this house into this discussion would be very welcome. this might not seem particularly optimistic, especially for the 12 member states concerned, but it underlines the rapid and effective improvements that have already been made to the way in which public finances are managed in europe. we need to have the right tools in place to monitor progress, address risk and propose remedies well before a crisis hits. we must make sure that the crisis that we are now going through will never again be repeated. thanks to widespread agreement between the commission, parliament and the council we now have the tools and, although it is early days, i would say that we have very strong indications that they are working. i fully expect the positive spirit of the informal council to continue through to the spring council, that the heads of state and government will endorse the guidelines for growth and, more importantly, that they will meet their commitments on the ground.

in writing. the schengen area, which includes 22 eu member states and 4 non-eu countries (iceland, norway, switzerland and liechtenstein), offers their citizens the possibility of free movement. the abolition of internal borders between these states in favour of a single external border leads them to harmonise their external border controls and to strengthen their police and judicial cooperation. in order to fulfil the objective underlying the schengen agreements, the creation of an 'area of freedom, security and justice', it is essential to fully involve these four third countries. i therefore voted in favour of their participation in the work of the committees which assist the european commission in implementing the schengen acquis.
in writing. the schengen area, which simplifies the daily lives of our citizens and businesses by opening the internal borders of the european union to people, capital and services, is now expanding. i supported the request of iceland, switzerland, lichtenstein and norway, countries in the heart of europe but not part of the european union, to become associated states of the schengen acquis. the aim of this text is to formalise their participation in the process of drawing up the texts within the schengen comitology committees, which are composed of representatives of the governments of the associated states, the council of ministers and the european commission. the latter have the opportunity to explain the problems they face in relation to a measure or to respond to the problems encountered by the other delegations. they are also entitled to make suggestions. however, as they only participate in the preparation of acts, the associated states do not participate in the votes in the schengen comitology committees and withdraw when they vote , says rapporteur timothy kirkhope.
in writing. i voted in favour of this agreement, which allows iceland, liechtenstein, norway and switzerland to participate in the commission's work on the implementation of the schengen acquis. this limited and supervised participation will make it possible to strengthen the area of freedom, security and justice of the european union and to identify more rapidly the problems related to police and judicial cooperation and the control of the external borders of our territory.
in writing. i voted in favour of the kirkhope report. in adopting this report, parliament gave its approval to an arrangement between the european union, iceland, liechtenstein, norway and switzerland on their participation in the work of committees assisting the european commission in the implementation of the schengen acquis. the agreement provides that these states will be associated with the work as observers without having the right to vote. in addition, they will be asked to contribute financially to administrative expenses. finally, the arrangement contains a joint declaration stating that this association cannot be regarded as a legal or political precedent for any other area of cooperation.

in writing. in the digital age, the demand for radio waves is increasing. it is therefore essential that the union develops a genuine policy in this area. that is why i have approved the first common european radio spectrum programme. the gradual switch-over from analogue to digital tv by 2013 will free up radio frequencies for mobile internet. the programme also advocates access to high-speed internet in remote areas.
in writing. i supported the recommendation to make the 800 mhz frequency band available to telecom operators. today it is used for television, tomorrow it will be used to extend and make much more efficient our wireless broadband internet access, starting on 1 january 2013. this scarce resource is a driver of economic progress for citizens, as strategic planning and harmonisation of spectrum use will be used in many areas, including shipping, health, the environment and defence. this programme 'will offer us opportunities for european industry as well as for new services and new growth', said my swedish colleague gunnar hökmark of the european people's party, adding that 'it is not just about telecommunications but also about giving the eu a new economic momentum' to regain its competitiveness in a new global economy that now includes major competitors such as china and india.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text which will encourage the use of mobile broadband and stimulate economic growth in our territories. in may 2011, we approved measures to accelerate the development of mobile broadband for all, using the radio spectrum freed up as a result of the switch from analogue to digital television. the allocation of radio frequencies is a matter for national authorities and not the eu, but the rules on how to share the spectrum between internet providers and users must be decided at european level. under the agreement, eu member states should free up the 800 mhz frequency band for wireless broadband services by 1 january 2013. a pan-european telecommunications market will thus be created, where new services can create new opportunities to open up territories and stimulate growth in a market of 500 million consumers.
in writing. at the request of the european parliament, the commission published its multiannual radio spectrum programme in september 2010. this programme sets out the policy guidelines and means to be implemented for the harmonised use of radio spectrum in the european union for the period 2011-2015. it also provides for common measures to increase efficiency and flexibility, to promote innovation and to encourage competition. finally, it called for the implementation of an inventory of current and emerging spectrum needs. access to radio spectrum is essential for a wide range of activities from telephony and broadband to transport, energy, research and development and space applications. it also enables all european citizens, in urban and rural settings, to enjoy the benefits of digital technologies and fast broadband connections. for all these reasons i supported this report in plenary.

in writing. i voted this week for a text which directly concerns dairy farmers. the sector has been in a severe crisis, prolonged and aggravated by the global economic crisis. the resulting price instability is deeply destabilising for our producers, who already face the planned end of milk quotas by 2015. the text amends the contractual rules to increase the bargaining power of milk producers, to guarantee them fairer prices for the raw milk they produce and to help them prepare for the end of quotas. like all the parties except the green group, we have taken our responsibilities! producer organisations will be able to negotiate on behalf of their collective up to 33% of a state's milk production or up to 3.5% of european production. the text will also improve the transparency and in-depth analysis of data on milk production in the union, which should help to restore the relative stability of the past. although the rapporteur, james nicholson, felt that this text could have been more ambitious, this compromise represents a considerable step forward for our dairy farmers and is designed to protect the most vulnerable.
in writing. this text is partly a response to the terrible crisis experienced by the sector in 2008-2010, when prices paid to producers had collapsed dramatically. producers will now be able to group together to have a greater say in negotiations with processors and distributors. new tools, provided for by european legislation, are at their disposal to promote their interests and participate in the management of their markets. the european parliament will continue to pay attention to the dairy sector, particularly as other steps are approaching, such as the issue of contracting throughout the chain or a mechanism to ensure that disadvantaged areas do not lose their milk production once quotas are abolished, which is planned for 2015. we will ensure that the 2014 and 2018 progress reports provide an opportunity to make further proposals to avoid an insurmountable shock to the dairy sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of the nicholson report because i believe it provides a number of answers to the crisis in the milk sector in 2009. i am satisfied with the solutions proposed by the agri committee, which lead to greater stability in the dairy sector. i think it is urgent to regulate supply and to ensure a fair price level, as we move towards the end of milk quotas by 2015. this is essential to end the unfair commercial practices that are plaguing dairy farmers. two proposals in the report have particularly caught my attention: the introduction of a new european legal framework for inter-branch organisations and the obligation to draw up contracts fixing volumes and prices over time. this is good news for dairy farmers who are seeing their protection strengthened.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on contract negotiations in the dairy sector. the commission notes that the aid is part of the compensation for the damage caused by the crisis in the dairy sector in 2008-2010, when prices paid to producers plummeted. it also prepares milk producers for the scheduled end of milk quotas in 2015. to this end, it aims to increase the bargaining power of milk producers, in order to guarantee them fairer prices for their products, without, however, infringing the right to competition. to this end, the new regulation provides, inter alia, that milk producers will be able to join producer associations to create a real counterweight to processors, and thus ensure a fairer distribution of added value from one end of the supply chain to the other. in the long term, this approach aims to provide milk producers with fairer living conditions. today, i therefore encourage milk producers to make full use of these new tools provided by european legislation to put their interests first, to find their place in the market and to prepare for the 'post-quota era'.
in writing. the adoption of this text is to be welcomed, as the reasons for satisfaction are real. while not all is perfect, the policy shifts from the decisions taken in recent years are substantial, particularly with regard to the power given to producers to group together to give greater weight in negotiations with processors and distributors. interprofessionalism has become an integral part of the european vocabulary, and the need to allow producers of pdo/pgi cheeses to manage their production volumes has finally been recognised. other advances, such as contractual arrangements along the whole chain or a mechanism to ensure that disadvantaged areas do not lose their milk production as soon as quotas are abolished, will have to be made in the coming years. the 'smooth landing' promised by the then commissioner, mrs fischer boel, must be a reality for european producers. producers will now have to make full use of the new tools provided for by european legislation in order to promote their interests as much as possible and to participate in the management of their markets.

in writing. the european union decided that agriculture was a sector like any other, subject to the vagaries of the world market. that is why it decided to abolish milk quotas, which helped to regulate the milk market and did little to support the prices paid to farmers, at a time when large producing countries want milk to be considered a strategic product and, as such, to be excluded from wto agreements. the solution it has found to replace this disgraceful regulation is the contractual relationship between producer associations and the dairies. but this does not solve any of the problems in the sector, at least at the level of the farmers. it does not guarantee the prices paid to them, their strengthening in the negotiations with the major dairy groups, or even their survival. the vast majority of professionals believe that this system, which is designed for the agro-food industry and is financed by the industry, will lead to a concentration of production in huge industrial plants located in easily accessible areas, at the expense of established and small farms. and this without any benefit to the consumers. we therefore voted against this report.

in writing. the adoption of a roadmap for the creation of the conditions for the joint issuance of part of the sovereign debt in the form of eurobonds is a longstanding demand of the socialist and democratic group. that is why i supported the adoption of this resolution, because eurobonds not only establish a system of responsibility and solidarity between member states, by helping the most heavily indebted countries to gain access to credit at a reduced price, but also because they commit to deepening economic and monetary union. moreover, they are a means of strengthening the stability and resilience of the euro area in the long term. eurobonds therefore provide a sustainable alternative to the drastic austerity measures imposed on citizens and provide a common european response to the sovereign debt crisis affecting states and their populations.
in writing. parliament asked the commission to present a report on the possibility of introducing european securities, which is an integral part of the agreement between parliament and the council on the six-pack of economic governance legislation. this resolution is a first response to the commission's green paper of 23 november 2011 on the feasibility of introducing stability obligations. it will be followed by an own-initiative report. i voted in favour of this resolution, which shows that stability bonds could be an additional means of encouraging compliance with the stability and growth pact and of promoting stability in the euro area in the medium term.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the feasibility of introducing stability bonds, following the green paper launched by the european commission on this subject. these so-called 'euro bonds' are among the options for promoting the stability of the euro area in the medium term, but they cannot be a one-size-fits-all solution to the problems we are currently facing, in particular the european sovereign debt crisis. the necessary prerequisite is, of course, the establishment of strengthened economic governance, the further consolidation of our public finances through common budgetary discipline, and the strengthening of the convergence of our economic and budgetary policies. it is only when these principles are established and the implementation of the treaty on financial stability is completed that a possible joint bond issue will be possible, useful and seen as such by the countries of the european union. in addition, technical issues, notably the question of debt segmentation, remain to be resolved.
in writing. this resolution argues that stability bonds can promote the stability of the euro area. yet these bonds foster dependence on the free financial markets that are precisely causing instability. they also serve as a justification for forcing states to converge in stages towards a policy of permanent rigor. in doing so, they hide solutions that should be taken urgently. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right to vote and to stand as a candidate in the elections to the european parliament. i am voting against this text.
in writing. in the face of the crisis and the adoption of austerity measures, some sections of the population are hit harder than others. young people are the first victims. while they represent 20% of the total population of the union, 1 in 5 young people are unemployed. the employment of young people must therefore be a priority. that is why i voted in favour of the cornelissen report.
in writing. in the context of the annual growth review, which will be approved at the european council on 1 and 2 march, the resolution by rapporteur marije cornelissen analyses more specifically the social aspects and the importance of measuring the social impact of policies in each country. the resolution warns that new fiscal consolidation measures could hit those at risk of poverty or social exclusion. as you know, the fight against poverty in europe is also one of my main priorities. i share the vision set out in the resolution of a european union that would focus more on decent work and work-life balance. as a mother, these concerns are mine. the text also stresses the need to develop comprehensive strategies for young unemployed people and the importance of reducing forms of precarious employment among young people. however, i remain convinced that there is no contradiction between the fiscal rebalancing measures currently being applied and the long-term growth objectives of the european union.
in writing. strengthening economic governance, reducing public deficits, modernising public administration, etc. is this enough to provide employment for 75% of the population or to reduce by at least 20 million the number of people affected or threatened by poverty and social exclusion by 2020? i don't think he did. employment and social policy issues are becoming increasingly rare in the current political discourse. ensure that fiscal austerity policies do not impede social justice, increase poverty and increase unemployment... in short, it is essential to ensure that the social effects of the crisis are not compounded by the social effects of austerity. it is not acceptable to have only rigour as a political horizon. the strategy put forward in the cornelissen report involves refocusing budgets on employment and social policy in order to support the creation of quality jobs, to combat effectively youth unemployment and also poverty and social exclusion. ignoring the perverse effects of austerity policies is not an option. the road to the social europe that citizens have been waiting for seems to be a long one, but the ideas are there.
in writing. it is urgent that the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy be a top priority for the european commission and the member states. in the national employment plan that each member state will publish next april, training must be adapted to the needs of enterprises; continuing training and retraining must be offered to employees; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. our social policy as a whole must be more adapted, we need more crèches, more favourable social incentives than those linked to unemployment, and active support for all socially virtuous enterprises. we must offer young people without qualifications paid apprenticeships or traineeships. there are 23 million smes in europe, we have 23 million unemployed, and unused european employment funds. let us not wait any longer, let us encourage initiatives and quickly implement those that have a positive assessment of employment. it is our responsibility to demand that the same energy that is used to take strong economic measures is also used to take ambitious and effective social measures.
in writing. for several months now, austerity plans have been proliferating in europe. greece is the most striking example. despite the efforts needed to combat the debt crisis, growth is still extremely low. there will be no exit from the crisis without a return to growth. austerity alone will not get us anywhere. i wanted to reiterate this by voting in favour of this text. budgetary discipline must be accompanied by strong measures for investment and employment. in the difficult economic and social times we are living through, the recovery of our public finances must not hinder measures to combat unemployment, and in particular youth unemployment.
in writing. i supported this report which, in the run-up to the spring european council, calls on the council to ensure coherence and show greater ambition in achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. in the report, parliament also called on the council to support sustainable job creation through investment and tax reform, to improve the quality and rate of employment and the conditions for an increased rate of activity, to combat youth unemployment and poverty and social exclusion. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. this annual growth survey report stresses that the european commission's budgetary priorities for the coming year must be the economy, employment, social policy and reforms. the central message of this review presented at the end of 2011 is to call for efforts to be directed towards supporting jobs and growth. i voted for this report because it stresses the importance of finding a middle ground between support for growth and balanced public finances.
in writing. the text calls on (without naming her) mrs merkel to "stimulate domestic demand" in germany. it advocates a taxation system which is "fair, progressive, redistributive, efficient and effective". he is concerned about "endangering the public pension systems". i can relate to him on those points. but i cannot accept the increase in the retirement age, the flexibility of wage relations, the abolition of early retirement or the abolition of the 'tax burden of non-wage costs' which this text advocates. i vote against it.
in writing. i abstained from voting on this report. it contains a number of positive things, such as increased investment in education and training, the fight against youth unemployment, increasing employment for women or ensuring the involvement of the social partners. one might hope that this is not just fine talk, but one may have doubts, especially when one reads that fiscal consolidation must be based on social justice or that austerity measures do not compromise social protection, or that there is no endangerment of public pension systems. unfortunately, we know how these guidelines are being implemented at present, particularly when it comes to helping businesses by removing the tax burden of labour-related wage costs, setting up benefit systems adapted to the new needs of the market to maintain employability or pushing governments, under the weight of the current crisis, to implement the necessary reform programmes. we know all too well the disastrous consequences of such reforms. to stop the system, it would take more than wishful thinking.

(applause) i would like to thank i am the representative of a state which is considered to be geographically peripheral and i have no objection to this geographical connotation; at the same time, i should like to point out that the central states - and italy too, from the point of view of responsibility, if we want to start with the two largest economies in the euro area, germany and france - were the cause of the crisis of the stability and growth pact and its limited credibility in 2003 when, with the complicity of italy, which was then chairing the ecofin council, those two countries preferred to exert their political influence on the other member states in order to, in essence, break the enforcement mechanism. this is a fact which is now recognized by the governments of both germany and france, so i am not saying anything unpleasant to my colleagues, the german chancellor and the president of the french republic. but it is a fact that a great blow to the credibility of budgetary discipline has come from the central point of the eurozone, which had a great historical merit in establishing and promoting that budgetary discipline. we cannot therefore forget that there is a responsibility for the centre, as well as for the periphery, because it is true that several peripheral states, including the one i represent here, have at some point - (applause) - allowed themselves to be too much drawn into budgetary indiscipline. but there are no good people and bad people in the european union, mr president, ladies and gentlemen. we must all feel partly responsible for what we have done in the past and, above all, for building the future. (applause) now i do not think this is the time to put aside the moment of budgetary discipline, content that we have the fiscal compact and to move to another page of the european agenda, that of growth. i think we have to reconcile both of these aspects. and this is also true of the daily life of our countries. for example, yesterday, with my colleagues in the council of ministers in rome, i had to make a difficult and unpopular decision: the commission's proposal is to deny the italian state's financial guarantee to a magnificent project to bring the 2020 olympics to rome. there was a lot of disappointment in italy about this decision, especially in rome. but we have argued - and i have the impression that italian public opinion has understood - that the essential imperative for italy today, in its own interest and in the interest of europe - and last week in the united states, i had the testimony in washington of how the stability of the eurozone is considered an essential good also for the world economy - is another and that therefore, at this moment, any gesture of postponement of possible burdens of uncertain quantification does not appear in line with the responsibility that we governors must assume - although too often avoided in the past in all countries - that is to avoid unloading burdens on the future and on future generations. i hope that there will be other occasions for major events in italy, as there have been many times in the past, where italy has been able to make its contribution to culture, sport and events at european level. but i think that these are also small examples that we must offer to show that budgetary discipline is not a recent acquisition that we want to get rid of as soon as possible, but is a new way of living civic life. member of the commission. - mr president, i am pleased to be able to answer the question which your assembly and your rapporteur, mr juan fernando lópez aguilar, are putting to the commission and to give you the opinion of my colleague, cecilia malmström, on this subject for which she is responsible. ladies and gentlemen, family reunification accounts for a large proportion of legal immigration into the european union. there is a trend of a decrease in this family grouping from half in the 2000s to a third today. the migrants covered by the directive i.e. third-country nationals who join a non-eu citizen account for 21% of all permits issued 500 000 persons for our 27 member states in 2010. i should like to briefly touch on the content of the green paper and the questions it raises on the scope of application, the conditions for the exercise of the right of association, in particular integration measures, and procedural problems. some questions also concern possible ways of combating fraud and marriages of convenience, and, in addition, the rules on expenses. in its 2008 report on the family reunification directive, the commission had already identified some implementation problems at national level, for example cases where visas are not issued under a simplified procedure to a person admitted as a family member. the commission also noted shortcomings in the directive where some of its provisions are too vague, for example as regards the possibility of applying certain conditions such as integration measures. member states called on the commission, both at the time of the 2008 pact on immigration and asylum and in the 2009 stockholm programme, to continue the development of this policy at eu level, with particular attention to integration. the tendency of some member states to apply stricter rules, due to what they claim are integration problems and certain abuses, has revived the debate. in view of all these elements, the commission considered that it would be useful to organise an open consultation at union level. the green paper is the most participatory approach. it provides an opportunity for all interested parties to engage, to make their views known. it also leaves us the choice as to whether to act further and how to act. as regards, ladies and gentlemen, your questions on human rights and fundamental rights, i would like to make three points on behalf of mrs malmström. firstly, the directive recognises the right to family reunification as a necessary means of enabling family life. secondly, as the court of justice has confirmed, the directive must be applied in compliance with the charter of fundamental rights and in conformity with that charter. this is particularly the case with regard to the right to respect for family life, the right to marry, the right to found a family and the right of the child to have a personal relationship with both parents. the court of justice has confirmed in another judgment that the optional conditions laid down in the directive - for example, the requirement that the applicant for family reunification have sufficient financial resources - must be applied restrictively in order not to impede the right to family reunification. finally, thirdly, the green paper invites interested parties to clarify whether safeguards should be introduced to ensure that integration measures and fees are not used as a means of limiting the right to family reunification. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, with regard to forced or fraudulent marriages, the green paper calls for more information to be provided to the commission so that it can tackle any problems in a more targeted manner. firstly, the commission is trying to establish in this green paper whether there is a link between forced marriages and the minimum age of the spouse, as some member states have claimed. it also asked for statistics on registered marriages of convenience and for information on how the provisions for checks and inspections could be made more effective. i would like to emphasize the open nature of this consultation. the commission will decide on the basis of its findings what action to take. there are several possibilities. interpretative guidelines are one possibility. this can be an effective instrument if accompanied by other tools, such as expert groups and in-depth dialogue with each member state. in addition to the green paper, the european migration network will complete a targeted study in the second quarter of 2012 to inform the consultation process and its follow-up. whatever the form of the follow-up measures, the commission will ensure the correct implementation of the current union rules on family reunification. if necessary, it will be prepared to initiate infringement proceedings.

member of the commission. - mr president, i should like to begin by thanking mr menéndez del valle and mr moreira for this report and for this question, to which i wish to reply on behalf of my colleague, mr algirdas šemeta, who regrets that he cannot be here in person to assure you, ladies and gentlemen, of the commission's full commitment to the progressive establishment of a genuine like to reply specifically on behalf of mr šemeta. firstly, the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin is one of the first concrete responses to the historic and positive events that have recently occurred in many of our southern mediterranean neighbours. this convention is important for several reasons. first, it will promote trade between the european union and its southern mediterranean neighbours. it will therefore strengthen their economic integration. it will then pave the way for the simplification of the rules of origin and their adaptation to the new economic situation in the region. it will also allow the integration of other european neighbours, notably the western balkan countries, into the pan-euro-mediterranean area by providing them with new opportunities within an expanded trade area. since i am speaking of the economic integration of this region and its association with the european union, i express my concern as commissioner for the internal market and the idea that one of the ways in which this region can open up to democracy and the world is that these countries on the other side of the mediterranean should first of all succeed in establishing a common market among themselves. i was listening the other day to the new tunisian president advocating the creation of such a market, which would facilitate trade, communications, lower borders and remove barriers between countries, particularly those in the arab maghreb. but we also have the tools, as i said, to move towards an organized free trade area between them and us, beyond the mediterranean. a second question you have asked: although there is no dispute settlement mechanism in the convention, there is one in article 33 of appendix 1 to the convention, which is quite logical, since the disputes which may arise between partner countries will concern essentially bilateral issues relating to the verification of proofs of origin. the text of this appendix will be legally binding, ladies and gentlemen, and it will replace the protocols on rules of origin, which are currently annexed to the bilateral free trade agreements between partners in the pan-euro-mediterranean area. thus, all free trade agreements concluded between these partners will refer to the same rules of origin and thus to identical provisions on dispute settlement. thirdly, the convention and its annexes can be revised at any time. for example, after several years of implementation and in the light of experience gained, amending decisions may be adopted by the joint committee, as specifically stipulated in article 4 of the convention. i quote: 'the joint committee shall adopt by decision the amendments to be made to this convention, including the amendments to the appendices'. so we are not in a totally static procedure that will never move. in the light of experience, and you have mentioned a number of problems, there are possible developments. this mechanism will be developed in the rules of procedure of the joint committee established by the convention. fourthly, i would like to assure you, mr menendez and mr moreira, on behalf of mr šemeta, that the commission is closely monitoring the implementation of the technical arrangement between the european union and the state of israel and is taking the necessary measures to improve its functioning, if necessary. the notice to importers on imports from israel is currently undergoing a very detailed examination with this objective. the commission services are currently examining, in close cooperation with the customs authorities of all member states, the possibility of making the list of settlements public and of issuing an amended version of the notice to importers. the objective of such a measure would be to oblige importers to verify themselves the postal codes appearing on the proofs of origin established in israel which they intend to submit to the customs authorities of the member states of the union. i believe that this should lead to improved controls, since the burden of checks will in future be shared between importers and customs authorities. to ensure that no settlement product is unduly favoured in the eu through cumulation with partners with a free trade agreement with israel, the commission considers that the best approach is to invite these partners to negotiate with israel similar or identical arrangements to those negotiated by the eu. finally, i want to say quite frankly that the commission is satisfied with the way the technical arrangement is working. therefore, the commission does not consider it necessary to amend its legal status at this stage. these are the answers mr šemeta wanted to give to the four questions you kindly put to the commission.

in writing. budgetary restrictions are necessary in times of crisis, the rigorousness is everywhere in europe, we cannot ask the states to make considerable efforts without doing so ourselves! the vaughan report rightly calls for a freeze on the european parliament's expenditure for 2013. we all know that this is necessary, but we must also take the necessary measures. but let us not forget that croatia's accession may increase eu spending... we will then have to be even more proactive than we are today and make the necessary budgetary adjustments for future expenditure. it is only natural that, in solidarity with the citizens of europe, we should freeze travel expenses and individual allowances until 2014. in parallel with these measures relating to our individual expenditure, the report recommends that we identify long-term savings opportunities in order to keep expenditure within the budgetary limits we have set ourselves. it is crucial to identify budget lines that overlap or lack efficiency in their action. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval, and the council will be consulted on the matter.
in writing. in these times of crisis, strict budgetary discipline is required of the greatest number and the european parliament must not deviate from the rule. a freeze of parliament's operating budget for 2013 has therefore been decided. in concrete terms, the staff budget and the budget for travel of members will be identical in real terms to that of 2012 and the individual allowances of members will not change until the end of the parliamentary term. to identify other possibilities for savings, parliament's budget will soon be the subject of an independent evaluation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this austerity budget because it is important that the european institutions contribute, in these times of economic crisis, to the effort of budgetary discipline initiated by the member states.
in writing. the european institutions are all the more costly because they are harmful and generate unnecessary or excessive expenditure in an attempt to justify their existence, to increase their own powers or visibility. in this context, the candle-lit savings and hypocritical calls for moderation in budget increases contained in the report and addressed to all the institutions except the commission appear hypocritical and ridiculous, especially when we know that the european union, paradoxically, employs fewer civil servants than the city of paris alone, and that members have systematically opposed, often in an opaque way, the reduction of their own standard of living! we are eagerly awaiting the report on the commission's budget, its management and its policies, to see whether this assembly will dare, for once, to cut back on unnecessary expenditure, advertising or patronage.
in writing. as in 2012, the european parliament is embarking on a period of budgetary austerity: we have voted this week to freeze the budget of our parliament for 2013. indeed, as the eu is going through a period of unprecedented financial and budgetary austerity, it is essential that the european institutions show responsibility and participate in budgetary efforts. i voted in favour of this report and i welcome its adoption. we also ask for an independent evaluation of the european parliament's budget. in addition, our individual allowances for members will be frozen until the end of the parliamentary term, as will budget lines for travel and staff. in particular, i would like to point out that i voted against amendment no 2 in favour of a single seat for the european parliament because it is yet another attack on the seat of strasbourg. i strongly advocate its maintenance, not only for historical and symbolic reasons, but above all in the name of the principle of diversity of the european union. this is above all a political question concerning the independence of parliament: the choice of strasbourg reflects a desire for a decentralized europe, not one "concentrated" in a single seat of power in brussels.
in writing. parliament was due to vote on its operating budget for 2013 on thursday 16 february. the budget did not raise any major difficulties, except for the introduction of an amendment calling for the european parliament to have only one seat. i am very sorry that this amendment was adopted, and that has opened the way to an internal battle between those who support and those who oppose the siege of strasbourg. for the sake of convenience, some of the work is being done in brussels, but let us not forget that strasbourg is the only official seat of the european parliament, the symbol of the rapprochement between france and germany, the symbol of the european unity desired by the founding fathers. today, some members of parliament declared open war in strasbourg. however, a report by the european association of young entrepreneurs presented on 14 february overturns the financial, institutional and environmental arguments put forward by critics. i therefore call on members to respect the letter of the treaties, because if we are to pursue the logic to the end, why not make strasbourg the sole seat of the european parliament?
in writing. the adoption of guidelines by means of a resolution is the first step in the budgetary procedure. all the institutions except the commission are concerned. the parliament's budget is the largest of the other institutions. the second stage will be the vote in march on a resolution with concrete estimates. in this crisis and in the face of the need to reduce our public expenditure, i supported the adoption of these guidelines which provide that, like the commission's administrative budget, the budget of the european parliament and the other institutions should be frozen, that is to say simply indexed to inflation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the guidelines for the 2013 budget. while i support the freezing of our institution's budget for 2013, i voted against the amendment which targets the european parliament's seat in strasbourg. two days earlier a report was presented which substantially corrected the erroneous but very often heard figures, raising the cost of the strasbourg seat from 169 to 203 million euros per year. the reality is quite different, according to the parliament's secretariat-general, the total specific costs of strasbourg are €51.5 million, or €10 cents per citizen per year. similarly, the estimated carbon footprint of 19 000 tonnes of co2 is four times higher than the actual figure of 4 199 tonnes. i note that my colleagues are not disarming on the subject of the siege of strasbourg and that this is a matter of politics rather than really budgetary or environmental issues. i think that if the european parliament is to have a single seat, it must of course be in strasbourg.
in writing. i fully support the motion for a resolution tabled by mrs maria do céu patrão neves which highlights the multifunctional nature of the fisheries sector. i have always fought for the cfp not to be conditioned solely by environmental concerns. because it gives life and structure to many territories, fishing is a key element in the production of public goods. it is the expression of know-how and culture and offers many opportunities, in particular to strengthen scientific knowledge and to ensure the development of coastal areas. it also has a structuring effect on the development of maritime areas. that is why i am in favour of the development of the public goods provided by fishing.
in writing. the fisheries and aquaculture sector generates €34.2 billion a year and employs more than 350 000 people in europe. environmental sustainability - improving the level of fish stocks - is a prerequisite for the economic and social sustainability of the sector. the reform of the common fisheries policy must therefore ensure that stocks are fished in a sustainable way to ensure the sustainability of the sector and the future of coastal communities. it must be ambitious and include clear, prioritized, measurable objectives and a timetable.
in writing. the resolution on 'the contribution of the common fisheries policy to the production of public goods' is a missed opportunity for the european parliament to take a clear position on the common fisheries policy. there are some positive aspects, but this is still very theoretical. the resolution calls for the establishment of a sustainable fisheries sector, food and employment security and the maintenance of vibrant fishing communities. the resolution also calls for the preservation of marine biodiversity, which is itself a public good, and for the recognition of the seas - which cover more than two thirds of the surface of our planet - as a resource that plays a crucial role in the reproduction of other natural resources. the resolution is deliberately vague and imprecise, whereas there is no shortage of issues on the common fisheries policy. i therefore abstained on that vote.

in writing. in the aftermath of the arab spring, as morocco makes significant democratic progress, it is essential that the eu fully supports it. in this sense, it was important not to abandon the agreement on reciprocal agricultural liberalization after lengthy negotiations. however, this agreement, as presented to us, raises many questions. unfortunately, parliament had no choice but to accept or reject this agreement, without being able to amend it. the resolution was therefore necessary, and although i would have liked it to go further - i am thinking particularly of the producers in the south-west - i supported it. in this text we stress the importance of small farmers taking advantage of the agreement; we are asking the commission to assess the impact of the agreement on european producers - this should have been done beforehand - (i supported the amendment stressing the need to compensate for the negative impact they might have, but unfortunately it was rejected). calls on the commission to promote the equivalence of measures and controls between morocco and the union in the field of environmental and food safety standards; we call on morocco to improve its water management.
in writing. under the new powers conferred on the european parliament by the lisbon treaty, we can only approve or reject the conclusion of a trade agreement, which does not allow us to change our position. the resolution, on which we voted at the same time as the protocol to the agreement, has precisely this function: to show that despite this limited possibility, we are studying all the implications and consequences once implemented. this resolution is balanced and summarises the different views of the stakeholders. it also stressed the benefits to both parties of the new liberalization: it consolidated the position of european exporters on the moroccan market while maintaining the mechanisms for protecting the most sensitive european products. that is why i supported it in plenary.
in writing. this agreement between morocco and the eu is questionable in many respects. i can only regret that we have to vote on it even though the impact study has not yet been published... nevertheless, since a decision had to be made, i chose to vote in favour. this is not a vote against french, greek, italian or spanish producers, it is a vote for the moroccans and for the coherence of the development policy we are trying to pursue. even though the arab spring has completely changed the situation in the countries of the southern shore of the mediterranean, we must now support the development of morocco. the agreement is far from perfect, and free trade agreements as such pose many problems. but morocco is our neighbour and we cannot promote the economic and democratic development of these countries if we completely deny them access to our markets.
in writing. i am pleased to note that the majority of meps have chosen, as i have, to continue to support and strengthen the eu-morocco ties and to support the transition to democracy following the arab spring. i am one of those who believe that this agricultural agreement will help alleviate economic, migration, and security problems. parliament took account of the many concerns raised by producers in southern europe. so there are safeguards, which have been required to moderate the increase in quotas for certain products, such as tomatoes, strawberries or cucumbers. the agreement also sets seasonal quotas to combat distortions on the eu market and recalls that moroccan imports should meet european health standards. it therefore called for strict monitoring of the application of quotas and for increased checks to prevent any alleged fraud in the entry price system. the european parliament also called for an assessment of the impact on the incomes of european producers and farmers.
in writing. i have decided to approve this agreement which follows the spirit of the specific association agreement signed in 2000. it is important to remember that the european union is engaged in a process of rapprochement with the southern shore of the mediterranean. this agreement is therefore more broadly in line with the logic of dialogue, which can legitimately be expected to have a beneficial effect on the economic development and democratic development of morocco, which has implemented considerable reforms. this agreement is balanced and respects the principle of complementarity of production (no overlapping of production periods). it also provides for a consultation mechanism in the event of a significant increase in european imports of fruit and vegetables. as regards european fishery products, i would like to stress that this agreement increases the possibilities for exports to morocco. it is also a positive signal to morocco after the non-renewal, against my wishes, of the fisheries agreement we had with that country.
in writing. after the unfortunate vote against the fisheries partnership agreement in december, a positive vote in favour of the agreement on reciprocal liberalisation measures for agricultural and fishery products was more than necessary. the agreement is a balanced agreement, which takes account of the specific features of the european and moroccan markets and contributes to our mutual prosperity. it is an essential tool, in particular, for the integration of moroccan 'small farming' into international trade. morocco is a country that must be supported in its stability, as the eu has committed itself to do. voting in favour of the agreement is to act in this direction and to reaffirm the solidity of the commercial, economic and political ties which unite us with morocco.
in writing. i know what the eu-morocco agreement means for this country. symbolically, while the arab spring changed the landscape in the southern mediterranean. economically, because agriculture represents a very important part of morocco's development, and employs up to 75% of the workforce in rural areas. however, i did not approve this text for at least two reasons. in substance, this agreement risks weakening the already exhausted fruit and vegetables sector without providing sufficient guarantees to limit distortions of competition. it is no longer acceptable that the european parliament should not have a say in the content of liberalisation agreements. we must be involved in the negotiations with third countries from the outset. to amend the texts, to improve their content, taking into account their impact on european producers, and to raise the level of requirements on moroccan production. finally, it is not acceptable that this agreement should be presented even though the results of the impact study on the economic, social and environmental consequences are not known. this way of doing things by the commission cannot continue.
in writing. the reforms initiated by the king of morocco, which are allowing a smooth development of this country, should certainly be welcomed and cooperation with this great country encouraged. but certainly not at the cost of a free trade agreement on agricultural products, a step towards morocco's participation in the european internal market, a very questionable objective. such an agreement would be devastating not only for european producers but also for moroccans, especially those who live on family and subsistence farming, whose importance and crucial role in the food security and independence of nations cannot be stressed enough. a free trade agreement, however far-reaching, is certainly a win-win for the big multinational corporations and the global financiers. it is always a loss for the peoples and the workers, ruined here and enslaved there.
in writing. morocco is a privileged and priority partner for the european union in our trade and must continue to be so. morocco and the eu have made significant progress in the areas of political dialogue, institutional relations and exchanges of views on bilateral and international issues. in agriculture, as in other areas, we must, however, demand reciprocity in accordance with european health and environmental standards. however, morocco does not currently meet these standards for a number of agricultural products, such as tomatoes. the agreement would therefore be likely to affect french and european fruit and vegetable production, which would be in a difficult competitive situation. that's why i abstained.
in writing. the issues related to the agreement between the european union and morocco on the reciprocal liberalisation of agricultural and fishery products have provoked strong reactions from our farmers, who fear that their activities will be undermined by unfair competition. i want to reassure them, the guarantees are there. in view of the sensitivity of this sector and morocco's offensive capacity, mechanisms for preserving the sector are in place. this includes the maintenance of quotas for the most sensitive products (tomatoes, cucumbers, strawberries, clementines, etc.) which will be subject to monthly management; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the price of fruit and vegetables is maintained. special provisions are also provided for tomatoes, a highly endangered product. the liberalisation granted by morocco also contributes to strengthening the position of european exporters on the moroccan market with immediate and almost total liberalisation of certain sectors. finally, this agreement seals a commitment made in 2008 when morocco obtained "advanced status". it reflects the eu's willingness to support the democratic and reform process in the country and to achieve a common economic area in the long term.
in writing. i voted in favour of the eu-morocco agreement on reciprocal liberalisation measures for agricultural and fishery products. i welcome the endorsement of this agreement by the european parliament. firstly, it will make it possible to strengthen the position of european exporters on the moroccan market while maintaining the protection mechanisms (quotas, entry price regimes) of the most sensitive european sectors, and in particular french ones, in particular the fruit and vegetable sector. above all, this balanced agreement is a very important step in the deepening of economic and trade relations between the eu and morocco: it accompanies the moroccan rural development policy, while representing an opportunity for european exporters. finally, by this vote, the european parliament is affirming its support for the courageous process of political democratisation and economic modernisation in which morocco has embarked.

in writing. i voted in favour of approving this protocol to the eu-morocco agreement as it represents a step forward in the union's policy towards the countries of the southern mediterranean, particularly in the context of the arab spring. it is an essential component of the convergence of values and economies towards a common euro-mediterranean economic area and should benefit all moroccan farmers. in addition, this protocol embodies the advanced status which morocco and the european union agreed to in principle in october 2008, and marks an important intermediate step before the launch of negotiations for a comprehensive and in-depth free trade agreement, currently under consideration. finally, it consolidates the position of european exporters on the moroccan market, while maintaining the mechanisms for protecting the most sensitive european products. so it is ultimately a protocol which will produce balanced effects for both sides, and that is why i supported it.
