in writing. we vote against this resolution. we can only see the serious impasse in which syria finds itself. the plight of the syrian people under the regime of bashar al-assad and the brutal repression are terrible. we condemn this regime and its policies. but we must find another way than the one presented in this resolution. indeed, paragraphs 15 and 18 are part of the strategy recently defined by the arab league for sending a "force" to syria. the deployment of such a force without the agreement of all the actors, including the syrian authorities, is impossible without military intervention. the syrian government, like the democrats and progressives in that country, rejected this proposal. the european parliament would be committing itself to supporting a very dangerous political-military escalation if it adopted a more ambiguous formulation. we are back to the situation of a few weeks ago, when france had already proposed humanitarian corridors and turkey a no-fly zone. it is still the pressure for military intervention, implicit pressure and in language that masks the risks of an all-out civil war in the country and foreign occupation.
in writing. this text condemns in the strongest terms the brutal repression of the syrian people by the regime of bashar al-assad. he demands the immediate resignation of the regime. it calls for the opening of borders to humanitarian aid, human rights organisations and journalists. in that sense, i support it. but the text calls on mrs ashton to negotiate with turkey, the arab league and the syrian opposition on the modalities of setting up humanitarian corridors on the syrian-turkish border. the humanitarian corridors involve sending military forces to protect them. it is inconceivable that such negotiations should take place in any other framework than that of the un. this text is free from that obligation. binding clauses preventing the risk of military escalation must be clearly and explicitly guaranteed. nothing of the kind is required here. i am voting against this motion of censure.
in writing. according to the un office for the coordination of humanitarian affairs, 1.5 million syrians need international food aid. the consequences of the repression affect the living conditions of nearly 3 million syrians. there are more than 5,400 dead and more than 15,000 refugees, mainly in turkey. in the face of the syrian people's revolt, the repression led by syrian president bashar al-assad continues without the international community being able to intervene because russia and china are preventing any action by the un security council. this intolerable situation must end, and i call on the high representative for foreign affairs and security policy to do everything possible to ensure that a un security council resolution is adopted, in cooperation with russia and china. these are the reasons why i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in syria.
in writing. the european union, which has been a guarantor of the fundamental rights of its citizens for several decades, must build on its experience and continue to extend its fight to the rest of the world. to do this, it must assume its role as a global actor and seize the opportunities offered by multilateral organizations with one hand. in the field of human rights, the adoption of binding standards is the key to rapid progress and concrete improvement on the ground. however, international bodies do not always agree on procedures quickly enough. it is therefore imperative that the european union and its member states join forces in a specialised intergovernmental platform: the united nations human rights council. the institution, which will meet for the 19th time from 27 february to 23 march, shares our universal vision of human rights and puts on the agenda priority issues such as the current human rights situation in syria. the european parliament adopted this resolution to show its interest in the work of the united nations human rights council and its willingness to establish closer cooperation with this institution.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the nineteenth session of the human rights council because i welcome the increased integration of human rights in the work of the united nations, as evidenced by the increasing number of interventions by the office of the united nations high commissioner for human rights in the security council. the question of respect for human rights must not be subordinated to political or commercial considerations but must be regarded as a central element of the european union's foreign policy. i would also like to stress that i voted in favour of keeping in this text the reference to the tangible and sustainable implementation of the un high commissioner's resolution on sexual orientation and gender identity.
in writing. "the hunger for books"... is the phrase used to describe the situation of many blind or dyslexic citizens who are prevented from reading. 95% of publications are never converted into 'accessible formats', such as braille, large print or audio recording. the petition initiated by the european union of the blind (eub) and the dyslexics association (eda) was followed by an oral question in plenary on wednesday 15 february and a resolution on thursday 16 february. in view of this appalling situation, i have spontaneously supported this resolution. if publishers do not publish enough books in special formats for blind and partially sighted people, we must be able to force book publishers to do so. the time for non-binding recommendations must be over in favour of our commitment to produce a legally binding text to re-establish this manifest discrimination against access to reading.
in writing. the resolution we have just adopted unanimously is a reminder of how difficult access to culture can be for blind people. literature is a perfect example of this. we must support all initiatives based on new technologies, particularly those aimed at making books more accessible to the blind. promoting the publication of books in braille with lower copyright costs would allow younger people to have books in their hands, to facilitate their learning of braille, but it is also necessary and above all to optimize the solutions offered by new technologies with digital books. why not also offer a discounted download card for the visually impaired, blind or illiterate? more than an international treaty, we need a genuine political will on the part of the member states to take measures to facilitate the production and exchange of braille and audiobooks.
in writing. only 5% of books are currently accessible to the visually impaired. indeed, 95% of all published works are never converted into accessible formats such as braille, large print or audio recording. the world intellectual property organization (wipo) is considering an international treaty to improve access to books for the blind and other visually impaired which would introduce a specific exception to copyright rules and increase the number of braille publications. but the commission and the council have consistently opposed a legally binding text, preferring recommendations on a voluntary basis. the european parliament would like to point out that it is the duty of the european union not to stigmatise a section of the population suffering from a particular disability. the states must therefore decide in favour of such a treaty.
in writing. less than 5% of books are now accessible to blind, visually impaired and reading disabled people in europe and less than 1% in the rest of the world, or what is called a real 'book famine' for these people who are deprived of their right to access culture. negotiations are currently under way within the world intellectual property organization to establish an international treaty on limitations and exceptions to copyright, in order to facilitate the cross-border circulation of books available in accessible formats, negotiations which are currently blocked. i therefore voted resolutely in favour of this resolution, which seeks to unblock the situation, in order to guarantee the fundamental right of access to culture for these people. copyright laws should not, in this specific case, constitute a discriminatory barrier to access to cultural products by such persons.
in writing. 95% of all published works are never converted into formats accessible to blind, visually impaired and dyslexic people. unfortunately, to date there is no international legal standard allowing a specific copyright exception for the transnational distribution of publications adapted to people living with a reading disability. that is why i voted for this resolution, so that the council and the commission can vote in favour of a legally binding international treaty to facilitate access to books for those affected by this shortage of books. this resolution follows a petition by the world blind union, the european blind union and the british institute of blind people.
in writing. parliament voted in favour of making books available to blind and partially sighted people. what could be more natural than to be able to read any book at any time. however, persons who are blind or visually impaired do not always have access to books in accessible formats (braille, large print, or audio). there is a legal constraint which prevents the transnational distribution of publications adapted to people with reading disabilities. the european parliament wanted to point out this inconsistency and called on the commission and the council to support any initiative by the world intellectual property organisation which would facilitate this public so that culture is truly accessible to all.
in writing. blind and partially sighted persons have limited access to books and other printed material. as many as 95% of publications are never converted to 'accessible formats', such as braille, large print or audio recording. i supported the adoption of this european parliament resolution calling on the council of the european union and the european commission to vote in favour of a world property organisation treaty providing for derogations from intellectual property law in order to enable blind and partially sighted people to no longer be discriminated against in access to culture.
in writing. the petition is an essential democratic tool which allows any european citizen to engage in direct dialogue with the politicians who represent him or her and to ask them questions on issues of concern to him or her. it is vital to take this into account and to react to it. in this case, the petition reminded us of the lack of measures to make books accessible to the blind and visually impaired. their disability must not condemn them to having access to only 5% of the books and publications, and thus limit their access to culture, training and openness. to this end, the draft international treaty to improve access to books for the blind and other visually impaired of the world intellectual property organization must be supported and ratified by the european union. on such an important subject, which affects the rights of many european citizens, a binding legal standard is essential to allow a specific copyright exception for the transnational distribution of publications adapted to the visually impaired.
in writing. the associations of the visually impaired confirm that at present, in the european union, the blind and visually impaired have very limited access to books and other printed publications. the number of titles available in adapted formats remains woefully inadequate, as 95% of publications are never converted to "accessible formats" - audiobooks, large type, or braille - for copyright reasons. however, restricting free access to publications has important cultural and social consequences. it also has a negative impact on the empowerment and independence of the visually impaired. since non-binding recommendations have not been sufficient (and if national exceptions exist, they stop at borders), it is time to consider exceptions or limitations to copyright in favour of the transnational distribution of publications adapted to people with reading disabilities. in this context, we must demand that the council and the commission vote in favour of a legally binding wipo (world intellectual property organization) treaty to facilitate trade in adapted works. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which is a strong signal in that direction.
in writing. within the european union, 95% of publications are not made accessible to the visually impaired (braille, audio format), mainly for copyright issues, an essential point of our community legislation. it is essential to remember that access to culture, education and participation in society are also rights to be guaranteed to european citizens, whether they have full visual capabilities or not. the world intellectual property organization (wipo), which is at the forefront of this field, is already considering an international treaty to facilitate access to books for the blind and visually impaired. europe is responding cautiously, if not frivolously, by issuing only non-binding recommendations. the resolution i supported in plenary calls on the council and the commission to vote in favour of the legally binding wipo draft treaty which would bring about a major improvement in the lives of blind people of all ages.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution. against the wishes of the council and the commission, the vast majority of meps voted in favour of a legally binding international treaty within the wipo framework establishing exceptions to copyright to allow wider access to culture and the written word for the blind, to broaden the cultural and creative media for the blind and to facilitate exchanges between countries, taking account of technological advances in this field. most books are never converted into a format accessible to the blind, mainly for copyright reasons. with this vote we are asking the union to adopt a clear strategy on this matter and to take action to put an end to discrimination against the blind. with this vote, we want to come to the side of our fellow citizens living with this disability and put an end to their "hunger for books".
in writing. it is essential that the countries of the southern mediterranean feel fully included in a euro-mediterranean economic area. the new convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin is a step in this direction. the 'preferential origin' system allows certain goods to benefit from reduced customs duties when they enter the european market. the convention will also harmonise more than 100 preferential rules of origin already contained in bilateral agreements between the eu and mediterranean countries. this single and simplified instrument will stimulate the development of south-south trade and thus contribute to economic growth, social integration and democratisation in the region.
in writing. this resolution rightly points to the problem of companies taking advantage of the eu-israel agreement to export products from the territories occupied by israel. it is concerned that the text may facilitate or encourage this type of practice which encourages the spirit of force majeure and contempt for conventionally given speech. it denounces the fact that the agreement does not provide for a dispute settlement mechanism. it also denounces the fact that the convention does not provide for revision or review. despite all this, its authors are in favour of the convention. that's not consistent! i therefore vote against this inconsistency, but i support the denunciations and the request to create a blacklist of israeli companies which deliberately violate the spirit of the eu provisions by abusing the export of products from the occupied territories.
in writing. the barcelona process, launched in 1995 and transformed into the union for the mediterranean under the french presidency of the european union in 2008, aims to create a common area of peace and stability between europe and the mediterranean countries surrounding it. on the economic front, this union must make it possible to establish a free trade area. it's been on standby for many years. the arab spring, supported by the european parliament, has shown the need to revive this objective, which the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin intends to address. i therefore voted in favour of the menéndez del valle report.
in writing. we have just approved the conclusion of the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin. this convention is an important step forward because the simplifications it entails will have a positive impact on facilitating trade and the economic and social integration of the countries of the region. any measure to promote the development of relations between the countries of the region should be supported. hence the importance of facilitating the use of the system of cumulation of origin and ultimately strengthening north-south and south-south trade, and of extending the system of preferential rules of origin to other neighbourhood countries.
in writing. i supported the adoption of the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin, which will strengthen north-south and south-south trade. i support the resolution tabled on the initiative of the rapporteur, mr menendez del valle, who points out that this convention is of major political importance in the current context of democratic transition on the southern shore of the mediterranean. i welcome the establishment of a pan-euro-mediterranean system of cumulation of origin which clarifies the rules in force until now and contributes to the achievement of the commission's objective of 'shared prosperity'. i hope that this convention will be implemented quickly so that we can start to move towards the countries with which we already have free trade agreements.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin because it is a step towards the creation of a free trade area in the mediterranean, in line with the proposals made by the french head of state.
in writing. i am against the establishment of the euro-mediterranean free trade area envisaged by the barcelona process. the convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin, which we are here being asked to approve, is intended to speed up its implementation. it even allows for a wider geographical scope. moreover, the agreement does not guarantee the cessation of imports of products from the occupied territories and in so doing encourages the spirit of coup de force which prevails in the present government of israel. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted against the european parliament's position in support of the council conclusions on the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin in trade. the report points to a number of real problems in trade between the eu and the rest of the mediterranean, including the preferential treatment accorded to israel for selling products from the occupied territories. i do not think, however, that the text goes far enough in terms of equal treatment between all the partners. the difference in treatment with regard to palestine is still to be applied when it is decided to simply freeze the agreements. such a difference in treatment is intolerable for a european union which claims to give lessons to the whole world in the field of democracy and human rights. i would venture to add that even from a purely liberal point of view, it is not relevant, since according to their great principles, equality in trade should be the rule. they don't even respect the basics of their ideology, or more precisely, as always, we choose the rules according to the interests at stake.

in writing. in its communication of june 2011 on the community budget, the european commission proposed to finance the european earth monitoring programme (gmes) outside the budget, on the model of the european development fund (edf). it is an unlikely proposition, which jeopardizes the future of a promising sector. the european parliament recalled this in its resolutions of 19 january and 16 february, as did many member states, including france, germany and the united kingdom. gmes is a major programme for the future, but the commission considers that the union does not have the means to support programmes of such a scale. but gmes is a symbol. it embodies the member states' willingness to invest together in a european project. what are the consequences for employment and competitiveness if this programme is financed from the community budget? what is the impact of the sentinels satellites planned for launching in 2013? what are the consequences for our smes, which will not be able to invest without the certainty of having access to gmes data? what is the impact on the union's international standing? these are all issues that require ambitious responses and not half measures.
in writing. the european global monitoring for environment and security (gmes) programme provides state-of-the-art services - the most advanced in the world today - in the fields of environment, civil protection, crisis management and mobility, via databases. it also provides an effective framework for stimulating innovation. last june, the european commission proposed in its financial perspective to exclude this programme from the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, preferring to leave it to the discretion of national funding. some of us had warned the european executive of the dangers of such a decision in the beginning of 2011. our main arguments have been taken up by this resolution: the risk of making financial aid unstable, of losing its european dimension and the investments already made, of creating disparities in terms of access to information and the benefits of this programme, etc. i have therefore signed this resolution to call for the reintegration of gmes into the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 because it is unacceptable to jeopardise such an important programme, which is considered to be one of the two flagship european space initiatives along with galileo, and at a time when it is beginning to bear fruit.

asked. this is just one more factor in the accelerating rate of disasters in the world. who does not remember the earthquake in haiti and the deepwater oil disaster? the european union reacted nuclear safety risk assessment of all power plants in the european union. the european commission was invited to review the june 2009 nuclear safety directive and the programme was set up. today all research. i welcome the commission's proposals in this respect, extending the euratom research programme for two years. we cannot solve our energy and competitiveness problems, our social comfort and global warming without addressing all the issues that are necessary for the operation of nuclear power stations around the world, including maximum safety.

president of the european council. − mr president, honourable members, the meeting of the european council on 1 and 2 march was positive and not overshadowed by an immediate crisis. but, there can be no complacency in facing the enormous economic challenges that still remain before us. sustained effort on several fronts remains necessary. one front is fiscal consolidation. another is the growth and employment agenda. some claim that these two are contradictory. it is our job to make sure that they are not. since the 1930s the main response to an economic downturn has been a fiscal stimulus: deliberate deficit spending by governments to boost demand. indeed, in 2008 a coordinated fiscal stimulus was agreed, which undoubtedly helped in the short term. however, the ability to use this instrument is limited in most member states, because of their already excessive debt levels. what had been a solution became a problem. the reasons behind the debt problem are diverse. in most cases, it is not because of gross profligacy in public spending. in some, it is because of large banking sectors, insufficiently supervised, which collapsed and had to be rescued by the taxpayer. in some others, economic growth, fuelled by asset bubbles, artificially boosted budget revenues which quickly collapsed, with the crisis increasing budget deficits and debt. but for several, it is because debt levels have accumulated gradually over time, leaving most member states with debts well over the agreed maximum of 60% of gdp. they applied keynesianism asymmetrically: deficits during a slowdown were rarely eliminated during peaks – let alone replaced by surpluses. they were left with no safety margin when the crisis hit. that is why the rules agreed in the new treaty on stability, coordination and governance, which was signed on the occasion of this european council, are so important. they do not prevent countercyclical deficits as long as the structural deficit over the economic cycle is balanced, or at least remains very small. nor do they limit public expenditure: they simply provide that this must not be financed by excessive borrowing. the european council stated that all member states should continue to respect their commitments under the stability and growth pact, which has been strongly reinforced by the six-pack. but at the same time, the focus on consolidation, especially in the short term, must go hand in hand with further efforts to secure economic growth and improve employment prospects. how to do this was the focus of both the european council, in the context of the european semester, and, as i reported to you already, the one in january. we approached the question from many angles. making sure that, at the same time as we bring budgets under control, we keep investing in our future, in education, in research and development, in innovation. stimulating investment. looking closely at expenditure. making assistance to the unemployed more pro-active. looking at revenues, for instance by tackling tax evasion and tax fraud. exploiting to the full the single market, especially the services and digital markets, as emphasised again in a letter by 12 colleagues. reducing the tax burden on labour, especially on low-income earners. increasing trade. opening sheltered sectors, such as professional services and retail. improving the business environment, cutting red tape and paperwork thanks to digital public administration. in short, making the right choices for jobs and growth in the midst of fiscal consolidation.all this will be monitored by the institutions. as you know, the semester is our annual policy coordination tool, running from the release of the commission’s annual growth survey to the june european council, which will adopt country-specific recommendations, a key moment in the semester. of course, some of the supply-side measures take time to have an effect, whereas fiscal consolidation has a more immediate dampening effect on demand. but we may be able to avoid an overall contraction in credit and i hope the banks will take advantage of the ample liquidity support provided by the european central bank to pass on some of these resources to businesses and households. the action taken by governments and the ecb is also helping to stabilise sovereign debt markets in the countries under pressure. it is crucial for countries also not to relent in their efforts and to stick to their commitments under the stability and growth pact and the new fiscal stability treaty. alongside this monetary policy, the overall policy of restoring confidence in the euro area at different levels will contribute to restored confidence by consumers and investors and will in that way contribute to growth and jobs. our strategy is starting to work. we have reached a turning point in the crisis while being fully aware of the remaining vulnerabilities. we need a short- and a longer-term strategy for growth. the latter is embodied in the europe 2020 strategy, now also closely monitored in the semester, but we also need a specific employment policy, especially for young people. even if the main responsibility lies with the member states, the union can give guidance, as we have done in the european council conclusions. we look forward to the commission’s forthcoming ‘employment package’ to take this work further. we also talked about the situation in greece and we welcomed the progress made on the new greek programme. the aim is to put the greek economy back on a sustainable footing, both in terms of debt sustainability and competitiveness. euro area leaders support the efforts undertaken by greece. and may i just underline, for those who claim that the european union is ‘imposing’ austerity on greece, that, in fact, euro area countries and the imf are providing another eur 130 billion, on top of the first package of eur 110 billion, of long-term low-interest loans to greece, and helped it to secure a write-down of 70 % of the net present value of its debts to private banks. overall support to greece represents more than 100 % of its gdp. without all this, greece’s situation, difficult as it is, would be far, far worse. but we also need a strong growth agenda for greece mobilising european funds, foreign investments and maximising the growth potential of the greek economy. the commission was asked to step up its technical assistance to greece to achieve this. euro area leaders also confirmed their commitment to reassess the adequacy of the overall ceiling of the efsf/esm firewall by the end of the month, via the euro group. in addition, they agreed to accelerate the payments of the paid-in capital for the esm. during this european council, we had a wide range of other issues to discuss also. on serbia: we agreed to grant it the status of eu candidate. this is a remarkable achievement – a result of the efforts demonstrated by both sides in the dialogue between belgrade and pristina. i hope it will encourage serbia to undertake further efforts in order to meet the political and economic criteria for eu membership and to continue to support regional cooperation and good neighbourly relations in the western balkans. we expect further normalisation of relations between belgrade and pristina. on the accession of bulgaria and romania to the schengen area: we have asked the jha council to adopt its decision in september and, in the meantime, to identify and implement safeguarding measures aimed at contributing to the success of the process. on syria: facing an appalling situation, we focused on three key aspects of this crisis. on the humanitarian side we called for an immediate end to the violence against civilians and human rights abuses, making it clear that those responsible for atrocities will be held accountable. we also called for humanitarian agencies to have unhindered access – the eu has already mobilised humanitarian funding. on the political side we confirmed the eu’s commitment to further increase the pressure on the syrian regime, and invited the council to prepare further targeted restrictive measures. we called on president assad to step aside. as soon as a democratic transition begins, we are ready to develop a new partnership and provide assistance. on the diplomatic front, we supported the efforts by the arab league, the mission undertaken by kofi annan and the launching of the group of the friends of the syrian people. we also called on all members of the un security council, particularly russia and china, to work together in an effort to stop the violence. let us not forget that we cannot act decisively without a un mandate. this view was unanimously supported. evidence, i remind you, that there is more common foreign policy than some think. we have a common position on iran, on syria, on libya, on the southern neighbourhood and so on. in other words, in the world’s most dangerous region, the 27 are working hand in hand. this is a fact often overlooked. finally, i was honoured that all 27 heads of state or government of the european council decided to ask me to continue as their president for another two-and-a-half years. furthermore, 17 of them, from the euro area countries, also asked me to chair the euro summit meetings. looking forward, it will not come as a surprise that my first priority will remain the economy. it is our lifeline. we need a strong economic base to preserve our social models, to achieve high levels of employment, including for the younger generation, and it is the only way to play a role on the world stage equal to our potential. it is a privilege to continue the work in this decisive moment for europe.
president of the european commission. − mr president, president of the european council, distinguished members of parliament. first, while i have already congratulated president van rompuy on his reappointment, i would like in this chamber to reiterate my thanks and appreciation for the work that he has carried out over the last two-and-a-half years. i look forward to continuing to work with him to build a stronger european union – stronger in defence of the interests of our citizens and also stronger in the world. the president of the european council has already outlined the main outcomes of this summit, including the important discussions we had on external relations issues – namely the situation in syria and relations with iran and of course the very important decision to grant candidate status to serbia. on my side i would like to highlight a few elements that demonstrate that the european union may be turning the corner towards renewed stability and growth. let us be clear; there is now less tension regarding the euro area, but we are not yet out of the crisis. the situation remains fragile and we have to complete our work, including the reinforcement of the firewalls. these are an indispensable counterpart of our reinforced economic governance. as i have said before in this parliament, i expect heads of state and government to focus not just on short-term crisis management, but also on growth: smart, sustainable, inclusive growth, which is the key to job creation and the future prosperity of europe. this was, and remains, the first objective of the europe 2020 strategy and is at the centre of the comprehensive approach behind the roadmap to stability and growth which i presented in this parliament last october. this approach is now gaining support and this european council was a step in the right direction, although a lot remains to be done. at this summit, progress was achieved concerning key elements of this comprehensive approach: first, an agreement for a response to the problems in greece; secondly, financial stability; and thirdly, job-creating growth through our europe 2020 agenda, namely through concrete initiatives frontloading targeted investment. let me start with greece. some people continue to say that greece will not make it. i ask why? why should greece not be able to carry out the necessary reforms for its competitiveness? i believe it is possible. the greek government and the greek parliament believe it is possible. the decision on psi shows that it can be possible. the priority now is to make the second programme work. this is our collective task, supporting the greek authorities and the greek people. to that end, the commission is already taking concrete steps. together with those commissioners most closely involved, i have had very concrete talks with prime minister papademos and his team about getting key growth-enhancing decisions taken immediately. as you will have seen from my letter, we have agreed to concentrate on a number of key priorities: improving youth employment, promoting a more business-friendly environment, providing liquidity to smes and sweeping away barriers to the absorption of structural funds. these are all areas where we can make real progress in weeks, not months or years. the commission task force under horst reichenbach is currently on the ground discussing how to put these measures into practice with the greek government. finally, just yesterday i held a meeting with president hoyer of the european investment bank to examine how our support for greece can be made more effective. to cement this approach i intend in the coming weeks to present, together with vice-president rehn, a communication on growth and jobs for greece, taking stock of the progress that has been made and setting out the top priorities for the future. as i set out in the roadmap to stability and growth, finding a lasting solution to the problems in greece is an essential prerequisite for stability. without stability there is no confidence and without confidence we will not get growth and jobs. the signature of the treaty on stability, coordination and growth was a further sign of the commitment to discipline and convergence. this, as you know, was not the commission’s preferred mechanism due to its intergovernmental nature. however, its signature – not only by euro area countries, but by 25 out of the current 27 member states – is a political statement that the euro is not just the currency of some countries but of the european union. it is a strong political message about the irreversibility of the euro, and it was very well received by investors in europe and outside europe. it is the very culture of financial stability that is a condition for a true economic union. together with the six-pack and the european stability mechanism, it is an important step in this process. it is therefore vital that all its appropriate provisions can be brought into line with european union law as soon as possible. the contracting member states have agreed to integrate the provisions of the treaty into european union law within five years. already the commission has proposed further amendments to the ‘two-pack’ to make sure that important provisions of the fiscal compact are implemented under community law: that means also with the active participation of this parliament. naturally this agreement could not – and perhaps it should not – cover all the elements of an economic union and its most pressing objectives like the internal market or economic, social and territorial cohesion. these objectives are indeed better pursued, from a community perspective, in the framework of the existing treaties, and through the european institutions and the community method. implementing the europe 2020 agenda for growth and jobs dominated our agenda at the european council. financial stability is indispensable but it is not sufficient. as we said several times, we need financial stability and economic growth: the one and the other. as the roadmap made clear, there are a number of elements towards growth that must be implemented at the same time. these include, among others, structural reforms, deepening of the single market, targeted investment – yes, we need investment – and boosting trade with foreign markets. on these points, i made clear to the european council that member states must do more to close the implementation gap between political will and decisions taken on the ground. i made it clear that it was not sufficient to talk about europe 2020 only in brussels in the justus lipsius building but that we need to own this strategy at all levels, including the social partners, the regions, and our societies. i also made clear that we need a perspective of social inclusion because there are some situations of social emergency, and indeed rising poverty, in many of our member states. i made a point that structural reform must be politically, but also socially acceptable to our citizens. social dialogue is vital in this respect; that is why i place such importance on the tripartite social summit at european level, and social dialogue between employers and unions at national level. this is one element in demonstrating that the path we are taking is a fair one, where the burden and the benefits are both shared. fairness was a key motivation behind the commission’s proposal for a financial transaction tax last year. more broadly, the last three european councils have highlighted taxation as a fundamental component in our recovery efforts. this should not be a surprise. recent figures indicate that as much as eur 1 trillion is lost every year in the european union through tax evasion and avoidance. compare this eur 1 trillion to what is needed to consolidate national budgets, and you can imagine that many problems could be solved. a strong, unified stance is the only way forward to tackle the issue. the commission is working on concrete measures to toughen our stance against tax evasion and fraud but member states have an important duty to fulfil at european level too. there is no reason for any further delay on adopting the revised savings directive and the negotiating mandates for tax agreements with third countries. this is blocked, as you know, at council level. this is another negative example of the implementation gap i mentioned earlier: positions that are taken at the european council but are not afterwards followed up by the council or by the member states. i have said that the programme for achieving growth is europe 2020 and the instrument to achieve it is the multiannual financial framework. the european budget is a budget for investment; i hope that it will be in this perspective that we will have constructive discussions with the member states about it, and i am pleased to see that the european parliament has taken that position. i am also pleased that commission proposals on project bonds for infrastructure development and the roll-out of broadband were accepted at this european council. together with other priority actions, such as accelerating some initiatives under the annual growth survey and completing the single market, these measures will create jobs in the short term and make the european economy more competitive in the longer term. our citizens want to see real action that will make a difference to their daily lives. since the informal european council at the end of january, the commission has been taking this action with regard to slashing youth unemployment and providing support to smes. smes are the answer to the need to create more jobs in europe. commission teams have visited eight member states since then. in almost every case, in close cooperation with the national administrations, they found ways of helping to get more young people into work. let me close by reiterating that we have now come a long way in creating more stable conditions which will enable us to do the bulk of the work still before us. what we need is not constant drama about the euro, but hard work and determination in our action to sustain the european social market economy. no, the european social model is not dead. but in a more challenging environment, we need a more competitive europe that delivers stability and growth through responsibility and solidarity.

in writing. i voted in favour of the agreement between the eu, iceland and norway on the application of the convention of 29 may 2000. the provisions of the agreement are intended to strengthen judicial cooperation in criminal matters between the two countries. they concern both the hearing of witnesses and the sharing of information. this agreement, which is concluded between the member states, requires the approval of the european parliament under the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. in 2002, negotiations on mutual legal assistance agreements between the european union and our neighbours, norway and iceland, were launched. at the last plenary session, i voted in favour of an agreement to improve this judicial cooperation. as the rapporteur, mr claude moraes, has said, these include provisions on the hearing of witnesses, experts and prosecuted persons by telephone or videoconference, controlled deliveries, discreet investigations and joint investigation teams, and requests for information on banking transactions, bank accounts and their monitoring in order to combat crime in general and organised crime in particular. strengthening cooperation with our neighbours also involves exchanging information for our security. i fully endorse the progress made in this report.

in writing. the convention of 29 may 2000 on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the european union has facilitated mutual assistance between judicial, police and customs authorities. the purpose of the text, which i voted for, is to extend a significant part of this international agreement to relations with iceland and norway. it contains provisions on the hearing of witnesses, the setting up of joint investigation teams and requests for information on banking transactions and bank accounts. i am convinced that this agreement will make it possible to combat crossborder crime more effectively and will strengthen cooperation between these two countries and the european union.

in writing. the current system of crossborder successions in europe faces many obstacles. differences between member states in the law of succession create legal uncertainty for european citizens. what is the law applicable where the deceased person's will concerns heirs of different nationalities? in a europe where the free movement of persons is a fundamental principle, such a question cannot remain unanswered. that is why i voted in favour of clarifying the legal rules on this matter and introducing a european certificate of succession.
in writing. this new regulation on cross-border successions will avoid legal conflicts and lengthy succession settlement procedures in the future when the laws of several eu countries apply. today we travel, study and live in several countries of the european union and intermarriage is, in fact, on the increase. the aim is therefore to promote the free movement of citizens and to strengthen the internal market. i therefore voted in favour of the creation of the european certificate of succession, which will enable heirs to prove their status as heirs or the assignment of a specific property. i welcome the adoption of this text, which simplifies the lives of europeans and shows that the european union also cares about the daily lives of its citizens.
in writing. we have just taken a further step towards making life easier for european citizens by adopting this report. in the context of inheritance within the eu we know of court-based systems of settlement of inheritance, where the passage before the judge is mandatory, and non-court systems where the settlement of the inheritance is carried out by the notary. it was therefore important to obtain the principle of circulation of authentic instruments and thus to have them recognised in another member state, which was not the case until now. the adopted regulation also introduces a european certificate of succession (cse) to be used by heirs and legatees with direct rights in the succession to prove specific elements, such as the status of heir or the assignment of specific property. finally, we have succeeded in ensuring that heirs, who are nationals of a member state which applies the mechanism of the estate reserve intended to protect a portion of the estate for the deceased's children, can claim it in the event of an international succession.
in writing. i agree with the rapporteur, kurt lechner, who stresses the need to simplify and harmonise the rules on succession in the member states. the purpose of this regulation is to facilitate the administrative procedures of european citizens in matters of succession and to guarantee the rights of heirs and legatees. within the european union there are judicial and non-judicial systems for the settlement of successions. i am glad that the competence of notaries has been preserved. one paragraph provides for universal jurisdiction for notaries which will ensure that, when all the heirs agree to settle their succession amicably, the competent court will have to close the proceedings so that the notary can settle the succession.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text on the creation of a european certificate of succession because it will harmonise the rules of succession in europe and avoid litigation and lengthy procedures to settle successions where the laws of several eu countries are likely to apply. it is not right that in the age of the single market and european mobility, the law of heirs and legatees is not better regulated and that our fellow citizens faced with the difficult question of succession cannot benefit from legal certainty and predictability of the law allowing them to benefit from the best advantages for the transmission of their heritage.
in writing. the european parliament approved at its march 2012 plenary session the compromise text negotiated with the council of the european union on 'succession' which marks three years of work and discussion. this text recognises the principle of the circulation of authentic instruments, which means that a document has the same evidentiary effects (content, date) in a member state as in the member state of issue. above all, it recognises the universal jurisdiction of notaries despite the diversity of succession systems within the european union, which should ensure greater efficiency between systems. among other notable developments, the text introduces the european certificate of succession (cse) to facilitate the rapid settlement of international successions. with this certificate, heirs and legatees can assert their direct rights in the estate. finally, the principle of reservation of inheritance, which is not recognised in all member states, is preserved.
in writing. i supported the lechner report, which is a real step forward in the matter of succession for the european union. the lechner report, which has been compromised, advocates the principles of the circulation of authentic instruments and the protection of the hereditary deposit. it also allows the creation of a european certificate of succession for use by heirs and legatees with direct rights in the succession. finally, in order to safeguard the powers of notaries, the report expressly provides for their universal jurisdiction.
in writing. the free movement of people within the european union is one of the greatest achievements of european integration. however, the wide diversity of rules on succession between the different member states constitutes a barrier to this freedom of movement and creates legal uncertainty. i voted in favour of this text, which is intended to avoid legal conflicts in the case of successions where the law of several countries might apply. the regulation will enable citizens to decide, on the basis of specific criteria, which eu country's law they wish to apply to their inheritance. the text also provides for the creation of a model "certificate of succession" common to the member states which will help heirs to prove their rights in any member state.
in writing. i wished to support the report by mr lechner on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of judgments and authentic instruments in matters of succession and the creation of a european certificate of succession. it had become necessary to adapt to changes in society, in this case the steady increase in mixed marriages within the european union and the legal problems this can pose. the report therefore supports the creation of a european certificate of succession to simplify notarial procedures in crossborder successions. this will make it easier for heirs to be recognised as heirs across borders. it is a further step for the europe of citizens and proves that europe offers concrete solutions to enhance mobility within the european internal market.
in writing. it took three years of work to reach a compromise text between our institutions. this text, which i supported, should facilitate succession and avoid conflicts when a person dies leaving a will involving the legal systems of several member states. it should be noted that crossborder successions still account for 10% of all inheritances in the eu. the new system, which will enter into force in 2015, will speed up procedures and reduce red tape for heirs by introducing harmonised criteria on the national law applicable to wills where the succession concerns more than one member state (the default rule will be that of the last residence of the testator). it will also introduce the possibility for people living abroad to choose, when drawing up their will, their country of origin as the applicable law reference. finally, it is worth noting the creation of a european certificate of succession, designed to clarify the legal position of persons drawing up a will, and to help heirs and creditors to prove their status and safeguard their rights in the union. one regret: the british and irish opt-outs, plus the non-application in denmark, will reduce the impact of the text on the ground.
in writing. europe continues to work, even at the height of the crisis, to make life easier for its 500 million citizens. parliament today approved an important text which aims to facilitate the settlement of crossborder successions and to avoid conflicts when a person dies leaving a will involving the legal systems of several member states. according to some studies, this type of inheritance represents 10% of all inheritances in the union and would involve an amount of eur 123 billion. it took more than three years of discussions to reach agreement on this extremely sensitive subject for the member states. the new regulation will now enable a spanish citizen living in france to decide whether his heirs will inherit under french or spanish law, thus avoiding the costly procedures that would have resulted from previous legal uncertainties. in the absence of a specific will by the deceased, the law of the country of residence shall apply. this simplification concerns us all and reflects a europe of free movement, which acts, coordinates and protects.

in writing. almost 13 years after its launch and now implemented in 47 states, the bologna process, which aims to increase the attractiveness of european higher education and increase student mobility through the creation of a european higher education area, is generally a success, although mutual recognition of degrees is sometimes difficult and the rate of mobility remains relatively low. despite the large-scale reforms already undertaken, further progress is still needed. that is why i voted in favour of the berlinguer report, which calls for a rapid consolidation of this process, including greater harmonisation of university standards, improved recognition of diplomas throughout the union and increased student mobility. it is not enough to decree it, we must also provide the means! it is therefore clear that to achieve this, european universities necessarily need a greater contribution from the european institutions and a stronger will from the member states.
in writing. i share the rapporteur's view that the process which the european union embarked upon following the bologna conference in june 1999 needs to be consolidated. two aspects attract my attention: student mobility and the recognition of diplomas in the various member states. they help to facilitate the occupational integration of young europeans. i am in favour of the generalization and consolidation of these two principles in order to complete the construction of the european higher education area. i am also pleased with the agreement on increased funding for public and private universities and support the proposal to increase the level of cooperation between the worlds of education and research.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which deepens the bologna process on the recognition of diplomas within the european union by strengthening mobility, fighting for better occupational integration of young people and improving cooperation between the higher education and research sectors in europe. as the crisis has severely affected our national economies and negatively impacted unemployment figures, it is important that the european union mobilizes in favour of employment, growth and training for young people.
in writing. the bologna process introduced a three-cycle degree system (bachelor, master, doctorate), quality assurance and mutual recognition of qualifications and periods of study. however, there are still many administrative obstacles to the recognition of diplomas and the harmonisation of university standards. that is why i voted in favour of the report by my colleague luigi berlinguer, in order to send a strong signal to the ministerial summit of the bologna process, which will be held in bucharest on 26 and 27 april, to support greater involvement at european level in the process, in the form of incentives for european universities and the creation of joint programmes. these measures must be accompanied by increased public investment in higher education, in order to reconnect with sustainable growth based on high-level skills and knowledge and the promotion of partnerships between universities and business.
in writing. the berlinger report aims to support the completion of the bologna process. it points to areas where improvements are still needed, particularly in the areas of mobility, recognition of qualifications, vocational integration and cooperation between the higher education sector and the research sector in europe. i supported this report in the plenary votes.
in writing. by signing the bologna declaration on 19 june 1999, france committed itself with 28 other states to building a european higher education area by 2010, the primary objective of which is to offer every student with a diploma from a european university that it is recognised throughout the european union. while much progress has been made, mutual recognition of certain diplomas is still imperfect. i welcome the fact that parliament has adopted this report which calls for the creation of a european certification system in order to achieve full mutual recognition of the academic qualifications of each member state, which is a prerequisite for the creation of a genuine european area of knowledge.
in writing. the bologna process aimed to create a common framework for higher education in europe by 2010. its objectives have been largely achieved, but efforts are still needed. the report by luigi berlinguer, which i supported, lists the areas of action on which we must concentrate our efforts in order to benefit fully from the potential of this initiative. first of all, i welcome the recognition of the key role of higher education, reinforced by the bologna process, in achieving the europe 2020 targets for jobs and growth. this requires the involvement of all actors: teachers, students and businesses in particular - this is essential to improve the university offer and to offer professional opportunities to students. i particularly share the desire to strengthen the dialogue between enterprises and universities in order to offer more opportunities for internships throughout the university course and thus facilitate the entry of young graduates into the labour market. finally, i welcome the desire to increase the intra-european mobility of students. in this respect, i also think it is essential to ensure full portability of student grants and loans in order to avoid any discrimination against disadvantaged students.
in writing. europe has always placed youth mobility at the centre of its priorities since the creation of the erasmus programme in 1987. in 2010, more than 2 million students had benefited from european aid to study in another member state of the european union. however, it is pointless to encourage young people to study or work abroad if the states do not recognise the qualifications and experience acquired during such mobility. the bologna process, launched in 1999, was designed to remove all administrative barriers to the recognition of diplomas and to harmonise university standards by 2010. unfortunately, some states have fallen behind and there are countless students who find themselves in intractable situations because of the lack of effective harmonization. this situation is not only damaging to the people concerned but also to the image of the european institutions, which are accused of being inconsistent. parliament is today assessing the efforts to be made to consolidate the progress of the bologna process. the member states and universities must respond to the very high expectations of our fellow citizens.
in writing. the quality of training for young europeans is an imperative which must guide our action. i therefore supported this report by giving an account of the bologna process, which has been under way since 1999 to establish the framework for excellence in higher education in europe. my aim is to achieve a genuine single market in higher education, based on the broad structural reform under way, known as the 'mdr'. however, i regret that there are still obstacles between the academic world and the world of work. our assembly thus sends a strong message about the need for better integration between higher education and the labour market. europe's ambition is to be the most competitive knowledge-based economy in the world, thanks to the europe 2020 strategy. this is of course dependent on the quality of its teaching, the recognition of diplomas and qualifications, mobility, but also on the ability of students to integrate into the workforce. that is why i support efforts to encourage the opening up of the business world to students through internships, alternance training. our growth and competitiveness are inseparable from the level of training of young european citizens and their integration into the working world. the bologna process must succeed in this bet.
in writing. the sovereign debt crisis has highlighted the importance of the reliability of statistics provided by member states. reflecting the realities of a country, the quality and independence of these statistics are two of the most important factors in the development of effective european policies. the scicluna report, which i supported, calls on the european commission to offer its expertise to the member states.
in writing. as a member of the parliamentary committee on economic and monetary affairs, i have followed closely the report by my colleague edward scicluna on european statistics. accurate, relevant and high-quality statistics are essential for measuring our demographics or analysing data on our economy. they are needed at european, national and even regional level because they have a weight in political decision-making. if we develop statistics using more standardised, accurate and reliable methods, the union's policies will be better able to respond to the economic, social and environmental realities of our daily lives. i therefore approve the implementation of the european statistics code of practice.
in writing. i supported the scicluna report, which has as its main objective to strengthen the quality and management of european statistics.
in writing. accurate and reliable statistics are essential for any state to be able to adopt effective economic strategies. what is true of the states is also true of the european institutions, which must have access to relevant statistics. the quality of statistics at eu level is largely dependent on the relevance of the data provided by the eu member states. i voted in favour of this report which calls on the member states of the european union to take the necessary measures at national level to ensure the production of reliable statistics. the report also stresses the need for a systematic approach to the production of european statistics in order to improve their reliability.
in writing. reliable and accurate statistics are essential to ensure the effectiveness of economic and budgetary policy-making by the member states and the european union. the debt crisis in the euro area has also highlighted the risks of statistical inaccuracy and fraud, often stemming from weaknesses in the quality of upstream public accounting data. it therefore seems to me crucial that public decision-makers have relevant, up-to-date and accurate data, collected and developed by national agencies in accordance with the principles of impartiality, objectivity and professional independence. the text of the report on quality management for european statistics calls on the commission to provide support and expertise to member states to help them ensure compliance and the provision of high quality data at all levels of government. it also encourages eurostat to publicly express any doubts it may have about the accuracy of all types of statistics. the text also stresses the need to preserve the independence of statistical services from possible political intervention at both national and european level. i gave him my support.

on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, i shall confine myself to one point with this reduced speaking time. i would like to thank and congratulate commissioner lewandowski and say that after two years of budgetary austerity, the situation of the european budget is becoming untenable. for member states which finance the bulk of the budget, the level of payment appropriations is no longer sustainable. some member states are themselves ruined; they can no longer increase their contribution to the european budget. the others are busy supporting the previous ones; they are therefore also not in a position to increase their contribution, which is calculated on the basis of payment appropriations. but on the other hand, for community programmes, in the last years of the current multiannual framework, the level of payment appropriations is so low that in reality the union is practically in default. this is not a fault of the lenders but of the local authorities, the companies, the researchers, the innovators, all those who are carrying out the investment projects on which the return to growth depends. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the more difficult the political agreement, the more we have to ensure that the figures we are discussing are the same. we must be realistic, but a budget based on the principle of reality must start with the same figures. i hope that from there we can arrive at the optimal solution for both the council and parliament.
mr president, efforts to stabilize national budgets are necessary, but they undermine immediate growth. beyond the measures to restore budgetary balance, a number of necessary structural reforms such as basel ii, solvency, etc. have further weakened the natural economic dynamics. without investment, without growth, the recession cancels out debt reduction policies, increases deficits, collapses competitiveness and purchasing power and, in total, the opposite of the desired result. investment is needed to get our economies moving forward with three priority chapters: innovation, education, infrastructure. it is at european level that these areas are most effective. to apply pure austerity reasoning at european level is to believe that each state will be better off by restricting itself. the structure of the european budget, its allocation and its objectives are not those of national budgets. the budget, although modest, is still the best integrated anti-crisis tool and as such it must be boosted rather than restricted.
in writing. the parliament, by defining the 'general orientations of the 2013 budget', wanted to focus it mainly on support for employment (in particular for young people) and smes. these priorities bear a striking resemblance to the priorities set by parliament for the 2012 budget. the events of the last budget negotiations have already left doubts as to the outcome of the discussions which will soon take place for the preparation of the 2013 budget. the budgetary guidelines, the wishes of parliament? this is to be feared, since for the past two years the negotiations have followed the same dramatic course: the commission's budget proposal, supported by parliament, is being cut by the council, which is more interested in reducing its contribution to the community budget than in increasing its value. this is the same trick that has been played since parliament failed to use its new powers as co-decision-maker on the budget in 2010 to oppose the council's fruitless wishes. 2012 will also be the year for the preparation of the financial framework 2014-2020. it will be difficult to prevent the council's short-term vision 'in times of crisis' from being applied to the definition of the financial perspective 'after the crisis'. but it is an ambitious position that must be supported, for a europe that is in line with the expectations of europeans!
for the gue/ngl group mr president, better late than never. finally, it is proposed to lower the co-financing rates required of member states to benefit from the european fisheries fund. this principle of european union/member state co-financing is a bad one because it restrains the weakest countries, those who are suffering the full brunt of the austerity plans imposed on them by the union, and amounts, more or less, to lending only to the rich. it is a shame to see european funds not being spent because the member states concerned are in too great a difficulty to provide the necessary share of the funding for the release of these funds. it is also scandalous that most of the fund is being used to finance the demolition of fishing vessels instead of helping to create jobs in the fisheries sector. it is also clear that this proposal is late because small-scale fishing in the union is dying, which does not solve anything about the necessary preservation of the fishery resources that are threatened with destruction by factory ships flying the flag of japan or russia. it is the small fishermen who drink to the occasion while the representatives of the sea exploiters quietly lobby in the corridors of brussels. if we want to continue fishing under the flags of the member states of the union, we must therefore urgently redirect the european fund towards production and employment, towards sustainable fishing, towards safety and towards the search for engines that use less fuel. above all, europe needs a truly comprehensive fisheries policy for the 21st century which finally turns its back on the liberal dogma of market regulation.
mr president, commissioner, this is an important agreement which is being concluded today with the revision of the regulation authorizing an autonomous tariff quota for the import of high-quality beef in otherwise very limited quantities. we are witnessing the epilogue of a longstanding trade conflict between europe on the one hand and the united states and canada on the other. we should thank the rapporteurs, and in particular my colleague mrs quisthoudt-rowohl, for their work, as did those who have come before me. but let us also join our voices in calling for support for the implementation of the second phase of the agreement. this is a victory for european diplomacy. it is a victory for the respect we owe to the citizens of europe, since hormone-laden beef is banned from our stalls for good. the sanctions imposed by our transatlantic partners in an attempt to change our minds have not shaken our conviction that an agreement must be reached. the system of restrictions on entry into their markets was particularly punitive for a large number of european food products, since customs duties could be as high as 300%, preventing them from maintaining their presence on those markets. we all remember the sad episode of roquefort or shallots, as far as my country is concerned. at a time when europe must re-establish its balance of trade, the end of these sanctions therefore appears to be an oxygen bubble for european producers. it has been a year since the americans lifted all the restrictions they had imposed, eight months before the date set by the agreement. and so, now it's time to move on. the discussions were fruitful. they showed how much we can work together. let us therefore continue to work in the same direction with pedagogy, with demand, with diplomacy, but above all on the essential basis of reciprocity. because reciprocity does not preclude openness. reciprocity is the guarantee of win-win, mutual respect and collective success.
in writing. the european fisheries fund (eff) entered into force in january 2007. it aims to improve the competitiveness of the sector and to help make it environmentally, socially and economically viable. to achieve this, it has a budget of €3.8 billion for the period 2007-13. however, some countries are in difficulty and have been particularly affected by the sovereign debt crisis. because the spirit of community solidarity is the greatness of europe, i have approved the european commission's proposal to increase union co-financing for countries in major difficulties, while reducing proportionately the national effort required for the use of funds.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the ferreira report at first reading. the current economic situation required rapid agreement on the emergency mechanism proposed by the commission to deal with the lack of co-financing by certain member states experiencing financial difficulties. i support the proposal to increase the maximum co-financing rate by 10 points. this is an additional guarantee for the proper implementation of the eff. this agreement shows that european solidarity is not a mere word. i think it is important to recall that the new mechanisms put in place will have no impact on the next budgetary programming period.

in writing. in 2008, the council adopted a regulation in response to the crisis and its socioeconomic consequences. the commission considered that additional measures were needed to facilitate the management of eu funding, to help accelerate investment in the member states and regions and to improve the availability of funds for the economy. the ferreira report supports the commission's proposals. i voted in favour of this report in the plenary votes.
in writing. as you know, exports of european veal and beef to the united states have been blocked for a decade due to us restrictions related to bse (bovine spongiform encephalopathy). the united states has removed sanctions on certain products from the european union, while the european union offers significant market access for hormone-free beef. we finally put an end to this fight. the agreement allows the eu to maintain the ban on imports of hormone-treated cattle in exchange for increased import quotas for high-quality beef from the us and canada. as my colleagues agnès le brun and tokia saïfi of the european people's party have pointed out: 'this is a victory for european diplomacy, but above all it is a victory for respect for european consumers. the united states and canada failed to impose hormone-laced beef on us, the europeans didn't want it. the sanctions were not enough to change our minds.
in writing. 20 years of trade disputes between the eu and the north american continent have just come to an end. in the context of this war on 'hormone beef', the european union was condemned by the wto for having always refused to compromise on its principles, considering that european consumers could not be deceived about the quality of imported meat. the agreement allows for the permanent lifting of sanctions in exchange for import quotas of high-quality, hormone-free beef from the us and canada. a solution that should satisfy farmers and consumers, both in europe and the us, and that rewards the eu's tenacity in ensuring quality food for its citizens.
in writing. i supported this text, which will put an end to the trade dispute which has affected the transatlantic exports of our products since 1998. the compromise proposed here allows the european requirements for health protection to be maintained while opening the door to a revival of exports of our handicraft products. good news for quality products.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the report on the import of high quality beef which brings to an end a trade dispute with the united states and canada that has lasted for more than 20 years. the agreement will increase imports of high-quality meat from across the atlantic while maintaining the embargo on hormone-laced beef. this increase is expected to represent only 0.36% of the total beef and veal market in the european union, which represents a limited competitive risk for our farmers. this is a good outcome for trade relations between our two continents, which i particularly welcome. the united states and canada will continue to lift the customs surcharges which have been imposed since 1999 on our products such as roquefort, truffles, mustard and chocolate.
in writing. i supported this report which aims to amend a regulation of the council and the european parliament on the opening of an autonomous quota for imports of high-quality beef. the adoption of this report has put an end to a trade dispute with the united states and canada that has lasted for more than 20 years. this report will oblige the european union to increase its imports of high-quality beef in exchange for maintaining its embargo on hormone-treated beef.

in writing. in the late 1980s, when the european union decided to impose an embargo on meat treated with growth hormones, the united states and canada won a case before the wto, which authorised them to take trade sanctions measures against the eu. as the economies of these two regions are closely linked, the measures had a negative impact on each of them. this is why an "amicable" solution was sought and is now being implemented. i voted in favour of this report because its adoption puts an end to some 20 years of 'trade war' with two of our most important trading partners, while maintaining a high level of protection for european consumers and without too heavy consequences for the agricultural sector. the 'high quality meat' referred to in this report is nothing but meat not treated with growth hormones, of a lower quality than beef produced in europe. the quotas allowing imports of this meat are limited, so the impact on the european sector will be extremely limited.

in writing. a special parliamentary committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering has been set up by the european parliament. it will have one year to investigate the infiltration of the eu's legal economy, public administration and financial systems by organised crime, including mafias, and to propose ways of combating it. the misappropriation of public funds, the infiltration of the public sector and the contamination of the legal economy and the financial system are the main threats posed by criminal organisations in the european union. during its mandate, the commission will assess the extent of the impact of organised crime on the eu economy and society and recommend legislative and other measures to enable the eu to respond to these threats at national, european and global levels. finally, europe is sending a clear message to criminal organisations and gangs. we shall vote on the composition of this committee at the next plenary session, and it will then be able to start work at the end of april.
