in writing. i voted in favour of a report which aims to harmonise and coordinate existing judicial training in europe and to promote dialogue and contacts between professionals in the sector. today, judicial cooperation is indispensable and it begins at the training stage. for judicial cooperation to be effective, it must go beyond borders. the need to promote multilingual training is therefore urgent. i approved a report which allows, among others, judges, legal practitioners, professional organisations, academics and law students to go to erasmus or, more generally, to take courses abroad. to encourage cooperation, the commission will organise an annual forum where judges of all seniority levels working in areas of law that often raise national and cross-border issues can discuss together current or recently controversial or problematic issues.
in writing. language problems, lack of knowledge of neighbouring legal systems, lack of contacts and exchanges between institutions: all these are obstacles to the construction of a european judicial area. the challenges of judicial training at the level of the european union are therefore enormous, because it is impossible to build a european judicial area without properly training those involved. we therefore need to give real consideration to this issue and to make a great deal of effort to train not only judges but also all other legal professionals: lawyers, notaries, mediators - in other words, all legal professionals. there is a great need today to build a european judicial culture and to use all the means to achieve this. we must encourage contacts and exchanges and i would particularly like to stress the importance of creating a genuine 'erasmus for judges'.
in writing. europe is still making too little progress in building a common european judicial culture. to go further in building common mutual trust within the european judicial area, it is necessary in particular to establish networks between judges from different cultures and to improve the coordination of existing networks in order to create 'circles of coherence'. although new technologies make it possible to circumvent the budgetary constraints associated with the organisation of direct contacts involving many trips for judges, electronic communication cannot be sufficient. the creation of a forum for the judges to meet is essential, as is the participation of the judges of the luxembourg and strasbourg courts. finally, there is a need to coordinate better the training provided by the existing judicial training establishments and to facilitate and promote dialogue and contacts between professionals in the sector. otherwise we will have to regret in a few years that we have made too little progress.
in writing. i strongly supported a resolution which aims to combat child labour in the cocoa sector. this sector requires a large workforce, a large proportion of which is made up of children. i have just returned from burkina faso where many children are sold to work in the cocoa plantations, which is shocking and unacceptable. while the resolution acknowledges that producers are under great pressure to keep labour costs down, it calls on cocoa farmers and manufacturers, governments, traders, producers and us chocolate consumers to take responsibility in the fight against forced labour and child trafficking in the sector. to effectively combat child labour related cocoa products, we wanted to encourage the signatory countries of the unctad agreement to take action to ensure traceability throughout the supply chain.
in writing. the global cocoa economy must not be subject to uncontrolled speculation. we must ensure that fair prices are set for both producers and consumers. but above all we cannot ignore european values, including human rights and the rights of the child. children may not be used as forced labour on cocoa plantations under any circumstances. the european union has a duty to promote responsible development and a smart economy by combating all forms of exploitation of children.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which makes it possible to combat a form of exploitation which is unfortunately still very much alive. globalisation must not make us forget respect for fundamental rights such as the prohibition of human trafficking and the rights of the child.
in writing. the european union is the world's largest consumer of chocolate, 70% of the world's cocoa is grown in west africa, and around 18 million children worldwide are estimated to work on cocoa plantations. the european union cannot ignore this humanly dramatic and absolutely unacceptable situation. these children work in extremely dangerous conditions, they are often exposed to pesticides, many of them are victims of human trafficking. i therefore voted resolutely in favour of this annexed resolution, which follows parliament's consent to the renewal of the international cocoa agreement in terms of production and trade. this resolution aims to emphasize the issue of child labour in cocoa plantations and above all it strongly condemns the use of child labour (and unacceptable forms of labour) in the cultivation and harvesting of cocoa beans.
in writing. according to some studies, it is estimated that more than 250,000 children work in cocoa plantations in west africa. they handle pesticides without protection and use tools that are very dangerous for their age. as the main importer of cocoa beans, the european union has a major responsibility in the fight against child labour, particularly in the cocoa sector, in order to establish a sustainable cocoa supply chain in which children do not intervene. children should not be in cocoa plantations but in schools, and actions should be supported to promote this change. finally, more generally, all trade agreements should include provisions to reduce poverty and promote decent work and safe working conditions, and include legally binding clauses on respect for human rights, social and environmental standards, with penalties for breaches.
in writing. this resolution accompanies the european parliament's approval of the international cocoa agreement. while i am in favour of the agreement, i can only reiterate the concerns expressed by my colleagues on the committee on international trade in our discussions. the sector is still very much affected by the problem of child labour and the european union has a dual responsibility in this respect: on the one hand, it is the largest importer and the largest consumer of cocoa; on the other hand, it is the largest importer and the largest consumer of cocoa. the commission has also to promote its core values in all areas. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution, which is the european parliament's position on this matter and will enable us to verify how our demands are being implemented. the resolution will also serve as a basic text for the european commission in its relations with the other members of the international cocoa organization.
in writing. the cocoa sector represents a significant labour force and a source of income for millions of people if all the players in the sector are taken into account. i therefore voted in favour of the international agreement to strengthen cooperation between producing and importing countries. the resolution will also strengthen the role of the international cocoa organization (icco), a structure that provides data on the world market and encourages cooperation between its member countries, and make global cocoa trade more equitable and sustainable. while aimed at strengthening social and environmental responsibility, the new agreement does not explicitly address the problem of child labour, which is discussed in another report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this international agreement on cocoa because it establishes rules for transparency in cocoa farming and emphasises capacity building for small local producers in a poverty reduction approach.

in writing. the agreement adopted today replaces and improves the agreement in place since 2001. i supported its adoption because it will increase the transparency and sustainability of the sector. it will set up a more effective and participatory leadership structure within the international cocoa organization (icco), where the eu is based. the european union is the world's largest importer and consumer of cocoa and is home to the main cocoa processors and chocolate manufacturers. it bears a large share of responsibility in improving the sustainability of the cocoa sector. this question has been raised several times during our debates, and we have therefore decided to adopt a resolution on a recurring problem in the sector: child labour. this text will provide a basis for the work of the members of icco and will serve as a reference point for us to monitor the progress made by the parties involved.

in writing. i have approved the 2010 international cocoa agreement. i am satisfied with the improvements it makes to the previous agreement in terms of health standards and working conditions. the conclusion of this agreement by the european union is a real breakthrough for the cocoa industry. it is a balanced agreement which takes account of the interests of producers and consumers. it promotes international cooperation, increases transparency in the sector and ultimately ensures a sustainable future for the sector. i also welcome the adoption of the resolution on child labour in the cocoa sector.
in writing. 32 million europeans aged 20 to 79 are now suffering from diabetes and the numbers are growing. i have followed closely the development of this report, which calls for more prevention, screening, treatment and research. as a member of the parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety, i felt it was essential to develop a targeted european strategy to combat this disease. for my part, as a member of the new national sports council (cns), created by the french minister of sport david douillet, i believe that sport must be an integral part of public policies to prevent diabetes and obesity. several studies have shown that type 2 diabetes can be controlled by effective prevention strategies focusing on risk factors (such as poor or unbalanced diet, obesity, lack of physical activity and alcohol consumption). the european commission has already set up a european platform on physical activity and health and has a strategy on nutrition and physical activity, but we need to go further to protect our children and ourselves from these diseases!

in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the fight against the diabetes epidemic in the european union, which calls on the commission to define and implement a targeted european strategy to combat diabetes through prevention, screening, education and research and on the member states to implement national programmes to combat diabetes, focusing on prevention. diabetes affects nearly 10% of european citizens, and this rate is expected to increase to 16.6% by 2030. it is therefore necessary for the eu to adopt a strategy at its level to complement national efforts in order to provide continued financial support for research and to encourage early detection of the disease.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which stresses the prevention, screening and research of diabetes. it is one of the most widespread non-communicable diseases, affecting more than 32 million citizens in the european union. it is important to distinguish between type 1 and type 2 diabetes as different diseases. research is still needed to identify with certainty the risk factors for type 1 and genetic predispositions. in type 2, the causes have been identified. however, up to 80% of type 2 diabetes could be prevented by eliminating the risk factors for these diseases (smoking, poor diet, sedentary lifestyle, harmful use of alcohol). the resolution recommends strategies to be implemented from an early age through education on healthy eating habits and physical exercise in schools. major advances in health care, combined with healthier living, will ensure a higher quality of life for people diagnosed with diabetes at an early stage.
in writing. i supported the joint resolution on the fight against the diabetes epidemic in the european union. this resolution was supported by a large majority in the european parliament, and i welcome that.

member of the commission. − mr president, my colleague mr janez potočnik unfortunately cannot be here today so he has asked me to replace him and i am happy to do so as i had the chance myself also to participate in part of the water forum in marseilles as have my colleagues piebalgs and georgieva. in reply to your questions, first i would like to recall that a ministerial declaration was developed by the host, france, together with states’ representatives and the commission. second, the eu has developed over several decades a comprehensive water policy. since the year 2000, with the adoption of the water framework directive, water policy aims at achieving good status of all eu waters by 2015 on the basis of integrated river basin management. this brings together all users and stakeholders to address all pressures on the water environment in the whole river basin, beyond administrative boundaries. the eu will continue to promote this approach worldwide. but, in spite of our efforts, the achievement of eu water policy goals is still challenging due to a number of old and emerging water management issues related to both water quality and quantity. we also have to look ahead at the vulnerability of the water environment to climate change and ensure that adaptation to climate change is taken into account in our water policies. the commission presented at the world water forum a unique eu web-based platform: the european climate adaptation platform, which is a concrete solution, focusing also on water issues like drought and flooding. at global level, the eu will do its utmost through its development cooperation policy to promote integrated river basin management as a key tool to achieve the millennium development goals and multi-level governance. third, i would like to refer to the 2012 blueprint to safeguard europe’s water resources that will present the eu policy response to current water challenges. the blueprint should, subject to an impact assessment, suggest actions in seven specific areas: on land use; on economic incentives to propose recommendations on how water pricing can reflect the true cost of water use and pollution; on water efficiency targets, to provide tools to develop indicative water efficiency targets – at eu, member state, river basin and sectoral levels; on innovation, the blueprint will be complemented by a water innovation partnership with stakeholders and the private sector. the blueprint will also look at ways to improve governance, including analysing the administrative setup and the potential to reduce administrative burden. consideration will also be given to the knowledge base for water policy-making, where the blueprint will seek improvements in statistics on pressure exerted by all activities on water resources; the enhancement of the water information system for europe and the development of a road map for water research. finally, the blueprint will reinforce the eu’s commitment to achieve the mdgs on access to drinking water and sanitation, while taking into account relevant outcomes of the rio+20 conference. the implementation of the new commission policy framework on water management in developing countries will translate integrated water management into concrete action, that is by expanding the eu water initiative. the ministerial declaration of the world water forum complements the commission communication on a development agenda for change, by highlighting the key water-related issues for the implementation of eu development policy.

mr president, the sixth world water forum is under way, and the main water markets are meeting there. it is not therefore a single platform for dialogue as our resolution says. next door is an alternative forum where the fundamental issue is the right to water. because water is not a commodity like the others, it is a natural commodity like air, sun, it is essential to life and not only to that of human beings. the water belongs to no one. it is not subject to appropriation, even public. it cannot be a source of profit. what is at stake is the management of this water, the water that is useful to humans. and here, the drift of the public-private partnerships is dramatic within our countries. water is getting more expensive without improving its quality. and we should ask ourselves what responsibilities the european union has, particularly in the way public service concessions are being misused. it is time to react, to take a global approach, and i for one welcome the fact that in france many municipalities are deciding to take back control of their water management. author. - mr president, commissioner, after mad cow disease, bovine tuberculosis, foot-and-mouth disease and bluetongue, there is a new schmallenberg virus, as it is called, which is beginning to affect our farms. the extent of the disease will not be known for a few weeks, when cattle and sheep are due to give birth. there are several questions. that is the point of our oral question. what discussions do you have, commissioner, to prevent the embargo on our beef? are we finding ways to speed up the detection of this disease and try to slow or contain it? i also think that a european fund should be set up to compensate farmers affected by this disease, in cooperation with each of the member states. finally, do these health crises not raise new and serious questions about our agricultural systems, which are increasingly concentrated and increasingly free-trade-oriented, but which are ultimately becoming increasingly fragile, and where food security and health are increasingly under threat? this should be reflected in the discussion on the new reform of the common agricultural policy.
in writing. last year, the european commission adopted a 'roadmap to a competitive low-carbon economy by 2050' with the objective of reducing co2 emissions by 80% by 2050. to achieve this, several action plans in different areas (transport, energy, climate change, etc.) are being put forward. the european parliament, in an own-initiative report, proposes various measures to complement these action plans. this report focuses on the shortcomings of the emissions trading system (ets) and on energy efficiency. on the eqf, i advocated a stepwise approach rather than binding targets.
in writing. i have been particularly invested in the roadmap to a low-carbon economy by 2050 . i am convinced of the need to work towards a europe that emits less co2. in this respect, the roadmap recommends sectoral strategies in transport, electricity and agriculture, aimed at gradually reducing co2 emissions while maintaining a globally competitive economy. however, i do not hide from you that this text has also been the source of deep political disagreement. as so often, the left wanted to do more for the climate without considering the economic realities. it called for the emissions trading system to be revised to make it even more binding. that would undermine our businesses, and i was strongly opposed to that. i am in favour of a long-term vision, more realistic than that advocated by our socialist and green comrades. in the short term, such a review would make it even more difficult to restart our economy. i think we need to give our companies more incentives rather than constantly stigmatising and punishing them.
in writing. the transition to a low-carbon economy is an absolute and unavoidable necessity in europe today; it is a big company that demands ambitious goals in all areas. the report by our colleague chris davies has the merit of covering a very wide range of issues: from energy efficiency to cap reform, from the quota trading system to smart energy networks and rail corridors, there is no shortage of areas of action to ensure that by 2050 we are firmly and definitively committed to a low-carbon economy. we can discuss objectives and percentages, but i think this report lays the foundations for what we should do. i have abstained, however, not because i disagree with the substance of the matter, but because i think we must not make nuclear energy appear to be green energy! by including it in the list of decarbonised energy sources, along with renewable energy sources, we are denying its dangers and the many risks it entails. nuclear power is nothing more than a transitional energy source, it is by no means an energy source for the future!
in writing. we need to promote a low-carbon economy, and take all measures to follow the roadmap to reduce co2 by at least 40% by 2030, 60% by 2040 and 80% by 2050. the emissions trading system needs to be improved and the transport and agricultural sectors must also be involved in this effort to reduce emissions. member states should be encouraged to take legislative measures to include air transport emissions in the ets without succumbing to commercial pressure from third countries opposed to the ets. the eu must continue to promote investment and stimulate technological innovation in order to remain competitive and exemplary at the global level.
in writing. the message that the european parliament wants to convey by adopting this report is that we are all ready to endorse the commission's major long-term commitments on climate policy. i am clearly in favour of strong eu ambition and want parliament to send a positive signal on climate. i cannot, however, legitimise instruments which are not good for climate, social and economic policy. although i am aware that at european level we have a different way of doing politics from the national scene, often with the need to seek compromises, i cannot bring myself to vote in favour of a text which conveys the myth of nuclear and clean coal. the lesson of the copenhagen resolution, which we all learned, is still very much alive. that is why i did not vote in favour of this road map which mentions nuclear energy as an instrument for moving towards a competitive low-carbon economy by 2050.
in writing. the european parliament approved on thursday 15 march 2012 the roadmap to a low-carbon economy by 2050. with this text, the european union sets out its long-term vision and continues its reflection on the outlines of a green economy. i welcome the adoption of this report which will give greater visibility to economic and institutional actors for the coming decades with a step-by-step approach for 2030, 2040 and 2050. it is true that profound differences have emerged about the functioning of the ets, since the carbon price is currently very low. the proposal of the parliamentary left to artificially inflate the price of a tonne of carbon was not acceptable because it does not take account of the particularly difficult economic and social context of recent years. the truth is that the left has absolutely no regard for the reality on the ground and the difficulties faced by our entrepreneurs. rather than acting under duress and being overwhelmed by a measure of which we were unaware, we preferred a prudent and discerning approach by asking the european commission to assess the situation and make proposals where appropriate.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which sets out an ambitious and realistic roadmap for reconciling competitiveness and the fight against global warming. europe is an example in decarbonising the economy, but it cannot act alone: emissions generated by one country affect all of humanity. there is no barrier to stop pollution and there is an urgent need for action on a global scale. many areas are involved: energy, transport, industry, housing, agriculture. an integrated approach is therefore needed to create the conditions for truly green growth. the fight against global warming requires reducing greenhouse gas emissions, an energy transition to phase out fossil fuels and more responsible behaviour. it will not be done in a few years, but i believe that we need sustained efforts in the long term, because it would cost us more to wait and we cannot compromise when it comes to protecting our planet and our environment. i believe that we need to focus on innovation and research to produce alternative energy, and to support businesses and households in this crusade to fight global warming.
in writing. the party for freedom (pvv) in the netherlands has been controversial in recent weeks for its xenophobic statements. the party's website encouraged the dutch to complain about eastern europeans living in their country. in this resolution, we strongly condemned the content of this website, which we considered to be a violation of the free movement of persons and an open incitement to discrimination against workers from the countries of central and eastern europe in the european union. i have taken a firm and unhesitating stand against the pvv party platform, which has posted clearly malicious statements and flouts our fundamental european values of human dignity, freedom, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights.
in writing. a simply outrageous website that can only be denounced! in early february 2012, the party for freedom (pvv) in the netherlands launched a whistleblowing website called central and eastern european citizens alert platform, explicitly inviting citizens to report their complaints against the immigrant workers who have flooded in from central and eastern europe. in defiance of the most basic rights and with a clearly discriminatory aim, this site is simply unacceptable. it is to fight against this kind of dangerous drift in democracy and to reaffirm our fight against racism and xenophobia that we have voted a political resolution condemning this website. the european union has no place for the blatant infringement of the free movement of persons and the open incitement to discrimination. the prime minister must also dissociate himself clearly and quickly from this deplorable initiative. the commission and the council must urgently cooperate to stop the spread of this kind of behaviour which tarnishes european values and the european project.
in writing. why is the title of this resolution in the plural? this text is aimed at only one site, the dutch party for freedom (pvv) and the only dutch government, which refuses to condemn it. the pvv now claims to prove its analysis correct by appealing to concrete testimonies of citizens, after having campaigned against the enlargement of the european union in its time. we're calling a whistle-blowing site! there is a discrimination against eastern european nationals! but let me say this: the freedom of expression and opinion that you preach so well in russia or africa, you are very quickly putting barriers in europe. the only views that can be expressed here are that the european union is a marvel, its single currency a source of prosperity, the accession of turkey, morocco and uzbekistan an exciting prospect, immigration, invariably an opportunity even if it ruins the host countries and robs the countries of origin of their competences. the one thought police are on the lookout! its leader, guy verhofstadt, even has an unstoppable solution to ensure that everyone conforms to political correctness: banning opposition parties. he made it at home. this is democracy!
in writing. we are not only facing a simple infringement of free movement but also an unacceptable stigma. the website set up by geert wilders' party to anonymously denounce foreign workers by explicitly targeting workers from central and eastern europe encourages amalgamations. he feeds the other's rejection. intolerance is hidden behind the mask of anonymity. i am extremely surprised and shocked by the lack of reaction from mark rutte. has he forgotten article 1 of the dutch constitution which prohibits discrimination and proclaims equality for all citizens living on dutch soil? has he forgotten the european values of tolerance ? or is he so afraid of losing the support of geert wilders' party that he shuts his eyes and turns a deaf ear? has he forgotten that his role as a politician is precisely to enable people to live together? has he forgotten that it is his duty to guarantee european citizens their right to live and work peacefully in the netherlands? or does it take refuge behind strategic and political considerations at the expense of the common good? to not report it is to endorse this degrading initiative. it's his duty to respond.
in writing. we have built the european union on a foundation of values. they can be called into question at any time. as meps, it is our duty to defend them. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution because it is inconceivable that in europe a government should fail to take action against private initiatives which aim to incite racial hatred and xenophobia. this is the case in the netherlands. the government must quickly condemn the websites set up by their pvv partner. the far-right party openly claims the authorship. there are many questions that need to be asked.
in writing. following the events in russia, the fraud observed by european observers on the ground during the presidential elections, we wanted to inform the russian authorities that it would be more than desirable for their electoral system to change. according to the osce and the parliamentary assembly of the council of europe, the electoral process had strongly favored one candidate, due to shortcomings in the candidate registration procedure, uneven and biased media coverage and the use of public means to the benefit of one candidate . international observers have reported that there were bottlenecks and irregularities in one third of the polling stations checked. on the one hand, we urge the new russian president to simplify the rules for registering political parties and on the other hand, i think it is time for vladimir putin to start a "sincere dialogue" with the protesters.
in writing. vladimir putin's first-round victory in the march 4 presidential election, marking his return to the kremlin after four years as head of government, comes as no surprise to anyone. this election, once again tainted by fraud despite the installation of webcams supposed to guarantee its smooth running, was only a sham election. the massive protest movement that has swept russia since the controversial legislative elections last december no longer allows vladimir putin to pretend that the opposition does not exist! twenty years after the collapse of the soviet regime, vladimir putin must listen to the opposition and undertake the reforms necessary to move towards democracy and respect for human rights. for all these reasons i supported the european parliament's resolution on this subject, in which the european union calls on russia to reform its political system in depth and to establish a real rule of law.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which shows our concern about the political situation in russia. mr. putin is turning democracy into a tsarist oligarchy, and he is eroding freedom and civil rights. i want to express my solidarity and support for those who oppose this system, but also my deepest respect for the peaceful struggle.
in writing. following the duma elections on 4 december 2011, and then the presidential elections on 4 march 2012, the russian people expressed through large demonstrations their aspiration for more democracy and a deep reform of the electoral system. despite recent modest initiatives by the russian authorities to improve electoral laws, the general rules remain excessively complex and vague, and result in inconsistent application of the legal basis. the text of the resolution strongly criticises the shortcomings and irregularities in the preparation and conduct of the elections, in particular the unequal treatment of candidates by the russian audiovisual media during the election campaign, and condemns the arrest of dozens of protesters during the protests. it also stressed the need for a critical eu commitment to russia, fully supporting the political modernisation agenda. the text calls on president medvedev to ensure the adoption of the necessary reforms of the political system, and encourages the various russian democratic opposition groups to unite more closely around a positive programme of political reforms. convinced of the usefulness of this scripture, i supported him.
in writing. on march 4, russian citizens went to the polls to elect their head of state and it was vladimir putin, who was the president of the russian federation from 2000 to 2008, who won the election with more than 63% of the vote. the report of the international observers (osce) is worrying: serious shortcomings and many irregularities were noted. the european union is deeply concerned about the outcome of the elections, which were held in the context of the opaque parliamentary elections last december. indeed, this confirms the undemocratic tendency of the russian electoral system. that is why i voted in favour of the resolution by which the european parliament calls on the russian authorities to investigate this latest missed election meeting. above all, we insisted on respect for freedom of expression and encouraged the kremlin to open dialogue with civil society as soon as possible.

in writing. nigeria's history is marked by tensions between muslims and christians. however, the chaos caused by boko haram is unprecedented. i therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution which strongly condemns the recent violence, including the attacks by the islamist terrorists of boko haram and the tragic loss of life in the affected areas of nigeria. it is imperative that we seek peaceful means and that all communities try to engage in dialogue to end the violence. but the nigerian government also has a duty to promote inter-religious dialogue in order to ensure the safety and protection of its people and respect for human rights.
in writing. nigeria is a complex country both from a socio-economic point of view and from its geopolitical situation. although the country is the eighth largest oil producer in the world, a majority of its people live below the poverty line. the events of recent months with the increase in violence against religious communities, in particular the persecution of christians in the north of the country by the boko haram sect and the execution of european hostages on 8 march, called for a collective awareness. parliament therefore, echoing the high representative's statements, strongly condemned the violence and recalled that religious freedom is a fundamental and unquestionable right. however, the causes of his attacks cannot be reduced to interreligious or interethnic tensions. they are often the result of exploiting poverty and exploiting fear. the nigerian authorities are already taking many actions to combat insecurity and i welcome this. however, governance and development efforts, with the support of the eu, need to be stepped up to achieve stability in the north of the country. the conditions for security are inseparable from those for development.
in writing. already facing multiple social, economic, ethnic and religious challenges, nigeria has been experiencing weeks of intense violence perpetrated by the islamist terrorist group boko haram. targeting christians in particular in their fight for an "islamic regime", the group is held responsible for the deaths of over 900 people to date. in view of this situation, i am indignant and have voted in favour of this resolution in which we strongly condemn this violence, call for peaceful measures to resolve intercommunal disputes and stress the importance of respect for the principles of freedom of religion, belief, conscience and thought. we also recall the need to monitor any possible rapprochement between boko haram and aqim, which, if proven, would be particularly harmful to the security and stability of the region. the union has appointed mrs ashton as its high representative for foreign affairs. it is high time that mrs ashton worked for the region, combining diplomacy and long-term development cooperation, to try to bring peace, security, good governance and respect for human rights back to nigeria.
in writing. on the sidelines of the 6th world water forum, we discussed water-related issues and called for sustainable solutions, including access to clean water. water is a vital resource but also a strategic one. only 2.5% of the water on earth can be used. water-related challenges (climate change, growing demand for energy and agricultural products, etc.) are not exclusive to developing countries. the water issue requires a global response.
in writing. i tabled the motion for a resolution on the world water forum, an event that brings together political, economic and associative actors concerned with water issues at the global level every three years. for me, access to water and sanitation is a critical issue because it's the health of billions of people that's at stake. first, despite progress, it is necessary to achieve all the un millennium development goals and the fight must continue, including to improve access to sanitation. secondly, water management by catchment areas and the problem of pollution at source must be addressed. finally, i would like to mention the idea of the 1% solidarity for water principle, which is being applied in france and which makes it possible to raise funds to improve access to water and sanitation in developing countries. following the adoption of this text by my colleagues in the european parliament, i presented the main lines of the text to the 35 000 participants in the world water forum on friday morning. the european union, the developed countries and humanitarian aid associations must now step up their efforts in terms of both financial and technical support.
in writing. in december 2010, i participated, alongside danielle mitterrand and some other meps, in the action of the collective "the water carriers": for water to be recognised as a common good of humanity but also for public water management. in the resolution we have just adopted, the european parliament, which is holding the world water forum in marseille these days, declares that water, a common good of mankind, must be accessible to all. access to drinking water and sanitation, but also the preservation of water resources and the guarantee of its quality, are all challenges we have to face and we find them in this text. what is not included is the need for public water management. in my view, water is far too precious and essential to the survival of both humans and ecosystems to be left to private interests. if in some respects, for certain uses, water can be considered a commodity, it is certainly not a commodity like any other! therefore, in terms of access to drinking water, water sanitation or keeping water affordable, water should be managed in a public way.
in writing. there is an urgent need for concrete commitments to promote and protect water resources. while access to clean water and sanitation was recognised as a human right by the un in 2010, water is becoming a geostrategic issue in some parts of the world, such as the middle east, china and latin america. we therefore call for greater consideration of access to drinking water in regional development policies. in europe too, access to water for all users must be ensured and decentralised action at regional and local level must be taken rapidly. parliament wanted to remind member states of their obligation under the water framework directive to achieve good water status by 2015. the dialogue and debate in marseille at the 6th world water forum should promote the establishment of 'water governance' and thus make it possible to make commitments at the global level at the rio+20 conference in brazil in june.
in writing. i voted for this resolution. water is a public good and access to it should be a universal fundamental right. each local authority must be able to choose the management method of its choice. on this subject, many strongly criticize the european union, its institutions and in particular the commission as responsible for privatizations, but it is necessary to recall that there is no mandatory european directive on the internal market as is the case in other public service networks. we will ensure that the european union does not embark on a policy of liberalisation but, on the contrary, guarantees the free democratic choice by each public authority of its methods of organisation and management.
in writing. access to water in sufficient quantity and quality is a major environmental, health and economic issue. this resolution encourages the development of actions to address some of the most crucial aspects of this issue. for that reason, of course, i voted in favour of this text. it advocates local as well as global solutions, as the issue concerns farmers in our developed countries as well as citizens in developing countries, and places this issue within the larger issue of climate change. it encourages major investment in research and development and the development of rational use of resources.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which proposes concrete actions to address the challenges facing europe and the world in order to preserve water resources, ensure water quality and availability across the planet. i hope that the marseille forum, as our resolution calls for, will be a step towards making the use of water a right, which was not the case in istanbul in 2009, where only a "fundamental human need" was recognised. unsafe water kills more than 3.6 million people every year. we need to accelerate the implementation of major technological solutions: desalination of seawater, construction of large dams, public-private partnerships. the collection and development of water sources are now well-established techniques which must be rapidly implemented in conjunction with the local population.
in writing. this week the 6th world water forum was held in marseille, which was an opportunity to remind that water is a precious commodity for which we have a duty of responsibility. according to a study by who and unicef, 89 percent of the world's population will have access to safe water by 2010. this is a remarkable advance. yet, 2.5 billion people still lack access to safe water. water is a development issue, an ecological issue, and a health and food security issue in a context of population growth and climate change. more than ever, we need to put this issue at the heart of our policies and develop a comprehensive eu water strategy. we must make universal access to water by 2030 and make sanitation a priority by carrying out solidarity actions alongside developing countries. we need to develop sustainable water management by fighting waste, by investing in innovation and green technologies. there are many projects and ambitions. i now expect the conclusions of this strategic forum to be translated into concrete commitments at the rio conference in june.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the sixth world water forum, which is intended to contribute to the discussions held in marseille from 12 to 17 march. while water management has a direct impact on human health, solutions are needed to upgrade water infrastructure systems in developed countries and make them adequate in developing countries. water should not be a source of profit and access to it should be a fundamental and universal right. it is imperative if we are to make progress in the field of health, to invest in the protection of drinking water resources. we need to encourage research to develop innovative techniques in all water-related sectors and at the same time use water more rationally, more efficiently. we must now commit ourselves to a long-term policy.
in writing. water is a precious but scarce resource. yet, he is the source of all life. we must fight to preserve it for future generations. i would like to welcome the initiative taken by france to host this world forum. because of course the dialogue must be opened up at the global level. only by calling on governments to take more responsibility for the day-to-day management of water can we avoid a disaster that would cost us dearly. that is the meaning of my vote in favour of this text. but beyond conservation, i want to make it clear that water supply is another major problem. it is the cause of many diplomatic tensions, territorial disputes and even, unfortunately, sometimes armed conflicts. in the collective consciousness, water needs to be given the same recognition as climate change. i'm sure you do.
in writing. water is a human right, and access to water is fundamental. climate change may lead to a decline in the quantity and quality of available water, including drinking water, as well as an increase in the frequency and intensity of floods and droughts. the european parliament resolution calls for water to be used more efficiently, particularly in the sectors which consume the most water, such as agriculture. the resolution therefore reinforces the need for concrete commitments to promote and protect water resources, particularly in the run-up to the next rio+20 conference; i am therefore voting in favour of this resolution, even though the world water forum is taking place in marseille this week.
in writing. deforestation, population growth and climate change are putting increasing pressure on the availability and quality of water resources, and water infrastructure systems are often inadequate in developing countries and obsolete in developed countries. the 6th world water forum - a unique platform where water specialists and policy makers from around the world worked on developing solutions to achieve water security - was a pivotal event, and i welcome the adoption of this resolution by the european parliament. the text recognizes - and i strongly supported this idea when i voted - water as a common good of mankind. it should not be a source of illicit profit: access to water should be a fundamental and universal right. we also call on the commission and the member states to increase their commitment to the full achievement of the millennium development goals in the field of water and sanitation. finally, we need to increase public and private investment in research and development in all water-related sectors.
in writing. our water consumption is constantly increasing. today, it takes 11,000 litres of water to make a pair of jeans and 15,000 litres of water to make a kilo of beef. water, we tend to forget, is the root of everything. and as the world's population increases in the future, it will become an even more valuable possession. in some parts of the world, it is considered impossible to satisfy a basic need such as drinking. the terrible drought that struck the horn of africa last year, forcing women and children to make a real exodus, reminds us of the urgency of global coordination to meet this challenge. in my constituency we also feel the need to preserve this gift of nature better. the water stress faced by our farmers, the pollution of rivers and coastal areas are issues that the eu must address. this is a global, european, national and local issue. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution which proposes solutions taking into account the different scales of the water management challenge and which will feed into the discussions to be held at the world water forum in marseille.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report which provides for the revision of the statutes of the international rubber study group (irg) and recognises the importance of this organisation. the aim is to reinvigorate cooperation between producing and importing countries. as the rapporteur recalls, the iceg is an intergovernmental organisation set up in 1944 in the united kingdom, whose headquarters were moved to singapore in 2008. it provides a forum for discussion between the rubber producing and consuming countries on all aspects of the supply chain. this structure provides data on the world market and encourages cooperation between its members. apart from the european union, nine countries are currently contributing members, including the republic of cameroon, côte d'ivoire, india, japan, malaysia, nigeria, the russian federation, singapore and sri lanka. some 120 industry representatives are members through a panel of partners. in recent years, as high price increases and considerable volatility have affected certain raw materials, including natural rubber, i felt it necessary to reaffirm this international cooperation.
in writing. the european union is a member of the international rubber study group, in accordance with council decision 2002/651 of 22 july 2002. on 14 july 2011, following several rounds of negotiations, the heads of delegation of the international group approved the text amending its statutes and rules of procedure. the adoption of the moreira report made it possible to approve these new statutes and internal rules, which were a prerequisite for confirming the group's establishment in its new headquarters, budgetary contributions and decision-making procedures.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the taylor report which calls for clarification of air passenger rights. airlines have a duty to provide information and assistance in the event of a long delay and cancellation of flights. they are also called upon to make their pricing practices more transparent and to indicate the environmental impact of travel on the air ticket.
in writing. we have put in place, several years ago, european legislation that regulates the practices of airlines and protects us from their abuses. yet our rights as air passengers continue to be regularly violated, and that is why i supported my colleague keith taylor's report. the rights of air passengers in the event of delays, cancellations and overbookings must be respected, and we had to be the spokesmen of the citizens on these issues. the rules will be more precise, in particular as regards the notion of 'extraordinary circumstances' and 'cancellation'. this inaccuracy is the margin of manoeuvre which still allows airlines to mislabel a plane that takes off 24 hours after its scheduled time as "delayed" in order not to compensate the passenger. i also supported the idea that a blacklist of abusive clauses should be drawn up, for example, the non-transferability of tickets, or the prohibition on using only the return leg of a return ticket.
in writing. strengthening air passenger rights: that's what the eu is for! the union has been working for several years to improve travellers' rights, but there is still work to be done. this is particularly the case when passengers are stuck and delayed: informing, assisting, simplifying the claim, compensating, these are the obligations of the carriers. another problem is the rules on carry-on luggage: today, everyone has his own weight and size criteria, and travellers have a very hard time finding their way around. the rules must therefore be harmonised to make them more transparent. finally, more flexibility in booking with wider possibilities for cancellation and amendment seems essential. in short, in this resolution we make the diagnosis and call for action.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which proposes to standardise and strengthen european legislation on air passenger rights. it will provide passengers with better information on prices, clarify the criteria for compensation in the event of lost or delayed baggage and protect them against unfair commercial practices they face today, such as extra charges when booking online, unilateral re-organisation of flights or tariff discrimination based on country of residence. i fought for the adoption of these measures. passengers must not be left behind in the tremendous development of the aviation sector and i believe that all the players have understood this. i will ensure that my proposals are incorporated into future legislation.
in writing. flights cancelled, lost luggage, delays, overbooking and so on these are all problems which are not adequately addressed by the current regulations. it was therefore necessary to define a new framework and new instruments to guarantee the rights of air passengers in all circumstances. this has now been done with this resolution, which above all offers more transparency. transparency on information in case of delayed or cancelled flights, but also transparency on prices announced by airlines. this need for clarity was accompanied by an imperative to improve passenger assistance. the resolution also states that passengers in difficulty should be able to contact contact staff directly who can offer a solution and immediate response. the text also considers that if a baggage is delayed for more than six hours, compensation proportionate to the passenger's needs should be offered to the passenger so that he can support himself while waiting for his baggage to arrive. the resolution also stresses that people with reduced mobility should have easier access to aircraft.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which is a positive step forward in the protection of the rights of air transport users. it is necessary to strengthen their legal certainty, to provide sufficient and simple remedies and to provide accurate information to passengers. but the measures which will be applied in the near future must not be used to add unjustified and excessive costs to the current tariffs at the expense of consumers.
in writing. the european parliament adopted, on thursday 29 march, by a large majority, the report on the operation and application of the established rights of persons travelling by air. this report proposes concrete measures for air passengers which should influence the copy presented by the european commission in 2013 when it reviews the legislation on air passenger rights. in the face of repeated delays and lack of information, parliament has made recommendations which ensure that passengers' rights are fully respected. among its demands, parliament called for better information for passengers, with the presence of a contact person for each airline at airports, price transparency, the fight against the proliferation of unfair terms, clarification of the criteria for compensating passengers and improved care for people with reduced mobility.
in writing. the taylor report on the rules protecting air passengers was adopted by 509 votes to 20, with 53 abstentions. i'm glad you did. the report first deals with the common rules on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of a flight. it also deals with the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility when travelling by air. it also recognises the need to strengthen legal certainty, improve clarity of interpretation and harmonise the application of regulations throughout the european union. the report also calls for greater accountability and transparency, and for consumer rights to be clarified and strengthened by ensuring that consumers are well informed. once again the european parliament is coming to the rescue of air passengers!
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the operation and application of the acquired rights of air transport users, in order to lay the foundations for future common rules on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of a flight, and on the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility when travelling by air. we want airlines to offer all passengers the possibility of submitting a written complaint in an immediate, simple, accessible and free of charge manner, in addition to the possibility of submitting a complaint by other electronic means. it is also necessary to ensure that passengers have complete, comprehensible and accessible information, including on co2 emissions.
in writing. air traffic is expanding rapidly in europe with the development of competition in the sector, the creation of shorter routes and the decline in ticket prices. but these low prices cannot justify the violation of passenger rights. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report, which i have been particularly involved in, and which sets out our requirements for the revision of the rules for the protection of passengers. as a result of this vote, i expect the commission to guarantee the right to board with purchases made at airports without excessive charges. i believe that restrictive commercial practices in this area are a historic setback for passengers and create a form of unfair competition for duty-free on the ground. i also want the commission to make us concrete proposals to control the practice of overbooking which leaves thousands of passengers waiting every year. it is imperative to reconcile this technique of filling up aircraft with the provision of the service under the conditions laid down at the time of purchase of the ticket, which is the most basic right!
in writing. i have approved the new european programme for the resettlement of refugees from third countries, which will give more resources to member states wishing to take in refugees fleeing war, famine or persecution. i have supported this programme which, in cooperation with the united nations high commissioner for refugees, aims to strengthen the role of the european union in terms of international protection. in 2013, priority will be given to iraqi refugees in turkey, syria, lebanon and jordan, afghan refugees in turkey, pakistan and iran, congolese refugees in burundi, malawi, rwanda and zambia, somali refugees in ethiopia, burmese refugees in bangladesh, malaysia and thailand, and eritrean refugees in eastern sudan. the europe i stand for is also the europe that protects the vulnerable, children and women at risk, unaccompanied minors and people with special medical needs.
in writing. managing migration flows is one of the great challenges of our time. as the european union struggles to build a common migration policy that is progressive and ambitious, i welcome the adoption of a new common programme for the resettlement of refugees. according to figures from the united nations high commissioner for refugees, 200,000 people are forced to leave their country each year. it is our responsibility to support them. the new programme strengthens the eu's role in international protection and encourages member states to increase their efforts to resettle refugees and to focus on the most vulnerable groups such as women and children. thirteen european countries have so far established resettlement programmes. finally, the adoption of this new programme will mean that european countries will receive more substantial financial support from the european union to welcome refugees to their territory, through the european refugee fund, which was set up in 2000.

in writing. i supported the tavares report, which sought to amend the decision establishing the european refugee fund, in view of the establishment of a common european resettlement programme. resettlement is the transfer of refugees from a first third country of asylum to a member state of the european union where they could enjoy permanent protection. the tavarez report calls for financial aid for member states carrying out resettlement and for a list of priority refugees to be drawn up.
in writing. this new programme, by providing financial support for the resettlement of refugees, and in particular for those resettled by member states participating for the first time in the programme, is helping to encourage more countries to show solidarity. only ten member states, including france, are currently participating in the programme, which is still not enough. resettlement programmes are necessary: they allow a refugee who cannot return to his country of origin or remain in the country that has granted him international protection to be welcomed in a country where he will not risk his life. in addition, the new framework makes it possible to identify vulnerable persons such as unaccompanied minors or victims of torture who require special attention.

in writing. i have given my approval to the new regulation of otc derivatives. in the context of the economic crisis, i think it is essential to moralize our economy. as far as otc contracts are concerned, unlike stock exchange transactions, operations are often less standardised, less standardised, in a more flexible regulatory framework. i therefore approved this regulation on european market infrastructures, which requires traders to report all derivative transactions to central repositories within 24 hours of the transaction. however, as an active advocate of small and mediumsized enterprises, the heart of our economic fabric, i felt it was important to protect them. the clearing requirement was suspended in particular for development banks, cooperative banks, small banks, pension funds, eu rescue funds and transactions between members of the same group of companies.

in writing. after 18 long months of negotiations with the council, parliament was finally able to give its consent to the new regulation on over-the-counter derivatives. traders will now be required to clear these contracts via ccps and to report all derivatives, even those not traded over-the-counter. in addition, the powers of the european securities and markets authority (esma) to intervene in the settlement of disputes between national regulators have been increased. these decisions were made necessary to improve the transparency of financial markets, as derivatives had greatly aggravated market volatility during the 2008 crisis. however, this is only the first step in the regulation of the financial sector: others, which could not be supported by parliament because of the council's opposition, will have to be taken in the future, in particular with regard to strengthening the role of esma.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague e. morin chartier which calls for an extension of the transposition deadline for the 2004 directive, which expires on 30 april 2012. this directive lays down minimum requirements for the protection of workers against the risks arising from exposure to electromagnetic fields. a new directive is planned to improve the safety and health of workers. however, the issue of exposure limit values should be set in a proportionate manner and should not constitute an obstacle to the use of medical techniques such as mri. therefore, an additional transposition period was requested in order to have the necessary time to debate it.
in writing. the deadline for transposing the 2004 directive on the introduction of measures to protect workers from the risks related to exposure to electromagnetic fields was 30 april 2012. it is very difficult to transpose this text into our national legislation, especially when it comes to the medical community. the maximum exposure values included in this directive could unduly limit the use and development of medical applications using magnetic resonance imaging, which is considered an essential tool for the diagnosis and treatment of many diseases. i therefore supported the decision to delay by 18 months the transposition deadline for the directive on the protection of workers exposed to electromagnetic fields. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. but our aim remains to have new legislation before 2014 that will take into account the specificities of the different sectors of activity.
in writing. today we voted not on the substance of the matter but on the question of the date of transposition. the directive laying down minimum safety and health standards for workers exposed to the risks arising from electromagnetic fields was adopted in 2004. its transposition has presented many problems in some member states, with the result that the deadline for transposition has already been postponed once. it appeared that the exposure limit values set by the directive were likely to disproportionately restrict the use and development of magnetic resonance imaging (mri) technology. the european commission has therefore planned to carry out a thorough impact assessment and wishes to postpone the transposition deadline once again. it proposed 20 april 2014, but we decided, first in the empl committee and then in plenary today, to set the date at 31 october 2013 so as not to let this unsatisfactory situation continue for too long.
in writing. i voted in favour of extending the deadline for transposing directive 2004/40/ec on minimum safety and health requirements. i think it is necessary to extend the transposition period by 18 months in order to find appropriate answers to the questions raised by the draft new directive. the report shows that this is a technical matter which requires time to be dealt with properly.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text on the exposure of workers to electromagnetic fields because it proposes to grant an additional period of time before the limit values defined by the european union are put in place. these exposure limits, according to the medical community, could hinder the use and development of medical imaging techniques (such as mri), which are now essential for the diagnosis and treatment of many diseases. this will allow further discussions with the experts to find the right balance for the protection of workers.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive, which aims to shorten the time limit for transposing directive 2004/40/ec on the minimum safety and health requirements regarding the exposure of workers to the risks arising from physical agents (electromagnetic fields). the transposition should take place before 31 october 2013, instead of the date of 30 april 2014 initially planned. the aim is to minimise the risks to workers' health arising from the short-term adverse effects of occupational exposure to electromagnetic fields. no worker may be exposed to field values above these limits, which are based on health effects and biological considerations. these values are directly measurable and correspond to thresholds at which the employer must take one or more of the measures provided for in the directive.
in writing. the european parliament, meeting in brussels, has just approved an extension of eighteen months to the transposition deadline for the directive on the protection of workers exposed to electromagnetic fields. as the transposition deadline expired on 30 april 2012, parliament, alerted by the medical community that the maximum exposure values imposed by the directive were unduly restrictive to the use and development of magnetic resonance imaging (mri) techniques, decided to extend the deadline in order to continue consultations and allow the most appropriate decision to be taken. the challenge will be to strike a balance between the protection of workers and the effective monitoring of patients in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases.
in writing. the protection of workers exposed to electromagnetic fields is the subject of two reports in parliament. the first report concerns the revision of directive 2004/40/ec on the fixing of maximum exposure values for workers to electromagnetic fields. the second report, which we adopted today, deals with the reduction in the time limit for transposing the same directive. the objective is to postpone the deadline from 30 april 2012 to 31 october 2013 in order to allow for a proper review. the 2004 directive has not been transposed in all member states because the maximum exposure values are disproportionate and would have unduly restricted the use and development of medical applications using magnetic resonance imaging, such as mri. mri is an essential tool in the diagnosis and treatment of many diseases. the report by elisabeth morin-chartier was adopted by 610 votes in favour, which i welcome. as rapporteur for the opinion of the envi commission, i call on the member states to take stock of the impasse in which the medical community could find itself if mri technologies were not exempted from the exposure limit values recommended by the commission in its proposal for a directive.
