in writing. the 2013 budget freeze is a minimum. in all european countries we are trying to reduce expenditure to reduce public debts. we are voting today in favour of this, even though the effort remains modest, i agree, to freeze our budget in 2013. we will continue to look for savings to increase the rationalisation effort in the coming months. we also remain vigilant in defending the great democratic principles in this troubled period, so that political parties which do not respect the basic principles of freedom, the rule of law and democracy cannot receive funding from the institution: again, this is a minimum.
in writing. i voted in favour of the vaughan report on the estimates of revenue and expenditure for the european parliament for the financial year 2013. i regret, however, that the original version of paragraph 2 has been retained, which calls for a single workplace for members and officials of the european parliament. the report deliberately avoids specifying which city should become the single place of work of the european parliament, which creates confusion. i also regret the lack of clarity on the part of some journalists who have said that members want to move their parliament to brussels. i would like to remind you that strasbourg is the only seat of the european parliament recognised by the treaty. this siege must be maintained in the alsatian capital, a symbol of the reconciliation of the european nations.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which freezes the european parliament's operating budget for the financial year 2013. the european institutions must also take part in the budgetary discipline efforts undertaken by our heads of state, at a time when our fellow citizens have been hit hard by the crisis and are still suffering the consequences of unemployment and low growth in europe. it is all of us who must band together to get through this difficult time.
in writing. while the debate on the general budget of the european union for 2013 is already proving tense between parliament and the council, we meps are in the process of drawing up our institution's next operating budget. aware of budgetary constraints, we estimated the evolution of our financing needs at + 1,9% compared to 2012, i.e. an increase below inflation. certain expenditure items will be frozen to meet this objective, such as members' allowances, transport costs, etc. other avenues will have to be studied closely to avoid any slippage: this is the case of the costs of maintaining the buildings, or those necessary for the creation of the house of european history. during the year we will have to be more vigilant about certain additional appropriations that are needed, such as those relating to the accession of croatia, which are not yet included in the budget forecasts. parliament must set an example in drawing up its budget, so that it can exercise its democratically vested powers fully while keeping its expenditure within reasonable limits.
in writing. i voted against the vaughan report on the draft budget of the european parliament for the financial year 2013. i fully support the measures and guidelines contained in this report, such as the freezing in real terms of the budget of our parliament, the freezing of members' allowances, the cuts in the travel budget, the many savings made, etc. this report contains three clearly anti-strasbourg provisions/paragraphs. that is why i voted against him. the debate and the attacks on the location of the european parliament's seat are coming up more and more regularly, and i am paying close attention to them. it was a symbolic issue for a long time, but today it is above all a legal and political issue. i remain firmly committed to this ongoing fight to maintain the seat of the european parliament in our beautiful european capital.
in writing. once again, a number of meps chose to revive the debate on the single seat of the european parliament when voting on the report on the parliament's 2013 revenue and expenditure forecast. if that is their ambition, then let's talk about it! i therefore invite them to read over the treaties governing our institutional system: the official seat of the european parliament is in strasbourg and if, for convenience, we have transferred some of our activities to brussels and luxembourg, we will not be able to discuss the legal basis on which we are united. strasbourg is above all a symbolic reference point, the will of the founding fathers to erase the stigmas of war and to bring france and germany closer together around common ambitions. i am surprised today at the persistence of some of my more recent colleagues in wanting to challenge this symbol of europe, even though by joining the community and then the european union, the nations they represent have recognized in their entirety the principles and symbols which unite citizens around the european project.
in writing. the vaughan report was adopted by 548 votes to 69. it marks the beginning of the budgetary procedure for the european parliament, which, like the other institutions, must draw up a statement of estimates of revenue and expenditure for its 2013 budget. the commission will use this estimate as a basis for presenting its draft budget for 2013 in april.
in writing. i wish to abstain on the report by our colleague mr vaughan on the estimated state of the european parliament's revenue and expenditure for the financial year 2013 in that it takes a position, on three occasions and in an ambiguous way, against the maintenance of the current situation prevailing in the organisation of the european parliament: 3 workplaces and one seat. it should be recalled that, under protocol no 6 to the treaty on the establishment of the seats of the institutions and of certain bodies, offices and agencies of the european union, the european parliament has its seat in strasbourg. i did not want to endorse the vague guidelines in the vaughan report which could call into question the european parliament's seat in strasbourg, so i abstained.
in writing. in order to effectively support the european parliament's seat in strasbourg, i voted against paragraph 2 which calls for the parliament's workplaces to be 'limited to a single seat for members and officials'. the treaty states that 'the european parliament shall have its seat in strasbourg, where the 12 periods of monthly plenary sessions, including the budget session, shall be held. additional plenary sessions shall be held in brussels. the european parliament's committees sit in brussels. the general secretariat of the european parliament and its departments shall remain in luxembourg.' moreover, the official figures for the annual cost of the parliament's seat in strasbourg have recently been published and are far below previously estimated figures. they amounted to eur 51.5 million in 2010. finally, i am pleased to note that the energy consumption of parliament's seat in strasbourg has fallen by 74% between 2006 and 2010. these are the reasons why i support the seat of parliament in strasbourg.
in writing. for the second time in a few weeks, a majority of meps voted in favour of a single seat for the european parliament, and therefore in fact against the strasbourg seat. i deeply regret that once again this subject has been introduced almost in a whisper, by way of a report on another subject. this time it is through the budget of the european parliament, citing the need to save money. the change in the seat of the european parliament, which is enshrined in the european treaties, deserves a real debate, which will allow us to consider all the consequences of such a decision and take account of the complex historical circumstances which have made strasbourg the seat of the only european institution whose members are directly elected by the citizens of the member states. for the rest of the budget, the european parliament's priorities for 2013 are a few proposals for freezing various budget lines relating to administrative operation, but with a rationalization logic that may call into question the defence of multilingualism or the financing of projects aimed in particular at raising citizens' awareness of european history or the issues of european elections.
in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to support european workers who have lost their jobs. it allows them to reintegrate professionally. exceptionally, the financial and economic crisis is a sufficient reason for a member state to apply for a grant. the construction sector in spain, hit by the crisis, is experiencing several waves of redundancies. in an effort to show solidarity with the latter, we have released €1.6 million in aid.
in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers suffering from the consequences of major changes in the structure of world trade. in this difficult time, it is our responsibility to support the reintegration of displaced workers into the labour market. the european union launched a european economic recovery plan and found that the crisis had a very negative impact on the construction sector in particular, which saw demand collapse. to remedy the shortness of breath in this sector and to help to minimise the adverse effects of the economic crisis which has hit us hard, i voted in favour of this report, which allows the european globalisation adjustment fund to be used, in this particular case, in favour of spain.
in writing. eur 1.6 million to help over 1000 spanish employees to change their jobs and find new ones: the aid was granted in extremis! the reason: their dismissal because of the economic crisis! we're stepping on the head! let me explain: the egf was set up in 2006 to help the reintegration of employees made redundant as a result of globalisation. the economic crisis has come and a derogation has been introduced so that employees made redundant as a result of the crisis can also benefit; that derogation expired on 31 december 2011. despite the european parliament's vote to extend the derogation, the council of ministers decided otherwise! as a result, while the effects of the economic crisis are still being felt in some cases very severely in the member states, employees will be deprived of assistance from the egf: this fund can only support redundancies directly linked to globalisation. it is an aberration, and a situation totally incomprehensible to our fellow citizens. the egf is again going to be under-used by this distressing decision of the ministers who represent us.
in writing. i voted in favour of mobilising the european globalisation adjustment fund for the 1 138 workers in the construction sector who have been laid off. this fund, with an annual budget of eur 500 million, provides additional support to our citizens most affected by the economic and financial crisis by helping them to find new jobs and acquire new skills.
in writing. i supported the matera report, which responds favourably to a request from spain for a mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. like my colleagues in the epp, i am pleased to see that this report has been adopted by 567 votes.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my french colleague from the european people's party, alain lamassoure, which reaffirms the new institutional balance achieved for the benefit of the european parliament since the treaty of lisbon. as you know, the european parliament has become a true co-legislator of the european union, since it has powers equal to those of the council of ministers in the ordinary legislative procedure and in the budgetary procedure. we, your representatives, are now on a genuine par with the ministers representing the national governments. the practice of putting questions to the council of ministers on the agenda of the plenary session therefore loses its legitimacy. but at the same time, as the report points out, the lisbon treaty "created new institutions on the government side: the european council and its permanent president, the high representative, the eurogroup". i therefore believe that not only should the possibility of holding question hours with the council of ministers and the president of the european commission be maintained, but that such a procedure should also be provided for with the president of the european council, the high representative for foreign affairs and the president of the eurogroup.
in writing. the treaty of lisbon completed - on paper at least - the process of parliamentarisation which had been under way for a long time. the european parliament became co-legislator on most matters, deciding on an equal footing with the council. in reality, it still has to fight to see the rules applied: it is as if the states had not read the lisbon treaty! the links between the institutions are being strengthened and it is essential to increase the power of inquiry of the ep vis-à-vis the council: the possibility of questioning the council, within the framework of an hour of specific questions, on matters related to those of its competence which do not fall within the exercise of its legislative and budgetary functions must be maintained. the possibility of organising question hours not only with the president of the commission but also with the vice-president and the president of the eurogroup must be maintained, particularly in the context of the crisis in which these new institutions have been called upon to take major political decisions. these exchange times are essential if the ep is to take its full place in the interinstitutional balance of power and be a central element of the public debate and the legitimacy of the eu vis-à-vis the citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by alain lamassoure. i share the rapporteur's view that the question time in the council should be adapted in the plenary following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. it seems to me important that the european parliament, now on an equal footing with the council in legislative and budgetary functions, should make the most of the new powers granted by the treaty. this amendment to the regulation is therefore welcome, since it puts an end to the asymmetry of relations with the council. i would also point out that it will always be possible to ask the council about its specific powers.
in writing. since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, parliament has had powers equal to those of the council in the ordinary legislative procedure and in the budgetary procedure. in the light of this new institutional balance, it no longer seemed justified to maintain question time in the council in its present form. nevertheless, it appeared essential to maintain the possibility of asking the council questions on matters relating to its powers outside the exercise of its legislative and budgetary functions, within the framework of a specific question time. i supported the report by my colleague alain lamassoure.
in writing. i voted in favour of a resolution condemning the situation in belarus, where repression is on the increase. we renew our support for the belarusian people and call on president alexander lukashenko to engage in dialogue.
in writing. we had to reaffirm our commitment to the authoritarianism of the belarusian president. this report is intended to promote democracy in that country. i invite the commission to support, through financial and political means , the efforts of belarusian civil society, independent media and non-governmental organisations to foster the emergence of democracy. i condemn the deterioration of human rights and fundamental freedoms, the lack of democratic and economic reforms, the persecution of human rights defenders and members of the democratic opposition, and the harassment of civil society activists and independent media. we therefore asked for new sanctions, so that our actions would be in line with our political message!
in writing. parliament approved the resolution on belarus, which echoes the decisions taken by the foreign affairs council on 23 march on the strengthening of sanctions against the entourage of alexander lukashenko and his companies. at the doorstep of europe there is an arbitrary and repressive regime that silences the media and violates fundamental freedoms with impunity. we cannot tolerate it. the european union has repeatedly demanded the release of political prisoners, but the minsk regime, which has close economic ties with russia, has decided to harden its position towards the union by expelling the polish ambassador and the head of the european union delegation. the resolution will not bring about any significant changes in the immediate future, but it is important that parliament stands in solidarity with the restrictive measures taken by the council (asset freezes, visa bans, arms and equipment embargoes) and expresses, on behalf of the european citizens, its indignation at a regime which flouts the most essential rights and freedoms.
in writing. since the presidential election of 19 december 2010, the political situation in belarus has deteriorated severely. the regime continues to take significant repressive measures against members of the democratic opposition, the media, civil society activists and human rights defenders, despite repeated calls from the international community for an immediate end to the crackdown. the eu is also calling on the belarusian authorities to take all necessary measures to ensure that the situation in belarus is not further destabilised. calls for the immediate and unconditional release of all political prisoners, and recalls that the dialogue between the european union and belarus cannot progress without progress in belarus on democracy, human rights and the rule of law; calls again on the commission to support, through financial and political means, the efforts of belarusian civil society, independent media and non-governmental organisations in the country to promote democracy.
in writing. threatening the eu's internal security, organised crime, corruption and money laundering must be combated to uphold the democratic values promoted by the union and to put an end to the distortions in the internal market which they cause by putting pressure on the legal economy. a special parliamentary committee was therefore set up. the commission's mandate is to assess the situation in europe and propose measures to combat these threats.
in writing. as i announced at the end of the last plenary session, a special parliamentary committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering has been set up by the european parliament. it will have one year to investigate the infiltration of the eu's legal economy, public administration and financial systems by organised crime, including mafias, and to propose ways of combating it. the misappropriation of public funds, the infiltration of the public sector and the contamination of the legal economy and the financial system are the main threats posed by criminal organisations in the european union. the members have just been appointed and two women have been nominated to my french delegation from the european people's party, my colleagues véronique mathieu and marielle gallo. the european parliament is finally taking up this issue and is sending a clear message to criminal organisations and gangs!
in writing. the eu must be able to react quickly to democratic changes in its immediate neighbourhood. however, when the arab revolutions broke out, the eu was unable to mobilise immediate support for the actors of these revolutions. that is why we have decided to set up a european democracy fund.
in writing. i am an active campaigner for the european union to be a tool for transmitting our democratic values and progress. that is why i voted in favour of the report which calls for more effective and targeted european action on the use of the new european democracy fund (fedem). it must be given priority to our neighbours to the south and east, in the framework of the union for the mediterranean and the eastern partnership. moreover, support for democracy in these countries can only be beneficial to us, both politically and economically. the adoption was unanimous and, as the rapporteur, my colleague alexander graf lambsdorff, points out, this fund must be able to offer 'tailor-made assistance, flexible, responsive, responsive to the needs of the beneficiaries and capable of being reprogrammed quickly'. it must also grant grants directly to the beneficiaries. while avoiding 'double-use', this fund should complement existing financial instruments, including the european instrument for democracy and human rights.
in writing. i support the possibility of creating a european democracy fund. the arab revolutions show how important it is to put in place relevant and adaptable accompanying measures. two aspects of the report have caught my attention: the prominence of parliament in ensuring that the fund is used properly and the european union's commitment to democracy.
in writing. the european union has planned to set up a new tool dedicated to supporting all actions in favour of democracy and the rule of law by civil society and its representatives in the countries neighbouring the european union. the proposal to create the european democracy fund was launched in the wake of the events in the southern mediterranean to provide a more targeted response that does not duplicate the objectives of other existing european instruments and programmes such as the european instrument for democracy and human rights (eidhr). the fund, which responds to the eu's necessary adaptation to the new challenges posed by the arab spring, should support efforts towards democratic transition by providing concrete support to actors involved in strengthening democratic values and the rule of law, such as ngos, the media, trade unions, bloggers, etc. in adopting this report, parliament endorsed the process of developing and implementing the new fund with a view to making this new instrument operational by 2013.
in writing. my colleague mr lambsdorff's report aims to set up a semi-autonomous entity, through a european democracy fund, to help people working for democracy and to support democratic developments around the world. the fund should be managed in a non-bureaucratic way and should intervene at the first stage of the transition to give impetus to projects which until now could not be supported by the european union because of bureaucratic constraints. i supported this fine initiative in the plenary session in brussels.
in writing. the arab spring has shown the urgency for the eu to strengthen its commitment to democracy and to provide appropriate assistance to democratic transition processes around the world. in this sense, the creation of the european democracy fund (edf) seems to be one of the most tangible responses that the eu can provide to the challenges of democratisation in our neighbourhood and beyond, and i hope that the discussions currently under way in the council can lead to its establishment very soon. in this context, it seems to me crucial that such a fund should play a synergistic and complementary role in relation to the action of all the european institutions, and that it should bring real added value by complementing existing financing instruments. the mission and values of the emff should also be clarified in order to have precise criteria for the selection of beneficiaries. i also believe it is essential to accompany the establishment of an adequate control system to assess the effectiveness of the funding provided and the sustainability of the actions financed. that is the message i wish to convey to the council by voting on this text.
in writing. the creation of the european democracy fund (edf) responds to the need to provide the european union with an instrument for responding rapidly and adapted to the democratic challenges of today's world. it will be supported by a wide range of actors working for democracy and the rule of law (ngos, media, bloggers, activists and political movements). this fund, and this was mentioned in the recommendation i supported, must not interfere with the other instruments already in existence. its added value lies in its lightweight structure, flexible procedures and simplified funding channels. the edf, unlike the european instrument for democracy and human rights (eidhr), will be more of a short- and medium-term approach to providing rapid assistance to pro-democracy actors in need. we also stressed the importance of the european parliament's oversight of the fund, not just on budgetary aspects.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the enlargement of the union to include serbia. in this resolution, parliament endorsed the decision of the european council of 1 march to grant candidate status to serbia and recalled that the opening of accession negotiations must be conditional on the continuation of democratic reforms.
in writing. the council of ministers decided to grant serbia candidate country status and called on the european union to open accession negotiations with serbia as soon as possible . the report i supported recognises serbia's willingness to respect the copenhagen criteria, which are the prerequisites for any accession. it stressed the importance of continuing the dialogue between serbia and kosovo and of implementing the agreements reached in good faith. we are still calling for more efforts to guarantee the protection of minorities, the independence of the judiciary and the public administration. the country has resolutely turned to a functioning market economy. it must pursue its structural reforms and reduce its budget deficit.
in writing. more than two years after knocking on the door of the european union, serbia was granted candidate status on 2 march 2012. while serbia was the scene of nato bombing 13 years ago during the kosovo war, this nomination is a historic step forward and a reward for belgrade after its efforts to arrest ratko mladic and for its reconciliation with kosovo. i supported this resolution, which recognises the important role of serbia in maintaining security and stability in the balkans. it also called for action to be taken in accordance with the european values of reconciliation, compromise and peaceful coexistence.
in writing. at the thessaloniki european council on 19 and 20 june 2003, the european union committed itself to granting candidate status to the western balkan countries, provided they fulfil a number of criteria. serbia has since made considerable progress, including in ensuring the democratic functioning of its institutions, respect for human rights and the protection of minorities. for example, the government respects the prerogatives of the various minority councils and ensures their proper functioning. i therefore voted in favour of a resolution calling on the council to open accession negotiations with serbia as soon as possible. this new step would encourage serbia to continue its efforts, particularly in the justice sector. in order to continue its progress towards the rule of law, serbia needs to improve the efficiency and transparency of its judicial institutions.
in writing. despite all the bad trials, the eu is such an attractive political and economic force that many countries on the continent are knocking on its door. serbia is one of the last countries to have expressed its desire to join us and has, after considerable and remarkable efforts, obtained candidate status. i voted in favour of this status in the light of the efforts of the serbian authorities to reform the country and to satisfy requests from the hague for the extradition of individuals suspected of war crimes. i see in this the goodwill of a country that is resolutely european and that is determined to join the eu when it is ready. but there is still a long way to go for this country, which still has to integrate a significant part of the community acquis, implement many essential reforms, improve its relations with kosovo and meet the copenhagen criteria, before it can claim to open accession negotiations. i do not think we should be too hasty, because in these troubled times the union must first of all ensure convergence and solidarity between its members. this is necessary to maintain the unity and cohesion of the european family.
in writing. kosovo's independence is still disputed by serbia and continues to divide the international community. but it is in the heart of europe that differences remain. i voted in favour of a report which requires the five member states of the european union which have not yet done so to recognise kosovo's independence. they must play a more active role in the discussions between serbia and kosovo. to varying degrees, these countries fear that this precedent will fuel or validate separatist temptations at home, on the part of the catalans or the basques in spain, the hungarian minorities in romania or slovakia, or the turks in cyprus. we call on serbia to continue to demonstrate its willingness to achieve the objectives of the ongoing dialogue. a second aspect of the report, which i also fully support, stresses the need for reforms in kosovo, particularly in the constitutional and electoral spheres. as a colleague from the european people's party has pointed out: the kosovars finally have the chance to create a democratic european state. although there are still challenges, they have already done a lot. it is our role to acknowledge their efforts and help the kosovars .
in writing. while 88 countries have already recognised kosovo's independence, it is regrettable that there are still 5 eu member states that have not done so. we are waiting for the presentation of the road map on visa liberalisation by the commission this summer. it will certainly be a positive first step towards a future stabilisation and association agreement between kosovo and the european union. another strong symbol for kosovar nationals would be if the international olympic committee allowed kosovar athletes to participate in the next olympic games in london. kosovo is on the right track, but there is still a long way to go and key challenges remain, including the return of refugees and internally displaced persons and the fight against corruption.
in writing. the report on enlargement to kosovo was adopted in the committee on foreign affairs on 24 january 2012. i supported the report by my colleague mr lunacek, which shows that peace in kosovo is still fragile and that it still has a long way to go before it is granted candidate status.
in writing. in plenary, i voted in favour of a balanced resolution on kosovo. it is a realistic text which does not conceal the many challenges to be met. among the most important, i note the fragmentation of the political scene and the difficulty the government has in effectively engaging with the opposition. we nevertheless encouraged kosovo to continue its efforts and recalled the progress made, such as the fight against corruption and organised crime, the reform of the police and the judicial system. it should be noted that kosovo remains the "poor relative" of the western balkans: it does not benefit from any trade agreement with the eu or from the liberalisation of short-stay visas with the countries of the schengen area. the european perspective must be 'tangible', however, because it is the best lever for the democratisation of kosovo and the normalisation of relations between kosovo and serbia.

in writing. in writing. turkey is a strategic partner for the eu. it is a key economic partner, with an economy that has tripled in size in the last ten years. with eu-turkey trade reaching €103 billion in 2010, turkey became the eu's 7th largest trading partner. secondly, turkey is a country essential to the security and prosperity of the eu (essential energy corridor for the oil and gas resources of the caucasus and the caspian, geographical proximity to iraq). finally, it is a leading regional player, a strategic partner for our neighbourhood policy. however, it is clear that freedom of expression, media pluralism, democracy, the rule of law and the right to a fair trial, which are at the heart of our european values, are still far from being respected. the most consistent position is therefore to stick to an extended and strengthened strategic partnership with turkey. turkey is not in europe and therefore has no intention of joining the european union, which must be a coherent geographical entity. i have therefore decided to vote against this motion for a resolution.
in writing. turkey is a driving force in the region: its thriving economy despite the crisis, and the conduct of the june 2011 general elections, with their pluralism and high turnout, are a real example for the region. it is regrettable, however, that turkey is not making a greater commitment to international cooperation. for this to happen, border disputes, particularly the kurdish question, must be settled as a matter of priority, and the statute of the international criminal court ratified. it is also important that relations with the european union remain sustainable. it would also be good to ensure the protection of freedom of expression and media pluralism, and to pay particular attention to the reform of the judicial system, in order to promote a fair and democratic modernisation of the country.
in writing. this resolution is an opportunity to take stock of our relations with turkey. despite some progress, significant shortcomings still exist, which are holding back the negotiations for eventual accession. the commission has decided to complement this process, provided for in the treaties, with a 'positive timetable' which sets out the discussions for better convergence between the union and turkey. this is a good initiative, but it cannot replace the formal framework for negotiations. however, it is too early to consider enlargement of the union to include turkey, as many obstacles remain, both internally and externally. let us not forget that cyprus will hold the next presidency of the union and that turkey categorically refuses to recognise that state. in these circumstances, and given that the union is based on the principles of sincere cooperation and mutual solidarity between its members, how can we imagine any progress? in my vote, i therefore wanted to reaffirm my desire to make turkey a privileged and strategic partner of the union. it would be a historic mistake to want to go too fast, and we must be careful when it comes to choosing the members of the european family.

in writing. due to their particularities (remoteness, insularity, etc.), the european rules and programmes cannot be applied to the so-called 'outermost regions' (ors) in the same way as to the rest of the european territory. they therefore enjoy a special status which allows them to adopt a 'territorial' approach. the purpose of this own-initiative report is to analyse the role of future cohesion policy in the octs in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. by voting for this report, i renew my support for the ors and strongly condemn the european commission's proposal to reduce the additional specific allocation for the ors by 40%.
in writing. the outermost regions of the european union (canary islands, azores, madeira, martinique, guadeloupe, french guiana, réunion, saint martin) receive a special allocation under the cohesion policy because of their specific situation. the european commission is drawing up a new plan for these regions and is considering reducing the funds allocated to them. we therefore stressed the importance of compensating for the structural handicaps of the outermost regions, as well as those of other regions in europe. my experience with cohesion policy funds allows me to say that subsidies for the economic diversification of these regions are necessary and that it is equally important to support european citizens living in these regions.
in writing. the eu's outermost regions suffer from serious economic handicaps, due to their small size, remoteness and difficult terrain and climate. they have a special status enshrined in the treaty. as the conditions and difficulties of these regions are of a permanent nature and differentiate them from other european regions, eu rules and programmes cannot be applied in the same way as in the rest of the eu. their implementation must follow a territorial approach. the teixeira own-initiative report, which i supported, stresses the need to analyse, with regard to future cohesion policy in the ors, how these regions can achieve the smart, sustainable and inclusive growth objectives of the eu 2020 strategy, despite their permanent characteristics and constraints, in particular their remoteness from the heart of europe. however, this differentiation does not only mean paying special attention to compensation, but also and above all including them in a suitable strategy providing for a development model capable of taking real advantage of their strengths, for greater competitiveness, more growth and more job creation.
in writing. as the debate on the future of cohesion policy after 2014 has just begun in the european parliament, which has become a co-decision-maker on this subject by the treaty of lisbon, parliament wanted to recall the specific nature of the outermost regions - including the french octs - and the need to provide them with adequate means for their economic and social development. because of their remoteness, insularity and extreme climatic conditions, these territories require differential treatment, both for the viability of local industrial and agricultural production and for the successful implementation of the various programmes and competences of the european union. the commission's proposal to halve the amount of compensation for the additional costs in these areas is therefore very regrettable. i had in fact proposed amendments on this subject in the opinion of the committee on budgets on the teixeira report, just as i had recalled the need to include in the financial forecasts for these regions for 2014-2020 the planned accession of mayotte to the status of outermost region. mayotte will become the fifth french outermost territory recognised by the european union in 2014.
in writing. the outermost regions of the european union, because of their specificities, characteristics, geographical remoteness, structural weaknesses of their economies and dependence on the outside, etc., must be entitled to differential treatment within the framework of the european union's cohesion policy, so that their particularities are sufficiently taken into account and protected. at a time when we are negotiating within the european institutions the new budgetary programming of the union, our parliament has firmly opposed the commission's proposal to reduce the specific allocation for the outermost regions by almost half, recalling that a differentiated treatment for these regions is necessary. in this resolution, which i supported, we also insist on the inclusion of the specific features of the ors in all the european union's policies: fisheries and maritime policy, transport, the environment, etc.
in writing. the european parliament adopted by a large majority the report on the role of cohesion policy in the outermost regions (ors) in the context of the europe 2020 strategy, and i welcome this. the outermost regions, because of their physical and structural specificity, geographical remoteness and isolation, enjoy a special status and, therefore, a well-justified differentiated treatment, as the report states. like the other regions of the european union, the ors must strive to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. it's a condition of their development and growth. however, given their specific characteristics and constraints, european policies must be applied in a way that is appropriate to the octs, both in their internal and external dimensions. the european commission must take these regions into account in trade negotiations with third countries, as they can have a strong impact on their economic development. the rups have both advantages and disadvantages. it is up to the european union to strike the right balance between the implementation of its policies, its approach to governance and promoting their integration in the geographical areas to which they belong.
in writing. i supported the own-initiative report on the definition and implementation of european policies in the outermost regions for 2014-2020, taking into account the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the report rejects the european commission's proposal to reduce the additional specific allocation for the outermost regions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the urps, many of my proposals were adopted. parliament, on my initiative, asks the european commission to combat the high cost of living in the french overseas departments and to draw the attention of the european commission to the situation of monopolies, abuse of a dominant position and illegal agreements which have an unfair effect on the high cost of living. parliament therefore called for a study on price formation in the overseas territories. another of my amendments was that parliament should denounce the european commission's lack of interest in taking account of the specific features of the ors when negotiating economic partnership agreements and urge the commission to continue to seek compromises in the epas which respect the interests of the ors concerned. the adoption of this own-initiative report on the octs by the european parliament by a near unanimous vote is good news, but it does not in any way remove the threat of a reduction in the structural funds allocated to the octs and the poorest european regions, and the member states are still calling for a revised downward european budget for 2014-2020.
in writing. mr president, once again we have demonstrated our commitment to a strong but sensible cohesion policy. i think it is obvious that economic recovery will depend on the dynamism of our regions. i believe in good ideas and entrepreneurship. and europe has a key role to play: to support the initiatives of our regions in an intelligent and pragmatic way. the creation of the new intermediate category of regions, which will benefit languedoc-roussillon, is a step in the right direction. unfortunately, some decision-makers do not share my view and question this idea. so i say very clearly, as a semi-independent mep and elected by the people for more than 20 years: our territories need to feel that they are being helped. europe must move forward with ambition, not backward.
in writing. the outermost regions (ors) of the european union are characterised by remoteness, insularity, difficult terrain and climate. they face a great challenge: to turn their constraints into opportunities for growth. unfortunately, the economic, social and financial crisis has particularly affected the ors, highlighting certain structural weaknesses in their economies and their dependence on the outside world. in this context, eu action in their favour is more essential than ever. the text of this report stresses the need to adapt european fiscal and customs policies in order to strengthen the competitiveness of the outermost economies, as well as the importance of supporting smes by allocating community funds for the development of the productive fabric of the outermost regions. it also stressed the importance of the tourism sector for these regions and called on the commission to speed up the implementation of the european action plan in this field by ensuring better coordination of existing funding lines. i support this report because i believe that european investment in the ors is not just a policy of making up for delays and compensating for handicaps, but is also for the benefit and benefit of the european union as a whole.
in writing. i welcome the positioning of our assembly today. i would like to return to two essential points in this report. it was important that our assembly should express itself clearly against the commission's proposal to reduce the specific allocation for the urf by almost half. this reduction is all the more unjust because it affects a budget which finances the compensation of disabled people, who by definition are not being reduced. they are described as structural and permanent in our treaties. these regions would thus be the only territories, indeed the only ones, within the cohesion policy, which would see a reduction in their funds which would not be justified by an effect of growth, a change in the category of regions. secondly, i would like to stress the request we made for a comparative analysis of price formation in these territories. economic mechanisms that are contrary to the principles of the single market seem to be at work here and regularly lead to extremely worrying social movements. we must have better informed and more targeted action in this area to meet the urgent needs of the people.
in writing. i welcomed with enthusiasm the statement by the high representative of the european union, catherine ashton, in favour of the creation of a post of eu special representative on human rights. with this vote, i wanted to emphasise that, as the rapporteur points out, to be a credible actor in external relations, the european union must act consistently, but also as an example, and avoid double standards between human rights policy and other policies, both internal and external. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.
in writing. the european union's foreign policy must above all be based on promoting the values that have made europe what it is today. that is why i supported the adoption of this report, which defends these humanist and republican values, but also monitors the proper allocation of european funds in this area. promoting our values is important, but controlling the budget we allocate is equally important. however, i could not support certain points which give a wrong interpretation of the role played by france in the negotiations.
in writing. the european parliament once again takes a position on the external relations of the european union. parliament is alarmed by the many violations of human dignity, but the report as a whole is nonetheless ideological in that it calls for european action which will be ineffective and bureaucratic by nature. the proposals on "digital diplomacy" and "sustainable democracy" may leave us with a hint of caution, to say the least. the principled support for "bloggers" and other "activists" (new heroes of human rights-ism) is two-edged. the european parliament, far from the euphoric speeches of some leaders on the democratic aspirations of the maghreb and the middle east, expresses its concern (albeit belatedly) about the persecution of minorities, especially christians, in these regions of the world. however, diplomacy and international relations must remain the exclusive competence of the states.
in writing. there is a need to develop a genuine common eu strategy on human rights. as the report stresses, this new strategy must be based on clear actions, a pre-established timetable and an effective distribution of responsibilities, which will include clarification of the roles of the council and the european parliament in this area. the two-sided attitudes between human rights policies and foreign policies should be avoided, particularly in relation to asylum policy. the integration of the protection of human rights into the different policies of the union, in particular its external actions and its cooperation and development strategy, is still imperfect and will require greater collaboration with civil society. finally, the prospect of future accession of the european union, as an autonomous entity, to the european convention on human rights is to be welcomed.

mr president, commissioner, mr president of the commission, just as much as the recovery of public finances, the question of growth is at the heart of the success of the european strategy. what would be the role of the ecb, which has shown extraordinary creativity during the financial crisis? let's not get this wrong. it is not a question of any revision of the treaty, which is totally unrealistic. the aim is to create the right political conditions for the ecb to step up its action by buying up sovereign debt on the secondary market and injecting liquidity into the financial system. experience shows that this is possible within the current legal framework without undermining the ecb's independence or its tasks. it is a question of european solidarity and political will, not of legal status. but the recovery of public finances and the prevention of crisis risks remain imperative. the economic government of the euro area is being strengthened. the mechanisms for detecting, preventing and sanctioning misconduct have been strengthened by the six-pack. the two-pack is under negotiation and it is important that we reach a conclusion quickly. the negotiations must in particular make it possible to develop effective concrete measures for the benefit of member states in difficulty or with excessive deficits. in this respect, we must ensure that democratic control is normally exercised at european level to make the measures taken in this context acceptable to the population, to the citizens. finally, i would like to stress the value of the commission's proposal being supplemented by a legal protection system for a state in very serious difficulties - not to encourage laxity but, on the contrary, to enable it to recover and meet its obligations - this status being controlled by the commission under the control of the council and parliament.

in writing. we had resisted so far in 2004 and 2007, but this time the ep gave the green light to the eu-us agreement on the transfer of air passengers' personal data (pnr), despite the opposition claimed by rapporteur sophia in't veld. in line with mrs int'veld's warning, i rejected this new agreement, which completely destroys the safeguards necessary to ensure the protection of personal data and the respect for passengers' privacy. the agreement is based, for the most part, on blind trust in the us authorities. in concrete terms, the "nominative passenger" data will be kept for 15 years, and in anonymous form for an indefinite period, without any real judicial recourse outside the territory of the united states. it is a denial of individual liberties and a legal aberration. such processing of passenger data is simply unacceptable and incompatible with the principles of proportionality and purpose, since personal and commercial data of an undetermined number of non-suspect persons are processed for security and counter-terrorism purposes. the concern remains as to the precedent this agreement sets for future agreements of this kind with third countries.
