in writing. the new pnr agreement with the united states provides satisfactory additional guarantees in the field of data protection, while at the same time strengthening the fight against terrorism. it gives european citizens a right of access, rectification of their personal data and a right of appeal. the transmission of data on european citizens will be strictly controlled and may only be carried out for the purposes of combating terrorism or serious transnational crime. the agreement also strengthens the security of european citizens by allowing the european union to benefit from us analyses of terrorist risks. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the agreement is implemented.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new pnr agreement because it strikes a balance between data protection and the security of european citizens. the united states, a historic partner, and europe share the same goal: the fight against terrorism. but as a member of the european parliament, i will continue to ensure that our high level of privacy protection is the standard in any agreement signed by the european union. finally, a rejection would be tantamount to leaving a legal vacuum for airlines and passengers. without the endorsement of europe, the united states would have preferred bilateral agreements. and the safeguards would have been insufficient for european passengers. it was to defend all these fundamental freedoms that the agreement had to be adopted.
in writing. i voted in favour of the international agreement between the european union and the united states on the use of 'passenger data'. the agreement approved today by the european parliament will create a clear legal framework for the exchange of such data. it is the result of long negotiations with our american partners and it provides far more guarantees for european citizens than the temporary agreement which has been in force until now. the tragedy in toulouse has shown us that we cannot slacken our efforts in the fight against terrorism ! this must be a priority for the european union and it can only be achieved through mutual help and close cooperation with our american partners. it is our duty to guarantee the highest level of security for european citizens.
in writing. the european parliament has a consultative power on taxation matters. in this case, we were consulted on the accis. it is not a question of having a common tax, the setting up of which remains the responsibility of the member states, but of having a common basis of calculation. the replacement of 27 tax bases by a single tax base will make it possible to strengthen the functioning of the internal market. from now on, companies will calculate their taxable profits on the basis of a common set of rules. i therefore voted in favour of such a scheme.
in writing. i approved the report by my colleague marianne thyssen, who supports the introduction of a common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb). the aim is to help businesses by harmonising the internal market. this means, for example, reducing paperwork (businesses will now have only one tax return to complete for all their activities in the european union, and their only contact will be the tax administration of the country where their head office is located). the cost of complying with 27 different tax systems will be greatly reduced. it will also make the eu more attractive to foreign investors by offering a single taxation system. we went further than the commission's proposal, in wanting this tax to become compulsory after five years for all companies, except for smes for whom it would remain optional because we have to protect them from any additional costs.
in writing. one of the causes of the current crisis in europe is the lack of fiscal coordination. we voted in favour of consolidating the common corporate tax base (ccctb) to establish a set of rules for calculating the taxable income of companies. the reform does not aim at tax harmonization, does not impose common tax rates but contributes to increased tax coordination between member states. while the commission had initially proposed a voluntary system, we felt that this system should be mandatory after a transitional period - which i fully agree with. this reform will of course be gradual: for the first five years, the ccctb will apply only to european companies and cooperatives. after a period of five years, this scheme will be extended to all enterprises except smes, which will, however, have the possibility of participating voluntarily. simplified accounting rules, reduction of bureaucracy, emphasis on economic and social aspects rather than purely fiscal considerations when companies choose their headquarters: it is high time to work in this direction to make progress in tax harmonization in europe.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this new accis scheme which allows europe to go one step further in supporting our businesses. this is an important step for businesses in our crossborder territories, since we are now removing new obstacles to their development. european companies will now be able to set up branches more easily throughout the union, while ensuring that there is no overtaxation. among the measures that will come into force, the one-stop-shop principle will make it easier for the smallest of our companies to deal with one and the same administration for all their branches, wherever they are in europe. our entrepreneurs should no longer be afraid to enter new territories outside our borders!
in writing. i voted for this report. it provides for the harmonisation of the content of the corporate tax base at european level, i.e. taxable profit, and for the possibility for companies and groups of companies operating within the internal market to add up the profits and losses of their subsidiaries located in different member states. the net result would then be distributed among these different states according to a mathematical formula and predefined factors. the european parliament has unanimously voted in favour of the gradual introduction of the mandatory nature of this consolidated common base, which is a major step forward in terms of political positioning against fiscal dumping and intra-european relocations. however, there is a key element missing in the fight against this phenomenon, because no agreement has been reached, and this was not the aim of this directive, on the tax rate per member state, which remains different. it is a political step forward, but it will be difficult for the council to take it up. this is only the first step in a long struggle to regulate the european market.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive, which aims to establish a common consolidated corporate tax base within the european union, known as accis. the common consolidated basis of assessment will be intended to apply to all undertakings established in the european union which so wish. member states will remain free to apply the tax rate they wish to the share of the accis base that would be allocated to them. the establishment of a ccctb in the european union has many advantages, both for economic operators - by eliminating tax obstacles within the internal market - and for the member states - by allowing for more transparent, and therefore healthier, tax competition between member states. these measures are in line with the work on franco-german convergence in corporate taxation, which is being pursued by nicolas sarkozy and angela merkel.
in writing. i supported this report on the establishment of a common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb). the accis is used to calculate the tax base for multinational companies and does not relate to the tax rates themselves. the introduction of such a system will reduce red tape for businesses, reduce costs linked to differences in tax systems between member states and make the eu more attractive to foreign investors.
in writing. the existence of tax rules specific to each member state of the european union is a major obstacle to the full realisation of the internal market. this is particularly true of corporation tax, where 27 different tax rates apply. this situation creates distortions of competition and is a handicap for european companies operating in more than one member state. that is why i supported the council's proposal to create a common corporate tax rate for the 27 member states of the european union.
in writing. in the field of energy taxation, the european parliament has a consultative power. in this case, the aim was to make recommendations to the council on the basis of the european commission's proposal to amend the taxation of fuels and electricity in the union. such a system would oblige the member states to respect, in their national tariffs, the differences which exist at the level of the minimum rates (principle of proportionality). this would lead to a rise in diesel prices and would be harmful to consumers and traders alike. i therefore opposed this tax neutrality.
in writing. another major topic of this plenary session was the taxation of energy products and electricity. with this revision, the commission aims to align the energy taxation framework with the eu's energy efficiency and climate change objectives. i am a member of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety and of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, which is responsible for this text. as such, i am committed on a daily basis to ensuring the best possible balance between achieving the european union's climate change objectives on the one hand and strengthening the competitiveness of our companies on the other. i personally voted against an increase in the tax on diesel and asked for a special scheme to protect those who use diesel in their daily work: farmers, transporters, taxi drivers, etc.
in writing. using the austerity period as a justification for rejecting environmental measures, the conservatives in the european parliament decided to postpone indefinitely the commission's proposal to remove tax benefits on certain energy and electricity products such as diesel. the majority of meps are therefore in favour of mechanisms that give a benefit to polluting fuels in the european energy taxation system. i denounce this competition, manufactured by hand, between social measures and environmental measures. i am committed to an ambitious environmental policy and i voted against mrs lulling's report. this report has oversimplified the commission's proposal to discredit it by explaining that the commission's draft directive on taxation would have a negative impact on social terms due to the increase in the prices of coal, natural gas, oil and diesel. false, since the aim is not to penalise diesel specifically, but to tax fuels neutrally, so that all fuels compete on the basis of their benefits and not their taxation.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report on the taxation system for energy products and electricity in the european union. parliament has clearly shown that co2 emissions are harmful and that it is not reasonable, in a crisis, to tax energy consumption alone heavily. i note that the report as adopted takes a position in favour of taxation which is as fair as possible and which does not penalise diesel consumers. i believe that the objective of reducing co2 emissions should not be a brake on activity. i expect the council to follow the european parliament's position. this is the case for the competitiveness of companies and the purchasing power of european citizens.
in writing. i voted against the lulling report and against the european directive on energy taxation. not that it's unusual to tax energy, but it's already heavily taxed at the national level. the text will increase the tax burden by adding a tax on co2 emissions to a general tax on energy consumption. the french government, incidentally, is in favour of imposing this "carbon tax" at european level, knowing full well that it will raise the price of gasoline or heating for millions of impoverished citizens. the greatest flaw in this report is the alignment of the tax rates for products subject to the same use. in short, diesel taxed like gasoline, still with government support and a potential increase of 20 cents a litre at the pump. with the blessing of the french government, it's a bad blow to the french auto industry. as for you, my dear colleagues, you have shown a singular hypocrisy. you approved all this in committee and you reject some of it, the most annoying part, in plenary. it is not a question of substance, since you agree with it: it is just a question of avoiding problems before the elections! and to hand the baby over to the council...
in writing. the european parliament was consulted on the reform of the taxation system for energy products and electricity. i voted in favour of mrs lulling's report, but i believe that in order to be understood and accepted by the citizens, this development must be gradual, taking account of the current socioeconomic realities. however, the cost of fuel is already a major burden on household incomes, and some households have begun to adjust their consumption patterns. that is why i opposed the principle of 'proportionality' between the different thresholds applicable to each type of energy, which would have the potential to increase the cost of diesel, a fuel widely used in france, very sharply. europe's environmental objectives must not be achieved at the expense of the objectives of employment, competitiveness and consumer protection, but they must all go hand in hand. the council, which alone has the power to take decisions on taxation, should hear this message from the members of parliament.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of mrs lulling's report on the reform of the taxation system for energy products and electricity in the european union. the draft directive proposes to revise the minimum rates of energy taxation. the methodology proposed by the european commission would have led to considering energy as bad in principle, whereas emissions are harmful. it would have led to a substantial increase in excise duties on diesel fuel in most member states, notably in france. we have been very active in preventing excessive taxation of diesel vehicles which would harm consumers, our farmers and the competitiveness of our companies, particularly in the energy and road sectors. although only consulted, the european parliament has sent a clear signal to the council: we want a green europe, but also a europe that protects our competitiveness, our jobs and the purchasing power of europeans.
in writing. i have supported this report on the revision of the rules governing energy taxation in the european union, to which the european parliament is contributing through a consultation procedure. the aim of this revision is to bring the framework for the taxation of energy products into line with the objectives pursued at european level in the field of energy efficiency and the fight against global warming. i particularly opposed the continuation of the proportionality principle proposed by the european commission, as this would lead to a significant increase in the tax rate of diesel (and therefore its price) by aligning it with the tax rate of petrol, which would have negative consequences both for european consumers and for the european automobile industry.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report and even more so of amendment no 53 which abolishes proportionality, i.e. the commission's proposal to tax fuels on the basis of their energy efficiency and not on the basis of the pollution generated by their combustion. according to this logic, diesel, which offers better energy efficiency than petrol, should have been taxed more heavily (390 euros per tonne against 359 euros for petrol). in this period of constantly rising fuel prices, it was necessary to defend the purchasing power of the french, who use diesel engines more than their european neighbours.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague astrid lulling on the reform of the taxation system for energy products and electricity in the european union. in view of the successive crises that have hit the world economy and our continent hard, we here express our disagreement with the commission's proposal to change the energy taxation system in the eu, which could lead to a significant increase in the price of diesel at the pump. with this report, we, the members of the european parliament, are taking a firm stand to preserve the purchasing power of our citizens and to maintain the competitiveness of our companies. the report thus emphasizes the need to meet the legitimate expectations of economic operators, consumers and farmers, who all use diesel fuel for their activities.
in writing. for the period 2020-2030, europe has set itself ambitious targets for reducing greenhouse gases. we want to increase the share of renewable energy in production, and reduce the use of fossil fuels that are too harmful. the protection of the environment is a fundamental issue for the maintenance of a certain quality of life for future generations. but this will not be achieved by putting a burden on purchasing power today, or by threatening a whole section of the economy of our countries from the outset, especially in the midst of the crisis. it is by conducting an educational and incentive policy that we will change the habits of our way of life. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution as a whole, because it is a duty, but against the principle of proportionality, which would have caused fuel prices to explode in the coming years.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the taxation of energy products which adapts the structure of energy taxation to support the objective of a low-carbon economy which is also energy efficient. the report does not, however, provide for excessive taxation of diesel, which would have a serious impact on consumers, farmers and the competitiveness of european companies. in this period of economic crisis, i believe that a rise in the price of diesel would have been an irresponsible decision, the main victim of which would have been the purchasing power of millions of europeans.
in writing. i voted against this revision of the directive to prevent distortions of competition in the energy sector. theoretically, the aim is to establish common rules on taxation and permitted exemptions by setting minimum rates, essentially based on the amount of energy consumed, above which member states are free to determine their taxation rates. a co2 related element is introduced to support the goal of a low carbon economy. the objective is commendable but it overlooks two essential points. firstly, the harmonization of european taxation standards removes the possibility for member states to exempt certain sectors from energy taxation, particularly in the transport sector. consequently, the increase in transport costs will affect the economically disadvantaged in the first place. secondly, energy taxation will be a burden for households: like vat, it can only be socially unfair. the fight against climate change, and more generally environmental protection, must not forget social justice if it is to be effective and efficient.
in writing. at a time when refueling has never been so expensive, it would be foolish to impose an additional 23 cents on the price of a litre of gasoline at the pump. i therefore welcome the vote of our assembly, which rejected an unjustified tax increase and refused to tax not only the co2 emissions of diesel but also its energy efficiency. this was an ecological aberration, since it amounted to taxing diesel 9% more than petrol. in other words, we would have taxed the most efficient and therefore cleanest energy. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. i have no doubt that the council will follow our advice and reject this measure, which, as you will have understood, would be to the detriment of purchasing power, employment and, ironically, the environment.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which calls for a strengthening of european tax systems to combat tax fraud and evasion. this requires increased use of information exchange tools and better cooperation between tax authorities.
in writing. i voted in favour of a resolution calling for the concrete mobilisation of eu actors against tax fraud and evasion. we need to review our tax systems and, imperatively, make them more effective and efficient. unjustified exemptions must be eliminated, the tax base widened, the tax burden on labour reduced, tax collection improved, tax evasion fought, the fight against tax evasion and avoidance, particularly with regard to third countries, intensified and reported for june 2012. all the measures we are asking for here in the european parliament, such as the common consolidated corporate tax base, can play a role in combating tax evasion. europe, in this time of crisis, must, more than ever, help itself to climb the ladder.
in writing. the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion is a major political issue today. in addition to reducing public expenditure, the fight against tax evasion must help to find a way out of the current economic crisis. as demonstrated by greece, which is in the midst of an economic slump, tax evasion represents a considerable loss of revenue for the state due to uncollected revenues. the european union must act urgently as national policies have failed to produce any tangible results. the commission's action must focus on combating tax havens, in particular by developing a comprehensive strategy focusing on transparency. it is high time that the european union put in place concrete measures to make tax evasion more difficult and to prevent the use of tax havens which refuse to cooperate with foreign tax authorities. in this resolution we also call for the rapid implementation of better cooperation and coordination in tax matters not only between the member states of the european union but also with third countries. it's about social justice in our state.
in writing. i voted in favour of the martin report because i believe that democratic monitoring and control are fundamental elements that the european union must implement. i share the rapporteur's view that parliament's committees of inquiry must be given sufficient resources. it is a question of their effectiveness and credibility. i also welcome the new powers granted to the committees of inquiry, such as the possibility of carrying out in situ investigations and the greater ease of using witness interviews.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this resolution which calls for the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion to be strengthened. the text calls for greater transparency and stricter controls to prevent the use of tax havens. it is in line with the conclusions of the g20 in cannes, which were adopted at the instigation of the president of the french republic, nicolas sarkozy.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on strengthening the fight against tax fraud and evasion because it stresses key points such as strengthening the automatic exchange of information, increasing cooperation between member states and coordination between tax systems, and also strengthening transparency and developing stricter controls to avoid resorting to tax havens.
in writing. this report is a step in the right direction, but the findings are not enough. no reference is made to european tax havens (andorra, monaco, lichtenstein, etc.) or to the european parliament's desire to abolish them. these european tax havens are places where tax evasion is a crime, and we must tackle them. there is no reference to the problem of shell companies which artificially set up their headquarters in a state where they have only a letterbox, in order to avoid the taxation and tax rules of the state in which they operate. there is no reference to the insufficient resources allocated to the fight against tax evasion and avoidance, which are the only effective means of combating tax evasion. without adequate means nothing can be solved. no denunciation of the arrangements allowing for the taxation of companies with their headquarters in europe and which make their profits mainly abroad (cope niche), a system which allows companies, such as total, to be taxed almost entirely in france. tax dumping, tax evasion and tax fraud are not over in the european union, and they have a bright future ahead of them.
in writing. tax fraud and evasion represent a significant loss of revenue for eu member state governments because of the uncollected revenues they generate, increasing member states' deficit and debt levels, and reducing the funds available to boost public investment, growth and employment. it is crucial that action be taken to prevent such phenomena, and it is with this in mind that i have supported this resolution.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the call for concrete solutions to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. tax fraud and tax evasion represent a significant cost to the governments of the member states of the european union. this loss of revenue contributes to increasing the levels of public deficit and debt of member states and therefore reduces the public funds available to stimulate public investment, growth and employment. the resolution also stresses the importance of widespread exchange of information between the european union and third countries in order to put an end to banking secrecy.
for the gue/ngl group madam president, there are a few of us in this house who consider human rights to be fundamental values not only for the european union and its citizens but for all of humanity. the echr, like the universal declaration of human rights, was born out of the horrors of world war ii to protect citizens, including from the drift of states and their governments. western european countries have been particularly affected. they have been pioneers in this field for a long time. however, in recent years, particularly since the attacks of 11 september 2001, respect for human rights in these countries has declined. the judgments of the european court of human rights are there to show this. an increasing number of member states are convicted more and more regularly. the accession of the european union to the echr is therefore a symbol and we can see that for a number of member states article 6 of the treaty was just a piece of paper. there are debates about what is european law and what is national law and there is the question of the compatibility of the european charter of fundamental rights with the echr, with some member states seeking to reinstate the reservations they made to the charter in the debates on accession to the echr, whereas all member states are parties to the convention. so what's the problem? there are those who say that accession to the european union should not call into question the competences of the cjeu. having been involved in numerous meetings with the judges of this court, i also do not see where the problem lies. the ecj has been integrating fundamental rights into its case-law since 1970. the integration of the charter of fundamental rights into the treaty, such as accession to the echr, will help it to better enforce fundamental rights. still others are concerned about the echr's jurisdiction beyond the territory of the european union. but that is its nature and i would venture to say that it was at the time of the incorporation of article 6 that these questions should have been asked. the problem is that some member states are seeking to challenge the very content of the echr and the role of the european court of justice, and they are prepared to do anything to do so. in these benches, there are a number of us who defend a universal and indivisible concept of human rights. we reject the double standard in human rights. we believe that in order to be credible in the fight they claim to be waging internationally for human rights, the european union and its member states must begin by sweeping up their own backs. yes, the european union's accession to the echr is a symbol and all the current hesitations are symptomatic of the deviations of some member states in this area. these member states are constantly breaking their human rights obligations. it is not the court that has changed, contrary to what i have heard, but the respect for fundamental rights by the member states. for almost two years now, we have been hearing about rapid accession. it's time to act.

mr president, iter is first and foremost a huge public research effort in the framework of transdisciplinary international cooperation and mutualisation, which is new and promising. with thermonuclear fusion, this is the promise to mankind of abundant, infinitely renewable, nonpolluting, affordable, and accessible electrical energy - a promise that other forms of energy production cannot fulfill. the success of iter is all the more important for the future of mankind as the demand for electricity will continue to grow. but to succeed in iter, we must turn our backs on the predatory and destructive logic of competition and the financialisation of the energy sector. we must put an end to privatisation. the major integrated publicly owned enterprises of the 21st century must be built to meet the scientific, technological and economic challenges posed by iter and its industrialisation. we have to plan ecologically. in the energy sector, research, design, production, transport networks and distribution cannot be separated unless this leads to the worst waste, social inequalities in access to energy and the risk of major accidents.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i am pleased that this amending budget for the financing of iter was adopted by a large majority in the committee on budgets on 29 march. by financing this additional cost, we are avoiding the disruption of a strategic basic research project in which the european union plays a leading role and we are honouring our international commitments. it should be noted that none of the seven partners of the euratom community has questioned its overall contribution to the project. japan, despite the fukushima disaster, has decided to strictly respect its budgetary commitments in iter. without this agreement, hundreds of researchers would have had to suspend their work and the iter project would have suffered damaging delays. today, a thousand people work for iter in cadarache. from 2015 and until 2017-2018, the construction phase of the buildings and the assembly of the machine could involve up to 4 or 5 000 people on this site. in conclusion, mr president, iter is a pride of europe and a symbol of our excellence.
in writing. at the end of 2011, the 2012 budget procedure was marked by strong disagreements between the parliament and the council on the financing of iter, the thermonuclear fusion research project based in cadarache, in the bouches-du-rhône. eur 750 million of additional costs compared to the initial estimates had to be found for 2012, and only eur 100 million had been agreed at the end of 2011. the only thing left to do was to find a compromise for the remaining 650 million. after lengthy negotiations with the council, parliament succeeded in getting this money released by raising the financial ceiling of the budget line concerned, whereas the council had originally envisaged only funding by redeploying funds from the 7th framework programme for research and development. the additional financial needs for the iter project in 2012 will therefore be available without compromising other research programmes. the commission is also proposing to increase the number of member states that have not yet adopted the euro by a factor of two. it is our duty to ensure that the iter project is not financed at the expense of other priority policies of the eu 2020 strategy.

organisations must be heard and supported. secondly, measures of protection and training which enable a virtuous cycle to be established for women, from victims to agents of change. thirdly, in writing. the resolution on the situation in burma was adopted by a large majority in the european parliament and i welcome that. in this resolution, my colleagues and i acknowledge that, despite some irregularities reported during the pre-election period, the elections on 1 april were conducted in a transparent and credible manner. we also reaffirm our respect for the decades of struggle of the great opposition figure, aung san suu kyi, winner of the sakharov prize, and congratulate her on her election victory. finally, we welcome mrs ashton's decision to establish a diplomatic presence in the country and to inaugurate the european union office during her next official visit.
in recent months, burma has made more progress towards democracy and peace than in the past decades. the parliamentary by-elections held on 1 april 2012, widely regarded as free and fair by the international community, are a sign that burma is on the path to democratic change. this development opens up important prospects for the establishment of much better relations between the european union and burma. however, the next general elections, due to take place in 2015, will be the real test of whether the burmese authorities really want to democratize the country. in the meantime, caution is in order. the report of the un special rapporteur on human rights in burma highlights the serious human rights concerns - hundreds of political prisoners are still being held there today. the text of this resolution on the situation in burma seems to me to be balanced. it acknowledges the recent efforts made by the country, but also reflects my concerns, particularly with regard to the situation of the burmese political prisoners. i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. burma is on the path to democratic change. this is the main message contained in the resolution on the situation in burma voted by meps in plenary. the elections on 1 april marked the victory of the party of the historic oppositionist aung san su kyi. the elections, which are considered free and fair by the international community, consolidate the reforms undertaken by the burmese government for more than a year (release of political prisoners, demobilization of former combatants, actions in favour of freedom of expression). in this text we have sought to highlight the unique opportunity that exists to build a special relationship with burma. although encouraging, recent developments are not enough to rule out all risks. the european parliament therefore encouraged the council to suspend, rather than lift, the restrictive measures against burma (with the exception of the arms embargo).
in writing. as an environmentalist, i voted against this resolution which prioritizes the economic and geostrategic interests of a european company over the social and environmental rights of the argentine people. repsol has always put an extractive model at the forefront, ignoring all other considerations. the argentine state therefore has every right to decide sovereignly on the management of its resources and its energy policy, even if this is not a guarantee of exemplary behaviour in this area. the european union and spain should instead focus on investing their economic, political and diplomatic resources massively in promoting a new energy and development model based on renewable energy and reducing dependence on fossil fuels.
in writing. i supported the resolution on the legal security of european investments outside the european union. the argentine government announced on monday, april 16, its intention to nationalize the ypf subsidiary of the spanish repsol group. the takeover of ypf must be done through the passage of a bill in the argentine congress. the spanish company demands 8 billion euros for the redemption of its shares, an amount that the argentine government does not seem to be ready to accept. the resolution aims to clarify the situation for disputes over bilateral contracts concluded before the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. it provides that, until the adoption of the regulation ensuring the stability of these bilateral agreements concluded before the treaty of lisbon, member states and their operators must manage their investment disputes and any retaliatory measures themselves.
in writing. since the beginning of the plenary session, we have seen a surreal reaction from the european institutions to the argentine government's decision to nationalise the shares of the spanish company repsol in the hydrocarbon company ypf. with this decision, the argentine government has only reversed the privatization of the main argentine oil company by the ultra-liberal government of carlos menem in the 1990s. the european parliament resolution attacks the decision of a sovereign state with the sole motivation of protecting european investments. it is perfectly legitimate for a sovereign state to nationalize companies which do not respect their commitments to economic development and respect for human rights and which favour the interests of their shareholders over the interests of national workers. argentina has made a political choice for the benefit of the argentineans and the public interest of the country. so it is not "political interference in the free market". asking for sanctions is nonsense. the european union would be more credible in calling for such sanctions in the event of human rights violations, as in colombia.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this report, which welcomes the reforms implemented within the european commission to streamline the running costs of delegations while ensuring a better allocation of funds allocated to third countries. the european union can no longer afford to help third countries with european taxpayers' money without properly checking that it is being used properly. as the report points out, the commission must improve its own control instruments governing its interventions and behave more responsibly in this area.
in writing. i voted in favour of the kaczmarek report. this own-initiative report deals with the impact of the decentralisation of external aid management from the commission's central services to the european union delegations. it first recalled the objectives of decentralising external aid: speeding up the deployment of aid, increasing the reliability of financial management procedures and improving the quality of aid in the partner countries. it noted that there had been marked improvements in the way assistance was provided (more efficiency and speed), and encouraged the commission to continue its efforts.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which takes a positive view of the commission's decentralisation of the management of the european union's external aid from its central services to its delegations. this report highlights the main benefits of decentralisation, namely increased aid effectiveness and speed of response. it called on the commission to continue its efforts. the committee also called for better evaluation of the quality and results of the eu's financial interventions, which would, in its view, make the eu more accountable and ensure greater visibility of its actions.
in writing. i supported this report because it highlights the positive effects of decentralisation on the management of external aid, already highlighted in the court of auditors' 2011 report, in particular the acceleration of the deployment of aid or the improvement of the quality of aid in the recipient countries as well as the effectiveness of that aid. it is also an idea that i have long supported: in my view, eu delegations in third countries are best placed to judge when, how and on which projects eu aid can bring real added value. for example, i introduced this concept in the resolution on the reform of the european neighbourhood policy adopted in april 2011. however, the commission needs to make further efforts to improve the way it assesses the quality and results of its interventions and, above all, to further strengthen its links with each of its delegations. better coordination will make aid more effective and, more generally, better information exchange between the commission's headquarters and its delegations will make european policy in this field even more relevant.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which takes into account the role and place of women in the fight against climate change. in many countries they are a high-risk population and will suffer the consequences. i particularly welcome the inclusion in this report of an important reminder: the transition to a green economy will only happen with more women scientists and engineers. the report also recalls our ambition to see quotas for women in senior positions, particularly in the context of climate diplomacy. while this report focuses solely on the situation of women, it should not make us forget the situation of other populations particularly exposed to climate change.
in writing. according to a study by the london school of economics and the max planck institute, women are the main victims of climate change and are more likely than men to die in natural disasters. furthermore, 75% to 80% of the world's refugees are women and children, and climate change is increasing these movements of people and very often their precariousness. that is why i voted in favour of the kiil-nielsen report on women and climate change, because the european parliament must demonstrate that the gender dimension must be taken into account and integrated into european policies to combat climate change. the approach and measures proposed in this report are relevant whether it is the introduction of a minimum quota of 40% of women in the european delegations in charge of climate negotiations, the collection of data by gender, awareness raising during the evaluation or launch phases of projects on climate change, investments for increasing financial independence and the means of empowering women within their community...
in writing. i supported my colleague nicole kiil-nielsen's report on women and climate change. this own-initiative report calls for gender to be taken into account in the fight against climate change.
in writing. the consequences of climate change affect women more than men because they are more vulnerable. climate change is fuelling the development of these discriminations. however, the emerging green economy is a source of hope. there is still time to fully integrate women into this green economy. i support this report because it raises the need to strengthen women's training capacity. i believe that access to education and the raising of the level of education of women is a necessary prerequisite for reducing their vulnerability. it was therefore appropriate for parliament to alert the commission, the council of the european union and the member states and to call on them to take action in this regard. i therefore voted in favour of this report because it encourages member states and institutions to continue to support projects in developing countries. the resolution also recommends that the commission establish indicators to assess the impact of the projects we support and to raise awareness of the impact of climate change on the situation of women.
in writing. although i believe that the implementation of a biodiversity strategy is very important, i voted against this report, which is flawed on certain specific points concerning fisheries. i also hope that the european parliament will follow the advice of the johannesburg and nagoya conferences which propose to achieve maximum sustainable yield by 2015 if possible, if not 2020. that is the position i support. the report also gives inaccurate figures, particularly on the number of stocks fished beyond maximum sustainable yield today. i also believe that the reform of the common fisheries policy is based on an undefined and unproven principle, namely the alleged overcapacity of the european fleet. i think that since there are no figures on fishing capacity, there can be no policies based on overcapacity.
in writing. the final text submitted to parliament for a vote ignores a number of scientific findings and remains a caricature of agricultural issues, showing a lack of awareness of the agricultural reality, that of 13.5 million european farmers. i believe that the cap must remain an economic and social policy as well as an environmental policy.
in writing. while the general objectives of the report are laudable (protecting biodiversity), i could not support the adoption of this report, which calls for a break in the traditional organization of the cap: greening the agricultural policy falls exclusively within the 'second pillar' and should not, at this stage, concern the first pillar. european farmers are already facing many constraints and are making many efforts to green their practices. it is important not to impede their production any further, at a time when it is essential to preserve european production capacity and our food independence.
in writing. i voted against this report because, while fully aware of the importance and richness of biodiversity, it seems to me that the text is nonetheless excessively important and may unfairly stigmatise certain areas. i think that the passages concerning the common agricultural policy and the common fisheries policy are problematic: agriculture and fisheries should not be seen as intrinsically bad for biodiversity. we must instead take a more constructive view of their role in protecting and enhancing biodiversity, because the actors in these sectors have a vital part to play. the role of certain groups, such as hunters, is therefore presented in this report as negative, even though hunting plays a very important role in the management of biodiversity in our natural areas. despite some positive elements (the emphasis on better collection and sharing of scientific data, for example), this report does not seem to me to promote a balanced and fair view of the role of the various actors in our society in protecting biodiversity.
in writing. i deeply regret that the european union has not achieved the target it set for 2010. europe has a very high biodiversity both in terms of habitat and animal species, which must be protected. ecosystems are part of our cultural heritage and make the european territory unique. i voted in favour of the report on biodiversity because it advocates an active approach to environmental protection. in agriculture, biodiversity and the promotion of more sustainable agriculture are considered in a complementary way, without in any way detrimental to each other. the resolution also calls for the pooling of resources, the means of combating damage to biodiversity and the pooling of available scientific resources. it is important to understand that no country can tackle the problems of biodiversity loss alone and that this pooling of our efforts is a necessity. i also strongly support the international dimension of this text.
in writing. following the failure of the strategy to halt the erosion of biodiversity in 2010, and in response to the european parliament's request in september 2010, the european commission presented a new strategy for 2020. the report lists a large number of actions, but these are too often limited to good intentions without giving the means, including financial, to achieve its ambitions. the report is also not sufficiently critical of the current tools that are damaging to biodiversity, particularly in the areas of the cap and international trade. i therefore do not think that this new strategy is up to the mark. i therefore abstained, regretting the eu's lack of ambition in the face of the increasingly alarming situation in terms of biodiversity.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the environment action programmes have been a powerful driver for the adoption of sound environmental legislation in the european union. that is why i think it is important to look to the future now and to set concrete targets for 2020 and a vision for 2050. if we want to build a dynamic and environmentally friendly europe, we must have a long-term perspective, so that all economic and social actors can take the necessary measures without being short-changed or destabilised. one of our priorities must be to implement properly existing environmental legislation, which is not always respected. finally, it is important to communicate our intentions, because citizens need to know where europe is going in terms of environmental protection. our environmental policy must set an example for our non-european partners by being realistic, coherent and fully integrated into our growth objectives, without causing panic among our economic actors.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague jo leinen on the seventh european environment action programme. since the early 1970s, the environment action programmes have guided the development of european union policy and have helped to move towards strong and coherent european environmental legislation. the report calls on the commission to present rapidly a proposal for a seventh action programme with concrete and ambitious long-term objectives. it proposes that the programme be based on three main lines: strengthening environmental legislation, integrating environmental objectives into all sectoral policies and the international dimension of environmental protection.
in writing. our environment is constantly under threat. i am particularly concerned about our unsustainable consumption patterns. to move, to enlighten ourselves, our daily gestures have an even larger carbon footprint. improving the energy efficiency of the products we use every day must therefore be encouraged. at the same time, fossil fuel reserves are dwindling and we are increasingly dependent on the countries that supply us. the next eu environment strategy focuses on reducing our dependence on oil and gas by promoting the development of renewable energy. this 7th environment action programme, which was put to our vote, also calls on the member states to better implement the existing body of legislation in the field of water. this is a strong signal for improving water quality in europe. finally, this revision of the existing programme sees the green economy as a great source of jobs and growth, which will enable us to achieve our goals for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in europe by 2020. it is for all these reasons that i voted in favour of this new environmental strategy.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the general thrust of the report and the three main priorities of the 7th environment action programme: - implementation and strengthening of environmental legislation; - integration of environmental objectives into all sectoral policies; - the international dimension of environmental protection. the european institutions must do all they can to strengthen environmental legislation and integrate environmental protection into other union policies. i abstained on paragraph 65 of the report, which calls for a shift from taxation of labour to the protection of resources and the fight against pollution. tax reform to be effective must be comprehensive. and as expressed here, such a transfer can only result in the maintenance of the present tax rates. once again, we must put the fine talk into practice.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today we are celebrating europe. this holiday of 9 may is of particular importance at a delicate moment in the economic, but above all political, construction of europe. the progress made by our countries since the signing of the robert schuman declaration is often forgotten. yet never in our history have we experienced such an area of peace and prosperity despite the current crisis. we europeans have paid a high price to understand that there is no difference between our neighbours and us. we know the value of tolerance, dialogue and solidarity, which take precedence over individualism. the rise of extremes and the temptation of populism are a challenge to us. just as right-wing populism has no place in europe, so does left-wing populism. i urge all mainstream political parties to remember that they have nothing to gain and everything to lose by trivializing extremes. intellectual shortcuts and easy solutions are nothing but demagogy. they only feed the illusions of our citizens, who are quickly disappointed. and how, in this context, can europe's democratic deficit be reduced? as i said, europe is going through a difficult period and the decisions of the coming months will be decisive for the stability of our economies and for the social cohesion of our countries. the debt crisis, the attacks on our currency in the markets in recent times, have at least had the merit of making us aware of the drift of public finances in several european countries for decades. we have shown at parliament's level, with the six-pack, with the budgetary package and soon also with the two-pack, that europe has shown the courage to take matters into its own hands and correct this trend. but we are only at the beginning of our efforts and we must not let up. i have to say, what worries me most is this current political debate between national fiscal consolidation and growth. in fact, beyond the caricatures, there are no pro-management and pro-growth groups in europe, simply because they are two sides of the same coin, as i have often said here in this house. the reality is that we cannot separate deficit reduction from growth, and you said it. there will be no sustainable growth without reducing our debt, and that reduction will be even faster the stronger the growth. the reality is that growth-promoting measures cannot be synonymous with additional expenditure. we can't afford to do that anymore. the reality is that as long as the countries with the highest expenditure do not pursue a policy of debt reduction, the countries which are making an effort to manage their affairs properly will no longer be willing to show solidarity. ladies and gentlemen, investment and growth will come from trust. and i'm not talking about artificial growth. there is only one way to do this: by making our economies more competitive in a globalised world. europe has a promising future if we all take our responsibilities and implement the decisions already taken. we know very well what is needed: to complete the single market, to invest in research and development to continue to play a leading role in the economies of the 21st century and to reduce administrative burdens to unlock the potential of our smes and our companies. in this way, and by improving our public finances, we will guarantee growth and create the jobs of the future. the declaration of robert schuman has opened a new way for europeans. now more than ever we are connected to each other. we are in solidarity, we are responsible to each other, and this implies budgetary convergence, which is under way, but also fiscal and social convergence. but this solidarity can only work if everyone makes an effort and is willing to combine sound public finances and sustainable growth. you know that robert schuman's declaration has brought us a peace plan, which is a success. let's say it too. but i would like to end with these words: solidarity, responsibility, enthusiasm, conviction and let us have a plan for the future, for growth and for jobs.

mr president, after visiting the field in july 2011, i was of course deeply moved, as were all my colleagues, by the stories, the journeys, the courage, the path traveled by these men, women and children who suffered, arriving every day in italy on the island of lampedusa, before being crammed into detention centres in painful conditions, sometimes defying all humanity, flouting all human dignity, far from the european dream so coveted. there are both questions that arise and long-term political effects. questions: following our visits, we all complained about the lack of information and today, after a year, we still lack information. how are new arrivals handled? how many people have arrived? what are the conditions under which they are housed today? how many have been transferred to other centres or to the mainland and what about the programmes on the island itself? we would like to know how the italian authorities have used the more than 232 million euros that have been given to them to be able to respond to this difficult situation. but there are also long-term political effects. apart from the fact that the italian island with its dream beaches will forever be dramatically famous the island of all hopes for the arrival of these many mediterranean boat people , i regret that this lampedusa crisis has brought us to where we are today. this migration crisis was caused by the unfortunate management of the arrival of these migrants, which led to the famous france-italy episode, to the granting of temporary residence permits to migrants by italy, and then to the closure of borders by france and mr sarkozy, leading to a dramatic result for europe and the construction of europe, to a debate, which is now highly politicized, on the schengen area, and to a situation where europeans no longer like europe because of schengen and where this is reflected in the ballot box. so we need a real policy ...
in writing. concrete and realistic proposals: this report is the pragmatic counterpart to the commission's communications following the 2011 democratic movements in the arab world. the rapporteur stresses the need for a coordinated, flexible and proactive eu policy, and in this respect he echoes the aspirations of civil society in the southern mediterranean countries. i would add, however, that the economic integration which the eu advocates and wants to develop must above all focus on south-south economic integration. the european commission, in its communications, considers that economic integration necessarily requires integration into the european market. i believe that this is only the second step: once the markets of the countries of the south are integrated and the eu has helped them to adapt to its technical and health standards, then access to the european internal market will be of real interest and will have a real impact on the economies of the south. i also support the rapporteur's idea of analysing, through regular impact studies, the effects of european trade policy on the economic systems of these countries. such monitoring will allow for rapid adjustment of european measures.
