in writing. i have approved the proposal to amend the regulation on protection against dumping on imports from countries not members of the european union. certain provisions were in fact contrary to the wto anti-dumping agreement and to the wto agreement itself in article xvi.4 of the wto agreement. my vote shows my commitment to wto standards. however, when the european union considers that there is unfair competition from certain foreign companies, we are not prepared to accept everything. because our companies depend on it, suppliers who import from countries which do not respect the rules of the market economy will be financially sanctioned.
in writing. on the basis of the report by portuguese mep vital moreira, i supported the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the 2009 council regulation on defence against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community. on 28 july 2011, the dispute settlement body of the world trade organisation (wto) adopted the report on appeal in the case 'european communities - final anti-dumping measures concerning certain iron or steel fasteners originating in china'. in those reports, it was found, inter alia, that article 9 (5) of the council regulation of november 2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community was incompatible with wto rules. the purpose of this legislative proposal is to implement the recommendations and decisions of the lord. i hope that the european commission and the committee on international trade have respected the principle of reciprocity.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report in order to allow the implementation of the recommendations of the dsb concerning european 'anti-dumping' arrangements. i agree with the rapporteur's amendments to the basic anti-dumping regulation and welcome the adoption of this report, as the deadlines for implementing the recommendations of the dsb will be respected. i would like to remind you that while the european union must respect the agreements reached in the wto, it is nevertheless essential to ensure that the development of our trade with china is carried out in accordance with the principle of reciprocity.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this text, which will make it possible to combat unfair competition from certain foreign companies. suppliers importing from countries which do not respect the rules of the market economy will have to pay higher customs duties at europe's borders. we must protect our companies against this distorted competition, which we can no longer tolerate!
in writing. parliament approved by a large majority the report to clarify the measures to combat subsidised imports from non-eu countries. the aim of the scheme is to bring the eu's anti-dumping measures into line with the recommendations and decisions of the dispute settlement body of the world trade organisation (wto). on 19 january 2012, the european union and china agreed to implement these recommendations within a reasonable timeframe, which is set at 12 october 2012.
in writing. this report and the amendment it endorses do not protect against abuse. it only maintains and codifies discrimination against states which do not adhere to the market economy. it targets nations that have a significant influence on prices and production, or companies in which the state is the majority shareholder. the european protectionism proposed to us serves liberalization instead of serving the interests of the citizens of europe and of third countries. not a word here against social and environmental dumping and the misuse of devaluations. that is the main thing for me. the only thing that is at issue here is the refusal to conform to the laws of the market economy and of free and undistorted competition. i am voting against this text.
in writing. in the framework of the partnership and cooperation agreement, the european community and the government of the russian federation concluded an agreement on trade in certain steel products in 2007, setting quotas. but as you know, russia recently joined the wto after almost 20 years of negotiations. we therefore no longer have any reason to impose steel import quotas, especially since the continuation of these quotas would be a violation of wto rules. this is good news for the international community and for the european union itself. the european commission estimates that additional european exports of metal and steel products will amount to approximately €107 million per year.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which provides for the repeal of council regulation (ec) no 1342/2007 on trade in certain steel products with the russian federation. i note that the european steel import quotas cannot be maintained after russia has become a member of the wto. i hope that the liberalization of bilateral trade in steel products will improve the competitiveness of the european steel industry. i believe that the repeal of this regulation could allow european union companies to improve their access to the russian market.
in writing. this approval takes note of the recent accession of russia to the wto in december 2011. the european union must maintain and develop its trade relations with that country, which must be based on mutual respect for the commitments entered into under the agreement. this decision should not, however, prevent us from remaining vigilant to possible obstacles to trade that could be maintained both in russia and within the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which draws the consequences of russia's accession to the wto. in accordance with the rules of this organization, it is in fact aimed at the total elimination of trade barriers, which the european union and russia will now have to comply with scrupulously. the reciprocal benefits and restrictions will finally be at stake with this economic partner!
in writing. the report endorses the lifting of import quotas for russian steel products in europe. in doing so, it favours large groups such as arcelor mittal, which are relocating to russia and closing down blast furnaces in france and belgium. obviously, no social or ecological considerations prevailed in this decision. i am voting against this text, which is contrary to the ecological planning which i am promoting and to the relocation of the steel industry which it implies.
in writing. for the sake of efficiency, the administration must move to the digital age. it is the guarantee of a fast, accessible and safe administration for all european citizens. it is also a way of limiting the cost of administrative procedures. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the eu, including the eu's external borders. this will make it easier for citizens to do so, and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the electronic version of the official journal of the european union will now have a legally binding character. this is an important step forward for european democracy, which confirms our desire to make the union's legislative texts visible, now accessible to the greatest number. this innovation simplifies the eu's work and at the same time saves money by eliminating paper, which makes the management of financial resources more efficient.
in writing. i have supported this new regulation, which establishes the electronic edition of the official journal as the only authentic version of the oj, replacing the paper version. the text promotes better access to european law for citizens, by recognising the major role played today by new information technologies, including the internet, in the dissemination of european law. the resulting reduction in the printing of the oj will also, in the long run, save money and reduce the environmental impact of the european institutions' activities.
in writing. i believe, as my colleagues have pointed out, that the circumstances surrounding the acts of corneliu vadim tudor are not directly or obviously connected with the performance of mr tudor's duties as a member of the european parliament and, therefore, i have decided not to defend his immunity. this decision means that the legal proceedings can continue.
in writing. regional airports in europe are too often underestimated. it is imperative that they be supported and better integrated. as my colleague philip bradbourn has pointed out, the commission tends to overlook the opportunities that regional airports represent for eu integration and prosperity. you already know my commitment to the development of europe's regions. well, these airports can help to revitalise local economies, which is what europe badly needs. in this resolution i call for the better integration of small airports into the transeuropean transport network, because they make it possible to give greater dynamism to regional networks and are a source of job creation. the increased use of regional airports would also provide relief to the major airports by reducing congestion. i also pointed out that airlines accumulate fees as they book tickets online, which is tantamount to misleading the consumer and putting regional airports at a disadvantage.
in writing. it is through spatial planning that we can strengthen social and territorial cohesion in the union. i therefore welcome this report which recalls the vital importance of regional aviation in the development of europe's regions. we want to ensure a tightly knit territory. however, the report also points out that care must be taken not to encourage the proliferation of regional airports, since this trend would ultimately run counter to the initial objectives, both in economic terms (too high costs to bear) and in environmental terms, or in terms of territorial logic (insufficient traffic). the report also provides an opportunity to highlight certain abusive practices by low-cost airlines. the restrictions on luggage, for example, deserve more scrutiny, as do the fees added to the original ticket price. consumers must be provided with high quality service, regardless of the company. this report is going in the right direction. it is now up to the european commission to make regional airports key elements of an efficient european transport network, covering the whole territory.
in writing. i have approved the bradbourn report, which aims to develop the attractiveness of regional airports. i am glad that this text recognises the driving role of airport infrastructure in regional growth and development. it seems to me important that the commission should take account of the specific features of regional airports in its legislative proposals for the air transport sector. two aspects in particular have attracted my attention: the need to reduce congestion at the main airport hubs and the need to promote interconnection of spaces. this objective is consistent with the logic of the atlantic strategy, on which i am the rapporteur.
in writing. the report has the merit of clearly and effectively highlighting the added value of regional airports as growth engines. multimodality, interconnection, these airports are the beating heart of the regions' economic activity. the report aims to give them the importance they deserve in european legislation. the european parliament, which is due to vote on the airport package in the coming weeks, is sending a strong message to the european commission today.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this text, which aims to give a special legal status to airports and regional services. the european institutions have finally understood the importance of supporting our regional airports, which actively contribute to strengthening the local economic fabric and promoting our territories. legislation cannot be made without taking account of the specific features of each airport and the expectations of the citizens. we are also sending a strong message to the european commission by asking for the inclusion of certain regional airports among the major infrastructure projects which will be eligible for european funding via the transeuropean transport network.
in writing. i voted against this report because it calls for specific attention and financial support for regional airports, without any conditions relating to safety or the environment. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods by road, rail and inland waterway, and to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods by road. these amendments were all rejected, which left me no choice but to vote against the report.
in writing. as the crisis and disparities between regions in the european union intensify, territorial cohesion must be at the heart of eu policies more than ever. it is this essential principle that i have wanted to reaffirm in voting for this report. the commission notes that the airport services agreement concluded between ryanair and ams was signed on the same day as the agreement between ryanair and ams. moreover, as we are discussing the revision of the ten-t, regional airports should be given a prominent place in this debate alongside the other major european transport hubs. this seems to me to be essential to achieve an optimal networking of the european territory.
in writing. ensuring the future of our regional airports is essential for two obvious reasons: firstly, they are strategic transport hubs that allow the horizons of traditional trade routes to be broadened, and secondly, they contribute to the development of our territories and the strengthening of the local economic fabric. i am therefore pleased that the european parliament has adopted by a large majority the report on regional airports and air services, which aims to clarify the special legal status of regional airports and to clarify certain sensitive issues such as state aid and start-up aid for airlines, the question of price transparency, the 'one-way baggage' rule and any other restrictions affecting competition.
in writing. this report rightly states that the proliferation of regional airports must be avoided. the committee also calls for the construction and extension of a regional airport to be subject to local and regional consultation, as should be the case for notre-dame-des-landes. i agree with him on that. but the text also promotes the transport of goods by air. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment against the risks arising from the use of certain substances in the manufacture of certain products. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. i cannot vote for such a text. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which underlines that european air transport policy does not currently pay enough attention to regional airports. the latter have real potential for growth. the work on the single european sky initiative must be accelerated and the specific role of regional airports in our transport networks better taken into account: they are an important source of social and economic development for regions - especially those where other forms of transport are lacking, they are an attractive pole for new businesses, and they can be a vehicle for increasing regional tourism. the report also addresses an important point for consumer protection: the practice of certain of the main low-cost airlines, namely excessive booking fees and restrictions on carry-on baggage, which discourage travellers from buying goods at airports. tackling the practice of 'single baggage' - by setting common weight limits or by capping the charges for excess baggage - will stimulate the development of retail trade at regional airports and even in the regions themselves.
in writing. discharge is the final control of the budget for a given year. after the audit and finalisation of the annual accounts, it is up to the council of the european union to issue a recommendation and then to us, the members of parliament, to decide whether or not to give discharge for the implementation of the budget for the previous financial year. this decision is based, inter alia, on an examination of the annual accounts and on the annual report of the court of auditors. discharge is therefore the political part of the external control of budget implementation. in the european parliament we were voting this week on whether or not to grant discharge to the budgets of the european institutions and agencies for the year 2010. as regards the 2010 budget of the european commission, we voted for it. however, we ask the european commission to reduce the error rate, which was up to 7.7% in the areas of cohesion, energy and transport.
in writing. i voted to discharge the european commission on the basis of the report by my excellent colleague christofer fjellner, who has done a tremendous job in difficult circumstances. i cannot understand why the european court of auditors and the 27 national audit bodies do not work together sufficiently. concerning the consolidated accounts, it is not normal to present them with negative equity and not to recognise the claim that the european union has on the member states for the pensions of staff whose debt is, moreover, provisioned for liabilities.
in writing. the european commission, through commissioner algirdas šemeta, has just shown its goodwill by finally committing itself to further implement the interinstitutional agreement. what we were asking for most was for the commission to publish the annual reports sent by the member states on their accounts. there is a regulation to improve public access to eu institutions' documents. it is a fight we are waging in the european parliament for greater transparency and closer cooperation between the institutions. it is therefore good news that the commission is listening to our requests. however, we remain vigilant and will ensure that the dissemination of documents is actually improved, because the interinstitutional agreement should have been in force for too long and we should have a real overview of the implementation of the eu budget.
in writing. i voted in favour of the discharge to the commission on budgetary implementation. i note, however, an increase in the error rate for expenditure under cohesion policy, but also for energy and transport. i fully agree with the report on increasing transparency and budgetary efficiency. i am also committed to the use of the various control mechanisms to ensure that the member states manage european funds properly.
in writing. parliament approved the european commission's budgetary expenditure for 2010 after obtaining transparency commitments. better management and more effective control systems are needed. in future, national political authorities will have to account for how european funds have been spent in their country by signing national management declarations. the financial crisis currently affecting europe is also having an impact on the eu budget. we cannot tolerate scandal or mismanagement of funds.
in writing. any budget with an error rate of more than 2% is considered by the european court of auditors to be materially flawed. however, i felt that the commission was not alone responsible, as the member states have the necessary instruments to detect some of the errors. the systematic sanction is not based on a constructive approach; i preferred to vote for discharge and to give the european commission the means to correct the mistakes.
in writing. we, the parliamentarians, are obliged to vote on whether or not to grant discharge to the other institutions and agencies of the european union. we must also conduct our own self-criticism and this time we have endorsed our own accounts. within our budget and as an example, we have europarltv, the parliament's television channel launched in 2008, which unfortunately does not attract enough european citizens. we also have a budget for hosting tens of thousands of visitors (283 000 last year). each member of parliament has the opportunity to sponsor 110 visitors per year. you can also visit my website www.sophieauconie.eu for more information!
in writing. i voted in favour of granting the european parliament discharge for the financial year 2010. i agree with the rapporteur that we need to allocate the available funds more effectively and avoid unnecessary expenditure. i note the difficulties faced by europarltv. i would like to stress, however, the importance of having adequate communication tools to keep citizens informed of the european parliament's activities.
in writing. the vote was an opportunity to revive the debate on the location of the european parliament's seat. however, this situation refers to historical references and legal texts which cannot be called into question by often erroneous attacks on the costs or damage of the dispersion of the european parliament's premises. the question of strasbourg or brussels does not arise here, since according to the treaties on which our union is historically founded, strasbourg is the rule and brussels the exception.
in writing. i abstained on the resolution accompanying the discharge for the implementation of the 2010 budget of the european parliament. while i support the general guidelines contained in this resolution, i strongly oppose two amendments (amendments nos 6 and 15) which are clearly anti-strasbourg and which have been adopted and incorporated into this resolution. the debate and attacks on the location of the european parliament's seat are coming up more and more regularly, and i am paying close attention to them. it was a symbol for a long time. but today it is above all a legal and political issue. i remain firmly committed to this ongoing fight to maintain the seat of the european parliament in our beautiful european capital. i also voted against amendment no 4, which called for the abolition of the lux prize, which is awarded annually by the european parliament to films that are at the heart of the european public debate and illustrate the universality of european values, cultural diversity and the process of european integration.

in writing. the european parliament is the eu's budgetary authority, on an equal footing with the council. this is still a hard truth for some to accept: by not voting for discharge, we want to push the council towards greater transparency. the answer to the questionnaire we send each year, the attendance at meetings and public hearings are all actions which can embody the good interinstitutional relations we expect from the council. cooperation is not a matter of course, while the european parliament shows responsibility by voting each year a budgetary discharge for each eu institution and agency - an action that is far from superfluous, as we see every year. the council should finally enter fully into this cooperation relationship between two institutions which are on an equal footing in budgetary matters.

in writing. as a member of the parliamentary committee on the environment, public health and food safety, i argued for the discharge to be given to efsa, the european food safety authority. very involved in the european parliament on food safety issues, i visited efsa to better understand the functioning of the agency, discuss its scientific opinions and raise the issue of its financial management. i have seen the quality of the work carried out by this agency. however, a majority of my colleagues have asked for the vote to be postponed in order to investigate possible conflicts of interest affecting the functioning of the vote. the deferral now gives the european parliament time to audit the agency's accounts in more detail.
in writing. a sure sign: on the day we vote to discharge efsa, the chair of the agency's board of directors resigns. the reason: she had accepted a job in an industrial lobby, which was incompatible with her job at the european agency. unfortunately, this is not the only instance of conflict of interest in the agency: some managers, for example, joined pro-gmo companies after leaving efsa, or, conversely, are now responsible for efsa while they were part of pro-gmo lobbies. these conflicts of interest must end! the agencies which we consider to be independent, and which have been set up to provide advice and authorization in an impartial manner, should not be subject to the control of certain industrial interests. today in parliament we have said 'stop' by a majority, and we are awaiting the court of auditors' report in june next before we take a decision again in october on the discharge to the agencies in question.
in writing. i voted in favour of the amendments denouncing the risks of conflict of interest within european agencies and proposing to guard against such practices in the future. i also chose to abstain on the final vote on the cases of the food safety authority, the european medicines agency and the environment agency. the french socialists, anxious not to impede the proper execution of the important programmes currently being carried out, did not wish to go beyond abstention. the aim is to shed light on practices that may be contrary to the agencies' original objectives.
in writing. i voted against the discharge for the european food safety authority (efsa) because it is unacceptable that an eu agency is subject to conflicts of interest. efsa is the agency in charge of the health of citizens, it cannot have any links with private interests. the european parliament has just voted to oblige the commission to commit itself to taking rapid and mandatory measures to ensure the independence and transparency of efsa, which needs a thorough reform.
in writing. i voted in favour of the discharge for efsa. i therefore deeply regret that the discharge was postponed to october because the conditions were not met. the european court of auditors has not expressed any reservations with regard to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions for efsa. the internal audit service, on the other hand, does not mention any "critical" recommendations, which would constitute the most worrying level of ias recommendations. i also do not think that the rapporteur's approach in his report, which mentions 'alleged conflicts of interest', is relevant. the agency has established rules to prevent potential conflicts of interest, but it also needs the expertise of agents who have worked in the private sector. the cases of experts with previous experience in the private sector do not mean that they do not exercise their new functions objectively. you'd have to prove otherwise before you'd convict the agency of that. however, these elements are not mentioned in the report.
in writing. as president of the women at the centre association, i consider the work of the european institute for gender equality to be essential. i voted to discharge the 2010 budget of this institute. discharge is the final control of the budget for a given year. after the audit and finalisation of the annual accounts, it is up to the council of the european union to issue a recommendation and then to us parliamentarians to decide whether or not to give the commission a discharge in respect of the implementation of the union budget for the preceding financial year. this decision is based, inter alia, on an examination of the annual accounts and on the annual report of the court of auditors. discharge is therefore the political part of the external control of budget implementation.

in writing. the annual report on the protection of the european union's financial interests and the fight against fraud contains the most recent information on irregularities and suspected fraud reported by the member states. this year's report pays particular attention to the risk of double funding in the area of cohesion policy. the report considers that this is not a satisfactory situation, and i voted for the european commission and the member states to inform the european parliament of all irregularities and fraud that have been found. the control of the management of european funds is imperative, they are a valuable tool that i try to defend every day in the european parliament and in my constituency.

in writing. i supported the adoption of this report, which presents the suspicions of fraud and irregularities observed in the actions carried out by the european union. i was particularly concerned by the increase in irregularities in a large majority of the union's policy areas and by the risks of double funding in cohesion policy. i hope that the commission and the member states will take our recommendations into account and take their responsibilities to ensure that parliament is fully informed of all irregularities and fraud that have been found. we must have better control over the management of european public funds, to which all our citizens contribute, directly or indirectly.
in writing. until now, mobile phone charges abroad have been significantly higher than domestic charges. the text of angelika niebler was therefore approved by an overwhelming majority. this text illustrates how much europe is working to make your everyday life as a consumer easier. after tough negotiations, the 'roaming' regulation will require mobile operators in europe to charge the same prices, lower than those currently charged, as from july. the text introduces for the first time structural solutions which will allow consumers to choose freely another operator for roaming services, independently of their national operator. the text provides for the temporary application of new retail and wholesale tariff ceilings for voice calls, text messages and, above all, data transfers. we now have a future solution. injecting competition into the roaming markets will, for the first time, provide structural and sustainable consumer protection. because competition is the best way to ensure low prices in the long term", said neelie kroes, commissioner for digital strategy.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the niebler report which calls for the introduction of roaming tariff ceilings for mobile communications. i note that the report lowers the ceilings originally proposed by the commission. this is very good news for european users who have been penalized when travelling abroad. two points in particular caught my attention: the idea of enforcing the roaming regulation outside the european union to extend the protection of european users, and the possibility of subscribing to a roaming contract separate from the national mobile phone contract from 2014. both measures are designed to improve the situation of users.
in writing. i voted in favour of the compromise text negotiated with the council on the roaming regulation, which will allow europeans to use their mobile phones abroad at lower rates. we socialists have called for the abolition of these artificial frontiers within the internal market, because they are contrary to the very spirit of the european project and its founding fathers. that is why we have asked the commission to act quickly to bring the end of roaming into effect as early as 2016. in addition to the application of mobile roaming tariffs lower than those currently applied from july, the text introduces for the first time structural solutions which will allow consumers to choose freely another operator for roaming services, independently of their national operator. this has been the case since july 2014.
in writing. we voted in favour of a report which makes the idea of a europe that protects consumers a reality for all european consumers. the lowering of the price ceilings for calls, sms and mobile internet will be immediate and gradual. moreover, consumers will be able to benefit from it as early as this summer. i am very pleased with the progress that this new regulation promises to bring to the mobile telephony market.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which improves the control of european consumers over their mobile phone bill when travelling abroad. the european parliament is setting a ceiling on prices for data, calls and sms exchanges from abroad, in order to reduce the high cost of mobile communications outside the national territory. it also ensures better information for citizens, who can now make informed choices about these communications. by adopting these measures, the european parliament has committed itself to creating competition in the mobile telephony market and thus putting an end to unfairly charged overheads by telephone operators as from 1 july 2012.
in writing. while three out of four europeans use their mobile phone when travelling, many have experienced a 'bill shock'. competition in the mobile roaming sector within the union is still weak, resulting in very high prices for consumers. i am pleased that agreement was reached at first reading on a text which i am convinced provides effective solutions to improve the situation on the mobile roaming market for european consumers. on the one hand, decoupling of domestic and roaming mobile telephone service activities will improve competition: a consumer will thus be able to choose whether or not to keep the same provider for his communications when travelling, and will benefit from more favourable tariffs. on the other hand, the gradual reduction by 2014 of the maximum prices allowed for billing calls, sms and data volumes will greatly benefit consumers. in addition, consumers will benefit from a number of measures to improve transparency: information on prices for roaming outside the eu, information on accumulated consumption expressed in the unit or currency of billing, safeguard ceilings (default €50).
in writing. after three years of reform which did not sufficiently reduce the bill for consumers using roaming services, we can now look forward to a significant reduction in roaming charges in the coming months, starting this summer. the socialists have been particularly active in this fight. the time has come to implement structural reforms, rather than regulating prices forever. our ultimate aim must be to eliminate the price differences between roaming and national communications in the next few years. despite the commitment of the socialists, a majority was not achieved, but this is the direction in which we must orientate our reforms in the future. it is no longer acceptable for operators to charge prohibitive rates for mobile data downloads, which have the effect of causing the unpleasant surprise of extremely high bills, due to the lack of transparency in the rates for these services. finally, i welcome the proposal to allow customers to buy roaming services from another operator than the one providing them with the national services. finally, a healthy competition that should serve the interests of the consumer!
in writing. mobile phone prices are about to drop. that is the decision which was taken by the european parliament on thursday, 10 may, and i welcome it. the report on mobile roaming provides for a number of measures to help consumers and 'virtual' operators who have so far been restricted in their access to networks owned by other operators. the main measures will include the reduction of the tariff ceilings for calls, sms and data roaming. from 2012, the price per minute for an outgoing call will be 29 cents instead of 35, 8 cents for incoming calls instead of the current 11 and 9 cents instead of 15 for sms. the price of a megabyte download will be set at 70 cents, whereas there was no ceiling until now. consumers in border regions who incur unintended roaming charges should be informed by their provider to avoid this inconvenience. when a user travels abroad, he will be able to access local data services in order to choose the most advantageous offer among the various local providers, such as for access to wifi.
in writing. under the pretext of lowering the prices of roaming services, this report organises the total deregulation of the mobile telephony market. once again, the choice is made to intensify competition in a dogmatic way without any assessment of the benefits and harms of competition already at work. i vote against it.
in writing. exports and imports of hazardous chemicals require close control. this report provides the necessary legal and environmental certainty. the main elements of the proposal now provide greater clarity for exporters, while not entailing any additional administrative burden. in my political group we nevertheless wanted to make some changes to dan jørgensen's report. but he has made important concessions in favour of what we stand for. the main objective of my political group has therefore been achieved. it provides that chemicals from the european union that meet all european legal standards for the environment and health are not banned from world markets or replaced by chemicals that meet lower standards. in this way, the european union can now export its chemicals, but also its legal standards.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which sets out the rules for trade in dangerous chemicals, in order to ensure the safety of people and the protection of the environment. this report requires in particular the prior consent of importing countries for trade in these dangerous products, including where these countries are not part of the european union. the adoption of such regulations by parliament is in line with our international commitments under the rotterdam convention and goes beyond its requirements in the service of better protection for our fellow citizens.
in writing. i voted for the jørgensen report on the revision of european legislation on the export and import of dangerous chemicals. it implements the rotterdam convention in the union, and it regulates trade in these products through the exchange of information between the parties to the convention and the application of the prior informed consent (pic) procedure, i.e. the formal consent of the exporting countries to export by the importing countries. the commission proposed to revise the legislation in particular to clarify certain definitions, to involve the european chemicals agency (echa), but mainly because european legislation covering more chemical substances than the convention, the convention provided for facilitating the export of products in the absence of a response from the importing country by extending the possibilities of derogation from the pic procedure for substances which are either banned or severely restricted in the union, because of the risks they pose to human health or the environment. the report continues to frame the possibilities for derogation and opposes the possibility of exporting products against the will of importers. the report also limits echa's prerogatives by preserving member states' prerogatives in controlling trade in hazardous chemicals.
in writing. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has profoundly changed certain legislative procedures, particularly in favour of the european parliament. the comitology procedure has therefore been adapted to take account of the new powers of the european parliament. it was the system used by the member states to control the european commission when it adopts implementing measures under community legislation. but since the entry into force of the new treaty, this procedure has been transformed into a system providing for the adoption of delegated acts and implementing acts. i have approved the amendment of the new articles 87a and 88, which determine the procedure to be followed in the most general case.
in writing. while the preparation of delegated and implementing acts by the commission is necessary to ensure the effective implementation and application of decisions adopted by the council and the european parliament, the latter must have a right of access to those acts, in the context of its supervisory role over the commission. this will be the case with this text, which sets out the procedure to be followed, and which i have therefore supported. it is essential that the union acts in the sole interest of its citizens and that they have a say in all the legislative stages.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report which makes the necessary changes to non-contractual obligations arising from a breach of the right to privacy and the rights of personality. i stress the right balance between freedom of expression and respect for privacy. i share the rapporteur's view that the existing legislation needs to be adapted in order to extend the scope of the law to cover the various content published on the internet. the report also helps to better determine which law is applicable in the event of a crossborder dispute.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to clarify the situation on the national law applicable to breaches of privacy and human rights. it was necessary to ensure legal certainty on this issue, since defamation complainants competed with each other in national courts to choose the courts most likely to win their case. the development of this "defamation tourism" in turn threatened freedom of expression. it is in the european interest to protect our fellow citizens in the union better, while respecting the rights of everyone!
in writing. since the arab spring, the european union has been working to promote stability and democracy in the mediterranean neighbours. to support them in their transitions, we believe it is essential to increase our trade by focusing on small and medium-sized enterprises. as the rapporteur, niccolò rinaldi, has pointed out, this trade strategy could create jobs and help to dismantle the oligarchy. our cooperation must necessarily involve financial support for small and mediumsized enterprises through the european bank for reconstruction and development and the european investment bank. we must also promote cultural and educational exchanges within the framework of the erasmus and da vinci euromed programmes. we are thus transmitting our democratic values by creating a genuine euro-mediterranean free trade area!
in writing. the report's approach supports the european commission's policy in a liberal approach. the ftaa implies a tariff dismantling and market opening which can weaken these emerging economies. the social, environmental, educational and cultural aspects are not sufficiently present, contrary to the aspirations of the people. the ftaa is also part of a long process with heavy criteria, including the obligation to align with the european internal market regulations. moreover, these numerous requirements are not linked to the prospect of integration into the european union as was the case for the countries of eastern europe. we must remember the failure of the union for the mediterranean. the approach of these agreements focuses on bilateral relations, thus neglecting support for regional integration of these countries. on the contrary, it puts them in a system of competition to be the "champions" who meet the criteria of these agreements in relation to each other. at a time when europeans are debating the possibility of a certain european protectionism, we are demanding the opposite from our partners in the south. is that consistent ? and fair ? what 's fair ? i do not think so, and that is why i am voting against this report, although there are some positive aspects to it.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this text, which sets out the priorities for cooperation with our mediterranean neighbours and for helping them to rebuild and embark on a path of genuine economic and social development that benefits all. the arab spring revolutions have indeed provided the european union with a unique opportunity to align its foreign and trade policy interests with its core democratic values. i therefore support the commission's approach, which is to see that the political and democratic advances under way go hand in hand with greater economic and trade openness.
in writing. on the one hand, this report calls for further progress, particularly in the area of human rights and the involvement of civil society; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i could not help but abstain.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which calls on the european union to proactively support democratic transitions in north africa through trade. the report stresses the need to complete existing trade agreements and to develop them further in a dynamic manner adapted to the specific characteristics of each country. it is also an opportunity to give a clearer direction to the union's programmes, by promoting organic farming and fair trade, by regulating the arms trade, by providing general technical assistance and by supporting smes.
in writing. the european parliament reiterated its support for the process of economic development and democratisation in the countries of the southern mediterranean by adopting a report which sets out the eu strategy around two main areas: trade and investment. the report, which was adopted by a large majority, contains ambitious proposals for strengthening euro-mediterranean relations: the 'more for more' approach linking the political and economic dimensions, the active participation of civil society, support for smes, notably through the european investment bank (eib), the promotion of the european neighbourhood programme for agricultural and rural development and regional integration. the development of a special relationship with our mediterranean partners is essential for the prosperity of the area, for the deepening of economic partnership and for genuine political cooperation. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report, which shows a broad consensus in parliament on this subject.
in writing. the only horizon offered by this report to the arab revolutions is the establishment of the free trade area that the european union had "agreed" with the overthrown regimes. he claims that this is the aspiration of the arab peoples. those who vote for this text despise the struggle of the arab peoples for a better life. i am voting against.
in writing. the arab spring is a revolution without precedent in the mediterranean world. these revolutions have redefined the relations of the southern mediterranean with the european union, building a new trade partnership, based on fundamental values such as human rights and democracy. the strength of this partnership must therefore be based on the acquis of a free trade area, regional integration and a commercial strategy. this presents a unique opportunity to cooperate in the fields of employment, growth, and to strengthen regional integration and the european union's presence through its trade, investment and financing activities. the report therefore reaffirms trade as a solid pillar of the european neighbourhood policy and as a means of involving smes by making it an additional tool for economic democratisation.
in writing. the european parliament voted today on a report on the eu's trade and investment with the southern mediterranean. another report from the european union which still fails to learn the lessons of the demands expressed by citizens during what has been called the arab spring. in this report, relations between the two shores of the mediterranean remain primarily economic relations based on free trade. niccolo rinaldi (rapporteur of this text, a liberal) even dares to say that "trade (...) facilitates a more equitable sharing of wealth". he adds that some mediterranean countries "have a great deal of natural assets and resources". do we still have to ask who exploits them? and the eu is more concerned with protecting the interests of its big business than with seeing the wealth of these countries benefit the people who first and foremost made the revolution for social reasons. the gue/ngl has succeeded in getting the necessary review of the debt in the light of the odious debt incorporated in this report. i was not able to vote for this report, which is profoundly opposed to the vision of international relations which i defend.
in writing. i am a firm believer in the need for a harmonised patent system at european level, because it is an essential tool for technology transfer. however, i voted in favour of this report which provides for the protection of european breeders against excessive protection by patents. most of us have recognised that when patents provide too broad a protection, it is likely to hinder innovation and progress and to harm small and medium-sized breeders by blocking their access to plant and animal genetic resources.
in writing. on thursday 10 may i voted in favour of the resolution on the breveting of essentially biological processes. the question of patentability is a sensitive one, since it highlights, on the one hand, the need for a stronger and more appropriate protection of european innovations and, on the other hand, the need to support european enterprises by stimulating research. it is also important to set clear limits in line with our ethical principles: we cannot allow patents on life. that is why parliament voted by a large majority against the patentability of plants and animals obtained by traditional breeding methods. this vote confirms our resolve to fight the appropriation of the living. it is therefore necessary to continue our action in the following dynamic: we must protect intellectual property without limiting access to these species, preserve agricultural biotechnology without hindering european innovation.
in writing. by voting in favour of such a resolution, the european parliament sends a decisive message to the european commission and the european patent office (epo), echoing the demands of citizens: we want to put an end to the appropriation of living things! the commission is responsible for enforcing european law and the epo is called upon to respect european legislation prohibiting patents on conventional seeds. the threat of the concentration of the world's agro-genetic resources in the hands of a few seed and agro-chemical firms has dramatic consequences for our farmers and, beyond europe, for those in developing countries. while 90% of the world's biological heritage is owned by developing countries, 97% of patents are owned by industrialized countries. indigenous peoples and the poorest are also the forgotten victims of multinational corporations. the greens in the ep will remain extremely vigilant about future changes to the patent system, which is totally inadequate and which must be reformed.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the patenting of biological processes. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. it is an important subject because of its many consequences, including on agriculture, industry and food security, as well as the risks of privatisation and patentability of living things. a number of pro-gmo amendments have fortunately been rejected by the european parliament and i also welcome the fact that the european patent office (epo) is now excluding from patentability processes considered to be derived from natural crossbreeding. the resolution also proposes to extend the exclusion of patentability to a range of derivatives and genetic sources in order to avoid circumvention of exclusions. the european parliament is therefore moving in the right direction with the vote on this text, which aims to ban all marketing of live animals. the positive effects can be many and the consequences many, especially for biodiversity, and we can go even further.
in writing. the problem of piracy has become a real scourge. the current situation in the horn of africa is unacceptable and that is why we have asked the high representative of the european union, catherine ashton, to take urgent action to secure the release of the nearly 200 seamen currently held hostage by pirates. but this call must not make us forget that it is essential to address the problem by addressing the root causes of poverty in the horn of africa and the failures of somalia.
in writing. on thursday 10 may i voted in favour of the resolution on maritime piracy. just because the subject has disappeared from the news does not mean that the phenomenon has died out. on the contrary, in 2011, the indian ocean, and in particular the somali coast, is plagued by an increase in acts of piracy. since 2008, despite parliament's prioritization of the fight against piracy, piracy remains a thriving $12 billion-a-year business. the piracy trade, which is fuelled by ransom money and the diversion of international aid, must be stopped as soon as possible. it also poses a threat to regional stability and maritime transport. this resolution reaffirms our desire to improve maritime security and the coordination of military resources in this region, which is suffering from the failure of its institutions. in this sense, we have decided to extend the mandate of the atalante programme by two years. it would also be counterproductive to neglect the social aspect of our work in this region known as the 'horn of hunger', considering that these criminal behaviours are partly symptoms of poverty and violence.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution on maritime piracy and the consensus it has created among the various political groups. i believe that the situation in somalia requires the european union to reaffirm its commitment to operation atalanta. i also share the rapporteur's view that land-based operations should be carried out in addition to maritime operations. i believe it is important to participate in the building of a strong somali state, capable of offering its people prospects for the future.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which reiterates our support for operation atalanta, which is currently operating in the horn of africa to protect our ships from pirate attacks. the european union must show firmness so that these attacks from another time, which terrify our sailors operating in the area, cease. this operation, launched under the auspices of president sarkozy in 2008, shows the usefulness of tackling such major challenges together in external fields. it is a real success and we can also welcome the development of a genuine european strategy for the horn of africa. by acting in this area, the european union is sending a strong message to the rest of the world: any attack on a european citizen, including those beyond our borders, will not go unpunished.
in writing. once again, pirates in the horn of africa are attacking cargo ships that pass off their coast. the gulf of aden and the indian ocean are not only becoming more and more dangerous, but also more and more frequent. at the same time, more than 190 sailors are still held hostage and poverty is increasing in this part of the world. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution which calls for a strengthening of military means, but also for solutions to be found to deal with the root causes of piracy. the increase in the military presence is obviously essential, but it is imperative that this be combined with an increase in humanitarian aid. the horn of africa is a region of extreme poverty, which is the main source of piracy and violence.
in writing. this motion for a resolution on maritime piracy is a clear reinforcement of the european union's integrated maritime policy. indeed, shipping is an important driver of european economic growth and beyond, with more than three quarters of world trade carried by sea. it is therefore in the interest of the european union itself that the safety factor should be integrated into the common maritime policy. the news has shown an increase in crime at sea in recent years. the greatest number of acts of piracy are found in specific areas, often concentrated in the red sea, through which many european and international transport and trade vessels pass, and most of which go unpunished. this is why this motion for a resolution is indispensable, because it re-launches the urgent call for immediate and effective measures against this impunity, and calls for the need for strategic coordination between the european union and third countries.
in writing. i voted against the joint motion for a resolution on maritime piracy, considering that it does not take into account the socioeconomic factors that explain this phenomenon and that the international action put in place is not the right response. military intervention is not a solution, and european development funds should not be used for this purpose. in this context, eu navfor atalanta must be considered a failure. i say that the improvement of the situation requires an improvement in the living conditions of the population, which is caught between civil war and ecological and economic disasters. european economic interests must not be the dominant decision-making factor. piracy is the result of poverty and the lack of cooperative policies to address it. it is therefore a complete reversal of the international policies of the rich countries that the countries of the south need. until that changes, poverty, hunger and conflict will continue to be the daily lot of the southern countries.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution, which recalls that the fight against piracy at sea is necessary above all for obvious reasons of the protection of human lives. we cannot justly abandon our ship owners and sailors, who work every day for trade and global growth, to their fate, nor can we abandon the local people, who live off fishing and cannot go to sea. the urgent need to mobilize a full legal and military arsenal against pirates, who are using ever heavier weapons and taking ships ever further from the coast, is clear to both local communities and the international community. this is the wish clearly expressed by our assembly and which i have emphasized in the drafting of this text. i hope that mrs ashton will now be able to urge the states to increase the military capabilities of atalanta and to fully implement the united nations convention on the law of the sea, in order to put an end to the unacceptable impunity of pirates.
mr president, the heads of state and government are meeting in informal council. it was customary for the president of the european council to report to the councils, even when they were informal. i think you will speak at 7 p.m. - i hope they will keep you for dinner so that the president of parliament can remain in the european council - but has the president of the european council been invited? why does he not come to the council to report, even though he is informal?
mr president, i will speak - and i hope you will not mind, mrs malmström - only about the comprehensive economic and trade agreement between canada and the european union. i fear that this agreement will be like acta. the least that can be said is that these negotiations on ceta lack transparency. these negotiations began in 2009 and we are in the 12th round of negotiations. however, we cannot say that we are very well informed about the content of these negotiations. the commission's own website is blocked in the ninth round. it contains no real information and the most relevant information comes from canada. worse still, in every resolution the views of the european parliament seem to be ignored. this is the most ambitious agreement ever negotiated with canada, or indeed with any other state in the world. it is based on a so-called negative list approach to the liberalisation of services. however, most public services do not appear to have been excluded from the negotiations. what will happen to health, education, electricity, telecommunications, drinking water and even culture if only the economic and commercial approach prevails on both sides of the atlantic? the only thing that seems to be taken into account are the interests of the large public companies which want to conquer new market shares, in defiance of the general interest, the public interest of the people. but this world view has already done enough damage to stop the race to the front. but no, it's not working. the views of the experts studying the impact of these agreements seem to be divergent, to say the least. some speak of the creation of 80 000 jobs in canada, others of the elimination of 30 to 150 000 jobs. the same type of study does not appear to have been published for the european union, and that is a pity. the impact of this agreement could also have a serious impact on local authorities and their public procurement, which for the most part seem to have been left out. could we have a precise statement of this agreement and similarly precise impact studies on its consequences? acta should be a lesson to us, but it is not, i regret.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the media agenda seems to be rediscovering the importance of having a long-term growth strategy, even though growth has been one of our political priorities for several months. the economic recovery obviously requires better use of public resources to support job-creating enterprises, the most important of which are smes. it is therefore necessary to recall that the 23 million smes in europe are the vital organs of economic development in our territories. however, they are facing structural difficulties in obtaining financing, and the current crisis has only made the situation worse. in february we were discussing here the use of regional funds to combat youth unemployment and support smes. the court of auditors' report in march confirmed what we have known for a long time: their access to financial engineering instruments is far too complicated. the commission, commissioner, had a budget of 27 billion euro for smes for this period. do we know what happened to them? the difficulties are well known. the time is not so much to discuss the definition of smes, but to determine how to better understand their differences and needs in the implementation of our policies.
mr president, that is good news. the european parliament has just adopted a text to better protect vulnerable consumers. first, there was a problem of definition: traditionally, a vulnerable consumer is someone who is elderly, someone who is disabled or someone who has difficulty asserting their rights. that is true, but the reality is that things are more complicated and that everyone can, at one time or another, be a vulnerable consumer, especially given the arrival of new and extremely aggressive commercial practices. i'm thinking particularly about all the online commerce, behavioral advertising and so on. so we needed a text, and i think that is welcome. the second point is that this text must not only affirm rights but also give the vulnerable consumer the means to exercise those rights. i believe that this is also the great step forward in this text, and we should all welcome this european step forward.
