in writing. in pursuing the construction of a european area of freedom, security and justice, the european union needs a genuine european strategy on internal security. the own-initiative report, which we adopted by a very large majority, states first of all that this strategy and any measures that are taken must absolutely meet their obligations in terms of fundamental rights and respect for the rule of law. our report then calls for this strategy to be given sufficient financial resources for the next budgetary period so that the european union can really face these challenges in a comprehensive, coordinated and united manner. finally, our strategy identifies five priority areas of action in which the european union has real added value and where we need stronger european cooperation. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. i supported the own-initiative report by my colleague, rita borsellino, because i believe it is our responsibility to give a new dimension to the eu's internal security strategy, so that it is both more democratic and more respectful of fundamental rights. on the one hand, the european parliament, like the national parliaments, must have a say in the definition of priorities and the evaluation of policies that have been left for too long in the hands of national governments. on the other hand, i believe that respect for human rights is essential to ensure the full credibility of this policy. finally, while respect for the principle of subsidiarity in the context of a policy as sensitive as security cannot be called into question, it is essential that member states should show greater solidarity in order to deal as effectively as possible with threats to the security of their citizens, in accordance with the principles of necessity and proportionality.
in writing. organized crime is a large-scale phenomenon that requires a coordinated and concrete response from the member states. organized crime networks spread across national borders and require action based on intergovernmental cooperation at the operational level. the european union's internal security strategy adopted in 2010 sets five strategic objectives to make the union's territory safer: the fight against international criminal networks, the prevention of terrorism, the securing of cyberspace, the strengthening of border management and the resilience to crises and natural or man-made disasters. it is now necessary to make a first assessment of the progress made and of what can be improved. parliament therefore wanted to express its views, stressing that the fight against terrorism and organised crime must remain the priority of this strategy, but that fundamental rights, the principles of international protection and the rule of law must be respected. parliament also stressed that security policies are a shared competence between the union and the member states, but that the principle of subsidiarity should also be respected.
in writing. this own-initiative report by my colleague rita borsellino was adopted in plenary by 503 votes in favour, 55 against and 56 abstentions. identifying the most pressing challenges for the security of the european union in the years ahead, this report supports the five strategic objectives and actions proposed by the commission in its communication. it called on the commission to make the fight against terrorism and organised crime a key priority and to step up its response to man-made and natural disasters.
in writing. crime is changing and taking on new faces. terrorism is also a real threat. cybercrime continues to grow and costs society €750 billion a year according to a recent europol report. the security of our common borders is a challenge that is still relevant today. natural and man-made disasters are becoming more frequent and severe. the scale of these threats requires concerted action. we must develop a clear european framework based on a well-thought-out strategy to guarantee the internal security of the european union. the complementarity between european and national actions must also be strengthened.
in writing. i note that this report calls for an evidence-based threat analysis. i join the motion. it is high time that security policy was based on real threats and not on fantasy threats. i would also point out that the text recommends that more money be allocated to the fight against corruption, as i recommended last september. i'm glad you did. i am pleased to note again that the gap between the stigmatization of petty crime and the weakness of the measures taken against environmental, economic and corporate crime is denounced here. i cannot, however, vote for a report which endorses the commission's overall security strategy. the text also lauds cooperation with nato on internal security issues. i vote against it.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by a large majority of the report on the eu's internal security strategy. the adoption of this report is an important step forward in the fight against terrorism and provides a range of effective tools to be used against all types of criminal acts, such as white collar crime, organised crime, mafia-type crime and money laundering. the report also calls for the creation of a common threat assessment system for member states. the report also calls for the establishment of a cybercrime centre and for the eu's internal security budget to be commensurate with the threats to the security of european citizens. these are the reasons why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the harmonisation of european standards must also be done by law. our european model is based on values, particularly in the area of criminal law. i therefore approved the adoption of strong criteria in the implementation of the new european criminal legislation which is intended to recall fundamental principles: respect for the principles of proportionality and subsidiarity and absolute respect for the principle of the presumption of innocence. it goes without saying that european criminal law must respect the charter of fundamental rights and the european convention on human rights!
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which sets out a framework for the future development of a criminal policy for the european union. in the construction of a european area of freedom and justice, the criminal field has always been treated a little bit separately, because it is a very sensitive area, directly affecting the royal powers. it is difficult to imagine that criminal law is not part of the construction of a europe of law. the report also stresses the need to ensure that the criminal law is not only a challenge but also a necessity in the area of serious crime and crossborder crime. i am also pleased with the prospects offered by such a communitization of the criminal field in europe: first of all, 'eurocrimes'; secondly, the 'european crime network' (ecn) and thirdly, the 'european crime network' (ecn). the commission has already proposed that the council should be able to adopt the draft budget for the year 2000 and that the council should be able to adopt the draft budget for the year 2000 in accordance with the procedure laid down in article 149 of the treaty.
in writing. the harmonisation of criminal law remains a sensitive issue. while the lisbon treaty has made this a community matter, in that it allows the eu to use it to strengthen the implementation of its policies, criminal law remains at the heart of national sovereignty and the diversity of national legislation does not make the task easy. however, a step in this direction is needed to address the concerns of european citizens who do not want offenders to hide behind borders or exploit differences in national legal systems. we must define minimum rules at european level on offences, jurisdiction and sanctions, the main aim being to promote the application of the principle of mutual recognition in practice. finally, we must prevent the exploitation of criminal law, which would make it appear that the introduction of new rules would make it possible to combat crime. it would be a waste of time to ignore that other tools exist and need to be implemented.
in writing. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the pillar structure was abandoned and the basis for the development of a criminal law that is an integral part of european union law was laid. however, it must be noted that the european union has not created a separate area for criminal law provisions. these are not only to be found in instruments relating to justice but also in those relating to internal affairs. this own-initiative report calls on the commission to ensure a high-quality and coherent european approach to criminal law. with this in mind, the commission has set up an inter-service coordination group on criminal law. in his report, cornelis de jong calls for the appointment of a commissioner responsible for criminal law matters. the report also stresses the importance of mutual recognition, harmonisation of protection standards and respect for the principle of presumption of innocence. it also stressed that the key areas of criminal law should remain the responsibility of the member states.
in writing. the lisbon treaty, by integrating criminal law into eu law, is leading us to react. we now need to strengthen existing cooperation in criminal law and rethink our national and european approaches. greater coordination is needed between the european institutions in this area. it is also necessary to develop mutual recognition while preserving key principles of criminal law such as the presumption of innocence.
the protection of vulnerable consumers is a priority and we have therefore called for a genuine european strategy in this area! the rights of vulnerable consumers must be strengthened as much as possible. european legislation, through the decisions of the court of justice of the european union, protects european citizens by dealing with cases on a case-by-case basis. today, therefore, i am in favour of a comprehensive strategy to avoid unfair trading practices in the future. the report takes a sectoral approach to cover the diversity of forms of vulnerability. for example, the lack of information on claims and compensation systems should no longer penalise us!
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mrs maría irigoyen pérez on the strategy to strengthen the rights of vulnerable consumers. unfair commercial practices, misleading advertising and lack of information about certain products are hitting the most vulnerable consumers hardest. our priority is to prevent the exploitation of vulnerable consumers at all costs. in order to better integrate this category of consumers into the single market, the causes should be addressed and their protection improved. in this sense, certain sectors such as food, transport, internet, liberalised markets, justice and digitalisation of services need to be subject to enhanced scrutiny in order to facilitate consumer empowerment. to this end, stricter rules on advertising to children should be developed rapidly, adaptation to the digitalisation of services for the elderly should be made pedagogical and information for the visually impaired should be improved.
in writing. because consumers are easily exposed to vulnerable situations, the european legislator must take specific protective measures. i therefore welcome the adoption of the irigoyen pérez report. i am joining this initiative which aims to strengthen consumer rights and to make consumers more aware of the risks they face. i note that with the proliferation of consumer-oriented content on the web, we need to be more vigilant. i think the most important thing now is to ensure that these new protective measures are implemented uniformly in all the member states.
in writing. the european project has created a single market: a common space for buying, selling and moving. consumers are therefore essential actors. as consumers, we can all find ourselves in a vulnerable situation at some point. there is no one, but vulnerable consumers. this report offers a flexible approach to protect all of them. it calls in particular for children and young people to be protected from advertising for foods that are too fatty, too salty or too sweet. the report also raises concerns about access to information and complaint procedures for travellers. these are very concrete recommendations, useful to the citizens of europe, and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which calls for a strategy to protect vulnerable consumers. there may be several factors determining consumer vulnerability, such as age, disability, but also poor command of new technologies, which can make them vulnerable to marketing pressures, misleading advertising, or abusive contractual clauses. european consumer rights must be adapted to the particular situations.
in writing. meps approved on tuesday, 22 may, by a near unanimous vote, the report on strengthening the rights of vulnerable consumers. this report posits that all consumers are likely to become vulnerable consumers in their lifetime. the causes may be endogenous (reduced physical or mental capacity such as children, the elderly or disabled) or exogenous (education, etc.). we must therefore ensure that these populations are well protected but also empowered. the european parliament intends to contribute to the european commission's reflection on this subject by presenting this report. it should be noted that on the same day of this adoption, the commission published its strategy for strengthening consumer confidence, the european consumer agenda.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it contributes to the commission's thinking on the protection of vulnerable consumers, in particular with a view to the publication of the consumer agenda, which aims to define the main priorities and future actions of the commission in the field of consumer policy. as a fictitious rapporteur on this dossier, i argued for several important points, including a clarification of the definition of vulnerable consumers (extending beyond the conventional understanding of physical or mental disability to include the notion of situational vulnerability), the strengthening of the european strategy through both a development of the legal corpus and effective respect for rights and consumer empowerment (access to information, consumer education), the consideration of the vulnerability generated by the development of new practices related to ict (behavioural advertising, for example), and the need to empower companies in this area and to recognise the initiatives that they develop in the field of self-regulation.
in writing. i supported the own-initiative report by my colleague maría irigoyen pérez on a strategy to strengthen the rights of vulnerable consumers. the european parliament is thus showing its determination to prevent consumer vulnerability and to protect vulnerable consumers. every european citizen must be aware that anyone can become a vulnerable consumer during his or her lifetime (travel to a foreign country, illness, old age, use of new commercial media, etc.). i also welcome the fact that the current definition of the vulnerable consumer is maintained. the amendment of this concept would have entailed risks for consumer protection. it is essential that such a concept should remain balanced, neither too vague nor too precise, so that it can cover all situations of consumer vulnerability.
in writing. the report aims to protect 'vulnerable consumers'. he tries to define which category of people is concerned, but has to make it clear, over and over again, that everyone is concerned. from this point onwards, it is only a matter of admitting that 'consumers' are persons and that their interests are not guaranteed by free and undistorted competition. this text stubbornly refuses to cross it. it claims that competition "benefits consumers if they are properly informed". vulnerability is the result of a simple lack of information. while there is a need to better regulate people's information about the products and services they use, to make lack of information the main cause of vulnerability is a deception. the millions of people who have been plunged into precariousness by austerity policies and deregulation of the labour market are made vulnerable. they cannot buy quality products and services, whether they are informed or not. this text, full of good intentions, is an indecent social blindness.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the 'strategy to strengthen the rights of vulnerable consumers'. the report highlights the diversity of forms of vulnerability linked to physical or mental disability, but also takes into account disability linked to lack of knowledge of the language, lack of information or simply the need to use new technologies with which the consumer is not familiar. the european union must guarantee high standards of protection for all consumers by introducing measures to protect their interests against unfair commercial practices, misleading advertising and abusive contractual clauses. as a member of the board of the european consumer centre, i fully supported the adoption of this report.

in writing. ensuring the optimal functioning of the single market is essential to get europe back on the path to growth. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the information it receives. the internal market scoreboard is extremely useful in this respect, since it allows a periodic review of the functioning of the internal market. in 2007, the heads of state or government set themselves the target of a transposition deficit of no more than 1%. the current deficit is 1.2%, while in recent months seven member states have seen their delays in transposing eu directives increase. i therefore support this report, which calls in particular on the member states to reduce transposition deficits to 0.5%, calls on the commission to ensure that infringements are punished swiftly and calls for the establishment of an accelerated infringement procedure. the text also stresses the importance of strengthening the services offered to citizens and businesses to help them solve the problems they encounter in applying european law. i think that is crucial.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, the title of my report, 'the european union and china, unequal trade', expresses exactly the challenge we are facing today, when china is set to become the world's leading power before the turn of the century. relations between china and europe are unbalanced. i remind you that our trade deficit with china has more than tripled in ten years. this is a challenge to us, because the european economy is losing momentum and its growth setbacks are causing fears that it will no longer be able to face international competition with the confidence and determination of yesterday. the framework for our future is in upheaval. it is up to us to redefine it, not by turning inward, which would be nothing more than a flight forward towards decline, but by building with china a new partnership whose lines will ultimately be simple to define: reciprocity of rules, balance of trade and transparency of trade relations. i say this with all the greater conviction that in an open global economy, china needs europe, as europe needs china. i say this with all the more certainty because i believe that the crisis we are experiencing is a good time to deepen our relations on the basis of a more balanced partnership. this report by the committee on international trade, thanks in particular to the work of the fictitious rapporteurs and the opinion rapporteurs, whom i would like to commend, sets the framework and defines the requirements. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. the aim is to temper the chinese system of joint ventures and the transfer of strategic technologies, and to promote customs cooperation between the european union and china in order to combat counterfeiting. the aim is to encourage the eu to use trade defence instruments more frequently, where necessary, and to defend european industrial interests more effectively by revising the directive on intellectual property rights. the aim is to ensure that all chinese products in circulation in the single market are in full compliance with european standards. the commission is invited to negotiate an ambitious and balanced investment agreement between the eu and china, guaranteeing transparency. this is to level the monetary competition with a coordinated system to identify sovereign debt holders and encourage china to let the yuan be valued. it also calls for action to reform the organisation of international trade in the long term, including social, health and environmental standards. finally, i would like to stress one last essential point. all of this would be in vain if the european union refused to implement a concerted policy of production and reindustrialisation, and a research and innovation policy that is responsive to the new global challenges. and i would also like to add a demand, an absolute demand, for better coordination between the member states so that each other's bilateral relations with china do not weaken the union's position. europe needs to speak with one voice and to adopt and defend a single policy on this issue of relations with china, as on so many others, but especially on this one. ladies and gentlemen, by adopting this report we will be giving the commission and the council a coherent road map to ensure that our relations with china are rebalanced and that the deep concerns of european citizens are addressed in concrete terms.

stronger, deeper, and more balanced relationship with maximum mutual benefits for both sides.

in writing. the atlantic and mediterranean bluefin tuna stocks have been declining considerably over the years and there is an urgent need to protect them. the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (icct), to which the eu is a contracting party under the common commercial policy, adopted a new recommendation at its annual meeting in 2010. the amendments include a reduction in the allowable catch (tac) and a strengthening of the control measures used for the implementation of the recovery plan. i therefore support the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 302/2009 on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. the revenue generated by fishing is so important that it actively encourages illegal fishing and other illegal activities. it is therefore time to reassess and re-adjust the management measures adopted by iccat to current activities. it is also time for the european union to act rapidly on its own initiative and as a precautionary measure to protect bluefin tuna and ensure the recovery of its stocks.
in writing. following the various cruise ship accidents that have occurred in recent months, the european parliament has addressed the issue of double hulls on ships. my french colleague dominique riquet of the european people's party was responsible for the report on the recasting of the regulation on the accelerated introduction of double hulls on ships. the main objective was to implement new international rules established by the international maritime organisation (imo) in a regulation dating from 2002. as a member of the parliament's committee on the environment, i could not but support this report, which is also a tool in the fight against pollution. the double-hull regulation prevents the contents of tankers from leaking into seawater and causing serious pollution to oil in the event of collision or stranding. it is therefore essential that single-hull vessels speed up their compliance.
in writing. the environmental disasters of the erika in 1999 and the prestige in 2000 showed the need for better protection of oil tankers against damage, which has damaged our marine environment and coastal areas in the past. that is why i voted in favour of this text, which goes in that direction. the european parliament has for several years adopted effective decisions to increase the safety of oil tankers and reduce the risk of pollution.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague dominique riquet, which was adopted in plenary by 656 votes in favour, 4 against and 15 abstentions. the report is intended to reform a text which is resistant. this revision was necessary to take account of the numerous revisions to the text since its adoption in 2002 following accidents at sea involving oil tankers and the changes brought about by the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, in particular as regards the possibility for the european commission to adopt delegated acts.
in writing. this report calls for more parliamentary scrutiny of the delegated acts to be adopted by the european commission with regard to the regulation of tanker safety. i support that request. the subject is too sensitive for the commission to take decisions on it alone. in general, the control of the commission by the elected representatives of the people should be strengthened.
in writing. i have given my consent to the conclusion of a new fisheries agreement between the eu and mozambique. our countries are very present in mozambican waters, and many changes were necessary. these amendments are aimed at improving the management, control and governance of fishing activities in mozambican waters. other measures, such as the obligation to recruit mozambican seamen, are aimed at increasing the direct positive economic impact for the country. under the new protocol, the eu will pay €980,000 to mozambique: €520,000 for access to fishing waters and €460,000 to support mozambique's maritime and fisheries policy.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which will allow our vessels to fish legally on the mozambican coast. in a win-win approach, this agreement facilitates the economic activity of european companies (fisheries here), while allowing the union to contribute to the development of mozambique through its support for a sector essential to the country's economy. europe also promotes human rights and its democratic values, providing for the termination of the partnership if it finds that its principles are being violated.
in writing. the council aims to conclude a protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement with mozambique for a period of three years as a matter of urgency. the protocol will give 75 vessels from the european tuna fleet the opportunity to fish. the rapporteur, while recognising the urgency of concluding this agreement, nevertheless asks the commission and the council to submit a report assessing the results of the application of this protocol within a maximum of one year from its entry into force. i supported the report by my colleague, mrs dolores garcia-hierro caraballo, in the plenary.
in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation on a fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of mozambique. this text provides that the european union and european fishermen will give monetary and economic compensation when they exploit the mozambican seabed. european structural aid, taxes per vessel and per quantity caught, quotas for the employment of mozambican personnel per vessel, regular checks by the authorities of the country of the vessels and their log books are provided for. the whole thing will be set up with the participation of mozambican scientists and, in theory, with respect for human rights. in theory, if either party were to fail to comply with these clauses, the agreement would be suspended. in a country that has fallen into such misery, the agreement reached can be a blessing in terms of training, social inclusion and financing. for once, there seems to be reciprocity, something to which we in the european union are hardly accustomed. let us hope once again that the deeds will be in accordance with the speeches.
in writing. this week, the european parliament was consulted by european ministers on the creation of a financial transaction tax. as a member of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, i have long advocated the development of this draft and i welcome the fact that the european parliament has sent a strong message to the council, as 71% of the voting members supported the creation of a financial transaction tax. the ttf could generate up to €57 billion according to the european commission's forecasts. in these times of crisis, is this not a great opportunity for the financial sector to contribute to the recovery of europe, to revive its image and to regain the confidence of its citizens? finally, contrary to what the french socialists would have us believe, i would like to point out that the idea of a financial transaction tax was put forward by nicolas sarkozy both at national level (and it will apply in france from 1 august) and at european level. we can see the positive results today in the european parliament...
in writing. i voted in favour of the adoption of the podimata report, in favour of the introduction of a financial transaction tax (ftt). since the current crisis was created by stock market and financial speculation, i consider it logical and right that this tax should finally be introduced. the latest eurobarometer survey shows that 66% of europeans are in favour of such a tax. the financial transaction tax and the new resources it generates should also help finance growth in europe. from this point of view, we must defend the widest possible base and fight against exemptions and niches which would favour speculators. i regret the timidity of the european right, which has preferred to exclude pension funds, as if this financial instrument could not, like any other financial instrument, be used for speculation!
in writing. this tax is a tax for fiscal justice, which will make ultra-speculative activities pay and will help prevent new crises. the more we do it, the more effective it will be. this tax is also a tax on growth. from now on, finance will participate in the real economy, whether it wants to or not. it is in order that all, and particularly the states, may hear this strong message that we have voted in favour of this report in large numbers.
in writing. the european parliament has taken a major step forward in financial regulation by endorsing the commission's proposal to impose a financial transaction tax. the resolution adopted by parliament also sets out the contours of the tax in order for it to be truly effective: its scope must be as broad as possible and it must target, for example, all financial institutions located outside the eu that trade in securities issued from a member state. the resolution also calls for the implementation of an ambitious action plan to combat tax evasion. this resolution is a positive signal to the european citizens faced with the disastrous effects of the crisis.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which supports the creation of a financial transaction tax in the eu member states. this initiative, which president sarkozy wanted, would limit financial speculation, which is partly at the root of the crisis we are going through.
in writing. behind an attractive idea and laudable objectives, the taxation of financial transactions at european level is not satisfactory. the need to reconcile finance and the real economy is a necessity, since some practices in the field are disconnected from it. to make "the bankers" who have been supported in times of crisis pay may also seem fair. however, any tax on international financial transactions cannot be passed through the community channel. firstly, because the taxation of goods must be the exclusive responsibility of the member states. the european union hopes to appropriate this power of taxation while at the same time providing itself with its own resources, which would make it even more independent of the states. on the other hand, the scale of the continent is not suitable for the introduction of a tax which is intended to be a deterrent.
in writing. the main virtue of this report and of this proposal for a directive is that it sends a political signal to the financial sector, which is taxed so little in relation to the real productive activities and is so unsatisfactory when it comes to doing its real job: financing the economy. many speakers this morning said that this would hamper the access of businesses to the financing they need. but ask the latter if it can really be worse than today! i do not think that this is a strong signal, however, given the content of the debate this morning and the state of the matter in the council. but the transfer of all or part of this tax, if it ever comes into existence, to the european budget is completely unacceptable, as is any possibility given to the commission to adopt delegated acts in this area. the possibility that this tax, whatever form it takes, does not apply to the whole of the european union, and in particular to the united kingdom, is absurd. and above all, no one has raised the main problem: the unhindered free movement of capital at european and world level, the source of the financialization, speculation and 'short-termism' that undermine the world economy. so, in principle, but doubtful about the modalities, i abstained.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report recommending the introduction of a financial transaction tax (ftt) at european level, thus supporting the draft directive presented by the commission last september. the ftt is an excellent instrument for raising new revenue to finance recovery policies. it is one of the best ways of going beyond the mere austerity policies which are driving europe into the wall, plunging too many european citizens into precariousness and leading to political and democratic impasses, the extent of which some still refuse to measure. i regret, however, that the european parliament has granted an exemption to pension funds. this is a bad sign, especially as these funds - which are long-term investors - are marginally affected by the tax, which mainly penalises short-term players.
in writing. once again, the european parliament voted by a large majority in favour of such a financial transaction tax. i welcome this vote, which is a strong signal to the markets and to those states which are still reluctant to impose such a tax. risk-taking behaviour in financial markets has played a major role in the current crisis. it is more than urgent that they join the collective effort to bring europe out of the crisis and back to growth. the european parliament has made its views clear on this, and it is now up to the member states to do the same.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because a financial transaction tax is essential to the establishment of a new economic order which is more balanced and fair. it is not the citizens who are paying the price for the misuse of finance: the practices of finance have brought us to this situation, so it is only natural that it should help to correct it. the tax will thus discourage financial institutions from taking excessive risks and will also provide an additional source of revenue for the european union, both of which i believe are necessary to support the real economy. it was important to set a rate low enough to allow harmonization among european countries. moreover, the latter will make fraud unprofitable and the sanction mechanisms provided for will make it a very risky operation. despite this first step, the financial sector will only be able to face its responsibilities fully when this measure is adopted on a global scale. in the run-up to a global consensus, it is essential that the union should set an example by bringing to the international stage the proposal that was courageously put forward by nicolas sarkozy.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text setting out parliament's requests on the content of the future financial transaction tax. the question is no longer whether we are for or against the tax, but whether we want to be clear about the content of the tax. we are asking for the broadest possible range of taxable persons, and i regret that pension funds are exempt from this tax. this tax will discourage speculation and will make it possible to go directly to the european budget to increase its own resources.

in writing. the european commission has put the proposal for a financial transaction tax at the centre of the debate, in particular in response to the serious consequences of the financial crisis. the report by mrs podimata proposes that the financial sector be made to bear part of the costs of the crisis, that financial institutions be dissuaded from taking excessive risks, that regulatory measures be supplemented to prevent further crises, and that additional revenue be created to finance the general budget of the union by enriching the residence principle and by removing pension funds or occupational pension institutions from the list of financial institutions to which the ftt would apply. the report makes a strong case for the application of the financial transaction tax (ftt) at eu level . i therefore support this proposal. however, the report does not deal with the management of the revenue from this tax, and opts for the latter to be managed by the multiannual financial framework programme. the tff would represent a significant contribution to the european union's own resources, thus broadening the scope for financing specific policies, projects or public goods.
in writing. since the beginning of the economic and financial crisis affecting europe, the idea of introducing a financial transaction tax has been gaining ground. while the latest eurobarometer survey shows 66% of europeans support it, and parliament has been calling for it for almost two years, the commission put forward a legislative proposal to this effect at the end of 2011. the parliament, consulted on the proposal, has not questioned either the amount of the tax - set at 0.1% for shares and bonds and 0.01% for derivatives - or the timing (the entry into force will be before the end of december 2014). the text calls for the tax to be better designed so that more operators are subject to it and tax evasion is not profitable. the text also leaves open the possibility of financing the development of the least developed countries, at least in part, with the proceeds of the levy. i think these points are fundamental, which is why i supported this resolution. the ball is now in the council's court.

in writing. i voted in favour of the martin report on the detailed arrangements for the exercise of the european parliament's right of inquiry, which proposes a definition of the arrangements for the european parliament's right of inquiry. parliament acquired this right with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, subject to the council's agreement. article 226 provides that parliament may, at the request of one quarter of its component members, set up a temporary committee of inquiry to examine allegations of breach or maladministration in the application of union law. in order to clarify this provision, the text covers the subject matter and the general rules relating to the establishment of a committee of inquiry, the general rules of procedure and the inquiry.
mr president, the new republic of south sudan is only ten months old, but has been at war with its northern neighbour for eight months. more than 150,000 people have been displaced. fighting and bombing are continuing on the border, and these two countries, which have everything to prosper, are wasting their resources in a conflict with no end in sight that only adds to the tension in an already fragile region of africa. it is time for khartoum and juba to comply with the resolutions of the african union and the united nations, to end hostilities and to resume negotiations without conditions. the two new countries had pledged to their international guardians to settle the outstanding issues: the demarcation of the 20% of the border still to be drawn, the status of southerners living in the north and northerners living in the south and, above all, the sharing of oil resources. both the north, thanks to transit, and the south, which has 70% of the reserves, have an interest in concluding an agreement that would be mutually beneficial. but neither of them can count on the international community to remain silent in the face of the humanitarian tragedy that is unfolding. if dialogue between khartoum and juba is not resumed quickly, it will be essential for the united nations to apply pressure and take sanctions. i note that china has decided to take responsibility in this matter. that's good. but it is necessary - and indispensable - for the european union to continue to assert its position and political presence. our balanced position is the right one. let us make it more forceful and more readable and, above all - i say this to the eeas, but they know it well - let us not forget the conflict and the drama in darfur.

danish and polish presidencies, for bringing us to where we are today. i am happy to see that the compromise reached between inta and the council presidency endorses the core areas of the commission proposal. this is not a coincidence. our internal discussions in the commission were as complex as yours, and our proposal was the result of very careful reflection and a detailed impact assessment. the outcome was a balanced proposal which tackles head-on the true problems we face in the gsp. it is balanced because it focuses preferences on those who need them the most while, at the same time, expanding opportunities for countries which embrace core international values or values in human rights, labour rights and the environment. the commission proposal confronts head-on the real issues behind gsp. the first one is that the poorest developing countries will never grow sufficiently if we do not give them the space they need to export. this space is currently taken up by countries which are economically much more advanced and no longer need our unilateral preferences. we must focus preferences on the countries most in need. secondly, if we are serious about supporting sustainable development, we have to expand opportunities for those countries which are ready and willing to implement core international conventions. thirdly, without sufficient predictability, eu importers will never make best use of the gsp and the gsp will never fulfil its potential in terms of exports and growth for the countries most in need. the commission proposal squares the circle by providing answers to these three challenges, while safeguarding the legitimate interests of eu industry and respecting wto rules. while i would have preferred to do without some aspects of the compromise reached between inta and the council presidency, i can and will support it because it strikes a realistic balance between the very many different views in this particularly complex dossier, and one that ultimately well reflects the policy priorities the commission agreed on in the first place. i therefore count on your help to support a compromise that is as realistic as it is politically important – a compromise whereby the eu will help those who need it most and those who embrace international values while respecting the interests of our industry and international law.

in writing. i voted in favour of this decision, which allows the european union to provide financial support to italy following the extensive damage caused by the floods that hit the italian regions of liguria and tuscany in october 2011. the funds will be used, among other things, to rebuild the houses. by reacting swiftly to natural disasters, the european union is showing solidarity with the people affected by them.
in writing. the report by my colleague josé manuel fernandes was adopted on 12 june by 658 votes to none. it will make it possible to mobilise the solidarity fund to help spain and italy affected by severe natural disasters in liguria and tuscany. the adoption of this report will make it possible to mobilise around eur 18 million in commitment and payment appropriations in 2012. i supported this report in plenary.
in writing. last october, italy was hit by extremely violent rains. the equivalent of six months of rain fell on tuscany and liguria in a matter of hours, causing unprecedented flooding. the damage caused by water, landslides and mudslides was considerable: houses were destroyed, pipes destroyed, electricity and telephone lines were cut, roads and highways were damaged, etc. the italian authorities estimated the total cost of direct damage at eur 772,5 million and requested assistance from the eu solidarity fund. through the adoption of this resolution, which i support, we are approving funding of around eur 18 million to help repair the damage caused by these floods, and in particular to enable the rehabilitation of basic infrastructure such as water, gas and electricity supply. the citizens of these regions will thus be able to return to normal living conditions and economic activities, such as tourism, will be able to resume.
in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. this time it is direct aid to france amounting to eur 24 493 525. as the rapporteur explains, the total number of workers to benefit from the co-financed package of personalised services is 3 582, including 1 384 redundancies at renault and seven of its suppliers between 1 april 2009 and 31 july 2009, and 2 198 other workers made redundant by the same eight companies.
in writing. i share the rapporteur, mr kozlowski, in his view that the amount allocated to the commission's initiative for technical assistance linked to the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund should be reduced. the report confirms the amount of eur 730 000 decided by the council, out of the eur 1 750 000 which could theoretically be legally released, and takes a common sense position in a period when public money must be managed as efficiently as possible. i would also like to note that the rapporteur's proposal was accepted by the committee on budgets, which stressed the need to achieve the abolition of these specific funds allocated to the european commission as soon as possible.
in writing. while the european parliament and the council have since 2008 set up a european globalisation adjustment fund to provide financial support for workers made redundant for economic reasons, the text put to the vote was intended to take part of the amounts allocated for simple operational expenditure (monitoring, evaluation of the fund, communication). since this expenditure does not meet the objectives of the fund and could be borne by the commission's budget, i have chosen, in the interests of responsible management of public funds, not to approve this proposal.
in writing. i voted in favour of strengthening cooperation with latin america. under the terms of the lisbon treaty, our objective is to promote sustainable economic and social development. it is important to transmit our democratic values to the world. the region includes middle-income countries that have achieved remarkable successes in reducing poverty and inequality through economic growth and political and social reforms. so while there is still much to be done in the areas of malnutrition, food security, poverty, life expectancy, etc., we need to broaden our areas of cooperation. the average growth rate of these countries is too high for us to leave them out of the picture! europe must take account of these new economic models!
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the definition of a new development cooperation with latin america. as the main donor of development aid in latin america, the european union wishes to strengthen its cooperation in the region by promoting dialogue on climate change, innovation and the fight against drugs. although latin america has experienced the highest growth in recent years, the region needs to continue its efforts to consolidate the rule of law. indeed, despite progress in social justice and improved living standards, 52 million people still live on less than two dollars a day. in this sense, there are many challenges to be met in the fight against poverty and social cohesion, the promotion of entrepreneurship and the development of the private sector. it is also important to encourage social services by investing in research and innovation. this new cooperation is also intended to intensify bi-regional relations with the signing of the agreement establishing an association with central america. it also endorsed the creation of an investment mechanism for latin america and the implementation of the eu-lac foundation.
in writing. i have chosen not to support this text which proposes to devote one third of european geographical aid for cooperation and development to latin america. at a time when the countries of the european union are concerned about their low growth, or even recession, it seemed irresponsible to me to maintain a high level of funds for a region whose growth rates are far higher than ours. in the context of sound management of public funds, european development aid must be given priority to those countries which need it most!
in writing. we have been forced to decide on a reorientation of the priorities of our development cooperation with latin america. i voted in favour of mr cortés lastra's report because it stresses the need to move towards renewed cooperation with latin america. this is an opportunity for the eu to stop with the neoliberal recipes of the past. promoting growth does not lead to prosperity for all! social cohesion is of crucial importance in this process. growth and the fight against poverty cannot be systematically linked. the ep will soon be asked about its approval of the free trade agreement with colombia and peru and the association agreement with central america. they are totally contrary to the objectives of our development policy. the european commission has always had the failing to interpret development policy through the prism of international trade. it is time to reverse the logic and put policy coherence for development at the very heart of any agreement. the report stresses the need for coherence in all european policies and systematic respect for environmental and social standards, while also including civil society.
in writing. the european union is latin america's largest donor of development aid, and its largest investor and second largest trading partner. in this own-initiative report, parliament has chosen to define a new form of development cooperation which now takes account of the situation in each country and is based on broader indicators than income levels, such as economic and technological progress and the echo poverty, vulnerability and crisis index. i supported this report in plenary, and it was adopted by a large majority. i'm glad you did.
in writing. the eu is latin america's largest donor of development aid, largest investor and second largest trading partner. latin america was less badly hit by the economic and financial crisis than the european economies: +4.5% growth forecast for 2012. unfortunately, there are still 180 million people living below the poverty line in latin america. the definition of a new cooperation with latin america was therefore important, in particular by modifying the instruments of aid to this cooperation. the emphasis, as the rapporteur recommends, should be on phasing out bilateral aid to middle-income countries in order to increase aid to low-income countries. in view of the humanitarian and health situation in the countries of latin america, it is essential to re-prioritize the essential services of education, training, hygiene and health, which have been abolished by the european commission. finally, as a driving force for the future of this cooperation, regional policies must be stimulated in order to adjust budgetary and fiscal policies. my vote in favour of this report is a reminder of the need to reorient regional cooperation policies on urgent health and humanitarian issues.
in writing. the mobility of our businesses, citizens and children across the european union must not be hampered by red tape and language barriers. i therefore voted in favour of a report which aims to facilitate the practice of crossborder volunteering. an incredible opportunity for exchange and learning, volunteering can also be a growth factor, as it already represents almost 5% of the european union's gdp. we had to recognize and value the practice of volunteering!
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. as the 'year of volunteering', 2011 was an opportunity for the commission and the european parliament to study the challenges of volunteering activities in europe. as an indispensable tool for active support of society, volunteering brings the principles of solidarity and democracy to life in europe. voluntary activities account for 5% of world gdp and thus represent a real added value for european policies. it is therefore our duty to promote this sector in the future, to adopt a clear legal framework and to simplify administrative procedures. in this sense, i support the various actions proposed, including the creation of a centralised european portal on volunteering and the creation of a european voluntary humanitarian aid corps. one of the key measures in this report is the development of a european skills passport. it seems to me important to value the personal and professional skills acquired during these civic engagements. in addition, in order to facilitate crossborder volunteering activities, i believe that our action should be complemented by the development of a european statute for associations.
in writing. 100 million is the number of european citizens engaged in voluntary activities. in 2011, europe put them at the forefront of the european year of voluntary activities for the promotion of active citizenship. in 2012, the european parliament continued to act to promote their development and remove obstacles to their activities. that is the aim of this report, and that is why i voted in favour of it. one of the key measures he is proposing is the 'european skills passport'. the skills, competences and professional qualifications acquired through volunteering will now be better recognised, and this across europe.
in writing. europeans who wish to embark on international volunteering too often face paperwork or language barriers. it is, however, an incredible opportunity for citizens to exchange and learn. volunteering affects nearly 100 million europeans and contributes to almost 5% of the eu's gdp. the linguistic and technical difficulties faced by european citizens wishing to volunteer must therefore be overcome. new, effective and innovative tools need to be developed, such as a european portal that centralises all volunteering offers and the recognition of qualifications acquired. and finally, there can be no volunteer without organization. the commission must therefore move towards the recognition of a european status for associations.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to strengthen and facilitate crossborder volunteering and to reduce the administrative, legal and linguistic barriers to volunteering. in this report we call on the member states to set national objectives for volunteering and to recognise the rights of volunteers, in particular by establishing a european statute for volunteering. our report also suggests the setting up of an online information portal on volunteering issues. 100 million european citizens are currently engaged in volunteering activities! volunteering is an incredible opportunity for exchange and learning, and cross-border volunteering has great potential for education, employment and citizenship, to improve mutual understanding and to contribute to the development of a stronger european identity. volunteering is one of the ways of living an active european citizenship and, as the only french region neighbouring three other member states, i am very attached to it.
in writing. the european parliament in plenary session in strasbourg voted today by a large majority on my colleague marco scurria's report on crossborder volunteering activities in the eu. today 22.6% of young people are looking for a job in the european union. we know that the first difficulty for them is getting their first job, often rejected on the grounds of lack of experience. yet, many are involved in volunteer work. the technical and human skills they acquire in their humanitarian, cultural or sporting commitments are also assets on the labour market or for validating certain university courses. it is in this context that the scurria report calls for a european status for volunteering, official recognition of qualifications acquired through volunteering and the creation of a skills passport that is valid throughout the eu.
in writing. volunteering is a fundamental citizen commitment to democratic vitality. why stop it and restrict it? it is essential to facilitate volunteering activities, whether national or cross-border, by establishing a clear legal framework and simplified visa procedures for volunteers fulfilling all the conditions defined by the member states.
in writing. volunteering is an essential tool for promoting active support from society. it acts as a catalyst for greater social integration. studies also show that the development of volunteering could help to increase european gdp by 5%. however, there are still many obstacles to volunteering in the european union. i voted in favour of mr scurria's report, which proposes concrete actions to promote crossborder volunteering activities in the european union. for example, the creation of a european portal, which would allow for more effective cooperation between organisations active in the field of volunteering and encourage the dissemination of best practices. or the creation of a european skills passport, which could be very useful as each volunteer could have their skills acquired through volunteering recognised throughout the european union.
in writing. following the european year of volunteering, it seems to me essential that the european parliament also takes a step forward to make european volunteering a reality. volunteers contribute so much to cultural and environmental activities, to social and local missions, that the need to support them is undeniable. but they still face many difficulties. three out of four europeans think that there should be more volunteering programmes. i therefore supported this report, which proposes the setting up of an ambitious european voluntary humanitarian aid corps, which will train volunteers and send them on local missions. on the other hand, we are calling for the creation of a european skills passport which will allow for real recognition of volunteering. encouraging european volunteering also means encouraging european growth, in line with the europe 2020 strategy, and fighting youth unemployment. the technical and human skills they acquire are valuable assets on the labour market or for validating certain university courses. finally, volunteering helps to strengthen our sense of citizenship and our european identity for all.
in writing. a few months after the closure of the european year of volunteering (2011), parliament has just adopted a report on volunteering, almost unanimously, which is rather rich in terms of findings and proposals. i welcome the fact that many of my amendments have been incorporated, in particular the one reiterating the request for a european statute for associations after the long silence of the commission on this matter, and i ask for a clarification of the concept of subsidies to associations in order to provide financial support to associations, often the first victims of budgetary restrictions. one regret is the rejection by a large majority of members of the house of the proposal to abolish visas for volunteers. the same ridiculous anti-immigrant obsession, when the european parliament did not want to impose any obligations in this area. we should be pleased that the possibility of relaxing these visas has nevertheless been maintained.
cyberattacks are no longer just found in the movie "the matrix", they are a reality today and especially in europe. i voted in favour of a report on the protection of computer infrastructures. it covers a number of topics, cybercrime, data protection, but also the protection of our children. minimum standards of resilience are needed today!
in writing. the kalfin report on the protection of critical information infrastructures has received my support. the exponential development of the internet has made it an indispensable element of citizens' daily lives and economic activity. it is therefore essential for the european union to place the digital strategy at the heart of its political priorities. the report perfectly underlines the paramount issue of cybersecurity. in this context, parliament rightly calls for the establishment of a system of cooperation and international standards, and the development of a comprehensive, responsive, flexible and innovative long-term framework to ensure proper interaction between different internet users and to establish a system for reporting security breaches in critical sectors. it is also in this spirit that i joined parliament's special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering.
in writing. the internet is now at the heart of the lives of citizens and businesses alike. for its safe use, we need a robust digital environment. this report proposes concrete measures to improve the security, prevention of attacks and resilience of this crucial structure of our economy. i therefore voted in favour of it. i particularly support the report's approach to linking internet security and user trust. his proposal to raise awareness among european citizens about digital security issues through events, guidelines, advice and education and training initiatives seems essential to me.
in writing. while the internet and telecommunications are vast spaces for exchange and discovery, and promising sources of growth and jobs for the economies of tomorrow, they also pose a real security challenge, given the threats to the data they disseminate. that is why i voted in favour of this text, which supports the strengthening of the european union's policy on 'cybersecurity', for a safer internet and communications, for the benefit of our citizens, our consumers and our businesses!
in writing. the report by my colleague, mr ivailo kalfin, was adopted by 573 votes in favour, 90 against and 26 abstentions. this is an own-initiative report in response to the commission's 2011 communication on the protection of critical information infrastructures (piic), which takes stock and describes the next steps. the european parliament, in its own initiative report, calls for measures to protect the internet, including the prevention of cyberattacks and the resilience of the global network. it also called for the establishment of a system for reporting security breaches in critical sectors and for the resilience of the internet to be strengthened. i supported this report in the plenary during the vote on 12 june.
in writing. as cybercrime continues to increase, it is essential to protect critical information infrastructures and ensure an adequate level of information security. security must be at the heart of our concerns so that technological advances can be fully benefited. for example, member states should have national response plans in place in the event of computer incidents.
in writing. i have endorsed the idea of the joint purchase of energy raw materials by the member states. today, competition for energy resources and monopolies in the field of production pose important problems. energy cooperation in europe and beyond our borders must be deepened. for the rapporteur edit herczog, a better exchange of information is imperative. the major foreign energy suppliers have their own information on the consumption of european countries, while we ourselves have no idea what our neighbours consume. such knowledge would, however, strengthen our position as a buyer on the international market. we need new legislation on the provision and processing of this kind of information, which naturally must remain confidential.
in writing. seeking to build a strategy for a secure, sustainable and competitive energy supply is a good intention. despite this proposal, i have decided to vote against this report. this is mainly because one paragraph deals with shale gas, whereas in france i am one of those who are firmly opposed to the granting of licences for the exploration of shale gas. the only technique used to date, hydraulic fracturing, poses irreversible problems and global threats to the environment, especially to our drinking water supplies. the commission's proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling of foodstuffs is a very good one.
in writing. a strategic approach is urgently needed to ensure a secure, sustainable and competitive energy supply. the decline in the eu's internal fossil fuel resources will increase the union's dependence on energy imports, despite the growing contribution of renewable sources, energy efficiency and research in energy technologies. i support a common external energy policy based on solidarity. we need to step up our diversification and rethink our strategic cooperation with the major energy producing countries. ensuring the security of supply of the european union would strengthen the union's capacity to act in foreign policy matters and its credibility as a global actor, in particular in the field of climate change.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which seeks to find solutions to consolidate the internal energy market. the european union needs to create a broader regulatory framework and to emphasise key concepts such as sustainability, energy sustainability, better coordination between european networks and diversification of suppliers, sources and supply routes. i note that this report was the subject of a full agreement between the epp, the socialists and the liberals.
in writing. our energy needs are immense and growing. and much of that energy has to be imported. energy security is a challenge we must face together. this report contributes to the debate on the need for and how to develop ambitious common external action in the field of energy. i welcome the emphasis on relations with the countries of the caspian sea region, and in particular with azerbaijan. the country is very open to the infrastructure projects we want to develop in the region and to a constantly strengthened trade, energy and political partnership.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which supports a coordinated and effective foreign policy of the member states of the european union on energy supply. by speaking with one voice, the european union will be stronger in securing its supplies against trading partners who have, in the past, sometimes used energy as a political weapon. it will also be stronger in influencing the level of prices offered, and thus better defend the interests of our consumers.
in writing. on this roadmap for energy cooperation with third countries, the greens secured amendments, notably on reducing import dependence with increased deployment of renewable energy, on the need to align with long-term climate and energy policy objectives, on the need to ensure sustainable energy supply at local level in developing countries and on the need to be more skeptical of the use of biofuels. however, i could not vote for this report, which promotes shale gas and tar sands and supports projects such as iter.
in writing. the report by my colleague edit herczog aims to suggest ways of improving the internal energy market. the report calls for the extension of links between european energy networks and neighbouring countries and the creation of a broader regulatory framework. in order to improve the coherence and stability of the european external energy policy, parliament also suggested the creation of a strategic grouping for international energy cooperation to enable regular coordination between the member states, the commission and the council. finally, the report emphasises key concepts such as better coordination, diversification, energy sustainability/viability and strengthened partnerships with supplier countries.
in writing. as the world's largest energy importer, the time has come for the european union to define a european energy policy to effectively guide the use of energy, both within and beyond our borders. the report focuses on key concepts such as better coordination, diversification, energy sustainability/viability, and strengthened partnerships with supplier countries. the emphasis is on important areas such as major energy networks and infrastructures, strategic dialogues and international partnerships. it is also important to be able to exchange information, with the establishment of a platform that would enable such exchanges, and to know about european and third country projects in the field of energy. my vote in favour of this report is in support of one very important aspect: the improvement of cooperation with third countries in the fields of energy and infrastructure. this multilateral cooperation will aim at strengthening partnerships with third countries in several areas, from innovation and research to the construction of reliable networks and facilities ensuring a diversified supply for the european union.
in writing. the eu's energy security is a strategic and vital issue: the union is poor in natural resources and is heavily dependent on its external partners for its energy supply. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which stresses the need for large-scale energy infrastructure interconnected with neighbourhood networks. this is the whole purpose of the future transeuropean energy networks. i also believe that the union should encourage and support cooperation with its partners on innovative projects such as the mediterranean solar plan or desertec. strengthening coordination with our partners, promoting the diversification of our energy mix, both its composition and our suppliers, and ensuring energy sustainability are all guarantees of a policy that meets the needs of european citizens and businesses. partnership with third countries is essential, and i supported the creation of the strategic grouping for international energy cooperation. it is now up to us to develop an ambitious cooperation component, particularly to ensure the ecological transition: if we want to green our economy, but our energy depends on our partners, then we must convince them to develop clean and renewable energy. this is how this partnership will be a win-win for europeans, third countries and our planet.

is a key element of our overall strategy to ensure that europe emerges from the current situation with increased growth and a stronger economic basis. to put it very simply, europe needs growth and
