in writing. i supported the report appointing mrs ivanova as a member of the court of auditors for 6 years. this appointment, approved by a large majority of the european parliament, follows the regulatory procedure, namely a prior consultation of the european parliament before any decision of the council, which will be based on the proposals made by each member state.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls for the strengthening of international efforts to ensure that all human rights recognised by un conventions are considered to be universal, indivisible, interdependent and closely linked. we also need to integrate democracy support more fully into the eu's external action, supporting democratic governance through its various financial instruments.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which encourages european diplomacy to exert a greater influence on the decisions and actions of the united nations. our common commitment to human rights, but also to the values of peace, security and freedom, can indeed enable the european union to make its contribution to the development of democracy, peace and prosperity throughout the world, in a complementary and coordinated way with the member states.
in writing. by adopting the report proposing a recommendation to the council on the 67th session of the united nations general assembly, the european parliament affirms its commitment to creating a strong and stable partnership between the united nations and the european union. a will that i commend. it is vital to coordinate the union's action as much as possible by presenting unified positions and by strengthening its coherence and visibility as a global actor within the un, but also by consolidating its contribution to the un's work.
in writing. the european union and the united nations (un) share common values and standards which aim to ensure peace, security and the protection of human rights in the world. moreover, the eu and its member states are the main financial contributors to the un, providing 39% of the organisation's regular budget and more than 40% of its peacekeeping operations. however, cooperation between the two organisations is not yet well defined. in the report adopted this week in plenary, which i supported, we called on the council to clarify and strengthen the eu's relations with the un, in particular with its general assembly which will meet for its 67th session at the end of the year. this international meeting will be an opportunity for the eu to assert its leading role in a world where concerted action is increasingly needed.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by parliament of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council applying the scheme of generalised tariff preferences without distorting the original structure proposed by the commission. i note that the trilogue with the council and the commission has made progress in the same direction and has met parliament's objectives, particularly on the most sensitive points such as the clauses concerning the textile sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which revises the scheme of generalised tariff preferences (gsp). since 1971, the european union has granted trade preferences to developing countries. these provisions are regularly adapted to the economic growth of each country. today's vote is the first revision of this codecision system. the compromise reached with the council is almost hopeless, given the deep differences which remained between the member states. in our view, french socialists, this text reconciles two imperatives: that the large emerging countries no longer enjoy privileged access to the european market, and that exports from the poorest countries are facilitated. this new trade regime will therefore make it possible to help developing countries more effectively, and at the same time it will be a step forward in our fight for fair trade, since it will virtually exclude emerging countries from the international trading system.
in writing. to enable the poorest countries to participate in world trade, the european union has been using the system of generalised tariff preferences since 1971. this system facilitates the entry of products from less economically developed countries into the european market by granting them total or partial exemption from customs duties. but the world economy has changed a lot in the last 40 years. some emerging countries which have hitherto benefited from the gsp, such as brazil, china and russia, no longer have the same difficulties in participating in trade. the new system will focus on countries that need it most, so it is going in the right direction. a second major step forward is the introduction of an incentive system known as 'spg+'. it will reward countries that commit themselves to sustainable development and take action to promote human rights.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to improve the effectiveness of the customs benefits granted by the european union by targeting them on 80 developing countries instead of the more than 170 today. the application of these preferential tariffs should thus make it possible to promote international trade, economic growth and social development in the countries which need them most, without other foreign firms taking advantage of them to compete unfairly with european production on the internal market.
in writing. i gave my full support to the revision of the scheme of generalised tariff preferences, which was being examined for the first time since 1971 in codecision. the text reconciles two imperatives to which the social democrats are particularly attached: to ensure that the large emerging countries no longer enjoy privileged access to the european market, and to facilitate exports from the poorest countries. i therefore welcome the fact that this new trade regime will eventually make it possible to give better support to developing countries in the fight for fair trade, since this will mean that emerging countries will be almost completely excluded from this system. i welcome the message thus addressed to the ultra-liberals, that the logic of excessive competition must now give way to the healthy and balanced development that the socialists so ardently desire.
in writing. the system of generalised tariff preferences provides for the granting of preferential rights, including customs duties, to developing countries. the system, created in 1971, is a necessary mechanism in an increasingly competitive global economic and commercial environment. while europe is experiencing a crisis of unprecedented violence, some of the developing countries are experiencing significant growth and have become very successful. it is therefore necessary to update this system by concentrating efforts on the least developed countries and by raising the level of award criteria by requiring, for example, compliance with 27 international conventions on human rights, labour and the environment. it is now up to the commission to apply this tool in a balanced way, in accordance with the realities on the ground, and not to rely solely on a mechanical application of the criteria listed in the various existing schemes (spg, spg+, 'everything but weapons').
in writing. i have supported the report by my colleague mr fjellner on the restoration of the generalised tariff preferences (gsp) scheme. the trade agreement will give 80 developing countries and territories preferential access to the eu market in the form of reduced customs duties on goods they export to the eu market. it is an indispensable tool for foreign and development policy. i also welcome the extension of the gsp+ criterion, which makes the granting of trade advantages conditional on ratification of basic conventions on human rights, labour and the environment. it is an essential and effective means of promoting the values of the european union.
in writing. the generalised system of preferences (gsp) has existed in europe since 1971 and its benefits are no longer to be demonstrated. it was nevertheless necessary to adapt it to the world economic reality: some countries classified as less developed became, in a few years, very successful. under the new gsp criteria, these will no longer be able to benefit from the preferential tariffs, while the ldcs will be able to benefit more. that is why i voted in favour of the amendments in this plenary session. i also welcome the improvement in the monitoring and control of the gsp+, which makes the granting of additional preferences conditional on the application of 27 core conventions on human rights, labour and the environment. this is a point i made in my report of november 2011: trade can be a means of promoting the eu's core values if and only if the eu gives itself the means to enforce them. the revision of the preference withdrawal mechanism is a step in the right direction. this positive vote will also allow the proposal to be finalised and put into effect by the end of the year.
in writing. since 1971, as part of its common commercial policy, the european union has applied preferential trade tariffs (spt) to certain developing countries in order to encourage their economic growth. however, some emerging countries are now competing with europe in world markets, and these advantages are therefore no longer justified. the updating of the gsps will reduce the number of countries enjoying preferential access to eu markets from 176 to around 75. it will also reduce the total value of imports under the preferential system by some eur 20 billion. on the other hand, we are strengthening another special regime, called gsp+, which offers higher benefits but with conditions: countries will have to prove that they respect the 27 international conventions in the field of human rights and sustainable development. by voting in favour of this proposal for a regulation, we want to help those countries which really need it, by encouraging them to adopt our values, and also to strengthen our trade defenses against our direct competitors.
in writing. since 1971, the european union has granted tariff preferences to certain developing countries to make it easier for them to export certain products to the eu without reciprocity. more recently, the union has introduced a system called the generalised scheme of preferences (gsp+) whereby countries that commit themselves to a certain respect for human rights, democracy and the environment obtain additional trade benefits. this system is indeed not commercially favourable to the eu, but to destroy it on the grounds that it must comply with wto rules is a political choice and a further step towards the rule of market law alone. it cannot afford to suffer less and less from exceptions, even when it comes to supporting the poorest countries in the world. the new gsp+ system will therefore restrict the number of least developed countries (ldcs) that benefit from it and will not include the particularly fragile areas of the small island countries, as my reunion colleague younous omarjee has strongly denounced. i therefore voted against this report, to denounce this new hypocrisy of the european union in the field of development.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this measure which strengthens the surveillance of euro area countries in difficulty. it is essential that the commission and the governments of the monetary union know the exact situation of their neighbours in crisis, so that their financial assistance is as appropriate and effective as possible. the increase in surveillance also serves as a guarantee that the countries concerned are implementing the reforms needed to stabilise their situation and are not threatening the euro area economies as a whole with their irresponsibility.
in writing. i abstained on this report because, even if the socialists have succeeded in getting the 'golden rule' and the limitation of the structural deficit to 0.5% introduced by mr gauzès in his initial report, the generalization of the reverse qualified majority rule, which would excessively strengthen the power of the commission, deciding alone whether to place a state under surveillance, constitutes an unacceptable risk.
in writing. the two reports, known as the 'two pack', were put to the vote in plenary. i voted in favour of both reports in the votes on 13 june 2012. the two-pack represents a further step forward in budgetary surveillance. it complements the 'six pack', a legislative package adopted by the european parliament in september 2011, which provides for measures to strengthen economic governance. the first report by my colleague, mr jean-paul gauzès, concerns the strengthening of economic and budgetary surveillance of member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with regard to their financial stability within the euro area. it provides that once a state is under protection, it cannot be declared in default. in addition, the country's creditors must make themselves known to the commission within two months. in addition, interest rates on loans will be frozen.
in writing. the two 'two-pack' proposals were adopted by a large majority in the european parliament this morning. the powers of the european commission in budgetary surveillance of the member states are strengthened. it's called a custody order. the national budgets will therefore be consulted by the european commission and the other member states of the union with the obligation to make the structural reforms necessary to clean up public accounts. member states which disobey the directives of brussels will be fined more automatically. this is the end of the budgetary sovereignty of the states, the logical consequence of the loss of their monetary sovereignty. as manuel barroso has said, it is now a matter of making political union, otherwise it will be a matter of disintegration. the tone is set. the political coup d'état of the brussels technocracy, with the complicity of the european parliament and governments, is under way. the people will watch, powerless, as their freedom is destroyed. i have of course opposed the adoption of these two proposals for regulations.
in writing. this report aggravates the provisions of the six pack and the esm treaty currently under ratification. it gives the unelected european commission the power to place any eurozone member state under austerity plans and surveillance missions that it alone decides. the council may only revoke such decisions if it so decides within 10 days by the qualified majority provided for. the text also sets out the outlines of future adjustment plans. they will also have to promote free competition, particularly in the field of public procurement. the text would also apply to states which are already receiving 'financial assistance' and would therefore change the conditions under which these states can free themselves from the troika's tutelage. as for the "legal protection" put forward, it would only be effective from 2017 and would enshrine the repayment of the interest on the debt of the states without any condition of legitimacy. i am voting against this text and denouncing it.
in writing. in 2008, a us financial crisis led to a global economic crisis. today, let us not let the difficulties of greece ravage the euro area. but also, and most importantly, let us not allow the greek situation to happen again. we have the same currency. our economies are far too interconnected for decisions to be made unilaterally. the economic governance of the euro area is therefore necessary. these reports set out measures to strengthen the commission's powers in the monitoring of national budgets and to improve its democratic control by strengthening the role of the european parliament. in addition, a new rule would allow the commission to put a country at risk of defaulting under legal protection, with a view to giving it greater clarity, stability and predictability in dealing with its problems. by voting in favour of this proposal for a regulation, we are sending a clear signal to the council. the time for short-term and last-chance meetings is over.
in writing. at a time when greece and spain can no longer reasonably finance themselves on the markets, european partners must understand that they can no longer spend without consideration, and that it is now the control of their sovereignty and their future that is at stake. it is this principle of common sense that our political family has been able to put forward in this text, which endorses the new imperative deficit-control objectives contained in the stability and growth pact. the euro area member states which fail to meet their commitments to limit debt to 60% of gdp and to vote reasonably balanced budgets will now be subject to increased surveillance and a programme to clean up public accounts. this new method of monitoring budgetary discipline and correcting deficits is, in my view, a lifesaver in many ways. it will ensure a climate of financial stability which is essential to the restoration of confidence, which is the real engine of growth. it will also prevent future generations from bearing the burden of a debt they did not incur and will ensure that they are able to retain control of their own destiny.
in writing. several advances to be highlighted. the objective of debt mutualisation is specified. the redumption fund, originally proposed by the efta countries, will transfer the amounts of debt exceeding 60% of gdp. these pooled sums, amounting to eur 2.3 trillion, will be repaid over 25 years, allowing the creation of eurobonds which we have been calling for for many months. parliament proposed the creation of a growth instrument mobilising 1% of the gdp of the member states over ten years, or about eur 100 billion, for investment in infrastructure projects of european interest. because while some people talk about financial stability and fiscal consolidation and others about growth, we really need both. the member states are deeply in debt and it is up to the union to invest to restore competitiveness. it should go further, for example by using european savings. we have ensured the effectiveness of these tools by reintroducing the community method. in line with the six pack, an economic dialogue with the european parliament is being established. this restores democratic legitimacy to decisions that have long been taken between governments.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text drawn up by the socialist member for the european parliament, mrs ferreira, because she supports the draft regulation establishing a golden rule for the public finances of the member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of my colleague elisa ferreira's report because it incorporates proposals long rejected by the european conservatives such as growth facilities and the implementation of a roadmap for the introduction of eurobonds, which are more than ever needed to curb speculation. i regret, however, that because of opposition from the conservatives and liberals, it was not possible to pass an amendment allowing public investment to be given preferential treatment in the debt and deficit statistics of economies under pressure.
in writing. on 13 june, meps voted on the two reports known as the 'two packs' which complete the package of six legislative acts to strengthen economic governance. the text by mrs ferreira, which has given rise to the greatest number of disagreements, aims to increase the role of the commission in examining the budgets of the member states. the commission will thus be able to require a member state to present a new budgetary plan if the path taken by the state deviates too sharply from the requirements of the stability and growth pact. the adoption of the two reports should provide general guidance for the two rapporteurs who will be responsible for negotiating the regulations with the member states and the commission. however, the socialist group, through some rather inelegant stratagems, succeeded in getting amendments to the treaty to be included, such as the creation of a fund for the amortisation of debts exceeding 60% of the gdp of the countries concerned. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services. the european parliament must now support a principle which is far from unanimous within it.
in writing. the two 'two-pack' reports were put to the vote in plenary. i voted in favour of both reports in the votes on 13 june 2012. the two-pack represents a further step forward in budgetary surveillance. it complements the 'six-pack', a legislative package adopted by the european parliament in september 2011, which provides for measures to strengthen economic governance. the second report by mrs elisa ferreira lays down common rules for the monitoring and evaluation of draft budgetary plans and for the correction of excessive deficits in the euro-area member states. the report aims to oblige the 17 member states to consult the commission before any economic measure which might have consequences for neighbouring states.
in writing. this report proposes that all euro area member states should be placed under the auspices of the european commission. it places all states in an excessive deficit situation under the increased surveillance of the commission. it obliges all the member states to detail each provision of their draft budgets to the commission. this one can make amends. its amendments will have to be adopted by the national parliaments, or else sanctions will be imposed. the text also incorporates many of the provisions of the budgetary pact currently being ratified. it thus obliges the states to submit any investment to the commission for validation, to set up 'automatic correction mechanisms' in the event of non-compliance with the budgetary adjustments envisaged by the commission. it also establishes the 'economic partnership programme' provided for by the tscg for all states under an excessive deficit procedure. i vote against this democratic hold up
in writing. the time has come to restore the confidence of the citizens. this is now a vital imperative for the survival of the european union. even though there is something positive in the substance of this 'two-pack' which complements the economic governance package, i abstained on both the gauzès and ferreira reports. if we are not able to explain the added value and the rationale for implementing these measures to the citizens, then i do not see how we will be able to get out of the multidimensional crisis we are in. adding measures to measures without a substantive agreement on the project we want to build together will get us nowhere. i therefore abstain more from a scepticism about the mode of action chosen than from a total disagreement on the substance, because there are certain provisions in these reports which i support, such as the idea of a redemption fund, that of a road map for eurobonds or even a stronger coordination of budgets and the issuance of sovereign debt.
in writing. the european parliament voted this week on two regulations, the so-called 'two-pack'. these texts are part of the arsenal that is now being thrown at europe. they are in line with the european budgetary pact, which constitutionalises the golden rule, and with the '6 pack', the elder brother of the treaty, which aims to integrate the principle of austerity into european law with the european semester, which sets up the commission's control of national budgets. the first is the gauzès report (epp, french), which is intended to strengthen economic and budgetary surveillance of member states experiencing serious difficulties with regard to their financial stability within the euro area. the ferreira report (portuguese socialist) deals with the monitoring and evaluation of draft budgetary plans and the correction of excessive deficits in the euro-zone member states. i regret that the ferreira report was adopted by a large majority (501 votes in favour, 138 against and 36 abstentions), thanks to the support of the socialist and green groups. the few amendments on growth and eurobonds do not change the logic which remains profoundly austerity-oriented and anti-democratic, despite the sprinkling of nice words like growth and employment.
in writing. i voted in favour of the binev report on the proposal to amend the mandate of the european bank for reconstruction and development to extend its scope of operations to the southern and eastern mediterranean region. the european union must support the region's transition to pluralism and democracy, as well as openness and economic development in the wake of the hopes raised by the arab spring. the report stresses the need for a gradual approach, taking into account the specificities of each country and territory concerned.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this text, which authorises our european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) to help our mediterranean neighbours rebuild their economies and thus their democracies. as in eastern europe after the collapse of communism, the ebrd will enable the european union to promote more open, more liberalized and therefore more efficient economies, which go hand in hand with political and democratic progress, which are central values in our european construction.
in writing. originally set up to support the development of market economies in the countries of central europe and central asia following the collapse of communist regimes, the mandate of the european bank for reconstruction and development has since been extended to the countries of the southern and eastern mediterranean in order to support the countries of the region in their transition to market economies and democracy. as a co-legislator, the european parliament was invited to give its opinion on the extension of the ebrd's mandate. meps voted in favour of a gradual approach adapted to the specific situation of the countries around the mediterranean. eu representatives on the ebrd's governing bodies could thus advocate for the bank's actions promoting social inclusion and energy efficiency, as well as civil and human rights. since the arab spring, the eu has undertaken a series of measures to support the economic and political recovery of the eastern and southern mediterranean countries, whose situation remains fragile. so here is a new initiative that deserves to be welcomed.
in writing. this report provides for the extension of the agreement establishing the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) to the southern and eastern mediterranean region. this extension reflects the strong support of the european union for the transition of these countries to a market economy and a pluralistic society. a transition that was encouraged by the arab spring. i supported this report, which was adopted by the european parliament by a large majority.
in writing. on 30 september 2011, the board of governors of the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) voted in favour of the amendments to the agreement establishing the ebrd, which are necessary to allow the bank to extend its intervention region to the countries of the southern and eastern mediterranean. mr binev's report explains that in response to the political and economic situation in the southern and eastern mediterranean countries, the ebrd has developed a gradual approach to start its activities. this report provides the european union with greater flexibility in its cooperation with the countries bordering the mediterranean. the institutions' representatives within the ebrd will be required to encourage the ebrd to contribute to the transition towards open market economies, promoting social inclusion and energy efficiency, while taking into account the social context, poverty, civil rights and human rights. my work at european level is exactly that: to help and support the third countries of the mediterranean region, both in their democratic transition phases following the waves of revolutions of the arab spring and in their political and economic transition phases.
in writing. the extension of the mandate of the european bank for reconstruction and development to the mediterranean region, in my view, represents our taking into account the geostrategic revolution that the mediterranean area has experienced since 2011 with the arab spring. the ebrd was established in 1991 following the fall of the berlin wall and the soviet bloc. its mandate has always been to support countries in their transition to a market economy and democracy, in order to ensure stability and security at the union's borders. the aim is to take account of the reversal of the situation in the mediterranean countries in 2011 and to support them in their efforts to achieve a sustainable and secure transition, similar to that currently under way in the countries of central and eastern europe. it seems to me therefore absolutely necessary to go along with the g8 and also the 61 shareholders of the ebrd in voting this report, all of whom call for this enlargement towards a new south. this new mandate will be beneficial economically, security-wise and diplomatically for both sides of the mediterranean and will strengthen the union's role as a leading partner in the mediterranean basin.
in writing. extending the financial support instruments for the eastern mediterranean countries to the southern mediterranean countries may seem like a good thing. but in this case, doing so for the ebrd (european development bank) is a cause for concern. the logic of this financial institution is very clear: "the transition of countries to an open market economy and the promotion of private initiative and the spirit of enterprise". we know what the economic and social results of this logic have been in the eastern countries, including the states which are now members of the eu. this is the logic that is being imposed on the countries of the south, and i have been denouncing this constantly, particularly on the basis of the example of tunisia. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council and the council for adoption by the end of the year. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. the budget of the european union is an investment budget, let us say it once and for all. the union is not in deficit, the budget plays - or rather should play - a major role in putting into effect the investment strategy we are so anxious to see. i therefore supported this resolution on the union's own resources, because at a time of budgetary negotiations on the next multiannual financial framework (mff), it is extremely important that parliament should have a strong and united voice on the new system of own resources to be put in place. we would remind you that parliament will not give its consent to the mff without an agreement on own resources, but also the end of the rebate and other corrective mechanisms, for more transparency, fairness and sustainability in the budget. we are determined to make the union budget an instrument for investment and growth, and we are ready to use our co-decision power in this respect.
in writing. in the context of the negotiations on the next multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, as a member of the european parliament, i joined my colleagues in sending a strong message to the council: parliament is not ready to give its consent to the regulation of the next multiannual financial framework without a political agreement on the reform of the own resources system. the margin of manoeuvre of parliament in this area is very narrow. but to meet the challenges of economic recovery, the european union must have a solid budget, which implies in particular an evolution of the community budget on the basis of the 2013 amount, increased by 5%. we also call on the council to respect the european parliament's powers of codecision for sectoral policies.
in writing. the eu needs a strong budget to meet its political and economic objectives. i supported the resolution on the multiannual financial framework, which was adopted by 541 votes to 100, with 36 abstentions. in this resolution, the european parliament insists that the 2014-2020 budgetary framework should provide for increased budgetary flexibility to ensure that budgetary resources can be appropriately adapted to changing situations and priorities. i therefore voted against the resolutions proposed in parallel by the edr group and the efd group which did not correspond to this objective.
in writing. the european union needs a strong budget to meet its political objectives. by voting in favour of this resolution, i want to send this message to the council, which will soon be debating the draft eu budgetary framework for 2014-2020. i believe that budgetary flexibility must be increased, allowing more flexibility within and between budget headings and from one financial year to the next. this would allow budgetary resources to be appropriately adapted to changing situations and priorities. in addition, alternative sources of revenue must be provided to the eu budget - including part of the revenue from a financial transaction tax or a european vat. as the text of the resolution says, without political agreement on the system of own resources in the union budget, parliament will not give its consent to the regulation of the next multiannual financial framework. finally, what i am asking for above all is that the council fully acknowledges the role of co-decision-making of parliament in these negotiations and acts accordingly. parliament is determined to make its voice heard, let the council prepare for it!
in writing. the multiannual financial framework, also known as the 'financial perspective', sets out a medium-term programme of the union's main budgetary priorities. in this sense, it is fundamental. the commission's proposal for a resolution on the cfp states that 'the union budget must play a strategic role, alongside the fiscal consolidation measures currently imposed on national budgets' (b7-0303/2012, para. 1), legitimising the austerity measures. while the austerity policies imposed by the european union are undermining economies and social structures, the text put to the vote by the european parliament dares to claim that '94 per cent [of the european union's appropriations] are devoted to stimulating economic growth and employment and to strengthening the union's role as a global actor' (ibid). worse, while the council constantly gives the european parliament the upper hand in matters of budgetary power, the text merely calls for 'the political positions agreed by the european council to be the subject of negotiations between parliament and the council' (paragraph 5). i therefore voted against this resolution which confirms austerity policies which are destructive to the peoples of europe.
in writing. the 20th eu-japan summit in brussels on 28 may 2011 had set the stage for discussions to define the scope and level of ambition of the negotiations on the eu-japan free trade agreement. however, the eu will have to stand firm and get the regulatory barriers to trade removed, or we will again be faced with the same type of negotiations as those of the eu-korea agreement. a group was tasked with this delimitation exercise to assess the common understanding of the scope and level of potential trade negotiations between japan and the european union. until the european parliament has presented its position on the proposed negotiating mandate, we do not want the council to enter into negotiations. the stakes for european industry are too high not to be extremely vigilant about the safeguard clauses to be included in this type of agreement.
in writing. while the european union seems to be keen to conclude more and more free trade agreements with its trading partners, some countries do not have the same drive to enter into negotiations. this is the case in japan, which is not yet prepared to remove non-tariff barriers to its public procurement, pharmaceutical products or the automobile sector. the european union would therefore be premature in starting trade negotiations with japan today. the european council should therefore not be too hasty in giving the commission a mandate to start these negotiations. it is also essential that the opinion of the european parliament on the existing trade barriers in japan be taken into account before formal negotiations are launched.
in writing. on 31 may, the european union and japan concluded a framework exercise for a future free trade agreement. the european union last year demanded that japan meet certain conditions for the opening of negotiations. in this context, the european parliament, by this resolution, asks the council to give it a period of time to assess whether these conditions are being met before giving the commission a mandate to negotiate. these conditions are essentially based on the elimination of a number of non-tariff barriers and the opening up of public procurement to european companies. the european parliament supported this resolution by 517 votes, and i welcome that.
in writing. japan is identified by the commission as one of the eu's strategic partners. a high-level eu-japan dialogue has been in place since the early 1990s but has so far produced no tangible results. the sectors identified as being of common interest by the commission and the japanese authorities are sensitive to the european and french industry. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution, which asks the council not to allow the opening of negotiations on a possible bilateral trade agreement until parliament has given its opinion on the commission's mandate. it seems to me essential that parliament should have a say in the content of the negotiations.
in writing. since the coup d'état of 12 april, the opposition in guinea-bissau has been subject to violent repression. our first responsibility must be to call for calm and dialogue. but it is also the responsibility of guinea's top leaders to do everything possible to prevent a new outbreak of violence in a country that has suffered too much since its independence. since the beginning of events, the international community, europe of course but also ecowas (economic community of west african states) have spoken with one voice. they mobilized by taking sanctions against the transitional government set up by the ex-junta and in which the former ruling party does not participate and against individuals who support actions that threaten peace, security and stability in guinea-bissau. this pressure must continue and the measures provided for must be applied. we must not, however, let up our efforts until the situation has stabilized. it is the responsibility of the un, the african union and the european union to work tirelessly for the return of calm and dialogue.
in writing. the european parliament strongly condemns the coup d'état in guinea-bissau on 12 april 2012 before the second round of the presidential elections, and i welcome it. it is essential that democracy and the rule of law be restored immediately so that the country can decide its future at the ballot box. i therefore reject the continuation of the self-proclaimed government and support the decision of the economic community of west african states (ecowas) to impose sanctions, as the talks have not been sufficient to return to the rule of law.
in writing. the values we defend require us to strongly condemn the political situation in guinea-bissau, as well as the coup d'état by which the military coup d'étatists deposed and arrested the interim president and the prime minister. we demand a full restoration of fundamental freedoms, including freedom of expression and freedom of the press, as well as freedom of association and movement. we call for a consensus to be found to reconnect with the political stability of the country, which is crucial for this region of the world but also far beyond - guinea-bissau being a hub for drug trafficking to the european market. finally, like ecowas and the international community, we call for the immediate return to constitutional order and the rule of law, and for free elections to be held.
in writing. the republic of south sudan is only 10 months old, but has been at war with its northern neighbour for 8 months. more than 150,000 people have been displaced, fighting and bombing continues, and both countries are wasting resources in a conflict that only adds to the tension in the region. it is time for khartoum and juba to comply with the resolutions of the au and the un, to end hostilities and to resume negotiations. the two new countries had agreed to settle the outstanding issues: demarcation of the remaining 20% of borders and sharing of oil resources. both the north and the south have an interest in a deal. but neither of them can count on the international community to remain silent in the face of the humanitarian tragedy that is unfolding. and if dialogue between khartoum and juba does not resume soon, it will be essential for the un to apply pressure and take sanctions. china has decided to take responsibility. this is going in the right direction. but it is very important that the eu continues to assert its position and political presence, because our balanced position is the right one.
in writing. the situation in sudan and south sudan remains alarming. i have already asked the high representative and the european external action service (eeas) on several occasions about their intentions and what concrete actions could be taken to put an end to the hostilities between the two states. since south sudan's independence in july 2011, relations between the two countries have deteriorated steadily, causing a serious humanitarian crisis and straining the civilian population, which is facing a climate of permanent and unsustainable insecurity. parliament noted with concern the latest developments and called on the two states, which had committed themselves to them, to respect the roadmap approved by the un security council on 2 may 2012. the humanitarian crisis in the region, the resulting insecurity and violence are unacceptable and contribute to the growing instability of the region as a whole. i therefore call on the eu to implement through firm and concrete actions the 'comprehensive approach' adopted by the foreign affairs council on 20 june 2011.
in writing. relations between sudan and south sudan are currently marked by distortions in the final demarcation of the borders between them, resulting in violent conflict. the european parliament resolution calls on sudan and south sudan to show their political will to put an end to their differences. the eu is also seeking to reach an agreement by the end of august on economic issues such as oil use, border demarcation and humanitarian access. i supported that resolution and i welcome it.
in writing. while the election observation mission headed by ms nedelcheva welcomed the holding of a referendum in south sudan (which had allowed that region of africa to gain its independence), the current situation is quite different. it can be said that the independence process, which had initially proceeded democratically and peacefully, then took hold: after the referendum, there were strong tensions and a renewed upsurge of violence between the two states. the situation between the two countries, particularly as regards the humanitarian question and the transit of oil from south sudan, remains a matter of concern. we must denounce this situation and urge sudan and south sudan to stop fighting, to reach an economic agreement, particularly on the use of oil, and to allow humanitarian access to the populations affected by the conflict. both states must protect human rights in their respective territories. i fully support the idea that there can be no other solution to this conflict than a peaceful one, and i subscribe to the elements of this resolution, which i have supported.
in writing. the european union is the second largest trading partner of the andean countries, after the united states. europe has also accompanied their respective governments in the processes of democratic transition. on 13 june, parliament gave its green light to a trade agreement aimed at eliminating tariff and technical barriers to trade between the eu, colombia and peru. it is intended to provide access conditions 'equivalent to those available to the united states' in colombia and peru. however, parliament insisted before giving its assent that these agreements should have a positive impact on human rights, improvements in labour rights and trade union rights, otherwise they would be immediately suspended. these agreements are therefore based on a reciprocity clause: economic integration is the means of combating poverty, strengthening social cohesion and achieving sustainable development. in this sense, a group of independent experts will examine the situation of democracy in these regions in order to monitor compliance with legal commitments.
in writing. at present, the trade agreement between the european union and colombia and peru does not provide for any real dispute settlement and monitoring mechanisms for human rights provisions. i supported the resolution to set up a group of independent experts to ensure the effective implementation of human rights provisions and respect for democratic principles, as well as a legal framework for an open and democratic dialogue between the authorities and civil society.
in writing. this resolution expresses a number of the european parliament's concerns before the ratification of free trade agreements with colombia and peru. the resolution welcomed "the efforts made by the colombian government to combat impunity and the murders of trade unionists and human rights defenders". yet colombia remains the country in the world where the most trade unionists are murdered with impunity (90% of these murders go unpunished), a fate they share with human rights defenders and "indigenous" people. moreover, these free trade agreements do not promote the sustainable development policies that these countries need. it is also blind economic agreements that will further increase inequality. i therefore voted against this resolution to denounce the hypocrisy of the european union which is moving towards ratifying a free trade agreement with a country like colombia while claiming to be at the forefront of human rights and environmental protection. the eu/uk will be mobilising on this agreement, in particular during the vote in the committee on international trade on 10 july.
in writing. i am pleased that parliament has adopted the draft recommendation to the council on the creation of a post of european union special representative for human rights. under the authority and on the proposal of the high representative, this new special mandate should increase the visibility, accountability and consistency of the position of the eu institutions on this important issue. the special representative for human rights will be the eu's preferred interlocutor with the high-level international bodies responsible for this vital issue, the first of which is the un bodies (unga, unhcr).
in writing. the european parliament has long called for the creation of a special representative on human rights. this ambition cannot be compromised by any minimum. this special representative will not be the representative of the 27 but of the union as a whole. parliament therefore intends to play its part in the appointment procedure and in monitoring the whole of its mandate. the representative must also be given a strong, independent and flexible mandate, which is not defined by narrow and specific thematic responsibilities, but which allows him to intervene quickly and effectively. all human rights issues should be covered: abolition of the death penalty, human rights defenders, fight against impunity, fight against torture, freedom of expression (including on the internet), freedoms of association, assembly, religion and belief, minority rights, child protection, women's rights, peace and security, gender issues... finally, adequate financial and human resources should be made available to the special representative to ensure the effectiveness of his work and that of his team.
in writing. i abstained on this text. while the promotion of human rights in the world is naturally a laudable objective, the creation of an additional actor does not enhance the readability of european policy, nor does it contribute to the expected effectiveness. the function of the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy must be preserved.
in writing. i join my colleagues in this vote in expressing our wishes for the mandate of the future european union special representative for human rights, whom we have been calling for for several years now, namely: a strong, independent and flexible mandate; a mandate reflecting the eu's human rights policy and covering in particular the strengthening of democracy, international justice, international humanitarian law, abolition of the death penalty, freedom of expression, gender issues, child protection and armed conflict. he or she must be able to act as an intelligent and strategic advocate for human rights, democracy and the rule of law, across the world, by speaking out loudly on behalf of the european union. he or she must help us to ensure that our relations with third countries are consistent, that they actually contribute to the development of the most deprived countries, and that our countries stop turning a blind eye to the question of human rights for purely economic reasons.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague salafranca on the creation of a european union special representative for human rights. the european union needs a high-level interlocutor for its counterparts in third countries and international organisations. it ensures the visibility, effectiveness and coherence of the european union's human rights policy.
in writing. the european union is about to appoint its first-ever thematic special representative: the special representative for human rights (srhr). given the strategic importance of this post, i supported the recommendation of parliament to the council in plenary. this constructive and balanced text aims to clarify the criteria for selecting the candidate and to specify the nature and scope of his mandate. our assembly thus reminded the council that the purpose of this appointment was to strengthen the coherence and visibility of the european union's action in the protection and promotion of human rights. to do this, the hrd must have a sufficiently long mandate (2.5 years) and be renewable more than once (capitalize on the experience gained). the hrd should also be selected on the basis of objective criteria, in relation to his/her competence, experience and international reputation. finally, it is imperative that the hrd has adequate financial and human resources to fully implement its mandate.
in writing. i supported this recommendation setting out our expectations for the future eu special representative for human rights. the promotion of human rights and democracy in the world is at the heart of eu action. it's his raison d'être, his strength, his ambition. we have long been waiting for this position to be created, under the authority of the hr/vp. from now on, there's nothing to stop him from being appointed. after the creation of the eeas, this is the second major innovation in european diplomacy. i will be careful that this is not yet another honorary post, which would in reality be an empty shell. it is essential to me that it has maximum visibility, efficiency and capacity for action. it will be the face and the arm of the union in its quest to eliminate the denials of democracy, the deprivation of individual freedoms and the violation of human rights. i also expressed my wish that parliament should be involved in the appointment procedure and be informed of the representative's actions. how can we imagine that our assembly, elected by the citizens, has no right to look at the results of the one who promotes his values in the world?
in writing. the arms sector is a sensitive and crucial area for the european union, particularly in its relations with other states in the world. however, this trade needs to be more closely monitored and better regulated. the signing of the un arms trade treaty in july will be a first step towards recognizing the rights of civilians, the main victims of armed conflict. the treaty will improve lawful trade with an export control mechanism and combat the trafficking of conventional arms. it will ensure greater transparency and better governance of arms transfers. member states will have to report regularly to the european parliament on this issue and ensure that the treaty is strictly applied in their own legislation.
in writing. i welcome the fact that the issue of the negotiations on the un arms trade treaty (att) has finally been put on the agenda of our european parliament, thanks in particular to the pressure of the alde group to which i belong. we therefore wished that our parliament could express its opinion on this matter and that the european institutions as a whole should take a strong stand to find a solution to the problems of arms transfers. the signing of such a treaty by the international community will be a powerful act, in that it will establish universal and binding standards on the import, export and transfer of arms. the regulation of this trade is urgently needed, given the arms transfers that fuel conflict, poverty and violations of individual rights. we call for clear and binding provisions, which meet the highest international standards in accordance with international humanitarian law. it is urgent that we take the problem head on in order to ensure lasting security and stability in the world.
in writing. the arms trade, which is kept completely opaque, has a direct impact on respect for human rights and development conditions in the least developed countries. that is why i supported this resolution because i believe it is our responsibility as elected representatives to encourage, if not through the commission, the member states to take concrete measures to regulate this trade. a binding agreement is needed at international level and should cover the widest range of transfers and transactions of conventional arms. finally, i hope that this treaty will provide the means to monitor the transparent application of the rules it lays down.
in writing. the eu member states account for around 30% of all arms exports and are among the largest arms producers in the world. action is therefore essential to improve transparency and regulation of trade. the european parliament sent a strong signal to the un member states currently negotiating the arms trade treaty (att) by adopting the relevant resolution by 612 votes to 1. the resolution was supported by a very large majority, and i welcome that. it stresses the need for regular reporting to a un special unit in the att on all arms-related trade agreements, including transfers of small arms and light weapons. the european parliament also considered it necessary to provide for provisions obliging the states parties to adopt the required measures in their national legislation.

in writing. the presidential and legislative elections in congo in november 2011 were marked by numerous irregularities, fraud and violence. the european parliament, by a large majority, wishes to stress the need for the congolese government to intensify its efforts to ensure the rule of law and to strengthen the institutions responsible for the smooth conduct of elections. parliament also called on the commission and the member states to make the union's financial contribution conditional on the implementation of the recommendations and to support civil society, which had demonstrated its commitment to the building of democracy by its involvement in the elections. i have decided to support this resolution in plenary.
in writing. the situation of democracy and respect for human rights in the democratic republic of congo (drc) is of great concern. while the outgoing president won the last presidential elections, the eu election observation mission in the drc reported a lack of transparency and credibility due to the many cases of fraud and the many irregularities found. in addition, politically motivated human rights violations increased in the run-up to the presidential elections: the crackdown on human rights defenders and journalists has intensified, with arbitrary arrests and intimidation. in view of this, and given that the eu's financial contribution to these elections amounts to almost 50 million euros, i voted in favour of this resolution, which i co-authored. the text calls on the commission and the member states to make the union's financial contribution to the electoral process in the drc conditional on the effective implementation of the recommendations of the eu election observation mission and calls on the congolese authorities to ratify the african charter on democracy, elections and governance as soon as possible.

member of the commission. − mr president, we stand on the threshold of a first reading agreement on the revision of the so-called seveso directive on the control of major accident hazards involving dangerous substances. i would like to thank and congratulate the rapporteur, mr jános áder, who is today represented by mr seeber, as well as the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, for the excellent work carried out on this proposal; and, in absentia, congratulate mr áder on his new responsibilities at the very highest level in his home country. industrial accidents often have serious, even devastating, consequences: workers are killed; the public is exposed to chemicals resulting in immediate injury or long-term health impacts; water sources are polluted; companies may have to close. some well-known major accidents like seveso, bhopal, toulouse and buncefield have taken many lives and cost billions of euros. the seveso ii directive, which dates back to 1996, addresses this by setting rules for operators and competent authorities of member states. rules focus on accident prevention, through safety management, inspections and land-use planning. when accidents do happen, seveso seeks to limit the consequences for man and the environment, through appropriate information and emergency planning. the commission is satisfied with the compromise text on which parliament is invited to vote, which aligns the directive with the new international rules on the classification of chemicals and significantly improves the eu rules on accident prevention and control. let me explain why. firstly, the rules on inspections are far more detailed and effective than before, imposing inspection action plans covering all establishments and ensuring follow-up by operators. secondly, the rights of citizens are better guaranteed. citizens will have easier access to more information, including on inspections, and their participation in land-use planning projects will be better guaranteed by strict procedures. finally, in case those rights are not respected as they should be, citizens will now have the right to go to court, in line with the eu commitment under the aarhus convention. i am convinced that this will allow citizens to exert the necessary pressure on operators and competent authorities to implement – in the best way – the seveso legislation. the way the scope of the directive has been defined was a major issue in the negotiations, and will now reinforce the level of protection of citizens and the environment as the rules will now also apply to establishments handling substances with inhalation vapour toxicity, which were previously not covered. however, we consider that there is a need to deepen our knowledge regarding substances displaying dermal toxicity. the commission is therefore making the following declaration, announcing its intention to further analyse the consequences of accidents involving such substances: ‘the in writing. since 1982, the european union has encouraged the member states to develop a common policy for the prevention of major industrial risks. we voted for more frequent inspections and for better information to the public. this policy is a great success and we must update it.
in writing. the consequences of past chemical accidents have been disastrous for both human health and the environment, sometimes even across national borders. strengthening the prevention and control of major industrial accidents involving dangerous substances in the european union must therefore be a priority. this necessarily requires the revision of the seveso ii directive of 1996. i welcome the agreement reached with the council to adopt this regulation, which rightly calls for the introduction of clearer and more coherent provisions, the main ones being the introduction of stricter standards for the inspection of the approximately 10 000 high-risk installations in europe, the increase in the frequency and transparency of these checks, and the improvement of the general public's access to safety information and the participation of citizens in the decision-making process. i would like to welcome these measures, which were adopted overwhelmingly in plenary, and which i believe are moving in the right direction and carry a strong message. i regret, however, that they do not go further, particularly with regard to transparency and the provision of information to the public, which is essential.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of this measured and realistic report, which highlights the proper functioning of the current system for the prevention and management of hazards linked to the presence and use of dangerous substances by our industries. i particularly welcome its provisions to reduce the administrative burden on businesses: the european parliament points out that a high level of protection of the environment and the health of citizens can be achieved without unnecessary administrative burdens.
in writing. the european parliament adopted the third version of the seveso directive named after the italian village where a cloud containing dioxin was emitted in 1976 following an accident at a chemical plant. the existing rules on inspections have been strengthened. thus, high-risk sites will be inspected at least once a year, and sites with a lower risk every three years. in order to avoid the domino effects of chemical accidents, public authorities will also have the right to obtain information on nearby installations, even if these are not covered by the seveso legislation. finally, the integration of the requirements of the international aarhus convention on access to information, public participation in decision-making and access to justice in environmental matters strengthens citizens' rights. this will enable them to have direct access via the internet to information on seveso facilities close to their homes, accident prevention programmes and emergency measures to be taken. these new requirements will make it possible to better prevent and manage accidents involving hazardous chemicals.

in writing. just over a year after the adoption of the single market act, the european union needs to implement an action programme to make the internal market work better in practice and measures to complete the liberalisation of services. the idea is to rebuild the foundations of growth on the basis of a better functioning single market. the european union would have much to gain if all the opportunities of the single market were used effectively in the fields of energy, transport, retail trade, r & d, labour mobility and financial services. the correct and timely implementation of existing legislation and measures, as well as the reduction of unnecessary administrative burdens and laws, would stimulate economic growth. so it's a matter of making what we have work well.
in writing. european citizens are at the heart of the concerns of our institutions. the completion of the single market must make their daily lives easier. it is in pursuit of this objective that commissioner barnier proposed the single market act in 2010, supplemented in 2011 by 12 levers to stimulate growth and strengthen confidence in europe. on wednesday 13 june, commissioner barnier presented the commission's intentions for the future of the single market act to meps in plenary. a second single market act will be presented in september this year. in preparing this new document, the european parliament made the following comments, with which i fully agree: reduce the administrative burden and modernise our administrations, put the sectors which have a direct impact on the daily lives of citizens and consumers at the heart of our actions, give priority to the fight against youth unemployment, promote smes and their essential contribution to economic growth.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the single market act. this resolution is indispensable in that it calls on the commission to propose a 'growth initiative' which is needed to open up the single market further and unleash growth in the european union. the resolution also calls on the commission to adopt, by the end of 2012, the levers to stimulate growth and strengthen confidence in europe.
in writing. the single market, by removing barriers to the free movement of goods and capital, underpins european economic growth. it is essential that all measures to open up the single market are properly implemented and applied. similarly, administrative burdens must be reduced in order to stimulate growth: we have set member states the target of a 25% reduction in administrative burdens by 2015. finally, i support the use of the unused resources of the european union to combat youth unemployment.
our single market is a free-movement area for our businesses. but this large market is made up mainly of small and medium-sized enterprises. as a result of the consultation on company law, we have identified the main points which should form our reflection. we need to facilitate crossborder business operations, improve the regime for crossborder mergers and measures on crossborder divisions. the problem of the codification of company law is also on the table. we need to create a european model of corporate governance, in line with our values.
in writing. as european companies increasingly tend to operate on a cross-border scale, there is an urgent need to adapt our european regulatory framework for company law and corporate governance. the european parliament adopted a resolution in plenary calling on the commission to present an action plan as soon as possible. this action plan will have to set out the initiatives to be taken in the short, medium and long term to improve the regulatory framework of european company law.
in writing. this resolution, which i support, follows the commission's consultation on the future of european company law. it should be noted that the law is currently fragmented and complements the company law of the member states. this incompleteness may discourage companies from establishing themselves or operating in another eu member state, thus preventing them from taking full advantage of the internal market. we therefore encourage the commission to continue its work on the 14th directive on the crossborder transfer of registered offices, in order to facilitate the mobility of companies in europe. i would stress this point, however, so that the national criteria for linking are not called into question. as regards the regulatory framework for smes, the draft european private company must be concluded. the project, which is part of the small business act, could promote the economic development of smes and, more generally, of unlisted companies by providing them with a simple statute and a uniform organization relatively independent of national legislation. the key will be to strike a balance between the flexibility of the model chosen and its degree of harmonisation, to ensure its attractiveness while avoiding law shopping between member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text for a job-creating recovery. we must now be aware that economic activities in europe are changing and we need a conversion of our economy. we want sustainable growth, not illusory growth as advocated by the french socialists who continue to operate on economic models from another time! the job-creating recovery aims to facilitate entrepreneurial activity, to create new businesses, and to create new jobs.
in writing. a few weeks after adopting a resolution on youth employment in europe, i supported today the adoption of the resolution 'towards a job-rich recovery', which accompanies our question to the commission. given the millions of jobs lost in europe since the start of the crisis, how does the commission intend to ensure that wages in the member states enable citizens to escape poverty and create jobs? how will the commission put to use the studies carried out on the structural cause of unemployment, namely the gap between skills and labour market needs? in this resolution we reiterate our commitment to social progress and decent work and reaffirm our support for the initiative of a european youth guarantee. finally, we reiterate the absolute need for a 'european investment pact' that would shift from the unilateral approach of fiscal austerity to a more balanced approach to creating sustainable growth and jobs in key sectors such as the green economy, health and social services and information and communication technologies, which we urgently need.
in writing. i voted in favour of the commission's proposal 'towards a job-creating recovery'. the measures indicated are at the heart of the objectives of full employment and social cohesion which the european union urgently needs. they encourage member states to promote measures to create jobs and reform the european labour market. encouraging the recruitment of young people, supporting the development of smes, promoting labour mobility and addressing the skills mismatch are concrete policies that need to be implemented rapidly. to stimulate job-creating growth, we must also strengthen the coordination of collective bargaining and the maintenance of the purchasing power of employees. i particularly support the idea that the fight against poverty should be focused on ensuring a living wage and equal access to universal and quality public and social services.
in writing. at a time when the european council should be discussing a growth initiative, alongside other heavy dossiers, we must keep in mind the first expectation of europeans: to keep or to get back to work. the social situation is becoming more difficult by the day: we are living under the threat of a lost generation, 5.6 million young people are unemployed, one in five young europeans. we socialists welcome the new attitude of the commission on several hitherto taboo subjects, such as the minimum wage. this is a major issue if we are to solve the problems of poverty and internal imbalances within the european union.
in writing. with this resolution, i wanted to show my commitment to a growth initiative at a time when the economic and social situation continues to deteriorate and is hitting many young people very hard. this initiative is crucial on the eve of a european summit which, instead of dealing with yet another round of austerity measures, should finally address the question of growth. i welcome the commission's commitment to the introduction of decent minimum wages to reduce the phenomenon of the working poor and social dumping, and the plan to create a european youth guarantee to guarantee young people access to employment or training after a period of inactivity of up to four months. in this debate, however, i regret that the conservatives are still opposed to the coordination of collective bargaining at european level, to the raising of the purchasing power of employees in those countries which can do so, and to equal access to public and social services.
