in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution of the resolution on the elimination of female genital mutilation, which is a form of abuse for non-medical reasons, on children if the girls are minors. it is therefore necessary to integrate it into the fight against female genital mutilation in a comprehensive and coherent approach to combating violence against women. we therefore hope that the un general assembly will adopt a resolution at its 67th session to eliminate genital mutilation in the world. furthermore, since female genital mutilation is often performed on young girls, it is a violation of the rights of the child.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because i always support the texts which promote steps towards greater equality between women and men. the fight against violence against women is unfortunately an integral part of this, and female genital mutilation is one of the daily horrors suffered by thousands of women, mainly in africa but not only. although in theory, genital mutilation is now legally prohibited in most countries of the world, political will and concrete actions to combat this practice remain mostly superficial. these phenomena of violence against women, as well as those affecting children and in particular girls, can only be reduced by comprehensive policies and in particular by cooperative policies aimed primarily at combating poverty and all inequalities in access to education, health and social rights. despite its shortcomings, i can only share the findings of this report and that is why i voted for this resolution.
in writing. following the pip breast implants scandal, we voted in favour of establishing a register, stricter controls and traceability of these implants, and prior marketing authorisation. i spoke in plenary on this subject. this case has had and unfortunately will have an impact on the european and international level. the number of women affected in the uk is about 40 000, in france 30 000, and in spain 10 000... as legislators, we need to learn from this fraud and strengthen the system of surveillance and hardware surveillance for medical devices. we must strengthen and harmonise inspection obligations at community level. there is an urgent need for regular, unannounced and annual monitoring at all stages of the life cycle of a medical device. the conditions for the authorisation of notified bodies should be harmonised and the traceability, transparency and monitoring of medical devices placed on the european market should be strengthened. a balance must be struck between protecting our european patients and supporting innovation and research. we must combine security, transparency, consistency and flexibility.
in writing. the pip breast implant scandal that broke in december 2011 exposed the lack of cooperation between member states and the dysfunction of the medical device traceability system. more than 400 000 breast implants from the french company pip have been marketed worldwide despite non-compliance with quality criteria. the european union must react and learn from this case. the legislation on medical devices needs to be revised. measures to prevent a new health scandal from occurring must be taken as soon as possible. i therefore welcome the adoption of this resolution, which explicitly calls for increased controls and monitoring of the medical device market and for greater information sharing between the competent national authorities to ensure a better level of protection of patient safety. we also call for the introduction of a number of practical measures, such as prior authorization for the marketing of the most risky medical devices, a register of breast implants and an implant recipient passport, which the commission should now put into practice.
in writing. the pip breast implant scandal which broke in march 2010 has highlighted the glaring dysfunctions of european health security. these many tragedies force us to make a thorough review of the functioning of the european and national bodies responsible for health matters. the european parliament's reaction is scandalous: the resolution, which i voted for, calls for greater cooperation between the member states and for greater control of medical devices placed on the market. i think it is an ambitious resolution, since it also invites the commission to consider a system of pre-market authorisation for certain categories of medical devices.
in writing. the pip breast prosthesis scandal has exposed all the flaws in the breast implant legislation. indeed, for years one company was able to sell implants with defective gel to thousands of women around the world without worry. in matters of public health, there can be no half measures. that is the message i wanted to convey by voting for this resolution which proposes a strict framework to ensure that such a failure does not happen again. we are obviously calling for more safety checks, but also and above all for greater traceability and a more stringent system of marketing authorization.
in writing. the resolution on defective silicone gel breast implants manufactured by the french company pip, for which i was the epp rapporteur, was adopted by a large majority at the june plenary session. i'm glad you did. the main objectives of this resolution were to strengthen and harmonise the criteria for the authorisation and the roles (including control) of notified bodies, the supervision of notified bodies by the competent national authorities, and to raise public awareness of the health issues surrounding the use of medical devices. the resolution also calls for greater market surveillance and material surveillance. this resolution was generally supported by all political groups. unfortunately, the paragraphs referring to the establishment of a marketing authorisation for class iib and iii medical devices were adopted (paragraphs 7 and 16). my colleagues in the other political groups did not realise that such a system would be totally inadequate to the nature and commercial life of a medical device. a medical device is not comparable to a drug.
in writing. the pip breast implant scandal is a disgrace. nearly 90,000 women in the european union are reported to have been victims. parliament had to react and that is why i voted for this resolution on pip breast implants, which specifically calls for the quality of controls by certification bodies to be improved and for the traceability of breast implants to be improved in order to guarantee women safe and supervised operations. we in parliament have a duty to protect the interests of the european citizens, and their health must therefore be our undeniable priority. the health of our fellow citizens should no longer be endangered by a medical malpractice, or at the mercy of the greed of a man now charged with aggravated fraud and manslaughter .
in writing. breast surgery is now one of the most common cosmetic surgeries in europe. the manufacture of industrial silicone implants by the french company pip, a strictly prohibited material for medical products, has raised many concerns, especially because several patients who received these implants will have to undergo a new operation. fortunately, these deviations are rare thanks to high health standards, both at national and european level. but the main reason for this is the fierce competition between some medical companies, which are trying to use the cheapest possible raw materials to the detriment of patients and public health. the text adopted calls for these standards to be strengthened, in particular for better cooperation between member states on the control of medical devices and for the commission to set up a system of prior authorization for certain categories of such devices. i am anxious to support all efforts to improve health protection and have therefore voted in favour of this resolution.

member of the commission. − mr president, i welcome the positive views from the committee on international trade, the committee on legal affairs and the committee on the internal market and consumer protection on our proposal. jürgen creutzmann deserves special thanks for his hard work on this report. protecting intellectual property rights is a must in our knowledge-based economy. we tabled a comprehensive ipr strategy a year ago and put emphasis on enforcement. in view of your debates and reflections on the proposal, i would like to convey three messages. firstly, let me stress that there are no rights without enforcement. legislators who have granted intellectual property rights and customs are well placed to enforce them. the commission therefore sees no reason to exclude a priori any type of ipr infringement from the scope of the regulation. secondly, the reverse should also hold true, namely: no enforcement without rights. how ipr projection relates to the freedom of transit and justified derogations should be addressed in the substantive laws where ipr are established and not when discussing the competence of enforcement authorities. a reverse burden of proof on the final destination of the goods in transit does not feature in current substantive law, so if, following your proposal, customs were to detain goods, they would eventually have to let them go, as there would be no evidence of infringement in the eu. i am well aware of the constraints expressed on medicines in transit. plainly speaking, there was a problem, and we have dealt with it by involving stakeholders, engaging constructively with international partners and proposing revised legislation. i would therefore caution against any last minute amendments which disregard the efforts made and might have unexpected consequences. as regards the destruction of goods in cases of alleged complex infringements such as patents, the commission maintains that goods should never be destroyed without legal proceedings unless there is the express agreement of the parties concerned. this leads me to my third message, namely that we need to follow a practical and reasonable approach. to deal effectively with massive flows of small consignments we need a definition and procedure that works in practice. the definition is not straightforward and would need to evolve with new trends. the threshold should therefore be better defined in a delegated act. a reasonable approach means that customs should detain goods only where there is adequate evidence. ‘reasonable’ also means that operators deserve to be heard in advance when customs decide to detain goods. in conclusion, by equipping customs with tools to ensure the strong, reasonable and practicable enforcement of well-established intellectual property rights, i hope the eu will continue to set the gold standard at international level.

opens up a new field of development and synergies for the european union's policies within the same living area, whether it be a sea area, a mountain range or a river basin. the other problem is the crisis which the mediterranean area is currently going through on its european side, with the debt crisis, and on the other side, since the arab spring and the events which have affected all these countries in the european union's neighbourhood. the macro-regional strategy improves the effectiveness of the union's regional development policies. it gives you the big picture. it strengthens strategies between regions and states and also between the various development tools of the union, such as the european investment bank and the neighbourhood and pre-accession policies. this report therefore proposes to go further in the development of macro-regional strategies. it suggested that the commission coordinate a process of consultation and reflection on future projects. it stressed in particular the importance of such an approach in the mediterranean area. in this area, which is vital for the future of europe, such an approach must be taken as soon as possible, in a pragmatic and concerted manner. the first step is to approve the adriatic-ionian strategy, which covers the central mediterranean area and the adriatic sea. this is a very advanced, widely coordinated project, which will be a first step. it will lead to similar approaches in the western and eastern mediterranean and, through good coordination, to a comprehensive strategy for the whole mediterranean area. the difficulties facing the european mediterranean are great. regional development policy, in particular its territorial cooperation component, is a fundamental tool for finding sustainable solutions. the macro-regional strategy builds on existing budgets without requiring new financial means. what is needed is not just new funds but new projects. the macro-regional strategy is likely to bring about such projects, with real involvement of local actors, whether institutional - states and regions - or otherwise, through multi-level governance. in its conclusion, the report calls on the commission to contribute its experience and support to this project, and on the future cypriot presidency to encourage its emergence in the coming months. during the preparation of this report, i met with many of the officials concerned. the desire for cooperation around such a project of macro-regional strategy is very important throughout the mediterranean area. this is an eco-opportunity which must be seized to send a positive and promising signal to a mediterranean area which, as a whole, is affected by the crisis. in conclusion, i would like to thank my colleagues on the committee on regional development, and in particular the fictitious rapporteurs, who have shown - and their very many amendments show - a great interest in this report. i also thank the committee on culture and its rapporteur, mrs benarab-attou, and the committee on foreign affairs and its rapporteur, mr salavrakos, for the work they have produced, which has considerably enriched the report i have presented to you.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on culture and education, i should like to add a few words to what mr françois alfonsi has said, to whom i pay tribute. macro-regional strategies offer particularly interesting prospects for decentralised cooperation projects in the mediterranean region. i think this framework is appropriate to the problems of this region, where the events of the past year should encourage us to develop active neighbourhood policies, especially for young people. i would like to emphasize three points in particular. firstly, cooperation in the field of youth, by promoting the european programmes devoted to youth and by creating synergies with the work of the mediterranean youth office, which must be better known. secondly, networking of euro-mediterranean universities and removing obstacles to the movement of students, teachers and researchers by facilitating visa procedures, especially for these groups. it's essential and urgent. thirdly, the quality of teaching and research in these networks by adequately supporting and financing the tempus and erasmus mundus programmes, and - i stress this - by automatically granting visas to these audiences when they integrate these european programmes. i thank mr alfonsi for his fruitful cooperation and all my colleagues who have contributed to this report.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, president of the commission, distinguished leaders of the political groups, members of the european parliament and members of the commission, it is a privilege and a great honour to address this parliament again. when i last stood here, back in january, i ended my speech by saying that the economic crisis had put the european union to the test. that was when we took over the presidency at a time of unprecedented crisis in the history of the union. the gravity of the situation, the depth of the challenge, the severity of the predicament facing our union could not and should not be underestimated, and i said this right at the beginning of our presidency – not to lower the expectations for the danish presidency but rather to make clear exactly what is at stake as the eu tries to work its way out of this crisis. during the past month the eu has been forced to take critical decisions which will lay the foundation for the europe of tomorrow, of next year and of decades to come. this is no easy task in a union as vast, diverse and complex as ours, but leaders throughout europe must never lose sight of the core of the problem facing the eu today: that our very economic foundation, our future prosperity, the hopes and dreams and aspirations of our children are at risk. the storm has not passed yet and we are still facing a number of different and intertwined challenges. so i am reminded at this time of the inspirational words of the first chancellor of west germany, konrad adenauer, who once said: ‘the unity of europe was the dream of a few. it became the hope of many. today it has become a necessity for all of us.’ those words have perhaps never been as true as they are today. the eu is a necessity to all of us. as representatives of the european institutions we have and we feel an obligation to find the solutions which will bring our union forward, and we know that we owe that to our citizens. when i stood here in january i proudly stated that i am a european at heart, and the past six months have only reassured me in my belief in the european project. i believe in our institutions, our cooperation and our common responsibility. if we seek to ensure solidarity, growth and prosperity we must seek it together through common solutions to common problems. and that is what our presidency has been all about: ensuring solidarity, growth and prosperity together. we took upon ourselves the task of proving that the eu still works and is still capable of delivering necessary results for our citizens, and we did this inspired by someone that we all know. in 1950 he said: ‘europe will not be made all at once, or according to a single plan. it will be built through concrete achievements which first create a de facto solidarity.’ of course, it was robert schuman who said this, and the subsequent history of european integration has proved him absolutely right. there is an unequivocal truth in schuman’s words. our union is built from its very foundation with bricks made of solidarity. some stones have been small, some have been enormous but, brick by brick, we have strengthened our cooperation and solidarity with one another. this is to me the essence of our union: and this is what we have tried to do – to work inch by inch in creating results. jobs and growth, financial responsibility, a greener economy and a safe europe: these have been the priorities of the danish presidency. but priorities without tangible results are just empty words, and i believe that europe has, in fact, delivered over the past months. the compact for growth and jobs adopted last week in the european council is the perfect completion of our presidency. the compact does not solve all europe’s problems but it is a light in the dark for the many european citizens feeling the harsh effects of the economic crisis. for those outside the labour market, for those without opportunities, for those facing poor prospects, including not least our young generations, we are presenting a way forward. it is a result of our persistent efforts to promote growth and new jobs in europe but, of course, our work does not end here. we must be vigilant in transforming this compact from a piece of paper into practical reality. we must find a way to ensure that together – member states, the commission and the european parliament – we roll out the measures contained in the compact. we have a situation in which, for the first time in the history of the european union, we cannot assume that the coming generations will enjoy more prosperity and better opportunities than we have enjoyed. that, of course, leaves us with a huge responsibility for the conditions of our citizens and businesses, which has been a top priority for our presidency. let me highlight a few of the main results reached during our presidency. under the headline of ‘a more dynamic europe’, the danish presidency has pushed for robust eu measures in areas such as research and education, infrastructure and the single market, and we have done this to boost growth and to kick-start a job-rich recovery. i am particularly pleased that we have succeeded in achieving a historic compromise in the european council on the patent reform, after more than 30 years of negotiations. this could mean drastic cost savings for businesses across europe: savings that can be used to promote new jobs. we may not see eye to eye on all elements of this compromise but i truly hope that we can work as co-legislators to see the patent reform become a reality to benefit our companies. i am also very pleased that we have adopted the roaming regulation. this regulation will lower prices significantly for cellphone users in member states and will reduce costs to and the burden on companies. in short, it can contribute to growth. another important result is the regulation on the european system of standardisation. the agreement reached here will modernise the single market. furthermore, we have reached agreement on the proposal on venture capital and social entrepreneurship funds. this will boost access to funding for european businesses and social entrepreneurs. of course, this is also an important step in trying to create growth in the eu. we know that the single market has been one of the greatest achievements of the eu, and in order to realise its full potential we must continue to reform and modernise it. the second main objective of our presidency was to ensure a more responsible europe. the need for fiscal consolidation and greater budget discipline is crucial if we want to safeguard against the financial crisis of tomorrow. we have also taken important steps in this field during the danish presidency. the council agreement on the two-pack will enable stronger european monitoring of budgetary plans being drafted by members of the eurozone. stronger common rules will reinforce the vigilance of member states in avoiding large imbalances and unsustainable debt levels. we have come far, and i urge a rapid agreement between the council and parliament during the cypriot presidency. a similar important step is the directive on capital requirements, on which the council agreed its position last month. this directive will help minimise the cost and the risk of a financial crisis hitting us again as it did in 2008. furthermore, we have worked for a stronger commitment by member states to implement structural reforms. the completion of the first full round of the european semester is a decisive step towards a more responsible europe. all these results will help to increase confidence in europe’s financial system, and i am in no doubt that these surveillance measures will lead to greater political accountability and stronger budget discipline. finally, we have been working hard to streamline the next eu budget so that it helps to create growth in the union, and we took an important step last week in the european council. here too, i would very much like to thank parliament for its constructive cooperation throughout. it is our firm conviction that we need to direct more funds towards growth-enhancing areas such as research, education, energy efficiency and green technology. that has to be the way forward for the eu. ‘measures that will inspire growth and stronger job creation’ has been the mantra for the danish presidency throughout these six months, and i am pleased to note that the european council placed strong emphasis on this last week. as you also know, the transition to a green economy has been among the most important political priorities for the danish presidency, and i warmly welcome the common agreement reached on the energy efficiency directive. this was a landmark result which required a good deal of flexibility, patience and hard work on both sides, and i would like to thank everyone here who was involved in reaching this significant milestone. without you we could not have done it. this directive is of key importance in our efforts to achieve our two interrelated goals, of transforming europe into a competitive, low-carbon economy and increasing our energy security, all at once. in addition, the directive will create up to hundreds of thousands of new jobs in europe, and it will of course ensure that the eu gets much closer to our target of 20% energy savings by 2020. i consider this an excellent result. i would like to underline my appreciation of the dedication, high level of ambition, and willingness to compromise demonstrated by the european parliament on this road to the green transition. your continued engagement in making our economy greener will be ever more needed in the years to come. underpinning our aspiration for a dynamic, responsible and greener europe is the need to ensure a safe europe. denmark’s presidency has reached a wide range of tangible results in this field. we have granted candidate status to serbia and are opening accession negotiations with montenegro, which will influence the regional dynamics and contribute to stabilising the western balkans. we have also reached agreement on essential elements of the asylum package, which will help ensure efficiency, legal rights and more uniform asylum procedures in the member states. together with parliament and the commission, we have managed to conclude a lot of important business. and today i am pleased to say that we were able to reach important agreements only thanks to constructive cooperation with you – the parliament, with the commission and, of course, with the member states in the council. as i see it, the achievements of the danish presidency are also the achievements of the european parliament. we all play our part in realising the huge potential of the community method. having different responsibilities, playing different roles, and on some occasions defending diverging interests, the council and parliament will not always share the same view. the heated debate on the legal basis of the schengen evaluation mechanism was, indeed, a case in point, but i drew great encouragement from the fact that our negotiations over the past six months have been characterised by flexibility, a willingness to find common ground and, most importantly perhaps, a strong commitment to deliver on the needs and demands of the citizens. the relentless focus on results, stone by stone, brick by brick, represents the spirit of our cooperation within the eu. at the end of the day, as we strive to put europe on a path for future growth and prosperity, we have to be guided by our vision for the society that we want to create. for me, this is what sets the union apart and what makes our social model so unique. that is what i believe in. that is what has made our economies so successful over the years and that is what we must fight to obtain and sustain and develop in the future. moving europe beyond this crisis is not about abandoning our social model. it is, in fact, the opposite. it is about bringing our countries through the crisis with our fundamental values intact – values such as solidarity, safety nets and equal opportunities for all. the difficult decisions we are taking today and tomorrow should not be a departure from solidarity. on the contrary, we are doing these things to protect our way of life, our european social model and our values, and we will continue to do so. the only way forward is through stronger cooperation among all of us. the answer to our current challenges facing the union is more europe, not less, and that has been the guiding principle for the danish presidency throughout. (applause)
president of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank prime minister helle thorning-schmidt and her whole team, particularly europe minister wammen, for a very engaged and dynamic presidency. the presidency programme was called ‘europe at work’ and i think it is fair to say that you were a presidency at work. you made a real effort to contribute to ensuring stability for europe in these difficult times. i particularly congratulate you, prime minister, for your personal commitment to competitiveness and growth and to the green agenda, areas in which your country, denmark, is a great inspiration for many of us in europe, and indeed in the world. the results of this work are to a large extent reflected in the conclusions of the european council and cover the full range of the union’s activities. since we will be discussing the results of the european council and the euro area summit in the following debate, in this speech i will only highlight a number of specific issues. let me start with the economy. we have almost completed the second european semester. very serious and in-depth work has taken place on the commission’s proposals for country-specific recommendations and i am satisfied with the consensus that has emerged around them. this work cannot, of course, be separated from our agenda for economic growth. as the commission has made very clear, growth can be achieved only through the combination of structural reforms and targeted investment. the growth compact, which has now been approved, recognises this and, indeed, paves the way for determined pro-growth action. i therefore appreciate in particular the speedy and constructive manner in which the proposal on the pilot project bonds for transport, energy and telecommunications infrastructure has been handled. i am very happy that we have reached a final agreement on the commission proposal. the initiative will stimulate investment in infrastructure at european level. i also appreciate the efforts to reach an agreement on the so-called two-pack, which is a central element in the eu-level drive to strengthen economic and budgetary surveillance. this would also represent a first step towards implementing important elements of the fiscal treaty. thus i welcome the general approach in council and i strongly hope that parliament and the incoming cypriot presidency can come to a final agreement before the end of this year. equally important is our progress in the area of financial markets and financial services. agreement could be reached on our proposals on derivative markets and on the single european payment area. very importantly, we are making enormous progress on the bank capital requirements package, as well as on credit-rating agencies. while the commission proposal for a financial transaction tax has unfortunately not met with unanimous support from member states, i would like to welcome the decision to start negotiations, under enhanced cooperation, for all member states that wish to join the initiative. this is a very important development. after all, we have seen once again in recent months and weeks – both in the united states and in europe, including in some of the major banking institutions – that practices which fuelled the financial crisis have not yet been eradicated from the sector. once again we have been confronted with reckless trading and market manipulation. it is time for these practices to stop once and for all, and for a sector that owes so much to taxpayers’ support to agree to hand back a fair share to society. regarding the very difficult negotiations on the proposed directive on energy efficiency, the agreement found by the co-legislators at first reading will be a major step in delivering the objective of 20% primary energy savings in 2020. the commission estimates that the outcome reached would allow the delivery of approximately two thirds of the total energy savings in the commission’s original proposal. so, while we welcome what has been achieved, we must also say that further work on reaching our 2020 objectives will be needed. i was very pleased by the agreement reached on the roaming iii regulation. this is an example of legislation that truly benefits european citizens and consumers. the regulation entered into force on 1 july 2012. by putting a cap on data roaming, we are taking an important step towards protecting consumers against shock bills, and completing the digital single market. europe should be a global standard-setter. therefore i also welcome the agreement reached on reform of the standardisation system, which will enable more efficient standard-setting in europe. furthermore, the general approaches agreed in the council on the accounting directives, on venture capital funds and social entrepreneurship funds, and on alternative dispute resolution will hopefully prove to be a good basis for reaching agreement with parliament very soon. on the matter of professional qualifications, we could have wished for more progress, but work will continue. it is, of course, necessary to make special mention of the debate on the european patent, something which has been under discussion for decades. there was a compromise on this between the participating member states, but unfortunately it comes at the price of the deletion of important community elements of the original commission proposal. while recognising the great efforts made by the danish presidency on this difficult issue, and indeed thanking you sincerely for those efforts, prime minister, the commission has therefore reserved its position, and i made this very clear to the heads of state and government during the european council. the situation will now require an assessment by the three eu institutions. we are ready to work with you on this. a central theme of the past semester was the effort made in bringing forward the multiannual financial framework (mff). last week the european council considered that the negotiating box prepared by the danish presidency provided a basis and orientations for the final stage of negotiation during the cypriot presidency, with a view to reaching an agreement by the end of 2012. in this respect, let me reiterate that the commission is fully aware of and will call for full observance of the institutional prerogatives of all the eu institutions. it was the commission, by the way, which strongly insisted on this point during the preparation for this european council and, indeed, when its conclusions were adopted. the debate on the mff will now enter its decisive stage. the commission considers that the negotiating box is still missing some important elements or, in our view, is not the appropriate answer in some areas. while fully recognising the very serious work done so far, the commission will therefore continue to defend its proposals under the incoming presidency. i believe it is now clearer that the european union budget is an essential instrument for achieving sustainable growth and jobs through investment. i am particularly happy that we managed to agree on a new financial regulation. i want to extend my thanks to the relevant players in parliament and the council who have worked closely with the commission. i know we went through a process of long and difficult negotiations. the final adoption of the financial regulation before the end of the year will allow for proper implementation of all the sectoral programmes of the mff. thus i strongly hope that the council and parliament, with the support of the commission, will manage to reach agreement on the mff by the end of this year. the european union needs to send a signal that, until the end of this decade, it will have a strong budget for growth and cohesion. the european union needs to show that it is able to take difficult decisions in difficult times. in the area of justice and home affairs, there has been good progress on important issues. let me mention the asylum package, notably the dublin ii regulation and the reception conditions directive. negotiations have also advanced on the asylum procedures directive, and reform of the visa regulation is on track. however, the same cannot yet be said of another important issue, namely the legal basis and nature of the schengen evaluation mechanism. we are all aware of the sensitivity of this issue. as far as the commission is concerned, we want solutions that can work. that is why we believe, together with this parliament, that we need a schengen evaluation mechanism with a strong european dimension. we are convinced that an intergovernmental peer review model does not deliver on the mandate set by the european council of march 2011, and that it would have limited added value in practice. since the lisbon treaty in particular, free movement of people has been a genuine community concern. as i have said before, the commission cannot accept the current outcome as final, and it will continue to work for a better solution. let me end with a look at the external dimension. the focus on internal european issues has always had to be combined with a broader perspective on europe’s role in the world, and never more so than in relation to the preparations for, and decisions in, the rio+20 summit for sustainable development. although a number of our most ambitious objectives were not fully achieved, the european union remained committed and constructive throughout the negotiations, and our positions had a very important impact on the debate. i would like particularly to welcome the very good cooperation between the commission and the danish council presidency. in fact, both prime minister thorning-schmidt and i were present at this rio conference. and let me tell you that without european leadership in this conference we would not have achieved what appears to me to be a significant outcome. green growth is now explicitly and formally accepted by the international community as an indispensable part of our sustainable development agenda. important progress has been achieved during the past six months of the danish council presidency. i wish to reiterate my thanks for what has been very good cooperation. however, we are only too aware of how serious the situation is and how much we still need to accomplish in the time ahead. i therefore count on the ongoing commitment and ambition of all the eu institutions in meeting our common challenges.

mr president, this summit marks the first steps of europe towards a banking union and the possible recapitalisation of the banks in difficulty in troubled countries such as spain and italy certainly marks a step forward. direct aid from the european stability mechanism to banks can only be granted after the establishment of a european banking supervision. that's another step forward. but let us not be naive, mr van rompuy. there are still some crucial issues to be resolved. we will still need many european summits to try to provide the answers of economic and monetary integration of the euro area, simply political integration. because we cannot guarantee a growth model based on public spending without a clean-up and consolidation of public finances. because there can be no financial solidarity without budgetary, fiscal and social harmonization. because the premise is simple: you don't pay off a debt by creating another one. we know that by pooling the debts of countries which do not have the same economic and budgetary policies, we will put certain member states at risk by obliging them to guarantee debts they cannot control. i hope that france will ratify very quickly the treaty on stability, coordination and governance, which was signed last january and which, of course, could not be renegotiated. but mr. monti was a very good manoeuvre. however, the bonds of trust between the member states must be restored, because it is not desirable to see provocations between them and it is not desirable to oppose germany head-on. it's not worth it! the franco-german psychodrama is of no interest to anyone and that is not how the future of europe will be handled in these difficult times.

in writing. the european parliament welcomed the request for consultation of the european economic and social committee on the creation of a european social label. this label will inform the consumer that the product or service he is purchasing is part of an investment to improve his social model. i supported this request, which was accepted by all my colleagues, and i welcome that.
in writing. as with banks, we regulate the world of insurance and reinsurance. the solvency ii directive, which is being considered by the committee on economic and monetary affairs, of which i am a member, aims to make the capital requirements for insurance and reinsurance companies more commensurate with the risks they face in their business. it is necessary to ensure that the company is well managed, that it is able to calculate and control its risks and to ensure that it is well capitalised. i have endorsed the postponement of this report until january 2014, which was proposed by my colleague, the chair of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, sharon bowles, and which gives member states more time to transpose it into our national law.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on insurance and reinsurance (solvency ii). the insurance sector is currently affected by legal uncertainty due to the discrepancy between the legal system of the european union (solvency ii) and that of the member states (solvency i). this report is part of a drive to regulate and supervise european insurance companies. the establishment of the european insurance and occupational pensions authority would thus help to strengthen the sector.
in writing. the european parliament and the council have already adopted directive 2009/138/ec (solvency ii), which establishes a modern, risk-based system for the regulation and supervision of european insurance and reinsurance undertakings. the purpose of this report is to postpone the date of transposition and entry into force of the directive to 31 december 2012. this postponement is fully justified in view of the need to ensure the legal continuity of the provisions of the solvency i directive until the implementation of the entire solvency ii package. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. saint-barthélemy, a french island in the lesser antilles, was a dependency of the overseas department (dom) of guadeloupe until 1 january 2012, when the island officially became an overseas collectivity (com). the french republic had anticipated this change in status and asked the european council to adopt a decision on the island of saint-barthélemy, with a view to changing its status from that of an outermost region to that of a country and territory associated with the european union (oct). after the change of status at national level, it was consistent to revise the european status of this french oj. membership of the countries and territories associated with the european union now places the island in a new and lasting reciprocal partnership with the european union, which takes account of its particularities, without, however, calling into question its membership of the european family. oct nationals are european citizens, but they are not part of the european union and are not subject to european law. the island retains the euro as its currency and its citizens will remain european citizens. its links with the european union will therefore remain intact.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr ponga on the association of the overseas countries and territories with the european community. this report follows on from a letter from the french republic to the european council requesting that the island of saint-barthélemy be upgraded from an outermost region to an overseas country and territory associated with the european union. this new association framework would enable saint barthélemy to enter into a more reciprocal and sustainable partnership which would take better account of its particularities.
in writing. i support the change of status of the island of saint barthélemy. by becoming an overseas country and territory (oct) associated with the european union, the island of saint barthélemy will have a framework more suited to its specificities. this new partnership with the european union allows for greater flexibility in the implementation of community standards. i am pleased with the adoption of this report, which confirms the decision taken by the council in october 2010.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which recognises the change in status of the french island of saint barthélemy, which became the 26th overseas country and territory of the european union in 2010. this new status will enable our overseas territory to renew its relations with the other territories of the union and to strengthen its relations with its immediate neighbours in the caribbean, while remaining committed to the euro and european values.
in writing. on tuesday 3 july, the european parliament recognised the change in status of saint barthélemy, making it the 26th overseas country and territory (oct). this is a decision which i welcome and which was set out in the conclusions of the european council of 27 october 2010. the new partnership will be based on the principle of subsidiarity, which is the basis for the creation of a european union and a european union. this change in status will be more in line with the needs and specificities of the island. moreover, this change in the statute will not in any way alter two essential aspects of the island's proper functioning: saint barthélemy will retain the euro and its inhabitants will remain european citizens.

in writing. some regions are countries that share the same natural environment and the same historical and cultural reality. europe has therefore developed macro-regional strategies which open up new perspectives for territorial cooperation projects. these strategies are supported by cohesion policy, one of the european union's most valuable tools! i have therefore endorsed the strategies in this report which can contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the european union and ensure better coordination between regional programmes and the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. the examples of the baltic sea and the danube clearly show that macro-regional strategies, new forms of territorial cooperation, have helped to improve the effectiveness of the union's regional development policies and to strengthen synergies between regions and states. the eu must urgently open up such prospects for the mediterranean, a vital area for the future of europe. the implementation of a macro-regional strategy for the mediterranean basin would provide a common perspective to address the challenges facing the mediterranean countries and to structure this area, which is essential for the development and integration of europe. after the failure of the union for the mediterranean, it is time to send a message of hope to the mediterranean region as a whole, which is currently in crisis but also shaken by the successive revolutions on the southern side of the mediterranean. the european parliament has overwhelmingly expressed its support for this initiative in the mediterranean and intends to make it a political priority. it is now up to the commission to give its support and cyprus to use its presidency to move forward and lay the foundations for this strategy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on 'the evolution of eu macro-regional strategies: current practices and future prospects, particularly in the mediterranean'. i believe that the european macro-regional strategies offer good prospects for cooperation projects with the territories surrounding the baltic sea. the report underlines the union's interest in pursuing the strategy of cohesion policy, particularly in the field of inter-sectoral cooperation. i also think it is important to define more precisely projects which meet the local needs of the baltic peoples.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which stresses the need to develop macro-regional strategies at eu level. as rapporteur on the atlantic strategy for the european parliament, i share the rapporteur's view of the need for a multi-sectoral approach. i think it is important to support and develop territorial cooperation projects. the latter are relevant because they allow more effective responses to local problems. i also support the initiative to develop a macro-regional strategy for the mediterranean. this is welcome after the "arab spring" and the democratic transition of some countries on the southern shore of the mediterranean.
in writing. i supported this text which encourages the development of so-called 'macroregional' strategies to coordinate the efforts of several territories to solve common challenges. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. we hope that the principle of accountability, which is expressed here in terms of the three 'no's' (no to new expenditure, a new 'institutional machinery' and new regulations) and the three 'yeses' (yes to the complementarity of funding, the coordination of institutional systems and the opening up of new projects), will henceforth apply to all the policies of the european union.
the new european whim from brussels: the european macro-region. finally, it is certainly macro, but it is 'european'. the macro-region is intended to bring together regions (not states) around a common project (a sea, a river, etc.), even if these regions are not part of a member state of the union. the aim is, of course, to encourage the short-circuiting of nation states and to promote the blurring of external borders. the creation of such entities cannot be left to spontaneous initiatives, so the commission is asked to identify all possible macro-regions. and of course, encourage their creation. the alfonsi report therefore proposes two macro-regions in the mediterranean, thus grouping together areas north and south of the sea. it is a prelude to the inclusion of these countries, most of which are now threatened by muslim fundamentalism, in the european single market and the free movement of people between the two shores. and then what? a 'macro-region' of the atlantic to promote the implementation of the large transatlantic market? we have to stop this drift !
in writing. on tuesday 3 july, parliament approved by a large majority the report on the european union's macro-regional strategies. this unique form of cooperation has already proved its worth in the baltic sea, which is now the reference framework for other initiatives such as the danube strategy launched a year ago or the draft mediterranean strategy. this strategy moves beyond traditional cooperation at national or regional level by bringing together all institutional actors and partners such as universities, research centres and regional organisations from a wider area facing common territorial challenges in environmental, economic, migration and cultural matters. the development of a strategy in the mediterranean is fully justified by the existence of common characteristics and problems and european policies could be implemented more effectively at this scale. the report makes useful recommendations for future strategies, drawing on the lessons of the baltic sea experience. we have an interesting mechanism to exploit here and that is why i have decided to support this report.
in writing. the european parliament has adopted the report by my colleague françois alfonsi by a large majority, and i welcome this. the report aims to take stock of current practices in the framework of the european union's macro-regional strategies in order to define their prospects. in this context, it is necessary to provide a relevant reference framework for cohesion policy and to encourage cross-sectoral cooperation. the macro-regional strategy in the mediterranean has great potential, not only through the common natural environment, but also through a shared history and culture. for this reason, a priority must be given to strengthening the southern dimension of the european neighbourhood policy, ensuring better management of migration flows.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on 'the evolution of eu macro-regional strategies: current practices and future prospects, notably in the mediterranean', which recognises the added value of the baltic sea macro-regional strategy and of these strategies in general. macro-regional strategies make it possible to link the competent authorities of several member states in order to define similar frameworks for the same mountain, maritime, etc. area. these strategies allow investment to be shared by the different actors, priorities to be coordinated and regional financing to be developed in an integrated approach.
in writing. the innovation offered by the macro-regional strategies is interesting and the first results in the baltic and danube regions are encouraging. i am in favour of this text because it shows europe's interest in looking to the south, the region from which i myself was elected. but i would like to remind you that it will be much more difficult to devise a macro-regional strategy for the mediterranean than for the rest of europe, because the mediterranean periphery is a very special area. it's a meeting place, but it's also a border. the border between peoples who share a common history, cultures, sometimes even origins, but whose average per capita income is five times higher in the north than in the south. it's the most important border differential in the world. a border for countries that do not share the same characteristics. some in the south are experiencing a return to democracy with the arab spring, others are locked into autocratic logics. so yes, we need to develop a macro-regional strategy. but in stages: first with our closest partners, through culture, tourism, biodiversity, entrepreneurship. by combining different existing instruments, including the union for the mediterranean and the european neighbourhood policy.
in writing. launched in 2009, the baltic sea macro-region is a coherent set of territories that are designed to cooperate to better address economic and environmental challenges. this cooperation took the form of a 'macroregional strategy', designed to coordinate the strong sectoral cooperation already in place, and structured around four pillars environment, prosperity, accessibility and security and around an action plan with 15 priority areas and 80 flagship projects. the mediterranean basin shares the same natural environment and a common historical and cultural reality links all its shores. in the south of europe there is a great potential which cannot be exploited without the coordination and overall vision required by the definition of a macro-regional strategy. potential is the need to put maritime traffic at the heart of a transport strategy throughout the area, particularly for goods. the report also highlights the possibility of strengthening the southern dimension of the european neighbourhood policy, with a concrete territorial dimension that ensures better management of migration flows and has a positive impact on the performance of their own economies.
in writing. the macro-regional strategies of the baltic and danube regions have demonstrated the usefulness of policy coordination at the level of functional territories. in the wake of the arab spring, it is a historic necessity to re-establish our relations with the mediterranean countries. experience has shown that multilateral relations at local and regional level have as much impact as large bilateral agreements. let us use the european experience to help these regions in their democratic transition. a macro-regional approach has many advantages: it can address common challenges, coordinate neighbourhood policy and regional development policy, and rethink multi-level governance and subsidiarity in the mediterranean area. consolidating an area of peace, democracy and prosperity around the mediterranean is the european union's next challenge. we must live up to the hopes raised by the arab spring in order to revive a euro-mediterranean partnership of proximity and projects.
