in writing. the first railway package, adopted in 2001, was already aimed at improving the attractiveness of rail transport. this reform was not successful: ten years later, rail transport has still not managed to catch up with other modes of transport. this failure is mainly due to divergences between national regulations and the failure of member states to implement the first railway package. i therefore voted in favour of the revision of the european railway package, which aims to create a single railway area. as a result of two years of tough negotiations, i have supported, in particular, non-discriminatory access to the railway network, fair competition between railway companies, the approximation of technical standards and further harmonisation in the framework of national and cross-border rail transport.
in writing. last november, in the first reading vote, i voted against this revision of the railway package. i still believe that if progress has been made, whether in terms of transparency, enhanced cooperation between national authorities or multiannual programming of infrastructure projects, it is not enough to support this second reading. the main reason why i do not support this package is the commitment to continue on the path of liberalisation, and in particular the repeated and sustained commitment to open up passenger transport to competition. in this package, the commission and parliament also commit themselves to continue along the path of separation between infrastructure managers and transport operators, whereas we see clearly in our respective countries, and in particular in france, that this separation poses many difficulties and that it would be good to re-examine everything in order, perhaps, to consider something other than ever more liberalization.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mrs debora serracchiani on a single european railway area. in the context of the fragmentation of the railway area in the union, there is an urgent need to legislate for greater convergence of national regulations. the first railway package, adopted in 2001, was already intended to improve the attractiveness of rail transport, but ten years later, there is no evidence of its implementation. to make up for the lack of development and maintenance of infrastructure, the report proposes that rail, the main mode of transport, should be made an economic vehicle for european spatial planning. these structural reforms are aimed at stimulating private and public investment so that new operators can enter a more 'open' railway market. in addition, it is necessary to guarantee the rules of a fair and non-discriminatory railway market. fair competition between railway companies and access to reliable, safe and efficient services must also be ensured. the railway can, in my view, be a good showcase of european technology to the world.
in writing. in the era of free movement of goods, capital and people within the european union, it is appropriate that harmonised rules for the operation of rail networks are put in place at european level. this will improve transparency in slot allocation and management and promote transnational coordination at all levels: available capacity, investment, infrastructure works, operational management, etc. the creation of a single point of contact should also enable companies to have a single point of contact, a symbol of railway corridor management with a european perspective. this regulation thus sends a strong signal in favour of a genuine european transport and infrastructure policy. it is a key step towards making rail freight faster and more reliable, and thus a credible and environmentally friendly alternative to long-distance road transport. a truly european approach was all the more necessary since the rail freight market is relevant at this scale.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to improve the mobility of our citizens by ensuring the creation of a more efficient, competitive and safe rail network throughout the european union. the european parliament is thus committed to encouraging the development of modern infrastructure and safer and less noisy trains that will take travellers across the union at competitive prices!
in writing. after months of negotiations, we have finally adopted the reform of european rail legislation. while it does not cover everything, it does help to strengthen rail transport in the european union, in particular by clarifying the role of the various rail transport operators. key measures include strengthening the independence of the national regulator and establishing a european network of regulators to achieve uniform interpretation and application of legislation. another key aspect of this overhaul is the clarification of financial flows between the infrastructure manager and the railway operator. the vote does not mark the end of the reform of the european railway market. the european commission is expected to present new legislative proposals as early as next year, notably on the thorny issue of liberalising national passenger transport and on the separation of infrastructure management from railway operators.
in writing. the creation of a single european railway area aims to improve rail services by increasing competition, strengthening the competences of national regulators and improving the framework for investment in the rail sector. in this context, it is essential to ensure non-discriminatory access to railway lines and service facilities and to ensure transparency in the prices set by the independent national railway regulators. it also involves separating and controlling the accounts to ensure that railway undertakings, which are structurally linked to the infrastructure manager, are not favoured over their competitors. i supported this report at the second reading stage of the legislative procedure.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague debora serracchiani on the establishment of a single european railway area. the agreement, designed to optimise the supply and quality of transport service for international freight and passengers, is a further step towards railway integration. we have reached an agreement which ensures better use of public funds by monitoring financial flows. the directive also provides for the establishment of independent national regulators to ensure the application of the rules in the member states. it is therefore a further step towards the creation of a single european railway area.
in writing. i voted in favour of new rules to increase transparency in rail infrastructure funding. the aim is to open up the railway sector to competition and thus to offer better services to passengers and freight users. it is necessary to specify the arrangements for financing infrastructure, the conditions of competition and the rules for market surveillance. national and independent control bodies with broad powers should therefore exchange information within a european network of control bodies. similarly, the prohibition on transferring public funds from one field of activity to another should ensure more healthy competition.
in writing. i welcome the adoption today of our second reading position on the single european railway area. i am convinced that european integration requires the development of efficient and high-quality crossborder rail links. our action today is helping to ensure fairer competition by ensuring the transparency of financial flows between railway operators and network managers. the directive will also have the effect of strengthening the competitiveness of the european railway sector. incentives linked to the allocation price of railway sections, taking into account train safety and noise pollution, will be introduced to this end, thus encouraging the sector to modernise its railway fleet and infrastructure. finally, i approve the establishment of control bodies with enhanced powers, also known as national railway regulators, which will ensure effective compliance with the rules contained in this legislative provision.
in writing. the european union has developed a common currency, a common area of free movement, a common market. the four freedoms of movement - goods, people, capital and services - are only theoretical if we do not have the infrastructure to guarantee these freedoms. europe has therefore committed itself to implementing an integrated european transport network and a single railway area. we currently have more than 20 national signalling and speed control systems which are still not compatible. in addition, the absence of effective competition, insufficient regulatory oversight, weak public and private investment, missing links in border areas and bottlenecks are hampering the growth of the freight and passenger transport market. this report will guarantee the independence of the monitoring bodies and will be the first step in the liberalisation of rail transport, with a view to creating a common area of fast, safe, economical and sustainable transport in the eu.
in writing. the profession of professional driver is already highly regulated. however, driving and rest times are not always respected and increase the risk of accidents. i therefore voted in favour of the installation of tachographs on all lorries over 2.8 tonnes by 2020. the tachograph is the device that records the driving and rest times of professional drivers and the new generation of this instrument will incorporate satellite technologies. this means that the trucks already in service will have to be retrofitted. despite the strong objections of the international road transport union (iru), the arguments for safety and prevention have prevailed, and i am glad of that!
in writing. the current social regulations in the field of road transport are still too often violated and the tachograph control system, a box recording the driving and resting time of road drivers, is inefficient. failure to comply with the maximum driving times and minimum rest periods leads to greater fatigue for drivers and therefore constitutes an increased risk to road safety. the existing legislation must therefore be revised. the new regulation aims to better enforce social legislation and make fraud more difficult, mainly through 'smart tachographs' making full use of new technologies. these innovative, more efficient recording tools will enable the control authorities to directly target fraudulent trucks and better control the driving and rest times of road drivers. i therefore supported this text, which is aimed at improving the working conditions of drivers and making the road safer for everyone.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by silvia-adriana ţicău on the control system in the field of road transport. i am in favour of the introduction of an effective tool to combat road safety: the tachograph. this system is designed to combat non-compliance with the rules on driving time and rest periods for road drivers. in addition, this tool promotes better control productivity and improved working conditions for road drivers.
in writing. i voted for the ţicău report on the improvement of the tachograph system in the field of road transport. i believe that the respect of driving and rest times by road drivers is a prerequisite for improving road safety in europe. i also support the use of satellite geolocation to reduce fraud. this report proposes some sensible measures and i welcome its adoption.
in writing. ensuring that lorry drivers respect their driving and rest times is a health and safety necessity, not only for them but also for all road users. i have supported this report because the tools it introduces will make it easier to monitor compliance with the legislation in this area. the tachograph will make it easier to check that drivers and transport companies are obeying the law. but above all, parliament has offered a derogation to small businesses whose conduct is not their main activity: protecting small entrepreneurs from such additional costs was essential.
in writing. even as millions of europeans are preparing to hit the road for their holidays, we need to provide concrete answers to the question of road safety. the commission has also proposed a comprehensive revision of the legislation on the tachograph, a compulsory monitoring device installed in lorries. the failure of lorry drivers to comply with labour legislation, often under pressure from employers, is unfortunately all too common in europe: the stress and fatigue of lorry drivers is the cause of about 20% of road accidents. this new version of the tachograph will be used for heavy goods vehicles of more than 2.8 tonnes (and no longer more than 3.5 tonnes) and for vehicles carrying more than 9 persons. we have also paved the way for the electronic use of the device to replace manual use, heralding the advent of the so-called 'smart' tachograph by 2020, which is expected to save road transport companies the equivalent of 515 million in administrative costs per year and also prevent fraud.
in writing. i voted in favour of this reform which improves the respect for the social rights of road drivers by deepening the rules on the instruments in vehicles used to measure their driving and rest times. it is essential to monitor compliance with our social legislation in road transport, not only to ensure fair competition in this sector, but also to protect workers in the sector and to improve road safety more generally by fighting against fatigue at the wheel!
in writing. better working conditions and greater respect for legislation on rest and driving time for lorry drivers in europe, that is why i voted in favour of this text. it is also a matter of bringing more transparency to an area which is still very opaque. the current tachographs are too easy to use and do not provide the guarantees needed to ensure effective control of driving and rest times for road users in europe. the commission has also proposed that the directive be amended to include a new system of checks on the use of vehicles with a maximum speed of 50 km/h.
in writing. road safety and social protection are not incompatible. this is what the european parliament meant when it adopted the report on the improvement of tachograph systems, the first of which were introduced in 1985. parliament called for the introduction of 'smart tachographs' by 2020, which take account of technological innovations to improve the monitoring of goods and passenger transport vehicles and to limit abuses. driving time is not strictly enforced in europe. manipulation of tachographs has been found to extend the driving time of drivers. these irresponsible behaviours, which represent a real danger to the safety of our roads, call for proportionate sanctions. i am well aware of the competition that our road transport companies are facing because of the increase in fraud. i therefore felt that any initiative which would limit the fraud itself, fuelled by profound differences in social legislation, i am thinking in particular of rest time requirements, deserves support.
in writing. tachographs are boxes that record the driving and resting time of truck drivers. they play a vital role in transport safety in the european union and are a guarantee of respect for the social rights of drivers. in view of the latest technological innovations, it is essential to adapt the previous regulation. the report by my colleague, mrs ticau, advocates digital tachographs, so-called 'smart tachographs'. they will enable the control authorities to directly target fraudulent vehicles and improve controls. the report also calls for the training of police forces to be harmonised. i supported this report, which was adopted by the european parliament in plenary.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft report on the control system in road transport. the use of the most advanced technologies is necessary to improve road safety by regulating the supervision of road users. the tachograph will now be more efficient and reliable and will incorporate the latest technological innovations. it will make it possible to check more strictly that drivers' driving and rest times are respected. the text will not only improve road safety but also combat unfair competition in road transport.
in writing. in order to ensure optimum road safety for all road users and suitable working conditions for road drivers, strict standards for working and resting time have been established and digital tachographs (instruments for recording data on drivers' driving behaviour) have been made mandatory for new vehicles over 2.8 tonnes. in order to ensure that the current rules are better observed and to avoid the multiplication of unnecessary checks, new technical standards for tachographs had to be established (in particular for remote control). that is the spirit of the commission's proposal, which i support in general. nevertheless, in order to ensure maximum safety, it seems to me crucial that, in parallel with the driver's working and resting time, the speed of the vehicle and its weight - often factors in accidents - are recorded. in addition, in order not to impose unnecessary administrative burdens on the craftsmen, i am in favour of an exemption for lorries used within a 100 km radius by drivers whose main occupation is not this. i therefore voted in favour of the amendments which go in this direction.
in writing. with a view to reducing fraud and improving the application of social legislation for road hauliers, this amendment to the council regulation is useful, since at its core is the mandatory installation of a new generation of tachographs on all new road transport vehicles. the systematic and compulsory use of this new technology should make speed checks and especially driving times easier. it is therefore important in terms of road safety, but also for the working conditions of truck drivers. however, the use of these new tachographs entails data protection risks, previously raised by the european data protection supervisor, which are not addressed by this proposal, in particular in terms of data storage and access. in addition, some restrictions, such as the registration of the starting and the ending points, do not go far enough. i therefore abstained in this vote because i recognize the usefulness of this new regulation but i have reservations about it, particularly with regard to the protection of the fundamental rights of european citizens.
in writing. the european union legislates in many areas. our role as parliamentarians is also to ensure that the legislative provisions are in line with the changes in our society. for example, the 2003 legislation on customs enforcement of intellectual property rights is now obsolete due to the rapid growth of online commerce. one of the key provisions of this regulation is to introduce a simplified procedure for small consignments. online sales have led to a dramatic increase of 200% in postal sales. in response, the commission provides that 'small consignments of goods' suspected of being counterfeit may be destroyed without the intervention of the right holder, reducing administrative burdens and costs for customs officers. for greater legal certainty and to avoid confusion, we tabled an amendment to extend these provisions to patents. the text was therefore adopted despite the flexibility of the socialists, who were influenced by lobbies at the last minute.
in writing. in the eu, counterfeit products cost european businesses €250 billion. the report thus extends the scope of customs action to a wider range of intellectual property rights. as regards the control of medicines in transit by customs, this will only be carried out if there is sufficient evidence of their counterfeiting in the union. the report does not therefore prejudice their marketing but calls for vigilance against counterfeiting.
in writing. the counterfeit and pirated goods that still too often cross our external borders are a threat to european businesses and growth. customs officials should be given the means to combat such fraud effectively. with this text, which i voted for, it is done. i am particularly pleased that this enhanced protection for european companies is not at the expense of the health of citizens of third countries: parliament has ensured that generic medicines crossing our territory to third countries will not be subject to unnecessary delays. i support these measures because they are both necessary and just.
in writing. i supported this text, which strengthens the fight against counterfeiting by improving and strengthening customs controls in this area. we cannot tolerate any longer that piracy and counterfeiting cause european companies to lose 250 billion euros a year and endanger the safety (for example, counterfeit toys) and health (for example, fake medicines) of our citizens!
in writing. it is clear that piracy, counterfeiting and parallel imports are a scourge for our economies and often a danger to citizens, and that these unfair practices must be firmly combated. but this report merely notes the dismantling of services and the lack of resources in the customs field, which no one else is proposing to strengthen. whose fault is that ? where is the promise of increased external border controls in return for the dismantling of internal european border controls? the explosion in imports of counterfeit goods is a direct consequence of your ultra-barter policies and in particular your acceptance of china, the world's largest counterfeiter, into the wto. the first thing to do is to re-establish real customs frontiers, real trade protection at european and national level. otherwise, what you're offering sounds more like palliative care than actual therapy. in addition, the report's treatment of ordinary citizens seems to me both unclear and excessive. that is why, although i tried to do so, i could not approve the creutzmann report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal for a european regulation. the new legislation will strengthen the procedures enabling customs authorities to prevent the movement of goods suspected of infringing intellectual property rights. in the absence of resources, controls at the union's external borders are often inadequate. when external border controls fail, the damage is already done. internal control procedures thus appear to be very difficult and costly once goods are distributed in the different member states. counterfeiting is a real scourge, costing european companies 250 billion euros a year. much of the economic growth and employment in the union depends on the respect of intellectual property rights. some counterfeit products can pose a real threat to the health and safety of consumers. i was also rapporteur for a directive on the prevention of falsified medicines in the union in 2010. i have particularly investigated these criminal acts, which are deliberate poisonings, real attempts at premeditated murder.
in writing. economic growth and employment in the european union depend in part on the effective enforcement of intellectual property rights. in addition to economic impact, counterfeit products can pose a threat to the health and safety of european consumers. to combat this, customs authorities are best placed to enforce intellectual property rights at external borders, before goods enter the internal market. that is why i supported mr creutzmann's report. it provides for procedures enabling customs authorities to prevent the movement of goods where they suspect that they infringe intellectual property rights.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by jürgen creutzmann on the control by customs authorities of the respect of intellectual property rights in order to combat counterfeit products in europe. in concrete terms, this means giving customs officers at the external borders of the european union increased means to detect infringements of intellectual property rights, such as counterfeiting or trade in pirated works. i am pleased that the european parliament has voted in favour of this regulation, which i believe is a necessary step towards protecting our know-how and competitiveness. it is essential that the union has strong instruments to combat counterfeiting and to defend our economy and our businesses.
in writing. the proposal aims to strengthen the european customs system in the face of the current increase in counterfeiting flows in europe. under the guise of respect for intellectual property and the promotion of creativity, this proposal only makes sense in the european union's frantic pursuit of competitiveness at any cost. the union is once again seeking to strengthen the repressive apparatus, while at the same time restricting the freedoms of its citizens. in some respects, this text is similar to the battle against acta. the amendments tabled by the gue/ngl were rejected in the main. the distinction between 'evidence' and 'sufficient evidence on the basis of the applicable legal procedures' would have been essential to the acceptability of this proposal, but it did not pass the vote. the only point of satisfaction here is the mention of counterfeit medicines, which are a major health issue for all. i therefore voted against this proposal.

in writing. it is a recurring theme: water is a scarce resource that must be conserved, but it must also be made available to all. access to water must therefore be recognised as a fundamental and universal right. water pricing must also be as transparent as possible so that no unfair profit is made on this common good of humanity. the adoption of a lifestyle that uses less water must become a priority for european citizens in order to preserve this drying commodity. but it is also necessary to renovate and control the water supply networks of europe's large cities so that the loss of water before consumption, which now amounts to 20% of total volumes, is reduced as much as possible. finally, the fight against pollution of the natural environment and the treatment of waste water is necessary at a time when drinking water is far from being a reality in all parts of the world.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the european union water legislation with a view to improving european water legislation. water is a common good of mankind, and taking into account that access to water should be a fundamental and universal right, we must take responsibility for the good management of our water resources at european level. this is why the sectors that consume the most water, such as energy and agriculture, need to be particularly careful and adopt a rational use approach.
in writing. in this resolution, which i fully support, we propose a number of measures to safeguard the quality of water in europe and to ensure its rational use. the recurring problem of green algae proliferation, which we have in brittany for example, shows that we must act in this direction. the resolution focuses in particular on the use of incentive mechanisms such as the application of the 'polluter pays' and 'user pays' principles or the establishment of transparent and efficient pricing systems that would internalise both the costs of remediation and the environmental costs. however, it should not be forgotten that this should not lead to an unreasonable increase in the price of water. the text also contains proposals for the prospecting and exploitation of shale gas, a problem which is of particular concern to france, which has a large amount of shale gas on its soil. we therefore ask the commission to undertake research to assess the negative impact of the exploitation of these gases on the quality of groundwater.
in writing. road safety regulations can and must always be improved. i therefore ask that the ecall emergency system be made compulsory in cars. all new cars should be equipped with these ecalls free of charge by 2015 to automatically alert emergency services to road accidents via the 112 emergency call. the technology is ready and yet our states have taken no steps to impose it on the car manufacturers. in addition to the seat belt and airbag, ecall will reduce the consequences of accidents by automatically alerting emergency services in the event of a collision. this allows the accident site to be reported immediately and the rescue services to respond more quickly. of course, the location of vehicles can only be determined in the event of an accident and not on other occasions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the ecall system: a new '112' service for citizens. this system is a real technological breakthrough: it allows a car, whether it has been in an accident or not, to automatically trigger an emergency call while sending essential information about the accident such as the time, the precise position of the vehicle, its direction, its description, whether its occupants are conscious or not. this system, which can also be activated manually, is based on the single european emergency number 112 associated with the geolocation of the vehicle. it is estimated that the introduction of such a system in cars could save 2500 european lives a year and reduce the severity of injuries by 10% to 15% through improved emergency response. the ecall system is a sleeping system until an emergency call is triggered. it therefore fully respects data protection and privacy, which is a prerequisite for its adoption. in addition, ecall ensures technological neutrality so that car manufacturers can be free to choose the system they equip their vehicles with.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of the koch-sehnalová report. this new ecall device available to european citizens could save up to 2,500 lives every year. the new 112 service will make it possible, in particular, to ensure more effective care for road accidents by means of a faster intervention by the emergency services. in addition, the compulsory nature of this measure seems to me to be a good thing, since there have been few voluntary initiatives so far. it would be wise to extend this system to all new vehicles in the eu.

in writing. i hope this technology will be applied as soon as possible to save lives. the result of research funded by the european union, the 'ecall' is a small device based on sensors embedded in the car. in the event of a serious accident, this device automatically dials 112, the european emergency number. the location of the car, its direction and the time of the accident are directly communicated. the possibility should then be left to member states to choose the organisation of call routing, for example through sorting platforms that distinguish between calls for emergency and public service calls and those for assistance and private service provision. a european ecall would save time: 40% in urban areas and 50% in rural areas, according to the european commission. while 30 900 people died on eu roads in 2010 and more than 1.5 million were injured in 2009, ecall would reduce the number of fatalities by at least 4% and the number of serious injuries by at least 6%.

in writing. the socialists have always denounced the lack of transparency in the conduct of the negotiations on the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement (acta) and our fight for the rejection of this agreement has continued to gain ground in parliament, where five parliamentary committees rejected it. so there was only one responsible response we could give to the citizens for acta: the rejection of it by the parliament in plenary. despite the many delaying manoeuvres of the right wing, and of the epp in particular, that is what we parliamentarians have done today and i welcome that. our assembly thus remains at the forefront of protecting the highest european standards of fundamental rights. i would like to pay tribute to the work of kader arif, whom i am succeeding. acta was the worst possible response to a real problem: an agreement that was ineffective in tackling the scourge of counterfeiting, but above all an agreement that was potentially dangerous for the fundamental freedoms of european citizens because of its great legal vagueness. in addition, it raised many other concerns about neutrality, free access to the internet, access to generic medicines or protection of geographical indications. it was definitely not!
in writing. i chose to abstain from voting on the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement (acta) for two reasons. firstly, as a procedure is under way before the court of justice of the european union, i think it is necessary to wait for its conclusion before making a final decision. this is not only the result of common sense but also of respect for the rule of law and effective cooperation between institutions. secondly, while acta is not a perfect solution to counterfeiting, it is a constructive proposal, aimed at protecting innovation, jobs and our businesses. by protecting intellectual property rights, acta also protects us. in france, for example, counterfeiting destroys 30 000 to 40 000 jobs a year, and in europe nearly 100 000. therefore, in the absence of any certainty as to the compatibility or incompatibility of the agreement with community law, and in the current context of crisis, i considered that i did not have the information necessary to take an informed decision and therefore i preferred to abstain.

in writing. our old francs had the following inscription: "counterfeiters will be punished with forced labor for life". the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat counterfeiting. the protection of intellectual property rights is a driver of technical innovation and a fair reward for researchers and artistic creation. defending intellectual property is absolutely necessary. this anti-counterfeiting agreement negotiated by the european commission is not satisfactory in many respects. there is a lot of talk about border controls in this agreement, but the union has done away with them internally and not really strengthened them externally. furthermore, acta focuses on the spread of counterfeiting and probably not enough on the counterfeiters. anyway, it's done without them. in the end, the legitimate objective of acta is undermined by a poor methodology, a lack of clarity, too many objectives and therefore uncertain effectiveness and consequences.

in writing. i voted decisively against acta because it was too uncertain and too risky for the fundamental rights of europeans. but acta had the merit of tackling real challenges: protecting intellectual property against counterfeiting and piracy and bringing to the table real challenges for business, creativity and intellectual property rights in europe and the world, which are a necessity. but the negotiation of the agreement did not reconcile these imperatives with the protection of individual freedoms and the fundamental rights of citizens. the outcome of the vote could not have been different. this is a historic vote, as it is the first time that the european parliament has rejected an international trade agreement since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. i regret that the european parliament today refused to adopt an international instrument to combat counterfeiting more effectively without even waiting for the opinion of the court of justice of the european union. the aim of the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement (acta) is not to redefine the scope of protection of intellectual property rights, such as patents or trademarks, but to coordinate the mechanisms for protecting these rights in order to better combat counterfeiting. i would remind you that in 2009 the international trade in counterfeit goods was worth about 250 billion dollars. the number of cases identified in europe has increased by 920% in ten years. this is probably 2.5 million jobs lost. as far as piracy is concerned, there are 1.4 million smes in europe (out of 22 million) working in the film, music and book industries. contrary to some common beliefs, there was never any question of cutting off citizens' access to the internet, let alone monitoring individuals. it was really about creating a coherent global framework and making sure that in every country we have good intellectual property protection to protect our businesses and our jobs.
in writing. i voted against acta because it became clear during the discussions that this agreement was incompatible with the values and rules of european law, which i defend as a member of the european parliament. the formal outcome of the extremely opaque negotiations was impossible to guarantee, even though the rights of european citizens were at stake. in substance, this agreement is contrary to the charter of fundamental rights because some of its articles open the door to the risk of control of internet users, including innocent users, which would constitute a violation of the law. with a large number of vague wordings, it does not provide the legal certainty required to prosecute cases of infringement of intellectual property rights. if the fight against counterfeiting is a legitimate objective, it is still necessary to have an instrument which is really effective in this process, which acta does not allow, in the absence of important partners such as china or india. and, above all, we must defend the fundamental freedom of expression of our citizens.

in writing. on 4 july, the european parliament made some amendments to the commission's proposal on the application of the direct payments scheme for 2013, which is part of the 2014-2020 financial framework currently under negotiation. the long-term objective is to reduce inequalities in direct payments to farmers in different parts of the european union. however, as my colleague michel dantin, a specialist in the common agricultural policy, points out, in some member states 'a rapid reduction in support would lead to the closure of farms'. a balanced approach is therefore needed, taking account of the new member states of the european union while preserving the agricultural sector of other countries.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on direct payments to farmers. this proposal concerns the year 2013 of the next multiannual financial framework for 2014-2020 and the amounts of rural development aid that it will withhold. its main objective is to set net ceilings for direct payments for calendar year 2013 by establishing an adjustment mechanism similar to modulation in order to ensure continuity in payment levels, while taking into account the gradual introduction of direct payments in the new member states and the cessation of optional modulation. it is therefore important to maintain the volume of direct support in 2013 and beyond at a level similar to that of 2012 and to put in place a transitional mechanism for 2013 in order to avoid market distortions resulting from the different methods of application of the recent cap reforms in the different member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which proposes to extend certain financial provisions of the direct payments regulation until the end of 2013. it seems to me important to ensure continuity in payment levels pending the implementation of the reformed common agricultural policy from 2014. i welcome the idea of creating a reserve fund to meet financing needs in the event of an agricultural crisis.
in writing. the regulation on direct payment to farmers is in force until the end of 2013. however, some of the financial provisions it provides for will expire before that date. this report, for reasons of consistency, aims to amend the regulation by extending the application of these financial provisions until the end of 2013. the european parliament has adopted this report by a very large majority, and i welcome that.

in writing. as a member of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, i was particularly interested in the report on the strategy for the protection and welfare of animals. animal welfare is closely linked to public health and animal welfare rules must be applied appropriately throughout the european union, in particular to prevent the spread of animal diseases. these questions concern me all the more as my report on electronic labelling of cattle, which is currently under discussion, raises similar questions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on a strategy for the protection and welfare of animals. the priority is to improve the application of existing animal welfare rules in the member states. the directive on the protection of laying hens, adopted in 1999, is not applied uniformly in all member states, for example, and this leads to distortions of competition between european producers. to address these adverse effects, the action plan 2011-2015 aims to better monitor existing legislation and to link animal health and public health more systematically. for example, giving more weight to the european food and veterinary office would make it possible to have a more active watch. in addition, major projects still need to be studied: legislation on the transport of animals, rules on the identification of domestic animals and the prohibition of illegal shelters.
in writing. i voted for the paulsen report. i welcome the establishment of a european legislative framework on animal welfare. first of all, it seems to me important to enforce existing legislation and to ensure that third countries respect european standards. i note the need for a single definition of animal welfare. i support the idea of creating a european network to share good practice and ultimately to establish a european strategy on this subject.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which sets out recommendations for improving animal welfare in europe. unfortunately, although it does not call for a reduction in transport time, it does set a limit of 8 hours for live animals, as called for in a recent petition on the subject. the text also calls for the inclusion of animal welfare standards in trade agreements signed by the eu. the resolution, however imperfect, is therefore an encouraging first sign which i hope will lead to a real proposal for regulation from the commission.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because a high level of animal welfare plays a vital role in protecting public health and guaranteeing our productivity and competitiveness. whether it's through our food or just contact, the link between animal welfare and public health is clear. good animal husbandry, including in domestic animals, reduces the spread of disease and antimicrobial resistance. the commission must ensure that these issues are taken into account in its trade relations. animal welfare in third countries must be promoted, while maintaining a reasonable position, which does not harm our economy, by the use of reciprocity rules. a framework legislation on animal welfare would increase our competitiveness and improve the quality of animal products. this could make it easier for the eu to require imports from third countries to meet equivalent standards. at the same time, the horizon 2020 research programme must take into account the need for research in the following areas: biodiversity conservation, wildlife trade, development and validation of alternative methods to animal testing, impact of emerging technologies.

in writing. member states are facing difficulties in dealing with the dangers to european citizens posed by the wanderings of animals in eastern and southern european countries. the resolution calls on the commission to take the necessary measures to ensure the safety of the european population and to ensure the protection of animals. i voted in favour of this resolution, which was adopted by a large majority in the european parliament.
in writing. this week we discussed the conclusions of the european council. even if the decisions taken are progress, they are in reality only a small time-saver, without any truly innovative solution. firstly, contrary to what françois hollande has been trying to make us believe for months, france will not call into question the treaty which has already been ratified by many european countries, and that is a good thing! mr hollande has finally resorted to a growth pact to complete the treaty. but does the treaty differ in terms from the one signed by his predecessor, nicolas sarkozy? no, not at all! moreover, françois hollande has finally accepted the central part of the budget treaty, the famous golden rule, which nicolas sarkozy wanted. he also crossed the line on eurobonds. as regards the agreements reached in the framework of the global compromise, these are matters which have been under consideration for months in the european institutions. in other words, nothing new! so françois hollande delayed ratification of the treaty and finally accepted what we had proposed at the beginning of the crisis.
in writing. the best is often the enemy of the good, so caution is in order. if, like others, i consider that the latest european council has made it possible to move in the right direction, i would like to point out that it will not allow a kind of 'catch-up' with regard to the citizens and public opinion, which is still marked by the failure to take account of the 'no' vote in the tece referendum. a genuine growth policy must go hand in hand with the austerity measures being implemented throughout europe. the growth pact is a first step, but we need to go further: the states must understand that it is time to raise the eu budget to 1.24% of gdp as we have the possibility to do so. finally, the resolution recalls, and this is a good thing, that an agreement on own resources is essential to any overall agreement on the next multiannual financial framework.
in writing. this european summit is above all a summit of hypocrisy and lies. it allows mr hollande to impose the scandalous 'fiscal pact', this unacceptable budgetary prison, by making it appear that he now has a counterpart in the form of a 'growth pact'. but the latter is just a list of measures that are heterogeneous and have been planned for a long time, and the figures are manipulated. we're a long way from the 1% of gdp we promised. the sums to be mobilised are paltry: 120 billion, yes, but over two years. only 40 billion is public funds, the rest consisting of a series of loans or guarantees. the funds will be sprinkled throughout the 27 and not focused on emergencies or priorities. even if we help the states, we should give them their share of the billions of unused regional funds, it would ease their budget! as for the other measures, mr hollande will have to explain what he has agreed to submit to. i will mention only a few: the full implementation of the bolkenstein directive, the relaxation of the labour code and in particular of dismissals, the end of regulated professions, the opening up of public contracts to international (chinese?) competition, and... the 'reactivation of older workers', a very worrying expression. his constituents will appreciate it.
in writing. the conclusions of the june 2012 european council are in the red. they are symbolically moving towards greater solidarity and integration, the only way to cope with this economic crisis which is not ending, which is a positive thing. however, only about 10 billion of the 120 originally promised by the "growth pact" are really new and additional. moreover, the conclusions continue to be guided by the theme of 'growth', which is seen as the only remedy for all our economic ills. this rhetoric is not acceptable to us environmentalists. it is our whole development model that must be questioned and that must take into account the finiteness of resources, something which the summit conclusions do not or do not do. in view of this mixed assessment, i abstained on the vote on this resolution.
in writing. this joint proposal to the main political groups in the european parliament underlines the progress made by the last council, in particular the more flexible use of the fund and the crisis solidarity mechanism and the creation of a €120 billion growth and jobs pact. however, efforts must be continued. the budgetary and financial integration must be deepened and, in this respect, the role of parliament must be strengthened, particularly as regards the voting on the financial perspective and the control of budgetary control mechanisms.
in writing. the european council met on 28 and 29 june. the european parliament resolution adopted at the end of the summit welcomes the concrete measures adopted to deal with the euro crisis. parliament welcomed the idea of a response focusing on both fiscal consolidation and growth. parliament also welcomed the commitment of the european council and the commission to make the union budget an instrument of growth. it is essential that the european parliament be placed on an equal footing, beyond its role as co-legislator, in drawing up a roadmap for a genuine economic and monetary union. i supported this resolution, which was adopted by a majority, and i welcome that.
in writing. the european council meeting in june was nothing more than dust in the eyes of the european citizens. the so-called growth pact and the banking union are far from being progress. the first is essentially a reallocation of funds, while the second is a return to the one-way solidarity between the european institutions and the banks. the same banks that have never been held accountable. the crisis of globalised capitalism is being met by more and more capitalism. social europe and the green economy have been pushed to the edge of the spectrum of possibilities, and this in the greatest opacity and hypocrisy. contrary to what has been presented, this european council is therefore maintaining the same dynamic and is locking itself into a vicious circle of financial market dictates. the resolution tabled and adopted by the epp, liberal, socialist and green groups is sufficient to convince us of this. those who have everything to lose are once again those who live on european territory solely as a result of their work. i therefore voted against this resolution.
in writing. i have approved the draft resolution on banking for all. we in the european parliament ask the commission to make a proposal to that effect. i believe that having a bank account in europe must now be a right. banks must provide these services at cost to the 10% of our citizens who lack them, including the homeless, people with very low incomes, students, people with no credit history and expatriate workers. today, without a debit card, everyday life is very complex. the european union must fight financial exclusion and this starts with access to basic banking services.
in writing. a shocking figure, some 30 million european citizens currently do not have a bank account, the majority of whom are homeless, students abroad and expatriate workers. access to basic banking services must be recognised as a fundamental right of european citizens. anyone legally resident in the eu should be able to open a bank account and carry out simple transactions such as receiving a salary, paying bills and withdrawing money, free of charge or at a reasonable cost. it is shocking that low incomes, professional status or debt levels are still the reasons for refusing to open a bank account. it is imperative that banks provide services for the most vulnerable and no longer focus on the most attractive customers. the same is true for social inclusion: access to a bank account is often a prerequisite for access to employment, health services and housing. despite the european commission's previous recommendations on this matter, too many member states do not comply with them. it must therefore address this financial exclusion and present appropriate measures promptly.
in writing. access to banking services is a major factor in the ability of european consumers to benefit from the single market's range of goods and services and to move or work within it. the fact is alarming: the right of access to basic banking services is still not guaranteed at eu level, to the extent that 7 million citizens are excluded from the conventional banking system. to remedy this situation, the report aims to make available to european citizens the effective provision of essential payment services: opening an account, depositing and withdrawing money, transferring cash from one account to another and receiving bank statements. by promoting greater financial and social inclusion, the initiative aims to bring the single market closer to consumers.
in writing. i am satisfied with the adoption of this report. access to basic banking services is essential as it determines the access of european citizens to employment, health and housing. since basic banking services are essential for integration into society, i am pleased to see the european parliament adopt a text that facilitates access to them. i also welcome the initiative of the econ committee to get a legislative proposal from the commission and not just a recommendation.
in writing. one in ten european citizens currently lives without a bank account, even though the use of a bank account is almost indispensable for basic transactions such as collecting a salary or paying a bill. the homeless, people with very low incomes, students or certain expatriate workers are sometimes excluded from using basic banking services because of too few resources in the eyes of some banks or too heavy administrative formalities. access to basic banking services must be a guaranteed right for all europeans. this is why banks should unconditionally open a basic bank account for any european citizen who so wishes, regardless of his level of resources or his banking history. banks are essential to the financing of the economy, but they also have a duty not to exclude european citizens from life in society.
in writing. in 2012, 7% of the adult population in the union still did not have a bank account, or about 30 million people. to remedy this problem, i supported the adoption of this text, in which the european parliament calls for the recognition of the universal right of european citizens to have a basic bank account. everyone should be able to open an account and carry out banking operations which are simple (such as depositing a salary or withdrawing money), but which have become essential in our daily lives and which contribute to the functioning of our economy!
in writing. i voted in favour of the text on access to banking services to ask the commission to come forward with legislation to enable all european citizens to have access to a bank account. seven per cent of the adult population in the union, or about 30 million people, currently do not have a bank account. it is the poorest who are under this constraint of not having access to basic banking services. access to a bank account is also necessary for social inclusion and to ensure access to employment, health care and housing for all.
in writing. bank accounts are required to collect wages or allowances, pay bills or taxes, purchase goods and services, withdraw cash, or print bank statements. one in ten europeans do not have access to banking services: the homeless, people with very low incomes, students, expatriate workers... for all these individuals, access to basic banking services should be a right! in supporting this resolution, i call on the commission to bring forward legislation by 2013 to end this financial exclusion which i find unacceptable. the text states that institutions offering payment accounts should not refuse to grant such an account because of the applicant's low income, professional status, credit history or level of indebtedness. the text also states that the basic payment account should always be cheaper than any other product offered by an institution and that it should not be possible to make the basic payment account conditional on the purchase of other products or services. i now look forward to the commission's proposal.
in writing. 7% of the union's population (around 30 million people) do not have a bank account. 6.4 million of these people were either denied access or did not dare to apply for an account. banking exclusion goes hand in hand with social exclusion, can aggravate it and make any possibility of reintegration difficult. in addition, beyond the situation of the uncertain, a number of difficulties may arise for eu citizens who wish to bank outside their country of residence. and as the report notes, the fight against money laundering or terrorist financing sometimes has a good backing to refuse account opening. some countries have already passed legislation to ensure access to basic banking services and 100% of households are covered: finland and the netherlands are examples. the report by my colleague from die linke, jürgen klute, is a compromise report which calls on the commission to present a directive guaranteeing access to basic banking services and makes a number of recommendations as to the content of this directive. so i have chosen to vote in favour.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to congratulate mr göran färm on his extremely productive work on this matter. thanks to this work and to the cooperation with the council under the danish and now the cypriot presidency, we can hope for entry into force this summer. this initiative deserves support for two main reasons. firstly, this innovative financial instrument is based on the intelligent use of resources which are known to be limited: redeployment of existing budget lines on the one hand, and leverage effect on other investments on the other. fiscal stability policies will only bear fruit if they are supported by stimulus measures. the project bonds are specifically targeted at employment-generating areas, namely transport, energy and broadband infrastructures. i also believe that the text from the trilogue on which we are going to vote significantly improves the commission's proposals, by defining the instrument more precisely, by strengthening the monitoring tools, by introducing regulatory changes in case of success without discouraging the markets and by introducing the possibility of reusing interest and other income generated. finally, the possibility of merging the lgtt trust account, the current instrument for guaranteeing loans for transport infrastructure, with that of project bonds, ensures better financial management. in conclusion, mr president, we may be witnessing the advent of what you will allow me to call a 'mixed financial economy' between europe, its institutions, the eib as such and its expertise. this financial mixed economy will aim to create a genuine market for our projects and instruments in the future multiannual financial framework such as the connecting europe facility.

president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, it is my pleasure to present to you the eu’s position and latest activities on syria on behalf of the high representative/vice-president of the commission, catherine ashton. the situation in syria continues to gravely concern the european union. violence has increased and the numbers of casualties have reached unimaginable levels. the risk of civil war has become more real and there are already signs of increasing sectarian conflict. human rights abuses continue. any further militarisation of the conflict would have a serious impact not only on the syrian people but on the region as a whole. in response, the european union stepped up its activities on syria with the aim of urgently bringing about an end to the violence and finding a solution to allow for a syrian-led political transition to take place. this week is particularly busy as efforts take place at international level to consolidate, unify and strengthen the international community’s response to the syrian conflict. this is exactly what the high representative/vice-president presented in this chamber during the last plenary session: the need for a road map to support kofi annan, strengthen international pressure and make diplomatic efforts more united and robust, including the call for un security council action and the involvement of russia and china. the high representative/vice-president catherine ashton participated in the meeting of the action group for syria in geneva convened by joint special envoy kofi annan on saturday. as you know, the participants in the meeting, the united nations, the league of arab states, the european union, china, russia, france, the united kingdom, the united states, turkey, iraq and kuwait, agreed on the principles and guidelines for a syrian-led transition which includes the establishment of a transitional government body exercising full executive powers. the transitional governing body could include members of the present government on the basis of mutual agreement. the action group also reiterated its full support to kofi annan in his six-point plan, as well as for the united nations observation mission in syria giving the special envoy’s activities a new unified momentum. furthermore, the group committed to opposing any further militarisation of the conflict. there is now a path for a syrian-led transition and a mandate for kofi annan to take this forward even if implementation is the biggest challenge. these are steps forward and we will have to collectively ensure that they are followed up. the european union is committed to doing everything possible to help this process. further to the action group in geneva, the friends of syria group will meet on friday in paris. the high representative will attend the meeting with an expected number of up to 100 countries. it is our hope that the friends of syria meeting will endorse the outcome of the action group to ensure a unified response by the international community. the challenge is now to implement the agreed principles and guidelines for transition. key issues to be addressed include the appointment of an effective and empowered interlocutor by the syrian government which is also acceptable to the opposition. many components of the opposition have been quick to reject this very notion that, without a partner to negotiate with, a political solution is difficult to achieve. the effective implementation also requires a coherent and representative opposition. yesterday’s opposition meeting in cairo, organised by the league of arab states and with european union participation, was another step in trying to unite the different groups. we must help to bridge the gap between the views of the opposition inside syria and those outside syria. on the initiative of the high representative/vice-president ashton, the european union continues to meet with representatives of different groups. it has most recently supported and financed opposition seminars in brussels from the instrument for stability, organised by syrians for syrians on transition issues. the first seminar, which took place on 24 and 25 june in brussels, gathered a broad range of opposition figures to discuss issues related to the transition process, including supranational and constitutional principles, democratic principles, economic and social issues and, last but not least, minority rights. these are issues which you, the members of the european parliament, have drawn our attention to on several occasions. the message of those present was that syria is for all syrians. inclusiveness and respect for minorities are essential. the second eu funded seminar will take place in cairo in mid-july. these opposition seminars aim to contribute to the political process of ensuring a representative opposition. through this process the european union continues to facilitate syrian-led inclusive dialogue actions. in parallel the european union continues to call for united action by the un security council to add more robust and effective pressure. the syrian regime holds great responsibility for the violence perpetrated. massacres continue while international efforts to solve the crisis are ongoing. this is unacceptable and those responsible for crimes during the current conflict must be held accountable. the european union’s response is not limited to diplomacy and political engagement at all levels. the european union will continue to step up sanctions as long as the repression continues. the sanctions are targeted towards the syrian regime to deprive it of its sources for repression with minimal impact on the civilian population. on 25 june foreign ministers agreed on the 16th round of sanctions since may 2011. we must now continue to reach out to partners to ensure effective implementation and hope to increase international pressure in the friends of syria meeting. whilst bilateral aid is suspended the european union has stepped up assistance to a number of human rights organisations and activists. on 8 june the european union approved a eur 23 million special measure to support both civil society within syria and syrian refugees in the neighbouring countries in areas affected by an influx of syrian refugees. humanitarian access remains a concern and the european union continues to monitor the implementation of the agreement between the syrian government and the united nations closely. to date the european union has allocated over eur 44.6 million to address humanitarian needs inside syria and in neighbouring countries. finally, the european union supports the united nations observation mission with eur 8.2 million. the funds are used to finance 25 armoured vehicles, logistics and support for placing air ambulance capability if requested. further initiatives that facilitate syrian-led and inclusive dialogue that could help lead to a political solution can also be funded. i can assure you that the european union will continue to do its utmost to support the syrian people in their struggle for peace and freedom and to facilitate a peaceful transition process.
