mr president, commissioner, the failure of rio+20 is ultimately the failure of our society, which must, in this case, overcome itself, recover, in the face of the economic, social and climate crises. what do we have to do? to continue to pile up international summit after international summit, conference after conference, for nothing or little? or do we continue to see that the balance of power has been reversed in recent years, to the detriment of us european countries, in favour of emerging countries like china or india? what can i do? we have several leads that we think are important. first, to establish a new global governance of the environment, based on ngos, civil society, trade unions. let's create a global environmental movement! and then let's allow the emergence of a true green economy from local sustainable development policies. this is the action we must take and in which we must help the european institutions.
mr president, commissioner, neither mrs damanaki nor mr potočnik are present with us today. i have no comment . in european law, as in international law of the sea, the flag state is responsible for exercising control over the activities of its fishing vessels, whether in the matter of registration, fishing authorization, fishing register and, in particular, catch certificate. it is the flag state's responsibility to provide accurate information on the legality of their catches and to have this information validated by their flag state. the european union legislation on the issue of export licences is clear. the products may only be imported if they are accompanied by a catch certificate attesting to their legality. this certificate shall be issued by the flag state of the fishing vessels which caught the fish concerned, in accordance with its obligation under international law. in short, international law requires the flag state to respect international rules on the conservation and management of fisheries resources. cites has prepared a dangerous text for all fishermen active in the external component of the common fisheries policy. if adopted, this would allow the state which chartered the ship, and not the flag state, to be responsible for the control of the ship's activities. the chartering state could therefore also issue export certificates when it lacks the means to check the legality of the goods being transported. however, most charter states do not have the financial or technical means to control fishing activities. this text could therefore set a dangerous precedent which would lead to a legal vacuum in european union law, where the iuu regulation would no longer make sense. this is based solely on the flag state's responsibilities. giving the right to sign export certificates to states chartering fishing vessels is a breach of the legislation on combating iuu fishing. the european union already imports 70% of the aquaculture and fishery products it consumes, and it should not allow products caught illegally and criminally to enter its territory. this is the risk we run if the cites text is adopted. we must not open our doors to products which do not comply with community rules on health, social and environmental matters.
in writing. a change in the statute of the court of justice of the european union was necessary and i supported it. the aim was to reform certain provisions relating to the functioning of the three courts which make up the court. in particular: - proposals concerning the court of justice: the institution of the office of vice-president and the wider participation of judges in cases referred to the grand chamber; - proposals for the civil service tribunal: appointment of three temporary judges who could replace a judge in the event of long absence.
in writing. the court of justice of the european union has requested a change in its statute. the amendments aim to introduce the office of vice-president and to increase the number of judges from 27 to 39. the procedure for the appointment of the 12 additional judges and the role of the vice-president were defined. parliament voted by a very large majority for this report, which i also supported.
in writing. the court of justice of the european union (cjeu) has been overcrowded for several years. the overcrowding of the union's courts is very damaging both for the citizens of the union, who can no longer have a reasonable time to make a judgment, and for the cjeu itself, which sees the quality of its judgments compromised by the increased workload. proposals had been made to reform the organisation of the court of justice and the general court and to change the composition of the general court in order to improve the productivity of this institution. today we are taking a step forward by adopting our position at first reading on the organization of the courts in luxembourg. the action taken is aimed in particular at abolishing the automatic participation of the presidents of chambers in the composition of the grand chamber, adapting the quorums of the chambers to increase flexibility, creating the function of vice-president to assist the presidents of the court of justice and the general court in their duties and appointing an acting judge in the event of a judge being permanently prevented from taking part in the settlement of cases. i fully endorse the whole of that position.
in writing. the civil service tribunal of the european union is composed of seven judges. when one of them is permanently prevented from performing his duties for medical reasons, for example, the functioning of the court is affected. i therefore approved the possibility of recruiting temporary judges, a recruitment which will of course be very supervised, but which becomes possible with this report.
in writing. i fully support the request of the court that three temporary judges be appointed to replace a judge in the event of a long absence. it should be noted that this vote was partly conditional on clarification of the status of judges, between the members and the court of justice.
in writing. in accordance with article 281 tfeu, the court of justice of the european union has requested an amendment to its statute to appoint 3 temporary judges. these judges could replace a judge in the event of a long absence. the report then clarifies the status of these judges. i voted in favour of this report, which was adopted by 591 votes in favour by the european parliament at its july plenary session.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft regulation on temporary judges of the civil service tribunal of the european union, which will allow the appointment of 3 temporary judges who can replace a judge in the event of a long absence.
in writing. investment needs in transport, energy and information and communication technology (ict) infrastructure are estimated at eur 1 500 billion in europe for the period 2010-2020. while the private sector is expected to finance the bulk of these investments, most of which will be highly profitable, the role of the public sector in europe will be crucial in achieving these objectives. so we want to mobilize the private sector! in order to have everything running smoothly by 2014, we want to enter a pilot phase immediately. through the use of an eib "facility", supported by a contribution from the european union, this pilot phase should enable us to: •test the acceptance and reactions of the financial market to this initiative, as the private sector will need time to integrate the new instruments into their investment decisions; •testing the operation and optimisation of project-financing bonds in practice, in order to optimise the initiative.
in writing. i believe that a common policy on the infrastructure of trans-european networks (tens) is necessary for the proper functioning of the common market. as such, the european commission has proposed the creation of a mechanism for interconnection in europe under the next financial framework. the report also proposes the launch of a pilot phase in 2012-13 through the establishment of a new financial instrument to mobilise more private sector funds and project-based bond borrowing. this project is part of the europe 2020 strategy for 'a competitive, sustainable and inclusive europe'.
in writing. the european parliament voted overwhelmingly in favour of bond borrowing for transport, telecommunications and energy projects. these 'project bonds', which we have been negotiating for months now, will be financed by redeploying existing budget lines to the tune of €230 million. the commission will invest eur 200 million in transport networks, eur 20 million in information and communication technology networks and eur 10 million in energy networks. let us be clear: 'bond projects' do not open the way to a possible mutualisation of debt. in practice, these bonds are issued by private sector companies which respond to a call for tenders and are guaranteed by the european investment bank (eib) for 20% of the project. by attracting private capital and limiting risks, the eu hopes to raise €4.4 billion in the pilot phase by 2014, which will finance investment in reliable, long-term projects. i welcome this initiative by the european commission, which should stimulate growth in europe without creating additional expenditure. this is a thoughtful and responsible proposal.
in writing. in order to stimulate growth, mr göran färm's report calls for the issuing of loans for project promoters, on a proposal from the commission, with a partial guarantee from the european budget and the eib's capital. by reducing the risk profile of these loans, this european contribution will attract other investors. i voted in favour of this report, which was adopted by a very large majority in the european parliament at its july plenary session.
in writing. i voted in favour of the project finance bonds initiative because they will allow for a smart use of the limited resources that are known, through the redeployment of existing budget lines and the leverage effect on potential investments. moreover, fiscal stability policies will only be effective if they are supported by stimulus measures. the obligations in question are aimed specifically at areas that generate jobs and competitiveness, namely transport and energy infrastructure and broadband. we must now think about the next step, namely the establishment of the mechanism for interconnection in europe. this genuine eu 'infrastructure fund' will be based not only on grants but also on innovative financial instruments such as bonds to finance projects.
in writing. the development of modern and efficient infrastructure is of paramount importance if the europe 2020 strategy's objectives of a smart, sustainable and inclusive economy are to be achieved while reducing unemployment through the completion of the internal market. to this end, the commission proposed the creation of a connecting europe facility under the next financial framework, which will accelerate the development of infrastructure in the areas of transport, energy and ict networks, with a particular focus on strategic cross-border aspects. in addition to grants and equity instruments, the connecting europe facility includes a new financial instrument to mobilise more private sector funds, as well as project-financing bond loans. however, the initial report of the committee on budgets, as well as the subsequent negotiations with the council, concentrated on a limited number of issues, including, for example, the definition of project obligations and the evaluation of the mechanism. i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report, which is a very good report, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report.
in writing. since 2008, developed economies have been plunged into an unprecedented economic crisis. the recession we are experiencing in europe is the consequence of the disastrous state of our public finances. we have therefore embarked on deep reforms to put in place sound and rigorous fiscal policies. however, in order to allow a return to sustainable growth, it is imperative that this fiscal consolidation effort be combined with investment policies in projects that promote the competitiveness of our businesses and economies. this was the subject of the 'grand emprunt' in france, it is still the subject of the 'project bonds' and the report voted on today. the €230 million, redeployed from the current budget, will be used to guarantee private bond issues to invest in projects that promote growth and jobs, such as transport, energy and information technology. this report, which has been under negotiation for almost a year, owes nothing to the election of françois hollande and his empty and misleading incantations about growth. the political recovery of the socialists must not come at the expense of the credibility of the long-term work of the european institutions.
in writing. i welcomed the 1% surplus in the 2011 budget of the european union, i.e. eur 1.49 billion. in other words, 99% of this budget was implemented last year. i have approved this third draft amendment, especially since, under the rules applicable to the union budget, this amount of eur 1.49 billion will make it possible to reduce the member states' contributions to next year's budget by the same amount.
in writing. the report by mrs francesca balzani notes a budgetary surplus resulting from the implementation of the 2011 budget. more than €338 million of appropriations and payments remain on budget lines. they have not been and cannot be used. the report then considers that this amount should legitimately be paid to the union budget. the european parliament has adopted this report by a very large majority, and i welcome that.

vice-president of the commission. - mr president, allow me, also on my own behalf, to thank mrs flautre for her commitment and courage in taking up this very delicate matter, but also a matter of our values. the commission has constantly reiterated that the practices which are referred to as renditions constitute a serious violation of several fundamental rights: unlawful arrest, arbitrary detention, torture and ill-treatment. the fight against terrorism cannot justify such unacceptable practices. the full respect of human rights is not negotiable. the commission has always stressed that it is up to the member states concerned not only to initiate but also to continue in-depth, independent and impartial investigations to establish the truth. this is a positive obligation arising from the european convention on human rights in order to establish responsibilities and enable the victims to obtain compensation for such damage. that is also why you have quoted the court, which is putting these questions on the table. since 2005, when the allegations were first raised, the commission has been in contact with those member states that were said to have hosted secret detention sites. as regards aviation policy, the commission drew the necessary conclusions in the context of its communication on civil and business aviation of january 2008, and new rules on the procedures applicable to flight plans for the single european sky entered into force on 1 january 2009. they provide an additional means of monitoring the actual movement of aircraft, and i have heard with great interest that the contacts with the institution on this subject are very positive. the report also refers to the necessity of reinforcing the human rights compliance of judicial cooperation in criminal matters. in this regard, the commission is determined to ensure that member states do so when they apply the eu instruments on judicial cooperation in criminal matters and that member states comply with the charter of fundamental rights when they implement those instruments. as i have often said before this parliament, it is when european law is applied that the charter automatically applies, so in these cases the charter does apply. this concerns not only the internal aspects of judicial cooperation but also its external aspects. in this respect, the commission underlines the importance of the entry into force on 1 february 2010 of the two eu-us extradition and mutual legal assistance agreements. both clarify and unify the legal framework of judicial cooperation in criminal matters with the usa, and they clearly refer to the need to fully respect fundamental rights. as regards the national and institutional shortcomings highlighted by the report, let me recall that the current treaties do not empower the european union to establish a general mechanism addressing human rights violations. however, i can assure you that the commission is vigilant in ensuring that the charter applies within the scope of eu law, as i explained on the question of judicial cooperation in criminal matters. as regards the supervision of intelligence and security services, you are well aware that this is a very sensitive area which comes under the responsibility of the member states. the commission has repeatedly recalled that cooperation between intelligence services must not in any way run counter to or override the relevant eu instruments in the field of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. no cooperation between intelligence services can undermine the full respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law. i think parliament agrees with me that the only way to fight effectively against terrorism is to apply our basic rules on which the european union has built its very being. the commission is ready to cooperate actively with parliament to ensure that what happened in the framework of the so-called cia rendition programme will never happen again.

in writing. we voted by a large majority for the energy efficiency directive. on 8 march 2011, the commission presented a new energy efficiency plan (eep) which sets out measures to achieve further savings in energy supply and use, while establishing a common framework for promoting energy efficiency in the union for 2020 and beyond. this directive requires member states to set energy efficiency targets which take into account the general 20% target. but if energy efficiency is one of the sine qua non conditions for economic efficiency, the epp group felt that the requirements of realism for our companies must also be met, and urged the rapporteur to accept the compromise proposed by the council. the level of flexibility of member states, industry and public bodies has been increased. however, member states must implement incentive measures for citizens and businesses. we therefore favour gradual adaptation and flexible arrangements so that member states can adapt according to their industrial fabric and their economies.
in writing. i voted in favour of the energy efficiency directive, to achieve the european target of a 20% reduction in energy consumption by 2020. the measures adopted are varied and incorporate various mechanisms relating to the renovation of buildings, standards for public procurement, energy-saving obligations, transport and distribution. with the setting of national indicative targets, member states must commit themselves and choose the most effective measures to contribute to this common european effort.
in writing. the only progress made in this report is the introduction of binding energy efficiency targets. unfortunately, it is rendered insignificant by the narrow and unrealistic view of energy efficiency which the text proposes. it removes the obligation to take into account, in calculating energy efficiency, the total primary energy consumption that each product or service generates on the planet. worse, it exempts nuclear power plants from energy efficiency tests. add to that the validation of the carbon market and the validation of free energy competition, and you get a very high environmental bill for our ecosystem. i vote against it.
in writing. i support this report which calls for mandatory measures to reduce energy consumption in all member states. beyond environmental concerns, energy efficiency is an incredible driver of growth and employment and a key driver of our energy independence. the directive will reduce the rising costs of our dependence on energy imports - €488 billion in 2011 - which are sinking our trade balance, penalising our businesses and eroding the purchasing power of households. member states will have to set an example and renovate 3% of their public buildings annually. large companies will be obliged to carry out energy audits. the structural funds and other financial instruments of the union will be of valuable assistance in helping to finance this energy efficiency. we must make it a priority in the next operational programmes.
in writing. the high cost of energy, pollution, climate change: there are many reasons why we should support strong initiatives to ensure energy efficiency in our society and production models. it is not a question of going back to the days of the candle or of setting in motion a process of decline, but rather of adopting modern methods and concrete objectives to rationalize our consumption, both individually and collectively. that is precisely the purpose of this regulation, which i supported, and which sets the member states targets to be achieved by 2020. this is in line with the logic of the energy-climate package: to achieve 20% energy savings in the next 8 years. i believe that achieving energy efficiency means encouraging small everyday gestures, such as choosing public transport over cars or taking care of household consumption. but it is also for the public authorities to carry out a comprehensive programme for insulation and the environmental quality of buildings: this is where the main margin for progress lies. we have the right technology and know-how, all we need is the political will. this is how the union will continue to set an example and, above all, how we will have a real green growth engine.
in writing. i vote in favour of the waiver of the immunity of jarosław leszek wałęsa, as he has requested. immunity must ensure freedom of political action, not prevent the proper administration of justice in cases of common law investigations. i'd ask for mine to be lifted if i had to.
in writing. i vote in favour of the waiver of the immunity of birgit collin-langen. my vote is in line with the wish that she expressed in wishing justice to be done. immunity should ensure freedom of political action, not prevent the proper administration of justice in cases of investigations into alleged embezzlement in connection with a previous mandate.
in writing. the european parliament called on eu member states to investigate their collaboration in the illegal extraditions of suspected terrorists carried out by the cia between 2002 and 2004. as i myself believe that the eu should be a model of transparency, i supported this report which calls for the possible violations of fundamental rights to be brought to light. without compromising our support for our allies, it is our duty to ensure that the european union remains a model in the protection of human rights.
in writing. following the european parliament's inquiry into the illegal cia flights outside any framework capable of guaranteeing minimum fundamental rights, meps are calling for the necessary political and legal conclusions to be drawn now. fundamental rights in europe are a cornerstone of our collective project. however, from 2001 to 2005, the cia carried out no less than a thousand illegal flights directly involving 12 member states. we must complete this effort to bring transparency and urgently fill the legal gaps that have allowed such drift. i therefore supported this report, which seeks to give legitimacy to european discourses on human rights.
in writing. i supported this report, which we adopted to send a strong signal to the member states that the european union should move forward towards a more effective area of security, justice and freedom, closer to the european citizens. there is no longer any question of the union collaborating with the cia's anti-terrorist programmes in the same way as after the 9/11 attacks and allowing the transfer and detention of suspected terrorists by the cia in the member states. the fight against terrorism must be a priority for the european union, but it must not be waged at the expense of respect for human rights, which are the european union's core values.
in writing. eleven years after the events of 11 september and the war on terrorism launched by the united states, many areas of uncertainty remain over the question of the cia's secret prisons in europe. the fight against terrorism requires a determined commitment from the european union and its main international partners. it is imperative that the 27 apply effective measures to improve the daily security of europeans, and investigate to rule out any risk of attack. this process must be transparent and not violate human rights. the european union is a zone of full rights in which no member state can act illegally. the european parliament has already expressed its views on the situation in the former yugoslavia.
in writing. i voted resolutely in favour of this report which once again strongly condemns the unacceptable practices of 'extraordinary restitution', secret prisons and torture and, above all, the complicity of european states in these cia 'programmes'. for years we have demanded that the member states involved conduct thorough, impartial and independent investigations into the failings and abuses that have occurred, and we have demanded that the european union conform to its values. we are reminded of this in this new report. more detailed investigations must be carried out and responsibility established. the adoption of this report is a further step in the redress of these unacceptable practices. however, there is still an important work to be done to know the truth and to recognize all violations.
in writing. it is now five years since parliament adopted its final report on the illegal activities of the cia in europe, but member states are still reluctant to reveal what happened. this lack of transparency prevents the alleged violations of human rights from being brought to light. the idea that a secret imprisonment without trial has been carried out on the territory of the european union undermines the founding principles and moral authority of our institution. i voted in favour of clarifying the situation, but also to recall that respect for human rights is a fundamental principle of the european union which no one can violate.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which denounces extraordinary renditions, secret prisons and torture which violate the rights to liberty, security and human treatment. thus, states which are the subject of credible allegations must provide all available information in order to clarify the situation and assess responsibility where appropriate.
in writing. this text calls for an end to the interference of us special services in the european union. it recalled that the systematic secret detention of detainees constituted a crime against humanity for which the united states and its accomplices could be prosecuted. he denounced the role of nato in the secret detentions carried out on european territory. it called for the cessation of special procedures for terrorism suspects and for the united states to end the possibility of indefinite detention on suspicion of 'terrorism'. it recalls that state secrecy does not take precedence over fundamental rights. these are the reasons why i support this text, although i regret that it does not denounce nato and us interference in european affairs in general more widely.
in writing. some eu member states have reportedly allowed the cia, through a confidential programme, to transport and detain prisoners on their territory. in the face of such serious allegations, national parliamentary investigations were launched. but significant political and diplomatic pressures have prevented parliamentarians from working independently and making progress in their investigations. i am convinced that transatlantic cooperation between security and intelligence services is indispensable, particularly in the fight against terrorism. however, there is no excuse for impunity in the case of violations of human rights, fundamental freedoms, democracy and the rule of law. i therefore voted in favour of a resolution in plenary calling on the member states concerned to take responsibility and to support independent investigations as soon as possible. the territorial integrity of europe and the coherence of our action in the field of human rights and democracy are at stake.
in writing. the report by hélène flautre is a very good follow-up to the 2007 report, which gives an idea of the state of play of the union and the member states that may have been involved in this programme in terms of the recognition of human rights violations, which have reached an unprecedented level. despite pressure from some member states and some of their representatives in parliament, it takes stock of new allegations of complicity by member states that were not known in 2007, the reality of investigations in the member states and the obstacles encountered. violations of human rights are always intolerable, especially when they are committed by member states of the union who want to give lessons in this field to the whole world. there is no political realism in this matter, and even the fight against terrorism cannot lead to such deviations. the credibility of the union and its member states is at stake. there is still a considerable amount of work to be done to find out the truth about this programme and to recognize the countless violations that have been committed.
in writing. the member states of the european union are among the countries that most often grant asylum to persons in international danger. by voting this resolution, the european parliament wants to make more resources available for this policy. it is necessary to establish a joint processing of applications and to strengthen the role of the european asylum support office. this should allow for the need for solidarity between member states to be taken into account and thus promote closer cooperation between them.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on strengthening solidarity within the european union in the field of asylum. i particularly encourage member states to use the opportunities available under the european refugee fund with targeted actions to improve asylum systems in member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to complete the establishment of a common european asylum system by giving substance to the concept of solidarity and responsibility-sharing. it is important to me that the european union has the means to support member states facing excessive pressure and costs. i support the report's four pillars of practical cooperation and technical assistance, financial solidarity, sharing of responsibility and mutual trust at the heart of a renewed system of governance. i also share the view that we will have to identify the shortcomings of asylum systems to better guarantee the rights of asylum seekers.
in writing. by adopting this own-initiative report, we wanted to send a clear signal, on the sidelines of the negotiations between the european parliament and the council on the asylum package: the dublin ii system, which has shown all its shortcomings and limitations, needs to be reformed. our message is twofold: a message of responsibility and a message of solidarity. it is essential to strengthen solidarity between european states in the field of asylum. the recent migration flows (following the events in tunisia, then in libya and now in syria) have demonstrated this. more than ever, europe needs a genuine common european asylum system, and the implementation of the european asylum directives is urgent in order to make our european asylum system credible and effective.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on strengthening solidarity in the asylum field within the union. it was important to send a clear message to the member states and the commission on the approach which the european parliament now wishes to pursue in this area. the principle of solidarity is not new, but its practical application is still in its infancy. the failure of the union to respond coherently and effectively to the consequences of the arab spring has further underlined the lack of mutual trust between member states. in this context, solidarity can and must take many forms, through enhanced practical cooperation, targeted financial assistance or even an equitable sharing of responsibilities. this solidarity, however, cannot be achieved without making each of the actors involved responsible. as a force for solidarity, mutual trust can only be restored and boosted if each state fully assumes its responsibilities and obligations in the field of asylum. this is the approach we are advocating, an approach which is both supportive and responsible.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution to take account of the interests of asylum seekers and the solidarity needs of the member states. this resolution complements the previous mechanisms and allocates more resources to this reinforcement. in addition, the european asylum support office will also have wider powers to promote closer cooperation between eu countries. in adopting this text, the members of parliament have taken their responsibility on this matter, and i welcome that. i voted in favour of this text, which is in the direction of developing joint work between the member states. this will be accompanied by the provision of sufficient resources to the asylum and migration fund.
in writing. this report denounces the logic of the dublin regulation. it promotes the distribution of beneficiaries of international protection and asylum seekers. it stressed that such a distribution was one of the most concrete forms of solidarity which was supposed to be at the heart of the european project. i support the proposal in the report to establish a distribution key for refugees based on objective criteria and to make any transfer to another state subject to the approval of the refugees concerned. i also support his insistence that frontex should respect the un principle of non-refoulement. i regret, however, that this text does not return to the concept of a 'safe country of origin' and proposes to subject the allocation of additional funds to questionable criteria. i vote in favour, in accordance with the main points of the text.
in writing. the report by my colleague kyriacos triantaphyllides was adopted by a large majority. this report comes at a very opportune time in the laborious discussions on asylum policy and the creation of a common european asylum system, which have been going on for years. it sends a clear message to the commission and the member states, giving them concrete guidance on how to achieve real solidarity on asylum in the european union. the report calls for the relocation of asylum seekers to take account of the interests of these people when they are allocated between member states. during the debate on this report, the european commission stated that the number of asylum seekers had decreased over the last ten years, justifying this by the decrease in the number of asylum seekers arriving in the territory. we know all too well what is going on and how fortress europe is being built at the expense of the rights of migrants and the international obligations of the member states of the union. the report also stigmatises the over-bid of certain member states. let us hope that the commission hears this message and will quickly come forward with a legislative proposal that will put an end to the political game that asylum seekers are playing.
in writing. standardization and standardisation have proved to be valuable tools within the european union and with our trading partners internationally. in a market as evolving as new technologies, it was therefore crucial to allow for the establishment of clear and stable rules for businesses, especially smes, but also for all stakeholders. by agreeing this text with the council in less than a year, the european parliament is unifying the single market, making it more coherent and stable for the union's economic players.
in writing. i voted in favour of the adoption of new standardisation rules necessary to revive the single market. identified as one of the twelve levers of the single market act, these new rules will address three problems: the slow adoption of standards, the under-representation of the interests of smes and civil society actors, and the prevalence of standards adopted by non-european organisations in ict.
in writing. standardization is a driver of growth: it simplifies the administrative work of companies, lowers their production costs, and speeds up the time taken to bring their innovative products to market. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which simplifies the system at administrative and financial level while ensuring a high level of transparency. we want to involve small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) as well as representatives of environmental, consumer and civil society organisations in the development of these standards, to ensure that the views of end-users, in particular those with specific needs, such as disabled or elderly people, are taken into account and that products meet their needs. the new rules will also make it possible to achieve better compatibility with the international standardisation system, thereby boosting the global competitiveness of european enterprises. from 1 january 2013, these new rules will apply directly to the member states.
in writing. i voted for the comi report on the proposal for a regulation on european standardisation. i believe that standardisation is an essential instrument to ensure, amongst other things, the functioning of the single product market, a high level of consumer and environmental protection, and more innovation and social inclusion. it seems to me important that the modernisation of the 'standardisation package' preserves the many fruitful elements of this system, overcomes its shortcomings and strikes the right balance between the national, european and international dimensions.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which calls for further harmonisation of existing standards within the european union. by adopting these measures, we are extending a new hand to our entrepreneurs, by facilitating the export of products manufactured in our territories. the return to growth will not be possible without clear support for the actors that form the economic fabric of our territories.
in writing. to facilitate the administrative procedures of companies, the european parliament adopted on tuesday a european standardisation process. this will enable firms to access standard solutions to technical problems more quickly. this will enable them to reduce their production costs, disseminate good practice and stimulate competitiveness and growth. i voted in favour of this report on european standardisation. it allows for the revision and merger of several existing directives. this report is part of the eu 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. the european parliament insisted in the negotiations to involve small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) as well as representatives of environmental, consumer and civil society organisations in the development of these standards. consultation with these different parties ensures that the views of end-users are taken into account.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on european standardisation. the content of this report makes important progress in a concrete area which is essential for the internal market. european standards ensure continuity between a national and a european market. they thus offer new prospects for growth and a future for our businesses. however, in order to fulfil these functions, the system needs to be modernised and ensure transparency and representation of all actors, in particular smes.
in writing. this report does not call for the mandatory participation of parliamentarians in the process of european standardisation. worse, it supports the achievement of the single market in services through european or, where appropriate, wto standardisation of services. i am voting against this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the regulation to modernise the european standardisation process by simplifying the current system at administrative and financial level, while ensuring a high level of transparency. the text aims in particular to improve the use of standards in the services and information and communication technology sectors. these new provisions will give european companies faster access to standard solutions for technical problems, thus reducing their production costs. these provisions will also allow for better compatibility with the international standardisation system. the text will thus help to improve the competitiveness of european enterprises and stimulate growth. the commission estimated that standards have an impact on eu growth of more than €35 billion per year. during the discussions, i paid particular attention to the involvement of smes in the development of standards, as well as consumers - especially vulnerable consumers - to ensure that the views of end-users are taken into account and that products meet their needs. the final text seems to me to be fairly balanced, and i support it. the regulation will enter into force at the beginning of 2013.
in writing. to ensure optimum food safety, all cattle are monitored from birth to slaughter and must wear earrings with a reference number. this is called meat traceability. given the progress made in electronic identification technology, my report proposes the gradual and harmonised development of this technology, on a voluntary basis and therefore only for cattle farmers who wish to do so. in five years' time, we will take stock of this development. we will then see whether it is appropriate to make electronic identification compulsory in place of conventional identification by earrings. as regards the other part of this text, namely the labelling of beef, my report recommends simplifying the procedure for the use of optional particulars on meat packages. this may include information on the breed of the animal or the breeding method. too often the european union is perceived as a constraint. the european parliament called for the labelling of beef to be simplified for farmers and operators in the beef sector. i shall now begin negotiations with the european ministers.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the electronic identification of bovine animals. the extension of this technological mechanism will strengthen the current system for tracing cattle and food by making the system faster and more accurate. it also aims to make progress in reducing administrative burdens and improving disease prevention. in the long term, this type of innovation contributes to the competitiveness of the sector, and innovation is welcome in this sense.
in writing. i voted in favour of this parliament position for negotiations with the council because it seems to me to strike the right balance between respect for producers and modernisation of bovine identification and meat labelling. we must of course ensure simple and practical traceability and better consumer choice, which is why we must encourage the electronic identification of cattle, which makes it possible to streamline these processes. but we must not forget that we are in a time of crisis: we must not force the producers to make too costly investments, when they already offer us the best sanitation in the world! it would be irresponsible to subject small producers to such a non-urgent expense when they are already very weak from the current economic situation. as far as meat labelling is concerned, it is important to combat excessive administration: as long as the information is true and verifiable, producers must be able to specify elements that can help consumers in their choices. it is right to harmonize the situation between beef and other meats.
in writing. in the run-up to the negotiations with eu ministers responsible for agriculture, the european parliament has clarified its position on the electronic identification of cattle. progress has been made in the identification of cattle, but it is still imperfect. we have to be careful not to let the market fail. it was therefore essential that they should not be discouraged by increasingly burdensome bureaucratic rules coming from brussels. the electronic identification of cattle will therefore only concern voluntary farmers. in five years' time, a review will be carried out to assess whether compulsory electronic identification of bovine animals should be introduced. as regards labelling, the compulsory statements on the origin of the animals will not be changed. the european parliament, however, calls for the optional quality claims for beef (breed, breeding method, etc.) to be simplified and brought into line with the labelling rules for other types of meat.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague sophie auconie, which was adopted by a large majority. i'm glad you did. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. the report by my colleague sophie auconie on the electronic identification of cattle was approved by our assembly. i welcome the adoption of this text, which i supported, because it guarantees better control of the mechanisms in place. it also improves consumer confidence while ensuring that the administrative burden on producers is reduced. the report by mrs auconie opens up a great deal of work by advocating simplification of the labelling of beef and the generalization of the electronic identification of these animals.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on electronic identification of bovine animals, which will allow for better traceability of beef without imposing a disproportionate burden on the sector, as it is a voluntary measure. however, electronic identification is a major technological advance towards greater food safety.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i am convinced that my colleague sophie auconie has succeeded in finding a balanced and constructive position on the rules on the identification of bovine animals. the current traceability of cattle was introduced following the mad cow crisis in 1996, which revealed the need for full traceability from fork to fork. the traceability system for cattle as it currently exists is functioning. it is considered simple and well accepted in the field. however, in order to adapt this identification to technical innovations, the regulation provides for a gradual and harmonised development of this technology for voluntary breeders only. a review will be carried out in 5 years, giving farmers time to adapt, to assess the desirability of making electronic identification chips mandatory.
in writing. i was very pleased to see the rejection of the requirement for electronic identification of cattle, supported by some members who had clearly lost sight of the interests of farmers. this measure had aroused the indignation and concern of the farmers, which i shared and which had led me to speak to the commission to inform it of this incomprehensible situation. the additional costs and administrative burdens of this technique would have led to the disappearance of many farms, especially small farms and those in mountain areas, which would not have been able to comply with this obligation, although they are an essential part of our heritage, our rural fabric and biodiversity. while the strengthening of the legal arsenal can be understood in the light of the requirements of traceability and food safety, from the stable to the plate, it cannot be done at the expense of the freedom inherent in the profession of livestock farmer, especially since traditional techniques (tattoos, plastic loops) have demonstrated their reliability and durability. i therefore welcome the fact that, even with a small majority, the optional nature of electronic identification of cattle is now the rule and that this is being developed on a purely voluntary basis.
in writing. the european parliament has adopted new amendments to european pharmacovigilance legislation to prevent harmful medicines from being placed on the market within the european union. many people remember the scandal of the ombudsman, and the legislator had to intervene to ensure the safety of european citizens. by removing all room for manoeuvre for the states, the emergency procedure now takes on an automatic character as the commission had wished. in addition, the level of transparency required of companies has been greatly increased, requiring them to justify any voluntary withdrawal of a medicinal product or refusal to renew it.
in writing. while the ombudsman case has highlighted the serious gaps that remain in the field of drug safety, i welcome the agreement at first reading that we have approved today. this pharmacovigilance package meets an additional safety requirement. this requires an amendment to the 2001 directive to strengthen the legal framework: creating an automatic emergency procedure, strengthening the obligation of transparency for companies or providing for a blacklist of medicines subject to additional surveillance. it is the innovations of this reform which, it is to be hoped, will be able to overcome the shortcomings and strengthen the reliability of the european medicines system.
in writing. i voted in favour of the 2010 amendment to the european pharmacovigilance directive. this revision follows the mediator scandal. what does the european parliament want? in concrete terms, we want to strengthen the obligations in the event of withdrawal of a medicinal product: any withdrawal in a member state will now have to be notified and justified to all european health authorities. in the event of a suspected health risk, the withdrawal will be accompanied by an evaluation procedure to anticipate the possible consequences of a malfunction. we don't want to wait for the emergency to solve the problems. finally, as we voted in france, all medicines subject to increased surveillance will be freely available on a publicly available list. we believe that this duty of transparency is essential if we are to restore confidence between citizens, health authorities and pharmaceutical companies.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on pharmacovigilance. this monitoring mechanism, which was implemented by the commission and the supervisory authorities in 2001, was reformed in 2010, partly as a result of the ombudsman case. i particularly support the following measures: the creation of an emergency procedure which is automatic as soon as a medicinal product is withdrawn from the market; the introduction of a new trigger mechanism for the emergency procedure; introduction of a transparency obligation for companies (which must declare whether there are safety reasons behind the voluntary withdrawal of a medicinal product); the commission will also be preparing a comprehensive list of medicinal products subject to additional monitoring.
in writing. it is at european level that we must detect, assess and prevent adverse reactions to medicines placed on the market in the european union. following the ombudsman case, the european commission carried out a 'stress test' which identified weaknesses in the current legislation. this work has resulted in these revisions. the improvements made today are many: they include the introduction of an automatic emergency procedure, the creation of a new trigger mechanism for the emergency procedure and the clarification of the transparency obligations of companies. the european regulation today marks a significant step towards greater health security for europeans, and we welcome it.
in writing. the mediator health scandal has at least served to raise awareness of the urgent need to improve pharmacovigilance in europe, i.e. the monitoring of medicines and the prevention of the risk of potential or known adverse effects resulting from their use. in 2009, france decided to withdraw this drug from the servier laboratory - which caused the death of an estimated 500 to 2,000 people - while, as early as 2003, it had been withdrawn from the market in spain and italy, at the request of the laboratory. now, as soon as a medicinal product is voluntarily withdrawn from the market in one member state, the precautionary principle will apply and the medicinal product will be withdrawn temporarily or permanently from other european countries. companies will also be required to report whether safety reasons have led to the voluntary withdrawal of a medicinal product or the non-renewal of its licence.
in writing. because it is essential to ensure optimal protection for european patients, the union must do everything possible to ensure that pharmaceutical advances and economic activities find a good balance. it is important to learn from each of the past mistakes and thus to adapt legislation as much as possible to enhance safety for all. that is why i voted in favour of this text which, following the mediator case, strengthens the protection of our fellow citizens.
in writing. following the mediator scandal, a drug responsible for between 1000 and 2000 deaths in france, there was a particular urgency to review the pharmacovigilance systems in the european union, which were marked by profound shortcomings. in this sense i support the work of my colleague linda mcavan on better detection of dangerous medicines and accelerated withdrawal from the market. we have a duty to provide for mechanisms to prevent other harmful medicines from being marketed in the european union. in addition, the question of the influence of laboratories and the pressure they exert on the administrative authorities must also be asked.
in writing. in 2010, the european institutions agreed to revise the rules governing pharmacovigilance with a view to implementing the legislation in 2012. the new legislation aims to strengthen the coordinating role of the european medicines agency and to improve the system for detecting 'signals' of potential problems and for monitoring at european level. since then, the mediator scandal has led to further strengthening of pharmacovigilance measures. this is the conclusion reached by the stress tests carried out in the wake of the scandal. the european parliament has set itself the objective of improving the health protection of european citizens. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. however, to be more effective, better cooperation at european level is necessary.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text on pharmacovigilance at european level. in 2010, the european system was already significantly modernised to allow for increased monitoring of medicines placed on the market. nevertheless, the stress test following the mediator case showed that the system could still be improved. the new provisions are therefore positive in terms of patient safety.
in writing. following the mediator scandal, a drug potentially involved in more than 500 deaths in france, the european union conducted 'stress tests' on its pharmacovigilance legislation to ensure that it was well adapted. the commission has presented new measures to improve patient safety by adapting the way in which adverse reactions to an authorised medicinal product are detected, refining risk assessment and improving responses to such risks. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which improves the commission's proposal by strengthening the coordinating role of the european medicines agency and the detection of risk signals for a medicinal product.
in writing. the european parliament has adopted new amendments to european pharmacovigilance legislation to prevent harmful medicines from being placed on the market within the european union. many people remember the scandal of the ombudsman, and the legislator had to intervene to ensure the safety of european citizens. by removing all room for manoeuvre for the states, the emergency procedure now takes on an automatic character, as the commission had wished. in addition, the level of transparency required of companies has been greatly increased, requiring them to justify any voluntary withdrawal of a medicinal product or refusal to renew it.
