in writing. because it is essential to ensure optimal protection for european patients, the union must do everything possible to ensure that pharmaceutical advances and economic activities strike a good balance. it is important to learn from each of the past mistakes and thus to adapt legislation as much as possible to enhance safety for all. that is why i voted in favour of this text, which, following the ombudsman's case, strengthens the protection of our fellow citizens.
in writing. the european union had to respond to the ombudsman scandal which claimed hundreds of victims, due to the lack of sufficiently effective alert and response mechanisms to a dangerous drug. i voted in favour of this amendment to european pharmacovigilance legislation because it seems to me to be moving in the right direction: towards transparency and control. the three main measures introduced seem to me to be very important: the real reasons for the withdrawal of a medicinal product from a country by a company will be known, these medicinal products will be systematically subjected to an emergency assessment, which will make it possible to know its dangers, and finally a symbol on the packaging of the medicinal product will enable patients and practitioners to be informed when the medicinal product has been the subject of a further safety study. as part of the organisation of the medicines market, in which the union has competence, these measures make it possible to contribute at union level to ensuring that a health crisis such as the one we experienced with the ombudsman does not happen again.
in writing. the marketing of products in europe which are hazardous to health, such as distilbene, isomeride or mediator ink, and the scandal which this has caused, have made european states aware of the need to amend existing community legislation. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it is urgent to correct the shortcomings of the system through a new mechanism. the new system will introduce three major changes: an emergency assessment when a company decides not to renew a marketing authorisation, a notification requirement when a company decides not to renew a marketing authorisation and the creation of a consumer information leaflet on the packaging of medicines that have undergone a post-authorisation safety study.
in writing. preserving our oceans is one of the central objectives of european environmental policy. as a member of the committee on the environment, i welcome the support given by the european parliament to this text. by 2020, sulphur emissions from shipping will have to be divided by 7 in order to reduce pollution. their residual fuels contain on average 2700 times more sulphides than road fuels. this reduction is also very important from the point of view of public health. this reduction is expected to improve air quality and reduce the number of premature deaths from air pollution by some 50 000.
in writing. with our commitments on global warming by 2020, the european union must act on all pollution. the report sets an ambitious course to reduce marine pollution by strengthening fuel standards. this will drastically reduce sulphur levels. this is excellent news for environmentalists and further proof of the added value of the european parliament's and, more generally, the european union's action in the field of the environment.
in writing. i voted in favour of new standards to reduce sulphur emissions from shipping by 90% by 2020. these standards are more stringent and are in line with those adopted in 2008 by the international maritime organization (imo).
in writing. air pollution is unfortunately not only caused by emissions from the earth. the fuel for ships is a huge polluter, and has a huge impact on the environment. that is why we have approved the legislation which has been agreed with the member states. it sets new, stricter limits on the sulphur content of marine fuels, which will improve air quality along europe's coasts. by 2020, the general sulphur limit for fuels in european waters will be raised from 3.5% to 0.5%. fuels used in the baltic sea, the north sea and the english channel - the sulphur emission control areas in europe (escas) - will have to meet the new international standards of 0.1% by 2015. cleaner fuels and technologies exist. it is time to promote and use them wherever possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which aims to introduce new limit values for the sulphur content of marine fuels. this is a real step forward in the protection of biodiversity. the adoption of this text will, in particular, improve the protection of european citizens against the disposal of toxic products.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the current emissions from ships from marine fuels are high in sulphur. they contribute to air pollution in the form of sulphur dioxide and particulate matter which are harmful to human health and lead to acidification. the draft directive aims to substantially reduce these emissions by making the most recent rules of the international maritime organisation binding in the eu. the costs of the new sulphur emission reduction standards could have a negative impact on the competitiveness of the sector and lead to a shift from maritime to land transport. therefore, member states will be able to grant aid to operators in accordance with the applicable rules on state aid. vessels which fail to comply with these new limitations will have to pay fines to the national authorities which should be sufficiently high to avoid paying them being more advantageous than complying with the rules.
in writing. the european parliament voted this week on the report on the marpol regulation which sets maximum levels of sulphur in marine fuels. i voted in favour of this text, which is the result of months of parliamentary investment. i also made my contribution by voting for an amendment which will give france the opportunity to renegotiate the requirements laid down in the regulation, which would have very serious consequences for our shipowners if they were maintained. the report was approved by a very large majority, with 606 votes in favour and only 55 against. i welcome the adoption of this text, which is effective in protecting the environment while allowing governments to negotiate the directive in order to obtain adaptations adapted to specific local situations.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the prevention of pollution from ships. the fuel from ships is polluting the air because of its high sulphur content. the maximum sulphur content limit should be reduced from 0.1% to 1% instead of the current level. in order to avoid the negative impact of this more costly measure on the competitiveness of the sector, member states will be able to grant public aid to operators.
in writing. the deterioration of air quality caused by the use of hydrocarbons and the impact of this consumption on the environment and human health are no longer to be demonstrated. ships burn heavy, unrefined fuels that pollute. the ecological transition requires the fleet to be adapted to environmental requirements. this transition cannot be achieved without the appropriate support. the report merely states the obvious requirement, without specifying the amount. hundreds of jobs are threatened. i abstain because i support the proposed timetable for reducing sulphur pollution, but i am concerned that there is no substantial aid to implement the measures needed to do so.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the sulphur content of marine fuels. the eu is proposing to reduce the sulphur content of emissions from ships in the baltic sea and the north sea to 0.1% by 2015. it thus transposed into community law an obligation laid down by the international maritime organisation (imo), which was difficult to ignore. the 2015 deadline, however, seems to be very premature in view of the economic and technical constraints it will impose on passenger carriers in particular. the fear is that some ships will have to be withdrawn from the fleets because they will not have the means to adapt to the new requirements, and that hundreds of jobs will be lost as a result, in an economic context where passenger transport companies are experiencing difficulties. however, negotiations in parliament have allowed the authorisation of state aid to help operators in this transition. it is also recalled that member states can still apply to the imo for delays to enable their fleets to be equipped on time. these various safeguard measures have therefore led me to approve the transposition of the european union's international obligations into this directive.
in writing. the votes in parliamentary committees had led to the adoption of untenable positions, and i welcome the fact that the trilogue negotiations have led to a more balanced version of the text. we must not lose sight of the major issues facing the shipping industry and the considerable impact this directive will have on the industry. of course, we must combat transport pollution and reduce the ecological footprint of all modes. but not at any price! the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's fishing fleet is not disrupted by the introduction of new fishing vessels. i had stressed the need for accompanying measures, as a corollary to the reduction in sulphur levels in maritime transport. the commission must now propose the practical version of the toolkit it has announced. i'll be extremely careful about that. the eu is the world's leading maritime power and a world leader in the fight for the environment, proof that transport and sustainability are not incompatible, quite the contrary. we must put in place a thoughtful and flexible policy which no longer pits economy and ecology against each other.
in writing. the european parliament adopted the commission's proposal to amend a regulation clarifying the conditions for the payment of decoupled aid to wine growers. in the uncertain context of the reform of the common agricultural policy (cap), it is important to leave room for manoeuvre to member states so that they always have the necessary flexibility to decide to make additional payments, especially in the event of crises in this sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. in the context of the new cap, i support the commission's proposal that member states should decide, before the end of the year, to transfer funds from their wine sector allocations to the single payment scheme. however, caution should be exercised in the programming of aid, given that the new cap is currently being negotiated.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which allows for greater flexibility in the allocation of aid to the wine sector. it is more important than ever to give our full support to this sector and to those who promote our terroir around the world and help preserve noble traditions.
in writing. the commission proposes that member states grant decoupled support to wine growers under the direct payments scheme. in practical terms, this will allow member states to transfer funds from the 'vin' envelope to the cap direct payments system (first pillar). this is a positive development, since payments will now be made for an indefinite period, which will enable farmers to predict their income over time and thus to gain stability. the introduction of this system will, however, require some adjustments. this resolution will allow member states to test this new system for a period of one year before finally implementing it if they so wish. that is why i voted for this legislative resolution.
in writing. at a time when our parliament is setting the future of our main policies, we are faced with the question of the support model for wine growers. by 2015, member states will have to choose between the single payment scheme for all farmers and the mobilisation of funds for wine growers, which they could previously have pooled. i have of course supported this measure, which seems to me the best way of recognising the specific nature of the wine-growing profession and of providing them with appropriate support in a context of changes in the sector. france had already made this choice, since it mainly uses the specific support scheme for wine growers. this reform will not therefore upset french viticulture, but will have the advantage of ensuring greater transparency and predictability as regards the amounts and nature of the aid paid. i welcome the adoption of this report, which also gives me the opportunity to reiterate my commitment to plantation rights. this regulatory instrument, which, by the way, costs nothing to the taxpayer, guarantees the optimum quality of our wines and a stable income for the winegrowers. this system must be preserved, it is a commitment i have made and it must be maintained.
in writing. an effective single market requires the greatest possible simplification of administrative barriers. this is done with the internal market information system (imi) which promotes the exchange of information and cross-border administrative cooperation in different languages. the european parliament wanted to vote in favour of a new legal basis for this system. by appointing national coordinators, it hopes to further improve the system and increase its transparency, with a view to extending it to other areas in the future.
in writing. the internal market information system (imi) is a computer network which facilitates the exchange of information between national administrations. so far, this administrative cooperation has applied only to the vocational qualifications and services directives. the current legal framework limits any extension. convinced of the benefits of imi, i voted in favour of the bielan report, which seeks to consolidate the rules governing its use, particularly those relating to the protection of personal data. any future extension of imi will be under the control of the european parliament through co-decision.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on administrative cooperation through the internal market information system. imi provides an online application for cross-border information exchange and administrative cooperation in different languages for the benefit of 600 european authorities. the report aims to enhance the transparency and legal certainty of the data recorded and to ensure a well-defined data retention period. i support the idea that the system can be extended to other union acts as long as these extensions can be systematically made the subject of a proposal for a regulation.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this text, which will ensure and frame a good exchange of information within the eu member states and the regions of its territories. this will make it easier for national, regional and local authorities to cooperate, improving services to european citizens and increasing transparency within the internal market.
in writing. i voted in favour of this relative report. the internal market information system (imi) was designed to improve the functioning of the single market by providing, since 2008, a fast and secure online application for the exchange of information and cross-border administrative cooperation in different languages. in the single market act of 27 october 2010, the extension of the imi to other sectors is considered as one of the essential conditions for working towards better governance of the single market. in its report, the european parliament has shown its willingness to consolidate the rules applicable to the use of imi into a single legal instrument, thus enhancing transparency and legal certainty, and facilitating a future extension of the system to cover other areas of union law. at present, imi is mainly used in the field of recognition of professional qualifications.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the internal market information system (imi). imi is currently used for the exchange of information for the recognition of professional qualifications and for services in the internal market. the text adopted will allow the system to be extended to cover cooperation in other areas of eu law.
in writing. this report rejects the possibilities for delegation of powers requested by the european commission. it introduces some improvements in the protection of personal data, but these are too weak. the possibility of keeping such data for more than six years is maintained. third countries will continue to have access to this data without the citizens' knowledge. i shall abstain only in support of the parliamentary scrutiny rightly requested by the committee on the internal market.
in writing. i voted in favour of the regulation on administrative cooperation through the internal market information system (imi), which is a tool to improve the efficiency of administrative cooperation between competent authorities in the application of union legislation. i stress the importance of the protection of personal data in imi and i fully support parliament's efforts to increase the transparency of procedures, particularly with regard to the essential functionalities of the system and the categories of data that can be processed there. the amendment to the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications, which we are currently working on, proposes to make the use of imi compulsory, which will reduce costs, overcome linguistic and administrative problems and speed up the procedure for the recognition of a professional title. this is an effective way of strengthening the governance of the single market, which i fully support.
in writing. directive 2003/49/ec, as amended on many occasions, regulates the common tax regime applicable to interest and royalty payments between associated companies of different member states. for the sake of clarity, it is therefore necessary to simplify its use and to remove tax obstacles to the proper functioning of the internal market. crossborder interest and royalty payments are taxed more heavily than domestic transactions. where transactions are purely domestic, the payee of the payment is subject to corporation tax in his country of tax residence. in the case of european payments, they may also be subject to withholding tax in the member state making the payment. the aim of the directive is to put crossborder interest and royalty payments on an equal footing with domestic payments by eliminating double taxation, red tape and cash flow problems for the companies concerned.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on a common tax system for interest and royalty payments between associated companies in different member states. in these times of economic and financial crisis, it is urgent to make every effort to reduce tax evasion and avoidance as much as possible, which represent a considerable shortfall for the member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which seeks to improve the common tax system of the european union for companies established in the member states. the text will, in particular, make it possible to strengthen the fight against tax evasion and tax evasion and will limit double taxation within the member states. as the european union faces a difficult economic environment, it is important that it protects itself against all forms of loss of tax revenue from business, so that we can contribute together to the objectives of reducing our public deficits.
in writing. the report has the merit of highlighting the danger of tax evasion which the commission's proposal entails. but that does not mean that he gets all the consequences. if it refuses to lower the participation rate of a company to 10% so that it can be considered as a company associated with another company, it nevertheless maintains a very low tax rate for the companies concerned (70% of the average legal corporate tax rate applicable in the member states, or just 16.24%; this is much less than the vat rates that the troika imposes on the peoples of europe). the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. i vote against it.
in writing. the resolution's theoretical aim is to combat double taxation of companies by reducing taxes on interest payments and royalties paid between associated companies in different member states. in reality, the resolution is intended to facilitate access to tax exemptions. indeed, 'associated companies' enjoy exceptional exemptions on the payment of interest and royalties between them. this proposal broadens this category. the resolution also makes too little mention of tax fraud and evasion, which undermine the european union, and of tax competition between member states. the amendment tabled by the gue/ngl introducing a minimum corporate tax rate was rejected by a majority of 362 to 296. i therefore voted against this motion for a resolution, which only increases the tax privileges of companies to the detriment of european citizens. it does not solve the structural problems of the union's taxation, which is the key to the crisis that is unfolding before our eyes and which is hitting the peoples of europe so hard, especially those in southern europe.
in writing. in the commission's 2013 work programme, adopted by the european parliament, we wanted to express our expectations for the future of the eu. we want to start negotiations to achieve a real economic and monetary union leading to a stronger political union with more democratic accountability. it is also essential to promote growth initiatives and better controls of eu funds spending at national level.
in writing. in france, as in europe, 2013 is a crucial year. after several years of crisis, the european economy is now at a turning point which requires us to redouble our efforts to get out of this slump. in detailing our roadmap for 2013, the european parliament calls on the european commission to act immediately to consolidate economic and monetary union, build up the banking union and relaunch employment policies. i voted for this report, but i can only regret the fact that there was no agreement on the redemption fund, which is sorely lacking in order to get out of this crisis structurally.
in writing. the challenges facing the european union require firm and determined action by the commission to finally emerge from the crisis and return to the path of growth and solidarity. it is in the spirit of this call for a resolute commitment, which takes particular account of the needs of the most vulnerable, that i have supported this resolution. the rise of extremes, euroscepticism and populist discourse should especially alert us to the particularly serious state of our europe and the crisis of legitimacy it faces in the eyes of our fellow citizens. the same applies when we see, helpless, the return of an intergovernmental logic that is surreptitiously invited to the negotiating table. so let us stop paying each other with words and start paying each other with concrete actions. in this sense, let us demand that the european framework for national roma integration strategies be a legally binding instrument rather than an empty shell. it is only by having the courage to face these challenges that europe can regain the confidence of our citizens.
in writing. this joint resolution by the christian right, the liberals, the social democrats and the european greens is distressing. these four groups accept without a word that the commission should continue to have prerogatives which should be those of parliamentarians, such as, in the first place, the power of legislative initiative. they merely 'urge' or 'invite' this unelected body to table the legislative proposals they themselves would have tabled if they had had real legislative power. but the worst part is the content of these suggestions. not content with endorsing the europe 2020 strategy, the european semester, the euro plus pact or the employment and growth pact, these groups insist on the establishment of the single market for services, the single energy market, the maintenance of the carbon market and the fight against protectionism. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted against the joint resolution by the epp, s&d, alde and greens/efa groups on the commission's work programme for 2013. this resolution supports the current economic policies, the dramatic consequences of which are unfortunately all too well known, particularly in the social field. it thus urged the commission to grant more powers to the ecb, supported the austerity policy (two-pack, european semester, deficit reduction) and professed its adherence to the old liberal principles (opening up markets, combating protectionism, multiplying free trade agreements). the gue/ngl is promoting radically different proposals. we want to fundamentally change the role of the ecb and put an end to its independence, to put in place a european investment programme, a framework directive on an adequate minimum income, and a european guarantee for every young person in the union to be offered a job or further training in the event of unemployment. these are the proposals we have put forward in an alternative resolution.
in writing. tissues and stem cells are increasingly playing a central role in treating certain diseases. the european parliament has adopted a report proposing to increase the stocks of umbilical cord blood and stem cells through a highly regulated and unpaid system. these resources could help research into treatments for many childhood diseases. these free, voluntary, and strictly supervised donations will come mostly from deceased persons. by encouraging the establishment of common standards between public and private donation banks, this will facilitate the exchange and thus the availability of tissues and cells.
in writing. the european parliament has taken a position on voluntary and unpaid donation of tissues and cells following the european commission's second evaluation report on the subject. this is an own-initiative report which expresses the views of the members, and not a legislative text which regulates a sensitive area which is the exclusive competence of the member states. in france, we revised the bioethics law in 2011. in this report we remind you that donations must remain voluntary and not for profit. we also call on the member states to ensure full transparency in this area. we also encourage donation and collection of cord blood, which is useful for transplantation. as regards sensitive issues relating to research on embryonic stem cells, in vitro fertilisation or cloning from stem cells for research purposes, we would point out that the best decisions can be taken at member state level.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on voluntary and unpaid tissue and cell donation. i support the rapporteur's wish that donations should become more and more voluntary and not for profit in a transparent environment. the monetization of human body products is prohibited in france, unlike other countries where a genuine trade has been established.
in writing. i voted for the yannakoudakis report. it reinforces the view that donations should be voluntary and made without profit in a transparent environment. i believe that altruism is essential when it comes to donating tissue and cells. compensation by member states should therefore be managed with caution, and non-financial benefits should be considered. to help crossborder cooperation work, i support the introduction of strict controls to ensure maximum traceability in the donation chain.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which recalls, if it is still necessary, that organ donation must be voluntary and not for profit. organ donation saves lives and brings real hope for a better future for many families. this gift, if properly managed, is an opportunity for many of our citizens. however, the press has too often reported on the existence of an illicit parallel trade in organs from well-identified countries. every european citizen must have access to the new medical techniques for donation, while being protected from illegal practices such as organ trafficking.
in writing. i thought it was important to vote in favour of this resolution which reaffirms certain principles concerning tissue and cell donation. it is ethical, but many member states do not take it into account: donations of tissues and cells should be voluntary, unpaid and, with few exceptions, anonymous. these ethical failings in some states take place in a context of regular revelations of cases of trafficking in human products. the first reason for my vote is to send a signal to the member states to put an end to this traffic. the scope of this resolution thus goes beyond ethical issues and concerns issues of public health and the fight against criminal behaviour. the resolution also encourages mechanisms for better european and international cooperation to better manage the growing need for human tissues and cells for innovative therapies, which is also a major public health issue.
in writing. i particularly support this report which reiterates an absolute opposition to the payment of donated tissue and cells. these donations are essential for transplantation and for the care of many patients. despite the structures and information campaigns, about half of the member states still report regular shortages of tissues and cells, including bone marrow and gametes. to date, more than 20,000 cord blood cell transplants have been performed worldwide in the last 20 years to treat leukemia and lymphoma, genetic diseases, and immune deficiencies. but at birth, too few mothers are encouraged by maternity wards to donate cord blood. it would take a willingness on the part of the member states to see cord blood no longer regarded as hospital waste but as a real resource for research. public and private cord blood and stem cell banks should cooperate more closely. a regulatory framework for member states will have to be found quickly to ensure that these establishments operate in a transparent and secure manner. institutions must respect the principles of equity in access to care and solidarity.
in writing. the principle of voluntary and unpaid donation of tissues and cells is an absolute principle which cannot be called into question. however, the shortage of cells and tissues cannot be ignored as the number of patients requiring immediate needs and the list of applicants continues to grow. donations are essential for transplants and for the care of patients with heart disease, leukemia, genetic diseases, etc. the structures and information campaigns exist, but they are insufficient in different countries. better cooperation between member states is therefore essential to improve crossborder donation. the institutions must encourage the donation of tissues and cells, including cord blood. it's by changing perceptions, by demonstrating that the umbilical cord is a resource for research, that we can save lives.
in writing. stem cells are playing an increasingly important role in treating various diseases. the report proposing to increase the stocks of umbilical cord blood and stem cells through a regulated and unpaid system was adopted on tuesday 11 september. this report, which i voted in favour of, states that donations of tissue or cells must be voluntary, unpaid and transparent. the report also calls for common standards for public and private donation banks. this would facilitate the exchange and thus the availability of tissues and cells. the european parliament's adoption of this directive will make it possible to regulate organ donation even more closely, in order to avoid any costly trafficking or transfer.
in writing. this motion for a resolution sets out the broad guidelines for future regulations on tissue and cell donation. it reaffirms in particular the necessary principles of free and anonymity for all donations of cells and tissues. as stem cells become one of the great hopes of modern medicine, a clear position on the subject is essential. the establishment of a regulatory framework would ensure the safety of both donors and recipients. but this resolution opens the door to the creation of private cell and tissue banks in which individuals can store their own cells and tissues. in practice, cord blood from an anonymous donor is used and transplanted 100 times more often. it is therefore a clear breach of the individual protection (and ultimately selfish) that can only be done at the expense of anonymous donations. i therefore abstained on this motion for a resolution.
in writing. enhancing women's participation in the economic cycle is a central issue in my political commitment. as president of the association 'women at the centre', i can only welcome the support given by the european parliament to this own-initiative report. by promoting the positive role that women can play in decision-making bodies, the european parliament is once again demonstrating its commitment to gender equality.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on the role of women in the green economy. the report aims to encourage women's participation in new green jobs. thus, activities producing goods or services that are conducive to environmental protection, or eco-activities, are seen as a way of achieving greater gender pay equality and reducing economic and social disparities between men and women.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it is essential to look at the question of the role of women in a sustainable economy. why would you do that? because they are the ones who are on the front lines today and are paying a particularly heavy price in the face of the devastating effects of the ecological crisis. it is worth recalling that it mainly affects women in rural areas, who are impoverished by soil degradation, those in megacities who are forced to live at a pace incompatible with respect for human rights and who are exploited in degrading conditions, and women and their children who are victims of displacement due to conflicts and climate change. women are still too often excluded from sustainable development policies, even though they play a vital role in maintaining an agro-ecology that preserves biodiversity and strengthens social cohesion through their collective organisational practices. women have solutions to the crises we face, let's stop ignoring them.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report by my swedish colleague mikael gustafsson of the gue/ngl. the report stresses that the current economic and ecological problems are being tackled in a primarily technical way, ignoring that the solutions lie in a drastic change in social justice and a sustainable economy. women are both the first victims and the true pioneers in this field. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union's energy policy. the report calls on the member states to draw up action plans to enable more women to choose training and work in fields where a large proportion of future green jobs are open to them (engineering, natural sciences, information technology) but which are, de facto, largely closed to them for the time being. women's access to micro-credit for small businesses, or the development of childcare infrastructure and retirement homes to enable women to reconcile their personal and professional lives, are some examples.
in writing. this report gives an overview of the situation of women in the service sector, where they are traditionally in the majority. however, this observation conceals a very different reality. women are often part-time, excluded from managerial positions and subject to unjustified pay differentials. immigrant workers and parental leave are issues on which the european parliament has voted in favour so that the situation of women can finally be better taken into account in all the countries of the european union.
in writing. gender inequalities in the service sector are significant. this is a well-known phenomenon: women work in the sector in large numbers, sometimes in low-skilled jobs, and the proportion of women working part-time is disproportionate to that of men. these often unsuccessful part-time jobs are the concrete expression of a fragmentation of the labour market and the precarious position of workers, especially women. we must take this into account in the development of current public policies, both in employment and education. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union. finally, it should be remembered that equal pay for men and women has not yet been achieved, despite the fact that this issue has been present in the european debate for 30 years... equality is still a struggle in our respective countries.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on working conditions for women in the service sector. the under-representation of women in decision-making positions and the large gender pay gap are commonly observed. yet little progress has been made. at present, 80% of women's jobs are in the service sector: legislation must be focused on this sector if improvements in working conditions are to be expected. it is also urgent that states put in place easy-to-use assessment tools for different jobs in order to make equal pay a reality.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of my colleague iratxe garcía pérez' report, which perfectly highlights the profoundly inequitable characteristics of the organisation of services in our european societies. it is very regrettable that the employment of women in services is still deeply marked by stereotypes that are firmly rooted in society, according to which they have the primary responsibility for the welfare of their families, with jobs considered as an extension of the domestic tasks performed on a daily basis, such as cleaning services, teaching, textile manufacturing, etc. the jobs occupied by women are for the most part flexible, parttime, low-skilled jobs with considerable wage differences, in short, almost universal precarious work which cannot be ignored. it is in this context that national and european authorities must be committed to combating gender stereotypes, particularly from an early age. the issue of the employment - or rather exploitation - of migrant women, particularly in the fields of domestic help or personal care, must also be the subject of the greatest attention of the public authorities.
in writing. the garcia pérez report was adopted by a large majority in plenary, with 528 votes in favour, 57 against and 33 abstentions. this own-initiative report highlights the main statistics on working conditions for women in the service sector in the eu: in 2010, more than 80% of women's jobs were in the service sector. women are overrepresented in flexible and parttime jobs, underrepresented in decision-making positions and have to face the issues of the wage gap. women also occupy a large proportion of undeclared jobs, particularly in domestic help and care for people. the report also expresses concern about the situation of immigrant and unreported women working in the service sector.
in writing. as a member of the committee on women's rights and gender equality, i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by mrs iratxe garcia perez on the working conditions of women in the service sector. with this text, the european parliament is highlighting a statistic that is rarely mentioned in the media: the share of women in the service sector, the sector which is the biggest drain on jobs in the european union. furthermore, these jobs are usually part-time and pay less than male jobs. in view of this, i can only welcome the adoption of this report by the european parliament, which encourages the member states to improve the working conditions of women in the service sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on working conditions for women in the service sector. women are largely represented in the service sector and are predominantly in parttime jobs. we must also combat the wage gap, which is on average 17.1% between men and women in the european union. there are various solutions for member states, such as the introduction of tax incentives and service vouchers to combat the shadow economy, or the adoption of labour market reintegration policies for the most vulnerable workers.
in writing. 83% of the female labour force work in services. it is therefore necessary to look again at the working conditions of women in this sector. we cannot stress enough the importance of the full integration of women into the labour market, by combating discrimination against them. women are the source of most of the precarious jobs and are underrepresented in management and executive positions. the first measure must be about remuneration. how can we justify the fact that women still earn 16% less than men? we urgently need to enforce the principle of equal pay for men and women for equal work. this discrimination is everywhere, even in the political sphere. if the european union does not give women the opportunity to develop their skills, it betrays its values and leaves the field open to the kind of obscurantism that unfortunately prevails in other parts of the world. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which calls on the european institutions and the member states to put an end to the glass ceiling faced by women in their careers and to adopt measures to improve the reconciliation of family and working life.
in writing. i voted for this report originally proposed by my group, the gue/ngl. it highlights the fact that women are the first victims of precariousness, a persistent feature of the labour market in all the member states of the european union. women account for nearly 80% of parttime work; women hold a majority of fixed-term contracts; women in the same jobs earn on average 16.4% less than their male counterparts, with a difference of 17.1% in the service sector. this report shows how material inequalities between men and women remain high, despite eu commitments in this area. the report therefore calls on the member states to improve working conditions for women, for example by ratifying without delay the international labour organisation's convention no 189 ('decent work for domestic workers') or by transforming precarious work in the service sector into stable work through various measures (introduction of a special scheme for the personal services sector to combat undeclared work, council's unblocking of the amendment of the directive on pregnant workers).
in writing. education and training are central to the europe 2020 strategy. in these times of high budgetary pressures across member states, it is crucial to maintain quality education systems by minimising early school leaving and encouraging mobility to acquire new skills. this report adopted by the european parliament aims to show that drastic cuts in education budgets would save money in the short term but would have much higher costs in the long term. this would risk having a low or unskilled labour force, unsuited to the needs of the labour market and indirectly causing a fall in member states' revenue. thus, it is crucial to focus our efforts on investing in early childhood education in order to limit the social cost of early school leaving and school failure.
in writing. in the difficult times we are living in, it is important to remember that investing in human capital, especially in the younger generations, should not be seen as a cost but as an investment in the future, in sustainable growth and an inclusive society. it should be stressed that investing in the development of both knowledge and skills is essential to improve the social, civic and occupational integration of learners and to reduce unemployment. the report also highlights the role of employers in making lifelong learning a reality by promoting the benefits of continuing training and improving its accessibility to all workers. this is a necessity, while at the moment the rights to training are still under exploited.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on education, training and europe 2020. in a context of economic instability and an ageing population in the european union, education and training must be key areas of investment in order to combat unemployment and improve access to employment for young people. the heterogeneity of the education and training systems of the member states can be both a strength and a barrier: a strength from which we can draw and exchange expertise and good practice to combat school drop-out for example, but also an obstacle to the coordination of training and certification systems and to the transnational mobility of learners. i also believe that there is an urgent need to modernise school and vocational guidance programmes in order to improve the balance between training and employment in european companies.
in writing. i fully supported the own-initiative report by my colleague mary honeyball because i believe that we must now propose concrete actions which are proportionate to the seriousness of youth unemployment which is currently affecting many member states and which exposes them to an unprecedented risk of social exclusion and poverty. first, an increased level of skills and knowledge is needed to limit this phenomenon. in addition, an additional effort is needed to inform young people about the training available, especially about the possibilities of training in a country other than their own. but that is not all, we also know that many young people have too many degrees and are struggling to find work. finally, another difficulty is the situation of young people who do not have sufficient training and who drop out of school. education is an investment, this must be strongly emphasised, and member states should consider access to lifelong learning as essential, despite some budgetary 'clean-ups'.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my colleague mary honeyball entitled 'education, training and europe 2020'. with this report, we in the european parliament are showing our determination to promote the education of young children, which must be a priority, not only from a moral point of view but also from an economic point of view. it is clear that the current economic climate is not conducive to such investments. the current economic situation is characterised by widespread austerity policies affecting all budgetary lines, including education and training. yet the benefits of these investments are many: strengthening the future workforce, reducing future health care costs, reducing tax losses for governments. reducing early school leaving, strengthening support for higher education in lifelong learning and promoting transnational mobility for the acquisition of new skills are all objectives that i support with all my strength. i believe that this report contains proposals for the construction of a more harmonious society, and i am therefore delighted that all the political groups have approved this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on education, training and europe 2020, which recalls that young people are particularly affected by unemployment, which affects more than 20% of young europeans. alternative vocational training, for example, provides better access to the world of work thanks to the practical dimension it includes. the difficulty of young graduates in finding a job should lead the member states to analyse and assess the quality of their education systems so that they prepare effectively for the labour market by providing the opportunity for professional experience.
in writing. the report has the great merit of calling for public expenditure on education to be deducted from the calculation of the public deficit of the member states. i support this unprecedented request and hope to see this consideration extended to other public services. that is why i am voting for this text, despite the support for the europe 2020 strategy which i deplore.
in writing. i regret that the objectives for lifelong learning set by the european union in its europe 2020 strategy are still far from being achieved. i also regret that some member states are reducing the share of their budget allocated to education and vocational training, whereas the present period requires us to strengthen these policies. i am convinced that economic growth must be based primarily on education. i therefore fully endorse the resolution adopted by the european parliament, which calls on the member states to invest in education, training and research, with particular attention to young people and vulnerable people. efforts to establish a european system for the certification and recognition of qualifications are needed to improve mobility in both education and the labour market.
in writing. i support this report which warns member states of the disastrous economic and social consequences of school drop-out in the eu. the crisis seriously jeopardises the future of young people. youth unemployment rose from 15.5% in 2008 to 22.5% in 2012, while the proportion of young people aged 15-24 who are not in employment, education or training rose by two percentage points. in 2010, 53% of young people who left school early were unemployed. we ask the states to set themselves the objective of investing at least 2% of gdp in higher education and 3% in research. in addition, europe must achieve, by 2020, to increase the number of young people with a university education to 40% and to reduce school drop-out to less than 10%. this investment in education and training is absolutely necessary if the european union is to be able to compete with the new global economic powers.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on education, training and europe 2020. education and training are essential elements for achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and for europe's future growth. the current economic difficulties must not be used as a pretext for reducing the resources allocated to education and training. in order to guarantee investment for the future, the socialists proposed to exclude investment in education and training from the national deficit calculation of the budgetary pact. as the report points out, the cost of school failure is higher than that of the crisis. it is not a question of making short-term savings that will stymie future growth. for the same reasons, we encourage member states to devote at least 2% of their gdp to higher education for a knowledge-based economy. but the effort must also be directed towards the education and schooling of young children, a crucial step in the development of future workers and citizens.
in writing. the european audiovisual sector has to cope with the many changes in its market in recent years. the development of the internet must be seen as an opportunity to link content to online platforms while ensuring fair remuneration for authors. the european parliament's call for a genuine framework in this area must be heard. educating young people about new technologies, promoting the exchange and payment of works and allowing a balanced negotiation between authors, producers and consumers are all important issues for the future of this sector.

in writing. i welcome the adoption of the report by my colleague, jean-marie cavada, which allows for the improvement of the dissemination of audiovisual works on the internet. this will allow easier access to the various works for the public and their transnational dissemination. this greater accessibility of works will automatically lead to an increase in their popularity and thus in their audiences. this dissemination will not affect copyright as copyright is protected and recognised by the european parliament as a tool for defending creativity. thanks to this text, which i voted in favour of, photographs, films or other documents which are protected by copyright but whose owners cannot be identified could be made public throughout the european union. this legislation will allow everyone to have access to these "orphan works" and will advance the project of making this cultural heritage available online.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague jean-marie cavada on the dissemination of audiovisual works online in the eu. in this report, we, the members of the european parliament, insist on the need to implement the rules on the broadcasting, making available and viewing of european audiovisual works. the report also focuses on media and digital education for citizens of all ages, starting from an early age. i believe that at a time when the weight of new technologies is becoming increasingly important in our societies, it seems necessary to coordinate the rules governing all the measures implemented in connection with new technologies. these devices must be made available to all in a secure manner. that is why i welcome the fact that parliament is calling on the commission to act on the legal security of internet users and consumer protection.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the online dissemination of audiovisual works in the eu, so that public authorities do not remain on the sidelines of the development of new technologies but seize the potential it holds for ensuring cultural dissemination to citizens within a legal framework protecting creators and internet users. digital technologies are an opportunity for heritage works, they should be accessible to all and therefore taught to citizens of all ages, they should allow direct remuneration of creators.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the online distribution of audiovisual works in the european union. i am convinced that we must act at european level to combat the fragmentation of this sector and move towards a digital single market. the development of this digital market presents important challenges that we must overcome together. i am therefore pleased that this resolution takes account of the need for a competitive audiovisual sector which creates jobs and protects the interests of consumers and rightholders. in this spirit, i supported the call for member states to ban all rights-sharing contracts for the online distribution of audiovisual works. i believe that authors and performers should receive adequate, fair and proportionate remuneration for the volume of online exploitation of their works. in the same spirit, i voted in favour of the principle of chronology, which allows audiovisual works to benefit from an efficient system of pre-financing.
in writing. 6.9% of gdp, 14 million jobs, €860 billion turnover per year, continued growth despite the crisis: the cultural and creative industries have a high potential for creation, growth and jobs, which remains largely untapped. following my report on 'unlocking the potential of the cultural and creative industries' voted last year, parliament is today voting a resolution on the online distribution of audiovisual works in the european union. i supported this report, which aims in particular at improving access to audiovisual works available online - films, music or streaming - particularly outside national territory and language limitations. counterfeiting and piracy discourage investment in this sector. the report therefore stresses the importance of developing a more diversified legal offer and more flexible operating windows. finally, legal certainty of copyright and improved collection of copyright must be guaranteed at all stages of the creation and distribution process.
in writing. the internet has evolved faster than european law. we must therefore now ensure legal certainty in the european online digital space and ensure that unequal treatment between online and offline services is avoided. the resolution reaffirms the principle of net neutrality, which allows the broadcasting of offers to the widest possible audience, thus promoting media pluralism and cultural diversity. it also rejects the principle of a pan-european licence, which would have opened the door to the monopoly of the audiovisual market by a few large players to the detriment of many smes, which are the real heart of the film and audiovisual industry today. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution which seeks to guarantee universal access to a wide range of internet content while protecting the small players in a major european industry. we demand that the european commission and the member states take this into account in future european legislation.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we must welcome the final result of this text, which is aimed at taking better account of the vulnerability of victims - victims who too often, and rightly, feel that they are not sufficiently respected and, sometimes, that they are not as well supported as the perpetrators of the crimes themselves. it is a small step backwards, because we would all have liked to go further, to extend the list of vulnerable victims, but the council did not agree, citing financial cost, which is a complicated subject in this period of economic crisis. however, the principle of individual hearings for each victim remains, which should prevent any risk of discrimination in access to services. this is a major step forward which will make it possible to better define the rights and needs of victims throughout europe and to respond to them in the most appropriate way, taking into account the specific needs of each individual and, in particular, of women victims of violence. we must welcome these advances, as we must also welcome the work of the two rapporteurs on this dossier.
