member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam president, i would first like to thank sharon bowles for the question she has asked today, when the european commission, after a long period of work which i had the honour of leading under president barroso, is making public its proposal for a single banking supervision in the euro area. i would therefore like to thank you very much, madam president, for giving me the opportunity to listen to you, to reply to you and to listen to the other members who have something to say on this subject. with this banking union we want to provide answers to the challenges facing europe and, in particular, the euro area. ladies and gentlemen, you are aware of these challenges, since you have been acting on them and talking about them for a long time. the first concerns the link between the banking sector situation and sovereign debt - a link which we want to sever. the second is the temptation for each bank to turn to its own national area when it is in difficulty. the time is therefore ripe for action, and that is what we are doing today with these two legislative proposals which go together and which should allow the establishment of a single and effective monitoring mechanism. the commission firstly presents a proposal for a regulation based on article 127 (6) of the treaty, which would give the european central bank specific tasks in the field of prudential supervision. this system is simple, it is credible and we think it is robust. it will allow the european stability mechanism to play its role if necessary, and in accordance with the rules laid down in its decision-making procedures. this system is credible because the european central bank will have ultimate responsibility for making the key supervisory decisions, i.e. those that have an impact or consequence on financial stability. for example, other supervisory decisions - and your assembly is very attentive to this - concerning consumer protection will clearly remain within the remit of the national supervisors. the single supervisor will thus be able to grant and withdraw a licence to a bank, to check the risk management of an institution or, in the context of european prudential regulation, to require it to strengthen its funds. this system is also simple because we plan to give the european central bank the responsibility for the supervision of all credit institutions in the euro area. this, ladies and gentlemen, is simply one of the lessons of the crisis. systemic crises can be caused - as we have seen - by the difficulties of medium-sized banks, sometimes small banks, and not just by large international groups. this system is also robust because, of course, it is not a question of asking the european central bank to do everything alone. we want to maintain a role and responsibility in the framework of common supervision for the national supervisors who, as we well know, have in each country the resources, the expertise, the experience, which this single supervision will need to prepare the decisions, to execute them, and to implement and apply what i shall call the single supervision manual for each of the institutions, but to do so at national level, again, with the support of the national supervisor. finally, this system, if you will, will be open. we propose that member states which are not, or are not yet, in the euro area join the single supervisory mechanism voluntarily. i know that some of you are concerned about the legal basis we have chosen. they rightly point out that this basis does not provide for a codecision procedure but for the unanimity of the council, even though your assembly played a decisive role - i do not forget this - in setting up the authorities responsible for the supervision of markets, banks and insurance companies. ladies and gentlemen, to be very frank, and i have always been frank with you, the choice we have made is the result of several objective considerations. the purpose of article 127 (6) of the treaty is precisely to entrust supervisory tasks to the european central bank. it was therefore a logical and solid basis, and that is why the heads of state and government of the euro area explicitly asked the commission to work on this basis in their declaration of 29 june. but parliament, madam president, ladies and gentlemen, will play its part. i know that and i wish that. i will be attentive to your comments, proposals and criticisms, because the two proposals we are making today - for the regulation on the european banking authority (eba) and for supervision - go together, as president barroso said this morning in our name. the texts we are proposing also establish a real system of accountability of the new and future supervisory board to parliament, which i believe is a real step forward. the second regulation i have just mentioned will therefore aim to adapt the eba's operation to take account of the new balance resulting from the single supervisory mechanism. this regulation is based on article 114 of the treaty, which provides for codecision. the proposal revises certain voting arrangements within the eba to enable it to continue to play its full role in the development of common standards for the whole of the single market. the revision also aims to enable decision-making and to guarantee the integrity of the single market, while safeguarding the interests and rights of each of its members. finally, we present a communication which puts this unique supervision project into perspective. we will not build an integrated and effective supervision without solid foundations, and these solid foundations, these foundations for the 27 countries of the european union - and that is why i wish that we do not confuse the field of regulation, which remains that of all these texts that we have been building together for two and a half years, and that of supervision - are the legislative proposals already on the table and on the one hand, already approved - and for some already implemented - concerning in the future the resolution of banking crises, the deposit guarantee scheme and the own funds requirements through crd iv. these initiatives are key elements of what we have collectively called the single rulebook, the single internal market regulation, which must apply well in the 27 member states. the commission therefore does not intend to withdraw either of these proposals, which are not only compatible with banking union but also indispensable to its development and to the preservation and consolidation of the single regulation, this common regulation for the whole of the european banking economy. that is why i hope that the european parliament and the council of ministers - we shall be discussing this with the ministers from tomorrow in cyprus - will be able to reach agreement on these texts as soon as possible. this shows that the strengthening of the single market and the single supervision are two complementary approaches. the establishment of this banking union will naturally lead us to go further in strengthening our resolution and guarantee mechanisms, in line with the guidelines clearly set out in the report of the four presidents and in the communication from the european commission. ladies and gentlemen, we all know that there is an urgent need to get the euro area out of the crisis it is in, so that the european union, with its single market, can once again achieve the growth that citizens expect. i wanted to stress this urgency, and that is also why the commission, after 29 june, worked without improvisation, seriously but quickly, to be able to put on your table and that of the governments these two proposals which go together, for the creation of an open, robust and credible system of supervision.

the main purpose of a social enterprise is to generate a positive social impact. it is, for example, to integrate vulnerable or marginalised people into its human resources, its employees. they are also enterprises whose purpose is to support social activity. today, these companies are financed mainly through subsidies. we all know that it will be increasingly difficult for states and local authorities to support the financing of the programme through grants. these companies therefore see their future compromised, even though they need sustainable growth and innovation. we must help them to find other sources of finance, so that we can improve our social market economy. i would remind you that social entrepreneurship represents 10% of european enterprises and 11 million employees. the solidarity investment market is already very active in some of the emerging countries, but unfortunately it is extremely fragmented. at a time when the world of finance is being so much criticised, i am satisfied that this text can demonstrate that the profit for the world of finance is not the alpha and the omega, but that it can and must even play a major role in the solidarity economy and the real economy. i would like michel barnier to know how much i welcome this proactive approach. until now, the european commission has had a regulatory and supervisory relationship with finance, and this was appropriate. today we are taking a proactive approach, which is intended to provide an impetus to put finance at the service of the real economy. i thank the commission for this approach. why are we voting on this text tomorrow in plenary? we've been working hard on it this summer. my goal was twofold. it was about getting accessibility and security, because this label has to be open and accessible, but not at any price and not to just anyone. today we have reached a trialogue agreement - i am sorry to be slightly out of time, mr president, but this is a rather complicated matter - and i will ask my colleagues to support this agreement tomorrow. i hope that the council will follow us immediately when we have adopted this regulation. i would remind you that this is a real lever for growth in our economy and a vehicle for inclusion and progress in our society.

in writing. there are currently three quality labels for agricultural products in the european union (pgi, aoc, gst). the commission is planning to reform the system in order to simplify it or to facilitate new registrations. the greens felt it was important to take advantage of this reversal to encourage the emergence of a new label for 'local farming and short-distance farming'. we also wanted to introduce a 'mountain' label to highlight the high added value of products from these areas where agriculture is mostly traditional and extensive. the vote in the committee on agriculture was on both measures, which we welcomed. however, in the trilogue negotiations with the council and the commission, meps representing parliament have touted the label 'local farming and short circuits', which is important in encouraging this kind of farming practice. that is why i voted against this text, which was initially encouraging.
in writing. i denounce the retreat of all the parliamentary groups, with the exception of the gue/ngl and the greens/efa, in the face of the pressure from the european council. they agreed to remove the possibility for producer organisations to ask their national government to regulate their production. they have backed away from establishing a label for local farming and direct selling. the committee on agriculture had approved these two major advances! the principles of liberalism and free trade will continue to take precedence over the general economic and ecological interests. we did not expect less from the right wing, but we are entitled to question the decision taken by the social democrats. i abstain to denounce this despicable renunciation.
in writing. i abstained on the 'quality package', which includes a proposal for a regulation on quality schemes for agricultural products and a proposal on marketing standards. these texts are part of the revision of the quality policy for agricultural products. they have positive elements: recognition of the high value properties of products (labels) and their regional specificity, place of origin, emphasis on european symbols in particular. however, if such measures contribute to consumer information, they are nevertheless part of the policy of liberalization of the agricultural sector. in practical terms, it prevents farmers from supplying quality products and threatens the survival of entire regions. as long as the general direction of this policy remains unchanged, any measures to increase the value of production and to mark consumption will be purely cosmetic.
in writing. one in four new businesses created in the eu today is a social enterprise. in other words, it seeks to generate a positive social impact for our citizens. as rapporteur on this project, i can only welcome the unwavering support i have received from the european parliament. the sector, which accounts for more than 11 million jobs in europe, should finally be awarded a european label for solidarity investment. investment funds that invest at least 70% in solidarity enterprises will be eligible for the label. social entrepreneurship thus has a real lever for growth, which is crucial in these times of economic depression.
in writing. i am pleased that parliament has largely supported the rapid introduction of the european solidarity investment label. the adoption of this regulation bodes well for the establishment, in the near future, of a social label for all enterprises, not just for investment funds for social enterprises. we should see the adoption of this text as a first step towards encouraging and identifying socially responsible enterprises, which could attract new investors. because, knowing that the solidarity investment market is estimated at €1 billion, this can only encourage all companies to become a little more socially virtuous and to make this known through a 'european social label' as i have had adopted by the employment committee in the programme for social change and innovation and in the recast of the esf regulation.
in writing. the competitiveness of enterprises is an element of the economic recovery in europe. in these times of crisis, however, access to finance for firms is difficult. there is a solidarity investment market in europe which today represents one billion euros. this market is a growth lever which deserves to be fully exploited. social enterprises, i.e. those whose primary objective is to generate a positive social impact, employ 11 million employees. the european parliament, on a proposal from the commission, has therefore logically decided to support the creation of a european label for solidarity investment which will benefit investment funds which invest a minimum of 70% in social enterprises. by proposing this investment instrument, the european parliament hopes to contribute to stimulating the market and to encourage more investment in social entrepreneurship.
in writing. social enterprises are enterprises whose main purpose is not to make a profit but to generate a positive social impact, such as the integration of vulnerable or marginalised people. beyond grants, they need other sources of funding to help them achieve their mission and thus improve our social market economy. it is in this context that my colleague sophie auconie's report proposes the creation of a european passport for european social entrepreneurship funds. the report was adopted partially by a large majority (no vote on the legislative resolution). the aim is to enable the rapporteur to launch negotiations with the council with a view to reaching an agreement at first reading.
in writing. the european solidarity investment label would respond to the growing desire of investors to invest their money in support of solidarity actions and not just looking at financial returns. if accepted, the agreement would lay down rules to give investors assurance on the functioning of these funds through a label on european social entrepreneurship funds.
in writing. the aim of this regulation is to channel funds towards the social economy. it's far from satisfactory. its almost complete similarity to that on venture capital funds says much about the importance of the social economy in the eyes of the european commission. the few safeguards which parliament proposes remain too weak. the possibility that the latter offers these funds to finance companies financing or supporting social economy enterprises, but without being themselves social enterprises, raises fears of deviations. the possibility for any fund to register and operate throughout the european union without the need to obtain prior authorization also opens the door to the usual abuses. i do not want to impede the development of the social and solidarity economy. but i condemn the deviations that this regulation makes possible. i'll abstain from it.
in writing. together with the amendment to the financial transparency directive currently under consideration in parliament, this proposal forms part of a package of measures to promote corporate social responsibility adopted by the european commission at the beginning of the year. this easily identifiable label, granted to investment funds that invest in socially responsible enterprises in the majority, should help to meet the needs for transparency and fairness that more and more citizens have expressed since the beginning of the crisis. it will also stimulate economic sectors which are still under-exploited. that is why i supported these proposals in the plenary.
in writing. venture capital provides finance to companies that are still small but have a high potential for growth and innovation. when the us raised €131 billion between 2003 and 2010, european venture capital funds managed to raise only €28 billion. this lack of available funds is a major obstacle to european competitiveness and job creation. in addition to my initiative in favour of social entrepreneurship, i strongly support the rapporteur, philippe lamberts, in his efforts to secure and standardise this venture capital market in europe.
in writing. this report supports the commission's proposal to offer a european passport to all venture capital funds, whether european or from a third country, from the moment they register in one of the member states. the only limitation on this is the prohibition on being established in a country recognised as a tax haven. there is no mention of the penalties for infringements of these funds. however, it is clear that they will only be implemented by the member state responsible for registration. the state which is at fault for this authorization would therefore be in the best position to punish the consequences of its proposals? the whole of the european union is thus at the mercy of the euro, at least in terms of financial security. of course, this ultra-liberal report even accepts that these venture capital funds can value their assets according to their own criteria, effectively preventing any reliable expertise. i vote against this dangerous bill.
in writing. in june 2012, the european union, colombia and peru concluded an association agreement. as a precautionary measure, a safeguard clause was added to allow the original customs tariffs to be re-established in certain circumstances. this is particularly the case for goods imported in such significant quantities that they cause (or threaten to cause) serious injury to the union industry producing a like or directly competing product. parliament thus wished to activate the stabilisation mechanism for bananas which allows, until 1 january 2020, to suspend preferential tariff treatment when a certain annual volume of imports is reached. the main concern here is the banana producers in the outermost regions, who could be affected by this agreement.
in writing. while ratification of the trade agreement with colombia and peru is under consideration, safeguard measures for the european banana sector have been adopted for good reason. if the colombia-peru free trade agreement is ratified by the european parliament in the autumn, it will therefore be accompanied by a specific clause protecting european banana producers, and in particular those in the french overseas territories. more specifically, if european banana producers suffer serious damage as a result of the opening of trade with colombia and peru, the reduced customs duties provided for under the trade agreement would be increased. this is essential to protect our european producers, since the union is the most important market for banana exports and already 72.5% of the bananas sold in the union come from latin america.
in writing. i supported the adoption of these measures to protect an industry which sometimes concluded agreements which no longer needed to be applied. this stabilization mechanism will make it possible, in particular, to control more closely the volume of products circulating freely within the internal market, thus limiting excessive speculation which endangers our producers. it is with these provisions that the union supports our industries and avoids the temptation to use a labour force that is cheaper but also less qualified.
in writing. while it is expected to ratify the eu-colombia/peru free trade agreement shortly, the european parliament has just voted on a text introducing safeguard clauses for the banana sector. safeguard clauses allow normal customs duties to be temporarily re-established or the process of tariff liberalization to be suspended. the text acknowledges that there are problems with labour rights in the countries concerned, even if this recognition is insufficient. the rapporteur also calls for greater consideration of social and environmental aspects in the context of future economic liberalisation. the commission must hear this message. the texts also make clear the need to take greater account of the economies of the overseas countries, of which the banana sector is one of the pillars. this vote should not make us forget that the real challenge for these territories is a transition to a more diversified and sustainable economy. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this text.

in writing. copyright protection is one of the central issues in the european union's digital strategy. orphan works are protected by copyright, but the owner of the copyright has not been identified or located. by supporting this text, i wanted to create a framework for institutions whose missions are in the public interest (archives, libraries, museums, etc.) to become the sole beneficiaries of these orphan works. the beneficiaries may only receive revenues from the use of such works in the context of their public interest missions and only for the purpose of covering their costs of digitising and making available such orphan works.
in writing. i am voting in favour of this text, which will make it possible to better protect the use of works within the union. more than ever, the need for policymakers to take account of the needs of the industry is crucial to its survival.
in writing. i have given my full support to the report by my colleague lidia goeringer of oedenberg so that we finally have clear legislation that gives public institutions, such as museums and libraries, legal certainty in the online use and dissemination of orphan works whose rights holders are difficult to identify. it is not acceptable that public institutions should have to conceal work for fear of retaliation under the current rules of intellectual property, with very expensive lawsuits involved. culture and creativity are not just a matter of the market. by making works available for our archives, based on the rule of law, we are moving towards an ever more necessary redefinition of intellectual property, and we should welcome this.
in writing. the report by my colleague lidia geringer of oedenberg was adopted by a large majority, with 531 votes in favour, 11 against and 65 abstentions. i am very pleased with this result. orphan works are works protected by copyright or related rights and whose owner has not been identified or located. the aim of this report is to establish a legal framework to guarantee online access to orphan works across borders and in full compliance with the law.
in writing. we have adopted a directive that responds perfectly to the challenges of the digital age in which we live. more specifically, it is the digitisation of cultural material concerning orphan works, i.e. works whose rights holder cannot be identified or located. without the permission of the copyright holder, these works are not accessible to the public. we therefore wanted to allow libraries, educational institutions, museums and archives to provide specific services within the single market which involve the online placement of orphan works. however, in the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, which was consulted for its opinion, we wanted to clarify the copyright situation in order to avoid any abuse. i take this opportunity to emphasise that copyright remains the foundation of innovation, creation, investment and production in all creative industries. in voting in favour of this text on orphan works, i have therefore fully supported the promotion of the union's cultural diversity and the multiplication of sources of knowledge and learning through supervised access to orphan works at union level.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text on orphan works, which will allow for a better dissemination of cultural works through their digitisation. in some member states, works for which the rightholders cannot be located or identified cannot be made available online by libraries or other public bodies. now there is a framework, with measures in case a rights holder comes to light.
in writing. this draft directive attempts to reconcile copyright with the making available of orphan works for cultural or educational purposes. by combining the obligation to actually search for the authors of the work before it is distributed, the obligation to properly remunerate them, even if they are discovered after the distribution of their work, and the obligation to use orphan works only for public interest missions, this report does a fairly good job of this conciliation. i vote for it.

in writing. the european parliament met in plenary session on tuesday 23 october, a few days after the european summit of heads of state and government in brussels. if parliament's traditional position is to call for an ambitious budget in opposition to the drastic budget cuts advocated by some member states, i will take from this vote that the priorities of the french delegation of the epp group have been respected, in particular the maintenance of the cap budget and an advocacy for a better use of european funds. i am, however, concerned about the amendments on the seat of parliament and the emergence of an anti-strasbourg movement which is gaining new votes with each vote. it should be remembered that it is not for parliament to decide on its seat and that such a decision would involve an amendment of the treaties, a decision which is for the member states, in particular the founding members who naturally have a special responsibility because of the initiative of european construction which they have been the driving forces behind. on the other hand, it can be considered that the other countries, while choosing to join the european community, had in fact acceded to the provision conferring on strasbourg a status of which they were obviously aware.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleagues giovanni la via and derek vaughan on the general budget of the european union for 2013. after lengthy negotiations, the report was adopted by 492 votes to 123, with 82 abstentions. i'm glad you did. the eu budget for 2012 is just under €150 billion, representing around 1% of the eu27's gdp. while the eu budget is still in balance, the council wants to reduce the estimated 2013 budget by more than €5 billion. the european parliament, for its part, wanted to increase payments by 6.82% compared to 2012. my colleagues and i want the increase in payment appropriations to contribute directly to growth and employment in the eu.
in writing. the imperative need to return to growth in europe in order to definitively emerge from the successive crises we have been through has led my colleagues in the house and myself to take full responsibility for the 2013 budget. we felt it was important to cancel the cuts in the commission's budget which had been introduced by the council. so my colleagues and i voted in favour of the reinstatement of the 1.9 billion euro cut by the council last june. these funds will be allocated to priority sectors for growth such as the economy, research, entrepreneurship and employment. an amending budget was also presented to ensure the "survival" of the erasmus mundus programme. this programme enables our young people to study throughout europe, which gives them an opportunity to discover different cultures and languages and to become aware of their european citizenship. in agriculture, most of the proposed budget cuts have also been cancelled, and i welcome that. we also approved budget cuts of eur 8.9 million in the administration of parliament. so the goal is now to do more with less.

in writing. i opposed a reduction in the european budget as requested by the council. this is the case for the survival of many european programmes, such as the erasmus student mobility programme and the european social fund, which are essential and fundamental programmes. the kind of failure to pay that is threatening to occur for these two programmes should never happen again. growth and jobs must be a top priority.
in writing. the amendments to the draft budget for 2013 submitted by the council and advocated in this report have four undeniable merits: rejecting the council's indecent cuts in the structural funds, which it calls for strategic use elsewhere, restoring the eur 300 000 withdrawn from erasmus by the commission and the council, increasing the funding allocated to palestine and unrwa and maintaining the budget allocated to the food distribution programme for the most deprived people (pead). however, i cannot vote for a budget which restores the excessive funding for frontex which the council had refused, reinstates the increase in funding for iter which the council had refused and is in line with the logic of the europe 2020 strategy. i abstain in respect of the excellent erasmus programme and in support of the continuation of the edp and the increase in aid to the palestinians.
in writing. the multiannual financial framework makes it possible to establish a budget for the european union in a coherent and organised way for a period of seven years. the economic crisis is affecting all budgets, national and european. nevertheless, it is necessary that the european union remains able to finance its many policies and projects that contribute to recovery and growth. this is why the european parliament voted in favour of this text, calling for the strengthening of this european budget and even for the creation of financial resources of the european union.
in writing. the budget in europe and at member state level remains the nerve of the war. it is the test of the ambition of public policies. we have often, if not always, had to deal with a very poor deal in the last budgetary procedures. in the grip of public debts, many member states are holding the brakes as soon as the subject of a real budget for europe is raised. but we must be aware that any recovery plan worthy of the name to get us out of the present stalemate will require concerted action at european level. the end of the crisis tunnel will not appear by magic. if europe condemns itself to a 1% budget throughout the 2014-2020 period, it is feared that we will again talk in 2020 of a hypothetical exit from the crisis.

in writing. at a time when the european economy is particularly battered, it is important that the union has an ambitious budgetary programme for the next seven years. for this reason, the draft multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 should be able to support the return to growth in europe. future research and investment budgets must be substantial to support competitiveness, create activity, and enable job creation. at the same time, it is right that part of this european budget should be devoted to emergency aid and solidarity towards citizens in difficulty, in particular through the continuation of the european programme of aid to the most deprived (eapd) and the european globalisation adjustment fund. finally, the eu budget should now be able to be fed from own resources without increasing the national tax burden.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which recalls the european parliament's strong and united position on the multiannual financial framework (mff) for the period 2014-2020, ahead of the november european council summit on the subject. this report recalls our support for a 5% increase in the budget compared to 2013, i.e. an additional €100 billion. the multiannual financial framework is the only way to get europe out of the current crisis. in view of the challenges it faces, it must be able to meet and finance the commitments made by all the european institutions, in particular in the fields of climate, development aid, research, employment and the fight against poverty. apart from the question of the percentage, the other key issue is that of the eu's own resources. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the environment.
in writing. we are sending a clear message to member states, who are obsessed with austerity cures, neglecting the need to invest in growth and jobs, by providing budgetary means that are commensurate with our ambitions. it is very regrettable that, at a time when europe is faced with increasing responsibilities, the states refuse to take responsibility for the crisis. what the european commission is proposing is still far short of what is needed to meet the challenges of the crisis. this is a minimum threshold below which we cannot go without risking affecting whole sections of european cohesion policy. the european budget, as i see it, must therefore remain an instrument of solidarity. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. far from short-term visions, we must see the european budget as a lever for growth, and not as the member states do as a simple means of collecting a check to finance their national policies alone. finally, it is clear that there can be no agreement on this budget without an agreement on own resources.
in writing. the report on the multiannual financial framework contains the words: growth, jobs, crisis response. unfortunately, the proposed provisions say otherwise. the budgetary logic is still the one that has led europe to the impasse and the crisis. beyond words, it is always the same ultra-liberal options that are supported against and against everything. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. with such orientations, there is no chance for europe to emerge from the chaos it has created. on the contrary, there is a greater risk that europe will sink deeper into crisis, to the sole benefit of finance. it is time to change the focus completely: to give priority to public services that are bulwarks against the crisis. to provide concrete assistance for the development of jobs and industry against finance by calling for a public financial pole whose objective will be to provide concrete assistance to projects and people rather than to profit. revitalise social protection, harmonize from above and immediately stop leveling it from below by pitting citizens against employees. without these essential changes, europe cannot emerge from the crisis. it is for this europe that i am working with the citizens...
in writing. key session for the european parliament which adopted its position on accelerating negotiations with the council and the commission on the multiannual financial framework which will determine eu actions and policies for the next seven years (2014-2020). the aim was to set out the priorities and guidelines of the european parliament in preparation for the european council on the budget on 22 and 23 november. although the european parliament has only a limited negotiating margin under the treaty of lisbon (assent), it is a decisive power which gives it a say in the negotiations. the european parliament therefore intends to preserve its prerogatives by voting this way, but also the unity of the budget, because this is not the time for a dispersion of funds which would affect the transparency and predictability of the european budget. the european parliament recognises, however, that introducing a form of flexibility in the european budget would make it possible to adapt it better to the contingencies linked to the crisis and to cyclical and structural developments.
in writing. the report by my colleagues reimer böge and ivalio kalfin was adopted by 517 votes to 105, with 63 abstentions. i supported this report in plenary. it constitutes the mandate of the european parliament in the forthcoming negotiations with the council. the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 started 11 months ago and accelerated sharply with the announcement by president hermann van rompuy of a european council on 22 and 23 november. since the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament has had the power to give its assent, that is to say yes or no to council proposals. in this context, the report by my colleagues reimer böge and ivalio kalfin aims to draw red lines. if these were not respected in the future, then the european parliament would be obliged not to give its assent. the red lines that have been drawn are: respect for parliament's prerogatives, unity of the budget, greater flexibility to facilitate the adjustment of budgetary resources, reform of the own resources system.

in writing. this vote is a decisive step in the discussions on the 2014-2020 financial framework and determines the parliament's negotiating mandate. a balance must be struck between two realities: the treaty of lisbon has created new community competences, requiring additional resources, but the crisis does not allow for an increase in national contributions to the community budget. this equation will be difficult to solve if the states persist in their double refusal to raise their contribution and to provide own resources to replace it. the french government of sarkozy had set in motion a process which led to a tax on financial transactions, the proceeds of which will be paid to the community budget, thus reducing the contribution of the countries implementing it, which is a first positive sign. in these negotiations, parliament will defend several red lines: the budget must be a vehicle for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, be flexible to meet structural and cyclical needs and developments, and support projects with high european added value. in this iron fist, parliament must give a conciliatory opinion, with the power to say yes or no. the ball is clearly in the court of the member states.
in writing. enabling the european union to obtain its own financial resources is an objective enshrined in the treaties. this report adopted by the european parliament and which i voted in favour of aims to redefine the way vat is calculated in europe. the long-term objective is that, by harmonising these rates, the european union will be able to collect a share of the vat collected in europe, thus reducing national contributions to achieve fiscal autonomy.

in writing. this report proposes to make vat the alpha and omega of the financing of the european budget. it is therefore not surprising that the european commission is obsessed with raising vat rates and abolishing vat rates, even on the most essential items, such as water and energy. it devotes the most unfair tax and the funding of austerity institutions to the mass of the poorest. i vote against it.
in writing. the eu's own budgetary resource based on vat will now be based on supplies of goods and services, as well as purchases and imports subject to a standard rate of vat throughout the european union. it is therefore based on the actual harmonisation which already exists for goods and services subject to the normal rate. the proposal also transfers to the commission the calculation currently carried out by the member states. this own resource was created in 1970 to be a genuine own resource. it assumed that a continuous process of harmonization of the national vat laws of the member states would lead to the harmonization of national rates. this has not been the case, and at present the vat own resource is another contribution by the member states to the community budget calculated in terms of gni. i abstained on this proposal from the european commission because it risks pushing upwards the harmonization of vat rates, like the proposals to increase vat, which the right wing in france unfairly calls 'social', in exchange for lower social security contributions from employers.

in writing. by making 2013 the year of citizens, the aim is to make citizens more aware of their rights, particularly in relation to mobility between member states. this text, which i voted in favour of and which the european parliament as a whole also supported, will make it possible to set up awareness-raising and information campaigns for european citizens. conferences and events will also be organised and exchanges of information will be promoted. finally, particular emphasis will be placed on the multilingual platforms set up by the european union, as language differences remain one of the main obstacles to the mobility of european citizens.
in writing. for many european citizens, europe remains, in the words of jacques delors, an 'unidentified political object'. yet european citizenship has been built and is constantly advancing. family rights, pension rights, vocational training, recognition of qualifications - it is our common responsibility to make the practical and useful provisions of european citizenship known to everyone in everyday life. the 2013 european year of citizens is therefore excellent news in this respect.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the european year of citizens (2013). according to a 2009 eurobarometer survey, almost one in five europeans feel that working in another member state presents too many obstacles. the problem is the lack of information on the rights of european citizens, administrative issues, social protection systems and the recognition of diplomas. i believe that when employment is to become the priority of european policies, it is important to facilitate and encourage the cross-border mobility of workers. the report therefore proposes to carry out various communication and dissemination initiatives at eu level to help european citizens better understand their rights to freedom of movement and residence.
in writing. european citizens enjoy rights, but they have yet to exercise them fully. it is time to tackle head-on the obstacles that still hinder their mobility. the european year of citizens will enable us to do everything we can to achieve genuine european citizenship from next year onwards. the first step in making this citizenship a reality is for each of us to be aware of what it covers. the first objective of this action, which i supported, is to inform and debate.
in writing. i fully supported the report by my colleague antigoni papadopoulou in favour of the establishment of the european year of citizens in 2013. in these times of economic and social crisis, it is essential to highlight the rights attached to european citizenship in order to restore the confidence of our citizens in the european project. too few people are really aware of the rights of european citizenship. it is therefore necessary to support all actions which help to highlight the rights of european citizens and to ensure that they are properly applied. the issue of european citizenship cannot be limited to declarative matters; it is a highly political one. it is through the defence and publicity of existing rights and the construction of new guarantees for citizens that this notion of citizenship can take on content, weight and become tangible for everyone. and it is also for these reasons that i support an ambitious budget for this 'year', beyond the million agreed by the member states, but still far below what is needed to achieve our objective of european citizenship on a daily basis.
in writing. the most common complaint about the european union is the gap between these institutions, which are considered technocratic, and citizens, who have difficulty identifying the main actors, understanding their role and the distribution of competences and, above all, the concrete impact of european decisions on their daily lives. many communication campaigns are carried out each year to bring citizens closer to their institutions and to give them a better understanding of the actions undertaken at eu level. for example, in 2009, 11.9 million eu citizens were living in a member state other than their own, and the creation of the internal market has steadily increased this movement. however, many europeans still consider the barriers to intra-community mobility to be too high, including the lack of information on administrative issues, social protection system issues and the recognition of university degrees. that is why 2013 has been designated the 'european year of citizens'. the aim will be to raise awareness of the rights of european citizenship in a cross-border context. let us hope that this initiative will succeed in reconciling citizens with the eu.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the 'european year of the citizen 2013'. today, almost 12 million european citizens live in a country other than their own, yet there are still many obstacles to mobility within our union. i therefore voted in favour of the various lines of funding proposed in the report, such as the development of communication tools for information campaigns for the general public. although it is the responsibility of the member states to inform the public, it is imperative that we set up multilateral information campaigns. we must enable the citizens of the union to exercise and defend their rights better, at local, regional, national and european level!
in writing. the latest eurobarometer surveys show that europe is experiencing a crisis of confidence and legitimacy. since autumn 2009, about 30% fewer people say they trust the eu. as we celebrate 20 years of european citizenship next year and less than a year before the european elections, it is a good idea to make 2013 the year of european citizenship, the year of european citizens. i supported this text because i wanted to give 2013 a special symbolic meaning in the current context. it has been shown that citizens suffer from a lack of information about their eu rights. it is essential that the european year of citizenship should succeed in effectively raising awareness among citizens of these rights. it must also stimulate citizens' interest in the activities of the european union, which is essential for the development of european democracy, which is so important for the eu's legitimacy. but the success of 2013 obviously depends on the financial resources mobilised, and in this respect i regret that the budget allocated to it is so meagre.
in writing. the choice to put the citizen back at the heart of european concerns in 2013 is particularly timely. we are celebrating the 20th anniversary of the internal market, which we often accuse of favouring the mobility of goods over that of people and competition over solidarity. there are still many difficulties in exercising the rights of european citizenship to the full. the first of these difficulties is to know them. in theory, no one is supposed to be ignorant of the law. in practice, unfortunately, no one knows what it is: the confusion in the transposition of directives, the complexity of the decision-making process and the lack of interest of citizens make it necessary to make european rights better known. moreover, once the benefits of european citizenship are known, they must be exercisable. the territory of the eu is far from being a uniform and homogeneous living space for its citizens. sometimes the removal of internal border controls on persons seems to have created as many problems as it has solved. in these times of crisis, the european project and european citizenship must regain their relevance. the year 2013 should be an opportunity to put the citizen back at the heart of the purpose of european legislation.

in writing. the single european sky project aims to establish common air traffic management rules in europe. we voted on tuesday on the report by jacqueline foster on the single european sky, which aims to increase the capacity, safety and efficiency of air traffic. this will be characterized by the eventual introduction of shorter, faster and cheaper routes. in addition to saving time for travellers, optimising air routes should result in significant fuel savings and a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions from civil aviation. the inefficiency resulting from the fragmentation of european airspace is costing the eu an extra €5 billion a year. the average flight length has increased by 42 kilometres, which translates into higher fuel consumption, higher emissions, higher fees and delays. the aim is to increase airspace capacity by three times and reduce traffic costs by two.

in writing. i fully supported this report, which calls for the faster implementation of the single european sky. the project will free aircraft from the constraints of national borders and allow them to make the shortest journey between two european airports. the project is based on a merger of the european air traffic blocks (fabs) and on the harmonization of flight operating technologies (sesar). unfortunately, this project, in which european added value should take on its full meaning and scope, is not worth it. the technological aspect has lagged considerably behind. there is an urgent need to accelerate and reverse this trend, as the usefulness and need for the single european sky will become increasingly felt, with air traffic expected to triple in the coming years. the benefits of the single european sky are well known: reduced ticket prices and travel times, a tenfold increase in safety levels, 50 million tonnes of co2 savings and 328 000 jobs created. so what are the member states and stakeholders waiting for to complete this european project?

in writing. on 23 october, the european parliament adopted the report on air passengers' rights in all modes of transport, including, in addition to the already regulated air and rail transport, waterborne transport and bus/coach transport. the report aims to coordinate the regulations in force and to establish common guidelines. mobility is one of the main achievements of the creation of the single market: facilitating the mobility of european citizens therefore had to be translated naturally into the removal of technical and administrative barriers in their daily commutes. i therefore welcome the fact that the eu is drawing up a list of fundamental passenger rights which ensures that regulations are responsive to passenger concerns. among these fundamental rights i would like to highlight the right to clear, accurate and easily accessible information before purchase and at the various stages of the journey, facilitated by the establishment of information points, but also the right to cancel the journey with full refund of the ticket price, the right to compensation in certain circumstances, the carrier's liability for luggage and easy and non-discriminatory access for disabled persons or persons with reduced mobility.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the community system for the control of exports, transfers, brokering and transit of dual-use goods. these rules aim to limit the risk of sensitive dual-use items (chemicals, telecommunications equipment or software) being used for military purposes. without impeding legitimate trade, it is important to develop a comprehensive system of general export authorisations of the european union in order to combat effectively the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. i think that this report makes it possible to pursue a policy of exporting our dual-use goods without risk.
in writing. some of the goods we use in our daily lives can potentially be used for military purposes. it is therefore necessary to monitor closely their export to other countries, but with great care not to impede trade where they are not dangerous. the text i voted for aims to streamline this control: not to impede legitimate trade while ensuring a high level of security, an objective which i fully support.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague christofer fjellner on the community regime for the control of exports, transfers, brokering and transit of dual-use goods. the report was adopted on 23 october by 378 votes to 263 with 17 abstentions. this framework for the control of exports of dual-use goods and technology (i.e. goods of a civilian nature that may have military use) is more than indispensable. it pursues a dual objective: to limit the risks of proliferation and military use while avoiding the hindrance of legitimate trade.
in writing. a balance has been struck between limiting the risks of proliferation and military use of dual-use goods and enhancing legitimate trade in such goods in this report. it is necessary to streamline the procedures for amending the annexes so that they can be updated regularly and rapidly if necessary. delegated acts shall be appropriate for such amendments. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. following a thorough review of the international convention on standards of training for seafarers, several changes were decided. this text, which was adopted by the european parliament and which i voted in favour of, is the incorporation into european law of the recasting of an international convention. it aims to improve training conditions and raise the level of certain requirements for the training of seafarers.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to strengthen the provisions on the training and assessment of seafarers, in particular on fraud and piracy. it consists mainly of incorporating into european legislation the reworking of the international convention agreed at the manila conference on 25 june 2010.
in writing. i voted in favour of the simpson report, which aims to transpose into community law the developments in international law decided upon within the international maritime organisation. i have been able to observe through my work as vice-chairman of the committee on fisheries how important it is that crews trained in different countries but working on the same vessel have the necessary skills to carry out their duties in the same way. i am convinced that training plays a vital role in maritime safety and i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. the sea is home to some of our most beautiful jobs, but also some of our most dangerous. the human factor is the key to this. ensuring that seafarers are properly trained by bringing european provisions into line with our international obligations is the aim of the text i voted for.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague brian simpson in the plenary on 23 october. the report was adopted by a large majority, with 619 votes against, 16 against and 16 abstentions. i'm glad you did. the aim of this report was to bring the minimum level of training of seafarers into line with international rules. the main improvements sought are: reinforced provisions for training, assessment and prevention of fraudulent practices, updated standards for medical fitness and alcohol abuse, new requirements for electrical officers and new provisions for safety training for seafarers.
in writing. the very important question of the minimum level of training for seafarers was put to the vote on tuesday and the report was adopted. after the recent tragedies at sea which have affected the collective conscience, i welcome the alignment of european legislation with the international convention on standards of training for seafarers. the human factor is essential for maritime safety and we had to update our legislation. i voted in favour of this text so that much needed improvements in the minimum quality of training for seafarers, a review of the requirements for their medical fitness and stricter standards for patents are implemented. these improvements will bring european law into line with international standards.
in writing. the aim is to adapt the rules on the training of seafarers to the new international rules, decided at the manila conference, in order to avoid a gap between european and international law. these amendments introduce, for example, new requirements for the licensing of qualified seafarers and safety training. the deadline for the recognition of third country systems is also extended from 3 to 18 months.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the minimum level of training for seafarers. the european parliament's margin of manoeuvre was limited since the member states had already accepted the stcw international convention. these amendments represent progress in training and harmonization in the issuing of certificates of competency. they also improve fraud prevention and standards for service qualifications, medical requirements and requirements relating to alcohol abuse. in a sector where there are no frontiers, it is in the interest of seafarers and in the general interest that certificates issued by member states and third countries are recognised throughout europe. however, to avoid a bottom-up leveling, care must be taken to ensure that a number of common criteria are required. which we can be satisfied with. i also welcome the commission's initiative to require member states to provide available information on certificates, a relevant provision for establishing a state of play and a strategy for employment in this sector.
in writing. i supported this directive transposing into community law the amendments adopted by the international maritime organisation (imo) to the convention on the training of seafarers. europe is the world's leading maritime power, and its maritime industry is one of our jewels, a source of jobs and a driver of growth. it is obviously important to support our maritime know-how, especially since the competitiveness of the sector depends on the quality of the training of seafarers. the imo is the relevant body for the establishment of such regulations, given the international nature of maritime transport. the fact that the member states and the commission sit on the committee is a sign of confidence in the expertise of this organisation. recent disasters have led to improved safety training on board, and i stressed the need for crew members to have documents and procedures in their own language for ship operations and emergency situations. i also advocated strict rules on the licensing and inspection of seamen. maritime safety and security are too important for us not to be exemplary, and i welcome the consensus reached in this house.

in writing. i voted in favour of the additional protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european communities and israel on conformity assessment and acceptance of industrial products. it provides for a procedure for the recognition of equivalence in the fields of technical regulation, standardisation and evaluation of the industrial products concerned and a mechanism for the mutual acceptance of industrial products. it is not a political assessment for or against the legitimization of israeli settlements or the occupied territories, which remain the domain of international diplomacy.
in writing. the european parliament has just approved the acaa the protocol on conformity assessment and acceptance of industrial products which will be annexed to the eu-israel association agreement. this agreement, as adopted, does not guarantee that the products that will reach our market will not be produced, in part, in the colonies, contrary to the provisions of european and international law. it should be recalled that the european union condemns israel's settlement policy as illegal and took the decision in 2009 to freeze the improvement of its relations with israel (after operation cast lead against gaza). so there is a double discourse that is incomprehensible and incoherent. that is why i voted against the agreement.
in writing. at the plenary session on 23 october, i voted against the request for referral back to the inta committee and voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr vital moreira, on the acaa treaty. finally, the request for referral was not adopted. the report was adopted by 379 votes in favour, 230 against and 41 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. i supported the agreement between the european union and the state of israel on conformity assessment and acceptance of industrial products (acaa). this agreement should enable exporters in the european union who so wish to submit their industrial products to a single verification and certification before export, on the basis of the same criteria. even if the left wanted to use the vote on this agreement as a pretext for the policies of the current israeli government, it is the extension of a vital trade agreement which strengthens economic ties between the state of israel and the european union, and i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. i supported the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the ec and israel on conformity assessment and acceptance of industrial products. this is a purely technical agreement which allows industrial goods of community and israeli exporters to be subjected to only one verification and certification. this saves time and money.
in writing. this report proposes to take a first step towards the full integration of israel into the european single market. under the pretext of completely liberalising trade in pharmaceuticals between the union and israel, the protocol endorsed in this text actually allows new products and services to be incorporated into this total free trade agreement without prior or subsequent parliamentary approval. i oppose this protocol for the strengthening of free trade it allows. but also for the political signal it sends. even as the israeli government continues its aggressive settlement policy and maintains the blockade of gaza in defiance of international law, this protocol strengthens its trade relations with the union without requiring any guarantees as to the origin of the products traded. by ratifying this protocol, the union would be sending a dangerous message to respect for international law. i vote against this text.
in writing. a majority of the european parliament gave its consent to this trade agreement between the european union and israel, known as acaa, which is part of the association agreement between these two parties. the agreement, which is presented as a purely technical agreement aimed at adopting common standards for pharmaceutical products, allows for the mutual recognition of certificates for pharmaceutical products, in particular by reducing the time taken for marketing due to the approval procedures. pharmaceutical products of both parties will have easier access to the market of the other party. other sectoral agreements, such as those on toys, cosmetics, etc., will follow shortly.) i voted against this agreement because it contributes to the improvement of relations between the eu and israel, without taking into account israel's policy towards the occupied palestinian territories. any deepening of relations between the eu and israel, including in the economic and commercial fields, must depend on israel's respect for the un resolutions on palestine and human rights. the majority of the european parliament, therefore, by giving its consent to this agreement, is affirming its unconditional support for israel's policy in the occupied territories and is sending more than a bad political signal.
in writing. like the european parliament, i voted in favour of this text which aims to redefine the european approach to aid to certain developing countries. the european union, the world's largest donor, needs to reform certain practices, including the criteria for the designation of countries receiving this aid. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft budget. the problem is no longer wealth creation, it's distribution. the new procedures should also strengthen controls on the use of eu funds and thus ensure that the eu remains a driver of social progress in these countries.
in writing. as we approach the mdgs deadline in 2015, even though some of the objectives seem to have been met, we need to ask ourselves how we can improve our aid, make it more consistent with our trade policy, with our agricultural policy and with our foreign policy. the future of european development policy must be based on specific, measurable commitments and a short- and medium-term timetable. we must explain to our fellow citizens that the development of third countries is not only charity and solidarity, but also a source of development for us. just look at the markets that are opening up for europeans in the emerging countries: china, brazil and india. this is why 2015 should be designated the european year of development and, above all, of responsible development.
in writing. to develop, our partners need our support and trust. the union has a key role to play and is helping them as much as it can. but such help must not be at the expense of our own interests. to do that, we need to make sure that every euro we spend is invested where it will have the most impact. it is therefore necessary to strengthen dialogue and set clear priorities. it is because this report makes these demands that i voted in favour of it.
in writing. i voted in favour of my colleague charles goerens' report on the future of development policy because i think it is generally positive. the aim of the report is to focus on the priority aspects of development policy, i.e. in particular the criteria for official development assistance, independent strategic thinking, the question of differentiation (emerging countries), support for local trade. i am particularly pleased with the positive vote on the paragraph introduced by an amendment of the green group in the committee on development to refocus aid for trade instruments, which is currently targeted at export sectors, so that it also supports local and regional trade.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr charles goerens, on the future of the european union's development policy. the report was adopted by a large majority, with 540 votes in favour, 36 against and 65 abstentions. i'm glad you did. in his communication of 13 october 2011 entitled 'increasing the impact of eu development policy: an agenda for change', commissioner piebalgs wanted to open a broad debate on how to change our development policy to make it more effective and of higher quality. the report by my colleague mr goerens proposes concrete ways of achieving this objective. the rapporteur proposes, for example, more selectivity in the choice of partners, more precise criteria for financial envelope and official development aid, or consideration of inclusive growth and the role of economic growth in developing countries, which are a driver of social progress.
in writing. the european union's development policy must focus on a few priority areas in order to be effective. for example, we need to invest in inclusive growth, which is the key to social progress. however, it is important to keep a close eye on any project and to evaluate it to measure its real impact in terms of poverty reduction. development aid must also take account of emerging economies and their impact on the situation of the poor in the global south.
in writing. the european union and its member states are now the world's largest contributors of development aid: more than half of the funds allocated to developing countries come from the european union and its member states. we must constantly monitor the use of its funds and continue to combat some of its shortcomings. i therefore welcome the european parliament's resolution on the future of the european union's development policy. i believe that we must set priorities in the aid we wish to provide to developing countries in order to bring real added value to the actions undertaken by the union. the resolution calls for european aid to be concentrated on those countries most in need and for aid to middle-income countries to be gradually reduced. i also support the idea of involving emerging countries more in the financing of future development policies and cooperation agreements with developing countries.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to restore the balance between the european commission's proposals and the reality on the ground. it stressed the lack of dialogue and coherence between the different branches of external action, which led to a loss of effectiveness of the funds allocated and of the actions carried out under the development. for example, i supported paragraph 51, which states that 'aid for trade and the union's trade facilitation instruments ... must change to facilitate trade for local and regional markets'. the latter are a necessary preliminary step before entering the world market. i also supported paragraph 61 which calls for european companies established in third countries to be able to be sanctioned in their home countries for breaches of basic international social standards. i proposed this option in an opinion for the committee on international trade last year and it seems to me still as relevant in view of the increasing interdependence of national economies.
in writing. poverty eradication is one of the eu's longstanding objectives, and the eu is the world's leading provider of development aid. nevertheless, it is time to put words into action and that is the whole point of this report, which i supported. we are behind the millennium development goals, and our assembly is proposing a strategy to make significant progress, politically and economically. political action must be a means of establishing democracy and respect for human rights in a lasting way. the economic aspect must be focused on concrete issues: targeting funding on basic social services to improve living conditions, supporting micro-enterprises by improving the economic and legal environment and combating unemployment, or coordinating the action of public and private actors to rationalize the distribution of available funds. it is obvious that we cannot solve all the problems at once. the commission has therefore decided to take action in stages, focusing on those actions which will add the most value. this is how the eu will make the best use of development aid, a tangible expression of european citizens' solidarity with those who have nothing.

in writing. i welcome the fact that the european parliament has taken up a major issue which is essential for growth in europe: the competitiveness of enterprises and industries. the commission and parliament share the same analysis: growth will only be possible if we undertake structural reforms aimed at modernising the european industrial system. this objective of competitiveness must be at the heart of our public policies. parliament therefore supports the lines of action proposed by the european commission: the internationalisation of smes, the reduction of administrative burdens and the strengthening of industrial competitiveness. the european parliament called for the launch of a multilingual portal to facilitate access by smes to essential information on the different legislations and administrative systems of third countries. parliament also called for the establishment of a european network of representatives of smes, which would be responsible for the coordination of the activities of the european commission and the member states. finally, parliament considered that strengthening industrial competitiveness and the competitiveness of smes also required exploiting the entrepreneurial potential of young people, women and migrants.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague paul rübig on competitiveness and business prospects for smes. the report was adopted by a large majority in the european parliament at its plenary session on 23 october. i'm glad you did. the report focuses on three areas: internationalisation of smes, reducing administrative burdens and enhancing industrial competitiveness.

in writing. as we are experiencing an unprecedented phase of deindustrialisation and social plans are being rolled out in succession, it is time to embark on structural reforms to get back to growth. we must create a competitive shock for our smes, which account for 99% of all businesses and 70% of all jobs in the eu. to achieve this we have several levers at our disposal and i think we must activate them all at the same time if we are to catch up. first of all, we must continue to reduce the administrative burden on businesses. considerable efforts have been made in this direction, but i believe that we can go even further, particularly with regard to the tpe. it is also imperative to improve lending to the real economy and to help mobilise private funds to support our smes. it is these wealth and employment creators who must be able to benefit from reasonable interest rates. finally, i would stress the need to reduce the tax burden which weighs too heavily on our companies. these three proposals must ensure the security and flexibility of entrepreneurship, which is essential if we want europe to remain a productive land.

in writing. parliament adopted the report by my colleague edit bauer which makes it possible to strengthen consular protection for eu citizens abroad. the diplomatic and consular services of all eu member states must give eu citizens seeking help abroad the same protection as they give their own nationals. the report was adopted by 596 votes to 66, with 12 abstentions. i voted in favour of this text because consular protection of european citizens by the embassies of the member states, in case of difficulty abroad, helps to consolidate the feeling of belonging to european citizenship. the european union delegations in third countries must now assume responsibility for ensuring cooperation and coordination between member states, including the division of tasks to ensure that unrepresented citizens are fully assisted in the event of a crisis.
in writing. when european citizens are abroad and in difficulty, they have the right to apply to any embassy or consulate of another eu member state if their country is not represented. this right to consular protection is a fundamental right which i have been anxious to reaffirm. i have been committed to ensuring that this right is better guaranteed, in particular by involving the delegations of the european union in a crisis situation, so that every citizen can be protected.
in writing. this report encourages solidarity between consulates of the eu member states in assisting european citizens, their families, whatever the nationality of their members, refugees and stateless persons. i am in favour of this and welcome the prospect of such solidarity. i regret, however, that the budget cuts introduced in the name of austerity, which the majority of this parliament is calling for, are reducing the protection that our consulates can actually provide. i am voting for this text to show my agreement with the principles of consular solidarity which it professes but to denounce the incoherence of the commission and the european parliament in this matter. i repeat my opposition to the creation of the useless, costly and empty service of so-called european diplomacy.

in writing. the creation of a large single market based on four fundamental freedoms (the movement of goods, capital, people and services) is a decisive step in the construction of the european union. however, there is still a gap between the expectations of european citizens and the reality of the single market. eu citizens and businesses still face too many obstacles, often in their daily lives, to exercising their rights. these may include the financial costs of registering a vehicle, the impossibility of opening a bank account abroad or the difficulties in recognising professional qualifications. it is essential in this respect that the community institutions are able to provide rapid and concrete solutions to the remaining shortcomings in order to respond effectively to the main concerns of the citizens of the union.

in writing. too many obstacles still prevent europeans from taking full advantage of the single market, as we celebrate its 20th anniversary this year. this is the conclusion drawn by the european commission in its working document listing the 20 main concerns of citizens and businesses about the functioning of the single market. i fully agree with the analysis presented in the resolution adopted today, namely that these concerns are due to three shortcomings: the first in information, the second in implementation and the last in legal loopholes. in particular, i support the proposal that member states should establish a single point of contact for all mobile citizens in the union, enabling them to handle the administrative procedures related to their work and home and to be kept informed of their rights and obligations in one place in their host country. it not only facilitates the daily lives of expatriate citizens, but also promotes the mobility of all citizens and the exchange of good practice between all national administrations. i believe that this is the kind of initiative which will bring all europeans closer together.

in writing. the amendment of regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 on measures against dumping by third country companies could have provided the european parliament with an opportunity to revise the list of criteria used to measure dumping. the practice of artificially low wages in relation to the wealth produced and european wages (wage dumping), the existence of tax exemptions or reduced taxes on companies (fiscal dumping), the endangerment of the ecosystem (environmental dumping) are all criteria which should be used to judge whether there is dumping or not. instead, the international trade committee merely approved the commission's proposal to be able to judge more arbitrarily and without having to respect any deadlines which company is worthy of being considered a 'market economy company'. the commission alone judges the market? but who is to judge the commission? the market? i am voting against this inept text.
