in writing. without falling into the trap of protectionism, which would obviously lead us straight into recession, europe has clearly failed in its duty to ensure the basic principle of reciprocity in its trade agreements with third countries. if we cannot talk about a europe of the straw, it is certain that we must speak with a stronger voice with all our partners to ensure the viability of our agreements. japan is a major test in this context. as a major industrial and commercial power and a major world power in asia, the european union has every reason to increase its trade partnership. it is still necessary that it be concluded on a sound and reciprocal basis, which is still not the case at the present stage of the negotiations.
in writing. following the much-publicized eu-korea agreement two years ago, parliament gave its approval for the eu to open free trade negotiations with japan. while it is true that increased trade could bring considerable gains in growth and employment, parliament stressed that negotiations should be suspended if japan refused to remove obstacles in key sectors, notably the automotive sector. we also wanted a binding review clause within one year of the opening of negotiations, to assess whether japan has achieved tangible results in the elimination of non-tariff barriers. similarly, the eu can no longer afford to negotiate trade agreements without reciprocity in opening up public procurement. only proportionate and reciprocal trade will help to revive growth and employment in europe and worldwide.
in writing. the european union and japan, two of the world's leading economic powers, need to maintain balanced trade relations. eu-japan trade must therefore be based on the principles of reciprocity and loyalty for the mutual benefit of both parties. it is therefore essential that the japanese authorities show good will in removing non-tariff barriers on their markets, particularly in the pharmaceutical and automotive sectors. european companies must be able to invest in japanese markets under the same conditions of openness as japanese companies in european markets. if japan does not produce tangible results in the short term on the elimination of tariff barriers on its markets, the european union could then suspend negotiations on the possible conclusion of a free trade agreement. indeed, no one in europe would understand why the principles of balance and reciprocity should not be applied between japan and the eu, which have reached a comparable level of development.

mr president, commissioner, by adopting mr ferber's report, the european parliament will be drawing important lessons from the mif i directive, by adopting a text which will mean that almost all financial transactions will have to be carried out on regulated platforms. that is the sense we should give to this text. high frequency trading, a technique that allows a large number of orders to be executed in a few milliseconds, will now be heavily regulated. the crisis has exposed abusive practices related to the use of high-frequency trading by some financial actors disrupting the functioning of financial markets in order to make substantial profits. the position adopted by parliament is a good one, discouraging the use of this practice; it will help to put finance back in its place, in the service of the real economy and long-term investment. the report also aims to prevent speculation in foodstuffs, which can be devastating for entire populations, by imposing limits on the positions of the various players on the trading platforms. the destabilising effects of commodity speculation are becoming increasingly evident, particularly in food markets. in this context, the proposals adopted today are a first step in the right direction, since they impose limits on the positions that can be taken by traders on trading platforms. this report also provides us with a significant step forward: the european securities and markets authority, esma, will be able to intervene to prohibit the sale of certain financial products whose toxicity to the economy has been recognised. i would like to conclude by commenting on an important point which links the debate between the mif i and the text we are going to vote on here. in its examination of mif i, the main contribution of the european parliament concerned the question of the advice to be given to investors, in particular small investors, when they undertook an investment. the conditions for financing this council are still a matter of debate and we need to clarify them to ensure that everyone, regardless of income, can have access to this council under conditions which are both transparent and which actually enable him to be wise in his investment.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, today's report is an assessment of what has become an important element of european economic governance. i would like to thank the rapporteurs for the groups with whom i have been able to do - and this is not just words - real constructive work and i believe that this report, as a whole, reflects the concerns of all of them, even if not all of them have been strictly taken up. this report was also drawn up in close cooperation, in accordance with rule 50, with the committee on employment and social affairs, which is why a number of provisions were included in full in the report, without a vote, in such a way as to fully respect these rules and the ideas of the committee on employment and social affairs; it was the rules that prevailed. i shall not go into detail on the various points on which we insist from the point of view of the content of the semester; i would like to speak instead about what has been our main concern, namely the method. the six-month period is, as i said, a very important element in the establishment of coordination of the economic and financial policies of the member states and it involves both the european and the national levels. this is the first innovation. if the commission's proposals are to be subsequently approved by the council before they are reflected as far as possible in the national budgets, then, as far as democratic control is concerned, there is a need for good understanding and coordination with the national parliaments. in this respect we know - and i think no one will mind me saying this - that some of our national parliaments do not have a full understanding of community mechanisms and that there is a certain apprehension that the european level will take over from the national level. that is why some people argue, quite rightly, that national sovereignty gives them the right to vote on the budget they want and that they do not have to follow instructions or oukases that come from elsewhere. there is certainly a lot of work to be done in terms of teaching and explaining, and more recently a meeting was held in brussels with representatives of the finance and economic committees of the national parliaments to explain the european semester. i have had the opportunity to say, as rapporteur, that the european parliamentarians had no intention of interfering in national relations and the functioning of national parliaments and that, in reality, the european parliament and national parliaments had a specific mission, that of ensuring democratic control at their level. i believe that in future such consultation meetings will be necessary to promote understanding of the system and its proper application. in this respect, it would certainly be desirable if these meetings, which are being organized in a rather empirical way at present, could be more formal and, in particular, those who come to these meetings could do so on a regular basis, so that a real dialogue could be established between the national parliaments and the european parliament. on methodological issues, we also stress the need, for example, for more explicit recommendations to enable the results to be evaluated and possibly corrected. i would also add that it is also important - this may seem obvious, but unfortunately the opposite is often the case - that the states keep their commitments.

in writing. the compromise to be voted on tomorrow marks an important step in the fight against terrorism, as it limits the general public's access to products that can be used as precursors in the manufacture of homemade explosives. the regulation identifies dangerous substances, listed in the annex, which will be banned from the public beyond certain concentration limits. we want to prevent as much as possible that malicious people have access to these substances. however, for the normal use of these products, the framework we will adopt allows flexibility through the possibility of limited derogations. it is therefore provided that member states may allow the purchase of such products by persons who obtain a licence from their administration. in addition, a more flexible control system is provided for three products which are widely used by the general public, for example as fertilisers or pool cleaners. finally, any suspicious transactions will have to be notified by traders to the competent authorities. these provisions increase the safety of european citizens by better controlling the purchase, use and possession of explosives precursors within the eu.

mr president, the technologies for accessing the internet are advancing at a remarkable rate. it is now childish to connect to the internet from a computer, mobile phone or tablet, whether at home or in a public place. this widespread access is an opportunity, but also a danger for our children. indeed, the internet can easily become a no-go zone. young users, who spend an average of two hours a day surfing, are often exposed to inappropriate, violent or pornographic images and content, and are easy targets for scams or harassment. the european union has a responsibility in the face of this danger. it must coordinate the member states' screening actions and strike a balance between the protection of children and the safeguarding of fundamental freedoms. it is essential that the union and the member states strengthen both enforcement measures to combat abuse and educational and pedagogical measures to raise awareness among children, parents and educators of the dangers of digital technologies.

of legislation from a technical point of view, which also serve to reduce the legislation in force. i am also glad that, as regards the typeapproval of agricultural and forestry vehicles, i made a commitment during my hearing as the commissioner-designate for industry and i am glad that i have kept the commitment i made but also that the measure has been approved by parliament. the long negotiations, as mr panzeri has pointed out, have produced positive results. i want to thank both speakers, but also the shadow speakers: the compromise texts are the result of a series of constructive discussions, including with the commission and the council, which lasted almost two years because, as we said, this is a very complex matter, even from a technical point of view. i would like to stress that the new regulations will substantially improve the environmental and safety performance of all the vehicles we are discussing, to the benefit of citizens and society as a whole, and they also provide sufficient time for industry to adapt production to the new requirements. in addition, the simplification amendments contained in the two legislative texts will enable public administrations and companies to reduce costs: so we've been able to get a number of positive results. the adoption of these two legislative acts represents an important step forward in the simplification envisaged by the better regulation project and also in consolidating the internal market, as was emphasised in the speeches of the two rapporteurs. the two proposed regulations in fact repeal and replace some 40 directives, each of which is accompanied by a number of delegated and implementing acts, on which i have taken note of mr van de camp's request and therefore we will also follow closely the aspect which the rapporteur has stressed. the consistency between the two type-approval schemes has also been improved. i should like to mention some of the main points in the two texts. first, provisions on access to repair and maintenance information have been introduced to ensure a level playing field for the benefit of operators and consumers. secondly, market surveillance requirements have been introduced. thirdly, a consistent classification of the different vehicle categories has been introduced: a special case concerns special purpose vehicles, i.e. off-road and side-by-side vehicles, which may fall within the classifications of both regulations if they are compatible with the relevant definitions and technical requirements. fourthly, the environmental and safety protection of the vehicles concerned has been improved: i shall not go into the details of the individual proposals, because that has already been made very clear by the rapporteurs. these are just a few of the many points which have been discussed and agreed by parliament and the council, with very satisfactory results, i would say. i would like to thank parliament once again for allowing me to keep the commitment i made to you and to the citizens, which i believe is good for the community institutions at a time when there is often a lack of confidence in us. to work well and to keep our promises is also to respond in a concrete way to the messages we receive from many parts of europe.
for the gue/ngl group madam president, if we want to regulate everything at once, we end up making regulation incomprehensible and ineffective. could we believe that quad bikes, electric bikes, mini bikes, sidecars, cross bikes, really belonged to the same category of vehicles? of course not! especially if some of these vehicles are, moreover, used outside the purpose for which they were created. it is therefore particularly relevant to create subcategories. consider just one class of motor vehicles. quads, like mini-bikes or mini-quads, have become in a few years a real scourge of modern times because used by a minority of their pilots outside the dedicated sites, in conditions of characterized insecurity. they have become dangerous to pedestrians, cyclists and animals, and are involved in many environmental degradations. in addition, they are often produced at low cost and do not generally meet the safety requirements for use on public roads. in france, 61% of the victims of accidents caused by quad bikes, mini-bikes or mini-quads are children under the age of 10. these machines are accident-prone by nature. that is why we feel it is essential to legislate as a matter of priority, giving even greater force to the law on safety, on pilot training, on noise emissions, on road conditions, the aim being - everyone understands this - to protect both the drivers who respect the rules and the affected populations. it would also seem to us to be appropriate to define a european concept of enhanced safety and compulsory recycling and, above all, to prohibit all imports which do not comply with this concept.

on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the euro area is once again entering a recession. the exit strategy, which was advocated until last june by the council or the commission, has plunged us deeper into the crisis. euroscepticism is gaining ground. in this context, the van rompuy report, which is intended to define the next stage of economic and monetary union, is of particular importance. unfortunately, the council has refused to involve the european parliament fully in the drafting of this road map. the report by our colleague marianne thyssen is therefore an opportunity for parliament to take part in this debate and send a strong message. i welcome the rapporteur's remarkable work, which has shown that constructive spirit, which makes it possible to show our fellow citizens that parliamentary debate has meaning. the point of this debate is to establish the levers that are sorely lacking in the functioning of economic and monetary union. firstly, we need an integrated banking union to control banks, guarantee deposits and resolve crises without making taxpayers pay again. secondly, we need a fiscal union, in which the fiscal seriousness of the member states is matched by support for sustainable development at european level. this union must have a budgetary capacity fed by new own resources, the allocation of which must be discussed within the framework of the community method, the only guarantee of solidarity between the 27 member states. thirdly, we need a genuine democratic seal, otherwise the transfer of sovereignty will continue to be experienced by our fellow citizens as a confiscation of powers by bureaucrats. parliament, the main actor in representative democracy, must therefore be involved at every stage of the european semester. parliament must be involved in the operation of the european stability mechanism. parliament must be able to control the troika, especially when the imf itself admits that it has been gravely mistaken. last but not least, we need a social pillar - the fifth pillar - which guarantees wage standards to prevent structural reforms from causing a downward spiral. a social pillar which prevents budgetary discipline from reducing the quality of public services and social protection. a social pillar that promotes the integration of young people into the labour market and access to housing for all. a social pillar that reassures our fellow citizens, for whom europe is synonymous with saving the banks on the one hand, but worsening the situation of the majority on the other. this is the strong mandate which the european parliament must give to its president on the eve of the november and december council meetings. this message will be all the more clearly heard in the council if it obtains the largest possible majority tomorrow - thanks to you, my dear colleagues.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. this report is a proposal for a recast of the brussels i regulation in favour of the european consumer. this reform is a real change in the legal framework of our single market: from now on, a consumer will be able to sue a seller or company outside the eu in his home country. moreover, any judicial decision recognised in one member state will be automatically recognised in all the other member states.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text which will allow for a better valorisation of european agricultural products. the european union must support the agricultural sector, which remains an important economic actor in the economy of our territories. in addition, beyond these economic considerations, it is now essential to promote the production of our farmers who undoubtedly contribute to the promotion of our land throughout the world and contribute to the preservation of noble traditions.
in writing. europe, with its diverse landscapes and cultures, has the opportunity to offer a variety of high-quality agricultural products. the cap offers instruments for the promotion and information of these agricultural products, which must be developed and adapted to demand while taking better account of the constraints on our farmers. this is the whole point of the report by josé bové, which my group adopted on tuesday, 20 november, with a large number of amendments. the rules on food safety and health, environmental conditions and animal welfare are much stricter in europe than in the rest of the world. these are the conditions needed to meet the concerns of consumers alarmed by the mad cow and e. coli crisis. but the trade-off for such constraints is the assurance of offering quality products that should be better promoted in europe and the rest of the world, especially in emerging markets. we have a unique agricultural heritage in europe because of the variety and quality of the products it offers. it is up to us to increase the world's markets in order to contribute to the growth of the agricultural sector.
in writing. the promotion of european agricultural products, both of a high diversity and quality, is essential to ensure the competitiveness and long-term sustainability of the sector. however, only 0,1% of the cap budget was spent on the promotion of these products in 2012. this resolution calls for an ambitious european policy in this area, and i support it. i welcome the emphasis on local and regional markets in the text, which states that a promotion policy should focus on the diversity and freshness of products and the proximity between producers and consumers. as regards external markets, i support the idea that we must make the most of the high demands placed on our producers in order to increase the market outlets for their products. in addition, european wine consumption is steadily declining, without any internal promotion measures for this product. given the importance of the wine sector in my constituency, i am pleased that the text raises the idea of information campaigns for the adult population on responsible consumption of quality european wines, highlighting the qualitative properties and characteristics of european wines.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the promotion of agricultural products, which aims to draw attention to the authentic, varied and high-quality 'tastes of europe' for the consumer. if, historically, agricultural promotion measures were introduced to deal with agricultural surpluses and then food crises, it is now time to define a policy in this area that encourages quality products, as well as more co2-saving practices that protect biodiversity and are better suited to soil protection. to this end, a clear definition of the objectives of the promotion policy for agricultural products is a necessary first step and cannot be separated from a significant increase in the budget devoted to it. the development of short supply chains is indeed needed to economically stimulate and socially requalify rural life, or to show schoolchildren, through educational actions, how food is produced and what life is like in rural areas. the european union should also strive to export a sustainable model of agriculture and the products derived from it. just need to put the good talk into practice.
in writing. while we hear about relocations all the time, we have an example in the food chain that proves that the eu is still a production land. the food industry is the largest employer in europe, with 4.2 million workers and a turnover of €1 trillion per year. if this sector is now profitable and creating jobs, it is thanks to the cap and its quality products, which allow the eu to be the second largest exporter of agricultural products. but we must not rest on our laurels and ensure our leading position in the international market. this is precisely the point of this report, which i supported, and which proposes to highlight our assets by means of an appealing, ambitious and targeted promotion policy. i am thinking of our quality labels, european cuisine, environmental and health standards in production. what may have initially appeared as constraints for the sector has become one of the selling points, which strengthen our position in the global market, where consumers are increasingly looking for quality and authenticity.
in writing. this excellent report, which has the support of the european parliament, gives a snapshot of the state of play in the art sector. this growing field (particularly in china) has been regulated at european level by a directive since 2001. the text stresses the importance of fair remuneration for authors and the need to review the appropriateness of applicable rates and thresholds. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the 'right of way' directive. i believe it is essential to guarantee authors of graphic and visual art a financial share in the success of their original works and to rapidly harmonise the application of copyright in the european union.
in writing. this report, which i supported and which was adopted by the european parliament, is a procedural act designed to simplify the ordinary legislative procedure. it is important that these rules of procedure are adapted so that the european parliament can become more efficient without compromising the transparency of its work.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of article 70 of the regulation on interinstitutional negotiations in legislative procedures. it is important to make procedures both more transparent, more efficient and more participatory, as advised by the conference of presidents in october 2012. in this sense, i support the introduction of a new article 70a on the approval of a decision to open interinstitutional negotiations before the adoption of a report by the committee on budgets.
in writing. it is true that the rapporteur's proposals and certain amendments seem to democratize and clarify a number of current legislative practices. but the root of the problem is that the adoption of vital legislative reports is now done in small committees. the rapporteur is appointed, which is logical. but now there are also fictitious rapporteurs (one per group) who pre-empt the work of the parliament's ad hoc committee. in the most serious cases, a handful of people are appointed from the outset to negotiate with the council and the commission, without representing political sensitivities, in order to reach a compromise adopted at first reading as soon as possible. the result is that, with or without debate in plenary, we are now adopting more and more reports which are actually adopted by a tiny minority of our technical colleagues. european laws are actually decided by five or six quidams who are supposed to have the expertise. the powerful technocratic commission at the centre, 27 member states, the majority of which are weak, a few members invested with the divine light of the other, that is what constitutes the legislative power of the european union. that is why i abstained on this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the guerrero salom report on interinstitutional negotiations in legislative procedures. the amendment is to amend the parliament's rules of procedure, in particular with regard to the internal working methods of our institution. this text is nevertheless important for our citizens because it improves the transparency of the negotiations before a compromise between the three institutions. in order for the text adopted by meps to be representative of the positions in parliament, we had to change our rules of procedure and make our procedures more transparent, more efficient and more participatory.
in writing. i welcome the proposal to inform all meps in their own language when negotiations are opened between a delegation from parliament and other european institutions, and to have the delegation's mandate approved by the plenary. i regret that the obligation to provide information in all languages does not apply to the minutes of the negotiations which the delegation will have to make before its parliamentary committee. this type of information should be easily accessible in their own language to all members of the european parliament. we work on and vote on all the reports that are passed in plenary and not just those that are passed in the committees of which we are members. we must therefore be able to obtain information easily and in our own language about all the work of parliament. there is an urgent need to redirect parliament's investments in this direction.
in writing. the text i supported aims to streamline the translation process within our institution. translation plays a key role in european democracy by making the work of parliamentarians accessible to all citizens. however, in order to save money and given the availability of video recordings of the debates translated into all the official languages of the european union, the debates will no longer be translated into written form. the content will remain accessible on the internet, at anytime and in all the working languages of the european union, through the live translated videos of the debates. modern technology has thus saved money.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of rules 181 and 182 concerning the in extenso report of the debate and the audio-visual recording of the debate. as part of the implementation of the 2013 budget's cost-saving measures and given the size of the budget allocated to translation in the european institutions, we need to make translation savings without jeopardising multilingualism. the minutes will therefore now reflect the speeches of members only in their original language.
in writing. in these times of budgetary discipline, the european parliament is setting an example. i voted for a sensible measure: to amend the rules of procedure of the european parliament so as to stop translating the minutes in extenso of plenary sessions, but without jeopardizing multilingualism. this translation was far too expensive. this will save nearly €8.6 million a year. however, all languages will remain represented in the final report, and those who wish to follow the discussions can continue to watch the videos on the internet, where they will have real-time interpretation in their own language.
in writing. i voted against this report. the aim here is to make a very small saving in the translation of the debates in their entirety into all the official languages of the european union. the so-called in extenso report will be available in writing only in the languages in which the speeches were delivered. those who would like to have access to the whole debate in their own language are asked to refer to the video broadcast, accompanied by translations which are clearly stated to be unreliable because they are simultaneous and therefore subject to human error. the catch is that they can do this if they are able to find themselves on the parliament's website, which is not within the reach of the first citizen to come as the website of this institution is complex, not intuitive and not user-friendly. either way, this access is limited in time. in short. the policy of transparency and openness that you boast about is an absolute hypocrisy.
in writing. we adopted a report for which i was the fictitious rapporteur for the epp in the afco committee. the report concerns the amendment of parliament's rules of procedure as regards rule 181, the in extenso report and rule 182 on the audiovisual recording of debates. in view of the tight budgetary context, the european parliament also wanted to make an effort by adopting savings measures for the 2012 budget. the bureau and the committee on budgets reached an agreement on 26 september 2011 that the systematic translation of the in extenso minutes of our plenary debates into all languages should be stopped. however, the same agreement provided for the retention of an in extenso english translation for convenience. i considered that translating the reports into one language, english, would create a hierarchy in the official languages of the union and would call multilingualism into question. i therefore wanted to propose that the minutes should reproduce the speeches of members in their original language and that the single translation into english should be deleted. and this too, by pushing the logic of translation savings to the limit. the majority of afco, and then the whole parliament, followed suit.
in writing. i voted in favour of the ilchev report on the amendment of parliament's rules of procedure concerning rule 181 on the in extenso report and rule 182 on the audio-visual recording of debates. with this report parliament is introducing significant cost reductions in the field of translation, since the in extenso reports which reproduce the speeches of members in their original language will no longer be translated into the other languages.
in writing. under the pretext of budgetary savings, this report makes translations of plenary speeches compulsory only if a member of the european parliament requests them! the fact that we are saving money on the translation work of members of parliament is absolutely shameful. with such a system, no research on the speeches of meps is possible, neither for parliamentarians nor for european citizens! we are referred to the video of the oral speeches (so nothing for the written speeches) and their unofficial translation. these are not working methods! parliamentary assistants must now listen to and transcribe speeches and citizens must guess where the videos are hidden to access information! i denounce this harmful report and call on my colleagues to reconsider their priorities in terms of budgetary savings.
in writing. the text, which was widely adopted by the european parliament, aims to reform the rules on two- or three-wheel vehicles and quadricycles. one of the key points is the mandatory introduction of affordable advanced braking systems (anti-lock braking system (abs) or combined braking system (cbs)) on all new motorcycles.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the approval and market surveillance of two- or three-wheel vehicles and quadricycles. i support this report, which aims to simplify the current legal framework and introduce new administrative and technical requirements, particularly in the areas of safety and the environment.
in writing. thanks to the adoption of this report, motorcycles will now be safer and cleaner. technology is advancing rapidly, and every day it is making the road safer. we adapt the rules to take account of these developments, and make the most of them. this text will make motorcycles safer thanks to abs and better monitored to reduce accidents.
in writing. within the european union, 16% of road deaths are two-wheelers, while they account for only 2% of road traffic. this statistic is unbearable. reducing it requires both improving the safety of motorcycles and related vehicles and of road infrastructure. from anti-lock brakes for cylinders over 125 cc to automatic lighting, the proposals are moving in the right direction. but the development of road areas deserves the attention of this parliament as well. we know the dangers of certain infrastructures such as slippery white stripes and sharp safety slides. these are matters that merit further consideration. finally, road safety prevention must be strengthened. we must think of a real culture of prevention and of probably more frequent awareness campaigns. in this connection, i would point out that the long-running awareness raising campaigns against domestic accidents have proved effective. they should inspire us.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which improves transparency and access to information for users of the two and three-wheel vehicle market. the new safety and environmental measures will benefit all european citizens, as reductions in accidents and co2 emissions are expected to be achieved.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i think it is important that we have safer and greener motorcycles. vehicles such as mopeds, scooters, motorcycles, all-terrain vehicles and quads number 30 million in the eu. they account for only 2% of traffic, yet they account for 16% of fatal accidents on european roads. we cannot leave the users of these vehicles in such a dangerous situation. it is therefore necessary that these vehicles meet very stringent safety and emission standards. the aim is to make motorcycles and similar vehicles safer, for example by including more brake assist systems (abs or cbs), and more environmentally friendly (harmonisation with european standards). the automatic lighting of headlamps will also be encouraged, although this will be left to the discretion of the member states. the text will also benefit manufacturers, who will benefit from a new regulation replacing the 15 existing directives. this should simplify their market and give them more visibility and prospects.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by a large majority on tuesday 20 november of the report on the approval and monitoring of the two- and three-wheel and quadricycle market, which represents 30 million vehicles on the road in the european union. these vehicles account for 16% of fatal accidents on europe's roads, although they account for only 2% of road traffic. new administrative and technical rules were therefore needed to ensure that these vehicles are better protected and reduce their emissions. the main points i would like to make about this proposal are the mandatory introduction of anti-lock braking systems (abs) and combined braking systems (cbs), automatically-ignited headlamps to make these vehicles more visible and the strengthening of sanctions against individuals who, by illegal manipulations, increase the maximum speed of their vehicle and therefore constitute a danger to the safety of other road users.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the approval and market surveillance of two- or three-wheelers and quadricycles to make two-wheelers safer and greener. these vehicles represent only 2% of road traffic but are involved in 16% of fatal accidents in europe. from 2016, anti-lock braking systems and combined braking systems will be installed on motorcycles and scooters.
in writing. two- and three-wheel vehicles are involved in 16% of fatal accidents on european roads, although they account for only 2% of road traffic. in addition, these vehicles emit disproportionately large amounts of air pollutants. the rules in force must be revised to make these vehicles both safer and less polluting, and i welcome the adoption of this text by parliament. from 2016, the most powerful motorcycles (above 125cc) will have to be equipped with anti-lock braking systems (abs), and the least powerful (below 125cc) will have to be equipped with at least combined braking systems (cbs). in addition, to improve the visibility of motorcycles and drivers, automatic headlamp lighting will be introduced when the engine is started. the text also increases the requirements for compliance with the emission standards of these vehicles: these requirements will increase gradually and will reach the euro 5 standard in 2020. the text also provides for the introduction of increasingly advanced on-board diagnostic (obd) systems, which will enable vehicle malfunctions to be detected and repairs to be carried out quickly when necessary.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new type-approval rules for two- and three-wheel vehicles and quadricycles, as they should ultimately provide a safety boost for two-wheelers, who are very vulnerable, since they account for one sixth of all deaths for only 2% of the distance travelled on european roads. the abs will now be compulsory for motorcycles over 125 cc, and the additional cost should be largely limited by the generalization of this equipment, as was the case in the automobile. in addition, new pollution standards will be applied gradually between 2016 and 2020. finally, the entry into force of this regulation in 2016 will see the end of the 100 hp bridging of french motorcycles, which had never really proven its effectiveness in road safety and which could pose problems of insurance coverage, in the case of an unbridged vehicle purchased abroad for example.

in writing. this report, which i supported, is the european parliament's response to the european commission's green paper on card, internet and mobile payments. it's a growing industry. it is necessary to give it a framework without hindering its development. we also call for the development of global standards, not just european ones.

in writing. thanks to the single market, you can now travel and shop anywhere in europe. however, as europeans are well aware, it is not always possible to buy things the way we would like. our cards, our internet purchases and, increasingly, our mobile phone purchases are still too often constrained by techniques and measures which impede the common market. it is to put an end to this incoherence that i voted in favour of this report. i am committed to this subject: i have in particular stressed during the drafting of this text the importance of taking better account of all the actors involved, and the paramount aspect of payment security for users. i will continue to work for consumers, traders and businesses.
in writing. harmonising european rules on credit card payments will make life easier for european citizens, who are increasingly mobile and increasingly use card payments over the internet. payments by credit card, internet or telephone will now be more secure and cheaper. currently, the fees for processing card payments are often too high. by making costs more transparent, operators will thus be encouraged to compare the invoiced cost with the actual cost. the establishment of a single card payment system modelled on the single euro payments area (sepa) is a step forward, as this mechanism has proven its effectiveness in improving cross-border bank transfers throughout the territory of the states parties. citizens will now be able to make payments in one country from an account in another. finally, the commission will need to establish clear and objective rules so that certain file hosting sites or services are not excluded from online payment without justification.
in writing. in view of the explosion in internet and mobile payments, the european commission has considered it necessary to draw up an overview of payment methods in europe in order to identify gaps between the current situation and the prospects for an integrated payments market. it is estimated that several million businesses and hundreds of millions of citizens are affected by these payment methods. in 2009, 58 billion retail payment transactions were carried out in the euro area alone. it is therefore important that the european institutions, whose task it is to anticipate and prevent obstacles, have decided to look into this issue and to propose measures to create the conditions for an integrated market for card, internet and mobile payments. all measures and regulations which can facilitate information and remove barriers for consumers must be supported. that is why i welcome the fact that the european parliament has spoken on this subject.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on 'payment by card, internet and mobile phone'. while payments take many forms that diversify with technological advances and make it easier for citizens to access various goods through distance purchasing, there is still room for improvement. there are weaknesses identified by consumers which are not acceptable, such as the fact that certain crossborder transactions are not accepted because of their origin. the costs involved are not sufficiently transparent and one can wonder about the excessive fees charged for cash withdrawals at atms outside the bank. the development of the digital economy must therefore be accompanied by transparent, secure and efficient payment systems to facilitate cross-border trade. the diversity of payment instruments and the creation of innovative payment methods should not compromise the security of payments. security standards for internet payments should be improved to ensure secure conditions for transactions.
in writing. with my support and the broad support of the european parliament, this text is the continuation of the banking decisions taken at the g20 following the 2008 crisis. although the european union is ahead in this implementation, several areas are still lagging behind, notably the shadow banking system (evading, hidden accounts, etc.) and this text is the first step towards their inclusion in a more transparent system.
in writing. five years after the financial crisis, european citizens are still waiting for the conclusions and lessons to be drawn from the legislation that would put an end to the most questionable practices in the financial economy. it is not only clear that lessons have not been learned and that we are still exposed to terrible financial shocks, but that practices have also been widely developed. this is particularly the case for shadow banking. the black hole of international finance, the billions of euros that are pouring into it are totally out of control. it's incomprehensible and irresponsible. the european parliament is therefore right to point the finger at this nonsense and must continue its work to move forward on this fundamental subject.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the shadow banking system. today, the shadow banking system represents 30% of the entire financial system, and in 2011, it had brought in over 50 trillion euros in 2011. the parallel banking system is the non-bank credit activities, whose benefits and risks need to be balanced. the report aims to increase prudential oversight to reduce the systemic risks posed by this system. i support the two major measures advocated in this report, namely the application of a capital regime to unregulated entities and the strengthening of the collection of data on transactions in this sector.
in writing. the shadow banking system is almost a third of our financial system, and almost half of the assets of banks. yes, it has played a sometimes harmful role in the outbreak and development of the crisis we are experiencing. for this reason, it is essential to provide better guidance. i voted for this because it takes a threat-proportionate approach: where its activities are potentially dangerous, the shadow banking sector must be regulated. where they are useful and complementary to the ordinary banking sector, they must not be impeded. the commission must now develop an arsenal suited to these challenges.
in writing. the parallel banking , which includes the intermediary credit activities of insurance companies and the activities of most hedge funds , is a booming market. it now represents 30% of the global financial system, or nearly $67 trillion. in a period of shrinking bank lending, this system of credit distribution deserves our full attention. while the european union benefits from the positive effects of this sector, it must also guard against the risks of drift inherent in this type of activity, particularly because the latter mainly contribute to the financing of risky projects via short-term loans, a potential source of destabilisation. the subprime mortgage crisis of 2007 and the financial crisis that immediately followed are arguments in this direction. there is therefore a need for an adequate legal framework, with transparent regulation and supervision, to safely ensure the recovery of our economy.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which strengthens controls on non-bank credit to avoid the kind of abuses we have experienced in the past and which are one of the causes of the current economic crisis. a stricter and more harmonised banking regulation in europe can only be beneficial for citizens.
in writing. the shadow banking system represents 25 to 30% of the entire financial system and half of the total assets of banks. the commission, with its green paper (of 19 march 2012) has set a first milestone on the way to a genuine control and supervision of the shadow banking system. this approach is based on indirect regulation of the system. but it is regrettable that there has been no criticism of the decisive role that banks as a whole have played in the present sovereign debt crisis. it is a direct regulation extended to some of its aspects that should be implemented. the proposed regulation seems to me to be quite inadequate, particularly in terms of consumer protection, and will not prevent financial institutions from transferring risky assets to these less regulated entities such as shadow banks. in particular, the commission could work towards changes in ifrs so that aggregates without compensation or risk weighting receive greater attention. i therefore abstained on this vote, which does not call into question the relationship between the banking system in general and these 'shadow players', whose number has increased considerably in recent years (short explanation of vote pursuant to rule 170 of the rules of procedure).

in writing. in europe, internet use by children is becoming commonplace. for example, a study shows that almost all children aged 9 to 16 in the eu use a computer for play or homework. while internet use can help children to learn and develop, it also exposes them to the dangers of violence, fraud, and pornography, all of which are often unknown to parents. by voting in favour of this resolution, i am asking that children be better protected in the digital world. to do this, i am particularly in favour of using additional technological options to prevent children from accessing content that is inappropriate for their age (parental controls, age verification systems, etc.). it also seems to me crucial that children, parents and educators are better trained in the use of new digital media. in addition, i believe that better coordination at european level of contact points such as hotlines for reporting illegal content or abusive behaviour, and better cooperation with third countries for the rapid removal of inappropriate content from sites hosted on their territory, are essential.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the protection of children in the digital world. the digital world offers a powerful tool for communication, information and education. children today are entering this world earlier and earlier. parents are not always able to protect their children in this complex and rewarding world that also presents dangers - commercial solicitation, sexual assault, harassment on social networks, and so on. i supported this report, which allows for better coordination of action at union level. this protection includes digital education, the fight against illegal and harmful content for minors, the protection of privacy and the right of reply. this report has managed to combine these two main principles, the protection of children and the defence of freedoms.
in writing. adopted by the european parliament, this own-initiative report, which i supported, is a text of general policy on social entrepreneurship. a real call to support the social and solidarity-based economy at european level, i followed this theme with interest, being myself rapporteur on a related text concerning the creation of a european label for investment funds wishing to invest in social entrepreneurship.
in writing. with almost 11 million employees in europe, the social economy sector is a key component of the so-called social market economy that the european union is seeking to develop. because it meets a double requirement - economic and social - and aims to meet social needs not or poorly met by both the market and the state, and because it is part of a logic of social and territorial cohesion, the sector has considerable advantages, especially in times of crisis. the aim today is to facilitate and support its development in all the member states, since it is a sector which is still undervalued and little recognised. i therefore welcome the adoption of the becker report which emphasizes all these elements and sets out some lines of action. i also supported mr vergiat's alternative resolution which sought to highlight the diversity of the sector, particularly in france, and to recall the difference between the social and solidarity economy sector and social enterprises. in the report we ask for a comparative study of the existing frameworks in the member states, but also for more flexibility in access to financial support.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the social entrepreneurship initiative. the report proposes to stimulate the creation of social enterprises, since they, like smes, are responsible for job creation, which is the european union's number one priority at the moment. i am also pleased that the social label, a project i have been working on for two years, has been included in paragraph 28 of the report, thanks to our voluntary work and the support of all the political groups. this is good news for the future of the social label, which is not limited to social enterprises alone, but to all companies wishing to promote compliance with social standards at work.
in writing. social enterprises are good for growth, they are a guarantee of inclusion and innovation. they already represent almost 11 million jobs. however, there is no clear legal framework for them. the commission has sought to lay the foundations for accompanying framework conditions. in voting in favour of this report, i am calling for more precision, but also for more ambition. it is time for local, national and european authorities to take an active role in supporting them.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report 'social entrepreneurship initiative' to support the action of companies whose aim is to provide goods or services to vulnerable people and who use their profits to achieve a social objective. a strategy and measures to promote social entrepreneurship are important for the development of this sector.
in writing. supporting social entrepreneurship is a good thing. but we need to agree on what we hear about it. social entrepreneurship cannot be limited to providing services to vulnerable, marginalised or excluded people. nor can it be intended to replace public services. its staff must be salaried and not volunteers. that is a number of points on which this report is at least vague. so we must be on our guard. the insistence on making social enterprises "competitive" enterprises in the context of the "social market economy" is equally worrying, because competitiveness is not the aim of a social enterprise. despite all these worrying aspects, i welcome the fact that this report pays particular attention to the recognition of social enterprises and supports increased support for social enterprises. i'll abstain from it.
in writing. this text, which i supported, aims to implement a real banking union between the member states. it is the european parliament's response to president van rompuy's initiative to redefine economic and monetary union. it also proposes to go further in fiscal union and economic union between member states while strengthening democratic accountability. the aim is to maximise the possibilities offered by the treaties in order to avoid any amendments - or new ratification - which would be particularly time-consuming. in this time of crisis, it seems to me that european integration is a big part of the solution. it makes it possible to manage better, to rationalize expenditure and to coordinate actions better. this is particularly true within the euro area, but the door remains open to anyone who would like to join us.
in writing. alongside banking supervision, the need for a genuine european budget based on own resources, and the strengthening of the fight against tax evasion, improving democratic legitimacy is crucial. it goes without saying that the union has been going through a deep crisis for some years now - an economic, social, societal, institutional and ultimately a crisis of meaning. that is why the idea of a social pact is fundamental to me. it is the idea that the union must be based on a fifth pillar - in addition to the four pillars put forward in the report by the presidents. the social dimension is the poor relation of the union's action in this period of crisis. binding rules on budgetary discipline and the monitoring of economic and budgetary policies must be accompanied by rules on employment and social criteria: we therefore call for the establishment of a social pact for europe which promotes, in particular, decent wages and the implementation of a social protocol to protect social rights and labour law. the citizens hard hit by the crisis and its social consequences expect more than austerity and fiscal rigor. it is up to the union to show its added value and to recover the meaning it lacks.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on economic and monetary union. i support the recommendations proposed, such as further integration of a financial, budgetary and economic framework, as well as strengthening democratic legitimacy and accountability.
in writing. strengthening economic and monetary union means facing economic and monetary crises with greater weight and coherence, which affect the union as a whole and cause considerable social and industrial damage. this strengthening means more powers for the union. and so this justifies new obligations for the latter but also for the member states. transparency of decisions and information for european citizens are, along with this pattern of increased integration, a necessity for democracy in a society of trust. in the necessary back and forth between the union and its members, which must be one of the union's privileged democratic tools, it is important to involve national parliaments so that they can appreciate the impact of their decisions at european level, just as it is important to involve the european parliament more closely in the policy to be implemented in the economic and monetary field. it would be right, therefore, for the single supervisor and the president of the european stability mechanism to be accountable to the european parliament. this would strengthen their legitimacy in europe but above all at international level, where the balance of power demands it even more. the treaties already allow us to make important reforms. the european parliament has a duty to act. why wait ?
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which calls for the strengthening of the economic and monetary integration of the union. as the eurozone enters a new recession, it is essential that europeans agree on the organisation and decision-making processes within the eurozone in order to pull the continent out of this economic slump. the recent progress has helped to calm the market frenzy, but we must maintain the course and move forward to ensure that the euro area is stable for a long time and that the periods of calm we are experiencing are not just periods of calm before a new storm.
in writing. i am happy to admit that a genuine economic and monetary union, as the rapporteur claims, requires a huge transfer of powers and funds to the european union. budget, taxes, social protection, banking supervision - everything must be the responsibility of the technocrats in brussels and the central bank in frankfurt, according to you. nothing should remain for national governments and parliaments except the financial privileges and material advantages of their members, paid to approve you as they have done for 30 years. the problem is: who wants this, apart from those in this chamber who already see themselves as the absolute masters of a tyrannical europe, sheltered behind a pseudo-democratic legitimacy? no one is! you want confirmation? so for once, have courage. ask the people after a genuine, open, honest and democratic debate! you would never dare, because you know very well the answer they would give you: "fuck you!"
in writing. the crisis we have been experiencing since 2008 has highlighted the fragility of the current architecture of economic and monetary union. we must now learn from the crisis and give the union the necessary framework to ensure its economic and financial stability and prosperity. that's the whole point of this report. i also wanted to support, by my vote, two democratic and social demands which i felt were indispensable in this next wave of integration. firstly, i believe that such a strengthening of economic and monetary union cannot be achieved without stronger democratic guarantees: the involvement and control of the european parliament and the national parliaments are necessary. secondly, in view of the serious social crisis in several member states, i particularly support the recommendation to introduce social and employment criteria, in addition to the existing budgetary and macroeconomic criteria.
in writing. on the eve of a major summit on the future of economic and monetary union, i joined my colleagues in calling for the introduction of a social pact. it is clear that strict policies alone are not effective in helping to overcome the serious endemic crisis with which we have been struggling for several years. i would like to join the socialists and democrats in calling for solutions that do not simply rescue the banks but take account of the challenges of preserving our european social model and give priority to employment and training for young people. moreover, these reforms cannot be carried out without the involvement of the european parliament, the voice of the citizens in europe, and also of the national parliaments. the heads of state or government in the council must realize that if they want to win the support of the peoples of europe for these economic reforms, they must allow democratic control of the measures adopted. this is essential for the democratic legitimacy of this process.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report 'towards a genuine economic and monetary union', which encourages economic integration in the euro area in particular. the report contains useful recommendations towards an integrated financial framework, relating to the single supervisory mechanism, the fight against tax fraud and taxation. these issues are at the heart of the european construction and the challenges it faces.
in writing. this report endorses all the decisions taken at the last two european summits. the budgetary pact, the growth pact, the european semester 2012, europe 2020, it is all there. the text even calls on the states to implement these decisions as soon as possible and calls for the designation of "bad pupils" (sic!). the banking union he promises us is just one more step towards the austerity federalism which the text very explicitly calls for. the usual round of demands for a little more power for the european parliament, of reminders of the importance of social inclusion and solidarity, will not change anything at all. i am voting against this text, its false solutions and its austerity measures.
in writing. the report by marianne thyssen (belgian epp member), instead of giving a genuine critical analysis of the recommendation of the quartet of the council, the commission, the ecb and the eurogroup, endorses all the initial proposals of the commission and the council, including increased surveillance of indebted countries, the adoption by the commission of binding economic policy measures towards member states, the implementation of the 'two-pack', the need to transpose the european stability mechanism into all euro area states. repeating and reaffirming the old recipes, which are dangerous for the population and the poorest, will not help europe to emerge from the crisis but will, on the contrary, contribute to deepening it further, as a growing number of economists argue, at the risk of plunging the continent into recession and dragging many other countries with it. the european parliament has thus missed a unique opportunity to give its views on a process from which it is carefully excluded. i therefore voted against this report.

member of the commission. the commission has already made a number of proposals. in addition to what my colleague mr potočnik has said, i would like to thank the two committees and the two leading members for the reports which show how varied the subject of unconventional energy resources, gas and oil, particularly shale gas, is. it is about environmental protection and also about climate aspects, it is about energy policy, it is about industrial aspects and also about social issues. the three studies commissioned by the commission, which we published a few weeks ago and which we are now analysing, provide a parallel basis for a comprehensive consultation and follow-up in the european union. we must not be fooled: as in many other matters of energy policy, we have had a wide range of opinions and interests on shale gas. some member states are categorically against it, others have moratoriums, and some see shale gas as an important contribution to solving their energy independence. the change in the united states of america is far-reaching: americans are largely independent of gas imports, and will be able to decide whether they are even willing to export gas. the price of gas in the usa is currently only about a quarter to a third of the price of gas payable on the gas markets of the european union. with shale gas, you have flexibility, you get away from long-term supply contracts with high gas prices tied to the world oil market price, and also indirectly, production in the united states of america is making a change for the world market: large quantities of lng, previously shipped from nigeria and qatar to the united states, are now free. they are increasingly being integrated into the energy strategy by japan following the shutdown of nuclear power plants after fukushima and also by europe with existing and planned lng terminals. in our view, for several reasons, it is unthinkable for the european gas market that shale gas meets all our gas needs: according to all initial analyses, our reserves are much lower, the cost of production is rather higher. and of course, the dense settlement of the european union with 500 million people will not reduce to zero the potential that exists in the united states in some of the deserted regions and states, but it will reduce it. acceptance questions are added. we will therefore continue to develop our policy of completing the internal energy market in order to increase security of supply, further develop renewable energy and effectively promote energy efficiency. shale gas is not a substitute for the internal market, energy efficiency or renewable energy sources. it can complement them. we now have a gas market within the eu with an annual consumption of about 540 billion cubic metres. a third of our deposits are produced within the european union, namely in the united kingdom and the netherlands. these potentials, these production volumes, will decline significantly over the next 15 to 20 years. and one chance might be that shale gas can partly replace the traditional production volumes so that in the future not one to one of every cubic metre produced in europe will have to be imported into europe. in this respect, shale gas could contribute to our diversification objective. at the moment we have only a few test drilling operations carried out in the member states. we will therefore be providing sound support for demonstration projects. we need more reliable statements on gas volumes and exploration costs. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the water, and i am sure that the commission will be able to take a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the water. the commission has deliberately included in its 2013 work programme an initiative to be attributed to several commissioners - mr potočnik, mr hedegaard, mr tajani, mr barnier and myself - which will deal with the relevant environmental, climate, energy and industrial aspects. we are particularly interested in the dialogue you have started today, in your speeches, in your opinions and in the very factual reports from both committees as a basis for joint conclusions next year.

mr president, we are having a very passionate debate today on a particularly sensitive subject. i would like to return to the two reports we are discussing and congratulate the two rapporteurs, mr sonik and mrs tzavela, for the very balanced and very realistic approach they have taken to shale gas exploitation. i support them for that, and for a number of reasons. the first is the cost of energy and competitiveness. we are in a period of serious economic crisis: many of our citizens are very concerned about the increase in the price of energy and we know that the energy bill is a fundamental element of the competitiveness of our companies. the example of the united states is very telling in this respect. the second reason is energy independence and diversification. emphasis should be placed on the search for new, less polluting extraction technologies and on strict compliance with safety requirements for the experimentation, exploration and exploitation of this resource. what concerns me is the loss of faith in scientific and technological progress - from which innovation, entrepreneurship and risk-taking are derived - which is undeniably contributing to the deindustrialisation of europe. we therefore need to gather more knowledge and information before we condemn shale gas once and for all. we cannot and will not be able to ignore for long the immense reserves of european shale gas and the opportunity it represents. i therefore do not think that a moratorium is appropriate. what i hope is that, in compliance with subsidiarity and with a strict regulatory framework, respectful of the environment, water resources and security, we can allow member states who wish to take advantage of this opportunity. so we need real regulation. let us start the debate with the studies which have been commissioned by the commission and i am confident that we will be able to obtain a legal framework which will be conclusive.
mr president, commissioner, nobody has mentioned it yet, but i think something important happened on sunday, as the world bank presented its report, announcing that by 2060 global warming would be over four degrees. it's the world bank that's announcing it, which means we're in a serious situation. what this means very concretely is that if we want to prevent this, we're going to have to go from 35 billion cubic meters of co2 in 2050 to 10 billion. that means that we will have to take very strict measures, not just to reduce, but to really divide by two or three our emissions. what this means in very concrete terms is that today, faced with this global and european challenge, we will be forced not to use all the energy available if we do not want to cause global warming to explode. i say this because everyone knows today that methane has a thirty times greater effect on global warming than co2, and that for shale gas, between four and eight percent of the methane escapes into nature from the well to the pipelines. this applies to all methane, of course. so this is a fundamental issue. finally, to illustrate the need for european regulation, i visited a shale gas well near wrocław, which is being drilled by halliburton in poland. there was no reservoir for holding water. the hydraulic fracturing had occurred. the water was back in the wild. that is why we need real legislation and a moratorium in the meantime.
in writing. this parliamentary report presents a balanced and dispassionate approach to a highly controversial subject, and i welcome it. i believe that the choice of the energy mix and the authorization of shale gas extraction are national matters. this is in line with the principle of technological neutrality which i advocate in the context of the energy roadmap 2050 debate. that is why i do not support the idea of a european moratorium on the exploration and extraction of shale gas. it is nevertheless the responsibility of the european union to define rules at european level to ensure environmental protection and high levels of safety. as it stands, hydraulic fracturing is a serious problem that cannot be ignored. there is also talk of large shale oil resources in europe, but no one can say for sure that the potential is promising enough to consider industrial exploitation. so, in order to make informed choices, let us continue to evaluate the presumed reserves and research exploration techniques. we must not close the door on this source of energy, given the developments on the world energy market and the challenges to europe's competitiveness.

in writing. russian wood now accounts for 60% of european imports from the pulp and paper industry. the eu-russia agreement on russian timber imports will thus allow european companies to import russian pine and spruce trees to the eu at preferential tariffs. in the past, the european forestry industry had suffered from import restrictions imposed by russia. this new agreement will thus help to revitalise the sector. it is also an important step towards a more stable and predictable trade relationship with russia, but also towards the affirmation of european trade policy, since for the first time the european union will manage the tariff quotas of a third country.
