in writing. this report adopted by the european parliament has been the focus of all attention. i also voted in favour of this text because i think it is measured and consistent. it recalled that the decision whether or not to exploit shale gas was a matter for the member states and thus recognised the french and bulgarian moratoriums, for example. however, this exploitation is only possible in strict compliance with european environmental legislation such as the water, air and impact studies directives. finally, the european commission is responsible for assessing as soon as possible whether this body of legislation is sufficient or whether it needs to be further strengthened to better protect european citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the environmental impact of shale gas and oil shale extraction activities. the complex debate on shale gas deserves to be taken out of the manichean framework of the problem. in this sense, i am trying to adopt a pragmatic approach: i am opposed to hydraulic fracturing, which is banned in france, because of the disastrous effects it would have on the environment, particularly on groundwater. since the member states are sovereign in the conduct of their energy policy, i could not support mrs rivasi's amendment. however, i am not opposed to the idea of prospecting or research to improve our knowledge of our energy potential. it is worth noting that these resources could help us to reduce our energy dependence and lower the price of gas. it is therefore better not to close the door on the extraction hypothesis, but not at the expense of nature or renewable energies, which represent the future of our consumption model.
in writing. in our view, as french socialists, national and european legislation must be extremely strict, for example on hydraulic fracturing, which is the only known method of extraction at present, in order to prevent any damage to the environment. this is not to deny the importance of energy independence and the place of energy costs in the competitiveness of industry. our priority must be to ensure a high level of protection of human health and the environment. i regret that an amendment which i co-signed calling for a european moratorium on hydraulic fracturing did not find a majority today. despite this setback, i welcome the action of the socialists and democrats, which has been decisive in giving priority to two particularly important principles: the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle.
in writing. public opinion, poisoned by the green lobby, is often hostile to the exploitation of shale gas and oil. these would be bad in themselves. their exploitation techniques would be devastating to water, air and health, and unlikely to evolve or improve rapidly. the economic interest would be disappointing. my country, france, is the only one that has decided to play the ostrich. the government, which is led by a militant minority, refuses not only to exploit the reserves but also to allow exploration to determine whether the estimates of reserves, which are now theoretical and based on computer calculations, are accurate. such an attitude is unlikely to encourage research, whereas hydraulic fracturing without chemicals or pneumatic fracturing are already technically accessible, if not industrially exploitable and economically profitable. in the face of the immense challenges of energy independence, employment, competitiveness and rebalancing the external balance, such an attitude is regrettable. the simple public ownership of the subsoil avoids many of the excesses and abuses that have been observed in the united states and that we are told about. but, strangely enough, the reports voted on today are relatively balanced on the subject. their main fault is that they attempt to circumvent or trample on the energy sovereignty of the states recognized by the treaties. that's why i abstained.
in writing. after a heated debate on shale gas extraction, a real game of ping-pong in the house where, as rapporteur for the deve committee, i was able to express my deep disagreement and raise the concerns of developing countries, particularly in terms of land grabbing and access to water, fertile soils and food, which is potentially a challenge to the food sovereignty of these countries. today we voted on the two reports by the itre and envi committees, finally giving the ep a position on this very controversial subject. if the itre report was pro-shale gas, totally irresponsible and unacceptable, mr sonik's report was more controversial. i finally abstained on the final vote on the latter. the reasons are simple: on the one hand, this report has the merit of taking a stand for an adaptation of european regulations, of increasing the ep's will to control fracturing and of responding to the challenges; on the other hand, the moratorium, or more precisely the amendment urging member states not to allow new hydraulic fracturing operations in the eu, was rejected. i am firmly opposed to the extraction of shale gas.
in writing. on the question of shale gas, we are faced today with many questions but too few answers. that is why i voted today in favour of a very cautious approach, given the risks and negative impacts of hydraulic fracturing on the climate, the environment and health. so far, i do not think it is appropriate for member states to allow hydraulic fracturing in the european union. the polluter pays principle should also be implemented to prevent industrialists from avoiding their responsibilities in the event of an accident.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague boguslaw sonik, which was adopted by 562 votes to 86, with 43 abstentions. this report presents a balanced and dispassionate approach to the controversial issue of shale gas exploitation. the report stresses that the choice of energy mix and the authorisation of shale gas extraction are matters for national competence and calls for strict control of drilling technologies, particularly hydraulic fracturing. the aim is to avoid any damage to the environment.
in writing. the report makes a damning observation about the lack of information we currently have on the consequences of shale gas exploitation and the use of the hydraulic fraction. he acknowledges that this activity can have dangerous consequences for the environment and human health, without drawing the necessary consequences. instead of calling for the practical application of the precautionary principle and recommending to the member states a moratorium on such activities, it merely sets out the framework for such activities in the future. it calls on the member states to exercise caution, as one would urge a suicide bomber not to jump off a bridge too violently. the dangers of shale gas exploitation are well known. the only reasonable position in this matter is to demand an immediate moratorium on this activity. this report does not. it is an unacceptable concession to the gas lobbies which have been active in the european parliament for months. i vote against it.
in writing. i welcome the fact that hydraulic fracturing is not explicitly authorised, that research authorisation is better regulated and that strict implementation of existing waste water treatment standards is called for. the report maintains a binding obligation for all operators to disclose the full composition of chemicals and the concentration of fracking fluids, and to fully comply with eu legislation in force under the reach regulation. today, we don't know how to measure the environmental and health impacts of these gases, but we do know that hydraulic fracturing techniques require a lot of drinking water and chemicals. the risks of water contamination are therefore very real. the european parliament has not really made a choice between the short-term vision of gas monopolies and a long-term vision capable of protecting the vital resource of water for mankind.
in writing. our assembly has just adopted a report which sets out in an objective way the potential impacts and benefits of shale gas extraction in europe. i have supported it wholeheartedly, because i believe that we must be able to know both the environmental risks associated with the extraction of this resource and the competitive advantages it can bring to our economy. i regret the ideological attitude of some members who have tried in vain to ban the exploration and extraction of shale gas throughout the eu without reliable data. i personally voted against this amendment, which goes against the principle of subsidiarity and makes a misuse of the precautionary principle. we can oppose hydraulic fracturing, which poses serious problems that cannot be ignored, but it is not reasonable to close the door categorically to shale gas, while the energy bill of households and businesses keeps increasing and our industries lose competitiveness. i therefore call for a european research programme to assess the available reserves of this resource and to develop environmentally friendly exploitation methods.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on industry, energy and other aspects of shale gas and oil shale. in the context of the energy roadmap 2050 debate, it is essential to uphold the principle of technological neutrality with regard to unconventional hydrocarbons. our strategy must be twofold: on the one hand, in the name of the principle of subsidiarity, the european union cannot impose or prohibit the use of one or another type of energy, and on the other hand, the union must guarantee rules that guarantee a high level of environmental protection. we must therefore continue to research innovative exploration techniques in order to improve our knowledge of our energy resources.
in writing. i voted for the tzavela report, which examines many issues relating to the development of shale gas and oil shale exploitation in the european union. in the interests of diversification of energy sources and security of supply, i support the use of shale gas in a reasonable manner and with all the necessary precautions. i share the view that each member state should be able to decide on its sources of energy supply, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity.

in writing. europe's limited hydrocarbon resources force us to import a large part of the energy we consume: oil comes from african countries, while most of our gas comes from russia. the eu is heavily dependent on the goodwill of these neighbours, who can set gas prices as they please, and in the event of a regional political conflict, such as the one between ukraine and russia from 2005 to 2009, we could find ourselves in a delicate situation. but the discovery of shale gas reserves in europe could change the situation. according to a us study, france's gas reserves are estimated to be equal to 90 years of our current consumption. the exploitation of these gases could restore a degree of energy independence to the eu, reduce the energy bill of businesses and households and lighten our trade balance. the challenge now is to find a technique that can extract them cleanly. that is why i supported this report, which calls for an unbiased and informed approach to this challenge, both economic and environmental. closing the door to shale gas is closing the taps of an energy that could be strategic.
in writing. the issue of shale gas divided parliament today in plenary. unfortunately the amendment, which i co-signed, calling on the member states not to authorize hydraulic fracturing operations was rejected by the european parliament: the 262 votes in favour were not enough. however, hydraulic fracturing is currently facing many unsolvable problems. moreover, the tzavela report, which presents shale gas and american experiments in a very positive light, and which i voted against, was also adopted. the only reason for satisfaction is that the sonik report on the environmental consequences of shale gas and oil shale extraction activities received a large majority. it calls for a ban on hydraulic fracturing in sensitive areas. it recalls that while each member state has the right to choose its energy mix, all member states should have robust rules on all exploitation techniques, including hydraulic fracturing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive on the protection of the environment. i welcome the adoption of this report, although vigilance is still needed in view of the contradictory votes today. the fight continues!
in writing. in the heated debate on shale gas in the european union and its member states, there is no absolute truth. between pro and anti shale gas, there is most certainly a middle line, and dispassionate debate is a necessity. to abandon this energy now without even pursuing research would be a major strategic mistake. but on the other hand, to give a blank check to the exploitation of this resource when the technology is not yet developed would be an environmental folly. shale gas has undeniable potential and should be seriously considered. but as they stand, their exploitation puts the environment at risk, and it would be irresponsible to do so.
in writing. on wednesday 21 november, at the european parliament's plenary session in strasbourg, i was asked to give my opinion on two reports on shale gas. on this burning issue, it is with a sense of environmental issues, of the urgent need to develop our country and our industry to meet the needs of our people, that i have decided to vote for these reports. in the present state of scientific knowledge, it is certainly undeniable that large-scale commercial extraction by hydraulic fracturing would be contrary to environmental protection. however, this should not jeopardize scientific research into this energy, which could enable france and europe to achieve a certain degree of energy independence. a sound, public and secure control of shale gas and oil extraction in the years ahead (provided that safer extraction methods are mastered) would not only be an asset for our industry but would also help to bring down the cost of energy for a significant number of households. i understand the fears and apprehensions which arise from the discovery and use of non-conforming extraction methods for this new energy source, and these fears are justified. however, my role as a communist member of parliament, who is seeking the happiness of the people of europe, is to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right to vote and to stand for election.

mr president, mr president-in-office of the council, madam commissioner, parliament has shown its realism and sense of responsibility on the budget. for two years in a row, a qualified majority in this parliament has accepted the level of payments voted by the council of ministers without adding a single euro. parliament has made sure that its political priorities prevail in its votes. these are the same as those of the european council: the europe 2020 agenda and, more recently, the content of the growth pact. the same sense of responsibility guides us today when we say - as president schulz did - that the 2013 budget cannot be discussed until we have guaranteed the financing of the arrears for 2012. none of the 27 ministers disputes the amount of these arrears, which is 9 billion. but now some of them do not want to pay in 2012 all the payments due for the programmes fully implemented in 2012. this is contrary to the financial regulation. it is contrary to the 2012 budget as we voted. it includes the commitment, read earlier by president schulz, to adopt an amending budget during the year if necessary. and above all, this attitude is contrary to the treaty itself. the european budget must be balanced, which means that it must be voted on in balance, but also that it must be implemented in balance. we cannot end the year with a debt of 9 billion euros. i would add that on the eve of the european council, refusal to pay yesterday's bills would deprive any commitment to tomorrow's budgets of credibility. in the meantime, the rejection of the 2013 budget is a reminder to those who have forgotten it in some capitals that in budgetary matters, whether it is a question of negotiating for one year or for seven years, nothing is possible without the agreement of the european parliament. we trust the commission - and i welcome its new commissioner for the budget - to prepare a new text which takes account of the state of our discussions and to play its role as facilitator, and we trust the particularly active cypriot presidency to take the necessary initiatives.

the rapporteur. - mr president, madam minister, ladies and gentlemen, there is no need today to enumerate all the crises and threats to our security which affect the stability of our continent and its neighbourhood. the news - we have just spoken about it - provides us with new reasons every day to consider that the multipolar world of the early twenty-first century is, in many ways, more dangerous than the one we have become accustomed to, because it is less predictable and less organized: civil war in syria, israeli-arab tensions, terrorism, nuclear proliferation, clashes and crime in the sahel, piracy off the coast of somalia, continuing war in the congo, to name just the dangers of today. in view of this, it would be irresponsible to regard the common security and defence policy as a luxury or an anecdote. it is a policy which is, admittedly, recent and still in the making. more than any other policy at european level, it is a policy based on the member states, on their material and human capacity, on their traditions and on their political will to share, or not, their almost absolute sovereignty in diplomatic and military matters. this fact leads too many observers and too many colleagues to regard the common security and defence policy as a negligible amount or as an unnecessary illusion. we believe, quite the contrary, without naivety or excessive illusion, that the csdp is a strategic necessity for the european union. that is why it is written in full in the treaty of lisbon. the european union simply can no longer afford to delegate its security and that of its neighbours systematically. of course, nato, which brings together 21 of the 27 members of the union, is still - and should be welcomed - the cornerstone of the continent's collective defence. of course, the transatlantic partnership must be reaffirmed and it is irreplaceable, but this is not the sole result of efforts and ambition on the part of the european countries themselves, quite the contrary! the americans themselves, who have initiated a real strategic shift towards the asia-pacific region, are asking us europeans to be more active, more robust, more self-confident in matters of security and defence. those who question the csdp, speaking of duplication, must realise that it is a pragmatic and intelligent complementarity between nato, a military organisation, and the european union. there are crises that affect our security and in which nato cannot intervene; the european union has been a major player in the development of the middle east, and it is not surprising that the european union has been a major player in the development of the middle east. unfortunately, such examples are likely to increase in the future. the european union often has full legitimacy to act, because it acts within the framework of international law, and there are few third countries that do not recognize it as a balanced role without ambiguous unilateral ambition. she has many means of action; it has the so-called global, civil-military approach, which it alone can take advantage of. unfortunately, the fault often lies in the political will - above all the political will of the member states - the lack of political will - we must also stress this - or of motivation on the part of certain brussels institutions responsible for the cfsp and csdp, the lack of vision, sometimes the reluctance to act vis-à-vis the council, the ideological reluctance because it is considered that soft power is more effective than the use of armed force, and also the absence, sometimes, of clear priorities which too often give the impression of navigation by sight. the strategic challenges we face are immense and unprecedented: a structural and sustained decline in european defence budgets, a reorientation of us priorities, and extreme volatility and diversity of threats. the european countries therefore have no choice but to undergo a major and collective strategic downgrade, or to recover and exploit to the best of their abilities the possibilities, albeit still modest, of the csdp. it is certainly in the area of capabilities that this effort must be most substantial today and we emphasize in the report the virtues of pooling and sharing promoted by the european defence agency, which is in the right direction. the economic and strategic crises must not be - mr president, this is an important subject - a pretext for resignation but, on the contrary, an opportunity to strengthen our common ambition. mr president, commissioner, the fisheries discussions of this part-session, each in its own way, prefigure part of what will be the building block of the future common fisheries policy. as architects of this policy, we must always bear in mind that each pillar of sustainable development determines the balance and strength of this edifice. in other words, fisheries policy must promote economic viability, job preservation and resource conservation. these five reports examine the main objectives of the future cfp, namely maximum sustainable yield, the fight against discards and the allocation of fishing rights. but these objectives must not be mere slogans. the technical measures in the gallagher report, even if they are only transitional, point to the difficulties of moving to practical cases, fishery by fishery, stock by stock. the ferreira report on small-scale fishing was wise in recognising that there is no single criterion, but a list of criteria, for defining small-scale fishing. the gróbarczyk report raises the question of the lack of data. the lövin report on the external dimension stresses that we are moving in a global context and raises the question of the conditions for exploiting resources outside european waters, as well as the import conditions for fair trade. it is no longer possible that the constraints imposed on our fishermen are not corrected by import constraints which prevent unfair competition. finally, the patrão neve report on sharks calls for the urgent need to strengthen the union's controls. success in ambition is not proclaimed; it is built by patient and meticulous work between goals and means. that's what we're trying to do.

in writing. although the practice has been banned in the european union since 2003, spain and portugal had a derogation allowing them to remove shark fins from fishing vessels. in march 2012, the european commission requested the withdrawal of this derogation. the european parliament has acceded to the european commission's request and voted to finally ban the practice from the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of council regulation (ec) no 1185/2003 on the removal of shark fins from ships. i strongly condemn the practice of finning, which involves cutting off the fins of sharks on ships before dumping them at sea, which has been officially banned by the european union since 2003. however, the complex system of removing fins within a 5% ratio between the weight of the fins and that of the carcasses does not allow for a simple control of the legislation. in this respect, i support the commission's proposal to make the method of requiring the fins to remain attached to the carcass mandatory in order to combat finning effectively. this will reduce the number of great white sharks and help to preserve the species, which is increasingly under threat.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which proposes to end the derogations which until now allowed certain fishermen to remove shark fins from vessels before discarding the carcass at sea. these barbaric fishing techniques, banned in the eu since 2003, must be banned as cruel to sharks who are thrown into the sea alive without their fins.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i want to make it impossible to cut the fins off of sharks and throw their bodies into the sea. the living animal is then condemned to sink to the bottom and die there. this practice is problematic from an environmental point of view (threatening the survival of certain species), from an economic point of view (a huge waste of a potential food source) and from a moral point of view (unnecessary suffering of animals). there is no economic need for "finning", as there is a market for shark carcasses, even though they are thrown into the sea for lack of space. however, the current regulations do not work properly: many infringements have been reported. it seems to me important to correct the shortcoming in the 2003 european legislation, which allows some fishermen to continue to use this technique. this practice is difficult to detect because shark carcasses and fins can be landed separately in different ports. it is therefore necessary that the sharks are landed whole. we must make the legislation clearer and stricter so that this practice is no longer possible.
in writing. shark finning is the practice of fishing for sharks with the sole purpose of cutting off their fins and thus supplying the asian market, which is very fond of this fish. for many years, the european union allowed 15% of shark fin imports to asia. finnish fishing was banned in the eu in 2003. however, exemptions have been granted to certain countries to allow them to continue this activity. the purpose of this report was to allow the continuation of the derogating measures. in total opposition to these practices, i voted against this report, as did the majority of my colleagues. the failure to adopt this report means that from now on, sharks will have to be landed with their fins 'naturally attached to the body'.
in writing. while europeans do not traditionally cook shark, asians are particularly fond of its fins - which can cost over $50 a pound. the fishery for this animal, whose presence at sea is necessary to preserve the balance of the marine ecosystem, has been regulated, in particular with a view to ensuring the conservation of its species. yet the current rules are too easily circumvented by fishermen, and shark stocks are declining: according to the international union for conservation of nature (iucn), more than 25% of all pelagic shark species are threatened, of which more than 50% are large pelagic ocean sharks. action is therefore urgently needed to ensure the conservation of this species by ensuring better compliance with the rules in force, which would also allow the european union to comply with its international commitments on the protection of sharks. that is the spirit of this regulation, and i support it.
in writing. i voted in favour of a ban on the cutting of shark fins on board ships. the practice has been banned in the eu since 2003, but some exempted fisheries in spain and portugal are suspected of using 'finning', which involves cutting the fin and throwing the shark's flesh into the water. the report therefore proposes that all fishermen should be obliged to cut their fins only after landing. this debate is a perfect illustration of the need to establish a genuine european fisheries control policy. this practice of 'finning' is unacceptable, but it has not been demonstrated to exist in europe. however, in the case of doubt, it was necessary to leave no room for such practices. faced with the failure of the control, the european parliament is forced to resort to a complete lack of derogation, which will not be without consequences for the professionals. the challenge now is to ensure that the issue of european fisheries control is dealt with more effectively. in particular, the uniformity of controls will have to be promoted and the resources allocated to this indispensable instrument of fisheries policy will have to be increased.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution to revise the legislation on the practice of 'finning', i.e. removing the fins of sharks from fishing vessels. it was already prohibited by council regulation (ec) no 1185/2003 of 26 june 2003. however, article 4 of that regulation introduced an exception which de facto allowed 'finning'. this resolution is a means of putting an end to this barbaric practice of making soup in asia. because the remainder of the shark's body has less commercial value, the living shark is often thrown overboard, its fins amputated, unable to move to oxygenate its gills, and thus slowly suffocates to death. today, 73 species of sharks, which play a vital role in the life chain, are threatened by overfishing. i am therefore pleased that all the amendments seeking to reinstate derogations have been rejected because it is now proven that they have been used to circumvent the legislation. at a time when bluefin tuna legislation is proving effective, it is time for everyone to show responsibility towards species that are actually threatened.
in writing. i voted in favour of tightening the rules on shark finning on board ships. the current rules allowed for derogations which did not guarantee compliance with the prohibition of the cruel practice of dumping live sharks after removing their fins. while the fins are the main ingredient in the popular asian soup, the rest of the meat is less sought after, and the temptation to take only the noble part and discard the rest of the carcass is great and encourages overfishing of an animal whose many species are endangered. however, while the obligation to land only fins attached to the body of the animal should facilitate controls, i remain convinced that the lack of resources allocated to such controls - on this issue but also for other species - remains the central problem in the area of overfishing, to the detriment of the environment and the overwhelming majority of fishermen who do their work with seriousness and courage and are faced with unfair competition that breaks all the rules.
in writing. child abduction is morally wrong and has serious consequences for children and their families. the hague convention on the subject provides the legal means to combat this crossborder scourge. this text seeks to allow eight new countries to accede to the convention and i therefore supported this resolution.
in writing. in view of the increase in the number of international child abductions, which goes hand in hand with the increase in the number of binational marriages, i supported the request made by the european parliament to see 8 decisions on accession of third states to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of child abduction. these decisions are essential to expand the possibilities for finding rapid positive outcomes in the face of child abductions. the council must therefore proceed without delay to the conclusion of this process.
in writing. this text is an appeal by the european parliament to the member states in the context of the revision of the international telecommunications regulations (itr) at the world conference on international telecommunications to be held in dubai from 3 to 14 december. in supporting this text, i call for vigilance against any threat that could undermine the open and competitive nature of the internet. the internet must remain an area of freedom and openness and that is the whole point of the european parliament's vote.
in writing. telecommunications are at the heart of a number of issues: not only have they become one of the pillars of our growth, but they also touch on sensitive areas, such as the protection of our privacy. for these reasons, i support the ambitions set out in this resolution: telecommunications regulation must be fair and realistic, and this implies in particular the guarantee that its development is open, participatory and respects the principle of neutrality.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to clarify the european parliament's position ahead of the doha conference which will end on 7 december. i supported this resolution because it is balanced and reasonable. particular attention was paid to the risks of carbon leakage which would harm the competitiveness of european companies. the european union is a leader in environmental matters. it must remain so, while allowing its economy to adapt and ensuring that these efforts are also shared by third countries.
in writing. global warming has been gradually and simply removed from the political and media agenda for many months. yet, more unanimously than ever, international experts have only confirmed their most pessimistic fears about climate change. the two degrees of increase that we were hoping to avoid by the end of this century seems to be an obsolete objective. we can only regret it. the european union, at the forefront of the environmental fight, must redouble its efforts and its teaching at international meetings. in this sense, the doha conference will be a new meeting place. but let us not be naive, i think it is essential to bring up the question of a carbon tax at the borders of our continent in order to prevent any distortion of competition for our european industries which cannot unilaterally assume ecological commitments.
in writing. by voting for this resolution, we wish to reiterate that we retain strong ambitions for the doha climate conference. the union must continue to play a leading role in this area, as there is an urgent need for action. i am particularly in favour of developing our climate diplomacy. the european union must remain a pioneer in this field, but it must not be satisfied with that: it must be a leader. and for that, she has to learn to speak with one voice, if she wants that voice to carry.
in writing. i am in favour of this resolution because, after copenhagen, cancun and durban, we must absolutely avoid leaving this conference once again frustrated and dissatisfied. the european institutions must have a greater say in the negotiation process if we are to achieve tangible results. this resolution repeatedly mentions climate diplomacy and the importance of speaking with one voice. the climate issue must be addressed in a transversal way, including through industrial policy: the effects on industry and how industry can play its part are an absolutely essential aspect of these negotiations. we cannot be the only ones to take action, at the expense of our economy and while our main partners continue to pollute. we must ensure that the major polluting countries ratify the second commitment period of kyoto: until we have a legally binding agreement for all the major economies, we will not move forward. it is also important to emphasise that climate finance must be able to come from a variety of sources: the role of the private sector is not to be dismissed. we need to be able to combine economic growth and climate management.
in writing. after durban, this new climate change conference must be an opportunity to translate past commitments into practical application as soon as possible. promises are no longer enough, we must act. it is in this sense that i voted in favour of this resolution, to raise the bar and pursue the objective of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 30% by 2020, in the interests of the european citizens. it is also essential that the major industrialized countries agree to renew the kyoto protocol, which expires at the end of 2012. the resolution also highlights the need to help developing countries, which are often the first to be hit by natural disasters, to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions without increasing their structural vulnerability. finally, from a european point of view, it is in our interest to take part in this process, given the positive impact that sustainable development could have in terms of new jobs, growth or a reduction in energy dependence.
in writing. this resolution supports a binding international agreement on climate change that respects the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities. it called for ambitious targets in line with the ipcc studies and for enforcement mechanisms to be set up. it stresses that the so-called 'developed' countries must provide the so-called 'developing' countries with the necessary means to adapt to and combat climate change, in addition to the aid already provided. it also advocates a gradual phase-out of fossil fuel subsidies. i support all those recommendations. i therefore vote in favour of this text, although i regret that, as always, it is being designed in the context of an enlarged carbon market and not outside this harmful mechanism, the limits of which the text itself recognises.
in writing. as the doha summit begins and the kyoto protocol expires at the end of 2012, i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on all states to increase their actions to limit global warming. current pledges to combat climate change fall short of the measures needed to meet the target of limiting global average warming to 2°c. it is crucial that a new international treaty with more ambitious objectives is ratified and that all countries step up their efforts. in this context, we call for the eu to set a target of reducing its emissions by 30% by 2020, we stress our support for the inclusion of aviation in the european ets, and we call for the issue of emissions from the international shipping sector to be addressed swiftly. unfortunately, it is likely that no new legally binding international treaty will enter into force before 2020, leaving a vacuum after the kyoto treaty expires at the end of 2012. this must be avoided at all costs, and i call on all signatory states to agree to a second commitment period for the current protocol.
in writing. the 18th united nations conference on climate change will be held from 26 november to 7 december 2012 in doha, qatar. it is part of the continuity of the major international environmental meetings in durban (2011) and rio+20 (2012). i supported this resolution because it is a road map for the european parliament delegation to the conference, which will have to work towards a legally binding international agreement. it also stresses that the union must lead by example in honouring its commitments and showing ambition in mitigation and financing and that, therefore, it is the duty of all eu institutions to engage in intensive climate diplomacy in the run-up to the conference. it also highlights and proposes ways of solving the problem of financing, which is more relevant than ever in this period of crisis. finally, it recalls a principle which i believe is essential: we must move towards a sustainable economy which takes account of the environment throughout the production cycle.
in writing. with this resolution, the european parliament, on the eve of the doha conference on climate change (cop), once again expressed its views on the issues related to the fight against climate change and the extension of the kyoto protocol, which expires at the end of december this year. parliament expressed particular concern at the latest scientific studies indicating that global warming could be more rapid and more pronounced than expected. can the european union set an example by first honouring its commitments? what about the adoption of binding commitments and actions to reduce co2 emissions by all member states? scepticism is warranted when we know that the commission's objectives are for 2050. i have nevertheless voted in favour of this resolution, considering that the proposed measures are still in the right direction. more generally, it is regrettable that the cop is content to wait until 2015 to take the necessary steps to commit to a determined fight against climate change.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which is a reminder of the positive aspects of the european union's enlargement policy. as the prospect of a third country joining the eu is a major motivation for deep reforms, it is important that enlargement policy remains clear, if not clearer. this call from the european parliament should enable the european commission to consider improvements.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the enlargement policies and criteria and the european union's strategic interests in this area. i believe it is essential to establish the copenhagen criteria as the fundamental basis for the enlargement process. the report also calls for better control by the european commission at all stages of the accession process. i also support the new negotiating approach for future negotiating frameworks which gives priority to issues related to judicial and fundamental rights as well as justice and home affairs.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which clarifies the criteria for enlargement and the strategic interests of the european union. the union must be clear about its enlargement policy and third countries must understand what rules to follow and what requirements to meet in order to become potential candidates.
in writing. this report is distressing. if the criteria for membership which you advocate had been met, and in particular the criteria for the prior settlement of disputes, turkey would never have been allowed to negotiate and cyprus, which it occupies militarily, would not be a member state. but at the end of the day, it's a fluke. because if i understand the report correctly, enlargement has become a policy in its own right, almost self-sufficient, and supposed to compensate in some cases for the failure of diplomacy or the political instability of an immediate neighbour. it is more like a leap forward, which has always preceded the strengthening of brussels' powers by a new treaty. and also to a kind of hope that there is a critical size that would make the europeanist utopia "too big to fall and to fail". the only idea that deserves any consideration is the proposal for an 'associate member' status. but i fear that in the mind of the rapporteur this status is more for switzerland or norway than for turkey.
in writing. while the emphasis on human rights and greater participation of civil society is welcome, the report is nonetheless based on respect for the copenhagen criteria, namely the establishment of 'stable institutions guaranteeing the rule of law, democracy, human rights, respect for and protection of minorities'; 'a viable market economy and the ability to cope with competitive pressure and market forces within the union'; 'the capacity to meet the obligations of eu membership, including the objectives of political, economic and monetary union'. voting in favour of this report would therefore be tantamount to implicitly or explicitly supporting these economic and social policies which are devastating for the people. on the contrary, i voted against this report because of the inalienable right of peoples to self-determination.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report enlargement policy and criteria eu strategic interests in this area it is important to meet the copenhagen criteria to ensure the credibility and effectiveness of the enlargement strategy. the commission must maintain and intensify its monitoring of progress in the accession process. the european union's capacity for integration must be assessed from the outset and properly considered in the commission's 'opinion' on each potential candidate country.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because it recalls simple principles which should continue to guide the work of the union in the context of enlargement. i support in particular the definition proposed by the committee on foreign affairs, to which i belong, of the capacity for integration. this is the essential counterpart to enlargement and it is important to take it more seriously. we also wanted to point out that failure to respect the basic social standards common to the eu constitutes a form of social dumping which harms european businesses and workers. in other words, it is a call for the widest possible dissemination of european values and their integration into the legal systems of our neighbouring countries. finally, this resolution highlights a point which i believe is essential: the eu must rethink its communication policy to accompany enlargement, which must be more effective and transparent.
in writing. i voted against this report on the policies and criteria for enlargement of the union. the report is based on compliance with the copenhagen criteria, which incorporate the objective of 'a viable market economy and the ability to cope with competitive pressure and market forces at home'. the main objective of european integration has been stated, and i am not going to support these policies, the consequences of which are becoming more and more evident. i also denounce the hypocrisy of this report, which states that 'enlargement facilitates respect for human rights', which is the poor relative of the copenhagen criteria and especially of their follow-up after accession. if so, how do we explain the impunity enjoyed by mr orbán's government in hungary? i regret that the sanctions mechanism for violations of human rights, as provided for in article 7 teu, is totally blocked by the member states, that its implementation is the sole responsibility of the council and that the latter needs unanimity to do so, which makes the provision totally inapplicable in fact. it is intolerable to expect the applicant countries to respect human rights when it is impossible for the member states to do so.

in writing. the european union is currently engaged in 14 civilian or military missions abroad. they are the first steps towards a europe of security and defence, long desired by all those who believe that europe, as a major economic power, cannot remain a diplomatic dwarf for long. but they are first fruits that do not yet announce obvious advances, because europe on the big issues of the world, and the conflicts are of those, difficult to find its way and to speak with one voice. even though everything - our economic weight, our democratic tradition, our diplomatic history, our vocation for balance and dialogue - calls for the union to be more involved in these most serious issues. and it is because they are among the most serious that we are obliged to move forward by setting clear defence priorities: sufficient material and human resources to act more quickly and more effectively; strengthened coordination of the diplomatic and military resources of the member states; consistency of analysis and action in our relations with international institutions such as nato. in this context, the development of a white paper on eu security and defence, as requested on several occasions, is more necessary than ever.

in writing. under the cover of so-called mutual defence and 'solidarity' clauses, the european parliament calls on the eu to commit itself further to european defence policy. the mutual defence clause (article 42 (7) teu) provides for an 'obligation' to respond 'by all means' in the event of armed aggression against a member state, which goes beyond the nato mutual assistance clause, as unarmed attacks will also be affected. the solidarity clause (article 222 of the feu treaty) opens the way for military intervention within the european union, in particular in the event of a terrorist attack or natural or man-made disaster. can social unrest and strikes be considered "man-made disasters"? this report favours military logic at the expense of peaceful logic, and even merely civil defence measures outside and inside the union. it is in particular pushing for increased militarisation and armament in the eu. such an incitement is at the very least inappropriate in view of the bellicose tendencies of some member states and at a time when, ironically, the eu has just received the nobel peace prize.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential that we adapt our infrastructures to the challenges of digital technology. this report addresses these concerns and seeks to put in place a genuine eu cybersecurity and defence strategy, which we are sorely lacking at the moment. cybersecurity challenges must not be ignored and we must be able to act together: it is important to improve coordination and action within the union. we also need to have a better understanding of the threats, by better assessing the dangers to our information systems and infrastructure. as independent hackers and those hired by major powers such as china increase their attacks, we must be able to take the lead and react immediately to any attack on our digital systems. member states should develop and coordinate national strategies for the security and defence of cyberspace. finally, we must also deepen our cooperation with our nato partners and the united states to increase the resilience of our information systems.
in writing. the main objective of the report is to establish comprehensive cybersecurity at all levels of the european union (eu) and, if necessary, a cybersecurity and defence strategy at both eu and member state level. while today's terrorist threat can be both terrestrial and virtual, it was important to strengthen our security in cyberspace which should not be considered secondary. i voted in favour of this report, which makes it possible to improve coordination and action within the union, to assess the risks posed by the various information systems in the union and to develop effective national strategies.
in writing. i voted for the report on the security and defence of cyberspace because we need to improve coordination within the european union in order to respond to the growing threat in cyberspace. member states should develop national strategies and find ways of coordinating them. it is also important to assess the level of threat to the union's systems and infrastructures.
in writing. the european parliament has been presented with a report on cybersecurity, which aims to better protect information systems from online attacks that could 'compromise the availability, integrity or confidentiality of data stored, processed or transmitted'. this report is a missed opportunity to demand better protection of the digital space. this report takes a very repressive approach. worse, because cyberattacks have been carried out against military organs, it even proposes military cooperation to combat cybercrime. it explicitly states that: "strengthening trust between the private sector, law enforcement, defence institutions and all other relevant institutions is essential in the fight against cybercrime". it also proposes 'public-private partnerships' which equalise all stakeholders, which is not without problems for all sensitive areas concerning the protection of personal data. i largely reject the concepts set out in this report, which only marginally takes into account the fundamental notions of net neutrality, freedom of expression and protection of personal data, and which forgets that "security" in this area must remain first and foremost under the control of the judge.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the role of the common security and defence policy in the event of climate crises and natural disasters. it is important to consider climate crises as a threat to the stability of the european territory, and to take their prevention into account in our current common security and defence policy, but this must not generate a new administration.
in writing. under the guise of responding to climate crises, this report justifies greater military integration of member states under the umbrella of nato and its concept of 'intelligent defence'. it legitimizes nato as a force for climate security. it is a further militarisation of the member states and therefore of the corresponding expenditure. i would remind you that the first priority is to combat climate change by implementing ecological planning in european policies. i would point out that it is not by militarizing on the one hand and destroying public hospitals by means of absurd austerity policies that we will make people safer. this text, in the name of legitimacy, advocates wrong solutions to a real problem. i vote against it.
in writing. the report concerns the ongoing negotiations for an enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement between the european union and the republic of kazakhstan. i voted in favour of this text because the european union needs strong trading partners. the eu's trade relations with many countries have led to the implementation of many reforms, often improving the human rights situation in kazakhstan, which remains problematic.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report containing the european parliament's recommendations to the council, the commission and the european external action service on the negotiations for an enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement between the european union and kazakhstan. the trade agreement, which is the subject of this report and provides a general framework for the current trade agreement, is intended to replace the current one and reflects the european union's increased attention to the integration of human rights clauses in its trade relations with third countries. while strengthening energy cooperation with kazakhstan and encouraging national authorities to align their legislation with that of the wto, the european union wishes to ensure a consistent strengthening of democracy and the rule of law.

in writing. the european union's trade policy must be consistent with its overall objectives as set out in the treaty on european union and contribute to sustainable development, employment and social progress in europe and in partner countries, and to a globalisation that respects human and social rights. the jaakonsaari report on a new enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement between the european union and kazakhstan highlights the serious shortcomings of the country in terms of democracy and respect for human rights, particularly with regard to workers' rights. the committee also welcomed the fact that the commission had already taken a number of measures to ensure that the eu's trade policy was not distorted by the wto rules. i call on the european commission to follow the recommendations of this report in the current negotiations. if serious human rights violations are found, the european union should not hesitate to use all the conditionality clauses of this agreement and, if necessary, to temporarily suspend it. this conditionality is a fundamental requirement for a just foreign and trade policy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the negotiations for an enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement between the european union and kazakhstan. the report is intended to replace the acp following negotiations opened in june 2011 with kazakhstan, the eu's first partner country in the region. the report calls in particular on the union to support kazakhstan in its reforms towards a strengthening of democracy and the rule of law.
in writing. i abstained on this report containing parliament's recommendations on the negotiations for an enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement (epc) between the european union and kazakhstan. eu-kazakhstan relations are based on a partnership and cooperation agreement (pca), which entered into force in 1999 for a period of ten years. in 2008, kazakhstan expressed its wish to sign a new agreement with the eu. the eu has acceded to the kazakh request while reducing ambition (no free trade agreement as long as kazakhstan is not a member of the wto, no visa facilitation agreement). reading the european parliament's report is quite astonishing, and we would like the european parliament to be equally vigilant with regard to all the countries with which the european union has partnerships. this is far from the case, as the negotiations that were initiated under ben ali with tunisia and under gaddafi with libya show. and we could also talk about the agreement we are discussing with colombia. while denouncing the dramatic situation in kazakhstan, i have therefore chosen, by abstaining, to denounce once again the double standards of the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it recalls that in the context of the reform of the common fisheries policy, special attention should be paid to small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing. these high-potential fisheries are also characterised by specific vulnerabilities that cannot be confused with the industrial fisheries sector on the high seas.
in writing. as we will soon have to decide on the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp), i wanted to give my full support to mr ferrera's report on small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing. it should be noted that almost 80% of european fishing is carried out by small vessels (less than 15 metres); the reform must therefore take account of the specificities of the sector. the challenge is nothing less than the maintenance of european small-scale fisheries: through the modernisation of the ageing fleet, the encouragement of youth employment, but also through the use of the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) to help the economic and sustainable development of vessels and to support the sector in emergency situations. the objective of the cfp reform is to move towards more sustainable development, to work towards the conservation of fisheries resources, but we must not forget the economic and social objectives, particularly those of small-scale fishing.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on small-scale coastal fishing, artisanal fishing and cfp reform. i support the proposal to develop a definition of small-scale fishing in order to create specific support mechanisms for this type of local fishing. it is necessary to adjust our action in order to exploit fully the potential of small-scale fisheries, to maximise their profitability and to ensure better local management, as part of the reform of the cfp.
in writing. small-scale coastal and artisanal fisheries are essential to the dynamism of our fishing sector and must be taken into account in all their specificity by the next common fisheries policy. i welcome the large emphasis on the role of women in this text, because they are also key players in the fisheries sector. as in other sectors, their training must be encouraged, their role supported and strengthened at all stages of the chain of activity. the value of their work must be recognised: it must be reflected in their status, in their pay, in their protection.
in writing. 80% of european fishing is carried out by small vessels (less than 15 metres). it is therefore a key economic sector which deserves to be strengthened and encouraged. an efficient reform of the common fisheries policy must of course take account of the specificities of this human-sized activity, which preserves the balance and fisheries resources. in this respect, the report makes some very useful proposals. this is the case with recommendations for fleet modernisation, encouraging young people to get a job, and the use of the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) to help economic development and support a sector often faced with emergency situations. a good reform of the cfp is to strike a balance between sustainable development and economic development. small-scale fisheries, which are a european specialty, perfectly embody this balance.

in writing. this report on small-scale and artisanal fishing and the reform of the common fisheries policy is important in that it recalls the importance of 'small' fishing in the eu, in particular in terms of job creation and regional diversity, development, as well as the general refusal of the european parliament to privatise access to fish stocks, the need for a flexible definition of artisanal fishing (what is small-scale in the netherlands is not small-scale in greece), support for the use of environmental and social criteria for granting access to fisheries and market distortion. however, the final resolution put to the vote goes beyond a red line: it supports the possibility of subsidies to sudden increases in fuel prices. the green group is clearly opposed to such subsidies. so i refrained.
in writing. coastal and/or artisanal fisheries play an important role in the social fabric and cultural identity of many european coastal regions. the definition of coastal and artisanal fishing varies from one state to another. while small-scale fisheries can be both commercial and subsistence, they can serve both local consumption and export. i voted in favour of this report, the main objective of which is to find an acceptable and clear definition of small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing and will allow for better recognition of these types of fishing in the reformed common fisheries policy.
in writing. this report supports small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing. it has the best ratio between the quantity of fish caught and the number of jobs created. it proposes measures based on the three pillars of sustainable management: ecological, economic and social. it rejects the mandatory application of transferable fishing concessions (tfp) to any type of fleet. i am voting in favour of this and i am pleased to see that several of the measures proposed by the left front have been adopted. i regret, however, that this text has no legislative value, as do many of the texts we vote on in the european parliament.
in writing. in the context of the negotiations on the reform of the common fisheries policy, we wanted to reiterate our position on small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing. we must support this small fishery which, given its structural weaknesses and the significant increase in its production costs - particularly due to the rise in fuel prices - is being badly affected by the economic and social crisis. of course, financial compensation must be provided for through the european maritime and fisheries fund when fishermen are inactive for reasons of biological rest of the species. on the specific question of a possible definition of small-scale fishing, i agree with the wish of this house to move forward, taking into account the diversity of small-scale fishing practices between member states.
in writing. as a fictitious rapporteur for this report, i helped define small-scale fishing. this term is used repeatedly in the texts of the cfp reform, without the european commission's definition appearing appropriate. it has chosen a simplistic definition: at present, all vessels of 12 metres or less are covered. this, however, does not take into account the different realities of european fisheries. as small businesses have more difficulty accessing eu funding, this definition may be necessary to ensure more equitable access to eu funds. in this context, the classification of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and the criterion of the employer on board seem to be more relevant parameters. even if the work in parliament has not resulted in a complete definition of small-scale fishing, this report is to be welcomed as a precursor to the debate on the financing of fisheries, and it was wise to recognise that there is not one criterion but a multitude of criteria for defining small-scale fishing.
in writing. the european parliament has received four reports aimed at strengthening the integration of sustainable development into the common fisheries policy (cfp). i therefore voted in favour of these four reports. the final report was presented by joao ferreira, a portuguese communist member of parliament (member of the gue-ngl). it aims to take better account of small-scale fisheries (in particular artisanal and certain types of coastal fisheries) in the reform of the cfp, its problems and its potential, in particular by advocating a lower fuel use per unit of fish caught and more selective techniques, which may have a smaller impact on living marine resources. it remains to be seen what will happen to these recommendations in other eu bodies.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the external dimension of the common fisheries policy. i believe that it is essential to improve the governance of bilateral fisheries relations and to preserve long-term sustainability at the global level. our action must be guided by the desire to eliminate illegal, unregulated and unreported fishing for the long-term conservation of resources.
in writing. the european union (eu) is an important market for fishery products. however, its role goes beyond economic considerations. it is now a major player in all seas and oceans, thanks to its fleets, investments, bilateral agreements with third countries and its participation in the main regional fisheries management organisations (rfmo). the aim of this report, which i supported by my vote, is to set out the new guidelines which will govern the external dimension of the reformed common fisheries policy (cfp). the main actions envisaged are the common strategy against illegal fishing, the strengthening of support for the development of international instruments for the conservation and management of fish stocks in the framework of the fao and the encouragement of the evaluation of the effectiveness of the rfmos.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the external dimension of the common fisheries policy, which sets out its new guidelines. it should contribute to long-term sustainability at global level to ensure the sustainable management and conservation of fisheries resources, while improving the governance of bilateral fisheries relations.
in writing. fish provide high-quality protein that is often needed by people in exporting countries. the eu is dependent on external supplies, despite having one of the world's largest fishing capacities. it must nevertheless endeavour to ensure the conservation of the resources of the exporting countries from which it benefits. it must also work towards sustainable fishing and the conservation of marine biodiversity worldwide. it must also ensure that the fisheries of the countries with which it negotiates comply with ecological and labour standards. this report proposes all of this and strongly opposes the eu promoting the adoption of transferable fishing concession schemes (tfcs) at global level. i am voting for it, but i regret that it has no real impact on the legislation and the negotiations conducted by the commission.
in writing. i voted in favour of the lövin report, an own-initiative text in response to the european commission's communication on the external dimension of the common fisheries policy (cfp). in a context of cfp reform, where the rules for european fisheries are becoming increasingly stringent, this report aims to promote a sustainable fisheries policy outside the eu's borders, thereby protecting european fisheries from unfair competition, by proposing that fishery products imported into the european union be subject to standards that are closer to its own in terms of ecological and social sustainability. fish know no borders. the european union's efforts to exploit stocks sustainably will therefore be in vain if we do not ensure that these requirements are disseminated globally. by tackling the question of reform of the common fisheries policy in a global context, this text thus prefigures, in its own way, part of what will be the building block of the future cfp.
in writing. the european parliament has received four reports aimed at strengthening the integration of sustainable development into the common fisheries policy (cfp). i therefore voted in favour of these four reports. the third report aims to support the establishment of long-term criteria for 'sustainable fisheries agreements' (sfa) with third countries. despite a problematic reference to wto rules, the conditions are encouraging. the precondition for any agreement should theoretically be respect for human rights. any fisheries agreement is limited to a scientifically proven 'surplus', i.e. fishery resources in excess of the coastal state's catch capacity.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text supported by the european parliament proposing changes to the organisation of the european elections to be held in 2014. among other things, we call for these elections to become an example in terms of parity and for the european commission to be truly representative of the composition of the european parliament from a political point of view. these measures should help to strengthen the representativeness and direct link between the european union and its citizens.
in writing. all opinion polls show a general lack of confidence in europe. one of the main reasons is the breakdown of the link between the actors of the european union and the citizens of europe. we don't know who does what, we don't know who decides and in whose name. it is the "citizen and democratic link" that we must restore. the european elections in 2014, a highlight of the democratic expression of the peoples of the union, will be decisive in this respect. the indispensable integration of the european union cannot be imagined without a powerful and real democratic counterpart. european democracy is first and foremost the fairest representation of opinions by means of proportional representation. the second is parity as an imperative principle. the recommendation adopted by our parliament to encourage european parties to nominate a candidate for the post of president of the european commission is another decisive innovation. these candidates would campaign on a project and thus give a face to european action. in a representative democracy, citizens decide through their representatives. involving them in the choice of the members of the commission is a full fulfilment of this founding principle.

in writing. this is a resolution first and foremost motivated by the role that the european parliament can play in the appointment of the next european commission and especially its president. it should be remembered that until now the european parliament had only approved (or disapproved) the decisions of the council of heads of state or government of the member states of the union. the lisbon treaty has gone through this and now it is the european parliament which will appoint the president of the commission on a proposal from the council. he's not sure that fundamentally changes things. but the majority of the european parliament has chosen to ask the "european political families" to propose candidates accordingly. the gangrene of presidentialism is therefore likely to have a major influence on the european elections; the choice of men (or women) is likely to prevail over that of ideas. furthermore, the european elections could take place in may 2014 (rather than june), which would bring us dangerously close to the municipal elections in france and shorten the debate on european issues. for these reasons i voted against this resolution.

member of the commission. − mr president, i am pleased to have the opportunity to explain to you why the association agreement with central america deserves parliament’s consent. the association agreement will radically upgrade the eu’s relations with this region, with which the eu has a long-standing commitment reaching back to the eu’s support for the region’s successful peace process in the 1980s. the association agreement relies on three complementary and equally important pillars, namely political dialogue, cooperation, and trade, which reinforce each other. these are the right tools to support economic growth, democracy and political stability in central america. in the political pillar, both parties have committed to a set of shared principles. they include democratic government, human rights, the rule of law, sustainable development and regional integration. it will allow us to coordinate our positions, take joint initiatives in the international arena, and both cooperate and expand our engagement in fields of mutual interest. through the agreement we have also furthered the important political objective of strengthening regional integration in central america. this is a real region-to-region agreement. this ever-stronger political dialogue is complemented by the cooperation pillar, which will give us the opportunity to work as partners in the region. it offers an excellent opportunity to boost all aspects of our relationship, in particular security, which is one of the most serious problems with which the central american region is confronted. insecurity in central america threatens both states and citizens. through this agreement, we shall further ensure that the region can count on the eu’s support to address these challenges. finally, the trade pillar completes the picture of this comprehensive agreement. it will further cement our strategic alliance, which is based on common values and mutual respect and is a fundamental tool to address the root causes of many problems that our partners in central america face. through the trade pillar we help implement internationally recognised core labour standards and key multilateral environment agreements in central america, and we strengthen the role of civil society. it will bring new business opportunities on both sides, and is both balanced and ambitious. that is because we negotiated it keeping in mind the needs of economic operators on both sides and the different levels of development of our central american partners. on trade in agricultural products the balance is also right. there is liberalisation, but we have agreed to the shielding of sensitive products in both regions. given the relative size of the economies involved – central america’s gdp represents less than 1% of the eu’s gdp – most of the economic impact, at a macroeconomic level, will be on the central american economy. we expect central america’s total gdp to grow by over eur 2.5 billion as a result of this agreement. these direct consequences are complemented by an important indirect benefit. increases in central american exports to the european union mean that our partners become less dependent on their other trading partners. a more diverse ‘customer base’ for central american exports means more resilience in difficult times and more growth in good times. in my view these real economic and political results are more than sufficient reason for the european parliament to give its consent to this deal. with your agreement, mr president, i would like to react briefly to mr salafranca’s remark with respect to the long time lag between the conclusion of the agreement and the vote on ratification, which will take place tomorrow. this is completely unacceptable from a number of points of view. we have to negotiate with a country – in fact, with a number of countries and regions – and implicitly tell them that whatever they agree with us will only come to fruition in two years’ time. we are convinced that trade will – and should – contribute to economic recovery in europe, but that of course is not achieved by having another two-year period after concluding a deal that could be of interest to our economies. from both a political and an economic point of view, that simply does not make sense. so what is the problem? the problem is that these are very big agreements – 1000 or 1500 pages – and before you can actually start the ratification procedure in the council, and afterwards in parliament, you need these documents to be translated into all 23 official languages of the european union. that takes an enormous amount of time. on top of this you have to do the legal ‘scrubbing’ to ensure that in all of these languages every word has exactly the same meaning, which is an enormous task. furthermore, we do not have the people to do this, because everybody wants us to have fewer officials. so if you really want to change this situation, what you should do is very simple: ask the european commission to take an initiative with respect to this matter. but you should also realise that this will mean that if we want to have the agreement in place more quickly, we will have to restrict ourselves to a limited number of languages, for example the language of the country concerned and an official working language of the european union. if you do not do that, you will never shorten that period. that is a fact a life. so please help us with respect to this and set apart this linguistic question, which i think is very important, especially in the european parliament. we have to reach a compromise between being very strict with respect to languages and trying to be effective with respect to the deals that we are concluding.

for the greens/efa group madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i can tell you quite frankly that the green group does not think this association agreement with central america is a good thing. it will not strengthen regional integration. it will not allow a political dialogue to develop, but will, on the contrary, reinforce an unbalanced economic relationship. this is a real disaster for the agricultural world, which will not allow the development of food crops, but on the contrary will strengthen export agriculture, such as sugar cane or bananas, that is to say an agricultural sector identified by the european union as the alpha and omega of central american exports. worse still, the agreement leaves no room for manoeuvre for developing countries to devise their own development policy. it will certainly do europe's business. it will certainly do the european companies' business, with increased access to telecommunications, increased access to water, increased access to public procurement, increased access to mining, which is contrary to the interests of local populations as shown by the number of conflicts that are developing everywhere. there is a human rights clause, but it is not binding and there is no reference in the agreement to corporate social responsibility or to ilo convention 169 on indigenous and tribal peoples. what an irony in this day of human rights, after the signing of the association agreement by the european union -
