madam president, in france, an advertising campaign, which remained popular in 2002, said: 'antibiotics are not automatic'. the simplicity of the message is not to be confused with a key issue: reducing the consumption of antimicrobials, the overuse of which for years has led to a very worrying microbial resistance. the who has sounded the alarm. if the widespread use of antimicrobials continues, the rise of bacterial resistance could set us back a century, when even the smallest bacterium could be fatal. there are solutions, and there are many. the first is an effective and robust regulatory framework to preserve the efficacy of existing antimicrobials, using them responsibly, safely, at the correct therapeutic level, when they are absolutely necessary, over a specific period and at the appropriate dosage. i would like to draw the attention of my colleagues to one point: pointing the finger at a profession - veterinary medicine - by forcing a prescription-release decoupling of the medicine, may be counterproductive. this measure could kill the territorial linkage of care in rural areas, discredit practitioners who actively contribute to risk control and prevention, and increase traffic, whereas this decoupling has only partially proven successful.

madam president, as my colleagues have pointed out, europe has been waiting for a european patent for 40 years. we are at a historic moment and i would like to thank commissioner michel barnier. this patent is an indispensable tool for promoting innovation, for encouraging european companies to invest in research and development. the european economy needs invention and creativity because the figures we have are not encouraging. today, there are 60,000 patents filed in europe, compared with 72,000 in china and 224,000 in the united states. so we are losing a battle and we have to react. the package we are voting on is being criticized by some mps and university professors. they say that the regulatory framework we are putting in place is not perfect. i agree with some of their criticisms, but we cannot be held back by academic discussions. what is important is the impact of this legislation on the european economy. unitary patent protection will divide the cost of filing a patent by six as we go from 30,000 euros to today's 5,000 euros. the patent will therefore become more accessible to smes and will strengthen the competitiveness of our companies. what is important is that we put in place a coherent system of unitary protection based on the proven practice of the european patent office and in compliance with the opinion of the court of justice of the european union on jurisdiction of 8 march 2011. what is important is that we finally overcome the difficulty of article 118 of the lisbon treaty, which requires unanimity in the council for the language regimes of new intellectual property rights. but given the circumstances, given the political and legal difficulties we have to face, this is the best result we could have achieved. i would therefore like to warmly congratulate mr rapkay, mr baldassare and mr lehne on their efforts, their patience and the spirit of compromise they have shown. let us give this new regulatory framework that is emerging a chance. let's see how it works. let's look at his strengths and weaknesses. the european legislator will always be able to make improvements or amendments to this system in the future. i would like to conclude by expressing my sincere hope that spain and italy will change their minds and participate fully in unitary patent protection, which is a great tool for growth and strengthening the internal market.

in writing. small and medium-sized enterprises account for 75% of private sector employment in the european union. but only 13% of them have activities outside the single market. in a context of crisis affecting the whole of the european union, this situation deserves to be corrected because it is an important source of growth for our economies. there is therefore an urgent need to improve the competitiveness of smes so that they can operate better internationally. this is both to provide them with adequate information and follow-up support and to facilitate their access to funding, which is currently sorely lacking. european programmes to help smes must also be more geared to their activities in third countries. it is also necessary for european smes to have relevant and up-to-date information on third country markets, for example by being put in contact with large companies already active abroad. finally, the european union chambers of commerce abroad must support european smes in their administrative formalities and legal procedures in third countries. the need to develop a comprehensive trade finance strategy to promote the internationalisation of smes is very much underlined in this report.

in writing. a realistic basic premise and pragmatic recommendations make this report a real roadmap for the european commission and the member states, which is why i voted in favour of its adoption in plenary. firstly, it is realistic, because it recognises that not all smes are destined to go international. at present, 13% of smes export outside the eu and 4% plan to do so in the medium term. above all, he advocates that smes first try exporting within the single market, before going beyond its borders. secondly, it is pragmatic, since it contains specific recommendations based on the demands expressed by smes themselves, particularly in terms of access to information and capital. for example, in the last two years, one third of smes that applied for a loan did not receive it or received less than they had requested. they can also obtain funding through the competitiveness and innovation framework programme, the new cosme programme or one of the 300 existing public support programmes.
in writing. the eu is a major destination for many foreign investments, but on the contrary, the investments of our smes, which represent 99% of enterprises, abroad are becoming smaller and smaller: this diagnosis is severe and has been steadily worsening. the lack of financing, the opacity of credit offers, the mistrust and frivolity of our smes, although innovative, prevent them from opening up to the world. for this reason, i welcome the adoption of this report, which highlights a number of solutions to stimulate entrepreneurship, through easier access to both credit and information. the renewal of the cosme programme for the competitiveness of smes is excellent news in this respect, which i have supported and which opens up great prospects for our companies. the commission must also hear our call for the exchange of best practice, the networking of kics and the creation of a single point of contact. in the future, it will be important that these identified strategic avenues are at the heart of all trade agreements with our foreign partners, to defend our companies against unfair practices and to ensure the internationalisation of their activities, which is a driver of growth and employment.

in writing. recent events in the maghreb have shown the power of information flow on the internet. as promoters of human rights and freedoms we must assert the right for citizens to move freely on the internet. however, it is also our duty to promote the interests of the consumer and to protect him against the abuses that the internet allows. if a binding law threatens the liberties of citizens, reasonable governance is necessary. i believe that freedom and security are necessary: we must be able to allow access to information, but also establish cyber security for users. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. so to improve the effectiveness of our development policies we need to introduce technologies to guarantee the freedom of movement on the internet.
in writing. as we saw in the debates on the anti-counterfeiting agreement, which triggered a real civil society uproar before the summer, the european union must adopt as soon as possible a real strategy on digital freedom within the framework of the european union's foreign policy. and it is true that now the struggle for human rights has a strong technological dimension: digital freedoms must now be considered as fundamental rights. i voted in favour of this report, hoping that it will lead the european external action service, the european commission and the eu special representative for human rights to undertake a comprehensive and thorough reflection on the subject and then to propose clear and pragmatic guidelines.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which stresses the importance of digital freedoms. these freedoms, which are closely linked to the development of new technologies, must be promoted and defended in the same way as all other fundamental freedoms, and enjoy maximum protection, not only within the union but also in third countries, where it is known that control of the internet is often one of the most powerful means of repression, but also of combating regimes that suppress freedoms. just remember how important they were at the time of what has been called the "arab spring". the eu should therefore be particularly vigilant on these issues in the context of partnership agreements, including trade agreements, which it concludes, including where they affect certain aspects of copyright. the report also refers to the need to uphold the principle of technological neutrality and a pluralistic approach to internet governance, for which increased participation of civil society and cooperation with governments are important to ensure a free and accessible internet for all. so this report is a step in the right direction. as usual, it remains to be hoped that it will be taken into account by the other european institutions.
in writing. i supported this report in plenary because the adoption of this regulation will allow the concrete implementation of a new eu competence: investment. bilateral investment treaties, which were previously negotiated and applied by the member states, will now be negotiated and applied by the eu. this regulation will make it possible to organise the transitional period of a few years during which the 'european' and 'national' treaties will coexist. in order to ensure legal certainty for investments and investors, it is important that this regulation enters into force rapidly to provide a common framework for all european players in the sector. beyond the purely technical aspect of this regulation, it is also a concrete manifestation of the progress of european construction.

in writing. georgia is currently experiencing economic difficulties due to the financial crisis, with production falling and tax revenues declining. georgia has requested macro-financial assistance from the union, despite already receiving budget support of eur 37 million per year under the european neighbourhood instrument and in particular the eastern partnership instrument. this €46 million macro-financial assistance will take the form of two components: a maximum of 50% in grants and 50% in loans over 15 years. this aid is closely linked to the conditions laid down in a memorandum of understanding with the imf in terms of budgetary balance, the implementation of structural policies and the dismantling of public services. we know that chorus. this is therefore nothing more or less than a new austerity plan implemented in this country with the complicity of the eu, or even at its express request. we know the disastrous consequences in europe and elsewhere. i therefore voted against this report. the same procedure is used for kyrgyzstan.

in writing. after lengthy negotiations on the mandate of the european maritime safety agency (emsa), i welcome the adoption of this report, which was intended to answer two questions: what should be the tasks of this agency created after the erika disaster and how to carry them out in a tight budgetary context? the agency's experience and effectiveness in preventing and reducing pollution at sea have been demonstrated. our parliament, however, had to reduce its ambitions in the face of the council's refusal to increase the budget allocated to it, and therefore accepted a limited extension of the agency's tasks. the agency's main tasks were to combat piracy in european waters and to assist in the training of seafarers. it is therefore a decision that sets the stage for further discussions on whether the eu wants to make the emsa a reference operational organisation to manage all aspects of the fight against marine pollution and the response to maritime disasters. this question is part of the debate on how to do more with less in a context of increasing needs and threats.
in writing. for more than thirty years, the european union has been seeking a single patent for the community. previously, it was necessary to carry out a registration procedure in all 27 member states, which was a significant waste of time and money for businesses. this regulation defines the single european patent as applicable throughout the european union, and will apply from 1 january 2014. because it is essential, i supported this text which finally gives the single market its unique patent.
in writing. the introduction of a european patent, which has been the subject of debate for 30 years, should have been a major breakthrough for the european union. but there are serious negative points which have come to cloud the conclusion of the agreement on the so-called 'unitary patent'. to satisfy certain member states, the union is deprived of the management of patent disputes. a judicial system is being created outside the european system, governed by an international agreement to which the eu is not a party, and on which the european parliament will have no say. that is most regrettable. despite the changes made to ensure compliance with eu law, legal certainty does not appear to be optimal. what will be the practical interaction between the international patent court and the epc? that is why i voted against the rapkay report on the creation of unitary patent protection and against the lehne own-initiative report on the court system for patent litigation. my vote is not a vote against the european patent, but a vote of dissatisfaction with what has been negotiated. a genuinely european patent would have been much more satisfactory, both in terms of legal certainty and political credibility.
in writing. i voted in favour of the creation of a unitary patent. the idea was launched more than 30 years ago and is now being realised. while filing a patent in europe currently costs €36 000, it will now cost only €4725, a reduction of 80% in costs. the new system will not only be less costly for the inventor but also more efficient. it will thus ensure automatic recognition and protection of the patent in the 25 participating member states (except italy and spain). smes will no longer be obliged to apply for a patent for each national market they wish to enter. this unitary patent is a victory not only for european smes, which will allow them to be more competitive, but also for the single market as a whole.

in writing. the adoption of this text by the european parliament is a turning point that will allow europe to catch up with its competitors in the field of patents. today, a european patent is 10 times more expensive than an american patent. what we have voted today is the division of the european patent price by six. it means more innovation and more competitiveness for our companies. i particularly welcome the emphasis on taking smes into account, so as not to impede the activity of our companies by dissuasive costs. they will be the first to benefit from the reduction in patent filing costs.
in writing. after 30 years of waiting, europe has finally got a european patent. today's vote is a major step forward in the drive towards industrial competitiveness. in practical terms, inventors, companies - especially innovative smes and smes - will be able to submit a single application, whereas they have had to repeat the procedure in each of the member states, with the same additional costs of registration and translation. the agreement will raise the cost of patentability of an invention from an average of eur 32 000 to eur 4 725 in the long term. with this single patent, the protection of inventions in the union will be considerably strengthened, and the whole european economy will benefit. a lower cost patent, of course, means more patents, which in the international competition we know represents a decisive upgrade. today, 60,000 patents are filed in europe, compared with 172,000 in china and 224,000 in the united states. the european patent is a guarantee that we will catch up with the two world giants and regain our leading position in the knowledge economy. so this is a historic decision.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text and more generally of the whole 'patent package' (report on the creation of unitary patent protection, report on unitary patent protection and report on the court system for patent disputes). after more than thirty years of waiting, the european union is offering its businesses an effective competitive tool. although europe is the world's largest single market, its industrialists had to file as many patents as national markets, thus limiting smes' access to the entire common market. the european union now offers protection valid throughout its territory. this patent is therefore equivalent to patents existing in other territories comparable to the european union and allowing research and innovation to be protected. i have supported this initiative from the outset by european commissioner michel barnier, who has promoted and completed a project almost as old as the european union.
in writing. the idea of offering protection at lower cost for inventions at the level of the european union is not necessarily a bad idea in itself. but the 'unitary patent' package as presented to us, despite years of negotiations, remains problematic. two important countries are not covered by this package: italy and spain. the use of enhanced cooperation leads to the creation ex nihilo of a specialised court with exclusive jurisdiction, composed of professionals in the field of intellectual property who have been promoted to the rank of magistrate, with the risks this entails for their independence, at least intellectual. their case law would be irrevocable. the link with the regulations in force, at national or european level, in particular the exemptions or limitations of rights (living organisms, software, therapies, etc.) is neither clear nor guaranteed. the future will tell whether the argument of the overall cost of a patent (instruction, validation, annual fees) is really relevant, since absolutely no model for fixing these costs, nor for an appeal to the new court, has been defined. all institutional actors must be self-financing. in an age of intense lobbying for software patents, attacks on internet freedom, and dreams of monopoly seed companies, none of this is trivial. i therefore voted against the rapkay report.

in writing. after 30 years of negotiations, our assembly has just voted to create a single patent application procedure covering 25 member states. this initiative replaces the time-consuming and costly procedure which has been in force until now, which involved filing a patent 25 times after having it translated into the language of each of the 25 countries. european patent applications will now simply have to be filed in english, german or french, or translated into one of these three languages. i regret that our italian and spanish friends, who were unable to enforce the right to file this european patent in their own language, have stayed away from this cooperation, especially since we have demanded that the translation of the patent into one of the three languages be reimbursed to smes and small and mediumsized enterprises. the european patent is a considerable asset for our companies (the filing of a patent will cost on average 5000 euros against 30000 euros currently) and i am sure that our neighbours to the south will eventually adopt this concrete step forward, support for the knowledge economy and a growth vector.

in writing. i wished to abstain on the european parliament's approval of the agreement establishing an association between the union and its member states, of the one part, and central america, of the other part, for two reasons. firstly, because this agreement poses serious problems for the socio-professional community in the outermost regions of the caribbean, and especially for banana producers. with a reduction in customs duties, caribbean overseas producers will indeed be in a difficult situation. the european union will have to help the outermost regions through its agricultural and cohesion policies. however, i did not wish to vote against this agreement, because even if it poses difficulties, it nevertheless creates a certain 'safety net' for overseas producers. in order to deal with any serious disturbances on the market, a safeguard clause and a stabilisation mechanism are provided for. if the system is not perfect, it has merit in existence!
in writing. i voted against the report by josé ignacio salafranca sánchez-neyra submitted to the european parliament calling for the ratification of the association agreement between the european union and central america. this agreement, like the eu-colombia trade agreement voted on the same day, is focused on commercial interests and denies human rights. while the agreement will have very concrete consequences in terms of economic liberalism (liberalisation, etc.) and while we refuse to see the social and environmental consequences, the clauses called 'democracy and human rights' are only non-binding suggestions. this is not acceptable. the union's double standards in relation to latin america are totally unacceptable.
in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendation on the council proposal concerning the conclusion of the eu-central america association agreement. i believe it is imperative to link the commercial side of the agreement with cooperation commitments to strengthen the legal system, fight corruption and social inequalities. i therefore support this recommendation.
in writing. the conclusion of this agreement will open up new dynamic markets for our companies. i am confident that this partnership will bring renewed growth and confidence, and more intensive exchanges between our two regions.
in writing. the association agreement between the european union and six central american countries (costa rica, el salvador, guatemala, honduras, nicaragua and panama) is not just a trade agreement. in addition to the dismantling of certain customs tariffs, which will be beneficial to the development of trade relations between the two regions, this agreement should foster the establishment of a genuine eu-central america political dialogue. regional integration of central america, consolidation of the rule of law, structuring of civil society and reduction of inequalities in these six countries are all objectives towards which this association agreement must aim. finally, it should be noted that, through this agreement, the european union, already the main provider of development aid to central america, will significantly increase the amount of its assistance. it thus reinforces our call for solidarity and our willingness to dialogue with central america.
in writing. this agreement between the european union and several central american countries (panama, costa rica, nicaragua, honduras, el salvador and guatemala) is the first regional agreement concluded by the eu. it goes beyond the simple commercial framework to include political dialogue and cooperation in fields as varied as democracy and human rights, the modernisation of the state and administrations, disarmament, the fight against terrorism, the environment and customs cooperation. when we examined the agreement, we were concerned that it might affect the production of the outermost regions of europe, particularly the french overseas departments and territories. that is why, together with my french colleagues in the committee on international trade, we have insisted on the need for a special safeguard and stabilisation clause for the banana sector. we have succeeded in obtaining a specific regulation and negotiating the terms of it through our amendments. that is why i voted in favour of approving this agreement.
in writing. the european union has concluded an association agreement with colombia and peru to simplify trade relations and reduce customs duties. however, a bilateral safeguard clause was inserted to allow the limitation of the customs advantages granted, in particular in the banana sector. this will be implemented when a certain quantity is imported each year. i therefore voted in favour of this text, which preserves the integrity of our local producers without jeopardising our trade relations with these central american countries.
in writing. while the trade agreement with colombia and peru was ratified by the european parliament in december 2012, safeguard measures for the european banana sector were adopted in the margins of the agreement. the colombian-peru free trade agreement will therefore include a specific clause protecting european banana producers, and in particular those in the french overseas territories. more specifically, if european banana producers suffer serious damage as a result of the opening of trade with colombia and peru, the reduced customs duties provided for under the trade agreement will be increased. this is essential to protect our european producers, since the union is the most important market for banana exports and already 72.5% of the bananas sold in the union come from latin america.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which introduces quotas for the import of bananas from colombia and peru following a trade agreement between the european union and these countries. although these trade agreements are desirable in order to strengthen our economic relations with third countries, it is nevertheless vital that the union protects its agriculture when competition proves to be insufficiently fair.
in writing. i voted against this report introducing a safeguard clause on bananas. safeguard clauses make it possible to temporarily re-establish normal customs duties or to suspend the process of tariff liberalization. this clause somewhat confirms the unbalanced relationship between the parties to the agreement, since the european union is the only one to have invoked a safeguard clause. the agreement is another example of the lack of consideration for the interests of the overseas regions. the clause will have very little chance of being invoked. nor will it be enough to protect the caribbean banana sector, a pillar of the economy, which will be exposed to competition that is difficult to sustain. finally, this vote must not make us forget that the real challenge for these territories is a transition to a more diversified and more sustainable economy.
in writing. the amendments put to the vote today represent a step backwards from those tabled in plenary last september. to accept this retreat would be to accept the pressure exerted by the chiquita firms to increase their profits at the expense of local workers, banana producers in our french overseas departments and territories and our ecosystem. chiquita estimates that for every €10 reduction in eu customs duties, it pockets up to an additional $112 million. i am voting against this text to denounce the complacent attitude of the majority of the inta committee towards the supporters of colombian paramilitarism.
in writing. i wish to abstain on the regulation on the implementation of the bilateral safeguard clause and the stabilisation mechanism for bananas provided for in the trade agreement between the union and colombia and peru. this mechanism does not meet the expectations of producers in the outermost regions. however, in the event of any serious market disruption, it is crucial to have a mechanism to protect caribbean overseas producers. of course, if the system is not perfect, it is better to have it than not to have it.
in writing. the european union has concluded an association agreement with colombia and peru to simplify trade relations and reduce customs duties. it is essential for the european union to develop a privileged partnership with these two latin american countries, which enjoy high growth rates. although the text was adopted by the european parliament, i abstained in this vote to send a message to the leaders of these countries about their people and the social and public health problems they suffer.
in writing. i voted in favour of a report on the trade agreement between the european union on the one hand and colombia and peru on the other. the agreement covers the abolition of customs duties, investment, public procurement and sustainable development services between the union, colombia and peru. if the union intends to strengthen its presence by granting economic advantages, the european parliament has ensured in particular that the agreement is conditional on compliance with the provisions on respect for human rights and the rule of law. a roadmap has been drawn up to step-by-step strengthen the judicial system to fight corruption more effectively. the protection of the environment and biodiversity must not be neglected. the eu will have to constantly ensure that this agreement does not allow for land grabs or the deprivation of the fundamental or social rights of local populations.
in writing. trade agreements concluded by the european union aim to increase trade relations with one or more states but also to contribute to the economic and social development of the partner countries. the free trade agreement with colombia and peru will facilitate access for european companies to very important markets, particularly in the automotive, services and public works sectors. but this agreement goes much further. it contains broad and binding provisions on respect for fundamental rights and democratic principles. as stated, failure to respect human rights and democratic principles would constitute a substantial breach of the agreement, which, in accordance with public international law, would give rise to the adoption of appropriate measures, including the possibility of denouncing the agreement or suspending it in whole or in part . parliament will have to pay particular attention to this.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which improves the transparency of trade relations between the european union and colombia and peru. as the text adopted today makes clear, these agreements must of course be conditional on respect for human rights and the rule of law, which are fundamental values for europeans. this text will also make it possible to promote our local products better by facilitating their export to the colombian and peruvian markets. the european union is thus showing its support for the products of our lands and is respecting its commitments to defend diversity.
in writing. i voted against this agreement. in colombia, 90% of crimes against human rights defenders go unpunished, while in peru, it is estimated that more than 250 environmental conflicts, most often related to mining, are taking place. despite these critical situations and the opposition of civil society and trade unions as a whole, the european parliament has just voted in favour of an agreement which has no regard for human rights, labour rights and even less for the environment. this agreement will only increase the competition for raw materials, with catastrophic consequences for local people and their environment. the european parliament called on the two countries to unilaterally draw up road maps for better respect for rights. these are, however, only a trickle, since they are not binding. moreover, they are only a list of existing public policies which are known not to have led to any significant improvements.
in writing. i voted in favour of the trade agreement between the european union on the one hand and colombia and peru on the other, despite the strong protests of citizens concerned about the economic and social consequences of such an agreement. the european commission was responsible for negotiating this agreement, which had to respect a number of imperatives. the concerns expressed about the human rights situation in these countries are quite natural but should not underestimate the efforts made by these countries. in addition, the agreement contains a binding provision stating that respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law is an essential element of the agreement and that in the event of a breach of these rules, the provisions and effects of the agreement may be suspended. i would add that following a written question to the european commission relaying these concerns, it was acknowledged that colombia and peru had made progress in the protection of human and labour rights and trade union rights.
in writing. the aim of this agreement is to facilitate trade between the european union and colombia and peru. the agreement was conditional on both countries submitting binding roadmaps for the implementation of labour and environmental clauses. these guarantees were given by both countries and this enabled the report to be adopted. i voted in favour of this report because it will be beneficial to european exporters. the abolition of customs duties will save them eur 270 million a year. the agreement will also benefit colombia and peru, whose gdp will increase considerably. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive.
in writing. this report validates the free trade agreement negotiated with colombia and peru to the detriment of the other member states of the can, bolivia and ecuador, and in defiance of any respect for this regional organization. in addition to being harmful to the colombian, peruvian and european peoples and to the environment, it constitutes an aggression against the bolivian and ecuadorian peoples and their governments. i denounce the fact that such a text can be approved even though president santos is putting in place a law guaranteeing impunity for his military which the un commission on human rights has denounced. in the field of human rights, the union's only compass remains the guarantee of free and undistorted competition in the exchange of all goods and services. i am voting against this text, which is emblematic of the union's amoral aggressiveness.

in writing. i voted against the report on the ratification of the trade agreement between the union and colombia and peru. this agreement will have dramatic consequences: liberalization of the financial sector in peru and colombia, which is tantamount to a dramatic setback in terms of anti-money laundering regulations (see the study by the centre for research on multinational corporations), liberalization of agricultural products, which goes against regional food sovereignty by endangering in particular the colombian dairy sector and the caribbean bananas (despite safeguard clauses), investment by large european companies in a regulatory framework that does not protect natural resources (appropriation by companies, especially water, land grabbing, etc.). moreover, the conclusion by the union of this free trade agreement legitimises the policy of the santos government, which is far from having broken with the human rights abuses of its predecessors. the impunity of the paramilitaries has not changed and half of the trade unionists killed worldwide are in colombia. a similar observation can be made in peru. i am very sorry that only a few socialist and green members have made the same choice as the gue/ngl group.
in writing. as the european trade balance deteriorates, the conclusion of a trade agreement between the eu, peru and colombia, which should allow the three parties to increase their gdp by 1% respectively, is a beacon of hope. in concrete terms, this agreement will open up new trade opportunities for our companies by guaranteeing them access to peruvian and colombian public procurement and service markets, and by removing the customs duties of these two countries on our industrial products. our exporting companies will thus save 270 million euros a year. in return, the eu will open its market to industrial exporters from peru and colombia in a reasonable way, in a win-win logic that will lift our three economies upwards, and ultimately stimulate production and job creation in our major export industries (chemical, automotive, pharmaceutical, construction and telecommunications). this vote is an illustration of europe's determination to no longer open itself to third countries without any compensation. in future, a simple principle must guide our trade negotiations: reciprocity.
in writing. i voted against the reports on the trade agreements between the european union, central america, colombia and peru. i am convinced that they will not have the miraculous effects for european companies that have been announced, even if their shareholders will benefit. however, i doubt whether they will have any impact on employment in europe. the commission's ability to activate the 'human rights' clauses, which this parliament is full of, is equally doubtful: it has always put free trade and finance above all other considerations. i voted in favour of the reports on the implementation of a safeguard clause and a stabilisation mechanism for bananas. i did it in a hurry, knowing that our banana producers would suffer from these agreements, and that this clause would be little or not activated at all, like the one accompanying the agreement with south korea. it is temporary anyway, as if the conditions of competition could be balanced in a few years. unfortunately, brussels has no interest in these cluttered islands at the end of the world with exotic products. it has nothing to do with european preference, when the germans want cheap bananas. i think we must defend these little parts of france, including against brussels.
in writing. 2012 is the european year of active ageing. this report, which i supported, calls for better european coordination in order to better inform european citizens. it is essential to educate the population on the issues of ageing and to provide the key to ageing well. this will have a positive impact on both the well-being of these people and on public health budgets.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the prevention of age-related diseases in women, as part of the european year of active ageing in 2012. the fact is that older women in europe are more affected by debilitating diseases and disabilities than men of their age. in addition, cardiovascular disease affects more women than men. in this sense, a twofold strategy must be put in place: prevention and information must guide the action of associations, national and european institutions, the media, but also institutions at local level. i would also like to commend the epp group for its strong commitment to this subject.
in writing. i voted for the angelilli report on the prevention of age-related diseases in women. i believe it is important to inform the general public in order to promote virtuous behaviour to accompany active and healthy ageing for all. statistics show that despite their longer life spans, older women are significantly more affected than their male peers by debilitating diseases and the progressive development of disabilities. i welcome the emphasis on prevention and the involvement of all the actors involved, including associations and the media.
in writing. women are particularly vulnerable to the risks of social marginalisation, precariousness and poverty: nearly 75% of women over 65 live alone. ensuring that they grow old in good conditions requires action today: guaranteeing their equality in employment and pay, the right balance between their family and professional lives, is laying a solid foundation for supporting them in retirement. i support the overall approach of this report, which proposes, in particular, to adapt the age threshold for access to screening programmes. 2012 was the european year of active ageing: it will soon be over, but we are not stopping our efforts to protect our elderly.
in writing. two statistical elements are worth linking: the fact that women's life expectancy is 8 years longer than men's, which exposes them to chronic and disabling diseases and to gender-specific diseases, which deteriorate the quality of life, and the fact that women are more vulnerable to poverty and precariousness due to more discontinuous career paths. these elements dictate the course to be followed to take better account of the specificities of women's health. the first is information campaigns on the risks of ageing, falls, poor diet, lack of physical or intellectual activity. this is of course to prevent serious diseases such as alzheimer's, certain cancers and cardiovascular diseases, and to train medical and paramedical staff. it is also about raising awareness among health and social care professionals about the risks of isolation and abuse. it is also about going beyond the medical and social fields so that every citizen feels involved. following the deadly heat wave of 2003, governments set up public awareness and vigilance campaigns. they have demonstrated that solidarity is the best prevention.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to strengthen prevention and information on age-related diseases in people, and particularly women. with the ageing of the population in the union, it is important that the european institutions take measures to accompany these demographic changes so that european citizens are aware of the public health issues. this will raise awareness among associations, national and european institutions, the media and local administrations.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the question of illness affecting older women has acquired a particular dimension, with a number of mutations that call for specific responses. more isolated, more often belonging to a disadvantaged group, victims of multiple discrimination, more affected than men by disabling diseases such as bone and joint diseases, with more smokers than in the past, older women, despite an increased longevity, need adequate support in terms of medical care in order to be able to lead an independent life and enjoy equal rights. information campaigns on the prevention and treatment of diseases, appropriate follow-up of cancer or osteoporosis are good examples of what is needed to enable women to cope better with active ageing. finally, the inclusion of these older women in society, by adapting certain facilities and increasing the number of activities in which they can take part, are all elements to be developed to help these people to face their loneliness and to remain autonomous, with dignity; i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the future of the community.
in writing. this report intends to make a number of proposals in the light of the increase in life expectancy, to enable healthy ageing for all through access to quality health care and preventive measures that help older people to remain independent for as long as possible. by increasingly taking this dimension into account, the eu is integrating the consequences of its ageing population. older women are significantly more likely than men to suffer from debilitating diseases such as cancer or alzheimer's disease, even at comparable ages. the eu must therefore work with member states and local partners to extend to the general public a prevention strategy aimed at promoting virtuous behaviours that promote healthy and active ageing. for this reason, issues such as access to medical services (complexity of systems, long waiting lists for specialists) are essential especially for the oldest patients, who are mostly elderly women, and are often isolated. this report is again a catalogue of good intentions, particularly in the context of austerity. i voted for this report, which favours the substance, without, however, having many illusions.
in writing. this report highlights the dangers of the growing threats of antimicrobial resistance. it affects both humans and animals and is a central issue in the european union's public health policy. i voted in favour of this text, which calls for a limitation of the use of antibiotics for animals for purposes other than curative.
in writing. the systematic use of antibiotic medicines is a real public health problem. it poses not only a health risk to europeans, by promoting the emergence of antimicrobial resistant strains, but also an economic risk, since the resulting infections cause billions of euros in additional health care costs. improved prevention and awareness-raising in this area and better guidance on the use of these medicines in human and veterinary medicine are therefore urgently needed.
in writing. resistance to antimicrobial and antiviral drugs is a matter of concern to the international community. who points out that the excessive use of antimicrobials leads to ineffective conventional treatments and compromises the control of the spread of infectious diseases. each year, 440,000 cases of multidrug-resistant tb are detected. in the eu, norway and iceland, 25 000 deaths per year are directly attributable to antibiotic-resistant bacteria. this calls for global action plans, as antimicrobial resistance is the result of complex and interconnected factors. the application of a rigorous precautionary principle therefore requires the implementation of preventive and information measures and an active research policy that ensures we are one step ahead. by focusing on prevention through monitoring mechanisms and information sharing, encouraging better hygiene regulation, stricter control of prescription authorisations - prescription-only requirements, rigorous reporting of resistance cases, and limiting the use of antimicrobials in medical and veterinary care, the eu will be able to effectively support the policies advocated by who, oie and fao. europe with its research know-how must mobilise its efforts to create new antimicrobial agents and improve the quality of treatments.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to respond to the decline in the effectiveness of certain antimicrobial medicines in the face of the large-scale spread of resistant strains. there is an urgent need to reduce waste in marketing and use of ineffective medicines in order to ensure better health protection for european citizens. the savings made should enable the development of alternative medical treatments that respond to mutations in infectious bacteria.
in writing. the massive and unwise use of antibiotics in both humans and animals has led to the rapid emergence of resistant bacteria. combined with the shortage of new antibiotics on the market, this poses a serious threat to public health, given the increase in the number of cases of drug failure. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report which calls for urgently strengthening measures to reduce the consumption of antibiotics in europe. however, i regret the adoption of the second paragraph of paragraph 16, which calls for the decoupling of the prescription and dispensing of antibiotics by veterinarians. the impact of such a measure in the fight against antimicrobial resistance has not yet been assessed globally at european level, although some member states such as denmark have already adopted this scheme. in addition, the ban on prescription-only dispensing would have a very negative effect on veterinary networking in rural areas and would lead to trafficking of medicines without any medical follow-up. we must trust the ethics of european veterinarians who are responsible health professionals, who respect the plans for antibiotic resistance and who work at their level for the rational use of antibiotics for technical, biological, ethical and economic reasons.
in writing. the european parliament has today sent a strong signal by adopting an ambitious report to combat the growing threat of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. the action plan launched by the european commission for the period 2011-2016 must be a strong incentive for member state governments to put in place the appropriate measures. but progress towards these goals has been slow and uneven. this emergency is becoming more critical every day, as 25,000 deaths a year in europe are caused by these tenacious microorganisms, leaving doctors helpless. we need to address two major problems: the inappropriate use of antibiotics in human and veterinary medicine and the backlog of innovation in the development of new medicines. unfortunately, there is no barrier to the spread of multi-resistant bacteria. antibiotics are not drugs like any other, and this awareness must be shared by all if we are to defeat this silent epidemic.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because it touches on a fundamental issue of public health. our main objectives are to combat the overuse of antibiotics, identified as the main cause of this growing resistance, and to address its worrying health consequences, which are estimated to be responsible for at least 25 000 deaths a year in the european union, figures which the medical profession considers to be underestimated. the resolution calls for urgent action to this end, mainly through the development of new antibiotic treatments, the more prudent use of existing ones and the improvement of animal husbandry.
in writing. i voted in favour of the rosbach report on the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance in order to better control the use of antimicrobials in human and veterinary medicine. the ability of certain microorganisms to develop resistance to certain antimicrobial agents has the effect of rendering some drugs ineffective. therefore, their use should be better regulated.
in writing. in europe, antimicrobial resistant bacteria cause about 400 000 infections and 25 000 deaths a year. while the commission's action plan on antimicrobial resistance is moving in the right direction, it is not enough to stem the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance internationally, and i believe that efforts to tackle this threat must be greater. that is the spirit of this resolution, which i support. the text calls for a focus on prevention - improving hygiene in hospitals, and improving the diagnosis and prevention of diseases in both animals and humans. it also calls for the right to prescribe antibiotics to animals to be restricted to veterinarians and separate from the right to sell these treatments in order to avoid an incentive to prescribe, and for antibiotics to be available to humans without a prescription - as is currently the case in some member states. the text also recommends that research into new antibiotics be better coordinated within the eu and at international level. i agree with those ideas.

mr president, commissioner, i want to say here that i fully support the conclusions of the commission's report, as well as the balanced work done by our rapporteur, mr wojciechowski, whom i would like to thank. the regulations in force have made it possible to improve the overall transport of animals for slaughter. however, efforts remain to ensure that the existing rules are applied uniformly in all member states. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. i think that the legislation on the eight-hour limit, which is still under debate today, must be properly applied, taking into account certain exceptions, such as the remoteness of certain areas, the state of the road networks or the persistence of unforeseeable delays beyond the control of the hauliers. as the commission says, in the present state of the law, there is no need for further legislation.
in writing. the transport of animals is not just a question of animal welfare. it involves many economic, environmental and public health factors. a reduction in the transport time of animals will improve the balanced development of rural areas through the development of local slaughterhouses. it will improve the quality of the meat and prevent the risk of transmission and spread of diseases arising during transport. it will significantly reduce the co2 emissions emitted by transport operators. it will allow better traceability of meat and processed products. it will ensure that consumers are no longer misled about the quality and origin of their products. for all these reasons, i ask the european commission to ensure strict control of legislation on the transport of animals and to take action against member states which do not comply with it. finally, we must also exercise strict monitoring and control of the transport of animals from third countries when the meat is destined for the internal market, in compliance with the reciprocity of trade and for reasons of public health and consumer information.

in writing. the adoption of the 2013 budget ends the deadlock in the negotiations. the agreement allows the eu to have a budget on 1 january, but the level of payments may prove insufficient. this is of course a cause for concern, as the european budget is financed by 75% national contributions. although the treaty gives the council and parliament the same power over expenditure, in practice the states have the final say on payments. given the budgetary constraints faced by the states at national level, they again agreed on a level of payments for next year below the estimated needs, while suspending 2.9 billion payments for 2012 which will still need to be financed in 2013. the pressure on the 2013 amending budget will therefore be very strong. our endorsement was given only with the council's formal commitment to provide this 2.9 billion in 2013, with any further extension if needed. we must not let our vigilance weaken, because we need a consolidated budget, the only lever to invest in the service of growth. these recurrent crises require a thorough debate on the eu's resources in order to increase its budgetary autonomy.

due to the crisis, some sectors, including social services, are receiving less funding. in an effort to show european solidarity, i therefore supported the request made by austria to help 350 dismissed social workers. the mobilisation of the european solidarity fund will help them to find qualified work again.

in writing. i voted in favour of mr kirkhope's report rejecting the commission's proposal to adopt a regulation on european statistics on crime safety. the commission stresses the importance of common statistics for the formulation of union policies, particularly in the field of criminal law. the european parliament followed up its committee on civil liberties which did not receive the information and clarifications requested from the european commission. it rejected this proposal because it raises questions about the method used, in particular in view of the questions asked (e.g. drug problems of the person questioned, possible possession of a weapon, etc.). beyond the methodological problems the commission is accused of, these intrusive questions are related to the perception that every resident of the union is a potential criminal. this is unacceptable in a society of law! in addition, the european commission is proposing a budget of €12 million to carry out this information gathering work. a disproportionate sum in these times of crisis and austerity, for an otherwise uncertain outcome. for these reasons i voted against this proposal which represents a further infringement of fundamental rights and privacy.

in writing. i voted in favour of referring the text back to the committee on transport and i welcome the result of the vote which will allow the text to be examined in a more calm atmosphere. this proposal provides real answers to the problems identified by the various stakeholders. but we are talking about a sector where working conditions remain difficult, and i can understand the fears expressed by the social partners in the face of any new proposals. i believe that a closer dialogue is therefore necessary before any measures are adopted, so that the actors concerned by this proposal for a regulation can understand the issues involved. the regulation would, in particular, strengthen safety standards, ensure greater transparency in the award of contracts, strengthen the role of airports in crisis situations and ensure that workers' rights are better protected. as for the slight opening up of these regulated markets, the arrival of a third provider to put an end to certain monopolistic situations while ensuring the quality of services to users seems to me to be in the right direction. that is why a rejection of the proposal would have been a missed opportunity for workers and consumers.
in writing. i welcome the european parliament's decision to reopen negotiations in the parliamentary committee responsible on the proposed opening of the market for airport ground handling services. given the sensitivity of the subject, i see this postponement as a conciliatory gesture to the social partners who were concerned that the increase in the minimum number of in-country assistance providers from two to three would lead to a precarious employment situation in the sector. this increase, which must be distinguished from market opening, was aimed at services such as baggage handling, runway operations, fuel and oil and cargo and mail, which are almost monopolistically owned by one or two service providers at some european airports, which can affect the quality of services. the fears expressed by airport staff are understandable, but the measures envisaged would not have affected france, which already applies them. however, the strong concerns raised by this proposal clearly demonstrate the need to strengthen the dialogue with all the partners concerned.

in writing. the proposal submitted by the commission to the european parliament was aimed at liberalising ground handling services (gas), i.e. services provided to an air carrier at an airport. the aim was to allow at least a third independent ground handling company to enter the market, which would have the effect of liberalising and increasing the number of ground handling service providers, with catastrophic social consequences for airport workers. the text was so controversial that the parliamentary committee on transport (tran) voted against it. i therefore voted against this text and for its referral back to committee. the proposal was indeed rejected by a majority of the european parliament, and i welcome that. my colleagues in the gue/ngl group and i will be keeping a close eye on this matter.
in writing. while 70% of flight delays are due to problems on the ground, it is essential to support the concrete measures proposed by the european commission to improve the efficiency and quality of these airport ground handling services (baggage, runway operations, fuel, etc.), streamline air traffic and improve passenger comfort. the creation of a ground services coordinator, the requirement for each airline to have a legal representative and the opening up of the market for ground services to a third party are all concrete proposals which will enable us to achieve these objectives in the interests of travellers. i therefore regret that some of my socialist and green colleagues have opposed this new opening up to competition for ideological reasons and have called, in vain, for the rejection of this proposal for a regulation, which nevertheless proposes concrete solutions without upsetting the system. it is up to the committee on transport, of which i am a member, to vote on this text again. i shall be defending the measures which i consider necessary to modernise the operation of our airports, which will double the number of passengers by 2030.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text which will provide a better framework for the rules on the allocation of time slots within the union. this text is the result of an agreement which reorientated the european commission's proposal, which did not respond in any way to the expectations of the sector and the need for increased capacity. it is very regrettable, however, that a majority of members supported the creation of a monetised time-slot exchange market. this opens the way for speculation in an industry already plagued by fierce competition. it would have been wiser to tackle this unfair competition before letting european companies loose in a market where the rules of the game are not the same for everyone. moreover, with this secondary market, there is a real risk to the survival of regional services which are so important for opening up our territories and maintaining the competitiveness of our economic players.

in writing. i welcome the adoption of this regulation which addresses the problem of airport congestion by encouraging airlines to make better use of the slots they get for take-off and landing. among the rules adopted to make more rational use of infrastructure, i would like to mention the renewal of the 'use-or-lose it' rule, which obliges airlines to use 80% of slots if they want them to be automatically renewed the following year. i also supported the reinforcement of penalties for late return from a flight cancellation slot. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment by the use of radioactive substances. finally, i welcome the possibility for companies to exchange slots or resell slots to each other. i would, however, call for strict application of the measures on the market for the resale of slots: the sale can only take place if the slot has been used for at least a year, otherwise speculation would be allowed to run rampant, to the detriment of travellers.

in writing. by voting in favour of this report, i support the launch of a financial transaction tax in europe. while the specific details of the agreement are yet to be agreed, i welcome the adoption of this text, which marks a key step in implementing the g8 commitments to combat the crisis and return to growth.
in writing. despite the reluctance of some states, and after 12 years of persistence, the green light is finally given to the enhanced cooperation of 11 eu countries to introduce a financial transaction tax. it is worth recalling that this is the first enhanced cooperation in the field of taxation, where all decisions require unanimity, and therefore it is a source of great pride for all those who have supported this project since 2000. it is now important to convince the other countries of the union to adopt this tax so that we have a substantial budget of several tens of billions of euros. with such a product we could both create a new own resource for the eu and devote a substantial part of it to innovative financing to combat major pandemics, such as hunger, illiteracy or climate change. in the meantime, this tax is a good signal to the world, because the aim is to reach an agreement at international level in the long term. the moralization of finance must become a shared objective to prevent the crisis we experienced in 2008 and which continues to have a negative impact on our economies.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to strengthen european cooperation with a view to introducing a financial transaction tax. this tax, initiated by nicolas sarkozy, will make it possible to strengthen the european budget with a stable resource, but also independent of the goodwill of the member states.
in writing. in substance, i am in full agreement with the creation of a financial transaction tax. after the hundreds of billions injected into public funds to save the banks, it is time for the sector to finally contribute to solving the economic and budgetary crisis it has caused. the problem is the increased cooperation. it has only 11 participating states, not including the two main financial havens, the united kingdom and luxembourg. with so few participants, is it really reasonable to allow the commission to legislate in this area? i am reminded of the commission's ultimate desire to pass the proceeds of this tax onto the european budget rather than the national budgets. it would be even more unacceptable if the very text introducing the new tax were to be adopted by the ordinary legislative procedure, as parliament is asking for. that is to say, by a qualified majority and with the right of all the members of the european parliament, including those of the 16 countries which have rejected the tax, to vote. if the governments of the eleven volunteer states have the courage, they can agree on the modalities of a similar tax to be introduced at the same time at national level, or even act independently.
in writing. i gave my full support to the resolution by my colleague, anni podimata, authorising enhanced cooperation between 11 member states - which alone account for 90% of the euro area's gdp - to introduce a financial transaction tax between them, even if the ultimate aim remains to have a ftt at world level. i share the view that this tax should cover as many transactions as possible, which would be a form of 'reparation' for the damage caused by the speculative financial crisis. finance must return to its original task of financing the real economy. the tax should also help to set the eu on the path to a budget with its own resources, which is a very good thing in a time when the member states are relying on their national budgets in times of crisis. finally, beyond the unanimity rules in the council which prevail in this area of taxation, it seems to me important that the european parliament can play more than an advisory role in the further decision-making process.
in writing. on wednesday 12 december 2012, the european parliament authorised 11 member states to launch the enhanced cooperation procedure (france, germany, austria, belgium, spain, estonia, greece, italy, portugal, slovakia and slovenia) for the establishment of a financial transaction tax. the financial transaction tax which president nicolas sarkozy had advocated on many occasions at the major international meetings of the g8, the g20 and at european summits, and which the european parliament had been calling for for over two years, should be implemented after the council of the european union has given its approval by qualified majority. if the financial transaction tax becomes operational, it will consist of a levy of 0.1% on shares and bonds and 0.01% on derivatives. the purpose of the proceeds of this tax, which still causes deep differences within the council, remains to be defined.
in writing. at the plenary session of 12 december 2012, the majority of my colleagues (533 votes in favour) and i gave the green light to the enhanced cooperation of a financial transaction tax between 11 member states of the european union. this is an important step as parliament has just approved the first enhanced cooperation in the field of taxation. i welcome this development.
in writing. the commission estimates that a financial transaction tax, with a proposed tax rate of 0.1% on standard financial products (shares and bonds) and 0.01% on other financial products, would generate revenues of around €57 billion in 2012 alone. the idea of a tax is supported by 64% of european citizens, as i am. i therefore welcome the decision by 11 member states to strengthen their cooperation in order to introduce a financial transaction tax. i believe that this is a fair and consistent way out of the crisis. fair, because this tax allows the financial sector, which is partly responsible for the financial crisis, to contribute more to the cost of the crisis, which i believe has not yet sufficiently borne its share. it is also coherent, since it will provide substantial funds for the annual budget of the union, which, in view of the extension of its powers, is in great need of them. this could lead to a reduction in the member states' contributions to the union budget, allowing them to make further savings.
in writing. i voted in favour of enhanced cooperation in the field of taxation of financial transactions. the procedure for enhanced cooperation is certainly not ideal and a commitment by all the member states would have been preferable. moreover, it is only a very small step towards better financial regulation, but it can be said that it has the merit of being a step in the right direction. this is the first enhanced cooperation in the field of taxation and it should lead, for the first time at international level, to the implementation of the famous taxation of financial transactions. at present, 11 member states (belgium, germany, estonia, greece, spain, france, italy, austria, portugal, slovenia and slovakia) are involved in the process. we are far from being behind, but in the gue/ngl - which was the first group in the european parliament to promote this tax - we will continue to fight for its eventual generalization.
in writing. the vote by our assembly to formalise enhanced cooperation between 11 member states for the creation of a financial transaction tax is a significant source of satisfaction. this project, which was supported by president sarkozy, who was able to dispel the doubts of germany in particular, is finally becoming a reality and proves that the eu is able to unite and act when the situation calls for an ambitious response. the idea is simple: in the face of europe's budgetary difficulties and with financial flows representing an astronomical sum, a painless breakdown of the amounts of transactions would provide a valuable financial boon to supplement national budgetary contributions to the common european pot. the expected effect is extremely positive, because once a member state introduces such a tax, it will be able to deduct the proceeds from its contribution to the eu budget. this is all the more beneficial as it will contribute to the consolidation of public finances and will support major european projects that generate growth, competitiveness and employment, with considerable leverage. however, only 11 of the 27 member states have such a tax in place at present, but there is no doubt that the benefits will soon far outweigh the reluctance to implement it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which aims to improve the conditions for the transport of animals. without calling for a specific timetable (8 hours requested by the european parliament), i believe it is essential to set better limits on transport, conditions and duration, particularly as regards the journey to the slaughterhouses. on the basis of this report, the commission should propose a draft regulation in the near future.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the protection of animals during transport. i believe that uniform implementation of existing european legislation on the transport of animals in the member states should be a priority in order to ensure the best possible protection of animal welfare. as a result of this standardisation, dissuasive and proportionate sanctions will be able to ensure full compliance with this legislation. however, i consider that a limitation of the transport time for animals for slaughter to eight hours is an excessive proposal because it is not based on any scientific basis. i therefore opposed this amendment.
in writing. since 2007, the european union has had legislation on the transport of animals to the place of slaughter. but these rules are accompanied by sporadic checks and often silly penalties, which lead some carriers to infringe: animals not watered or fed, failure to comply with rest periods required for long journeys or underestimated declarations of travel times. at the same time, the number of animals transported into the eu has increased sharply, with a 70% increase in pigs between 2005 and 2009. one third of these journeys take eight hours or more, increasing the health risks. to overcome these difficulties, which are sometimes linked to misinterpretations of european legislation, it is urgent that the commission publish appropriate explanatory and guidance documents. finally, to avoid unnecessary transport of animals over long distances, the eu should also help to create shorter supply chains to end the decline of small local slaughterhouses and promote meat processing at local level.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because animal welfare is a key consideration when transporting animals. we cannot accept the loss of livestock, the deterioration of health or stressful situations caused by transport alone. i have already supported the written declaration no 49/2011 from 2011 limiting the transport time for animals destined for slaughter to eight hours. i therefore await a legislative proposal from the european commission which takes account of the european geographical and social reality and scientific facts to improve animal welfare in this area.
in writing. at the plenary session on 12 december, i supported the report by my colleague janusz wojciechowski. the report was adopted by 555 votes in favour, 56 against and 34 abstentions. this is a balanced ratio which aims to improve the welfare of animals during transport. in his report, janusz wojciechowski advocates, in particular, the implementation of dissuasive and proportionate sanctions for effective compliance with european legislation, the slaughter of animals as close as possible to their place of rearing and, finally, the creation of training for transport companies and transporters.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the protection of animals during transport to encourage member states to put in place existing rules and to impose more dissuasive penalties where they are not respected. in order to avoid unnecessary transport of animals over long distances, the eu should promote short supply chains and take measures to end the decline of local slaughterhouses.
in writing. the number of animals transported in the eu from their place of production to the slaughterhouse has increased sharply in recent years - by 70% in the case of pigs, for example. a third of these trips took eight hours or more, often in precarious conditions. this resolution calls for better protection of animals during transport. i support it. this requires first of all better application of existing legislation in this field in the member states (better implementation, increased inspections and controls, dissuasive sanctions for infringers). while it is desirable to limit the transport time of animals to the slaughterhouse to 8 hours - with geographical and scientifically justified exceptions for certain species - this is not sufficient: the welfare of animals also depends on adequate equipment in the vehicle and their proper treatment during transport. i am also convinced of the need to create short and transparent supply chains, to take measures to stop the decline of small local slaughterhouses and to promote meat processing at local level. this would help to limit the transport of animals over long distances and thus to reduce unnecessary suffering.
in writing. despite very protective legislation, problems remain during animal transport leading to serious ill-treatment, mainly due to weak implementation of these regulations by member states. in this report, parliament therefore warns of these delays in transpositions, encourages the member states to remedy them and also advocates the introduction of these european standards on animal welfare in bilateral trade negotiations with third countries. the report also calls for the development of mobile slaughterhouses or small regional slaughterhouses to avoid unnecessary transport of animals over long distances and to try to halt the decline of small local slaughterhouses and promote meat processing at local level. finally, the question of the limitation of the transport time for animals destined for slaughter to eight hours is raised again. this would be a good thing for animal welfare but it cannot be done without taking account of transport conditions. that is why, despite the good intentions of this report, i abstained.
in writing. this report presents the state of fundamental rights in the european union. this is a sensitive subject at european level, because it affects the most intimate convictions of our peoples, which differ from one country to another. fundamental rights must be respected everywhere. in this spirit, i stood out by wanting to support a provision explicitly denouncing the abuses of the current hungarian government. it is important to be able to criticise such behaviour, including within one's own political family. i abstained on the whole of this text, some of the provisions of which i do not think are relevant, without, however, wishing to block its adoption.
in writing. the fight against discrimination and respect for human rights are principles on which the union is built. these values of europe are enshrined in its founding texts, in community law and in the european charter of fundamental rights. to preserve these european acquis, member states must ensure that they guard against any drift towards certain minorities, in particular members of the roma community, lgbt people, disabled people, migrants and asylum seekers. the european union must actively combat any increase in racist, xenophobic, anti-semitic or other acts that undermine media pluralism and freedom. to this end, the european agency for fundamental rights was set up to monitor and prevent any shortcomings in the protection of fundamental rights. the commission must be able to benefit from the necessary resources and multiannual strategies to be effective in its mission.
