vice-president of the commission. − mr president, let me first thank ms ždanoka for proposing that parliament gives its consent to the draft multiannual framework for the fundamental rights agency on the basis of the draft agreed by the council. i appreciate also the remarks made by the rapporteur to the effect that, while the situation is far from excellent, it would be better to accept it. we know that the fundamental rights agency plays an invaluable role in gathering comparative data, and we need such data as evidence to underpin our policies in the field of fundamental rights. so we need the agency to be able to continue its work. let me cite two examples that show how the agency has innovated in order to help us to carry out very far-reaching legislative or decision-making work at the level of the institutions. firstly, the agency played a crucial role in underpinning the effectiveness of our policies in relation to the roma minority. in 2012 the agency adopted a roma multiannual programme running up to 2020. it will provide us with the information we need to assess whether the member states’ efforts to integrate the roma population bring about real change in the daily life of the roma in terms of education, housing, health and employment. we need this information in order to take the next steps required. another example has been the agency’s work on access to justice and the survey on the perception of discrimination and hate crimes against lgtb people that the agency is conducting at the request of the commission. it plans to publish the results of the survey in 2013. these are only some examples of the very valuable work the agency conducts. they show why we need it to continue and why its work should not be interrupted. besides these very concrete actions, the agency also builds up strong methodologies and insights concerning the exchange of experiences and the identification of best practices. so all this is needed but unfortunately, as the rapporteur has already said, the good work of the agency is being jeopardised, as the council will not be in a position to adopt the multiannual framework for the agency by the end of december this year, as required by union law. we all knew about this deadline and we have put a lot of intense effort into working with the council. that is also the reason why there has been this concession to the council, which means that the agency will not be able to initiate work on police or judicial cooperation on criminal matters on its own initiative under the new multiannual framework. it can only work in this field if there is a request from parliament, from the council or from the commission. i really regret this solution and i will make a formal declaration to that effect when the proposal is formally approved. because — and this is a fundamental point — we cannot ignore the fact that we have a new treaty, the treaty of lisbon, with all its consequences. we do not have a pillar structure any more; there is only one european law. the fundamental rights agency needs to be able to collect data on fundamental rights in a comparable manner, including in the old ‘third pillar’ domains of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. but, as you know, when you have a unanimity rule you are blocked. there was no other option: to arrive at unanimity, concessions had to be made. despite all this, one member state has failed to take the necessary steps that would have ensured that the multiannual framework was adopted in time. the commission regrets this delay because it will have repercussions on the work of the agency and its staff, which will be in ‘caretaker mode’ as from january. this again shows that the requirement for unanimity is not a great help in our institutional work. the commission takes note that the justice ministers discussed this issue on 7 december in the council and that a request has been made to enable the agency to work during the interim period. this is a last-minute ‘patch’; fortunately we have this option, but in any case it is only a temporary solution. every effort should continue to be made by all the member states to ensure the swift adoption of the multiannual framework as early as possible in 2013. this is the only way to ensure that the agency can work at full speed to contribute to our work on the protection of fundamental rights. let me clarify nevertheless for this house that the multiannual framework which we are discussing is neither a work programme nor the instrument that establishes the powers and the tasks of the agency. the agency’s work programmes are adopted each year by the management board within the thematic areas determined by the multiannual framework. president, let me conclude by saying that the commission appreciates the sense of responsibility of the rapporteur and of parliament.

in writing. the report presents the european parliament's recommendations on the negotiations which started in 2008 for a new eu-russia agreement which is intended to replace the partnership and cooperation agreement in force since december 1997. i voted in favour of this text because my political group included provisions calling for respect for fundamental freedoms and a requirement of reciprocity with russia.
in writing. russia is the european union's third largest trading partner. it is also a country of vital strategic importance in the political, energy, economic, environmental and cultural fields. it is therefore natural that the european union should seek to maintain a relationship of trust with it. the 1994 partnership and cooperation agreement needs to be modernised and extended, especially as russia has just joined the wto. in the context of the current negotiations on a more comprehensive association agreement, the european union must ensure that progress is made in russia with regard to respect for the union's fundamental values of democracy and the rule of law. russian political life is still too marked by the violation of these principles, as illustrated by the recent trial of the members of the pussy riot group, as well as by other cases of arrests and detentions for political reasons and repressive measures taken against the opposition. the eu must make the signing of this new agreement conditional on progress in respecting fundamental rights and on russia's strict observance of wto principles.
in writing. the hannes swoboda report contains the european parliament's recommendations to the council and the european commission on the opening of negotiations for a new agreement between the european union and russia. the new agreement, which is expected to replace the one signed in 1994, should provide a comprehensive, forward-looking and legally binding framework for the development of relations with russia in the future. russia is an important partner of the european union and that is why i voted in favour of this report and i welcome its adoption. i will remain vigilant on the outcome of the negotiations but have full confidence in russia to continue its efforts with regard to respect for the rule of law or democracy. both the eu and russia stand to gain from a successful outcome of the negotiations.
in writing. this report is an anti-russian indictment. it is the very prototype of the european union's interest in human rights. he's asking russia to do what he's not asking the coup government in honduras to do before they ratify a free trade agreement. it even blames the russian government for the impasse in the negotiations, even as the eu endorses the deployment of nato's missile shield on the russian border. he denounced russia's selective trade diplomacy but refused to negotiate with the common economic area at least until an agreement was reached with russia alone. the energy issue, which is at the heart of the matter, is mentioned only once. i denounce the narrow-minded imperialism and bad faith that are concentrated in this report. i vote against it.
in writing. i supported this text, adopted by the european parliament, which calls on israel to promote dialogue with palestine rather than continue the expansion of settlements in the west bank. this behaviour undermines any chance of a calm approach to the negotiations and is illegal under international law.
in writing. the announcement by israel that it will build 3,000 additional housing units in east jerusalem and the west bank, including in the so-called e1 area, is extremely worrying. located between jerusalem and the settlement of maale adumim, where israel had pledged to the united states not to build, these new constructions would de facto link maale adumim to the settlement districts of east jerusalem. this announcement, following the un general assembly vote to grant palestine non-member observer status at the united nations, is likely to jeopardise the resumption of negotiations with a view to achieving a two-state solution. it is therefore very important that the israeli government reverse its decision and exercise restraint, because this attitude makes it even more difficult to resume direct dialogue between israel and the palestinians. the european union and its member states, together with the quartet countries, must continue their mediation and work fully to restart the peace process.
in writing. i vote in favour of this resolution. it reaffirms its support for the two-state solution based on the 1967 borders; it called for the immediate transfer of palestinian tax revenues which the israeli government had suspended. that's a good thing. i regret, however, that while the very purpose of the resolution was to condemn the announcement by the outgoing israeli government of new settlements and the withholding of palestinian tax revenues, the text is only capable of 'regret' and 'expressing deep concern'. i also regret that the text merely calls for the human rights clause of the eu-israel free trade agreement to be respected, without providing the means to do so. he does not ask for the freezing of the fund until this clause is respected. a soft consensus on minimum texts as soon as it comes to the rights of peoples, that is all this parliament is capable of doing.
in writing. the vote on this resolution, which i co-signed, is both good and bad news: good news because the vast majority of meps disapprove of the israeli strategy, which is in contradiction with the commitments of that state, and bad news because it highlights a new obstacle on the road to peace and is yet another call by our assembly to reach a resolution of this conflict which is poisoning the region. the decision of the israeli government to expand settlements in the west bank seriously undermines the prospect of creating two neighbouring, independent, peaceful and economically viable states in the middle east, one israeli and one palestinian, within the 1967 borders. it was also important that parliament should express its concern at the risk of a standstill and an escalation of violence. when we know that the israeli-palestinian conflict crystallizes all the rancor in the arab world, it goes without saying that the eu must do everything in its power to bring the two neighbours back to the negotiating table. any initiative that would ruin the peace efforts must be banned, lest it add to the provocation and despair of the two peoples who are destined to live side by side.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution. it recalled the need to further develop relations with ukraine, but that this would only be possible when fundamental rights and democratic principles were fully applied in that country.
in writing. the 2012 elections in ukraine, which were supposed to serve as a test of the country's commitment to the rule of law and genuine democracy, were unsatisfactory and even showed some regression compared to previous elections. in particular, we were concerned about intimidation of candidates and election staff, unfair media coverage and numerous irregularities in the counting of votes. the resolution which has been adopted and which i supported by my vote therefore makes the signing of an association agreement with ukraine, an agreement to which the european union remains committed, conditional on concrete progress in the area of democratic principles.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because it is aimed at supporting the steel industry. the industry must become more competitive to be viable and responsive to changing conditions in european and non-european markets, as it is essential for growth and prosperity in europe.
in writing. our steel industry is a victim of the crisis, which is hitting it hard, and we have an obligation to protect it. with this text we want to speed up the action of the union: it is urgent to study the situation and make proposals quickly. i supported this text, which reaffirms our ambition to avoid the relocation of these high-technology industries outside europe: they are a model of know-how and a pool of skills and knowledge essential to our economy. the commission will draw up an action plan for the steel industry by june 2013: this resolution stresses the importance that this action plan should attach to the fight against high energy and raw material prices. they are a threat to our industry, and it is imperative that we seek solutions to the problems they create.
in writing. the european steel industry is currently suffering from a difficult international situation, but most experts believe that this phase of depression is temporary. it is therefore necessary to have a long-term european strategy to preserve our human know-how and our production potential, since steel products, starting with steel, are indispensable to many sectors of our industry, such as the automotive, construction, machine tools and energy transport sectors. some of these sectors require very sophisticated technology, and we cannot afford to lose or let go of the skills that make our countries' steel industry excellent. this is a matter of a very european dimension. we need to coordinate our industrial policies better to prevent the risks of relocation, to encourage research, particularly in ultra-low-carbon steelmaking processes (ulcos).
in writing. when we vote on the resolutions on the future of the european steel industry, we must ask ourselves only one question: is there in these texts a beginning of a beginning to safeguard the european steel industry? it is clear to us that the desire for intervention stops at the level of incantation! the european steel industry is the victim of unprecedented financial vampirisation, is facing unfair competition, is the object of organized robbery and theft of its know-how, ... the only proposals put forward are: 'we ask the commission to do well ...'. this positioning is not at all up to the challenge, and we would even say that, by its very nature, it is far too cold, and it gives free rein to the destructive will of international groups like mittal. however, tens of thousands of jobs are at stake, unique know-how is about to be stolen from us, entire territories are about to find themselves in dramatic social situations ... the steel industry, like the european industry, needs other answers. the commission has also proposed a number of measures to help the regions in the community to meet the needs of the population. (explanation of vote abbreviated pursuant to rule 163 (1) of the rules of procedure)
in writing. in the present context, and i am thinking in particular of the situation with the blast furnaces in florange, it is imperative that the european union take up the subject of the steel industry in europe and help to curb this crisis which threatens the future of 360 000 jobs spread over 50 sites in 23 member states. recognising that the future of the sector requires coordinated national responses and european intervention, the european parliament has voted in favour of a european steel action plan to be presented by the european commission by june 2013. what an irony for the eu when this sector is at the origin of european construction! yet steel is one of the most traded industrial materials in the world. the european sector accounts for 1.4% of the eu's gross domestic product and a turnover of around €200 billion. it is time we imposed more reciprocity in our trade with shared social and environmental standards. president sarkozy himself had pledged during the presidential campaign to impose a carbon tax on the union's borders, as we already impose on our own companies. it is regrettable that the european parliament has not adopted this solution.
in writing. parliament adopted a joint resolution containing an action plan for the steel industry. given the recent difficulties faced by many sites, including florange in france, i felt it was necessary to adopt this text in order to improve competitiveness and encourage investment. the european steel industry is facing a sharp decline in demand, linked in particular to increased competition from imports from third countries which apply different regulations. we therefore urge the commission to monitor closely the development of the factories threatened.
in writing. there are two very positive points in this resolution. it states, and i quote, 'that it is in the interest of the european union as a whole to preserve the activities which feed its industrial fabric' and that 'high-tech industries such as the steel industry must be preserved by taking immediate measures to prevent their relocation outside the european territory'. both statements are relevant. it is a pity that the epp and sd groups, which are co-signatories of this text, do not draw any conclusions from it. the text reaffirms the rule of free and undistorted competition within the european union and in the world and merely calls for relocations to be made in 'strict compliance with eu competition law'. it merely invited the commission to 'monitor closely the future development of the factories' in florange and elsewhere. i am voting against this inconsistent text.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the steel industry is in crisis in europe. its maintenance is vital to our economy. it employs thousands of people and is a key link in the automotive, construction and mechanical industries. the preservation of our industrial and scientific know-how is a commitment which must be honoured. however, the steel industry is not resisting the pressure of unfair competition from certain countries, which are driving down prices by imposing lower social and environmental standards than ours. this is not sustainable. this resolution is in the right direction when it calls on europe to impose fairer trade, the same rules of the game for all at international level (reciprocity). i also regret that a very small majority of my colleagues did not have the courage to demand a carbon tax at our borders. we ask our industry to limit its impact on the environment, so it is only right that we should ask the same of industries that export to our markets. but nothing is lost yet. i shall have occasion very shortly to remind the european parliament of this.
author. - mr president, in the democratic republic of the congo, one word alone sums up the ills that have been eating away at that region for decades: makala! makala is a gold mine in the north of the democratic republic of congo, a symbol of the plundering of natural resources that is destabilizing the entire great lakes region. european multinational corporations are accused of participating in the corruption of local rebel groups and of hunting down local miners to expand their influence and seize the most lucrative land. makala is also the location of the main prison in kinshasa, where, again, impunity and corruption are rampant. the congolese government, as in the mineral regions, is non-existent. the prison administration is totally lacking. military prisoners make the law and demand that civilian prisoners bail them out. thousands of people, never tried or convicted, are crowded into this virtual death chamber. makala, a gold mine or an abandoned prison, is the symbol of these lawless areas. lasting peace in the democratic republic of congo requires the restoration of the rule of law, a real fight against the impunity that has plagued the entire region for too long. peace must not be at the expense of justice. we need to be clear. any peace agreement must exclude immunity or amnesty for war criminals like bosco ntaganda, the terminator, who set fire to this country and shed blood and are still not worried. fighting impunity in a country where nearly half a million women have been killed in 16 years is what dr mukwege, the tireless advocate for raped women, is trying to do. it's because he's exposing these atrocities and doing incredible work for these women that there's been an attempt on his life. we must condemn such acts in the strongest possible terms, but above all we must put pressure on the congolese government to ensure that this assassination attempt is investigated impartially and as quickly as possible. peace also depends, first and foremost, on greater social justice, that is, on a genuine sharing of natural resources.
